title: Replace continuous replication with periodic replication
body:
As discussed in [this document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/159qKQwYo02Cxh3T0YidK_2D-KAtWdLEkvq8slnwdMuc/edit) replace continuous replication with periodic one-shot replication to improve server scalability, phone battery usage, network data usage, and reduce code complexity.

- [ ] Implement polling to do a bidirectional replication every 5 minutes. The specific number is up for debate but 5 minutes is a safe place to start.
- [ ] Implement #3976 so users can manually trigger a bidirectional sync.
- [ ] Investigate using [online event handlers](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/NavigatorOnLine/onLine#Specification) to trigger a bidirectional sync when a user comes back online if it's been longer than the 5 minute timer above.
- [ ] Remove continuous replication code from the API changes endpoint.

title: Fix getting registrations via querying `medic-client/registered_patients`
body:
When sentinel data was pulled out into it's own database (https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/issues/3423), `medic-client/registered_patients` view started to yield no results, due to it's dependence of checking `registration` transition execution info to be present within the doc.
This view is used by Sentinel (to generate and mute messages), by API (`create-patient-contacts` migration) and Webapp to format data records ( generating `scheduled_messages` in the UI ).

title: Expose SMS sending capabilities in android wrapper
body:
We need to allow for the web app to send SMS messages. We can achieve this (on phones) by exposing an API endpoint in the JS bridge that lets you pass a phone number and a message, which the android wrapper will then send.

We do not need to read SMS messages or do anything more complicated at this time.

Things to think about:
 - Do we want to just blind-fire this request, or have it call a callback when it succeeds (or fails)?
 - Do we need some kind of queuing on the android wrapper side?

title: Support XForms that "compile" into SMS messages
body:
See this section of this document for discussion specific pertaining to the project that requires this: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Ygpi5JzVKYbfWF-uEIc1RCvAPSGq-ut0N8cHMSn5eXY/edit#heading=h.2vg9c5lgu2ld

The developer should also work with @maremegaye so they have the specific form that is needed to test with and make sure the implementation works for that form. This is important because:
 - We need to make all the information needed later fits inside one SMS (multi-sms is not globally supported by mobile networks and is generally dodgy AFAICT), and this form has the potential to be quite large
 - We need to either have this report *also* possibly contain patient demos if the patient was created offline (you can tell: if they have a patient shortcode they made it to the server) or also configure the new patient form to send SMS

We could also consider hooking into PouchDB and only sending SMS if the form can't be replicated upward immediately. That could be hard though, and for time constraint reasons it's fine to not do this

title: SIH integration
body:
See this doc for details: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Ygpi5JzVKYbfWF-uEIc1RCvAPSGq-ut0N8cHMSn5eXY/edit#

@maremegaye is the design contact, @Fatoufall is the PM contact.

We need to have a closed loop flow between us and SIH. We're going to use Sentinel (my boy!), triggered based on docs coming in via data/sms from the CHW, as well as inbound JSON docs coming from SIH itself, to both trigger api calls to SIH (from the former) and trigger SMS back to the CHW (from the latter).

We should:
 - Work out exactly what we want to send to SIH when a referral happens, come up with an example JSON and provide it to them so they can build their api
 - Work out what we'd like them to send us back for the different actions that can happen and create JSON forms with example JSON, provide it to them and configure those forms into [the shared dev instance](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/4844). SIH can then use [the records api](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/tree/master/api#post-apiv2records) to send us these JSON forms
 - build a sentinel transition that take incoming referral reports from a CHW, convert them into a SIH api request and send them along
 - build a sentinel transition that manages the JSON forms created above, and sends SMS' to CHWs based on rules described in the linked document

Things we need for a referral:
 - An identifier for the referral. Should be unique across the whole instance. This makes it easy for impact to link referrals and loop closing actions (the patient arriving at the facility etc) together. We would send this to SIH allowing them to send it back to us.
 - An identifier for the patient. Could be the patient UUID, or their shortcode[1]. Again, we would send this to SIH allowing them to send it back to us. Also lets them re-use / overwrite existing patient records in their system
 - Demographics for the patient: name, dob, sex
 - The CHW who is responsible for them: name, area maybe (check with SIH folks)
 - The referral data itself: danger signs etc, work with @maremegaye to come up with this (also see #4812)

[1] Remember that the patient may already exist, but this might also be the first time the server is hearing about them, because the CHW could be offline when they are created. If we can fit it maybe we pass the UUID in the referral SMS from the CHW and then send that as well.

title: Replace yarn with npm
body:
A few months ago [we decided to move to yarn](#3032) due to problems we were having with npm, but now I believe yarn to be a worse solution for us.

This will help solve:

- audit only works with npm
- yarn pack is completely broken
- requiring a yarn version doesn't work when working on older code (aka `--ignore-engines` hell)

Todo:

- [x] Change `yarn` to `npm` everywhere in our build scripts.
- [x] Replace the yarn.lock with package-lock.json everywhere.
- [ ] Enforce transitive dependencies either with [npm-force-resolutions](https://www.npmjs.com/package/npm-force-resolutions) or by rolling our own. Hook this into the npm scripts so it happens automatically.
- [ ] Ensure CI respects the package-lock so what is packed and released is exactly what was used in development and tested in CI.
- [ ] Use `npm audit` responsibly so we mitigate vulnerabilities (#3768).
- [ ] Check this fixes #4701

Adds an admin page with an overview of all outgoing SMS messages, split into 4 tabs:
 - a `scheduled` tab which contains all messages which are in the `scheduled` state, displayed in ascending order, sorted by their due date
- a `will not send` tab which contains all messages which will not be sent (statuses: `muted`, `cleared`, `denied`, `duplicate`), which have a due date in the future, displayed in ascending order sorted by due date,

title: 3327 - Date picker widget is not translated
body:
# Description

The Enketo Datetime-Extended widget isn't translated in the appropriate language.

#3327

# Review checklist

- [ ] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the [style guide](https://github.com/medic/medic-docs/blob/master/development/style-guide.md), documented if necessary.
- [ ] Documented: Announced in Changes.md in plain English. Configuration and user documentation on [medic-docs](https://github.com/medic/medic-docs/)
- [ ] Tested: Unit and/or e2e where appropriate
- [ ] Internationalised: All user facing text
- [ ] Backwards compatible: Works with existing data and configuration or includes a migration. Any breaking changes documented in Changes.md.

# Comments

There are a few broad approaches one could take to this: 

1. The enketo widget "datetime-extended" uses [bootstrap-datepicker](https://github.com/uxsolutions/bootstrap-datepicker) under the hood which directly supports many languages. Can flick this switch on.
1. We could use a pattern like using moment as the translator as in `webapp/js/enketo/translator`.  
1. I guess we could use the standard angular translation workflow. 
1. Others? 

Here is a solution based on 1 from above. Happy to revisit with another approach if people think it is better. Some background on the Bootstrap-datepicker:

* Bootstrap-datepicker includes locale data for 6/8 of the default medic languages [en, es, fr, sw, id, hi] plus many additional languages if required. [list of languages](https://github.com/uxsolutions/bootstrap-datepicker/tree/master/js/locales). I have little insight into the number of languages you support in practice ... 
* Nipali (ne) is not supported, but is already handled by a special widget bikram-sambat-datepicker. 
* Bamanankan (bm) is missing. 
* enketo-core uses a _two-year old build_ of bootstrap-datepicker@1.6.x. Which seems to be working fine, but doesn't support Hindi (hi). So some considerations there.

Next, I considered three approaches for getting the user's language down into the bootstrap-datepicker control.

1. Update Enketo-Core `Datepicker-Extended` widget to accept language information through the existing `options` widget parameter.
1. Extend the Enketo-Core `Datepicker-Extended` widget into some sort of Medic-specific  DatepickerExtendedLocalized which obtains language data via Angular (similar to `android-datepicker`).
1. Pass language information directly into bootstrap-datepicker.
1. Other?

I went with option 3 above. Option 1 requires a change in Enketo-Core but is possibly a cleaner solution. 2 was very messy and basically requires forking the full Datepicker-Extended widget. 3 seems reasonable, but is probably not the ideal division of responsibility between Medic/Enketo. Happy to revisit if you have suggestions!

title: 3675 - Blacklist outgoing messages to carriers
body:
# Description

The auto-reply functionality in sentinel can get into infinite loops of robots replying to each other. So, we want to not auto-reply to messages from carriers. Although a carrier is flagged in configuration and an additional blacklist exists, additional generic and default configurations would be useful to make initial configuration easier.

medic/medic-webapp#3675

# Approach 

I've implemented the general configuration mechanisms proposed in @alxndrsn solution # 1 in https://github.com/medic/medic-gateway/issues/122.

This consists of configuration

* `outgoing_deny_numbers_shorter_than=6` - to deny replies to messages from shortcodes (e.g. `60396`)
* `outgoing_deny_numbers_with_alphas=true` - to deny replies to non-numeric senders (e.g. `TELKOMSEL`, `one2one`)

Alternatively, I considered making the `outgoing_deny_list` support a list of regex instead of having multiple outgoing_deny configurations. This could achieve the same result while being a more robust and powerful tool. However, it may not be as intuitive to configure so I went with specific scenario-based configurations. As always, happy to revisit this using any other approach. 

If you like this approach, I'll also update relevant documentation. I'm not sold on the names of the configuration variables, suggestions welcome!

I've tested this with unit tests and using the [message test](http://localhost:5988/medic/_design/medic-admin/_rewrite#/message-test).  Code path is also hit by a bunch of transitions [accept_patient_reports, default_responses, registration, update_notifications] which I don't have a lot of context on, so unsure if it could potentially have negative effects worth testing out.

title: Allow supervisors to see CHW targets and support display of aggregate targets widgets
body:
[Product initiative detail ](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1EQHQI11XqI8aQeUsnmlrD3ny83fj5N6MZATrLzsm_-I/edit#heading=h.q31g948sivit)

Read more details and view additional screenshots in the MVP deck: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1AbOxkGgggUoI0QzRmwVqfX0AqC6aG6CByNd-CzdRgaI/edit?usp=sharing

**TECHNICAL STRATEGY**

We do not have the capacity for managers to see all of their CHW’s patients and documents (setting aside current unsupported/experimental workflows), without some kind of 100x performance improvements. The goal of this MVP is to provide a way for supervisors to view CHW performance data without requiring all of the patient reports offline. We hope to enable supervisors to have much smaller data sets and still accomplish what they need to do.

A clearly helpful thing is exposing CHW’s tasks and targets to their supervisors. This gives supervisors insight into what the CHW is doing, needs to do and has done, without requiring that they can see all of the patients and their documents. This MVP focuses on targets first - investigating how we can periodically write a CHW's targets into a document that can be synchronized to the supervisor's device.

Note to QA team: we should proactively test with high-volume instances.


**DESIGN OVERVIEW**

Note: All of the following require supervisor access/visibility to CHW targets in order to work.

**Support new performance condition card on CHW profile**
- Should be just adding another card type to the contact summary
- The data is based directly on CHW targets and is subject to the same limitations as the widgets/calculations on Targets
- The time period of the data will match what we already have, meaning we will only support data from the most recent month/time period
- As usual, the exact metrics displayed on the card and the total number of metrics displayed will be configurable per partner/project

**Ability to display targets last updated date on performance card**
- The “Date targets last updated” gives crucial context as it is the date when the performance data was last updated (i.e. “This information was true as of this date”)
- The targets "report" gets generated every 24 hours regardless of whether there is a new action by the CHW
- Should be styled just like any other condition card field and should appear first in the condition card

**Support display of aggregate targets widgets**
- Display aggregate performance metrics across all of a supervisor’s CHWs
- Calculating averages may need to be a new widget type??
- Some values may be totals, while others may be averages (total / # of values)
- Should support aggregate values on both count widgets and percentage widgets (depends on what gets recorded in the CHW report)
- Should also support goals - if the group of CHWs is performing on average below the goal, the value will be highlighted in red. If the group of CHWs is performing on average above the goal, the value will be highlighted in green. 
- If there is no goal, the value should be the default black
- Stefan says: Targets page is just like it is now, but unlike CHWs where targets are based on reports completed, Supervisor targets are based on CHW target documents. Should fit the current way targets get calculated (ie nools)
- Marc says: Seems like we need to store numerator and denominator so that we can calculate totals. We also need a way to add numbers to the target, as opposed as counting every target instance as a 1.

![screen shot 2018-09-19 at 12 43 09 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/45777081-a09a6280-bc09-11e8-88fc-dcd2a229f632.png)

title: Make targets widgets clickable and support target detail pages for supervisors
body:
[Product initiative detail](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1EQHQI11XqI8aQeUsnmlrD3ny83fj5N6MZATrLzsm_-I/edit#heading=h.q31g948sivit)

Read more details and view additional screenshots in the MVP deck: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1AbOxkGgggUoI0QzRmwVqfX0AqC6aG6CByNd-CzdRgaI/edit?usp=sharing

This new feature builds off of changes made in ticket #4839. The detail pages are considered a nice-to-have but not essential for the Supervisor MVP. Depends on further technical investigation and level of effort.

**New feature: targets detail pages**
- Aggregate widgets are now clickable
- Clicking on a widget takes you to a new detail page view of that widget with a breakdown of data by individual CHW
- The title of the detail page should match the title of the widget
- CHW names on the left are hyperlinked to a CHW’s profile
- The individual performance of each CHW is displayed on the right (could be a count or a percentage)
- The individual performance values are right-aligned 
- If the data is a percentage, we should also display the counts in parenthesis e.g. “90% (9 of 10)” 
- The list should be automatically sorted from lowest to highest performing and/or lowest to highest value. Lowest performing at the top.
- If a particular widget has a goal, it would be nice to support conditional styling based upon goals: If a certain CHW is performing below the goal, their value should be highlighted in red. If a CHW is performing above the goal, their value should be green.

Note from @SCdF : I think this is just visual: we should be able to make a new URL target that has the target in it and then displays all families by target, and ideally ordering is guessable based on the target type.

Any change to report filters are ignored while reports are being fetched. title: Make webapp header logo image configurable
body:
**Summary**
Our current logo will still be the default on the webapp. The feature we are working on now will allow partners to swap in their own logo/image in place of our logo, should they so desire. We will share some basic guidelines for making the best use of the space and formatting files correctly but we will not actively restrict/police/enforce how the space ends up being used.

Read more and see examples here: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1qv8WkVIDaNNPUntFoB6EnBpkfhXi1Ax61zXVZ8LGjAo/edit?usp=sharing

**Webapp header image**
- In essence, we are creating a blank container box in the upper left corner of our webapp that is configurable - meaning partners can upload their own custom image in place of the default Medic Mobile logo
- The size of the container box in the upper left of the desktop webapp should be 170 x 50 px. This is my recommendation based upon the overall size of the header bar now, the size of the bar after the nav update, the general horizontal shape of most logos, and the needs of responsive page scaling
- The box should be vertically centered within the black header bar
- The far left edge of the box should stay aligned directly on top of the far left edge of the LHS column as the page scales (just as our current Medic logo does)

![blank box](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/45906389-c742cf80-bda8-11e8-9493-b518a081ea16.png)


**File upload**
- Where should this custom image be uploaded from? Assuming it should ideally be a place that all admin users have access to (i.e. the admin console). That way, if a partner decides down the road that they want to swap out the image with something else, they don’t need to come back to Medic in order to make the change.
- My initial suggestion is this: We rename the “Icons” page to “Images” and then we add “Header logo” and “About page logo” sections or tabs
- Next to the “Choose file” button for image upload, it would be nice if we could display a few sentences with reminder text such as “You can upload an SVG, PNG, or JPG file. File must be less than 100 KB… etc” 
- Unsure how easy or hard it is to restrict the types of files being uploaded, but ideally we would restrict the image types allowed and if a user tries to upload an unsupported image type, we should display a warning message indicating such.
- It would also be nice to set some sort of reasonable cap on the file size. Then, if the user tries to upload a very large image (say 10 MB) we can display a warning message indicating that the file is too large.
- We aren’t going to worry too much about whether or not the image matches the recommended dimensions or ratios. Whatever is uploaded, the image should always scale to fit inside whatever bounding container we’ve coded
- If an image is uploaded that does not match the end ratio or is larger than the recommended dimensions, it should automatically be scaled down, keeping proportions intact, to fit within the available space.

title: Allow sentinel transitions to run synchronously against incoming SMS messages
body:
Currently the flow for an SMS with a default response is slower than it could be:
 - CHW sends an SMS to the gateway, which takes it and puts it in it's queue
 - Gateway wakes up every minute and sends the SMS to Medic, gets any existing SMS to send back and closes the connection
 - Sentinel asynchronously updates the SMS report to add a default response
 - 1 minute later Gateway talks to Medic, finds this response and sends it out.

We should look into extracting sentinel into a shared lib that we can run in realtime when receiving new SMS. This means we will any resulting SMS as part of the same request.

Combined with #4858 this could greatly increase the responsiveness of SMS.

title: 4680 - Translate startup messages for non-English speakers
body:
# Description

People who do not have English as their primary language find our startup messages ("Loading assets", "Fetching Info (100 docs)..." etc) very confusing.

medic/medic-webapp#4680

# Comments

Since this translator isn't really a "best practice", I've done my best to encapsulate all required translations into `bootstrapper.js`. Previously, there was logic for updating the startup status in app.js and in controllers/inbox.js (inside Angular).

Message | Current | Proposed
-- | -- | --
Loading assets... | Appears at DOM load | Can't have translated strings prior to assets loading. For now, I just have a spinner with no text. Unsure what to do here?
Loading app… | Appears if/when replication begins | Unchanged
Starting app…| Appears after replication completes and before "Loading Rules" begins | I removed this, since it appears for just a few milliseconds and only when replication is required.
Fetching info (100 docs)… | Updates as initial replication progresses | Unchanged
Loading rules... | Appears mid-way through inbox angular module initialisation. | Appears after successful sync or when sync is not required. We may consider changing this to "Initializing..." since it now captures the whole application initialisation instead of just the rules.
Loading error, please check your connection. Try again | On bootstrapper error | Unchanged but `bootstrapper.js` handles it instead of `app.js`

I have also looked briefly into progress bars - approximating the entire startup progress, or doing one  just for replication. I'd be interested to look into improvements we can make to shorten start-up times if that feels like a priority. For that, it would be very helpful to have access to live or realist simulated long startup times.

title: Adds muting transition
body:
# Description

Adds muting transition that:
- allows muting on any level in the hierarchy 
- all descendants of a muted contact will also be muted
- a muted contact is marked by a `muted = true` flag. The muted flag is present in the target of the mute action and all their descendants
- muting a contact will change the state of all (own and descendants) schedules that are `scheduled` or `pending` to `muted` 
- new schedules for muted contacts will automatically have `muted` state
- unmuting a contact will unmute the target and all it's descendants
- unmuting a contact will change the state of all (own and descendants) schedules that are `muted` to `scheduled`
- all new contacts that have a muted parent will automatically receive the muted flag and have their schedules muted

Deprecates `update_notifications` transition in favor of muting.
Updates `lineage` shared library to hydrate patient by `uuid` as well, not just by `patient_id`.

Webapp:
- muted contacts appear grayed out in the LHS (styled same as deceased)
- profile pages of muted contacts have grayed out icons and the `"Muted"` text displayed under the name
- muted contacts in profile pages lists appear grayed out only if their parent is not muted
- a popup informing that the contact is muted appears when clicking to add an action (that is not an unmute form) from the profile page of a muted contact. If the user "agrees", they are redirected to the form, otherwise the popup closes and they remain on the profile page. 
- When submitting forms from the reports tab, the contact dropdowns mark the muted contacts with `"Muted"` text.

title: Schedules are not cleared for offline contacts/reports
body:
When working offline, a report submitted about a person that is not yet replicated will never be bound to that person by `patient_id` field.
As a consequence, this report will never be considered a `registration` and it's schedule will not be cleared by any clearing mechanism. 

**Steps to reproduce**:
 - Login with an offline user (on `gamma.dev` for example)
 - Go offline
 - Create a new person
 - Submit a pregnancy for this person
 - Go online and allow replication to happen
 - Create a new pregnancy for the same user

**What should happen**:
 - Scheduled tasks from the first report should be `cleared`

**What actually happens**:
 - Scheduled tasks from the first report are `scheduled`

I think we should expand our searching for registrations by checking for the `patient_uuid` field as well. 
I am not aware of what value `medic-client/registered_patients` provides now versus say `medic-client/reports_by_subject` (which indexes by `patient_id`, `patient_uuid` and `place_id`). 
Is there any situation where we'd want to _only_ obtain sms/online reports? If not, maybe we could retire `registered_patients` entirely.

title: 3391 audit layer
body:
# Description

Removes the audit layer to stop logging/tracking data into the audit db.
Introduces request headers X-Medic-Service and X-Medic-User to be captured
by an haproxy that controls access to couchdb.
The user is identified and logged in haproxy by:
1. the cookie header when available (api's userCtx.name) 
2. the X-Medic-User header that is now included for the common dbpouch put/post/delete.

We do not always capture the user for those cases that include queries, views
and other bulk operations. But we might be able to capture the session (cookie auth session) 
for a more detailed audit.

Also, the audit layer had logic to setup unique ids when saving new documents. 
This pr uses dbpouch.post to save new documents that require a new id 
and dbpouch.put for documents that already have an id.

The initial logs have been formatted as CSVs but we should be able to configure
them in any format. Initial csv format:
| client ip | http status | http method |  uri | service | user | req body | bytes read | response time | response header Content-Length |

We have all these logging options (end of the page table):
[haproxy configuration](https://cbonte.github.io/haproxy-dconv/1.8/configuration.html)

title: Horticulturalist crashes when view warming
body:
When doing view warming, we assume that CouchDB view queries will timeout. We intend to catch these errors and retry the queries (successful queries signify that the view is warmed). 
Timeout errors are no longer marked with a `ESOCKETTIMEDOUT` code since the upgrade to PouchDB 7, result being that horti crashes when when the timeouts occur.

body:
https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/issues/4875 introduces a patch at https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/master/webapp/patches/enketo-inputs-always-relevant.patch to make sure that the `<inputs>` group in form submissions is always considered as `relevant`.

This approach is functional, but has problems:
* it's poorly documented
* it's liable to break when bumping the version of the `enketo-core` dependency

There may be a documented, supported way of achieving the same end.  If this exists, we should use it.  If it doesn't exist, we should explore how this might be better supported in enketo.  One option might be to embed the `<inputs>` group within the [`<meta>`](https://opendatakit.github.io/xforms-spec/#metadata) group.

If an online user were to log in to a large instance their browser would be overwhelmed by a constant stream of doc updates and the app would not be useable.

Consider disabling watching changes feeds for online users and require them to refresh or navigate to get updates. Alternatively we may get away with adding a dirty flag to the UI to notify users of new changes.

body: On a place profile, there is a header that describes the list of people in that place. For health systems where the lowest grouping in hierarchy is a family, this header is often "Family Members." However, it seems that this is the same for upper levels in the hierarchy as well. Of course, we can genericize this label such that it would be "People" but it's more ideal to be able to customize this label per hierarchy label.

title: CouchDB 2 performance issue
body:
In testing the performance of 3.0.0 on the new infrastructure including CouchDB 2 I found the initial changes feed request (from seq 0) was taking almost 40 minutes to complete. After playing around with code for a while I found the problem was the request splitting code that was introduced in CouchDB 1 to improve performance. Removing this reduced the query time to 2.5 minutes.

Now that we only support CouchDB 2+ we can remove this performance tweak.

body:
Unless we're listening for the `complete` event, we have no need for the `changes()` call to collect docs.  We changed this in webapp at d4beeaf78b, but not in other parts of the app.

title: Bump autoprefixer browser support
body:
We use autoprefixer to add browser compatibility prefixes to css rules. We configure it in our Gruntfile to support `browsers: ['last 2 versions', 'Android >= 4.4'],` but now we're not supporting Chrome 30 we can bump this to be in line with our [supported browsers](https://github.com/medic/medic-docs/blob/master/installation/supported-software.md).

Compatibility prefixes have gone out of fashion recently as they lead to people writing browser specific css code so it's likely that once we bump the autoprefixer configuration it doesn't actually do anything. Check if any changes are actually made and if not remove the plugin altogether.

In discussion today with @billwambua about #medic-projects/5352, we talked through the process that he goes through when investigating a crash or performance issue in the field. 

The minified crash stacks severely limit the value of the information available from field reports.

```
Exception at blah blah blah
(anonymous) @ inbox.js:3
(anonymous) @ inbox.js:3
c @ inbox.js:3
d @ inbox.js:3
a @ inbox.js:3
(anonymous) @ inbox.js:3
(anonymous) @ inbox.js:3
(anonymous) @ inbox.js:3
...
```

If the app's "debug mode" (or similar state to support investigations) allowed for un-minified script,  field personnel would be able to collect:

* more useful crash reports
* on-device performance profiles

title: Improve performance of loading Contacts in UHC mode
body:
UHC contacts lists relies heavily on quering views with `keys` parameter, which has a proven track record of slowness (because PouchDB would query the view database for each key separately).
Adding to the fact that for sorting by last visited date, `Search` service must intersect two whole views (`contacts_by_last_visited` and `contacts_by_type`), loading the contacts list for medium-large DBs on low end phones is incredibly slow.

Some benchmarks (results in seconds):

| UHC + visit sorting | Desktop | Nexus 5X | Tecno Y4 |  
| ---- | :----: | :----: | :----: |
| Load 50 contacts  | 1.2 | 8 | 75 |
| Load 50 contacts after home_visit form submission | 2.4 | 20 | 110 |
| Load 150 contacts after home_visit form submission | 4.5 | 30 | 195 |
| Load 150 contacts after contact edit | 3.9 | 26 | 178 |

| UHC + alpha sorting | Desktop | Nexus 5X | Tecno Y4 |  
| ---- | :----: | :----: | :----: |
| Load 50 contacts | 1 | 3.9 | 43 |
| Load 50 contacts after home_visit form submission | 1.6 | 6.9 | 56 |
| Load 150 contacts after home_visit form submission | 3.2 | 22 | 130 |
| Load 150 contacts after contact edit | 2.9 | 20 | 144 |

*All benchmarks performed using code from `master` against a local deployment, using data replicated from `muso-mali.app` restricted user (150 families, 600 persons, 4600 reports).*

title: [wip] [2.18.x] incremental UI loading for contacts
body:
Issue: #4445

### TODO

- [x] compare time-to-render a contact old code vs new code
- [x] fix tests
- [ ] fix report passing for contact-summary (thanks @dianabarsan; confirmed)
- [ ] port to `master` if required (contact-view-model-generator looks the same as 2.18.x, so it's probably applicable)


## Timed Tests

I ran through loading a specific content (AA) for a specific user (a) using a real data set (m-in.dev) on Samsung J1 mini play using the latest dev build of `medic-android`.  PouchDB debug was enabled, the phone was connected to my desktop, and Chrome Developer Tools were open.  Database view building was complete.  I tested first with the new code, and then the old code.  The phone's database was not reset between tests - the app was updated via a ddoc change.  Times are in seconds.

### Old Code

Commit tested: 91295914e10f3490c87b0d457135a73f8aedfe32

With the "old" (`2.18.1`) implementation, there is only one time measured, as the whole of the contact-content view renders in one moment.

Times to render: **22.71, 20.06, 20.92, 18.85, 21.36, 23.45, 18.92, 18.06, 19.33, 21.53**

Average time to render: **20.52s**

### New Code

Commit tested: 526e34ff0760382b825ba2c986c4d6673974c10c

The new code loads parts of the UI at different times, but the order of loading is predictable.  I timed each of these stages separately, the timings representing the _time after the previous element loaded_.  These are presented in loading order in the table below.

With the new code I tested both with the server online and offline.  There didn't seem to be a significant difference in the timings.

The "top-row render" is for the detail that appears below the contact's name.  On my desktop there is noticeable delay before this is rendered, but on the phone there is not.  This PR adds a loading spinner for that 

Online? | First render | Top row render | Children render | Reports Render | Total time
-- | -- | -- | -- | -- | --
no | 1.93 | 0.76 | 3.6 | 11.9 | **18.19**
no | 2.02 | 0.4 | 3.49 | 11.89 | **17.8**
no | 1.99 | 0.15 | 3.83 | 12.24 | **18.21**
yes | 2 | 0.29 | 3.97 | 11.2 | **17.46**
yes | 2.26 | 0.13 | 3.96 | 14.62 | **20.97**
yes | 1.99 | 0.14 | 4.33 | 12.7 | **19.16**

Average time to render: **18.63s**


## Conclusion

The new code appears marginally faster to render the complete page.  However, there is **significant** improvement in getting useful data and a usable interface to the user as quickly as possible.

title: #4445 - Cache UserSettings() lookup of org.couchdb.user
body:
# Description
The contact's tab fetches the org.couchdb.user document three times just to render. Although it isn't a particularly expensive operation, it is done frequently. Since this document has very low churn, it should be safe to cache it in UserSettings() in a similar style to Settings().

medic/medic-webapp#4445 (Suggestion 8)

In this change, I'm also caching the userCtx cookie in Session. I'm assuming this is low-risk since the cookie is symantically immutable. I did not attempt to measure the impact. I'm doing this because this is another very hot codepath and the `ipCookie('userCtx')` function does the following:

1. Split the document.cookie string by `;`
1. Split each cookie within based on `=`
1. JSON.parse each cookie in a try{}

# Impact
I timed how long the fetch for `org.couchdb.user` took while loading pages and while idle on my SM-G361H. An average range was between ~8-15ms when idle and ~80-130ms while the contacts page was loading.  This is not a large savings by any means (3x savings for contacts page), but this is a frequent fetch across many user-actions and experiences.

Navigating directly to `http://upstream:5988/muso/_design/medic/_rewrite/#/contacts` loads the org.couchdb.user 7 times (4 for any pageload + 3 for contacts page).

title: [WIP] Lazy loading content in the contact's left panel
body:
# Description

This change paints the "Contacts Panel" (left panel on the contact's tab) in two steps.  This results in increased perceived performance and can reduce the user's time to complete tasks. The user can interact with the page faster, while still getting the rich experiences which require longer load times.  

#4445

**The Downside** - This change requires the user to paint twice. Painting with Live-List is a costly operation, so the total time to the richer experience is regressed by this change (particularly when displayLastVisitedDates is false).  I'd say this is concerning and makes this a questionable win, particularly with #4998 in the pipe. We may want to consider performance optimizations to Live-List before considering this. 

The first paint triggers as soon as the contacts are fetched with no meta data (last visited date, primary contact, etc.). The second paint updates the existing page with the meta data after it is fetched.  

Related Changes - This can compliment both #4982 and #4998. Though #4998 reduces the time to fetch metadata and therefore reduces the upside of this change. 

An Edge Case - When the user selects to "sort by last visited," the content re-sorts on the second paint. This shuffle is likely confusing for users. Therefore, this lazy-loading experience is disabled when sorting by last visited date. 

The changes in GetDataSource and Search should scale to lazy loading content elsewhere (contacts-content panel, reports page, etc.) 

## Results 
All times in milliseconds.  
Times in format `x/y` - The `x` is time to first paint. The `y` is time to second paint.

title: Adds muting history
body:
# Description

For analytics purposes, a contact's `muting_history` log is saved in the sentinel info doc. Each time the muted status is changed, an entry is added in the `muting_history` log, following this format: 
```
{ 
  muted: [true|false],
  date: '<muting/unmuting sentinel date, in ISO8601 format>',
  report_id: '<report that triggered muting/unmuting>'
}
```

For analytics purposes, the contact's `muted` property now contains a human readable date (in ISO8601 format). When unmuting, the property is removed altogether, avoiding having mixed data types for the same property. 

The `muted` field value (when existent) is exposed to ContactViewModel, instead of a Boolean `true`. 

medic/medic-webapp#4767

title: #4445 - Reduce time to render contacts list through live-list
body:
# Description

#4445

Performance optimizations for the Live-List class as-used in the contacts tab. 

Contact controller currently calls `livelist.update` once per list item and then `livelist.refresh` after all items are added. 

This change updates the interface `livelist.set` to avoid the incremental dom changes from `livelist.update` and then the full re-paint from `livelist.refresh`. The proposed change inserts the items each item into the model once, sorts the full list once, and then draws everything once. To avoid unnecessary scanning, update `livelist.dom` to a hashmap. `livelist.set()` accepts an optional flag `reuseExistingDom` which can avoid expensive calls to `listItemFor` when the contents of the DOM are being reused and not updated (eg. pagination). 

## Measurements
On my SM-G361H. Times are a measure of milliseconds spent in `live-list.js` functions.

Five samples of the time spent in Live-List drawing a full LHS contact list (40 contacts).

Sample | Proposed | Master
-- | -- | --
1 | 391 | 546
2 | 304 | 660
3 | 261 | 856
4 | 277 | 499
5 | 387 | 800
Mean | 324 | 660

Two hundred contacts, displayed over four paginated pages. Table shows the time to render each page in the LHS contact list while paginating.

Page | Proposed | Master
-- | -- | --
1 | 519 | 725
2 | 419 | 738
3 | 464 | 876
4 | 311 | 671
Mean | 428 | 752

## Testing
I'm testing the following scenarios:

* Create a new user as admin. Syncs to offline user's live-list. 
* Delete the user as admin. Syncs to offline user's live-list.
* Edit user as admin. Syncs to offline user's live-list.
* Edit user twice as offline user. Edits appear in live-list, no pagination.
* Proper pagination.
* Edit the home place as admin (doesn't update in offline user's live-list) 
* Paginate to nth page, then edit an element within that page.
* Search
* Update the name of a primary contact for clinic

Fix favicon caching
body:
With recent changes to how we serve the favicon we have broken the caching implemented to fix #1913 and #3858 .

The [favicon test code](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/master/api/src/routing.js#L533) can be removed and move this line up to the [favicon route handler](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/master/api/src/routing.js#L156):

```js
writeHeaders(req, res, [['Cache-Control', 'public, max-age=604800']]);
```

To test this
- load the login page in an incognito browser you should see a network request for `favicon.ico` - make sure it has this header
- then load the login page in a regular browser and refresh the page and ensure you only see the request being made the first time
- then log in to the app and ensure the favicon isn't loaded again - the icon URL should now be the same for the login page, webapp, and admin app so it should only be requested once

title: Implement a custom pouch purge solution
body:
Our users have a lot of documents on their phones. This is causing reduced with query performance, and eventually phones will run out of space altogether.

To solve this allow projects to provide configuration which defines when a document can be deleted off the phone. The document must not be deleted from the server couchdb so analytics and administrators can still access all documents. To achieve this run a service on the phone that purges a doc and modify the db-sync filter function so purged docs aren't replicated to the server.

Based on some [performance profiling](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Y4ISvnunnYtm6Odxf2j4XloFI5vojt4hlBiB2_SHvvA/edit) we decided to implement purge using the [pouchdb remove function](https://pouchdb.com/api.html#delete_document). However it may be that removed docs no longer have enough information to be filtered out. If that's the case, implement purge by minifying the doc, eg: `{ _id: doc._id, _rev: doc._rev, _deleted: true, purged: true }`.

title: Memory leak when switching between tabs
body:
This is a script which switches between the messages and contacts tab every 5 seconds.

```JavaScript
setInterval(() => $('#messages-tab').click(), 5000);
setTimeout(() => setInterval(() => $('#contacts-tab').click(), 5000), 2000);
```

I did the following:

1. Load WebApp
1. Navigate to all tabs to ensure view warming.
1. Trigger GC
1. Measure Heap size and DOM Node Count.
1. Start the script
1. Wait some duration
1. Trigger GC
1. Measure Heap size and DOM Node Count.

Results after waiting 10 minutes:

Metric | Before | After
-- | -- | --
Heap | 163MB | 195 MB
DOM Nodes | 17,000 | 410,000

A second run for 5 minute without live-list drawing in contacts tab:

Metric | Before | After
-- | -- | --
Heap | 126MB | 327MB
DOM Nodes | 17,000 | 200,000

Measures imply some sort of resource leak. This was on Chrome 70, so could be bogus. Worth investigating further.

title: Loading Targets tab as admin logs an Error
body:
**Steps to reproduce**:
 - Log in as admin
 - Click on Targets tab

**What should happen**:
 - The message "Analytics are disabled for admin users. If you need to see analytics, login as a normal user." is shown on screen.
- No errors in the console.

**What actually happens**:
 - The message "Analytics are disabled for admin users. If you need to see analytics, login as a normal user." is shown on screen.
- An error in the console.

URL: /medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/#/analytics/targets

```
Error fetching targets SyntaxError: "JSON.parse: unexpected character at line 1 column 1 of the JSON data"
	targets http://localhost:5988/medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/js/inbox.js:193672:27
	init http://localhost:5988/medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/js/inbox.js:193666:14
	processQueue http://localhost:5988/medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/js/inbox.js:44052:37
	scheduleProcessQueue http://localhost:5988/medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/js/inbox.js:44100:27
	digest http://localhost:5988/medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/js/inbox.js:45213:15
	evalAsync http://localhost:5988/medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/js/inbox.js:45533:15
	completeTask http://localhost:5988/medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/js/inbox.js:47332:7
	timeoutId http://localhost:5988/medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/js/inbox.js:32928:7
 inbox.js:41674:16
```

The line corresponds to the `JSON.stringify` [call in the TargetGenerator service](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/master/webapp/src/js/services/target-generator.js#L96).

**Environment**:

- Instance: localhost
- Browser: Firefox
- Client platform: Ubuntu
- App: webapp
- Version: master (3.4.0)

**Solution**

The problem is when you're admin you don't have a `userContact` so it's trying to stringify `null` which throws so we should wrap that in an if block.

For extra performance consider skipping the `TargetGenerator.init` altogether if the RulesEngine is disabled because it's never going to get any targets emitted.

title: PouchDB replication _bulk_get is no longer batched
body:
Since the upgrade to PouchDB 7.0.0 (in 3.1.0), Webapp _bulk_get replication calls are no longer batched.
The specific update that causes this is [this commit](https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/commit/2987c56311ae2d170d7c1d856470894f760a819a#diff-39bf4acf1588841b5eb6168b8bd48e0d), which changes the moment the `onChange` event is emitted (instead of a sequential emit, which allowed the replicator to batch, events for all changes are emitted at once and processing happens on `nextTick`). 

This causes replication to consist of one `_changes` request which, as before, will return all changes (since the beginning of time for initial replication), regardless of the limit PouchDB sets, one `_all_docs` request for changed docs that are on first rev and one `_bulk_get` request for all the other changes. 

This means a potential `_bulk_get` to get thousands of docs. 
@garethbowen do you think this could be a problem?

title: Client-side Purging
body:
For your consideration.

I spent a couple of hours today knocking out the basics of purge on the phone:
 - Runs every N days on refresh (in my hard-coded configuration I have it at 0 so it runs on every refresh)
 - Runs over all reports for all contacts and executes the configured function
 - Converts the result (guarding against bad ids) into minimally deleted files and writes them into PouchDB
 - Doesn't sync those deletes upwards
 - ~Initiates a compaction if anything was purged~ Does nothing because we auto-compact

I have tested it and it seems to nominally work.

Still to do:
 - Write tests!
 - Actually pull config from config
 - Document that config's existence, write a TL / CHT guide on how to use the feature
 - Performance test to make sure running like this on startup doesn't destroy a typically full phone in an obviously bad way. If it does, consider pausing between sets for n seconds to reduce constant cpu usage
 - Consider exposing this on the about page so users can manually run purge.
 - Consider putting this behind a "persisted queue", so if a user gets halfway through and refreshes we pick up where we left off.
 - Consider view warming. Doesn't really seem worth it on PouchDB, idk. Which would you pick etc.

More notes:
 - If at some point we want purge rules to only apply to certain people we could allow for the function to return a map of id to role, e.g. `['id1', 'id2']` -> `{id1: true, id2: ['role1', 'role2']}`
 - If we decide that we don't want to ship without it running on the server, while it was good practice for thinking about the problem and not much time investment I'd probably have to throw the vast majority of it away.

Interested in your thoughts.

medic/medic-webapp#5048

title: PouchDB replication _bulk_get requests no longer batched
body:
Since the upgrade to PouchDB `7.0.0` (in 3.1.0), replication `_bulk_get` requests are no longer batched (in standard PouchDB 100 docs limit). 
This is caused by [this commit](https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/commit/2987c56311ae2d170d7c1d856470894f760a819a), which changes the moment `onChange` events are emitted.
Instead of being emitted sequentially, thus allowing the replicator to split the changes into batches, all `onChange` events are emitted at once and their processing delayed until `nextTick`. 
Together with the fact that our filtered replication ignores PouchDB limit of 100 changes per request, means that, for initial replication at least, there will be a single `_bulk_get` request to get all docs (potentially thousands). 

Do you think this could be a problem, @garethbowen? I'm afraid of timeouts specifically.

title: CouchDB 2.3.0 has reduced the allowed length of GET requests
body:
When making a view request PouchDB switches to use a POST if the URL with parameters exceeds [2000 characters](https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/blob/fb2ab0afe57a51da574ee3fac0bf1bd59fdbe502/packages/node_modules/pouchdb-abstract-mapreduce/src/index.js#L262). Against CouchDB 2.2.0 GET requests this long work as expected, but in CouchDB 2.3.0 they fail at around 1370 characters.

1. Raise an issue with CouchDB to change the limit back or at least document the change.
2. Raise an issue with PouchDB to change their limit - ideally submit a PR.
3. Patch our PouchDB in webapp, api, and sentinel to have a lower limit to be removed once it's fixed properly either by Couch or Pouch.

Thanks @dianabarsan for finding this!

Loading the primary contact slows down loading of the list and we don't feel like it adds any value. Remove this line to improve performance.

This is "Option 1a: No primary contact ever" in the [design slide deck](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1TThN7MkhEB12np2x3o7evJRz0Gqb3E69Zll68pb8X-I/edit#slide=id.g4860a84287_0_413).

> We don't feel the primary contact information adds value for any specific user group. Our vote was for option 1a "No Primary Contacts Ever"
> If/when it comes to pass that areas are not named after the CHW, then this data may be re-introduced at a later date for managers as necessary.

title: Lazy loading visit information on the contacts LHS
body:
In UHC mode, render the contacts list on the LHS with a spinner waiting for the last visited and visit count information to be rendered. Leave enough white space that this information will render without moving any elements around.

![loading mock up](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2064938/49708894-81562300-fc96-11e8-8967-2ecfc429bb1a.PNG)

If the user filters or sorts by the last visited information then multiple stage render will be chaotic - render everything in one stage for these cases.

title: Lazy loading contact RHS sections
body:
Don't block rendering the page waiting for all the content, instead each section will load with a spinner with the content being rendered when ready. 

The shifting of content within the page from spinners is concerning, but we discussed two mitigations which can be investigated:

1. when the UI shifts, attempt to adjust the scroll position to minimize the disturbance, or if that isn't possible.
2. ignore any user touch for 1 second after shifting of content above the current scroll position.

Information in the contact summary which requires reports to be loaded should be moved into condition cards.

This is "Option 2c: Loading spinners" from [this design deck](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1TThN7MkhEB12np2x3o7evJRz0Gqb3E69Zll68pb8X-I/edit#slide=id.g498531a5d1_0_424).

Split off from #4445

title: 5082 - Make content-security-policy more strict
body:
# Description

I believe this is our most tightly constrained CSP without breaking anything. It requires a few "unsafe" configurations:

1. `imgSrc: data:` - "developers SHOULD NOT include either 'unsafe-inline', or data: as valid sources in their policies. Both enable XSS attacks by allowing code to be included directly in the document itself; they are best avoided completely." https://www.w3.org/TR/CSP3/#csp-directives
1. `scriptSrc: unsafe-eval` - We use `eval()` about 88 times and use `new Function()` about 17 times in inbox.js. "AngularJS makes use of this in the $parse service to provide a 30% increase in the speed of evaluating AngularJS expressions." https://docs.angularjs.org/api/ng/directive/ngCsp
1. `styleSrc: unsafe-inline` - Our dependency, `angular-ui-bootstrap` injects about 8 inline style blocks. Here is an example issue where they fix one of them https://github.com/angular-ui/bootstrap/issues/5470. The risks from unsafe css are reduced by fully constraining imgSrc (not done here) and by avoiding unsafe-eval (not done here).

#5082 

## Questions for Reviewer

1. I'm explicitly allowing the inline script for telemetry `window.startupTimes` - through a whitelisted hash. Another option would be to move that script into its own file and appcache it. As-is, if the content of this script ever changes, the corresponding hash will need to be updated. If we keep it as a hash, I'm unsure of the best method to keep the hash and script in sync (new test, calculate the hash in api, just pray, etc.). 
1. We may want to whitelist a hash for each of the eight style blocks from angular-ui-bootstrap instead of using`unsafe-inline` - I didn't do it because I'm not sure they are always the same for all browsers but they probably are and can follow-up if we close on that direction.

## Additional considerations

This change also makes the header larger. Including it on all resources (js, css, application/json, etc.) isn't required so one minor performance tweak we might consider here is setting it for `Accept: html` requests only. 

CSP also supports `report-uri` which can alert us when the security policy is violated (due to bugs or successful attacks). Might be worth opening an issue to enable this down the road.

## Testing

I went through some basic workflows in webapp + tried each actions in admin pages. In general though, this has risks of breaking edge-case functionalities or workflows I don't know about. Best to AT across all browsers as there are apparently some differences.

# Review checklist

title: Improve SQL testing and deployment flow
body:
_NB: this work would be primarily be in the `medic-conf` repository, and split into many tickets. This ticket can be seen as a facilitator of discussion / coordination._

Currently SQL (used for impact as well as analytics) is not managed in any way, apart from being (by convention) stored in the project directory:
 - People often write SQL directly into postgres, meaning it is hard / impossible to either recreate production instances if required, or reason about what is in production already
 - One person's SQL can often cause a drop to occur or otherwise cause breakages in someone else's
 - There is no convention on how to deal with common SQL between multiple projects, even though this occurs frequently, meaning there is a lot of copy / pasting, as well as _slightly_ differing conventions / naming
 - There is no form of automated testing for SQL, increasing the fragility of the scripts in general
 - Tooling for other forms of application configuration but not for SQL is weird, in light of the CHT

@sarahollis, @michaelkohn and I are proposing that to solve these problems, SQL should be treated in `medic-conf` with a similar featureset that config / rules have.

## Step 1: SQL medic-conf deployment flow

`medic-conf` should support (and be the supported / correct way) to push SQL to production or testing instances, as it is for other forms of config. This would mean:
 - Formalising a directory structure that SQL should be in per project
 - Defining an execution order for different scripts (eg alphanumeric, or require that they start with a number)
 - Declaring a way to import scripts from other projects (eg if you're based on standard you want to start with standard's SQL scripts), which could be (in order, IMO of simplest+best to complex+worst):
    - Allowing for one super project whose SQL always runs first
    - Allowing many super projects whose SQL always runs first, in some declared order
    - Allowing for arbitrary "calls" to other projects to have their SQL run at some point (i.e. it could run between two of your scripts)
    - As above, but for specific scripts from other projects 
 - Adding a push command to medic-conf, as well as perhaps allowing for some kind of config around which server / db etc the SQL should be pushed to.

## Step 1b: Use the above to fix `medic-couch2pg` bootstrap scripts

Once there are offical import flows we can drop the hard-coded bootstrap scripts (which are now also very wrong, and are worked around with manual bootstrap scripts that run after these ones) from `medic-couch2pg` and instead have the bootstrap scripts checked into medic-projects.

## Step 2: Testing

`medic-conf` should suppoort testing SQL, locally and in travis, in the same way it does for nools etc.

These tests should be with the SQL, including with higher level SQL that others import, and should be run against the entire project. e.g.,
 - User runs `medic-conf test-sql --local` or whatever, to run the SQL tests against a local postgres they have somehow configured
 - The rules declared in step 1 are used to "compile" both an ordered list of all SQL files that need to be run against this DB, as well as all test cases
 - Any existing tests DBs are deleted
 - For each test
   - A new DB is created based on the test name as a suffix
   - All production SQL is run to completion. If it fails, the entire test suite is halted here (this would only happen on the first one presumably)
   - The test is run against that DB. If it fails, the single test fails
 - And all of this is printed out to the user

The important point here is that *all* SQL is run before *any* test runs, and *all* tests that are related to the SQL are run. We want a bootstrap SQL test to run against your projects complete production SQL.

In terms of what a test consists of, probably the simplest thing to start with is, for each test:
 - a json file containing the CouchDB documents to insert into the DB before running the test
 - One or more SQL files that contain a single query
 - One of more CSV files that should match the output of the query

An example of a directory structure might be:

```
postgres/
  tests/
    001-test-foo/
      data.json
      001-it-does-foo.sql
      001-it-does-foo.csv
      002-it-does-bar.sql
      002-it-does-bar.csv
```

Where `001-test-foo` is the equivilent of a `describe` in normal test parlance, and each sql / csv pair is an `it`.

title: Why are some users taking a long time to replicate, and how can we encourage them to replicate more?
body:
We get reports that some CHWs take weeks / months to replicate. This is determined by looking at the differences between the reported date on reports to the replication date in the corresponding info document.

Step 1: we should try to work out why some users are taking ages to replicate. Are they using the app correctly but there is a bug? Does the app work correctly but there is a misunderstanding on how to use it? Do they genuinely only have data once every 6 weeks? Do they just leave their phone off the internet for that long?

Step 2: given that information, implement fixes! If it turns out that users are intentionally not replicating for a long time due to a misunderstanding / over optimisation on their part, how can we change the UI to encourage them to replicate?

title: Only send tombstone deletes when document is still deleted
body:
If a document is deleted and then re-added (once or repeated), the deletes should not be included in the offline changes feed - even if the deleted `rev` is lower, PouchDB replication still considers the last rev it has received as winning. 

Discovered after fixing https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/issues/5078 (send form deletes to offline users). 
When updating forms, medic-conf first deletes existent forms and then uploads new ones.

title: #4713 - Replace appcache with a service worker cache
body:
# Description 
This change replaces the underlying technology which allows the webapp to load while offline. This change removes the use of the legacy appcache and adds offline support via a PWA service worker. 
#4713

# Method
## Chrome 53 Constraint 
The technical approach taken in this proposed change is guided by a non-obvious constraint of service works in Chrome 53. Prior to Chrome 66, the web requests from the service worker don't include credentials (cookies, basic auth, etc). This means all resource we wish to cache must be accessible via unauthenticated endpoints. 

## Overview of my Approach

* **Service Worker Code** - I use the [swPrecache library from Google](https://github.com/GoogleChromeLabs/sw-precache#service-worker-precache) to generate the service worker script at build time. SwPrecache has been replaced by [Workbox](https://developers.google.com/web/tools/workbox/) which is Google's latest solution for generating service workers. Details as to why I'm using the legacy technology discussed in "swPrecache vs Workbox" below.  
* **New public endpoints** - When API starts, I extract all cacheable resources from _design/medic and write them to a new directory in `api/src/extracted`. So instead of serving resources through the authenticated endpoint `/medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/js/inbox.js`, the same resource is served from the public `/js/inbox.js`. 
* **Initial service worker installation** - I updated bootstrapper to handle the synchronous install of the service worker and show an error + reload action if precaching of any resource fails. (#3568) 
* **Triggering Updates** - A service worker update should be triggered when any resource in the cache changes (if not, you have to refresh twice to get a change). Since the `service-worker.js` generated at build time contains a hash of every cached resource, watching the script itself for changes is sufficient to detect when a cache update is necessary.  I re-use "ddoc extract" pattern to trigger the updates. 
* **Updating** - When the service worker updates, only the files which have changed are downloaded. If the service worker fails to download a required file for any reason (eg. connectivity), I retry on a timer every five minutes until it is successful. Only after the service worker updates is the user prompted to refresh. 
* **Scope** - A service worker can't have a "scope" broader than its own location. So although I serve the javascript from `/js/service-worker.js`, I create an alias at `/service-worker.js` to give it broad control to handle all caching concerns. 
* **Upgrading from AppCache to Service Workers** - If you login to current master (where resources are cached via appcache) and upgrade to this change - it is important to clear the old cache before caching anew. It is not possible to clear the appcache programmatically. I set `<html manifest="empty">` which requests an empty manifest and clears the cache. 
* **Rewire** - I've added a dependency on the rewire library for mocha testing. It's awesome and we should use it! 
 
## swPrecache vs Workbox 
It is worth checking out the [Support Details for swPrecache](https://github.com/GoogleChromeLabs/sw-precache#support). TLDR: "We would recommend Workbox for new projects" but "we’ll continue to support sw-precache". 
 
Workbox looks awesome. Most notably check out [enabling offline Google Analytics](https://developers.google.com/web/tools/workbox/modules/workbox-google-analytics). So why isn't this PR using Workbox? The short answer is we probably should – but this is a big PR and Workbox is going to complicate things.  
 
Here is why I'm using the swPrecache library: 
 
1. **The community support isn't perfect for either option** - Workbox 3 supports Chrome >51, but modern [Workbox 4 only supports Chrome >56](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/workbox/releases) so really both swPrecache and latests Workbox are [both not supporting us](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bVwh8PW6r88). 
1. **Partial Precache State** - SwPrecache is pretty much exactly what we want by default: it fails to install the service worker if any resource doesn't get precached and thus the possibility of a partial precached state. Workbox delivers a best effort precache and it isn't immediately obvious to me how to best avoid a partial precache state. 
1. **Dependent Scripts** - SwPrecache inlines all dependencies directly in the service worker so we just serve one script and we are done. Workbox has a modular build which deploys dependencies along-side your service worker (~20 files). A bit messy and not a perfect fit for our build script which ends up adding twenty more attachments to the database. A quick attempt to build only the required resources ended up with some dependencies being pulled from a cdn – which is problematic for projects using domain-based data contracts.  
 
All solvable problems, but a bit of untangling to do. Imo -- the best case would be using Workbox to output a script which does exactly what swPrecache is outputting now. I'm confident we can get there if we are interested in other features of Workbox *cough* - offline google analytics - *cough*. 
 
# Questions for Reviewer 

1. Let's discuss the general approach in this PR and maybe somebody can test a few scenarios on a device or two? If we like the result, maybe it is easier to carve this into chunks and review and submit in pieces. 
1. I just copied the list of resources to cache from appcache.manifest. We cache 29 files (some things which we maybe don't use). Maybe worth following up with an item to reduce how much we cache? 
1. The Application tab in devtools reports the disk use of appcache as 20.6MB and the same resources cached using service workers as 39.7MB. Unsure of the reason, but possible discussion point. 
1. It would be nice to get some guidance on exactly what horti scenarios would be good to test for this. 
1. Should we use the service worker to cache the favicon? 
1. Should we use the service worker to cache the login page? Even if you can't login, it's a better experience than seeing the non-localized white unbranded error page for login when offline. 
1. Upgrading from master to this change doesn't give the user the "Update" prompt because there is no change to a document being watched in master. Since this change won't be deployed atomically and will be instead packaged with other changes in v3.5 - I think that is safe. But we can consider tombstoning the legacy `appcache` document to make this change prompt an upgrade and also keep the database a bit cleaner. Looking for advice as I'm unsure how to best handle that. 
1. For performance reasons, we could consider making the service worker download and precache resources on the login page instead of after login. It is a one-line change which could benefit some users but possibly annoy others. 
1. Instead of using "ddoc-extraction," I considered calculating the hash of the service worker file at build-time and setting a single attribute on the medic-client ddoc. Think this would be cleaner? 
1. I put the core grunt logic into its own file instead of dumping it into the Gruntfile.js. I find that Gruntfile really hard to parse, and easily get lost in its large indentations. What do you think of starting to chop up that file into separate more manageable pieces (as done here)? 
1. Want to add a new UI state into the bootstrapper which says something like "Downloading App..." For the duration of the period in which we precache the service worker's resources? 
1. This change will block testing on insecure origins except localhost. This is pretty awkward for testing dev builds on a phone – I ran a DNS server + nginx proxy + vpn on my phone to work around it. This is likely something we should address in this change or shortly after. Looking to discuss the best approach. 
1. Is it safe the remove the write access controls to the deprecated appcache document in this change? 

# Scenarios I Tested

1. Incognito, login. Go offline. Refresh: user should get offline experience. 
1. Incognito, delete a required attachment, login: user should see an error dialog prompting to check connection. Rebuild and click retry: login should succeed and page should work offline. 
1. Incognito, login, update a css file, build, sync: user should see prompt to update. Update: user should see change in css appear. Network shows only the css file being updated. 
1. Incognito, login, update a css file, build, delete the css attachment in db, sync: user should see error in console and should not be prompted to update. Rebuild: after five minutes user should see prompt to update. Update: user should see change in css appear. 
1. If service-worker.js results in 404, then the app should not load and user should see error prompting to check connection. 
1. Incognito, login, update a css file, build, refresh without syncing: user should see prompt to update after refresh. Update: user should see change in css appear. 
1. Incognito, login to master (AppCache version). Rebuild to proposed change, sync. User should see prompt to update.

body:
In some configurations the patient_id field holds the patient shortcode,
while the patient_uuid field holds the internal id.

For tasks and targets it's important that we know how to bind to the
UUID as well, because otherwise users may see bugs while offline. For
example, a task wouldn't close until the report that closes the task is
synced upwards, run through by Sentinel, and synced back down.

Less important for purging, but it's better that we keep the function
logic the same.
