body:
It would be cool if we could add an automatic documentation generation tool into our development flow. This would help newcomers as well as (hopefully!) help us to write good code-local documentation.

It should understand some kind of JS-friendly comment-based documentation (like [JSDoc](http://usejsdoc.org/about-getting-started.html)), and use that to generate some readable documentation (e.g. html or markdown) that we can store somewhere and refer to.

Whether or not that storage is part of the each commit (e.g. it gets run as part of Grunt and updates a git-commitable location) or whether we run it manually occasionally (e.g. on every release) to be stored elsewhere is up for debate.

It would also be useful if it understood Angular's conventions, so it could intelligently link controllers to services and so on.

title: Work out what we want to do with Enketo XML, and do that thing
body:
When creating reports we store the user-entered data effectively twice:
 - Once as the raw XML that Enketo returns to us, for use by subsequent Enketo invocations (i.e editing docs)
 - Once as extract JSON in `doc.fields.{}`, for use by everything else (on-screen display, configurable logic like rules and schedules, impact and analytics via couch2pg, etc)

Originally we stored the XML in the `doc.xml` property, as a string.

We later realised that this is inefficient / unhelpful, because CouchDB's view generation performance is a function of the size of a JSON document, and nothing refers to it except editing. So, we moved it into an attachment.

However, this has caused other performance problems:
 - Replication is less efficient in general, because the algorithm requests attachments separately
 - Replication is **far** less efficient relevant to CouchDB 2.0, because we can now batch document GETs, but not attachments GETs, so the disparity is far more obvious
 - For a reason yet to be investigated, PouchDB view generation is **far** slower with attachments present (it should be at worst identical).

We need to work out what to do here.

Obvious options include:
 - Prioritise replication speed and PouchDB view generation performance over CouchDB view generation performance and move the XML back into a string against the JSON
 - Delete the XMl altogether, and re-generate the XML from the `doc.fields` object when we want to edit (hat-tip @dianabarsan for that brilliant suggestion)
 - Do any amount of PouchDB investigation and performance improvements to solve any or all of the problems listed above

Diana's suggestion sounds ideal, and IMO should be investigated first, but it can be up for discussion.

Context: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1kXjsF-orndz0-V5UFf_Esx5J-ogeQ6_tALCwE1K0tvA/edit#heading=h.29bkt8nfi7kw

title: Measure and if possible improve CouchDB GET performance via API
body:
While doing some performance benchmarks (see Context below) I noticed that attachment GETs are really slow for what they are.

This may be true for all GETs, and could be due to our new security code making sure you're allowed to GET the thing you're asking for.

We should measure the performance of GET requests (and honestly authenticated interactions with api in general), work out if we're adding overhead and how much, and see if there are ways we can improve the code to remove those overheads.

Obvious things would be caching certain critical pieces of data, though it's unclear what we could easily cache (apart from UserCtx). At the very least we should understand what is going on.

Context: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1kXjsF-orndz0-V5UFf_Esx5J-ogeQ6_tALCwE1K0tvA/edit#heading=h.29bkt8nfi7kw

title: Investigate Geckoview as a replacement for Crosswalk
body:
When doing some performance tests recently (see Context below) I noticed that Firefox seems to have a much more performant implementation of IndexedDB than Chrome does (or PouchDB uses it in a way that Firefox likes more, or something).

Especially with Crosswalk EOL'd, and with us definitely wanting to squeeze as much performance out of the phones we're deployed to as possible, it may be worth checking out [GeckoView](https://wiki.mozilla.org/Mobile/GeckoView) as an alternative.

Things we care about:
 - Does our app work correctly in general
 - While PouchDB generates views faster, are other things faster? Or slower? Or the same? The performance of common actions (esp those picked out so far for Telemetry) should be looked into
 - As noted: Chrome *does* replicate faster than Firefox (and thus potentially Geckoview). We should see if this is true
 - Does it allow us to easily increase / make infinite our quota (the main reason we use Crosswalk today)
 - Does it get updated frequently? Does it allow us to stay closer to modern browsers (right now we're on Chrome 53 until we work out how to build Crosswalk again or move off it)?
 - Is is easy to integrate with and to build and use on Android?

Context: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1kXjsF-orndz0-V5UFf_Esx5J-ogeQ6_tALCwE1K0tvA/edit#heading=h.29bkt8nfi7kw

title: Use IDBNext
body:
We've done a bunch of work around getting IDBNext ready to go, but so far haven't put the final amount of effort into being able to use it.

Specifically, we need to find the time to:
 - Get PouchDB folks to be OK with and release the adapter into the npm ecosystem so we can use it as an alternative (or publish it ourselves under `@medic`)
 - Create a branch that uses it and takes advantage of it to use Mango efficiently, for testing 
 - If this goes well, work out how we want to migrate from the `idb` adapter to the `indexeddb` adapter, and implement it

This ticket is a medic-side ticket we can schedule into releases / time blocks so it doesn't stay under the radar.

title: Introduce a secondary server flag
body:
We've started to find use cases for running a secondary (aka satellite) server which runs its own copy of CouchDB with bidirectional replication to the primary server. This is useful where a facility needs to access all the data but doesn't have a reliable internet connection.

In these configurations it's easy to end up with database conflicts in situations where services on both servers assume they are the only copy of their service, most notably api and sentinel.

1. Find a way to pass a flag so our code can know when its running on a secondary server. This cannot be a simple flag in the Settings doc because this is replicated between servers. It may be easy to set an environment variable.
2. Investigate and fix wherever this flag should be used. I suspect sentinel should be disabled altogether and there are parts of api which are not required (eg: extracting the medic-client ddoc).

title: Expired tasks don't disappear from the Tasks tab when they expire
body:
1. Configure a task which will emit with a dueDate of today, and an expiry date of tomorrow.
1. Set your clock to 11:55pm, refresh the page, navigate to the 'tasks' tab and see the task.
1. Wait 5 minutes, and you should see the dueDate "today" change to "yesterday" and turn red.
1. Set your clock to tomorrow + 11:55pm, refresh the page, and view the task.

Expected: After 5 minutes, this task should disappear because it has expired.
Observed: Wait 5 minutes, and you will see the dueDate "tomorrow" change to "2 days ago". Refresh the tab and the expired task will disappear.

There is some [code in LiveList which is run at midnight](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/webapp/src/js/services/live-list.js#L543) which refreshes the description of the task. There is an expectation that we should maybe also remove expired tasks here.

title: Investigate how much space is required on phones to perform an upgrade
body:
We have reports from the field of phones not being able to complete version upgrades due to lack of space so we should investigate.

Firstly determine how much space is actually required, and if this is constant between versions, the number of docs you have, etc.

Secondly work out what is using the space. It's likely that view rebuilding takes a lot more space which is then cleaned up when complete.

Thirdly think about what solutions or mitigations we could implement. Some ideas here...

- Would using IDBNext help?
- Would using Mango help?
- Can we work out how much is needed somehow? If so, we could detect when the phone doesn't have enough space and warn the user before starting the upgrade.
- Can we recover when the phone runs out of space?
- Can we do compact/cleanup pouchdb during or between view rebuilds to reduce the required space?
- Can we do a compact/cleanup before starting the upgrade?
- _your idea here_

If there are any really easy changes feel free to do them as part of this issue but anything more complicated should be spun off as separate issues.

title: Improve the upgrade page to include information about which versions are supported
body:
On the upgrade page we show all releases that are newer than the currently installed version. Make the following changes to encourage configurers to follow best practice when upgrading.

1. Change this so by default only the latest patch, latest minor, and latest major are shown. Don't show duplicates if the latest major is the same as the latest minor, or if the version is the same as the currently installed version. This makes the UI simpler for the most common actions and encourages users to install the release that will be supported the longest.
2. If there are releases that aren't the latest but are later than the currently installed version it must still be possible to upgrade to them, so add an expandable section for less recommended options. It's better to upgrade at all than to be blocked on the current release.
3. Show a warning in Horti CLI as well as the upgrade page if upgrading to an unsupported version. Allow the user to accept the warning and continue.
4. Include the date the currently installed version will no longer be supported at the top of the upgrade page. This only applies if a newer version has been released. Otherwise show words to the effect of "no expiry date set". Style this with a warning if the date is within a month (eg: yellow exclamation mark). Style this with an error if the date has passed (eg: red exclamation mark).

The support expiries are as follows:

> Medic Mobile supports the latest patch of minor versions of our software for three months after the next minor version is made available, and the latest minor of a major version for twelve months after the next major version is made available.
> Once a version is no longer supported it will not receive any further releases and upgrading may be required before Medic Mobile can investigate any issues.

title: Use Mango to reduce the number of indexes needed client side
body:
We currently query for data records in PouchDB / CouchDB via mapreduce queries.

Each map-reduce defined query creates its own index that needs to be kept up to date as data changes.

Mango splits the creation of the index from the use of it in a query. So, if we can convert many of our mapreduce queries to Mango, we can reduce how many indexes that need to be generated.

An example of looking at this for startup is here: https://github.com/medic/medic/pull/5264 (along with some other changes)

We need to be careful and **measure performance**, in both offline and online situations, both for query speed and individual index generation time, as well as network costs in the online scenario, and balance _that_ against the fact that Mango allows for less indexes. It's complicated!

One core difference is that Mango queries are *always* equivalent to `include_docs: true` in relation to how CouchDB pulls data off disk into memory. One example of how this affects things is that a mapreduce view which doesn't include_docs will query much faster than the equivalent Mango query, when running in CouchDB (PouchDB should be equivalent).

The core goal is to reduce the count of indexes generated locally, while making sure we do not accidentally degrade performance elsewhere.

title: Fix UHC styling when using both UHC and muting at the same time
body:
There is a bug/oversight in our UI styling when using both UHC and muting features at the same time. 

**What it currently looks like:** 
When a contact is muted and is displaying a grey icon in the main contacts list, the UHC date last visited and visits per month text is still styled red. This is confusing as it sends conflicting signals to the user. The red says “look at me, I’m important”, while the grey icon and muted status is meant to say “don’t worry about me, I’m not as important”.

**What it should look like:**
- If a contact is muted, the date last visited text should always be colored black, even if over 30 days.
- If a contact is muted, the number of visits per month (right side) is always grey, no matter if the visit count is 0, 1, 2, or 2+.
- If a contact is muted, the number of visits per month (right side) does not have a warning sign icon associated with it, no matter if the visit count is 0, 1, 2, or 2+.

**Mockups**
On the left is the current problematic styling. On the right is the desired styling.

![Screen Shot 2019-04-19 at 9 12 45 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/56432724-55b9f980-6283-11e9-9761-e359d5816417.png)


IMPORTANT: Another option could be to remove all UHC information from muted contacts entirely (don't display the date last visited or visits this month at all for those who are muted). But this should only be done if we are also able to accomplish #5596. If the muted contacts remain intermingled amongst active contacts then I think it makes sense to keep the UHC information, as it explains the sorting method.

title: Sort muted contacts to the bottom of the contacts list
body:
Right now muted contacts remain on the main contacts list, intermingled amongst active contacts, the only difference being that their icons are styled grey.

Our initial proposal for muting was that we would like to collect all of the muted contacts in a separate folder that lives at the bottom of the list. However this posed some technical challenges and we dropped it from the muting MVP.

@dianabarsan  said theoretically we could re-sort the contacts, but this would require updating the form that lists the people, and all phones would have to re-index their data.

An alternative could be sorting muted contacts to the bottom of the list ONLY when the list is sorted by “date last visited”. In UHC mode the default sorting is configurable by project, and any UHC user can go in at any time and toggle the sorting back and forth between “by date last visited” and “alphabetically”. But if _most_ UHC projects set their default sort to date last visited (Muso does), and if _most_ users typically leave it on the default sort, this solution could help most users in most cases.

Would be nice if devs could explore the potential solution described above (which would only help UHC projects) and/or any other ways to sort the muted contacts to the bottom of the list, which might potentially work across all projects.

title: Integration with Africa's Talking SMS aggregator
body:
A new project EBS wants to use feature phones and SMS instead of smartphones and data. Usually we use medic-gateway running on android to send and receive SMS using medic-api APIs, but it has some issues including being dropped from the play store, the app going to sleep, low throughput, high latency, etc. It would be much better to use a specialized third party cloud hosted aggregator instead. For this project we've chosen [Africa's Talking](https://africastalking.com/sms/twowaysms).

1. Create a new routine to send SMS via Africa's Talking (both immediate messages such as auto replies, and scheduled messages generated periodically).
2. Create a new API (potentially multiple endpoints) that Africa's Talking will call when an SMS is received.
3. Create a new API to update the status of outgoing messages as they are delivered.
4. This integration must be disabled by default, and all the account information must be configurable.

Africa's Talking provides a sandbox mode you can use during development and testing, and have support if required. The also have an [npm SDK package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/africastalking) which exposes a simple API to use, as well as tutorials on how to integrate.

There will likely be more integrations with other providers at a later date so consider refactoring the gateway and Africa's Talking integrations to use shared services where possible to make reuse easier for the next integration.

@newtewt prototyped an integration using expressjs which almost worked and may be useful as a starting point.

title: 6042 fix case sensitive issue
body:
# Description
The immunization visit form (form: C_IMM) submitted from collect app has value `Yes` for a immunization received, i.e. `"received_bcg": "Yes"`. In the code, `addImmunizations(): vaccines_received['received_' + dose[0]] === 'yes'` checks for `yes`. And, since `Yes` and `yes` are different in case, the condition card is not getting updated for the immunization visit forms submitted from the collect app. To overcome this case-sensitive issue, `toLowerCase()` is used in the comparison in the relevant function. It is related to [GH Issue 6402](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/6042#issuecomment-483633418).

title: Changing user profile language prevents user from changing back to original language
body:
**Steps to reproduce**:
1. Log in as national or district admin
1. Go to user settings > Edit user profile > Language
1. Select a different language from what has already been set i.e. change from English to Swahili
1. Navigate away from user settings
1. Go to user settings > Edit user profile > Language
1. Select the language that had originally been set and apply i.e. change from Swahili to English

**What should happen**:
 - The language should change back to English from Swahili

**What actually happens**:
 - The language doesn't change back to English but can change to other languages other than the original language.

**Environment**:

- Instance: villagehealthworks-burundi.app.medicmobile.org
- Browser: Chrome
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.4.0

title: Broken functionality after upgrade to 3.4 with custom locales
body:
_Supported languages do not show on the languages tab of languages settings, specific to webapps upgraded to 3.4.0_.

**Steps to reproduce**:
 - _Login as admin on an upgraded instance (not a fresh 3.4.0, but an upgraded webapp), e.g. `pih-malawi.dev`_
 - _Go to App Settings > Languages > Languages_

**What should happen**:
 - _Supported locales should be listed on the page, where one can set a default language among other operations. See screenshot below._
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3928714/56903632-57ff2d80-6aa5-11e9-8a87-2ce963469417.png)

**What actually happens**:
 - _No language list is shown. See screenshot below._
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3928714/56903688-71a07500-6aa5-11e9-84fe-b8a3700bfc83.png)

_Browser console log has the following_

```
Error loading settings TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object

    at properties.js:81
    at createLocaleModel (translation-languages.js:25)
    at translation-languages.js:75
    at Function._.map._.collect (underscore.js:205)
    at translation-languages.js:74
    at processQueue (angular.js:17914)
    at angular.js:17962
    at Scope.$digest (angular.js:19075)
    at angular.js:19395
```

**Environment**:

- Instance: _pih-malawi.dev.medicmobile.org_
- Browser: _Chrome_
- App: _webapp_
- Version: _3.4.0_

**Other**:
_I was able to reproduce this on my local testing instance, upgraded from `3.3.0`. A fresh `3.4.0` instance works perfectly. Could be related to #5616?_

title: Update process needs to be clearer
body:
During our site visit Siaya was upgraded to 3.4. CHWs were opening the app after the upgrade and getting a 404. @dianabarsan  determined it was due to the user still replicating using an old version(2.14) and still downloading all the docs still for the new version. The hope is that we can detect an update has occurred and indicate this to the user that they're still downloading docs to get onto the latest client version. The way we were confirming is the sync status in the hamburger menu. Because of this people were shutting down the app and assumed it was broken.  

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be nice to show a progress bar saying how much work is left to be done(doc downloading, indexing, etc..) or a message that says the update occurred and we are still processing.

title: JavaScript errors and crash stacks not logged to the console
body:
**Describe the bug**
Not all JavaScript errors and crash stacks are reported to the console.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Open `webapp/webapp/src/js/controllers/inbox.js` in an editor and delete `Auth` from the ngInjection list (line 24).
1. Rebuild app
1. Login to the webapp

**Observed behavior**
The console has no errors.

**Expected behavior**
This is a basic scripting error in which we are using an undefined variable. The app fails to load (expected) but there should be an error in the console explaining why.



I think this bug is important and labelled it Priority 1 because these console errors are often our only way to investigate/understand live-site issues on the client.

title: Xform rendering hides choices when relevance condition and choice filter are applied to a secondary question
body:
**Describe the bug**
Choices for a secondary `select_one/select_multiple` field do not show when both relevance condition and choice filter are applied. Consider the following design xls immunization section:

| Question/Note/Label  | Type | Required | Choices | Condition (Relevance/Show only if + Constraints/Validation) |
| ------------- | ------------- | ------------- | ------------- | ------------- |
| Select the vaccines that were given on {{date}} *Tick every condition/symptom that applies*  | select_multiple  | yes  | BCG, Birth Polio (OPV 0), OPV, PCV, DPT-HepB-Hib, IPV, Rota, Vitamin A, Measles  | Don't show vaccines already reported. Birth Polio(OPV 0) if age <= 2weeks, OPV, PCV, Rota and DPT-HepB-Hib  if age >= 6 weeks, Vit A if age >= 6 months, Measles if age >= 9 months  |
| Select which dose of OPV was given on {{date}}  | select_one  | yes  | OPV 1/2/3  | If OPV is selected. Show OPV 2 if age >= 10 weeks, OPV 3 if age >= 14 weeks. Don't show doses already reported.  |
| Select which dose of PCV was given on {{date}}  | select_one  | yes  | PCV 1/2/3  | If PCV is selected. Show PCV 2 if age >= 10 weeks, PCV 3 if age >= 14 weeks. Don't show doses already reported.  |
| Select which dose of DPT-HepB-Hib was given on {{date}}  | select_one  | yes  | DPT-HepB-Hib 1/2/3  | If DPT-HepB-Hib is selected. Show DPT-HepB-Hib 2 if age >= 10 weeks, DPT-HepB-Hib 3 if age >= 14 weeks. Don't show doses already reported.  |
| Select which dose of Rota was given on {{date}}  | select_one  | yes  | Rota 1/2  | If Rota is selected. Show Rota 2 if age >= 10 weeks. Don't show doses already reported.  |
| Select which dose of Measles was given on {{date}}  | select_one  | yes  | Measles 1/2  | If Rota is selected. Show Measles 2 if age >= 18 months. Don't show doses already reported.  |

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Configure the above, a sample can be found [here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1rMD49QfSO-xHSjt3MZ5vBZqy-RggU_deVh6kMZ0fCKc/edit#gid=1042357020)
2. Convert and upload the form and pick a client profile to complete it
3. The behavior in the image below is observed, doses do not show
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3928714/57144422-b9870b00-6dc9-11e9-9c96-a8a8a9e4fd44.png)


**Expected behavior**
The expected behavior is to have the doses (choices) showing appropriately, as shown below. This happens when I either remove the relevance condition or the choice filter.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3928714/57144766-75483a80-6dca-11e9-9a4c-5833dc8e5ad6.png)


**Logs**
No logs on browser console.

**Screenshots**
See captures above.

**Environment**
- Instance: _pih-malawi.dev.medicmobile.org_
- Browser: _Chrome_
- Client platform: _Linux_
- App: _webapp_
- Version: _3.4.0_

**Additional context**
This was experienced in _3.3.0_ too. The workaround applied is merging vaccines and doses, i.e. instead of asking to select dose say for OPV, have vaccines as OPV 1, OPV 2 and OPV 3 ...

cc @derickl @smbuthia 


**Why Now?**
Partner(s): Internal
Reason(s): A partner will have CHWs/Supervisors with a detrimental experience, thus providing bad care

title: Add Zapier webhook to Travis
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently we have Travis CI notifications in a group Slack channel for all failures, and when the success status changes. These notifications occur for all branches, which becomes overly noisy in Slack.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
From internal discussion the first phase would be to reduce noise by only showing failures and changes of status of the master branch. Optionally, we could notify only the user in question.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Alternatively we could disable Slack notifications altogether, and rely on email notifications to individuals, otherwise have the notifications in another channel altogether, and they could monitor that channel with notifications for their name/handle.

**To Reproduce**

1. Using a instance on 3.4
2. Log in as an offline user and replicate everything to be synced up. 
3. I went off line at this point by disabling wifi on my phone and in browser ticked the offline in the network tab. 
4. Upgrade to 3.5.x

title: Timer widget beeps even after cancelling the form
body:
**Describe the bug**
Timer widget beeps even after cancelling the form

**To Reproduce**
1. Start a new form with a countdown timer widget

**Expected behavior**

title: Ability to calculate how many tasks are shown and completed by users
body:
To improve our impact we must first measure our impact.

One of our major features is tasks and we make it very difficult to measure how many tasks are being shown to users and how many tasks are being completed. This is due to tasks being ephemeral and generated on the phone so server side analytics queries don't have access to this information. Instead the impact team create custom queries based on the configuration of each project but this is error prone and time consuming.

One solution would be to write tasks to the database and replicate to couchdb but this could have a potentially serious performance impact.

Consider various implementations and analyse the performance impacts of each before implementation.

title: 5653 - "Upgrade" dialog does not appear when upgrading from 3.4 > 3.5
body:
# Description

> Upgrading from master to this change doesn't give the user the "Update" prompt because there is no change to a document being watched in v3.4. Since this change won't be deployed atomically and will be instead packaged with other changes in v3.5 - I think that is safe. But we can consider tombstoning the legacy appcache document to make this change prompt an upgrade and also keep the database a bit cleaner. Looking for advice as I'm unsure how to best handle that.

https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/5653#issuecomment-491642151

Turns out that modifying the `appcache` doc won't work to trigger the upgrade since the doc's name has been removed from the `validate_doc_update` and `docs_by_replication_key` etc. So I don't replicate down anymore once the 3.5 service stack is running.

Instead, this proposed changes introduces a benign attribute into the medic_client ddoc to trigger the update. If this approach seems non-hacky, we can merge this into the branch for #5648 and AT that single PR.

medic/medic#5653

title: Ensure we can configure collapsible lists
body: DHIS2 submission forms include fields like "Number of households visited". This will be prepopulated with a number we calculate. To allow users to verify the number we need to allow a section to be optionally shown with a list of household names that were used in the calculation. Enketo has the ability to show/hide sections so we need to confirm that the version we use works and is visually appealing and consistent with our other UI elements.

title: Calculate data for DHIS2 reports
body:
Every month CHPs are expected to submit a DHIS2 report which records information such as "Number of households visited". We have enough information to automate the calculation of much of this data so we can make the reporting much more efficient and less error prone by prepopulating the form. Note that as well as the aggregate data we also need to be able to view the items that contributed to this total (#5660), using the above example we need to show not only the number of households visited, but also the names of the households.

It may be possible to configure nools to generate a task which has collects all the data and passes it to the form using global variables to store data as the families are being processed.

Alternatively we could create a new doc type to store this data and create a new instance each month on the phone.

Analyse the implementations and prove and/or implement the correct approach.

title: Sentinel should have a status page
body:
It's hard to monitor sentinel as it stands.  It's usually determined based on if its actions haven't been performed that we know sentinel is down.

In order to be proactive in monitoring it, the best way seems to be to have a status page that just tells you that it's running.

This would make it so that we could monitor it from outside of the instances as well and build alerting on top of it.

title: Ability to configure forms access based on hierarchy
body:
_*User story*_
As LG scales up and work on many experiment projects, it’s becoming increasing critical to have a way to `dynamically configure which CHVs access certain workflows` and who don’t have access. Sometimes CHVs participating in experiments are not segregated in a clear way like per branch. We can have sample CHVs from multiple branches.

We also need an intuitive way for non technical staff to assign and de-assign workflows/forms to CHVs unlike the current method where we put CHV uuids on the contact summary to indicate CHVs eligible for a certain experiment

_*Suggested solution*_
Adding an array of forms on the place object. These forms should be visible to everyone below the hierarchy. If you don’t want a form visible to everyone, you configure it down the hierarchy on the relevant place object. Check the example below
```
{
    "name":"…..",
    "uuid":"………",
    "forms": ["assessment.xml", "pregnancy.xml", ….],
    …
}
```
We can have a web tool (maybe on the admin panel) where a non-technical user can assign forms to branches or individual CHVs

title: Import people blocked by CSP
body:
**Describe the bug**
Uploading people using the admin app isn't working.

**To Reproduce**
1. Create a JSON file with some people data in it. A minimal example:
  `[{"_id": "a", "name": "something"}]`
1. Go to Admin app > Import & Export > People
2. Click on the Browse button in the Import section
3. Select the file you created in 1.
4. Click Submit
5. An error is shown in the UI. There's an error in the log. The person is not imported.

**Expected behavior**
No errors are shown and a contact is imported.

**Logs**
```
Content Security Policy: The page’s settings blocked the loading of a resource at http://_db/undefined (“connect-src”).
```

**Screenshots**
![Screenshot from 2019-05-17 11-13-15](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2064938/57892882-d83ed480-7894-11e9-9539-505670264ebb.png)
![Screenshot from 2019-05-17 11-13-24](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2064938/57892883-d83ed480-7894-11e9-9447-37c27fe8dd41.png)

**Environment**
- Instance: localhost
- Browser: Firefox
- Client platform: Ubuntu
- App: admin
- Version: 3.5.0 (master)

**Additional context**
1. Before starting on this bug consider if we can drop this feature altogether. medic-conf provides similar functionality.
2. If it is worth fixing, consider refactoring it to use the existing APIs for importing people and places.
3. Also consider using bulk APIs instead of one call per contact.

Secondly the requests are made in parallel which is guaranteed to fail with a large enough import. Thirdly it's implementing the logic that's already implemented in the [/api/v1/people api](https://github.com/medic/medic-api/#post-apiv1people). Finally it would be better to be in medic-conf (https://github.com/medic/medic-conf/issues/193 maybe related).

1. Work out if this feature is needed in the UI. If not, implement it in medic-conf and delete it from the admin app.
2. If it is needed in the UI, create a new v2 API which takes an array of people to create or update, not just a single doc. Then update the UI to just call the API.

title: Update how the in-app tour pop-up reminder works
body:
Relates to #5597, #5680, #5681, #5682. Full design spec: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ErZ7eC-Cbrsgwu0uaIfGq9ZeLuhma1h5K0xvYeRv2KU/edit#

Users can access the in-app tour anytime from the secondary hamburger menu by clicking on the “Guided Tour” link. Users may also access the tour from a periodic pop-up window. Right now this window only appears when the app first launches, which means it might not even be seen by CHWs since oftentimes an admin is the one to first launch the app.

Improvement: We would like this tour reminder window to display whenever there is a new “unread” tour topic. This means we will need the ability to track whether or not a tour has been "read". 

**Determining read/unread status**
- Each tour page section/topic is technically a separate tour. We want to start tracking if and when we’ve shown a particular tour. 
- All tours will start off being marked “unread”
- As soon as a user launches a tour, we will mark it as “read” (we are not going to require them to click through to the last tip in the section) 
- Every time we load the app, we will check for tours the user hasn’t read. If we introduce three new topics, those three sections would automatically be marked “unread”, and the user should see the tour pop-up prompt.
- Do we mark a read tour as “unread” again if we’ve made a change? It depends on how big of a change/update we’ve made. If we want the user to see the prompt again, we would “rename” the tour so it looks like a new tour.

**The pop-up window**
- The first time this window displays for brand new users, it should say something like _“Welcome! Before you get started using the app, take our guided tour to learn the basics.”_ It could also say something like _“If you’d like to access this tour again at a later date, open the menu in the upper right and select “Guided Tour”._ There should be a checkbox option for “Remind me later” but there should also be a way to just close out of the window. 
- Current app users will only see the pop-up if the app detects a new “unread” tour topic. The window in this case should say something like _“Your app has been updated - explore new features now"_. Again, there should also be a checkbox option for “Remind me later”. 
- If the "Remind me later" box is selected, the app will pause the reminder about new unread tour topics for some period of time, perhaps for a week. After a week it will once again display, and the user can again choose to close out entirely, check remind me later again, or actually look at the new tour content.

title: Turn the in-app tour table of contents pop-up into a true page
body:
Relates to #5597, #5679, #5681, #5682. Full design spec: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ErZ7eC-Cbrsgwu0uaIfGq9ZeLuhma1h5K0xvYeRv2KU/edit#

Right now when you click on "Guided Tour" you get a pop-up window where you can select from different page topics. Improvement: The table of contents page will now be a real page, not a modal, just like the About page.

**Tour table of contents page**
- The page should have a short text description that says something like _“This tour gives a guided walkthrough of the app. To go through the full tour, select the button below.”_ with a blue “Begin Tour” button (clicking on this button will start the user at the first topic, General)
- Following this there should be a linked table of contents with the text “To jump to a specific section of the tour, select one of the links below”. There will be an order to the tours/topics but users can click on any topic to skip to a certain section.
- For this initial launch, there will be 6 total topics/tours (1. General, 2. Tasks, 3. People, 4. Targets, 5. History, 6. Messages).
- All users will see the “General” tour. Whether or not a user sees a particular page tour depends on whether or not they have access to that page. For example, many CHWs may never see the Messages tour/topic.

![2019 tour - 2 table of contents](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/58039138-b472cd00-7ae6-11e9-98ec-b6196cf661f9.png)

title: Updates to the in-app tour functionality, including linking tours together
body:
Relates to #5597, #5679, #5680, #5682. Full design spec: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ErZ7eC-Cbrsgwu0uaIfGq9ZeLuhma1h5K0xvYeRv2KU/edit#

Currently a user first chooses a page from the main table of contents (like "Tasks"), they complete the Tasks tour, and then they are done. If they would like to continue and view the "People" tour next, they need to go back to the table of contents and choose the "People" topic. Improvement: link together the different in-app tours so that a user can go through the entire app tour without returning to the table of contents.

In essence how we will do this is to insert a new transitional tip between each section that has a "Next" button instead of a "Finish" button. The transitional tip will say something like "_You have completed the “Tasks” section of the tour.  To proceed to the "People" section, select “Next.” To exit the tour, select “Quit.”"_ Note: the linked string of tours may differ from user to user, depending on whether or not a user has access/visibility to a particular tab. For instance, CHWs often don't see the Messages tab, so they won't see the Messages tour, and the sequence will skip over the Messages tour.

![2019 tour - 6 general transition](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/58039838-be95cb00-7ae8-11e9-9af0-61584fd7003b.png)


Just to summarize:

**Functionality we aren’t altering**
- We will continue to use the same bootstrap tour library that we currently have
- The tour will continue to use the real app instance for the walkthrough 
- Technically, each page section/topic will be created as a separate tour. If a user doesn’t have access to a particular tab (for example, Messages) then they will not see any tips relating to Messages, and they will not see Messages in their table of contents. 
- If a user does have visibility to a tab, but doesn’t have the appropriate data, for example if they can see the tasks tab but don’t currently have any open tasks, the tips will still display but on top of an empty page.
- We will attach tips to a certain element (like a button or an icon), so that when the element moves around as the page scales, the tip will move around with it automatically
- Text is translated but nothing else is currently configurable
- The tour is not mandatory - users can close out of it at any time by clicking on the X in the corner.

**Desired changes to functionality**
- The table of contents page will now be a real page, not a modal, just like the About page.
- For this initial launch, the tour will only include general page overviews, but in the future it could also include special feature topics such as “Muting” or “UHC mode”.  
- The page overviews will obviously be contained to a single tab in the app, but a feature tour may jump between different pages to demonstrate the full workflow.
**- The different sections/topics of the tour will now be linked together so that a user can optionally choose to go through the entire tour without going back to the table of contents at the end of each section.** 
- Tour content will be updated as needed (not necessarily with each release) alongside the public release notes process.

**Other notes on linking tours**

- The very first tip of the very first tour topic does not have a Previous button (The first tip on the “General” section, in this case)

![Screen Shot 2019-05-20 at 10 17 41 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/58039771-93ab7700-7ae8-11e9-9262-b29e6d179baf.png)

- At the end of a tour/topic, we will have a transition slide which names the next section and gives the user a choice to continue on or to close out of the tour (with Next and Quit buttons)
![Screen Shot 2019-05-20 at 10 17 48 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/58039785-9c03b200-7ae8-11e9-9daa-6b71ca8b9d67.png)

- The very last tip of the last tour topic has a “Finish” button instead of a “Next” button
![Screen Shot 2019-05-20 at 10 18 00 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/58039788-9f973900-7ae8-11e9-9c3a-9985f02ff480.png)

title: Cache the path accessed from _rewrite
body:
# Description

Another regression from #5361. The android app navigates the user to `/medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/` and does not use the root url. To support offline mode, we need to ensure that a redirect from that rewrite page to root is cached.

I see a few options here: 

1. Existing service workers - The `appcache-upgrade.html` could register the existing service-worker and redirect once registration completes. During an upgrade this would load all of the app's resources during an empty page and is not ideal.
1. Appcache - Given that we have the appropriate manifest already in place (required for the upgrade process), I think this is the easiest and is the fix I pursued here.
1. New service worker - Could also do this. But it's a new file, a new build step, and a bit of a registration process. If things go wrong on this page, we have no feedback mechanic.
1. I hoped a `301` permanent redirect would work here. But this really complicates how we clear the appcache during the upgrade to service workers.

#3986 

Nasty business in the app since we now navigate to `/rewire`, get an appcached version of that page, redirect to `/`, and get a serviceworker cached version of that page. So I'm coupling this with a build-time flag in the app to avoid this for partners when they migrate to >3.5.
https://github.com/medic/medic-android/pull/70

title: Update apps to use local shared-libs
body:
We use `npm pack` to zip `api` and `sentinel` and attach them to our build ddoc as part of build process. We also use a collection of scoped (`@medic/<library>`) [shared libraries](https://github.com/medic/medic/tree/master/shared-libs)  across our apps.

title: Update the levels displayed in breadcrumbs across the app
body:
We use breadcrumbs to display contextual information about where a person/place belongs in the app hierarchy. Depending on the user, sometimes the breadcrumbs can contain redundant and unnecessary information. In this example, I am Amanda Cilek, and "Amanda Cilek's Area" is the place I belong to. I do not need to see "Amanda Cilek's Area" in the breadcrumbs of every single report that I have submitted.
![Screen Shot 2019-05-28 at 4 52 21 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/58519816-03190a80-816a-11e9-9255-5acbc8f7763d.png)

This request is to update how we handle breadcrumbs so that we show all levels **except for** the level the user themselves belongs to, the top-most level. The data underneath will still have the entire hierarchy, we'll just choose how much to show based on the logged in user. For example, when I look at my reports tab in the above instance, I should no longer see "Amanda Cilek's Area" at the end of every breadcrumb. However if my manager logged in and looked at the same reports, my manager _would_ still see "Amanda Cilek's Area".

This update should apply to wherever breadcrumbs show on the **LEFT HAND SIDE** of the app (currently Messages and Reports, but also Tasks once [#5710](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5710) is done). 

Wherever breadcrumbs are shown on the **RIGHT HAND SIDE**, we should continue to show all breadcrumbs as users often use these as a shortcut to navigate back to the top level.

title: Schedules are not cleared with Unicode form codes
body:
**Describe the bug**
Reported in `medic-projects`: https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/6366

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Load standard config on an instance.
1. Replace "N" form with "क" (do this in the form definition and `registrations` config, alternatively you can duplicate the form and schedule from another form)
3. Submit your new "क" form, wait until your report is processed and patient created. The report should have one scheduled task. 
4. For the new patient, submit a "P" form.

**Expected behavior**
After your "P" report is processed, the previous "क" report scheduled task should be cleared.

**What actually happens**
The scheduled task from your "क" report is still scheduled. 

**Environment**
- Instance: any 3.4, 3.5 instance
- App: api, sentinel
- Version: 3.4, 3.5

**Additional context**
When validating whether a report is a valid registration, we extract the form code from the document `form` property with `/^[^\w-]*([\w-]+)[^\w-]*$/` [here](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/shared-libs/registration-utils/src/index.js#L3).
In javascript, `\w` does not match non-ASCII unicode even when using the `u` flag. 
Using the `\p` metacharacter along with the `u` flag instead works, like:
`/^[^\p{L}\p{N}_-]*([\p{L}\p{N}_-]+)[^\p{L}\p{N}_-]*$/u`

title: Contacts moved by "medic-conf move-contacts" do not disappear from user's device and synchronization of any changes fail silently
body:
**Describe the bug**
Medic-conf 2.0.5 supports moving contacts within the hierarchy via the action "move-contacts".  When an offline user has downloaded the details for some contacts which are then removed from that position of the hierarchy, the contacts do not disappear. The contact remains on the user's device, but any updates made to the contact (or any reports created for that contact) will silently fail to sync. This can result in silent data loss. 

Known fix is for the offline user to clear cache and perform a clean synchronization. However, it is not straightforward to drive all contacts to complete this task. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Given offline user with `facility_id='health_center_1'` which has child `clinic_1`. 
1. Log in as user 
1. Edit contact under `clinic_1` and resync 
1. `medic-conf move-contacts upload-docs parent=health_center_2 clinic_1` 
1. Synchronize as user 
1. Edit contact again under `clinic_1` and resync 

**Expected behavior**
The edits made by this user should sync or an error should appear so the user knows the data did not sync. Ideally, these documents should be removed from the client's device. 

Observed: Documents remain. Synchronization of data fails silently.

title: Update webapp e2e tests to be executed as an offline user
body:
Most of our webapp workflows target offline users, while all of our webapp e2e tests, except one, run as an online user account. 
In order to have our e2e test coverage be closer aligned with actual usage, we should update webapp e2e tests that cover workflows usually performed by offline users to be tested using offline user accounts.

Given that offline users require syncing (likely manual, in this case) to get updates from the server, we might consider grouping all these e2e tests, so they run using one set of settings/forms, if flakyness and complications around needing to sync and refresh become problematic. 

Some webapp e2e tests might make sense to be run as online users, candidates could be tests around Messages tab and everything that requires SMS (for example registration_by_sms, sms-gateway).

title: Webapp doesn't support languages that are not pluralized by `make-plural`
body:
**Describe the bug**
Reports fail to load when the user language isn't pluralized by `make-plural`. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Install 3.5 (or 3.4)
2. Create a new language with a code that is not-existent or is not pluralized by `make-plural`. For example "rn". 
I prefer to copy whole contents of a translation file that already exists and just change the `code` and `_id` fields to match.
3. Login as an online user to the instance and change your language to "rn". Go to reports. **Refresh**
4. Observe that no reports load on the LHS and translations are missing from some of the filters.

**Expected behavior**
Reports LHS should load. 

**Logs**
There are no errors logged in the console.

**Screenshots**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/58900966-dbe1b080-8708-11e9-9318-cf1a82afb049.png)


**Environment**
- Instance: local, [live instance](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/6310)
- Browser: Chrome
- Client platform: Linux
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.4, 3.5 (possibly earlier)

**Additional context**
There are no errors visible in the console because `angular-translate` [deliberately ignores all translation loading errors](https://github.com/angular-translate/angular-translate/blob/master/src/service/translate.js#L1950):
```
langPromises[key]['finally'](function () {
    clearNextLangAndPromise(key);
})['catch'](angular.noop); // we don't care about errors (clearing)
``` 
If I change the source to actually log the error, replacing `angular.noop` with `console.error`:
```
Error: Localisation function not found for locale "rn"
    at Object.get (plurals.js:31)
    at new MessageFormat (messageformat.js:37)
    at Object.setLocale (angular-translate-interpolation-messageformat:121)
    at eachInterpolator (angular-translate.js:1633)
    at Object.forEach (angular.js:401)
    at useLanguage (angular-translate.js:1638)
    at angular-translate.js:2324
    at processQueue (angular.js:17914)
    at angular.js:17962
    at Scope.$digest (angular.js:19075)
```
We plug in the `message-format` interpolation to handle plurals, which in turn uses `make-plural` library.
We wait for the `$translate` to be `ready` [before we load forms](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/webapp/src/js/controllers/inbox.js#L421), 
and we wait for forms to be loaded [before we load reports in the LHS](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/webapp/src/js/controllers/reports.js#L471).
We also wait for `$translate` to be `ready` to load report filters.

`$translate` throws the error before broadcasting the "ready" event, so forms never load, so reports never load.

`make-plural` covers lots of languages, but not all. "rn" is a valid language code for Kirundi.
[Link to the source of `make-plural` covered languages](https://github.com/eemeli/make-plural/blob/master/packages/plurals/umd/plurals.js)

title: Calculation of baseline risk scores in the app
body:
Currently, families in the pilot area have been manually assigned a baseline risk score which was calculated offline using R. For the pilot it has been assumed that this risk score will not change, though in reality it is based on several things which may change periodically (equity indicators, family size, etc.). Newly registered individuals are assigned an average risk score for any applicable risks and any household/community level factors 

This approach poses 2 challenges: 

1. Baseline risk scores are currently static but in reality the underlying factors can change over time, and baseline risk score should be recalculated. The frequency of this recalculation does not need to be high as it is assumed that these variables will not change frequently. 
2. New individuals are assumed to have an average baseline risk, so important family context is lost for these families. 

What we want: 

1. Periodic calculation of baseline risk scores: The system should be able to calculate key risk factors for individuals on a periodic basis (monthly?) and update the baseline risk score stored in contact documents on the health workers’ phones.
2. Calculation of baseline risk scores for newly registered patients: The system should be able to calculate key risk factors for individuals after registration and update the baseline risk score stored in contact documents on the health workers’ phones.

[Details of the calculation](https://docs.google.com/document/d/16-Cpm1DJDHZKdU2DEDBrnMt6CHv3AV3Ntuw2aOm-pao/edit?usp=sharing).

[Original issue](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/6345)

title: Custom risk thresholds per CHW
body:
Currently, each individual's risk is compared to a single threshold to determine whether they are high risk or not. We know that high risk individuals will often be located near each other, (for example, an area of a community that has a higher percentage of very poor families). This means that high risk individuals are not distributed evenly across health workers, and we have seen some health workers have a much larger number of new high risk tasks than others. 

Risk thresholds should be customizable by the health worker to ensure each health worker gets a reasonable number of high-risk tasks. 

One approach we have discussed is a Hybrid Risk Threshold: We maintain an absolute threshold which individuals must be above to receive any tasks, but also include relative thresholds for users who have more high-risk tasks than would likely be possible. This would allow us to manage health worker workloads while also preserving a concept of absolute risk.

[Original issue](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/6346)

title: Risk score recording
body:
The ability to store risk scores when they’re updated in a server-side doc. 

Right now, there is no way to know which individuals the app has identified as high risk. This makes it incredibly challenging to monitor and evaluate our initiative. Currently, our analysis plans require us to look at task completion rates for high risk tasks. To calculate this, we have to reproduce who the app thinks is high risk, and then also reproduce the rules for task generation. This gets even more confusing because people's risk status can change over time. Many of the concepts we want to evaluate require knowing who is high risk. 

There are also other requests that have come up for accessing this information including:
- supervisors being able to see how many high risk patients each CHW is responsible for

A note/idea from Matt: Creating a doc similar to [this](https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/2180#issuecomment-412700493) which is stored only server side so that we can use it in analytics to know when tasks are created and don’t have to recreate the calculations in postgres/elsewhere.

[Original issue](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/6347)

title: Add "belongs to" breadcrumbs to tasks in the LHS list
body:
#5697 is related and either needs to be completed before, or at the same time as, this request.

**User stories**
- As a CHW, when I look at my tasks list, I would like to know the family or primary contact that an individual person belongs to, so that I can identify patients easier. (For example, tasks about children currently only display the child’s name. But children often have similar names and some parents wait months to give their baby a name. The child’s name is not always enough information.)

- As a CHW, when I look at my tasks list, I would like to know the family or primary contact that an individual person belongs to, so that I can better plan my visits and can complete all tasks for the same family at the same time. (Currently a CHW may have more than one open task for the same family, but because the tasks list is sorted by due date and doesn’t list the family name, they may miss other tasks for the same family.)

- As a CHW, I would like tasks for the same family to be grouped together so that I can be more efficient with my visit time and planning. (This spec/feature doesn’t address grouping, but just noting that displaying the family name is probably a desired prerequisite to sorting by family.)

**Summary**
- After discussing many possibilities, we decided that we would like to add a third line of text to tasks to display the additional contextual information.
- This new line of text should display breadcrumbs showing where the person/place the task is about belongs to. 
- The functionality should match how we display breadcrumbs elsewhere on the app. Note that we are updating breadcrumbs across the app so that they do not list out the level the user themselves belongs to repetitively (i.e. CHW Janet will not see “CHW Janet’s Area” repeated all over the place, ticket #5697).
- The text should be styled just like breadcrumbs elsewhere on the app (Noto Sans 14px).

**Examples**
- For CHWs on the webapp looking at a task about a particular person, the breadcrumbs should most often be just the family name (e.g. “Beatrice Bass Family”). Only a single level is listed because the next level, CHW Janet’s Area, is the CHW’s own level. 
![Screen Shot 2019-05-22 at 12 16 03 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/58914178-b8037800-86d2-11e9-95f9-309408a24c34.png)


- Some tasks are for families instead of individual people, like family surveys or bed net distribution. In these cases, the breadcrumbs may not display at all, since there are no levels between the family and the CHW area.
![Screen Shot 2019-05-22 at 12 13 35 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/58914201-c2be0d00-86d2-11e9-84a6-8811ee497dae.png)


- IF we ever do eventually add in the concept of sub-areas, at that point the breadcrumbs could display both the family name and the sub area name (since there would now be two levels before the CHW area).
![Screen Shot 2019-05-22 at 12 13 42 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/58914217-cfdafc00-86d2-11e9-886b-55ca220481d9.png)


- For facility users on Standard, the breadcrumbs will start with the CHW Area (since Standard does not have a concept of families).
![Screen Shot 2019-05-22 at 12 16 09 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/58914239-d8cbcd80-86d2-11e9-824e-eaac30438d2f.png)


- For a CHW supervisor, if the supervisor has a task about a CHW, the breadcrumbs would display the CHW Area (and any other levels between the CHW and the supervisor, if applicable).
![Screen Shot 2019-06-04 at 2 14 50 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/58914381-28aa9480-86d3-11e9-85a6-0ce08d46e91b.png)


- Also, a reminder that we sometimes have high risk task styling. In the cases of high risk, the breadcrumb info should come after the risk message.
![Screen Shot 2019-05-22 at 12 13 12 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/58914277-f305ab80-86d2-11e9-8c37-55520beb188d.png)

title: Investigate the possibility of dropping Crosswalk
body:
Chrome 55 introduced the persistent storage API which means offline storage should not be cleared unless the user manually clears it.

> When storage on the local machine is running tight (“under storage pressure”), user agents automatically clear storage to make more available space. Of course, for offline apps, this may be unfortunate, as they may not have synced their data to the server yet, or they may be apps that the user expects to just work offline (like a music player); so the Storage spec defines two different modes for storage for a given domain - “best effort” and “persistent”. The default mode, of course, is “best effort”. Storage for a domain that is “best effort” (aka “not persistent”) can be cleared automatically, without interrupting or asking the user. However, “persistent” data will not be automatically cleared. (If the system is still under storage pressure after clearing all non-persistent data, the user will need to manually clear any remaining persistent storage.)

https://developers.google.com/web/updates/2016/06/persistent-storage

This is the main reason why we need Crosswalk.

1. Test the feature works as expected allowing us to use 100% of the available disk space without ever deleting data.
2. Investigate replacing Crosswalk with native android webview and ensure there aren't any other Crosswalk features we rely on.
3. Ensure we can increase our minimum Android version to 5.0.0 (required so the webview can be updated separately to Android) and our minimum Chrome version to at least 55 (so we can use the persistent storage feature).
4. Add code to request persistent storage for the domain.

title: Runs npm dedupe before packaging api and sentinel
body:
# Description

Post https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/5694 , our `api` and `sentinel` bundled doubled in size because of lots of duplicated dependencies ( `npm pack` straight up copies the symlinked folders ). 
Running `npm dedupe` reduces our bundle sizes to what they were before.

body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Muso's mRDT scale-up is scheduled for July. Muso's projection is that post-scale-up they will capture 10 photos per CHV per day, which would be several thousand images per day (3000?). There is reason to believe that after time this would cause some server-side bloating and potential slow-down. We would benefit from some sort of retention policy or hot/cold storage solution.

We can consider having a cron script which removes old photos from CouchDB. Potentially moving them to AWS's glacier storage if they need to be retained.

title: Makes replication _all_docs requests quicker
body:
When replicating down, after receiving a batch of changes, PouchDB will iterate them to comprise a list of docs that are on their 1st revision. If any are found, it would try to get them with an `_all_docs?include_docs=true` request, presumably as a performance shortcut.
Once it receives the results, all of the docs that are not retrieved (for any reason) or have attachments or have since been edited or have conflicts, will be retrieved with the next `_bulk_get` request. 

The `_all_docs` calls are particularly expensive, as the implementation composes the list of all allowed doc ids that the user is allowed to see and compose a response based on that.
While this implementation is correct for generalized `_all_docs` requests (requesting `_all_docs` without parameters is expected to return the full list of existent docs stubs), we could improve it for the specific case of replication requests (that use `keys` and `include_docs=true`) parameters to actually request the docs and run the view map queries over the results to filter the ones the user is allowed to see - similar to how we filter `_bulk_get` requests.

title: The `initial_replication_date` in info docs is always `unknown`
Improves performance of replication _all_docs requests
body:
# Description

During replication, PouchDB will always request with `keys` and `include_docs=true`. 
Since we would already run the query with `include_docs`, it's faster to run the authorization methods over the resulted docs to filter the allowed ones versus compiling the list of allowed doc ids and pre-filtering the requested ids. 

Running locally, using the seed data (from gamma.dev): performance difference: 

| Instance | Initial replication | Replicating 100 new docs from the server |

| master   | 40.5s               | 3.02s                                    |
| this PR  | 25.5s               | 2.21s                                    |

title: Immunization Condition Card not getting updated as per Collect Immunization Form submission
body:
Description

The [Immunization Condition Card](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/6042#issuecomment-478858331) is not getting updated as per the [Immunization report](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/config/standard/forms/collect/c_imm.xlsx) submitted from the collect app. As per the code in `contact-summary-extras.js`, the card gets updated if the value of corresponding immunization key is set to `yes` in the document. i.e. https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/be2fb83b4df072fcbeaa1b1688c307d8b9f31923/config/standard/contact-summary-extras.js#L249 But the document created in couchdb corresponding to an immunization form submission has values `Yes/No`, hence the check `vaccines_received['received_' + dose[0]] === 'yes';` fails and the card is not updated. To patch this issue, the code can be updated as [vaccines_received['received_' + dose[0]].toLowerCase() === 'yes';](https://github.com/medic/medic/pull/5615/files/9bff39a83f0f1630075f7e492fcf1dfbd7c50c8f#diff-084981c49a350848a9d6eecd777a9d23 ) but it does not answer the question that why the immunization report created in couchdb have values `Yes/No` instead of `yes/no` as set in the [Immunization Form](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/config/standard/forms/collect/c_imm.xlsx).

Investigation

The value `yes/no` is getting translated according to the translation key in the translation file (message-en.properties, message-ne.properties etc.). If translation file has entry of `yes=Yes` and `no=No`, then the `translationCache` gets set correspondingly in `config.js`: https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/be2fb83b4df072fcbeaa1b1688c307d8b9f31923/api/src/config.js#L81-L92 And then, when the immunization collect form submission is parsed with [smsparser](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/api/src/services/report/smsparser.js#L174) it returns `Yes` and `No` as the translated value of `yes` and `no`, and the same is set in the couchdb document. https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/be2fb83b4df072fcbeaa1b1688c307d8b9f31923/api/src/services/report/smsparser.js#L159-L178

Resolution

There could be multiple ways to resolve this: 1. Change `yes=Yes` to `yes=yes` and `no=No` to `no=no` in all the [translation files](https://github.com/medic/medic/tree/master/config/standard/translations). 2. Do not translate the `value of string` while parsing i.e. change `return config.translate(raw);` to `return raw;`. https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/be2fb83b4df072fcbeaa1b1688c307d8b9f31923/api/src/services/report/smsparser.js#L178 3. Find out what can be changed in `config.js` https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/be2fb83b4df072fcbeaa1b1688c307d8b9f31923/api/src/config.js#L119-L122 Please let me know your views on resolution of this issue. @abbyad @medic/development-team

1. Install the POE script following the instructions in [the README](https://github.com/medic/medic/tree/master/scripts/poe)
2. Go to `/ddocs/medic/_attachments/translations`
3. Run `poe export .`
4. See a bunch of errors, eg:

```
FAILURE: messages-loz.properties: Translation key messages.v.report_accepted on line 752 has placeholders that do not match those of messages-en.properties
FAILURE: messages-ne.properties: Translation key contact.primary_contact_name on line 426 has placeholders that do not match those of messages-en.properties
FAILURE: messages-es.properties: Translation key contact.primary_contact_name on line 426 has placeholders that do not match those of messages-en.properties
```

**Expected behavior**
It should only error when the placeholder is actually invalid. 

**Environment**
- Instance: localhost
- Client platform: Ubuntu
- App: webapp script
- Version: master

**Additional context**
The workaround is to ignore the errors - the script still does the export and the files can be committed regardless.

**Fix**

Examples of false negatives:

- Not using a placeholder that the reference language (English) uses - it may make sense in some languages to omit a placeholder altogether and this is valid.
- Using a placeholder multiple times or in a different order than the reference language does.
- Using a placeholder that does work but isn't used in the reference language.

We need to build a list of valid placeholders. Currently that list is only what is provided in the English translation, but that's incomplete. I think we need to include some sort of allow list of placeholders which are valid even if they're not included in the English translation.

title: Incorrect XLSForm meta data values in Enketo
body:
In XLSForm there are [keywords for meta data](http://xlsform.org/en/#metadata), some of which are relevant and available in our app with Enketo. Of those some provide incorrect values, such as `start` and `end` which always give midnight GMT for the given day. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Upload the [`meta` form](https://github.com/medic/medic/files/3340296/meta.zip)
2. Open the `meta` form
3. See the incorrect values as notes
4. Submit the form and see the same incorrect values being saved

**Expected behavior**
The `start` and `end` values should have the time included with the date.

To maintain consistency with XLSForm it would be nice to also have the user's `phonenumber`, `username`, `email`. That said, those fields are less relevant in our context, and are available via `inputs` as a workaround.

**Screenshots**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/789512/60361615-ae58f180-99ac-11e9-82bd-fc802f051be0.png)

```json
  "fields": {
    "start": "2019-06-27T20:00:00.000-04:00",
    "end": "2019-06-27T20:00:00.000-04:00",
    "today": "2019-06-27",
    "deviceid": "deviceid not found",
    "subscriberid": "subscriberid not found",
    "simserial": "simserial not found",
    "phonenumber": "phonenumber not found",
    "username": "username not found",
    "email": "email not found",
    "n": "",
    "meta": {
      "instanceID": "uuid:f31d64b7-19ba-43c1-8e34-657c050c81a3"
    },
    "deprecatedID": ""
  },
```

**Environment**
- Instance: gamma.dev.medicmobile.org
- Browser: Chrome
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.6 (pre-release), also tested on 2.18

**Additional context**
Being consistent with XLSForm keywords makes it easier for partners to build their own forms. In this case, a partner wanted to track the `start` and `end` time to see how long it takes users to complete a form. Alternatively, the `once(now())` could have been used to get the start time, but that would be a bit of a hack and we don't yet support `once()`. Also, having ODK events and actions (https://github.com/enketo/enketo/issues/300) could eventually be used for this as well, but doesn't fully override the need for supporting the XLSForm meta fields.

Also, this issue highlights the need to document differences with XLSForm and ODK XForm standards. If updating [the documentation](https://github.com/medic/medic-docs/blob/master/configuration/forms.md#custom-xpath-functions) is not covered in this issue we should create a new one for that.

title: Contact controller should load children/reports in parallel
body:
# Description

This is a minor perf improvement for how we load contacts. Prior to the redux refactor, the ContactViewModelGenerator handled this in parallel with the logic in the ContactsController. Now the ContractsController handles loading this in parallel.


Before | After
-- | --
1286 | 1139
1196 | 1150
1287 | 1143
1150 | 1078
1143 | 1113
  |  
1212.4 | 1124.6

#5755 

I've also never worked with redux + angular together before. I'm attempting to clean up a few things, but if I'm breaking any patterns here, please let me know. 

I personally find performance investigations quite difficult in our product. Part of this, is because profiles are hard to read on AngularJS. Another part is that many layers of the code (services, controllers, actions, shared-libs) can all query the database. I have worked on products previously that had the concept of a "data access layer" (or Repository Pattern), where only one specific layer is allowed to fetch data from the database. This refactoring makes it so at least actions are not querying the database. @rmhowe I'm wondering what you think of this suggestion?

Also, we previously had two actions which we would almost never call separately. One to say we are loading a contact's children, and one to say we are loading a contact's reports. My understanding of actions is that they should be mapped from interactions with the UI - and so it should be safe to combine these.

title: Show a prompt when we detect the user is logged out
body:
In 3.6.0 we implemented a [feature](https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/3919) to detect if the user's session has expired and redirect them to the login page. This cleans up a bunch of issues where the app started behaving strangely with no notification. As @dianabarsan [noted](https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/3919#issuecomment-503955033)...

> Every type of automatic (background) replication will redirect any type of user to the login page without warning and without being triggered by the user interacting with the app. If it's not too difficult, I think it would be much less intrusive to show a popup that informs the user that they have been logged out - similar to the one we use to prompt users to refresh once the app is updated.

Improve the current handling by showing a popup with an appropriate warning.

1. If the user chooses to login, redirect to the login page.
2. If the user cancels out of the popup, then show it again in some time (roughly 5 minutes?).
3. If the user doesn't interact with the popup at all for one minute then assume they've stepped away from the keyboard and not currently in the middle of a task and redirect them to the login page.

title: Make it easier to identify at risk individuals in the app
body:
We learned from CHWs in the PA pilot that they cannot easily see who their high risk patients are in the app. In fact, most told us that the only way you could know who was high risk was to wait for them to appear in the tasks tab. 

Currently, we have the patient profile configured to show an individual's risk status and display an icon (shield) if they are high risk. However you have to be on the individuals profile directly to see this, it is not visible anywhere else in the hierarchy. 

Some ideas: 
- Show the shield icon next to the individuals name in the people list in the household profile. 
- Show the shield icon next to the household that contains a high risk individual in the list of households
- Show a target that has a count of current high risk individuals
* recommend some design work to explore these (and other) options

title: Make it clear that tasks can be completed anywhere in the window, not just on the due date
body:
Through design feedback sessions with CHWs in the PA pilot, we learned that they believe tasks could only be completed on their actual due date, not before, and not after.  This was consistent across almost all CHWs we interacted with. CHWs expressed that if they were at a household and noticed that there was a task due for another member of the household the next day, that they would come back the next day to complete that task, rather than completing it in the same visit. 

This has the potential to be a huge time/resource drain for CHWs and likely contributes to observed low task completion. 

The "due date" language seemed to be particularly confusing.

title: Muso's mRDT supervisor tasks cannot resolve
body:
For Muso's mRDT supervisor workflows:
* A CHW creates a report with `needs_signoff: true` for patient C.
* Supervisor A logs in with replication depth 1. The report replicates to their phone only because of `needs_signoff`. They can review/approve the report.
* A task triggers action from Supervisor A. Clicking the task makes a second report indicating the supervisor has followed up.

**Expected Behaviour**
The action of the task should be able to resolve the task.

**Observed Behaviour**
The logic controlling tasks is scoped to only access data for one contact at a time. Therefore the report which is created must be assigned with a `patient_id` which is equal to the owner of the original report (patient C). 

Because of the replication depth, patient C is not present on the device and the app crashes when building a ContactSummary. The user sees no error (only an infinite spinner), but does this appears in the console:

```
Error: Document not found: cb547802-75f6-48ef-bce0-0a28539789d0
    at lineage-model-generator.js:26
```

**Second Problem**
If the follow-up report were to be properly associated with Patient C, the task would still be impossible to resolve. This is because reports associated with contacts which are not on the device are not grouped under the same contact (even though the associated contact id is the same) - each report is given a new unique anonymous contact, so they are never in scope at the same time for the task logic.




More details about these scenarios and other issues contained in: https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/6519 and https://github.com/medic/medic-conf/issues/205

title: Allow mRDT Supervisor Tasks to resolve based on multiple needs_signoff reports
body:
# Description

Because of replication depth, the `contact_id` for a task's action may not be present on the device. This change makes it so enketo does a "best effort" to inject contact data when none is present, instead of throwing when building a ContactSummary.

Reports associated with contacts which are not on the device are not grouped under the same contact even when the associated contact id is the same. This updates RulesEngine to group reports by contact id in such cases.

title: Warn offline users before replicating too many docs
body:
# Description

Adds `/api/v1/users-info` endpoint which 
- returns the number of docs a user will replicate and a `warn` flag if this number exceeds the recommended limit. 
- when queried as an offline user, returns the requester doc count.
- when queried as an online user, requires `facility_id` and `role` params, plus an optional `contact_id` param (either GET or POST). 
- is queried as a new step in `webapp` bootstrapper. When resulting `warn` flag is truthy, the user has to confirm to actually continue bootstrapping and start replication. Cancelling redirects to login.
- is queried as a new step in `admin` user creation/updating. When resulting `warn` flag is truthy, a warning message is displayed. The admin would need to click on "Submit" the 2nd time to actually create or update the user document. 

Once an hour, API will log warnings of users that have replicated more than 10 000 docs. 
Updates `webapp` bootstrapper to display correct doc count progression, even when interrupted. 

medic/medic#5362
