title: Make replication _bulk_docs requests quicker
body:
Similarly to https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/5759, the current implementation of `_bulk_docs` filtering for offline users makes use of getting all the allowed doc ids in order to determine whether the user is allowed to edit an existent doc. 
For large users, getting the allowed doc ids can be quite time consuming. 
Instead of getting all allowed ids, we can do an `_all_docs` to get all existent docs that the user is trying to update and run the view map functions over the results in order to filter the allowed ones.

title: Display page tab text labels even on mobile view, whenever there are 3 or fewer tabs
body:
It is hard for users to know which page of the app they are on when their only clue is an icon. Icons can sometimes be ambiguous, and trying to remember their meaning increases cognitive load. We already display page text labels on desktop views, but on small mobile devices the labels disappear (and the vast majority of our users access the app via phones).

We should tweak our design so that we can display page tab text labels even on small mobile views, whenever there are 3 or less tabs. This would add text labels for most CHW views, since most CHWs only see 3 tabs. Users with 4 or more tabs accessing via a small mobile device will still have too many tabs to display text labels, so they will continue to see icons only. 

To accomplish this with our current fontawesome nav icons, slightly decrease the size of the icons, move them up a few pixels, and slightly increase the height of the black mobile header bar to 60px. Text, if displayed, is 12px.
![Header with labels](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/61237083-7bbe3100-a6ee-11e9-9092-27d02be835e4.png)


To accomplish this with our new icons, as implemented in #5535, keep the icons at their standard 24 x 24 size, move them up a few pixels, and slightly increase the height of the black mobile header bar to 60px. Text, if displayed, is 12px.
![Header with labels Copy](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/61237086-7fea4e80-a6ee-11e9-8f7b-dc28335ea74e.png)

title: Ability to configure SMS sending to other contacts that aren't the primary contact
body:
**EDIT** The description below is outdated, see this comment: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5817#issuecomment-607838321

---

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
As it is now we do not have a way of sending an sms to anyone else other than `reporting_unit`, `parent`, `grandparent` or a phone number (either hard-coded in the config or as a field in the report) in SMS reporting configuration. 

User story:
> A supervisor who is in an area above a CHV area in the hierarchy needs to get a notification when the CHV submits a report. The supervisor is not the primary contact of the area.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
1) Ability to broadcast an SMS nottification to everyone at a level (levels being: `parent`, `grandparent`, et al).
2) Ability to send an SMS notification to someone who is not the primary contact of their place.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
There exists the option for the user to type in the phone number when sending in a report but that is just not user friendly.  

**Additional context**
Discussed this a bit with @SCdF and this is a probable way to approach (2) above:
_In addition to existing ways of specifying the recipient, add another option that uses a JSON path that resolves to a UUID or shortcode, which is used to pull a contact, where we will look for their phone number in the same places that we'd look for the hard-coded relationships above (`reporting_unit`, `parent` ...)_

Also came across #333 & #427 and while they seem related, they don't seem to address this particular problem.

title: Make it possible to "include" or "chain" a form
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
There are situations where I would like to use a form while I am in another form, e.g. register a child when I'm in the first PNC visit, or calling a form like poverty assessment, or person or household-related survey while I am already in a visit.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
When defining a form, I would like to be able to include or chain the form instead of creating an additional document when submitting. That way, updates to the original form would not need to be redone in forms that create the same document type as additional document.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
At the moment I could trigger a task or train the user to find the person and manually call up the phone.

what these dates should be, as they are now actually when the writes happen not
when sentinel notices they happen. 

Apart from being just "more correct", this fixes a few edge cases:
 - if sentinel is down for whatever reason these dates stay accurate
 - if sentinel touches a legacy document created before infodoc dates it doesn't
   incorrectly update its initial_replicaiton_date to now
 - it removes our quick fix where we presume that a document is only new if its
   rev is 1 or undefined, which will not be true if a CHW creates and then edits
   a data_record while offline.

title: Timestamp on image vs data is slightly different when capturing mrdt image.
Moving contacts doesn't update the contact who will receive scheduled messages when no patient_id is set.
body:
**Describe the bug**
We introduced the option to move contacts to new parents in medic-conf. When a report is missing the `fields.patient_id` the doc won't update correctly to the new parent. This causes the scheduled messages to be sent to the previous contact who submitted the report originally. This would need to be updated so that it send to the correct contact under the new parent. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. As an offline user. Go offline
2. Create a new female patient with standard config
3. Process a new pregnancy(this report should have no `fields.patient_id` because it is offline and sentinel hasn't given the patient_id)
4. Go online and sync.
5. Move the newly created patient to a new parent. 
6. Review the scheduled messages

**Expected behavior**
The scheduled messages should be updated to the new correct contact so when they are sent it is sent to the correct person. They currently will send to the original reporter. 

**Environment**
- Instance: gamma.dev
- Browser: chrome
- Client platform: linux
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.6.0

**Additional context**
From @dianabarsan 

> When hydrating a single doc (with fetchHydratedDoc) we end up with the fully hydrated patient lineage, including the primary contacts of the parents, but when fetching in bulk (with hydrateDocs) we end up with minified patient primary contacts lineage, which is required to map patient clinic correctly. The bulk hydration is used when scheduled messages are generated

title: Outbound tasks fail if one of the task documents is deleted
body:
If you create a data_record that creates an outbound task, and then you delete the data_record before the task is sent, it crashes the outbound scheduler and no tasks are sent.

This is happening here: https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/sentinel/src/schedule/outbound.js#L33

We don't filter out results that have no docs, which means null array elements are passed to `hydrateDocs`.

We should correctly detect tasks for deleted documents and delete the associated tasks.

Workaround script to do this manually incoming.

title: Lazy load unread count to reduce visible load time
body:
During our bootstrap process, we spend a lot of time building six mapreduce indexes. Two of these are indexes used by `webapp/src/js/services/unread-records.js`: 

* `medic-client/data_records_by_type` is used to count the total number of reports and the number of messages
* `medic-user/read` is used to count the number of reports read by the logged in user

This count yields a red bubble over the tab. 

![Screenshot from 2019-08-01 00-38-00](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9014751/62274498-d9dc5b00-b3f4-11e9-8d7b-9749e7262090.png)

This decorative data isn't required before first render. Although we don't explicitly wait for it to complete before first render, it likely slows down startup performance by competing for resources in parallel with our critical path (building the other four indexes). 

This seems like an excellent candidate for lazy loading after the bootstrapping is completed.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

**Describe the solution you'd like**

title: Reports with errors trigger tasks when created/modified but not on reload
body:
**Describe the bug**
If a new report with errors is created or an existing report with errors is modified, that report is passed into the RulesEngine and can trigger a task or a target. When the webapp is reloaded, that report is not passed into the RulesEngine and different tasks/targets will appear.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Clean webapp
1. Update a task in config to log the contact/reports which get passed into partner code. 
1. Create a new report with errors (eg. `await PouchDB('medic-user-ac1').put({ _id: 'test_report', patient_id: 'c8314e6b-8ac6-5a5a-b959-6f58cc015cfe',  type: 'data_record', form: 'test', errors: ['error'] })`)
1. You will see that this report is passed into the partner task/target code.
1. Reload the page
1. You will see that this report is not passed into the partner task/target code.

**Expected behavior**
Tasks and targets should be the same before and after a reload. We apply the same filters to reports on startup as we do when reports are created/modified.

**Performance Impacts**
In `RulesEngine.js` we have this line: [Search('reports', { valid: true }, options),](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/webapp/src/js/services/rules-engine.js#L226) which filters the reports to only valid reports.  This filter causes the `medic-client/reports_by_validity` index to be built, which can take a long time during bootstrap. If we queried all reports instead of valid reports, this bug would be fixed and application startup times would improve.

title: MoH Nepal erred reports vs. messages
body:
### Context
Currently, SMSes sent by FCHVs are divided into two webapp tabs:

1. Reports
     - Valid reports — accepted
     - **Invalid (erred) reports — a report-specific error message** is sent with an example of the correct syntax for the type of report that the FCHV was attempting to send, as well as other information pertaining to the specific error that was made

2. Messages
     - **All messages — a generic reply message** is sent, indicating that we have received their SMS, but if they were trying to send a report, they should check the format and resend

**“Invalid Report” - further detail**
If an FCHV sends an SMS such as [form code_space_non-existent ID number], or [form code_space_omission or mistake in required syntax] the SMS is categorized as an “invalid report” in the reports tab. The system recognizes which report the FCHV was attempting to send by the [form code_space], and replies with a report-specific error message, including an example of the correct syntax for that type of report, and any other information to help correct the error that was made ("99999 ID has not been registered, please confirm the ID and resend the form")

**“Message” - further detail**
In the case, however, that the FCHV sends an SMS starting with [form code_no space], the system will categorize the report as a “message” in the messages tab. After receiving any type of “message”, the system sends a generic reply, indicating that if the FCHV was attempting to send a report, it was not recognized, and to check the format and try again. This response does not outline correct syntax or point to other specific errors, as it does not recognize which form the FCHV was attempting to send.


### Feature Requirement

As an FCHV, when I make a mistake in my report, I want to be able to know both that it was a mistake, and how I can correct it, so that I can accurately report on my patient as well as improve my own skills using the mHealth tool.

As a Medic teammate, I want to be able to distinguish form codes followed by no space (a report error) from a free-form message that an FCHV sends through the mHealth tool (text communication) so that I can...
- have an accurate count of, and can therefore analyze, error rates
- have an accurate count of, and can therefore analyze, other indicators pertaining to engagement, performance, and timeliness
- easily sort through SMSes intended as messages to understand what FCHVs are communicating via text (rather than through reports)


### Unmet need or opportunity 

Unmet need: in the webapp and analytics, we currently only capture and categorize certain types of SMS errors, as errors. Therefore, we cannot understand the full extent to which FCHVs are making errors in reports versus sending text messages to communicate.
Missed opportunity: to help FCHVs to correct and learn from their minor mistakes.

**Impact of this “pain” for developers, patients, providers, managers, etc.?**
Analytics data is not entirely accurate (an issue for **Medic**, as well as for **managers** and **health coordinators** as they gain access to external dashboards); this could misguide greater programmatic decisions. **FCHVs** may feel confused or be mislead by receiving clear feedback on certain types of errors, but not others; this could lead to future inaccuracies, missed reporting, and/or a feeling of discouragement.


### Proposed solution

**Describe how you would like to solve the “pain” that you identified:**

- Categorize any SMS starting with [form code_no space_number], as an “invalid report” rather than a “message”, generating the correct report-specific error message, thereafter
- Categorize any SMS starting with several characters linked together as a "message", except for the following characters: **जघद, जघ, जस, जश, जष, जसद, जशद, जषद,** as these are potential report attempts for delivery (if an FCHV forgot to put a space between the form code and the delivery type)

OR

- Categorize any SMS starting with [form code_no space_a character or number], as an “invalid report” rather than a “message”, generating the correct report-specific error message thereafter. This potential solution may, however, capture many SMSes intended to be "messages", as "invalid reports"
 
**Examples of the future fix:**
A 25 Sarita (अ 25 सरिता) = valid report
A Sarita 25 (अ सरिता 25) = invalid report, triggers error message
**P25 Sarita (अ25 सरिता) = invalid report, triggers form-specific error message (proposed change)
JSD 35105 3 (जघद 35105 3) = invalid report, triggers form-sepcific error message (proposed change)**
Baby 25 Sarita (बच्चा 25 Sarita) = message
Sarita is having a baby! = message



### Example use case for this feature

All use cases in Nepal MoH deployments


**Provide an example of the solution value in terms of the “pain” it will alleviate using a real-world application:**

**FCHV Rama** is trying to register Sarita’s pregnancy. She makes an error in her form by forgetting to put the space between the form code and Sarita’s age. She receives a report-specific error message in reply, telling her that there was an error, and that if she wants to register a woman’s pregnancy, to please try again using this format: [अ age name]. Rama tries again, successfully registers Sarita’s pregnancy, and learns from her mistake.

**Municipality Health Coordinator Mina** has an accurate view of the FCHV error  and engagement rates of each HF in her municipality, and can therefore make an informed decision about where to prioritize refresher trainings.

**Service Designer Danielle** has access to accurate data about the most frequently erred reports, in order to inform the redesign of form structures and syntax.


### Links to supporting information

[Nepal MoH Basic Messaging Deep-Dive](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ktjIdcjpqeR76qrmtKaEN68J53c6T4VCZRlUR-eXGGE/edit#gid=0) - a look into SMSes received to understand what FCHVs are communicating via message, and how many “messages” are actually erred reports

title: Server side purge
body:
# Description

Adds serverside pseudo purge which runs on a schedule and executes a configurable "purge" function over all docs that would be replicated. "Purged" docs are added in auxiliary databases - one for every unique user roles group.
During offline user replication (both initial and subsequent), only docs that are not tagged as "purged" are downloaded. On a schedule, on application bootstrap, the webapp will check if new documents were "purged" and delete them from the device.

medic/medic#5443

# Long description

Executes a pseudo server-side purge which:
- runs on a configurable schedule
- computes a list of unique role groups from all existent users, each unique role group purges being saved in a separate database
- compiles groups consisting of: a contact, reports _about_ the contact, messages that the contact has sent or received
- over each doc group and for each role group, runs a configurable purge function which accepts the group + the roles as parameters and is expected to return an array of doc_ids which should be purged
- queries the purge dbs and compare the resulting list of purged ids compared to the existent purged docs and saves the differences (deleting old purges or by adding new)
- a doc is purged for a list of roles if a document with the same id, prefixed with `purge:`, exists in the corresponding purge database (eg. `purge:this_is_my_doc_id`)

When performing an initial replication:
- users will only download changes for docs that are not purged for their role set 
- the list of purged doc ids is cached for 5 minutes (with refreshed ttl)
- after initial replication, webapp calls an api endpoint which will create a "checkpointer" doc in the corresponding purge db that saves the current `update_seq`

When performing any replication:
- users will only download changes od docs that are not purged for their role set

On bootstrap, every 7 days or configurable via `purge: run_every_days` or when user roles change: 
- webapp calls an api endpoint which will query _changes from the corresponding purge db from the seq saved in the checkpointer doc
- the endpoint returns a list of new purged doc ids and the a seq of the purge db
- webapp deletes the docs locally, also marking them as purged
- webapp queries an api endpoint that updates the purge checkpointer doc using the seq received in the previous response

title: Make it easier to complete all tasks at a household in the same visit
body:
Relates to #5776 (make it clear that tasks can be completed anywhere in the window). Assumes that #5697 and #5710 have already been completed (updating hierarchy levels, adding belongs to breadcrumbs to tasks). 

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Some CHWs have a hard time navigating the tasks page when it is organized by due date. What we have heard is that they would find it more useful to have the tasks organized by area or household, so that they can prioritize other tasks nearby. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
1. Add the ability to group tasks together by family, and then sort those grouped families by nearest due date. This means that tasks for the same family will always appear next to each other, but the family groupings will not be sorted alphabetically but instead by due date.

Referring to this mockup:
![Screen Shot 2019-08-12 at 3 46 36 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/62903753-a238b180-bd18-11e9-8b0a-ca911ec3a099.png)

- The first two tasks are in the Beatrice Bass Family group. Because there is a task due today, this group (the Beatrice Bass Family group) is first.
- There is only one task for the Zelda Zed family. It comes next because the task is due in 1 day.
- The last two tasks are for Amanda Allen’s family. Even though this family would alphabetically go first, the group comes last because there aren’t any tasks due for at least 2 days.
- Note: The horizontal lines separating family groups are just for mockup purposes, no intended UI update.


2. Add a sort icon to the top tasks bar which gives users the choice to either filter "By date" or "By family". Also, I recommend that we change the default sort so that we sort "By family" by default.

![Screen Shot 2019-08-12 at 3 49 39 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/62903821-da3ff480-bd18-11e9-8e4e-1838fc518d47.png)


**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Considered a true alphabetical sort of tasks by family name, but this isn't as helpful, since it might put a task due in 2 weeks for Amanda Allen's family at the very top of the list.

title: Offline users download all their previous feedback docs
body:
**Describe the bug**
When a user is setup on a new device, they download all docs from their meta-db. Previously, the meta-db only contained `read` docs, which are relevant to the user, so the replication is not filtered. However, since https://github.com/medic/medic/commit/a0c57b1908f7b14dbcf008d0f84564d00fb1ff70 , users also store their `feedback` docs in the meta DB, which will also be downloaded when users setup a new device. These docs occupy storage space without being of any use whatsoever. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Login as an offline user and create a feedback doc (you can do this from the hamburger menu -> Report bug). 
2. Refresh the page to trigger meta db sync. 
3. Wipe device data and login with the same user. Wait until all networking is finished. 
4. Check your local meta db and observe that you have downloaded the feedback doc you created before. 

**Environment**
- Instance: any 3.5 + instance
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.5+

title: Users in projects have multiple configured roles
body:
When configurable roles (https://github.com/medic/medic/commit/a64d241d9f408786c9797b3d15d156ff1eecf65a) were implemented, the intention was to transition away from users having multiple assigned configured roles to just one role. 

>The user doc in the _users db and the user-settings doc in the medic database both
have an array of roles as this is consistent with CouchDB, but the configuration UI has a
dropdown so in practice users will have an array of length 1.

However, in practice, in projects that are up to date, users are created and updated (via the API endpoint or directly in CouchDB) to have multiple roles. 
For example, a user recently edited in an up to date project has the following roles:

`district-manager`, `kujua_user`, `data_entry`, `supervisor`, `mrdt`, `supervisor_mrdt`

With the configured roles being: national_admin, district_admin, **data_entry**, analytics, gateway, chw_uhc, **supervisor**, **supervisor_mrdt**, **mrdt**, mrdt_2, pm. 

If this is the direction that projects are going, we should probably update the admin UI to support this.

title: Cluster safe credentials
body:
With SIH and AT we use a special section of the couchdb node configuration called `medic-credentials` to store secrets such as passwords and API keys. This works well in that couchdb protects this so only admins can access it, however it's node specific so if we decide to have multiple couchdb nodes it will have to be separately configured in each node. With a greater focus on integrations and potentially plugins this concept will become more widely used so we should find a more future-proof way to store credentials.

The surest way to be cluster safe is to store the data in the database itself so work towards that. The issue then becomes how to secure the data so only admins can access it, for example, make sure it doesn't accidentally get replicated to the client or couch2pged into postgres.

title: Consider adding static analysis of css
body:
Just like we use eslint for javascript static analysis we should investigate using css linting tools, for example [lesshint](https://github.com/lesshint/lesshint). In particular rules like not using `!important` should be enforced. Ideally the `less` files would be linted before compilation to css to make fixing issues easier.

If the tool is found to be useful, integrate it into our build chain, decide which rules to enable/disable, and fix any existing violations.

title: Make declarative config mandatory
body: This would be a breaking change but it's the strongly recommended configuration approach and would give us more flexibility for implementation changes in future.

title: Make IDBNext the only supported PouchDB storage adapter
body:
Given that we'll be forcing users to download everything again in 4.0 anyway it would make sense to use this opportunity to download everything into a brand new IDBNext database to benefit from the performance improvements at the same time. This would also potentially save us from having to write a IDB -> IDBNext migration.

Be careful that all data is synced from the device to the server before throwing away the old database.

title: Refactor TasksContent controller to use unique URLs for actions
body:
Currently tasks have one or more actions associated with them. Having multiple possible actions is an underused feature of tasks but it would be really useful for example if an ANC visit task could lead to a Delivery or a Visit report being filed to resolve it.

If you select a task with exactly one action then you go straight to completing that action. If there are multiple possible actions, _or_ the task has a detailed description (another underused feature) then you see a summary page and can select one of the actions.

Currently these both invoke the `$scope.performAction` function, but this requires a redux listener to detect when a task is selected. This is bad form.

Instead each action should have a unique URL (eg: `/tasks/:id/actions/:actionId`) which is handled by a new child controller. Put the `$scope.performAction` logic in the new controller. When selecting a task with only one action we can go straight to `/tasks/:id/actions/0`. When selecting a task with multiple actions use the existing TasksContent controller to render the detail and have each action button link to the new action URL.

title: Rename initial and latest replication date and change the format to a number
body:
These are currently called `initial_replication_date` and `latest_replication_date`, but what they really represent is the dates which the writes occurred (irrespective of whether any replication occurred).

They should be renamed to something more appropriate.

They are also currently stored really awkwardly, as a string that represents a date. We should normalise them with other date storage we do and store them as a unix timestamp (i.e. `date.getTime()`).

title: Updates to reminders
body:
# Description

Updates reminders to:

- Not update leaf (clinic) docs to add a task for every reminder. Instead, create docs with significant
ids for every reminder task. The id pattern for these docs is `reminder:<form>:<reminder_date>:<place_id>`. They also have a new type `reminder`, so no offline users will replicate them. They are visible in the admin message queue and picked up as "pending" messages by the outgoing SMS services. The uniquely deterministically id-ed docs also make it easy to check if a reminder doc already exists for a place for a specific reminder instance.

- Not depend on a specific view (`medic-sms/sent-reminders`) to determine whether a reminder instance has been sent, instead, after every successful reminder instance run creates a log doc stored in `medic-sentinel` (`reminderlog:<form>:<reminder_date>`) that can be checked by compiling the expected id from reminder config. 

- Not depend on having a specific transition (`update_sent_forms`) update leaf (clinic) docs to add a `sent_forms` property storing the last date a form, that has a corresponding `reminder` config, was created by the primary contact of the place. Instead, with a slight update, make use of an underused existent view (`medic/reports_by_form_and_parent`) to get this date value.

title: Fully hydrate patient lineages in LineageModelGenerator and Shared-lib/Lineage
body:
# Description

This is a fix to our lineage code which fixes the two user-facing bugs identified in #5824. 

1. The UI fails to correctly identify the contact which will receive a scheduled message (bug in LineageModelGenerator)
1. Sentinel actually fails to send the message to the correct contact (bug in the lineage shared library hydrateDocs)

These bugs are both due to code paths which hydrate documents incompletely.

### LineageModelGenerator

This service implements three hydration code path for specific document types (`report`, `contact`, and `reportSubjects`). These interfaces reuse some of the code from the lineage shared-lib, but the `report` interface has a different output than the shared-lib's `fetchHydratedDoc`/`hydrateDocs` interfaces (bug). In the long term, it is my opinion we should consolidated to one interface for hydrating documents `hydrate(thing, options)`. This change moves toward that end by removing one of the custom hydration code paths in the LineageModelGenerator.

In this change, I've refactored LineageModelGenerator.report to use shared-lib's fetchHydratedDoc. This has the following affects on that interface:

* The report is now fully hydrated (bug fix).
* The `merge` parameter (ala `LineageModelGenerator.report(id, { merge: false })`) is no longer supported. In our code, it was always true.
* Returns a model without a lineage attribute. I did a reasonable scan through the code paths and believe it to never be used.

### Lineage Shared-Lib 

* Improve separation of concerns by splitting into multiple files (hydration/minification)
* Non-functional ES6ification 
* Add `{ options }` parameter to the `fetchHydratedDoc` interface supporting `throwWhenMissingLineage` (default: false). This allows the change in LineageModelGenerator to maintain the failover behavior.
* Update hydrateDocs to properly hydrate the patient's parents and the patitent's parent's contacts.

### Performance Impacts

title: Provide a UI to perform testing tasks on the phone
body:
**Describe the issue**
There are some things that only engineers need to do when developing or testing something but shouldn't be easily accessible in the UI because they would confuse users or potentially be dangerous to use if you don't know what you're doing.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We should provide a hidden "developer console" to make these actions easy for our team to do. On Android Google has hidden these options behind multiple clicks on a particular image. Consider doing this with multiple touches of some element on the About page. Add a warning dialog before loading the page as we don't want anyone to accidentally find it.

On the page add buttons to:
- initiate a purge replication
- wipe all offline data (pouchdb, cookies, etc) and reload

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- We could force people to use a specific URL but that's hard to do in the android wrapper.
- We could expose functions that people could type in the browsers dev console but that's hard to do in the android wrapper.

title: Record test coverage
body:

We don't have an easy way to tell which code is well tested and which isn't, or if a change is reducing or improving coverage.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
1. Update our testing grunt tasks (karma, mocha, and if possible protractor) to produce a report of which lines of code are touched during testing. This report should be gitignored.
2. Publish the results somewhere (AWS?) during CI.
3. Find some way to diff the results between the branch and master so they can be compared when doing a code review.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None.

Don't spend more than two days on this. If it's too hard to do with our current stack then we can delay it until we redo our stack (after Angular 8). If you only get the first task done in the time allowed then get that merged and we can come back to the CI improvements later.

title: Replace underscore with lodash in replication
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
We're currently doing two calls to `underscore`'s `uniq` function in our replication code:
here: https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/api/src/services/authorization.js#L185
here: https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/api/src/services/authorization.js#L234

This is done because we might end up with duplicates when querying views that will result in multiple changes for a single doc (CouchDB will return a change as many times as it's id exists in the request list). 

Unfortunately, the implementation of `underscore`'s `uniq` (and likely other array functions) has very poor performance and is also resource blocking.
```
const _ = require('underscore');
const uuid = require('uuid');
_.uniq(Array.from({ length: 100000 }).map(() => uuid()));
```
This code snippet takes a whooping 39 seconds to execute on my machine. Granted this is an extreme case, but there have been misconfigured users that have this many docs. It would be nice to not block API sorting their allowed doc ids.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Straight up replacing `underscore` with `lodash` looks like a good solution.
```
const lodash = require('lodash');
const uuid = require('uuid');
lodash.uniq(Array.from({ length: 100000 }).map(() => uuid()));
```
This code snippet takes 0.39 seconds to execute. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Alternatively we could write our own array/object functions and put them into a shared lib. 

**To Reproduce**
Create a misconfigured offline user (to have a significant impact, have at least 50 000 docs). Login with that user and start replicating. 
In the same time, logged in as an online user, try to browse the app and observe if it's responsive or not. 

**Environment**
- App: api
- Version: 3.7

title: Replace underscore with lodash throughout our codebase
body:
**Describe the issue**
`underscore` is proving to be having very poor performance when working with large data sets.
See https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/5942, where running a `uniq` over 100,000 uuids takes more than 30 seconds, where such an operation should be well below half a second. 

Besides the offline user replication, we also deal with potentially large data sets in our `Search` library, which also uses `underscore` across the board to process arrays. Our `search` library runs both on devices and server-side. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
`lodash` is looking like a good, performant and compatible alternative (most used `underscore` functions exist in `lodash`, having same name and same accepted parameters - there are exceptions though, so it won't be a 100% effortless replacement).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Alternatively we could write our own array/object functions and put them into a shared lib.

title: Patches webdriver-manager and switches to Xenial

# Description

Fixes the two problems our Travis builds ran into:
1. Chrome releasing a new version and protractor's webdriver having a *hardcoded* maximum Chrome driver version:

title: Consolidate the document hydration code
body:
We should use the shared-lib/lineage library for hydrating documents. This is well unit tested, performance tuned, and has clearly defined behavior.

There are a few places in the code which hydrate documents in custom ways and with custom behaviors. We should

1. Consolidate all hydration code to use the shared-lib/lineage library
1. Internalize the `fillContactsInDocs`, `fillParentsInDocs`, and `fetchContacts` interfaces on the shared-lib to avoid code paths that perform these partial hydrations and increase the flexibility of code changes within the library
1. If necessary, add additional `options` to the public interfaces if there are legitimate hydration scenarios which we should support.

### LineageModelGenerator.contact()

This interface is used throughout the code and has some strange behavior. When `{ merge: true }`, it returns a mostly-hydrated doc and a fully hydrated lineage array. When `{ merge: false }`, it returns an unhydrated doc and a partially hydrated lineage in which contacts are hyrated but parents are not.  If this were cleaned up, we would be able to internalize both `fillContactsInDocs`, and `fetchContacts`.

Presumably the `{merge : false}` option was largely added for performance reasons. However, the gains seem negligible since the lineage it returns is hydrated (even if the document isn't). So, the lineage is still fetched from the database ...

### Uses of fillParentsInDocs

* admin/src/js/services/message-queue.js
* LineageModelGenerator.contact()

title: Login page dynamic elements don't work correctly
body:
**Describe the bug**
Because the login page is cached by the service worker, any code that gets run when that page gets rendered only gets run once, at the point that the device first visits the login page. You can see all this code in [`login.get`](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/api/src/controllers/login.js#L186).

This logic includes:
 - White labeling / branding
 - Translations
 - Redirection (though this appears to be additionally broken by other code as well)

It gets more complicated, because somehow regardless after you wipe the service worker to force it to call `login.get` again fresh, the *next* reload defaults the login page back to a vanilla version, e.g. with no redirect url (despite what you passed it) and English (despite what your language is set to).

**Reproduction steps**

(bonus, boot api with a debugger via `node --inspect server` etc and put a break point in `login.get` for extra details)

1. Successfully and completely log in to the application as any English-language user (I used a online user) into an environment with multiple languages
2. Change your user's language to something else (e.g. French)
3. Log out
   - Here you would **expect** the login page's language to be French, but you **observe** it's still English
   - (also note that `login.get` never ran)
4. Unregister the service worker, by (in Chrome) going to dev tools -> Application -> Service workers and clicking 'Unregister' for your URL
5. Refresh the login page
   - (notice now `login.get` runs)
   - Note that the login page is now in French
5. Refresh the login page **again**
   - (once again `login.get` doesn't get run)
   - Note now that the login page is **back to English**  

**Environment**
- Instance: Localhost running master
- Browser: Chromium 76
- Client platform: Linux
- Version: master

locally run e2e tests.

database.

CouchDB is left running under 4984 so you can inspect the DB if you wish. It
will get cleaned out on computer restart or on the next e2e call.

effectively running CouchDB out of a RAM drive.

the command line.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

title: Sort/Filter tasks by priority
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
CHVs often have many tasks to do and currently, the only way they can prioritize them is by due date sorting or by reading all of the tasks doing their own prioritization.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We already flag some tasks as high priority, and with predictive algorithms may be able to identify additional high priority tasks (e.g., important tasks unlikely to completed or tasks where we expect the patient to show danger signs). Similar to medic/cht-core#5886, we can help CHWs plan and prioritize their activities by one (or more) of the following:

- providing the ability to order tasks by priority
- providing the ability to order tasks by due date-weighted priority
- providing the ability to filter tasks by high priority

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Alternatives include the current mechanisms to flag a task as high priority and change its presentation to the user, including its icon and text. However, for a CHW with many tasks, this may not surface high priority tasks as easily as sorting or filtering would.

Another alternative is for urgent tasks (e.g., those where we expect danger signs) to use SMS or a dialog box upon opening the app to remind the CHW of the importance of the task. However, this may be overwhelming for a CHW if too many tasks are high priority.

**Additional context**
This is relevant as we consider expansion and scale-up of our predictive algorithms initiatives through recently launched data science partnerships. These partnerships would be looking to close out in mid-2020, with implementation possibly in late 2020.

title: Store PA risk scores in the patient
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, predictive algorithm risk scores are calculated in the app in both tasks and targets and in the contact summary. This creates duplication of code, is a potential source of technical debt, and leads to unnecessary computation.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A better implementation of risk scoring is to set a minimum refresh window (e.g., 1 day, 1 week, 1 month) and store the risk score and its calculation date in the patient to be accessible by tasks, targets, forms, and contact summary. Scores would then be recalculated only when the age of the risk score is greater than the minimum refresh window.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Risk scores loaded to the contact page from the server side are infeasible in an offline-first context where we cannot guarantee that they will reach the phone in time to be of use.

**Additional context**
Depending on the approach taken in our screening work with PIH, this may be useful for implementation in that project in April 2020.

This is also relevant as we consider expansion and scale-up of our predictive algorithms initiatives through recently launched data science partnerships. These partnerships would be looking to close out in mid-2020, with implementation possibly in late 2020.

title: Monthly summaries/training goals for supervisors
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
As we implement additional alerts/reminders/tasks/features for supervisors, we run the risk of information overload. With many CHWs to track and lots of information coming in about their performance, we may want to support them in summarizing and setting goals.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Generate a monthly report or summary for the supervisor at either the CHW (for 1:1 training) or supervisor (for group training) that identifies target areas for improvement (or congratulations). For example, a supervisor-level summary might look like:

- Everyone met their target for newborn visits within 72 hours!
- 10 CHWs are lagging in visiting every household at least once a month
- 3 CHWs received more than 150 tasks this month
- 4 CHWs made more than 2 duplicate reports this month

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None

**Additional context**
None

title: Note when outbound send happened on the report's info doc
body:
To aid in confirming that and when an outbound message was sent, we should note the event on the report's `-info` document. This is a good place because it's not going to trigger re-replication and is also available to analytics.

Currently we have logs that can be viewed using a log viewer or other, but it's a pain to search through those and would be much easier if it was available on the companion doc.

(if this sounds familiar it's because it was a feature that was discussed but missed in the original outbound design)

title: Alert when outbound pushes are repeatedly failing
body:
Currently if outbound pushes fail (e.g., the server they are sending to are offline) the sentinel log is updated with an error and the push is retried in 5 minutes.

This scales fine for a small amount of pushes, but will probably not scale to larger numbers of pushes.

Ideally if there is a failure we should be able to alert a responsible person about it.

title: Format data for sending to DHIS2
body:
https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/5661 introduces the ability to calculate data for sending to DHIS2. Prior to sending this data to DHIS2 (or downloading it as a file to be uploaded), we'll need to format it in a way that DHIS2 can process. The DHIS2 documentation related to these formats can be found [here](https://docs.dhis2.org/master/en/developer/html/webapi_data_values.html#).

While there are a number of different formats supported, here is an example payload to help illustrate a few points. 

~~~JSON
{
  "dataSet": "pBOMPrpg1QX",
  "completeDate": "2019-10-03",
  "period": "201909",
  "orgUnit": "DiszpKrYNg8",
  "dataValues": [
    { "dataElement": "f7n9E0hX8qk", "value": 21 },
    { "dataElement": "Ix2HsbDMLea", "value": 17 },
    { "dataElement": "eY5ehpbEsB7", "value": 14 }
  ]
}
~~~

A `dataSet` is essentially a grouping of `dataElements` for the purposes of data entry. In Kenya, the **MoH 515 CHEW Summary** is an example of a `dataSet`, and the core dimensions that describe data in DHIS2 are as follows (*All data values will at a minimum have these 3 dimensions*):

- The **where** : *organisation unit* (ex. Bondo CHU)
- The **what** : *data element* (ex. Total Deliveries)
- The **when** : *period* (ex. September 2019)

Data can also be disaggregated further using `categoryOption` and `categoryOptionCombo`.  The diagram below attempts to illustrate the relationship between all these dimensions.

So for each of the calculations we define in https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/5661 , at a minimum we'll need to map to a `dataElement`, and possibly a `categoryOptionCombo` as well.

![DHIS2 Data Set Hierarchy](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10096985/66392678-4b85e600-e9f0-11e9-8d88-db7465b0370d.jpg)

title: Timeout option is not set during replication
body:
**Describe the bug**
During initial replication, the `timeout` option to PouchDB is [set to 10 minutes](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/webapp/src/js/bootstrapper/index.js#L103).  During routine replications, the `timeout` option is [not set](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/webapp/src/js/services/db-sync.js#L52) and uses PouchDB's default.

**Expected behavior**
The two replications should have matching timeouts.

**Additional context**
We should make this change in 3.8 along-side the features around writing tasks to disk since that feature is expected to increase the document count which will increase the time spent in _changes requests.

title: The outbound error response logging is needlessly verbose
body:
When the outbound scheduler attempts to send a payload over the network and something goes wrong (e.g. the target server 500s) we log out the entire error response:

https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/sentinel/src/schedule/outbound.js#L260
```js
    logger.error(`Failed to push ${medicDoc._id} to ${key}: %o`, err);
```

While this is delightfully general purpose (and this code path is used for all errors in that flow), the default output for responses is really massive and contains a bunch of unnecessary information that makes logs really hard to read.

We should reduce the amount of logging we do in that case, probably down to just the statuscode and response payload (if it exists), and if there is no statuscode because of some other problem (eg timeout) we just log that message and not the entire response object.

title: Outbound can halt scheduler execution permanently
body:
**Describe the bug**
We have noticed (cc. @senseibara) instances where the outbound push scheduled task appears to freeze, in one case a week before we restarted sentinel. This doesn't kill Sentinel completely, instead somehow the outbound promise chain never resolves (or rejects), which causes the scheduler to not progress, which also means nothing ever gets rescheduled.

No reproduction steps right now, it happened once once and there wasn't any interesting log output. Restarting sentinel pushed it forward (it processed 20 documents and then froze again, restarting it once more processed the last dozen or so).

The only two guesses I have are:
 - There is an instance where we haven't coded the flow right and we're breaking the promise chain (e.g. we manually create a promise because we're mixing in callbacks, and `resolve()` or `reject()` never get called)
 - Some piece of I/O that we're doing doesn't have a default timeout configured and is blocking indefinitely

title: Enable default config transitions in e2e tests
body:
**Describe the issue**
The default config was updated to enable two transitions: `generate_patient_id_on_people` and `death_reporting`. 
We also recently started using the default config when running our e2e tests suite. Having _any_ enabled transitions (especially `generate_patient_id_on_people`  which updates every contact doc uploaded) can cause our e2e tests to fail in unexpected ways. 
To release `3.7`, the quick solution is to remove transitions from the config before uploading when running e2e tests. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We should update the existent tests setup or assertions so they execute successfully using the default config.

title: Make sure app versions are always in sync
body:
**Describe the issue**
We display app versions in two places with two different sources
1. The logo tooltip is set using an Angular constant which is set when Grunt builds the app by pulling it out of the package.json.
2. In the About page which pulls it from the deploy_info on the local medic-client ddoc. This only exists for tagged releases and falls back to the package.json version for development builds, alpha releases, etc.

Updating the package.json is a documented step of the release process but it's easy to miss, which leads to [last minute bugs](https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/6048).

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
I can see two possible solutions...
1. Add a test or build time check which fails the build when a tag is created that doesn't match the package.json version, but that'll fail late in the process.
2. Set the package.json version to 1.0.0 permanently and show "unknown" for the version for non-tagged releases. This cleans up the code a little, removes a step from release management, and means the version will always be correct (unless unknown).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Nagging people constantly...

title: Add feature to format place IDs differently from person IDs
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
This is related to #5614. Conversation continued from the thread there. 

**Why consider?**

* CHWs or other users who would require an SMS based option for registering places are likely to have low literacy levels. Ability to accurately keep track of similar looking IDs and knowing which belongs to who would likely be a challenge. 
* Even though CHWs receive the ID specifying its for a particular family, very few are technically savvy enough to save and refer back to the SMS and find the ID or confirm if they have any confusions when having to use the ID. Many CHWs save the IDs in a notebook organized in many ways — they might not always clearly categorize and mark IDs accurately and consistently. 
* Whenever CHWs make an error in a text form, error messages are always configured to prompt them of the error and are as specific as our product allows. However, an additional step means a high risk of the user dropping the workflow at that point. Moreover, the error message is not helpful if they are not able to figure out which the correct ID might be (given the user capacity issues listed above).

**If we were to consider a different ID format, these are some of the questions to answer:**

* With the place ID, would we have a generic prefix like P for any place or specific prefixes like F for family, CA for CHW Area etc. Different prefix for each type of place eg. F11235 for family ID vs CA1134 for CHW Area or a generic prefix for all places e.g. P11235. Would the goal be to only differentiate between places and people or people and different place types?
    * My sense is that just differentiating between people and places seems adequate considering majoring of SMS registrations of places would be at the family/household level. Usually users at the CHW area level or higher would have access to our app. 
* If we have a prefix to place IDs, it is harder technically to assure that the digit portion is unique. e.g. a CHW could have a person ID that is 11235 and a place ID that is P11235. This gets even more complicated if we have specific prefixes for each type of place. 
* Is entering letter then number more likely to cause errors? eg A9999 might get typed as A 9999
* What do we do for other languages w other scripts like Nepal? Do we need the prefix to be in their script?
    * Yes, most likely. All other non-digit components in a text form are in the local script in the case of Nepal. 
* The idea so far for a different format is to add a letter as a prefix e.g. P11123. Could there be other ways to differentiate that would mitigate some of the concerns highlighted above? 
    * I personally don’t have any ideas ATM but worth considering. 

**After discussion it was suggested that we could add this feature in a future iteration and have place ids follow the same pattern as patient ids for now. If we did so, a deployment that was previously using the same format for family ID and person ID will have challenges if the format changes.**
 
On the user side, 

* CHWs will have a mix of formats for old and new families which may be confusing to the user. This issue will be longstanding as families will continue to exist and hence the family IDs. A way to mitigate this would be have them re-register the families but that would mean that any historical data associated with the family will be lost. 

On the config side,
 
* You would have to validate a place ID for both formats. There will likely be validation message if a place doesn't exist, but the response would have to be generic, like make sure to use a valid place ID, instead of being able to give a more helpful message like Place IDs are formatted "PXXXXX".

On deployment (consider training) 

* Some user groups might require re-training which has cost implications.

These are some initial thoughts based on the insights I have. @leah-ngaari @samkanga please add once you have a chat on Monday. Your additional thoughts/verification would be much appreciated. 

cc @abbyad

title: Prevent associating multiple users to the same contact
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
User creation process - Seen in v3.4

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
As discussed in [this](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/is-it-ok-to-have-multiple-user-settings-associated-to-the-same-contact-id-facility-id-combo/489) thread on the forum, it's possible to have multiple mobile app users associated to the same contact.  This makes it impossible to know who actually submitted reports. 

When adding new users, consider validating what is entered in the "Associated Contact" field. If the contact that was selected already has an associated user, show an error message and prevent the creation of the new user. The error message should include the `User name` of the user _currently_ associated to the contact so that the person configuring this can update/delete the other user account if necessary. 

![Screen Shot 2019-10-28 at 8 00 04 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10096985/67734164-8d85c480-f9bd-11e9-8c5e-611e0a512f6b.png)

title: Add a timeout to outbound requests
body:
There have been instances where the outbound request handler has hung
completely in production. It's not clear from logging why this occured
and it's not consistent or repeatable, but a good potential option is
that requests to external servers are hanging.

This change adds an explicit timeout to the two outbound IO requests.

Depending on various factors there may already be an implicit timeout,
but this makes it explicit and much shorter (10 seconds).

title: Timeouts for /api/v1/users leave user at "loading app..." forever
body:
**Describe the bug**
If a request to /api/v1/users-info results in a 500 timeout response there is an error on the server, but the user is left in state "Loading app…" with no indication of failure.

**To Reproduce**

1. Navigate to webapp
1. Login as user with lots of documents
1. Spoof connection to server to result in a 500 response for the request to `/api/v1/users-info`

title: Reduce inbox.js bundle size to meet targets for 3.7 release (800kb)
body:
**Describe the bug**
If a module in the `shared-libs` folder has an npm dependency (for example `shared-libs/search` and `shared-libs/lineage` both require `underscore^1.9.1`). The webapp's bundled script inbox.js includes one copy of the library for each shared-lib with the dependency. So in this case, there are 3 copies of underscore^1.9.1 (one for search, one for lineage, and one for webapp).

However, this does not seem to reproduce for all dependencies.

**To Reproduce**
To measure the size of the minified script, run: `grunt build-js minify && ls -l ~/webapp/build/ddocs/medic/_attachments/js`

1. View the current size of the script for master (2968125).
1. Go into the source for `shared-libs/search` and replace `require('underscore')` with `{}`. This will allow the code to build, but it won't function.
1. Repeat this process for `shared-libs/lineage`

**Expected behavior**
This shouldn't significantly change the size of the inbox.js script. Only a few characters have changed. Underscore is required elsewhere, so it should still be included once and only once in the bundle.

**Observed behavior**
Script weight reduces significantly 18kb (18038) for each shared-lib. Total of 36kb for this example with underscore. 
I can reproduce this for lodash for ongoing work with tasks/targets improvements.
However, removing `moment` from `shared-lib/search` and `shared-libs/message-utils` in the same fashion did not result in any savings. No repro for `google-libphonenumber` either. I'm not sure why.

**Additional context**
These are the shared-libs used by webapp and their dependencies.

Shared-lib | Dependencies
-- | --
Registration-utils | -
lineage | Underscore^1.9.1
Phone-number | Google-libphonenumber
Bulk-docs-utils | -
Message-utils | Underscore Moment Mustache Object-path Gsm Google-libphonenumber Bikram-sambat-bootstrap
search | Moment Underscore^1.9.1
Task-utils | -
Translation-utils | -

This is causing test failures for https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5657.

title: Refactor Auth service to return boolean not throw
body:
**Describe the issue**
The Auth service throws if the user doesn't have permission to do a thing. This was chosen because we expected to call the Auth service to ensure the user can do the thing they asked to do. However it's turned out we use it a lot just to decide whether or not to present the action when not having the permission is not an error case. This means we've ended up with a lot of code like

```js
Auth('can_edit').then(() => true).catch(() => false)
```

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Change the Auth service to always return a boolean. Update the calling code to check the boolean and throw if desired.

When implementing this also consider whether there is enough common code in the API auth.js module to warrant making a shared-lib for auth.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could have two implementations but because the boolean is overwhelmingly desired we should implement this one as default. We can add a separate implementation for throwing if that becomes popular.

title: Make configurable, marking of outgoing messages as duplicates
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
If a message similar to a recently sent out message is seen by the system, it is marked as duplicate and is never sent to the recipient. Generally, this is the desired behavior but there is a need to make it configurable such that this feature can be deactivated for a specif config. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
I imagine a configuration that allows specifying a delay i.e how long since last similar message was sent, that can be as low as 0 for cases where we do not want any messages to be marked as duplicate would be ideal.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Adding to the message something that makes the message slightly different from previous ones which works for some cases but not all.

**Additional context**
Imagine a situation where the system sends a validation message based on a user's submission but the user re-submits again using the same inputs. In this case, only the first validation message will go out and on subsequent submissions, the user will be left wondering if their submission was accepted.

title: DRAFT - Retry upwards replication
body:
# Description

Implements an upwards replication retry mechanism by "touching" failed uploads for 3 times - so they get pushed to the end of the changes feed.
Based on the fact that PouchDB emits a "denied" event when it receives a "forbidden" error - but doesn't fail replication (which is correct, it's not its business to care about your "validate_doc_update" rules):
https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/blob/master/packages/node_modules/pouchdb-replication/src/replicate.js#L100

Tries to fix edge cases where changes are decoupled from their context: an offline user creates a person, creates a report for the new person, does another 100 edits/adds, and then edits the same person. Pouch will batch these changes, so the report will be pushed before the person, and denied.

Risk is increased now that tasks are/will be created and saved on disk.

title: Retry upwards replication
body:
PouchDB does upwards replication in batches of 100 documents. For every batch, API will check each doc to determine whether the user is allowed to edit or create it, in the context of the current batch: if a batch contains a new contact that the user is allowed to create, and a report about this contact, API will allow saving of both the contact and the report.

However, if a new contact and a report about the new contact become decoupled, and are part of separate batches, with the report batch being uploaded first, API will not allow the creation of a report about an unknown contact. Saving the report after the contact is created will succeed.

To enable webapp to automatically retry the upload of such reports, we can listen to the `denied` event, which PouchDB emits when receiving a `forbidden` error, and "touch" the forbidden doc to generate a new rev that's pushed at the end of the changes feed.

title: Call 'db.close' for ephemeral PouchDB objects to avoid memory leaks
body:
**Describe the issue**


There is a "_known_" PouchDB memory leak bug documented here: https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/issues/6225
We use scoped PouchDB objects when interacting with user databases and purge databases.
Some operations create large numbers of these database objects that never get garbage collected. 

Easiest way of demonstrating this is to start sentinel with the `--inspect` flag and use chrome's memory profiler (accessed via  'chrome://inspect/#devices') to record and view heap snapshots.

Baseline:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/68605997-233d4b80-04b6-11ea-9aaa-a37748f759c0.png)

After 1000 deletes:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/68606031-35b78500-04b6-11ea-96ca-9f086ca98c9e.png)

After 2000 deletes:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/68606048-3f40ed00-04b6-11ea-8c8a-7efd585fac52.png)

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
To ensure that these objects get GC-ed properly, we need to call the `close` method manually.
Affects both API and Sentinel.

title: Batch processing of sentinel changes
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
Sentinel watches the couchdb changes feed and adds all changes to a queue for processing. This works fine most of the time but if it gets behind for whatever reason (bulk updates, crashed and restarted, etc) then all those changes are retrieved from couchdb and stored in memory. The objects are reasonably small and they get cleaned up as they're processed so we've gotten away with this for now but if we did run out of memory then Sentinel would get stuck.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
When we initialise the changes feed we should put a limit on how many results to get. This takes some load off couchdb and limits the number of objects in memory.

The implementation is a little tricky as we should only fetch the next page of the backlog once the previous page has been processed out of the queue. I suspect this means the changes request can no longer be `live`. We can watch for the `queue.drain` event before issuing another changes request.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to record the performance metrics:
1. Stop sentinel
2. Make 70,000 changes
3. Start sentinel
4. Track memory usage

**Measurements**
Memory spiked at 120MB and then gradually reduced.

**Environment**
- Instance: localhost
- Browser: N/A
- Client platform: N/A
- App: sentinel
- Version: 3.8.x, master

title: Improve the performance of deleting read docs
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
Every time a document is deleted sentinel deletes the associated "read" docs from the users databases. This is so the next time the user replicates the little red bubble isn't inflated (no pun intended) by counting docs that no longer exist. To do this we open up every user's user database and delete the doc if it exists. We do this in series so we don't crash sentinel by trying to open too many dbs at once. This makes sentinel very slow to process deletes.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Instead of processing the read deletions in the main sequence procession, introduce a new sequence processor which runs periodically (maybe every 30 minutes?). This processor will get changes from its last checked seq till now and for all deletions delete the corresponding read doc. Furthermore it turns out that the slow part is opening the users databases one by one, so instead, batch up all the deletions for that half an hour and delete them from each users database with a bulkdocs call. That way we only have to open each user's database once per interval.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could just run the deletions without blocking the main processing thread which would solve the responsiveness problem but would lose changes if sentinel crashed and would also not batch the deletions so we'd still end up opening the user's dbs too often thus slowing down the whole process.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to record the performance metrics:
1. Make 1000 users
2. Create 10000 docs
3. Delete 5000 docs
4. Create another doc
5. Measure CPU usage, RAM usage, time for all read docs to be deleted, and time for sentinel to process the doc created in 4

**Measurements**
Take measurements before starting development.

**Environment**
- Instance: localhost, recently happened with MUSO
- Browser: N/A
- Client platform: Linux
- App: sentinel
- Version: 3.7.0, master

title: Lineage hydrateDocs yields inconsistent results and possibly crashes when hydrating the same lineage
body:
**Describe the bug**
Our Lineage library tries to fully hydrate docs without relying on circular references.
When you have a case of "circular lineage" - for example hydrating a person that is primary contact of its place - we should have one "iteration" of hydration for each level.
This works fine in most cases, however, we do rehydrate contacts for every doc we with to hydrate. If any of these docs have the same lineage (for example reports submitted by the same person), our code will re-hydrate the contact object every time, resulting in a deeply nested doc.
This can prove very problematic when you have **many** docs to process at the same time:
I had added 8000 identical reports which were generating outbound tasks. Our outbound task job doesn't batch, so the script ended up trying to hydrate all 8000 docs at once.
Besides taking a LONG time and eating up a lot of memory (as the objects grew more deeply nested and much larger in size), the process failed with a `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`.
The range error happened in a `JSON.stringify` call, which apparently reported by others to throw this error when trying to stringify a too deeply nested object (https://github.com/Level/levelup/issues/276).
The error is also shown in this integration test: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/lineage_new_integration/shared-libs/lineage/test/integration.js#L798 shown to fail here https://travis-ci.org/medic/cht-core/jobs/611909779#L5991

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
We currently have (at least) 2 places where unlimited docs are hydrated in bulk: the due_tasks script and the outbound tasks script, both running as Sentinel schedule.
You will need to create docs that either have a "scheduled_task" in "scheduled" state that should be sent now or outbound tasks to be created for every doc.
1. Create some (thousands) of docs that are submitted by the same person, that is primary contact of its place.
2. Start Sentinel.
3. After a (potentially long) while, you should see a `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` in the Sentinel log.

Alternatively, you can script and run lineage.hydrateDocs yourself to check results similar to the interation test linked above.

**Expected behavior**
No matter how many times a "lineage" branch appears in the docsToHydrate, results should be identical.

title: Batch all sentinel operations
body:
**Describe the issue**
Currently, Sentinel runs a number of tasks on a schedule. Some of these tasks query the database, searching for specific docs that need to be updated.
The two examples I have are `due_tasks` and `outbound`.
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/sentinel/src/schedule/outbound.js#L29
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/shared-libs/transitions/src/schedule/due_tasks.js#L41
Both of these (and maybe others too) run queries without limit over the whole database. They run smoothly when Sentinel is up to date and running correctly.
If it fails or stops for whatever reason, and the queue becomes too large, we will be in an irredeemable situation where we would have to hotpatch instances in order to clear the queue.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We should not have any unlimited database queries that are prone to have documents queued up.
The selected limit should be a big enough number that it doesn't lengthen process periods with too long pause intervals but also be safe to execute under any circumstance. My initial though would be a limit of 1000, but that's just an idea.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could also consider refactoring these scripts so they operate in batches until their queue is finished, although it wouldn't necessarily be an improvement, as for long queues you could end up blocking Sentinel from executing other scheduled tasks for long periods.

title: Reports deleted from webapp interface are saved fully hydrated
body:
**Describe the bug**
Instead of just adding the `_deleted` flag on the original report json, deleting a report from webapp will result in adding the `_deleted` flag to the fully hydrated report (patient and contact). 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Load Reports tab. 
2. Select a report, and check it's JSON in the DB to verify that it is not hydrated.
3. Delete the report from webapp (pressing the "Trash can" icon in the action bar)
4. Load the JSON of the deleted report and verify that the it is now fully hydrated. 
To load the JSON of a deleted doc, you would need to get it's `rev` and request with `/medic/<report_uuid>?rev=<deleted_rev>`. 
The rev can be obtained by either: 
- `/_all_docs?keys=["<report_uuid>"]` - the value will be `result.rows[0].value.rev`
- `/_changes?filter=_doc_ids&doc_ids=["<report_uuid>"]` - the value will be `result.results[0].changes[0].rev`

**Expected behavior**
The JSON of the deleted report should not be hydrated.


**Environment**
- Browser: any
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.8

title: Request persistent storage
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
It's possible now or in the future that the browser will delete users data to free up space.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
 In browsers that support it we should request that the data is made persistent. If denied then it'll be treated the same as it is now, but if successful then the data will never be deleted unless the user explicitly requests it.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Our version of crosswalk may get around this by allowing 100% disk space usage, but we may not always use crosswalk and this is another layer of protection on top of crosswalk.
- Using native android storage but that is slower than keeping it in the browser and doesn't work in the browser.

title: Creating child documents using repeat groups causing android-wraper to crash
body:
**Describe the bug**
Creating linked documents as per the `Creating Additional Docs` sections of [this doc](https://github.com/medic/medic-docs/blob/master/configuration/forms.md) is not working as expected. If we created documents as outlined in `Repeated Docs Example` and the child document is explicitly bound to the repeat, there's an overallocation of memory (300MB) compared to 50 MB when the child document is bound to a group directly wrapped under the repeat. 

On typical CHW phones (1GB) , we consistently run out of memory and crash when using the original form https://medic.slack.com/files/U1ZF01J12/FQS6DJ2BF/pregnancy_outcomes.xlsx

I'm attaching two forms to illustrate when the feature is working and when it's breaking.

**Test files**
[pregnancy_outcomes_buggy.xlsx](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/files/4456881/pregnancy_outcomes_buggy.xlsx)
[pregnancy_outcomes_fixed.xlsx](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/files/4456882/pregnancy_outcomes_fixed.xlsx)


**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Upload one of the attached forms to an instance
2. Launch the form `Pregnancy Outcome`
3. Enter the 10 as the response to the question `How many children`
4. Take a memory snapshot and observe the memory used.

**Expected behavior**
No crashing when running on mobile, especially memory constrained models that we recommend to partners.

**Environment**
- Instance: moh-zanzibar.dev
- Browser: Firefox (v70), Chrome on latest medic-android
- Client platform: MacOS 10.15
- App: (webapp, medic-android)
- Version: (Probably 3.x but has been tested on 3.4-3.7)

**Additional context**
A workaround to what's explicit documented in https://github.com/medic/medic-docs/blob/master/configuration/forms.md is to bind the child document to a group immediately under the repeat. 

Using the original partner form, memory allocation jumps from around 50MB to 3GB.

This has been reported by [D-Tree](https://medic.slack.com/archives/CEQTMKFT8/p1574250502002000) and [PIH](https://github.com/medic/config-pih/issues/19)

title: Users with a lot of large docs to replicate continuously fail

**Describe the bug**

When replicating we use the default PouchDB batch size of 100 so we can efficiently send large numbers of docs in one request. If the docs include images (eg: MRDT photos) then this request can get large. On the server API limits the JSON parser to 32MB after which we respond with an error. title: Deployments that only update server-code components shouldn't force a client download and refresh
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Code deployment via horticulturalist

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Only force the clients to download changes if there are real code changes, and only prompt for app refresh if it's required. 

Deploying a branch via horti is a much nicer way to achieve server hot patching, because it's clearer that we're doing it and it's harder to mess it up.

However, whenever any deployment happens via horti:
 - The `_design/medic` document gets written to, changing the `deploy_info` parameter
 - The `_design/medic-client` document gets written to based on `_design/medic`
 - This forces the entire `_design/medic-client` to be re-downloaded by all clients (as of writing ~17kb, which is small but not nothing)
 - Which in turn forces a "you need to restart the app" prompt for all clients

This is overly damaging if you're doing something as simple as tweaking an API parameter, or adding more logging to debug an obscure production performance issue.

There are two potential tweaks here:
 - Consider not storing the version in `_design/medic-client`, so it doesn't re-download all view definitions unless required
 - Consider not asking for an app restart if `_design/medic-client`, as no code in that file requires that the app re-bootstraps to be applied 

Either or both of these would allow us to more comfortably use horti in place of hot patching.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Real server hot patching, which is much more dodgy and I think significantly harder in our latest infrastructure.

title: Limit patient_id to be a subject_id and not a uuid
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
The lineage shared library has two inputs for patients: a `patient_id` and a `patient_uuid`. The `patient_id` can be a subject id or a contact's id. For example, [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/shared-libs/lineage/test/integration.js#L517) in the integration tests where the patient_id is a uuid. 

The downside of this is that when given a patient_id, we need to check if it is a uuid and only if that query fails do we check if it is a subject id. So we are doing two queries to look up this subject id value - this is slow and clutters the already complex hydration code.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We should use patient_uuid for uuids and patient_id explicitly for subject ids.  Then we can cleanup the hydration code to avoid this unnecessary query. 

**Notes**
I have no idea if this feature is even used or how many forms would need to be migrated.
