title: Add a native GPS field that can be required in the UI
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently when you want to guarantee that a form has GPS coordinates gathered with it, you only have one option: add a enketo `geopoint` widget and make the input required. This is awkward, at best, because there is no good UI to indicate if the GPS is working and you should wait, let alone if the GPS is disabled and will never work. This is a pressing issue for the Covid MoH Mali (CMoHM) deployment where GPS is mandatory for all forms. The specifics of this issue are being worked on in [config-moh-mali#86 ](https://github.com/medic/config-moh-mali/issues/86).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Allow app builders to have a GPS input in the form be required.  Allow them to give  instructions to CHWs on how to use it.  Make the input be intelligent so that when GPS is off it alerts the user, "You must turn on GPS to proceed" as well as give status updates like "Searching for GPS, please wait" and give the option to show a spinner.  Upon success, allow a message to be shown "GPS coordinates found, you may proceed".  Upon error show a message like "GPS coordinates could not be found. Please try again"

All text should be available for translation and extension (eg they may add "Please move to an area where you can see the sky and try again")

While there are some helpful changes in 3.10, they don't allow you to *require* the field.  Here's the relevant description from 3.10 on GPS features for reference:

>  The app will wait up to 30 seconds to get a location lock before it gives up. If a user tries to submit a form before a location lock is obtained and before 30 seconds are up, the submit action will wait until 30 seconds are up. Also: This change also supports the latest updates in medic-android, where the Location permission is requested at runtime, when editing/creating a report, rather than demanded when starting the app for the first time.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Currently the best work around we can do is to make the `geopoint` field required and then give the error message, "GPS coordinates not found, please ensure GPS is enabled and click the cross hairs to try again". This is awkward b/c GPS may be off and will never work no matter how many times the CHW clicks the cross hairs.

**Additional context**
See  [config-moh-mali#86 ](https://github.com/medic/config-moh-mali/issues/86)
**NB** - If this feature is tied to an upgrade to [medic-android](https://github.com/medic/medic-android/) >0.4.39 (currently deployed [version](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.medicmobile.webapp.mobile.covid_moh_mali)) there is very little rush.  The reason is that any medic-android upgrade for CMoHM involves all 600+ CHW's returning their phones to a central location for upgrade.  So, the only reason to consider rushing this feature would be if it can be done independent of medic-android and done entirely in cht-core and subsequently the [CMoHM app](https://github.com/medic/config-moh-mali/).

title: Improve translations workflow to be more open but without losing accountability
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**

Today the translations workflow using POEditor.com is not as open as the CHT source code, I want a more open workflow to allow more people (everybody) be able to translate the CHT, in an accountable manner.

Current workflow: https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/overview/translations/

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

Currently the CHT source code is publicly available at Github, and everybody can propose changes but without modify the original source code, creating a fork and then a PR with the changes. Despite the same workflow can be used to translate the app editing the files [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/ddocs/medic/_attachments/translations), pull requests may not be suitable for non-developers audience, that's way we use POEditor.com.

I sent a question/suggestion to POEditor [here](https://poeditor.uservoice.com/forums/171919-general/suggestions/41509804--pull-requests-like-contributions?tracking_code=f696782b17bfce7a7c6d9cc2ccd8afb5), quote:

> _is it possible to implement a workflow similar to "pull requests" like the ones in Github? what I mean is: we want to let anybody to contribute with our projects, but when a contributor edits an entry, it would not change the original translation but create a "draft", a "proposal", that needs to be approved before saved._

The response (in the same thread) from the POEditor team is:

> _Perhaps adding an extra proofreading step to your workflow could help: https://poeditor.com/kb/proofreading-translations. Instead of exporting all translations to GitHub, you could add export filters on your links with GitHub files, so that only the proofread strings are exported. You can find more info on how to set export filters in the section ‘Importing and exporting string’ of this article: https://poeditor.com/kb/localization-file-management-with-github-bitbucket-and-gitlab-integrations._

But I don't think it would be a good solution, so I don't have a clear proposal now, but I wanted to create the ticket to leave open the discussion here.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

As mentioned above, we can use just Github pull requests, the user don't need an editor and git installed because the Github webapp allows to change the source code of any file clicking a button, with a web editor provided by Github. If we document how to do that it may work, the major problem is that .properties files despite are simple also have specific rules, like white spaces in keys needs to be escaped with `\`, same for line returns and some special characters. Also POEditor.com provide a more appealing interface for non developers users.

**Additional context**

Despite POeditor.com is open in the sense that we can add anybody to our projects to contribute, the need to add the user to the POEditor project first as a user within the organization to just change a few translations adds friction that may discourage people to contribute, while in Github anybody without invitation can do it. Also once a new contributor edit translations, we lost track of what was the original translation the contributor have edited (accountability), although we still have the original translations in Github, there is no automated way to rollback what the contributor edited in POEditor that we don't liked, that is because I would like contributions to be drafted instead of saved overwriting the original one, like pull requests.

title: isSensitive doesn't stop replication of reports when the patient_id is the subject of a report
body:
**Describe the bug**
Reports that apply to the [sensitive documents](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/performance/replication/#sensitive-documents) logic should not replicate to a users app. In this case the report is using the `patient_id` to mark the subject. Which allows the user to see the document.  When we do the check in code to see if it should replicate we are referring to the UUID. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Have a hierarchy of facility A > B
2. Have a user1(supervisor) with facility of A for place associated to their contact
3. Have a user2(subordinate) with facility of B for place associated to their contact 
4. Using a report that assigns a `patient_id` and sets `doc.fields.private` to 'yes'.  I modified the `on` report in standard. 
5. Submit the report as User1 from User2 contact page. 
6. The report will display on User2's contact page. 
7. Log in as User2 and ensure to replicate. 
8. User2 sees the report that should not be replicated.  If you modify the doc and remove `patient_id` and then clear User2s cache and re-replicate. The user will not see that report. 

**Expected behavior**
We should be checking all ways that a report could possibly be about a person and filtering if the private field is set. 


**Environment**
- Instance: localhost
- Browser: Chrome
- Client platform: Windows
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.10

title: Handle training app cut over to production app better
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
CHWs are often trained on one app which uses a test cht-core instance and then expected to use another app for live data entry on the production cht-core instance.  This can result in confusion as to which app to use, [most recently 50 CHWs entered 1800 documents in a test instance](https://github.com/medic/config-moh-mali/issues/98) that all should have been in the live instance.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
cht-core should offer a way to explicitly allow for CHW training in a way that both allows using the app that's as close to production as possible while still offering an explicit, and not confusing way to stop using the test instance on the go live data. This might include, but should not be limited to:
* a "test server" setting such that the app and web UI are very clearly branded "THIS IS A TEST INSTANCE", possibly adding a "DO NOT USE AFTER {{SPECIFIC_DATE}}" 
* Offer a routing option that before the go live date, all traffic is pushed to the test server.  After the go live data, with out any changes on the CHW's device, traffic is transparently pushed to the production server (this presents some issues on sessions and users persisting between the two back ends of course)
* Having the test app cease to function after the go live date, even if the CHW is offline
* Have automatic reminders in the test app to not use it after a certain date
* Allow a test app to push it's data to a different server when it's been discovered it's been used to gather live data.
* Alert administrators when CHWs are uploading docs to a test instance after a certain date

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Some solutions we've thought about:
* change all passwords for CHWs on a specific go live date
* installing the [generic app for testing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.medicmobile.webapp.mobile&hl=en_US), then telling CHW to use [the real app](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.medicmobile.webapp.mobile.covid_moh_mali) on a certain date
* manually migrating data, after it's been synced, from the test server -> production server

**Additional context**
A big problem we've faced is accounting for the offline first nature of cht-core.  That is, if a CHW is one of 50 CHWs entering data into the wrong system, preemptively changing their password _before_ they sync up to the server, means data is lost.  Data loss should be avoided at all costs.


FYI - @kennsippell , @binokaryg , @Marina-Kenf , @abbyad & @garethbowen

title: Barcode scanning using device camera
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
As a nurse/CHW, I do home visits to follow-up with patients who are in treatment for disease management, but did not show for clinic appointments. Patients are often taking multiple medications (or using other health products), which are hard to keep track of. Having an accurate list of these products is critical to creating and managing up-to-date health record for patients. The process for collecting this information is currently manual, making it difficult to capture it in a timely and accurate way. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
As a nurse, I would like the ability to scan barcodes for patient IDs or barcodes on medications (or other health products) to quickly and accurately acquire patient health information. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- manually inputting information
- taking photographs of products 

**Additional context**
bar code scanner is supported by [XLSForm](http://xlsform.org/en/#question-types) and [ODK Collect](https://docs.getodk.org/form-question-types/#barcode-widget)

Worth noting that ZXing is in maintenance mode, and ODK Collect had to build in the scanner as opposed to an intent since 1.7. There is more investigation needed to know if this is a relatively simple task (handle the XLSForm type and make/handle a new intent) or a big lift.

title: Make Telemetry Actionable Through Alerting and Visualization to Identify Production Issues
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
As the App Deployment team, we’re focused on building and deploying stable applications. To do this effectively, we need to be able to observe how the application performs post-deployment and understand quickly when a deployed application is not functioning the way it was intended. The current production logs (and proposed additional telemetry buildout) lack alerting capabilities and interactive metrics visualization, resulting in missed signals. These missed signals reduce the reliability and stability of CHT services due to increases in app down-time and undetected app error rates. It also impedes App Builders ability to make configuration changes with confidence. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A more robust monitoring system that gathers and organizes telemetry metrics to:
1) Automate client-side error alerts to System Administrators and App Builders when a system or instance isn’t working as it should. 
2) Visualize metrics to understand historic trends, correlate diverse factors, and measure changes in performance, consumption, or error rates
3) Enable tracing of a deployed applications data flow and progression to identify user activities that help to build context for system errors and changes

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Telemetry is currently dumped into spreadsheets

**Additional context**
Related initiative: [Client-side telemetry and monitoring for improved app deployment and ability to analyze how users engage with the product](https://github.com/medic/cht-roadmap/issues/29) contains additional context and monitoring requirements from across the Organization

title: User friendly CHT Contacts Management System
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
`csv-to-docs`, `move-contacts` and `upload-docs` commands in medic-conf are currently the command available for contact(persons and places) management in CHT. While the command work, there is an unmet gap in CHT contact management. Specifically, for a large deployment, we are not addressing the following requirements effectively:-
- Bulk creation of contacts. In particular, the creation of a new hierarchy and addition of contacts to an existing hierarchy.
- Hierarchy updates in bulk. This is mostly moving contacts from a hierarchy level to another. It includes situations such as a CHA who exists at a level above a CHW being demoted to a CHW and vice versa. 
- Bulk editing of contacts. Some details associated with contacts require updating at some point, for example, phone number.
- Bulk deletion / deactivation. Ability to delete contacts that are no longer active in the system for a reason or another. A thing to keep in mind here is the nuanced requirement to still be able to access data associated with these contacts even after they are deleted.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- A mechanism to synchronize a new list with what is in the target instance. For example, say a new community health worker(CHW) is being added under a community health assistant(CHA). It should be possible to query the instance for an existing CHA with the CHA details associated with the new CHW and use that when creating the CHW record. The unique identifier visible to the user for the mapping exercise for the linkage would need to be human readable as well.
- It should be possible to tell, in a snapshot, where a user exists within the hierarchy.
- User lists, especially in MOH settings are not managed by one single person and are mostly a concerted effort with a lot of responsibility devolution at play. It should then be possible to accommodate this. For a practical perspective, let us use a typical hierarchy, bottom-up: CHW, CHA, County Health Management Team(CHMT). Every CHA is responsible for collating CHW details then passing them along to CHMT who are then put together the complete list. The solution needs to factor in the whole process of contact lists management. 
- Effectively handle deletions and deactivations. When a CHA is deactivated, data under them should be available for analysis. If CHWs under them are assigned to another CHA, data associated with the new CHA should reflect from the point in time when the new allocation took effect. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Write a custom script specific to the project.

**Additional context**
[A more detailed write up with one project's study case.
](https://docs.google.com/document/d/18FXcgVFPBsZzx6eMQJYHx9y-UwXXCf5OZTVJfFU1CY0/edit?usp=sharing)

title: Variable static target goals.
body:
### TL;DR Part of #4771 which is summarized as: > #### The problem > Lack of flexibility in setting variable targets for CHWs based on varying factors like catchment area size, rural vs urban settings and other data available in the app. > #### Why is it important? > Partners would like to set different target goals for different CHWs, groups of CHWs, supervisory areas and branches that are realistic for CHWs operating in the different contexts. This is currently not possible. For this ticket, the proposal is to focus on, **varying _static_ target goals** for community health workers as informed by demographic, population differences as well as data points associated with the community health workers and their population ### User Stories 1. As a program manager, with a deployment spanning several branches, I would like to configure different target goals for the CHWs in the different branches so that they are working towards a realistic goal as informed by branch context. 2. As a program manager, I would like to give each individual CHW a different target goal specific to them as informed by an analysis of the CHW area population data captured in the app so that they can focus care on the right interventions or population sub groups. 3. As a community health worker, I want my target goal to be reflective of my context so that I am able to effectively deliver care to my community members. 4. As a supervisor, I want to tell in a snapshot, how my community health workers are performing against their target goals so that I know where to offer support as needed. 5. As a supervisor, I would like to drill down to the details of how my community health workers are performing against their set target goals so that I can offer required support where necessary. 6. As a program manager, I would like to set different target goals for different groups of community health workers under different supervisors so that those community health workers, with the help of supervisors, are working towards realistic goals. ### Mockups ![variable-targets-percentages](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3006199/96431591-68144b00-120c-11eb-9510-37bca1b158de.png) ![variable-targets-numbers](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3006199/96431593-69de0e80-120c-11eb-8a36-80714d7f7cf9.png) ### Acceptance Criteria 1. Variable targets should integrate well with the targets status quo:- - Hardcoded static target goals should continue working for targets that are not set up as variable targets. - Variable targets should work with both count and percentage targets. - Variable targets should integrate well with monthly vs all time targets options. - Just like it is in with the product right now, the target goal updates when an update is explicitly made either via config or otherwise and takes effect on the user’s phone when they sync, immediately. - The visuals of the target for a user looking at their target does not change with this feature. - The supervisor's aggregate target view should indicate the various target goals for the different CHWs under them and accordingly update the completion indication displayed for each target correctly. 2. The target goal should be available on disk for analysis. In addition, add an indication of whether a target is variable or not in the data saved. 3. Information on when the target goal took effect(i.e when it was updated to a new value) should be available in data, including a way to tell what the value was before the update. In other words, if an update is made to the target goal, the same should reflect in the document saved on disk including the timestamps when that happened. This should work well with both monthly and all-time targets. 4. If a target changes from a static to variable target, it should be possible to tell that from the data saved on disk. 5. The interface for setting a variable target should be fairly easy to interact with and scalable for the different combinations of user setups that are likely. For guidance, here are some examples: - It should be possible to specify a variable target at an individual level. For example, an isolated CHW X gets a target goal that is different from everyone else. - Extending (a) above, it would be possible to specify a target goal value for a number of users. - Ability to group users to get a specific target goal by a hierarchy level, factoring in a configurable hierarchy. For example, users under Branch X get a target goal of YY while the rest of the users get a target goal of ZZ. 6. Variable targets should be distinguishable as having goals and are not to be mixed up with targets without a goal such that it should not be possible to specify the same target as both having a goal for a subsection of users and not having a goal for another group of users. ### User Acceptance Scenarios #### Scenario 1 There are some projects that we know have implemented this by duplicating target object configurations. Re-implement those in a neat and scalable way using this feature. Expected result: One clean target config object that serves the different target goals for the different branches. #### Scenario 2 A hypothetical organization has the following hierarchy set up: ‘branch -> CHW area -> household’. Supervisors are created at the branch level. For purposes for scenarios below, the supervisor and supervisor naming has a ‘branch-role-number’ pattern e.g A-supervisor-1, B-CHW-1. `assessment` and `assessment-follow-up` are among the forms configured. The following is the requirements spec for this organization that we will validate with the scenarios later. _Some specific branches and CHWs are marked for specific target goals. In some situations, the criteria are a little more generic and the program manager will provide criteria to the app builder as we will see below._ For purposes of the scenarios below, below is a set of requirements for the hypothetical organization above. > The organization tracks assessments conducted(count of assessment) for all CHWs. CHWs in Branch D for the same(count of assessments) do not get a goal. assessment follow-up rate(count of assessment-follow-up / count of assessment) has not been rolled to all branches and currently, only CHWs in Branch B is seeing this target with an exception of one CHW in Branch A. Malaria assessment is included in the assessment workflow for branches marked as malaria endemic. A branch or community health unit is marked as malaria endemic using a flag in the place. Branch C among others is marked as malaria endemic i.e {name: Branch C, malaria_endemic: true}. title: Server-side target generation for SMS projects
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
cht-core has, since v3.8, had the ability to generate target documents and store them on disk. This has brought with it numerous advantages including using the same subsystem to help with DHIS2 metric aggregation.  However, one downside still remains with this approach, it is reliant on users accessing the webapp (either and pc or phone) and this making it unsuitable for SMS deployments.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We have SMS projects going for national scale - e.g EBS in Kenya. One key requirement that the government is pushing data to the national DHIS2 to help with analysis and reporting. The government and stakeholders are currently in the process of defining what data needs to be captured at DHIS2 and Medic has been brought to the table to help with that.

The improvement being sought is developing the ability to do target document generation server-side so that this feature works in purely SMS deployments.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Replicating the target logic in SQL to generate CSVs that could be imported into DHIS2. However, this replication is what go us to build the target doc generation feature.

**Additional context**
Having this will be critical for increasing SMS project adoption by governments

title: Evaluate third party telemetry tools
body:
This issue is to setup a test instance and deploy 3rd party telemetry tools for evaluation.

_Purpose of the evaluation_
The purpose of this evaluation is to understand if a 3rd party telemetry tool can help us to turn various types of telemetry data into actionable insights for product decision making and app deployment improvement outcomes. We are interested in evaluating whether they can provide necessary visibility into the health of CHT systems and trends in app usage and user behavior. 

_Functional areas we are interested in evaluating_
1) Automation of client-side error alerts
2) Visualization of metrics to understand historic trends, correlate diverse factors, and measure changes in performance, consumption, or error rates
3) Tracing of a deployed applications data flow and progression to identify user activities that help to build context for system errors and changes in user interaction
4) Ease of extensibility and team use for retrieving, interacting with, and reporting on data from individual and aggregate  project deployments 

_System requirements_
Must Haves:
- Low device data usage
- Low device CPU usage
- Low device memory usage to contain any app performance impact
- Device offline storage capabilities
- Open source solution that can be integrated into the CHT tech stack and be offered to partners as a self-hosted solution
- Automation of reports
- Automation of alerts
- Evaluate data trends over time
- Feature level usage and A/B testing
- Ability to define user cohorts

Nice to Haves:
- Accessible to non/less-technical team members (ie does not require understanding of sql data queries)
- Ability to setup defined workflows so can follow user activity through complete sequences
- Analyze both magnitude and ratios
- Download to csv

_Additional context_
Related initiative: [Client-side telemetry and monitoring for improved app deployment and ability to analyze how users engage with the product](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1c2UHfzaue4sNvQkiwRc93PBEdML9J9DlFNuQ23suk4k/edit?ts=5f92e9b0#) contains additional context and requirements from across the Organization

title: For targets without `idType`, the winning emission is not deterministic
body:
**Describe the bug**
https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/targets/#targetsjs

Targets will, by default, count a single emission per contact, even if they "apply to" reports. The only way to get a target to count multiple reports per contact is to set its `idType` to `report`. This is not the scope of this issue, though. 
When there are multiple emissions for one contact for one target (multiple reports that match the `appliesIf` and `passesIf` for a single contact), the winning emission (whose reported_date will determine which reporting interval the "contact" gets counted towards the target goal) is not deterministic. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Create a simple target that counts reports, this is an example, but you can use any form you desire:
```
{
  id: 'target_forma',
  translation_key: 'target',
  subtitle_translation_key: 'target',
  type: 'count',
  icon: 'no-icon',
  goal: 16,
  appliesTo: 'reports',
  appliesToType: ['forma'],
  appliesIf: function () {
    return true;
  },
  date: 'reported'
}
```
2. Create a bunch of reports that will match this target, all reports about the same patient. 
It's helpful to generate these in a CSV and upload them with medic-conf because you're going to need to change their reported_date and _id fields. 

Create reports in different reporting periods (different months) and make sure their _id fields are out of sort. When I tested, this was my report list:

| _id | form | reported_date | 
| --- | ---- | ------------- |
| a_report | forma | date in February | 
| b_report | forma | date in January | 
| c_report | forma | date in June | 
| d_report | forma | date in April | 
| e_report | forma | date in May | 

So I'm making a very clear alphabetically sorted list of _id with a completely scrambled list of reported_dates. 

3. Login as an offline user that would sync all these reports. Go to the targets page. 
Check if you get a count on your target.
4. Change your OS clock to be in June (`c_report` is the "latest" of its type, so theoretically it should be the one to generate the winning emission). 
Check your targets page and see that you don't have a target count. 
5. Change your OS clock to be in January (`a_report` is the "first" of it's type, so if the first chronological report is selected, this should be the one to generate the winning emission). 
Check your targets page and see that you don't have a target count. 
6. Change your OS clock to Feb / April and see that you don't have a target count. 
7. Change your OS clock to May and see that you DO have a target count. 

**Expected behavior**
I believe, pre 3.8 the last chronological report was generating the winning emission. 
Pre 3.8, we were using the Search service to get a list of reports:
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/3.7.x/webapp/src/js/services/rules-engine.js#L224
Relevant part of the search service is here: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/3.7.x/shared-libs/search/src/search.js#L33 where we sort the results by view value, which is the reported_date: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/3.7.x/ddocs/medic-client/views/reports_by_validity/map.js#L3

Post 3.8 we just query the `reports_by_subject` here https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/shared-libs/rules-engine/src/pouchdb-provider.js#L34 and never sort the results. 
CouchDB/PouchDB view queries will return rows sorted by the emitted key, and if the key is the same, sorted by _id. The emitted value - which is the reported_date in this case - is not taken into account. 
https://docs.couchdb.org/en/stable/api/ddoc/views.html?highlight=view#api-ddoc-view-sorting

**Environment**
- Instance: any 3.8+
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.8+

**Additional context**
This was reported as a regression by a partner after an upgrade to 3.9.1. 
Not sure about labeling and whether we should consider this production-urgent or not.

# Development

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Manager. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

# Releasing

Once all issues have passed acceptance testing and have been merged into `master` and backported to the release branch release testing can begin.

- [x] Until release testing passes, make sure regressions are fixed in `master`, cherry-pick them into the release branch, and release another beta.
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`

@channel *Announcing the release of {{version}}*

This release fixes {{number of bugs}}. Read the release notes for full details: {{url}}
```
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/), under the "Product - Releases" category. You can use the previous message and omit `@channel`.
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the project.

title: Form submissions hang in desktop browsers when location permission requests are ignored by users
body: **Describe the bug** In certain conditions, the CHT on version 3.10 fails to defend ~~against missing translation~~ location permissions being ignored. When a form is submitted in this scenario, the data is not written to PouchDB, the form controls are disabled (cancel, prev & submit) and a spinner is shown. **To Reproduce** This was recreated in docker but should affect any CHT hosting environment. The docker set up and Covid MoH Mali (CMoHM) app steps are listed here for completeness, but it's assumed we can isolate the behavior of the app. This assumes you have `node`, `npm`, `docker` and `medic-conf` installed: 1. Download [this](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/362-docs-update-docker-compose-to-3.9.0-rc.2/docker-compose.yml) `docker-compose.yml` - the one with medic-os `image: medicmobile/medic-os:cht-3.9.0-rc.2` and haproxy `image: medicmobile/haproxy:rc-1.17`. 1. Ensure you don't have a persistent docker volume that already has data in it by deleting the containers that use it, and then the volume itself: `docker rm medic-os haproxy` and then `docker volume rm medic-data`. 1. launch the two containers with `docker-compose up` . you now have a 3.9 CHT instance on htps://127.0.0.1 1. clone out the [CMoHM](https://github.com/medic/config-moh-mali/) repo (private) and `cd` into the config dir: `cd config-moh-mali/covid-surveillance/`. After you clone out the repo, be sure to switch to `b8e6c4a` branch in case the app config changed: `git checkout b8e6c4a` 1. In your browser Log in as `medic/password` on your local instance htps://127.0.0.1 1. go to htps://127.0.0.1/admin/#/upgrade and "Install" version 3.10.0 1. Back in the CLI, run `medic-conf` to install the CMoHM app: `medic-conf --url=https://medic:password@localhost --accept-self-signed-certs` 1. In your browser, click on 'people' icon on the top 1. click on "new district" on the bottom left 1. under "set the primary contact" choose "create a new person" 1. ensure their age is over 20, sex to femail and role to asc-s 1. accept all defaults on the next page and click "submit" 1. in the upper right click the hamburger menu and click "app management" 1. click the "Users" option, and click "Add user" at the top 1. enter a username you'll remember, for "role" choose "ASC-S", choose the place and associated contact you just created. Enter a password you'll remember and click "Add user" 1. log out as the admin user or open an incognito tab. Log in as the user you just created 1. click on the "Reports" icon at the very top, and then click "submit report" on the lower left, and click the "Formulaire..." pop up 1. For "User" accept the defaults and choose "Next" 1. For 1st "Village" choose "Autre", for 2nd "Village" enter any value 1. click anywhere on the map to choose a location and click "Next" 1. for "select what applies" choose "I am not currently in the household." 1. Choose "Next" 1. On the "Evaluation" page for "obtained the consent" choose "yes" and "next" 1. On the "Household information" page 1. enter any value for chief 1. enter "71234567" for phone 1. for "hand washing" choose "yes" 1. for how many people put 1 1. for children and all other values on the page put "0" 1. for "anyone in the household sick" put "no" 1. choose "Next" 1. On "Formulaire Evaluation" choose "Next" 1. On the final "Formulaire Evaluation" choose "submit" **Expected behavior** Ideally we defend against this and ensure the data is saved. As well, it'd be nice if we fall back to a default translation to show a message as needed about the transaction succeeding. In a worst case scenario, we should alert the user the data was not saved and they should try again. **Logs** Frustratingly, there are no logs in the browser console when the actual form is submitted :( There are prior errors that show up about missing translations (which turned out to be unreleated), as seen in the screenshots below. **Screenshots** [](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8253488/98174967-9059a600-1eaa-11eb-9536-4886cba9e539.png) **Environment** - Instance: local dev instance - Browser: Firefox & Chrome both latest - Client platform: Linux Ubuntu 20 and 18 - App: webapp - Version: 3.10 **Additional context** Note that this works as expected in 3.9, and then breaks in 3.10. This strongly suggests it's a regression in 3.10. If you follow the above steps, but do not upgrade to 3.9, the bug is not encountered. ~~In 3.10 you can fix the bug by uploading the missing translations by being in the `config-moh-mali/covid-surveillance` directory in CMoHM repo and running `medic-conf --url=https://medic:password@localhost upload-app-settings upload-app-forms upload-resources upload-custom-translations --accept-self-signed-certs`~~ This turned out to be wrong and I very likely choose to allow location permission. See below for [specific workarounds](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6711#issuecomment-722241502).

title: Adds translations compiler to support pluralization
body:
# Description

We used to rely on messageformat to provide pluralization. The AngularJS translator allowed you to control how you could interpolate a translation, but ngx-translate does not. 
It does, however, allow you to overwrite the default compiler and use that as the middle man between it and messageformat. 

I found a library that passed **all** translations through messageformat (https://www.npmjs.com/package/ngx-translate-messageformat-compiler) which is bad for use, because of all the caveats. for example, messageformat encloses params in single curly braces, versus double curly braces that we use. 

So I quickly created our own compiler that does a really stupid filter (only passes translations to messageformat if they use single curly braces!) and mostly rushed it to unblock @njogz with display last visited dates in contacts lists. I did add a TODO to investigate whether there are better options.

title: Replace Enketo geo widget with one that uses our angular location service
body:
**Describe the issue**
Enketo ships with a geo picker widget which uses the browser's geolocation service. The webapp also collects geolocation data for every form submitted using our geolocation angular service. Because of the slightly different implementation when both of these are used in a form they can behave a slightly differently. Furthermore to help caching and get a quick response we should make sure both use the same service.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Patch or replace the enketo geo widget so it uses geolocation angular service. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Leave it as is - it's mostly ok.
- Remove the widget - I'm not convinced it works well offline. How are people using it now?

title: Default config delivery form saves incorrect baby uuid
body:
**Describe the bug**
When submitting a `delivery` form part of the default config (https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/config/default/forms/app/delivery.xml) and you select to enter multiple babies (either alive or not), the report will have as many entries for every repeat type, but the uuids of each repeat saved in the report will be the same:

For example:

if you add 3 baby deaths, 3 distinct contact docs will be created, but the report doc fields
`report.delivery.baby_death.baby_death_repeat.0.baby_death_profile_doc`
`report.delivery.baby_death.baby_death_repeat.1.baby_death_profile_doc`, 
`report.delivery.baby_death.baby_death_repeat.2.baby_death_profile_doc` will all have the same value. 

If you add 3 babies that are alive, 3 distinct contact docs will be created, but the report doc fields
`report.delivery.babys_condition.baby_repeat.0.baby_details.child_doc`,
`report.delivery.babys_condition.baby_repeat.1.baby_details.child_doc`,
`report.delivery.babys_condition.baby_repeat.2.baby_details.child_doc` will all  have the same value. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Upload the `delivery` form from `default` config.
2. Fill a delivery report, selecting 6 child births, 3 alive, 3 dead. 
4. Save and load the report. Check the above listed fields.

**Expected behavior**
Each repeat should save the uuid of the generated contact doc. 

**Environment**
- Instance: gamma.dev.medicmobile.org (example report https://gamma.dev.medicmobile.org/#/reports/8fc63ed4-277f-4ea9-8e04-22ee614a5420)
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.10

**Additional context**
It's unclear to me if this is a configuration issue (where we don't specify which repeat to to get the uuid from, so the first one is always picked) or it's a code problem where we don't handle getting uuids from repeats properly.

Design and configure a Maternal, Newborn and Child Health (MNCH) reference app for the CHT including these below workflows:

- Growth monitoring 
- Immunization 
- Child assessment

This results in the follow forms and follow up forms:
- Immunization and growth

   - Child development follow up
- Child assessment

title: Setting selectMode while editing a form can produce unexpected behavior
body:
In version 3.3, we added a warning modal when users try to navigate away from an edited form: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/4013
There's some unexpected behavior between this modal (and how it prevents navigation if users select "no") and selectMode where, if you toggle select mode while editing a form and then selecting to stay on the page, the LHS list changes and adds checkboxes (select gets enabled) but the RHS part stays locked on the form edit.

**To Reproduce**
1. Use a desktop browser (so you see both LHS and RHS at the same time) and login as some user (type of user is not relevant)
2. Go to the Reports tab and open a form to create a new report. Edit at least one field (don't submit).
3. Click on the "Select" button to switch to select mode (in the LHS actionbar).
4. When the popup to confirm navigation appears, select to stay on the page (click "NO").
5. LHS switches to select mode (checkboxes appear) but the RHS stays on your edited form. Selecting a report from the LHS list will cause the RHS to show a loader, but after loading, the page will still show your edited form.

**Expected behavior**
I'd expect the select mode to not become enabled before the user confirms they want to navigate away from the edited form.

**Screenshots**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/99248373-03e7a580-2811-11eb-9519-684834d8e9a5.png)


**Environment**
- Instance: any 3.3.x+ (including gamma.dev)
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.3.x +

**Additional context**
Setting low priority as this has existed ever since the navigation confirm modal has been added and most of our users use mobile devices where it's not possible to trigger this behavior.

title: Webapp navigates from report list to detail after navigating back on slow devices
body:
**Describe the bug**
On mobile views, users may be redirected back to the report detail page, without user action, if they verify a report and then immediately go back to the list. This also happens when the user hits back while the report is still loading. 
This only happens on slow networks or devices with low performance.

**To Reproduce with verification**
1. Login with a user that can verify reports on a slow device or throttle your desktop browser's performance OR network (or both for overkill). If using a desktop browser, adjust window size to have a mobile view. 
2. Go to reports and open a report. Verify this report (which verification, correct or with errors is irrelevant). 
3. Very quickly, after the report was verified, click the back button up top to return to the list. 
4. Wait a few seconds (this depends on your device and your network).
5. Get redirected back to the report detail without performing any action. 

**To Reproduce without verification**
1. Same as above.
2. Open a report. While seeing the spinner in the detail page, click on the back button up top to return to the list.
3. Wait a few seconds.
4. Get redirected back to the report detail page and see the report or an empty page (like no report is selected).  

**Expected behavior**
Users should be redirected back to the report detail page after quickly navigating back to the list. 

**Environment**
- Instance: gamma.dev
- Browser: Chrome
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.10 and earlier

**Additional context**
This is either a very old bug (pre 3.0) or was caused by the Redux refactor.

title: Improve how Muting is handled on device before syncs
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
The [muting feature](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/app-settings/transitions/#muting) as it works right now requires Sentinel Transitions to update the relevant contact docs following a muting form submitted by the CHW. Because of very slow/unstable connectivity in the field, we notice some weird situations that arise from it. The most frequent one is that the muting form don't get synced for days/weeks, in the mean time the household or place and its descendants remain active and users sometimes continue to submit forms. 
A part from the form submissions, from a UX perspective it is not ideal if the contact is not muted immediately, the users sometimes submit extra muting forms as they don't understand what's happening. Some of our UX features like UHC are affected as well. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We would want ideally a muting feature that can work fully offline and that would be immediately effective after it was triggered. 
Another solution that would only prevent the form submissions after the muting, could be a improvement in configuration that would make it possible to check if the last form submitted for any of the parents of a contact or the contact itself is a muting form. we could add that check to the form properties to prevent it from being submitted in those cases ( this might be already possible and i'm just not aware of that ).

**Additional context**
We have noticed this issue for our partner MUSO, where CHWs continue to submit forms for a place/contact supposed to be muted, this make it confusing and difficult specially from a data analysis perspective, the reasons why those submissions are being done is unclear, is it a mistake ? Was the family not supposed to be muted in the first place ? Would the CHW had unmuted the family first before submitting the visit if the family was muted in time ? Are the chws submitting visits forms without actually visiting the family to not be penalized by the UHC scoring ? 

initial ticket : https://github.com/medic/config-muso/issues/44

title: Procedure and tooling for changing the hierarchy of an existing application
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
A CHT application's hierarchy is foundational and not easily changed once the project goes live. Hierarchy data exists in every contact, every report, etc. Whenever possible, applications try never to change the hierarchy once the application is live.  But sometimes hierarchies must change. In our 2021 SoWs, multiple projects include deliverables which require hierarchy changes including BRAC (3000 CHWs and 16M docs) and Siaya.

Hierarchy changes require the majority of documents to be re-synced, and sometimes require the user to clear all documents from the phone.  They can result in data-loss or invalid data due to clearing the device before syncing, or making the server-side hierarchy change before syncing reports which will still have the legacy hierarchy within them. Because of data-loss risks, heirarchy changes can be associated with down-time.

Because of the above factors, need to be tightly coordinated with teams on the ground and therefore carry intense operational burdens. Due to operational burdens, they often are requested to happen in phases.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
At a minimum, we need clearly documented repeatable steps to execute hierarchy changes at scale without data loss. We need these steps to be fast and easy enough that we can complete migrations for projects with thousands of users in 2021 Q2 latest so we can complete the rest of the SOW in 2021. It is recommended that we investigate core improvements or tooling improvements which ease the operational burdens on the ground and minimise the risk of data loss .

title: Alert Safari users CHT doesn't support their browser
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently the CHT allows users on the Safari browser to log in and use the app.  The problem is that this browser is not supported.  Further Safari breaks in subtle, non-obvious ways.  The net results is that users assume the CHT as a whole, or their instance, is broken. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
At a minimum, we should show a large alert that Safari is not supported in the app.  Personally, I think Safari users should be prevented from logging in at all and presented with a link to the [docs about which browsers are supported](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/concepts/access/). Given this list is short (2 browsers (currently ignoring Edge on Chrome)), and we're offline first, instead of a link to online site, we could just say, "Safari not supported.  Please use Chrome or Firefox.". 

We should be sure our browser checks cover both Safari on MacOS desktop and on iOS mobile.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Adding info in the docs site that Safari isn't supported.  While we may still do this, we already have a list of supported browsers there and there'd ultimately be a long tail of off the beaten path unsupported browsers (Explorer? Opera? Brave? IceCat?)

**Additional context**
The error manifested such that a Safari use was able to log in and only a very small subset of the form didn't work (date validation requiring dates earlier than today).  This made it very hard to debug what the issue was.

title: More accurately represent sex and gender in the default reference app
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently in our default reference app we ship with CHT core (see [`config/default`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/config/default)), we only capture `sex` as a binary field.  This is an antiquated and biased schema that we should extend to encompass current medical best practices which recognize that `sex` is not binary.  Further, we should audit that `gender` is discrete from `sex` and is also not binary.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
The specific improvements should be researched.  One solution would be to change `sex` to have `select-one` values of `male`, `female`, `intersex`. A more generic version might be  `male`, `female`, `other`. For both `gender` and `sex` values, we may review HL7's Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) documents.  Specifically their ["Patient Gender and Sex"](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/patient.html#gender) document, including their nomenclature on [gender identity](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/valueset-gender-identity.html) and [sex assigned at birth](https://loinc.org/76689-9/).

WHO also has [published related material](https://www.who.int/teams/gender-equity-and-human-rights) on their site as well.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Do nothing and leaving this up to partners to change upon implementation.

**Additional context**
There was some [healthy discussion on Slack](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C024ZK678/p1607750293180800) (private link) which was this ticket's inception and gives some background and internal champions including @garethbowen, @ecsalomon , @helizabetholsen , @marialma .

We may opt to couple this effort with the current effort of authoring the [MNCH reference app](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6727) which will live in `config/default`.

FYI @isaacholeman , @katanu , @rmugwanya and @michaelkohn

title: Support additional reporting periods: DHIS2 & Supervisor Targets
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
v3.9 introduced DHIS2 integration capabilities based off of Targets docs.  A [known limitation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/integrations/dhis2-aggregate/#known-limitations) was that it only supported dataSets that are submitted to DHIS2 monthly. We have a project that needs to support a DHIS2 dataSet that is submitted quarterly.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
At a minimum, support quarterly reporting periods. [Here](https://docs.dhis2.org/en/develop/developing-with-the-android-sdk/workflow.html#android_sdk_aggregated_data) is the list of reporting periods that can be configured in DHIS2 for aggregate reports, so technically all of these will be fair game at some point.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Using a [custom function](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/targets/#targetsjs) for the `date` property on target docs.

**Additional context**
The specific DHIS2 data set that needs to be implemented is the 097b in Uganda. Another consideration we should review is countries like Mali and Togo where often reports are run monthly, but not starting on the first of the Gregorian calendar (for example: August = 28-July to 27-August).

NOTE: Additional design work needs to be done, but wanted to get this on the radar.

**Why Now?**
Partner(s): Kiwi Apple
Reason(s): A partner will be blocked by this for a major release or expansion

title: Targets with property "passesIfGroupCount.gte" count intances with "pass: false" when aggregating
body:
**Describe the bug**
The `passesIfGroupCount.gte` was written to support Muso's target for "% of families with 2 household visits/month" https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5493. The result is a [muso target](https://github.com/medic/config-muso/blob/master/targets.js#L73) which emits instances with `pass: true` for instances that should be counted (home visits) and `pass: false` for instances which should not be counted (families). The `pass: false` instances are essential for ensuring a correctly counted denominator - counting families with no reports and no home visits.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Deploy Muso configuration
2. Create three new families A, B, C
3. For Family A - complete one household visit in current month
4. For Family B - complete no household visits in current month
5. For Family C - complete two household visits on different days in current month

**Expected behavior**
1 of 3 families have recieved 2 household visits this month

**Observed behaviour**
1 of 2 families (incorrect denominator, task does not count families with zero reports)

or (if you remove the comments)
2 of 3 families (task counts denominator correctly, but requires only 1 family visit in the month to be counted)

**Context**
You can work around this for Muso's case using `gte: 3` - assuming there is one and exactly one additional instance per family.

**Environment**
- Instance: muso-mali.app
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.8 - 3.10

title: When loading form, put focus on first element
body: **Describe the issue** When app developers are building forms, they fill the forms out a lot. Likely dozens, if not hundreds of times. To do this quickly, they often fill out the form via the keyboard (tab + up key fills out a series of radio boxes quickly) as using the mouse slows them down. However, we put the browser focus 10 tab key presses away from the first form element, necessitating use of the mouse to put the focus on the first input. Here's a form for reference: [](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8253488/103833623-49b53300-5036-11eb-9127-5a66e2e8c208.png) **Describe the improvement you'd like** Add a mechanism to put the focus on the first input of a form when the page loads to expedite testing. Something like `autofocus` [attribute](https://www.w3schools.com/TAGS/att_input_autofocus.asp) might work. **Describe alternatives you've considered** 10x more tab key presses ;)

title: 6190 Architecture v3 API & Sentinel containers
body:
# Description
This PR creates separate containers for medic-api and medic-sentinel as part of our Architecture v3 implementation: medic/cht-core#6190

This also includes a separate nginx container to be used on self-hosting scenarios that resolves medic/medic-infrastructure#254

# Usage

### Spinning it up:
To spin it up, checkout this branch in terminal:
```
export COUCHDB_USER=something
export COUCHDB_PASSWORD=secret123
docker-compose -f docker-compose-archv3.yml up
```
#### optional:
If you own a domain, and have port-forwarding for your router along with DNS configured, but need SSL issued you can export your domain:
`export CHT_DOMAIN=cht.example.com`

You can bring your own SSL certs by placing them in the main dir titled `ssl-certificate-key.pem` && `ssl-certificate.pem`, and uncomment the relevant lines underneath the nginx service container configuration in `docker-compose-archv3.yml`

If you want to avoid all this, do not export CHT_DOMAIN, and nginx entrypoint will create self-signed certs. You can use `thisisunsafe` on https://localhost to test

### Tearing it down:
```
Cntrl-C stops the container, and all temporary storage will persist.
docker-compose -f docker-compose-archv3.yml down # tears down the containers, and only persistent volumes will remain on next creation (medic-data, medic-couchconfig, and medic-ssl)
docker volume rm medic-data medic-couchconfig # deletes all project data, passwords and configuration.
```

### Hi, I changed some app code and want to test it in the container world
Yay! 
- Change your API or Sentinel code.
- Rebuild an image locally. From main project directory: `docker build -t hareet-tests-api:version-9000 -f api/Dockerfile .`
- Change the `docker-compose-archv3.yml` to reflect your new image tag. You can use any naming convention since docker will check locally before hitting a repository. You could also comment out the image declaration and change the docker-compose syntax to build a new image, but I would prefer that syntax to exist in a different docker-compose file for local dev setup, if we get there.


# Notes

When thinking about our hosting scenarios (docker-compose self-host and k8s medic-hosted), there were some hacks needed in order for our services to boot in the correct order across fresh installs & restarts while the image remained the same.

Isolated docker containers won't have a boot order, so typically you inject that logic using the entrypoint script. [wait-for-it](https://github.com/vishnubob/wait-for-it) is one of my favorites. Here's how we handle container boot sequence:
- CouchDB comes up
- API recognizes Couch is up, creates necessary db's, locks couch down and creates a service user for API. 
*Hack*: **Since horti doesn't listen on a port, we won't know if the horti container is up and finished installing the app (unless we essentially do the same thing as the horti check progress code and poll couchdb). For our fresh-install scenario, we use horti at the bottom of API's entrypoint script to install the same version of the docker image API app to CouchDB. Our horti isolated container for now, only watches for upgrades and avoids initial install.**
- Sentinel waits for API to come up
- Horti waits for API to come up and only watches for new deployments, does not install.
*Hack*: *In order for horti to upgrade to a new release, the code related to symlinking was commented out in the `dockerize` horti branch which is the current image used in our `docker-compose-archv3.yml`. For our MVP arch v3 implementation, this is the portion of horti code which could be reworked to talk to k8s API. SRE would provide the necessary credentials in an environment variable.*
*Note: Right now, the dockerize horti container will upgrade CouchDB docs if triggered through the admin panel, and you can reload the application and it will display the new release/branch, but the app will error if you try to invoke anything related to that new API or sentinel code. They won't be available in the 3.10 docker image!*
- Nginx can boot whenever
- HAProxy will keep booting until CouchDB is up. 
*We can/should add wait-for-it in haproxy's entrypoint to wait for couchdb, and have API wait for haproxy. Currently, API's entrypoint secures and sets up CouchDB with the given CouchDB admin user talks straight to Couch's port. Then the entrypoint launches the api service pointed to haproxy with its own service credentials.*

For production runs, each service container generates its own password, and recreates that password if temporary storage is destroyed. This gives us the benefit of password rotation and avoids having to share a volume across containers which impacts how we orchestrate containers in our medic-hosted k8s scenario.

### Building the image in CI:
I don't think this should be part of this PR, but part of the Github Actions work. 

After the code is tested the current way, at the point of publishing the npm package, we would also run our docker build commands from the main directory. For now, I think we should only trigger docker builds if specified by the git tag. We should have logic to handle two regex tags, build-* and release-* `docker build -t medicmobile/medic-api:build-$GIT_BRANCH-$DATE-[$GIT_JOB_# || $GIT_CI_#]`. This needs to translate to the same image tag that horti would send to k8s or docker-compose in the Admin/upgrade panel. For example, QA would tag a branch to trigger the build process, then go to gamma.dev admin panel and upgrade to that branch. Eventually, we would like to build and test the docker image as opposed to testing the code and then building the image. @newtewt Tagging you here because I think you are working on GH actions

# Related-PRs
- [couchdb](https://github.com/medic/medic-infrastructure/pull/256)
- [horticulturalist](https://github.com/medic/horticulturalist/pull/60)
- [couch2pg + postgres](https://github.com/medic/medic-couch2pg/pull/57)
*Above should be a draft PR. Sorry*

- api/docker-entrypoint.sh
- sentinel/docker-entrypoint.sh

- nginx/ssl-install.sh
*If a domain is present, uses letsencrypt to issue a cert and insert into our nginx config. If a domain is not present, will self-sign*
- docker-compose-archv3.yml
*Necessary environment variables*: COUCHDB_USER, COUCHDB_PASSWORD

title: Race condition in rules engine / task list interaction can result in a stale tasks list
body:
**Describe the bug**
Because of a race condition that can exist between rules engine and the task controller, the user could end up seeing a stale and incorrect task list.
The reproduction steps I'm about to provide (when a completed task does not disappear from the list) may not be the only situation when this race condition can be triggered. 


**To Reproduce**
1. Push default config (form and tasks). 
2. Login as an offline user with a considerable amount of docs on a slow device. I had 2000 docs (out of which 50 were "current tasks" - that I saw in my task list) and was using a Tecno Y4 (device performance is essential to reproduce the behavior). 
3. Submit a "pregnancy danger sign" form for a contact. This will create a task that will be visible immediately at the bottom of your task list. 
4. Complete this task, by selecting that the patient is not showing danger signs any more. Submit.
5. Observe that the task still exists in the task list, and is not disappearing even after many seconds. 

**Expected behavior**
The completed task should disappear from the task list after a few seconds (though we have no indication that we're actually "reloading" or expecting the task list to be updated). 

**Logs**
There are no relevant logs. 

**Environment**
- App: Webapp
- Browser: Chrome
- Version: reproduced on 3.10, but I suspect 3.9 and 3.8 are also affected.

**Additional context**
The race condition is caused by two distinct events that are in a race, both affecting what the user sees on the screen:
1. RulesEngineService listens to changes and, when it receives a contact/report change, it calls the shared library endpoint that updates the emissions for the affected contacts:
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/js/services/rules-engine.js#L146
This is an *async* operation, as the `subject_ids` that we have access to when we receive the change could be shortcodes, that we need to translate to contact uuids. This requires querying the DB before marking the affected contacts as dirty and, consequently, refreshing their emissions during the next calculation cycle. 

2. TasksController also listens to changes and, like the RulesEngineService, reacts to contact/report and task changes: 
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/js/controllers/tasks.js#L104
After waiting for an arbitrary second (the existence of debounce here is not to serve this purpose, but it's what makes this error less obvious by only being triggered in the lowest performing devices), the controller refreshes the tasks list. 

If both entities (the rules engine and the tasks controller) receive the change in the same "tick", but the "marking contacts as dirty" in (1) takes longer than the task controller (2) waits before requesting tasks, the result will be that the reloaded tasks will be stale, because the contact was not dirty at the moment of refreshing.

# Development

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Manager. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR to the release branch. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version patch`.
- [x] Write an update in the weekly Product Team call agenda summarising development and acceptance testing progress and identifying any blockers. The release manager is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing

Once all issues have passed acceptance testing and have been merged into `master` and backported to the release branch release testing can begin.

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag and when CI completes successfully notify the QA team that it's ready for release testing.
- [x] Create a new document in the [release-notes folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/release-notes) in `master`. Ensure all issues are in the GH Project, that they're correct labelled, and have human readable descriptions. Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/changelog-generator) to export the issues into our changelog format. Manually document any known migration steps and known issues.
- [x] Until release testing passes, make sure regressions are fixed in `master`, cherry-pick them into the release branch, and release another beta.
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`

```
@channel *Announcing the release of {{version}}*

This release fixes {{number of bugs}}. Read the release notes for full details: {{url}}
```
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/), under the "Product - Releases" category. You can use the previous message and omit `@channel`.

title: Update default config to use contact_types that match what is displayed to users
body:
### Problem

There are many inconsistencies in how we refer to or name different hierarchy levels in the default config, default forms, and doc site.

Currently, the hierarchy configuration in the [default config](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/f20cf655da6bf38eea98bb25944619e03cf181ba/config/default/app_settings.json#L289-L344) is:

- `clinic`
- `health_center`
- `district_hospital`

However, these are displayed in the app as

- Household
- Area
- Health Facility

And on the [doc site, for the reference app](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/examples/anc/#forms-hierarchy), as:
- Household
- CHW Area

And in the [generic hierarchy section](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/concepts/hierarchy/#places) as:

- Family
- CHW Area
- Supervisor Area

### Proposal
We should consider updating the contact_types in the default config to be in sync with how users interact with the system. Having different names here is cause for confusion in configuring other areas of the app as well as for analytics. 

### Some background
The reason the contact_types are configured the way they are is due to the legacy way hierarchies were set (they weren't configurable). When the configurable hierarchy feature was added, the default config was updated to use configurable hierarchies, but the names of the contact_types were just copied over from the old config. For mobile app deployments, "households" to the users were stored in the database as "clinics", there was no way around this. Now with configurable hierarchies, it is possible to bring these back into sync and name them the same/more meaningfully.

title: Update  start_webdriver.sh to check the OS and get the version to set.
body:
**Describe the issue**
Currently webdriver-manager will attempt to install the latest version of chromedriver when running e2e tests not in ci. The script we have to find the right version of chrome and chromedriver only works for linux based environments that add `google-chrome` to available commands.  This means you're likely to run into a chromedriver / chrome version difference. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Add an OS check, update the script to then look for chrome in the right place and get the right version. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We do nothing and specify the proper version in the gruntfile when running update and start. 

```
          './node_modules/.bin/webdriver-manager update --versions.chrome 87.0.4280.88 && ' +
          './node_modules/.bin/webdriver-manager start --versions.chrome 87.0.4280.88 > tests/logs/webdriver.log & ' +
```

We submit a PR to webdrivermanager to solve this [issue](https://github.com/angular/webdriver-manager/issues/470)

title: Allow configuring unknown languages
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Configuring new languages will fail if the associated moment and date-picker files aren't included. These files are hardcoded in to the CHT webapp ([here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/3.10.x/webapp/src/js/app.js#L38) and [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/3.10.x/webapp/src/js/enketo/main.js)), and can only be solved by raising an issue ([here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6861) and [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6849)) and releasing a new version of CHT Core. These packages both ship with extensive translation support ([here](https://github.com/moment/moment/tree/develop/locale) and [here](https://github.com/uxsolutions/bootstrap-datepicker/tree/master/js/locales)), but we're only importing a handful of languages we know we need.

We have also had issues in the past with adding a language that these libraries don't support.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Allow app builders to include moment and date-picker (and any other library's) translation files without changes to CHT Core. It should be easy to include the languages maintained by the library developer and possible to provide a completely bespoke file.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
1. Include all translation files. This is very simple, but adds a little bloat and doesn't solve for languages the library doesn't support.
2. Patch the libraries to use our own translation system. This is powerful but likely to be complex and fragile. It also duplicates effort that these libraries already put in to developing their own system and translation values.

title: Improves the overall performance of the app
body:
# Description

Improves the performance of the app by:
1. Updating contacts, reports & tasks lists to render inline templates instead of separate components
2. Switching from ngx-translate directive to ngx-translate pipe (except for situations where we need translate params, where pipes don't accept "inline" objects as params). 
3. Refactoring code that used method calls in templates
4. Attaching broad/expensive jQuery handlers outside of Zone.js
5. Running promise chains where we only care about the final results outside of Zone.js
6. Wrapping PouchDB methods so they run outside of Zone.js. This is done before DbService returns the db object, so no other code changes were/will be required. 
7. Removing calls to `detectChanges` from components that use default change detection strategies
8. Refactoring the mobile detection to avoid forced reflows. 
9. Refactoring contacts effect. 
10. Resetting state on destroy, to minimize next render time. 

Fixes parser logical operator bug where operator precedence was not respected. 
Migrates some telemetry references. 
Fixes bug where filter dropdowns are not closed when navigating away. 
Cleans up main.ts. 

More details about the changes [can be seen here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xDIxPjub-YBnRlt8KDDfLwxMrR29wG_f2TvAcDgOYl8)
Benchmarks [can be seen here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1tdyGmezXOM-94TztISEVNhvy1wd45v-ALM8IwYjC9SE)

title: Ability to access "user permissions" from tasks, targets, and contact-summary
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Contact-summaries

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Task and target code written in cht-app configurations has access to the current logged in user object. This user object is not available in contact-summary scripts. This results in weird hacks like [this](https://github.com/medic/config-muso/blob/master/contact-summary-extras.js#L7) in which is_uhc_enabled is maintained on both the user document and the user's contact document. This means that to enable uhc for a user, we have to turn it on in two places which is a pain.

Knowing the properties of the user that is viewing the contact summary would be useful for situations like "is the current user a supervisor" or "does the current user have a role for which UHC is enabled?"

title: Request: Access to Granular Telemetry Data for Post-Hoc Analysis, Monitoring & Research Initiatives
body:
This ticket is a request for support on accessing and writing granular telemetry data (and other product user metadata) for post-hoc analysis, monitoring & research initiatives. 

Ideally we'd like data to be uploaded daily, though weekly is acceptable, to enable monitoring for trends over time at different temporal intervals.

We'd like to be able to look at these data for specific role permissions, i.e. only for supervisors or in a specific geographic area. 

This work would be a component of a grant and would enable more routine monitoring and data analyses of our telemetry/product user metadata to detect data anomalies and performance differences on the platform within and across user groups.
