title: Ability to view UHC "home visits" in contact summary
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Contact Summaries.  Muso project team has requested to include "household visit metrics" when viewing households. https://github.com/medic/config-muso/issues/157. They would like to see 1) the number of a days a home visit was made, and 2) the most recent home visit. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Calculating "house visits" requires scanning through all reports at both the household-level and the patient-level reports for all patients in the household.  We currently show these metrics on Muso's contact summaries, but the calculations are inaccurate since only the household reports OR the patient-level reports are available to the contact-summary code. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

* Expose more data to the contact-summary code?
* Make this a first-class citizen of the UHC feature-set?
* If the target emissions for the hh visit target were exposed, the contact summary would be able to present an accurate count. In vein with the [targetDoc](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/contact-page/) parameter, but probably too raw to be friendly.

title: Users might start upwards replication from 0 after upgrade
body:
**Describe the bug**
Due to PouchDB internal algorithms and non-deterministic minification results (either from Uglify-js used pre 3.11 or Terser used post 3.11), users could restart upwards replication from 0 after an upgrade. 


**To Reproduce**
Reproducing is pretty tricky as it involves changing some code in way that will change certain variable names in the minified source. I've been pretty successfull in unwillingly triggering this in the migration branch. I'll add a comment if I find an 100% reliable way, but for now:

1. Generate a production build. 
2. Login as an offline user in a browser. Fully replicate, leave the browser tab open, watching the network. 
3. Make some code changes, but don't touch the filter function. Build again. Hopefully your changes will shuffle variable names in the minified source.
4. Sync with the offline user. Reload. 
5. Watching the network tab, sync. 
6. See `_revs_diff` requests (the batch size is 100, so if your user has 500 docs, you should see 5 `_revs_diff` requests).

**Expected behavior**
Users should not start upwards replication from 0. Seeing one _revs_diff request is normal - and should contain references to the latest docs that the user has downloaded from the server: probably only the service-worker-cache. 

**Environment**
- App: webapp
- Version: since this depends on internal workings of external libraries (PouchDB & Uglify-js/Terser), it's impossible to tell how long this has been going on without inspecting each release's minified JS and see how the filter function looked like. If between two releases there'd be changes (even a single character), then the bug would occur when upgrading.

**Additional context**
PouchDB generates a (hopefully) unique and stable replication ID for each replication, and uses some of the replication config options into compiling it. 
https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/blob/1db1700382604ab0dc3ddb337096d99641ea12d8/packages/node_modules/pouchdb-generate-replication-id/src/index.js#L15
One of the config options that is used to generate a replication id is the provided filter function. PouchDb calls the provided value (be it a function, or a string) `toString` method to get a value to use. 
The result of the `toString` call is not deterministic, because the actual code that runs is minified for production use. 
So, if between two versions, the minified string representation of the filter function changes, even if no changes have been made to the function itself, the newly generated replication ids will be different from the existent and cause a restart in replication. 

Fortunately, upwards replication is relatively cheap, as it involves hitting an unfiltered CouchDB endpoint (`_revs_diff`) with every pair of doc _id + _rev that exists on the user's device. For the overwhelming majority of cases, responses from the server will be empty (because the docs already exist on the server as well).

title: Overloads upwards replication filter function's `toString` method
body:
# Description

Given that Terser doesn't provide a way to select pieces of code that it should not minify and any other solution was substantially more complex or risky, overloading `toString` seems like the lesser of most evils.

title: Add an e2e test that simulates an upgrade for an offline user
body:
**Describe the issue**
We currently rely on manual testing to check that upgrades go smoothly between releases and have no e2e test that is designed to monitor that upgrades work. 

I realized, while working on a [separate issue](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/6921), that an e2e test that does an upgrade is needed to check that the replication ids don't change when upgrading. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Add an e2e test to that upgrades from the previous release to the test build. 
This can either be a new flow, or be the 1st test from the current flow - i.e. don't have horti install the test build, rather install the previous release build, login as an offline user, and then upgrade to the test build. 
The rest of the suite should continue like before. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Keep manually testing upgrade compatibility.

title: Release 3.12.0
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create a repo milestone and add this issue to it. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [ ] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Manager for this release.
- [ ] Assign product team members to complete end-user documentation improvements for this release.

# Development - Release Manager

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Manager. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`.
- [x] Raise a new issue called `Update dependencies for <version>` with a description that links to [the documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/guides/update-dependencies/). This should be done early in the release cycle so find a volunteer to take this on and assign it to them.
- [x] Go through all features and improvements scheduled for this release and raise cht-docs issues for product education to be written where appropriate. If in doubt, check with the product manager.
- [x] Write an update in the weekly Product Team call agenda summarising development and acceptance testing progress and identifying any blockers. The release manager is to update this every week until the version is released.
- [x] Announce the kickoff of development for the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org), under the "Product - Releases" category.

# Releasing - Release Manager

Once all issues have passed acceptance testing and have been merged into `master` release testing can begin.

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development using this template:
```
@core_devs I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag and when CI completes successfully notify the QA team that it's ready for release testing.
- [x] [Import translations keys](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/overview/translations/#adding-new-keys) into POE and notify the #translations Slack channel translate new and updated values, for example:
```
@channel I've just updated the translations in POE. These keys have been added: "<added-list>", and these keys have been updated: "<updated-list>"
```
- [x] Create a new document in the [release-notes folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/release-notes) in `master`. Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, that they're correctly labelled (in particular: they have the right Type, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate), and have human readable descriptions. Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our changelog format. Manually document any known migration steps and known issues. Provide description, screenshots, videos, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: medic-conf,  medic-gateway, medic-android). Assign the PR to a) the Director of Technology, and b) an SRE to review and confirm the documentation on upgrade instructions and breaking changes is sufficient.
- [x] Until release testing passes, make sure regressions are fixed in `master`, cherry-pick them into the release branch, and release another beta.

title: New users might be prompted to accept the privacy policy twice or shown the tour modal twice
body:
**Describe the bug**
When a new user logs in (one that is not "known") on an instance that has a privacy policy enabled for the user's language, the user could be prompted to accept the privacy policy twice or be shown the tour twice - in the first 2 consecutive loads (this is a half truth, as things change with different network connection qualities, and the user might see the tour multiple times, but that's not necessarily part of the problem here). 

**To Reproduce**
This is pretty tricky to reproduce reliably, as it requires a race condition to trigger and quick user actions / slow network. 
1. Add a privacy policy for your chosen language.
2. Create a new offline user.
3. Login with this offline user, choosing the language with the privacy policy. 
4. Replicate and accept the privacy policy.
5. Immediately close the tour and all other startup modals (being quick to click is hard!)
6. Reload. 

**Expected behavior**
On next reload, you should see neither the privacy policy nor any of the startup modals (including the tour). 
**If you see either, the bug has happened.**

**Environment**
- Browser: Chrome
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.10, 3.11

**Additional context**
This is caused by a race condition where two actions update the same document, causing a conflict: 
1. Accepting the privacy policy. This edits the user-settings document locally, and relies on replication to upload to the server. '
2. Closing the startup modals. This also edits the user-settings document (setting the `known` property as true), but hits the API endpoint directly, editing the doc directly on the server. 

A local doc edit will trigger upwards replication imemdiately, so it depends on whether this completes before the user closes the tours. 

On next load, the user will perform the required action again (either accepting the policy or closing the tour modal, depending on which rev won) and never have this problem again. 

To repeat testing using the same user, after each try, open the user-settings document (`medic/org.couchdb.user:<username>`) and delete `privacy_policy_acceptance_log` and `known` fields, sync and reload.

title: Mark for outbound might create tasks for already sent jobs
body:
**Describe the bug**
A race condition between Sentinel and API, both creating/saving infodocs, can result in mark-for-outbound creating a task for a document that has already been sent successfully. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Get on a fast and idle server (both important). 
2. Create a very simple config for mark-for-outbound, and disable all other transitions. 
3. Make sure that you mock the server that's supposed to receive your outbound request.
4. Submit a doc that should generate an outbound request.
5. Check that that the request has been sent and that no outboud task exists.
6. Sometimes, you'll find an outbound task for this doc, even if the request was successfully sent.


**Expected behavior**
If the outbound request was successful, the outbound task should not be created.

**Environment**
- App: sentinel
- Version: 3.9, 3.10

**Logs / Additional context**

The reproduction steps are identical to the ones in this e2e test: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/e2e/sentinel/transitions/mark_for_outbound.js - so do find inspiration there concerning how the transition is configured or how the pushed doc should look like. 
This test flakes on occasion with:

```
1) mark_for_outbound when external server is up correctly creates and sends an outbound request immediately
  - Failed: expected 1 to equal 0
```

Upon inspecting Sentinel logs, I found this: 
```
change event on doc <docId> 
isRevSame tested false on transition mark_for_outbound for doc <docId>
calling transition.onMatch for doc <docId> and transition mark_for_outbound 
About to send outbound request 
{
  "url": "http://localhost:41591/working-endpoint",
  "body": {
    "id": "<docId>",
    "rev": "<rev>"
  },
  "json": true,
  "timeout": 10000
} 
result from outbound request 
undefined <- this is expected, the endpoint from the e2e test doesn't return anything! 
Pushed <docId> to test <- means that the outbound task has been sent successfully
Creating outbound task task:outbound:<docId> <- yet, the task was still created! 
finished transition mark_for_outbound doc <docId> is unchanged 
transition results: [false] 
```

Looking at the code here https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/mark_for_outbound.js#L39
we catch all errors and consider the push as failed if there are any. 
Since the request was successful, I suspected that saving the infodoc had failed somehow. 

My hunch was confirmed by the couchdb logs, and seeing that the put had errored with a conflict: 
```
localhost:4984 172.17.0.1 admin PUT /medic-test-sentinel/<docId>-info 409 ok 3
```

title: Arch V3: Making Medic API horizontally scalable
body:
# Description

This PR introduces changes required to make Medic API scale horizontally. 

**Vertical Scaling vs Horizontal Scaling:**

Vertical Scaling: Also called scaling-up. When the capacity of the server is increased in order to handle extra load/traffic. E.g. Upgrade the server from a single core machine with 4GB of RAM to a quad core machine with 16GB of RAM. This can only go so far before you hit a saturation point.

Horizontal Scaling: Also called scaling-out. The number of servers or in container lingo, the number of replicas is increased and not the individual capacity of the server. A load balancer routes traffic to the different replicas based on their current load/availability. This is highly fault tolerant. When the load on the system is very low during the night or on the holidays, the system can scale-in, using fewer resources and saving costs, etc. This brings one closer to paying only for actual usage and high utilization for what one's already paying for.

**PR Details**
This PR seeks to introduce the capability for horizontal scalability for api by breaking api into two components: a helper and launcher processes. The helper starts first and runs initializations and taps into the changes feed to listen for config changes and applies required changes. The launcher process runs the rest of api and listens for requests from users and takes care of routing.

The changes were made in such a way as not to break automation scripts when developing locally. Grunt scripts as well as `node server.js` should work without issues.

When scaling api horizontally, the launcher process is the one that gets scaled-out or scaled-in.

medic/cht-core/issues/6189

title: Prototype integration with CloudWorks' Rapid Diagnostic Toolkit app
body:
As part of our work with CloudWorks we need to build a prototype integration to the [Rapid Diagnostic Toolkit](https://github.com/dimagi/rd-toolkit) Android application.  

The workflow for the prototype will be an assessment form that provisions a test, and then a follow up task which would have a button to check for the status of the test. If the test is still pending, the user could wait in the form to press the button again until the return status is that the test is complete. 


This [integration](https://github.com/dimagi/rd-toolkit/blob/master/docs/usage.md) requires an Enketo widget to provision a test in the RDToolkit app, and another Enketo widget to collect the test result:

> Since tests take a significant amount of time to resolve, the default execution mode is a two phase interaction. The first phase is an activity callout to provision a diagnostic test, and the second phase is request to capture the result of the test.


The result widget would store the return value as a JSON blob for now, with the status being queryable from within the form itself. That way the field could be required, and preventing advancing in the form until a completed/success status is returned.

title: api and webapp can disagree on whether a user has an online or offline role
body:
**Describe the bug**
Because of different ways of determining whether a user has an online or an offline role, api and webapp can sometimes disagree. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Create an offline role. 
2. Create a user for this offline role. Login and check how many docs the user should download.  Log out.
3. Update the config (you can't do this through the UI) and change the role to be online - by simply removing the `"offline": true` flag. 
4. Login with the user again (in a fresh browser).
5. Notice that you're getting the replication screen, no estimate about how many docs you have and and you just download lots of docs very quickly. 

OR:

1. Create an online role. 
2. Create a user for this online role. Login and make sure the user doesn't get the replication screen. Log out. 
3. Update the config (you can't do this through the UI) and change the role to be offline- by simply adding the `"offline": true` flag. 
4. Login with the user again (in a fresh browser). 
5. Notice that you're not getting the replication screen and then none of your lists load (offline users can't request CouchDB views). 

**Expected behavior**
API and Webapp should reach a consensus on whether this user is an online user or an offline user. 

**Logs**
The only suspicious log is that the initial request to `users-info` returns a 403 (because the user doesn't have permission to update users). 

**Screenshots**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/110068248-f5040f00-7d7d-11eb-93fb-7df4f3ebebc5.png)


**Environment**
- Instance: Live instance
- App: Webapp and API
- Version: 3.10

**Additional context**

In webapp, we determine whether a user is online or offline by checking if they have a role called `mm-online`. We don't manage this role when the other user's roles are changed:
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/services/session.service.ts#L112

In API, we actually check the roles' config, checking if the user has at least one role that has the `offline` flag, and completely ignore `mm-online` (the only mention to `mm-online` in API is in user creation). 
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/8e139e976ff785598bcdaf3edcfb8716766adfe4/api/src/auth.js#L65

The workaround, when a user gets into this situation, is to manually update them and add (or remove) the `mm-online` role.

title: Research ability to report on releases/features based off github ticket labels
body:
**Describe the issue**
Is it feasible to deduce when a feature or upgrade or initial launch went live based off the GH ticket and related labels alone?

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
After a chat in PO and R&L meetings and [slack discussions](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C024ZK678/p1614380372007900), based off @n-orlowski 's attempt to figure when #5776 went live for BRAC, let's try and see if we can add labels to GH tickets so that we can know when something went live. 

This likely looks something like:
* coming up with a label nomenclature we could use that would be tenable: detailed enough but not so overbearing that they're too verbose.  
* get sign off from relevant teams (eg Product & App Services) that adding a bunch of tags won't be too much of an imposition
* retroactively add a bunch of labels to some tickets to see if we can tell by close date when something went live and as well to vet the nomenclature has actually usefull

Lot's more scoping to do on these before this is actionable, but this _is_ a research ticket ;)

Lots and looooooots of guessing, asking around, trawling over old GH tickets.

title: Muting transition and update clinics don't handle contacts that use a hardcoded type and also have a `contact_type` property correctly
body:
**Describe the bug**


**To Reproduce**
For `muting`: 

1. Configure muting transition and set a muting form.
2. Create a place. 
3. Mute this place. Make sure Sentinel processes the report before proceeding. 
4. Create a contact under this place, making sure to add a type = `person` and some string in a `contact_type` property. (it's important you do this when you first create the contact, otherwise the code will work correctly!). 
5. Wait till sentinel processes the contact. 
6. Check the contact in the DB and observe it's not muted. The UI will show them as muted, because they are muted in lineage and they will count as muted if attaching schedules to them, but it's not 100% correct, and could prove problematic in some configurations. 

**Expected behavior**
A contact created under a muted place should be muted (in its json). 

**To Reproduce**
For `update_clinics`: 

1. Enable `update_clinics`. 
2. Create a place that has a hardcoded type and add a `refid` property, save some string in the field, also add a `contact_type` field with some string. 
3. Create a doc that looks like an SMS report with a `refid` property that has the same value as the `refid` on your place. Make sure it doesn't have a `contact` property, so update clinics runs. 
4. Wait until sentinel processes the doc.
5. Observe that your doc is not connected to your clinic. 

**Expected behavior**
The connection through the refid should have been processed. 

**Environment**
- App: api, sentinel
- Version: 3.10

**Additional context**
Muting not being saved on new contacts is mostly important for analytics, but the app should look and function as if these contacts were muted. It's possible some configurations that don't check for muting in a contact's lineage could also be affected. 
I'm not sure how the `refid` for update_clinics interaction works in production or if it even is used in production.

body:
**Describe the bug**
A new feature to [validate custom translations](https://github.com/medic/medic-conf/issues/254) was released in [medic-conf 3.4.1](https://github.com/medic/medic-conf/blob/v3.4.1/release-notes.md#340). **To Reproduce**

2. Deploy an instance. 
3. Checkout latest `master` or `3.10.x`. Try to install `standard` config by running `medic-conf --local` or `medic-conf --url=<your url>`. Alternatively, just run the `upload-custom-translations` job. 
4. See a bunch of errors. 

**Expected behavior**
The config should be updated to run with latest version of medic-conf. 

**Logs**
```
ERROR Cannot compile 'hi' translation with key 'messages.d.validation.days_since_birth' has placeholders that do not match any in the base translation provided

title: Changelog-generator script fails when there are too many org open projects
body:
**Describe the bug**
Our [changelog-generator script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/changelog-generator/index.js) fails with an error when there are too many open organization projects. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Checkout latest `master`. Go to `script` and `npm ci`
2. Go to `changelog-generator`. Open the file and check the `usage` comment (and create your `token.json` file that contains a valid token). 
3. Run the script as noted, and set `3.10.3` as the project. 
4. The script fails with: 
```
HttpError: {"message":"Projects are disabled for this repository","documentation_url":"https://docs.github.com/v3/projects"}
    at /home/diana/projects/medic/scripts/node_modules/@octokit/rest/lib/request/request.js:56:19
    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:97:5) {
  code: 410,
  status: undefined,
...<TRUNCATED>
```

**Expected behavior**
The script should run successfully regardless of the number of open projects. 

**Additional context**
The script fails because, apparently, the default page size of the projects API is **30**, while the project in question is **31st** - bad luck - and we don't implement paginated project navigation - which the GitHub API provides. 

The error is caused by the fallback to check repository projects, which is checking `medic` - an archived repo - instead of `cht-core`. 
The script wouldn't work even if the repo was correct, though.

title: Outbound Push- expand functions and syntax
body:

Outbound push has very limited syntax and flexibility around custom functions such as pulling data and using it in the request.

It would be helpful if we could make it more flexible and add custom functioning such as injecting information into a payload then pushing it.

Mature middleware that has this functionality can be integrated into the CHT.

title: Sentinel: Modify muting transition to do nothing if the contact is already muted.
body:
**Describe the bug**
When replicating muted contacts, a document gets the muted attribute updated to the date of replication. This is a source of conflicts.

**To Reproduce**
1. You need two instances, both running sentinel (muting transition)
2. Mute a contact in one instance (tested/observed in version 3.6.0)
3. Replicate the document in a destination (tested/observed in version 3.9.0) preferably on different dates.
4. Notice the document in the destination database gets muted updated to the replication date.

**Expected behavior**
The initial muting date should not be updated.

**Additional context**
Documents replicated from LG Mainstream instance (version 3.6.0) to CIHA instance (version 3.9.0) got the muted attribute updated to the date replication happened, causing conflicts. E.g. this document in the source
```
{
  "_id": "08a9977b-509e-47b4-8c75-03bf909c7726",
  "_rev": "6-f4ef913b23fbbaaa50a4a6d6a24dbc45",
  "name": "Some  Family",
  "type": "clinic",
  "reported_date": 1534867826795,
  "muted": "2020-12-07T07:05:45.405Z"
}
```
replicated to a destination on eb 25, would be updated to
```
{
  "_id": "08a9977b-509e-47b4-8c75-03bf909c7726",
  "_rev": "6-57a19f903726d51caf84487eb2abb1e8",

}
```

title: Form with truthy expression will be displayed despite permissions
body:
**Describe the bug**
A form context can have an `expression` and a `permission`  property. Both should be checked in order to evaluate whether a form can be displayed or not. 
However, if the form has an expression and it evaluates as truthy, the permissions check will be skipped. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Change a form's context to be shown to persons (for simplicity). Remove the `expression` and `permission` properties.
2. Login as a non-admin user and check that the form is displayed as an action for a person contact. 
3. Update the form context and add a `permission` property with `["non existent permission"]`. 
4. As the same user, check that the form is **not** displayed for a person contact.
5. Update the form context and add an `expression` property with the value "true" (quotes included, so string "true", not boolean true in json)
6. As the same user, check that the form **is** displayed for a person contact.

**Expected behavior**

title: Meta db sync throws an empty message error when offline, which generates a feedback doc
body:
**Describe the bug**
When offline and syncing the meta database, PouchDB throws an error that Zone.js thinks is uncaught.
This error has no name or message and is not "skipped" by our feedback service, so it will generate a feedback doc every time.

**To Reproduce**
1. Login as an offline user on `~3.11` on a desktop. Check your metadata db and see how many feedback docs there are.
2. Turn off your network (from the dev tools) and refresh the page **. Keep your console open.
3. Hit "sync" from the hamburger menu.
4. Observe a bunch of errors in the console - expected, the app is trying to sync and it can't, but among these errors is a weird one:
```
Error: Uncaught (in promise): {"name":"Error","message":""}
```
5. Check your local metadata db again and see a new feedback doc has been created for this error.

** Refreshing is so we insure that the forced sync will include the meta db as well. Meta dbs sync once 10 seconds after the app is loaded and then once every 30 minutes (even if you sync from the hamburger menu, unless 30 minutes have passed since the last sync, the meta db will not sync). 

To make sure that the meta sync - and not the medic db sync - is throwing this error:
1. Turn the network back on. Refresh the page.
2. Sync from hamburger menu and wait for replication label to go green (this will have synced your meta db, so it won't sync next time you hit the button). 
3. Turn off network again and sync from hamburger menu (do this within 30 minutes of step 2). 
4. Notice that the empty message error is not logged and you have no new feedback doc.

**Expected behavior**
Logging errors when offline is fine, as it's an expected state. We should not be creating feedback docs for these errors, though.

**Logs**
```
main.js?_sw-precache=e6e30284bb3fa10e63f769ab4c140a36:1 Error: Uncaught (in promise): {"name":"Error","message":""}
    at E (polyfills.js?_sw-precache=76abd25b3b164a682f388e7a347960ef:1)
    at E (polyfills.js?_sw-precache=76abd25b3b164a682f388e7a347960ef:1)
    at polyfills.js?_sw-precache=76abd25b3b164a682f388e7a347960ef:1
    at e.value (polyfills.js?_sw-precache=76abd25b3b164a682f388e7a347960ef:1)
    at Object.onInvokeTask (main.js?_sw-precache=e6e30284bb3fa10e63f769ab4c140a36:1)
    at e.value (polyfills.js?_sw-precache=76abd25b3b164a682f388e7a347960ef:1)
    at t.value (polyfills.js?_sw-precache=76abd25b3b164a682f388e7a347960ef:1)
    at _ (polyfills.js?_sw-precache=76abd25b3b164a682f388e7a347960ef:1)
```

**Environment**
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.11

**Additional context**
This is happening because all promises PouchDB are wrapped by Zone.js.
See this very relevant Angular issue: https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/31680
This was "fixed" by: https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/35873 - which just adds an additional zone flag to disable the wrapping of promise rejections.
Enabling this flag (`__zone_symbol__DISABLE_WRAPPING_UNCAUGHT_PROMISE_REJECTION = true`) does indeed solve the problem, but affects ALL promises, so I think we should find a way to do without.

title: Handle compiled messageformat translations throwing errors with missing translation params
body:
**Describe the bug**
Translations that match `messageformat`'s format, but are not given expected params, are throwing errors.

**To Reproduce**
1. Login as any user.
2. Update the translation document for the language you're using and change a visible translation (for example the one for Reports in the header) to contain curly braces: fe `Reports {thing}`.
3. Got to the frontend.
4. See an error in the console and no text in your header where the "Reports" link exists.

**Expected behavior**
No error should be thrown. You should see the "Reports {thing}" text in your header.

**Logs**
Something along the lines of
```
TypeError: Cannot read property '<what you had between the curly braces>' of undefined
```

**Environment**
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.11

**Additional context**
When migrating from AngularJS to Angular, we had to change a lot of the supporting ecosystem, including the translations library.
The translation library we chose is `ngx-translate`, mainly because it's one of the few options available and the fact that it's API is very similar to `angular-translate`, the library we used before.
As one of the key differences between `angular-translate` and `ngx-translate`, `ngx-translate` implements a pre-compilation step to determine the final version of translations and does not support passing an external "interpolator" at runtime.
Since we were using `messageformat` for pluralization, we needed to pre-compile the translation with `messageformat` in order to make use of pluralization in the app.
This means we need to better filter which translations we should pass to `messageformat` to be compiled ahead of time, instead of deciding on the spot or come up with a way to support picking `messageformat` as an interpolator at runtime (though this might mean creating our own translations library to wrap over `ngx-translate`).

title: Improve how we handle contact loading errors in webapp
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
When any of the steps of loading a contact in webapp fails, loading the contact is stopped and the selected contact is unset. 
To replicate: 
1. Update default config and break the contact summary function, for example add:
```
console.log(thisContact.field.field.field);
```
somewhere in the `contact-summary.template.js` file. This will generate a TypeError: `TypeError: Cannot read property 'field' of undefined`. 
2. Login as any user, go to contacts and try to load any contact. 
3. Observe that the contact begins loading, children and reports appear, but when loading contact-summary, the contact detail page unloads and displays "No person selected". If in mobile view, you're also shown the list instead of the contact page. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We should display an error page, and inform the user that there were errors while loading the contact. 
Our template even has a check for this and can display this error, so this functionality existed at some point. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Keep it as it is. 

**Additional context**
I'm unsure when this came to be. The likely culprits are:
1. When we added redux in ~3.5.x
2. When we added lazy loading of contacts in ~3.4.x

title: Improve behaviour consistency of empty state for webapp tabs
body: **What feature do you want to improve?** When there's an empty state some tabs will automatically select the first item and show it, but some others don't do this or don't do this after an item deletion. Examples: 1. When a item is deleted: - Messages tab doesn't redirect from **/messages/[id]** to **/messages** and it doesn't select first item in the list - Reports tab redirect from **/reports/[id]** to **/reports** and it doesn't select another report - Contact tab redirect to parent contact and select it and display information. 2. When loading from empty state - Messages tab select first item when loading **/messages** (no id in url) - Reports tab doesn't select first item when loading **/reports** (no id in url) - Contacts tab doesn't select item when loading **/contacs** (no id in url) if it's admin, but it does select an item when login in as offline user. **Describe the improvement you'd like** Implement consistent behaviour in tabs (messages, tasks, contacts, reports) to improve user experience about what to expect during empty state. **Describe alternatives you've considered** We need feedback about what gives more value to the user and that won't increase confusion. It can be either: - Load an item on empty state - Not load item on empty state - Redirect to tab's root url after delete (/message)

title: Improve admin translations UX
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
The admin app translations interface allows you to select which languages to use for the side-by-side display, and edit one key at a time. By default, the selected side-by-side languages are English (left) and 1st language (alphabetically) on the right, but can be changed to any combination or languages, or to show translation keys. 

However, the dropdowns are both reset when a translation edit is made. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Language select dropdowns should not reset after translations edits. One should be able to continue editing without having to select displayed languages after every edit. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Alternatively, for my scenario specifically, where I want to search by translation key, several options can be considered:

body:
Run performance tests on a simulated architecture v3 setup and architecture v2 setup and gather metrics from each in order to determine the degree of performance improvements to be expected from a move from v2 to v3.

We have enough of the required pieces available now to be able to manually set up (aka "cobble together") such a test without needing to write all the code/config to make everything production-ready.

For the purpose of the test, the 2 setups should match as closely as possible, only differing in the specific parts that make v2 and v3 different. This is meant to be a test, so keep it as low-effort as possible and throwaway code/config is fine.

title: Ability to complete tasks after they are Failed
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Muso users are experiencing problems in which they are unable to complete tasks through the CHT on time for a host of on-the-ground challenges (battery, phone unavailable, etc). However - they are completing the task on time in-person and have the completed information on paper. Users are unable to enter this data into the CHT system because the task has disappeared and so they wish to have a way to complete the task after it has failed/expired.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
"Failed tasks" are stored in task documents. It's possible to have some sort of _missed tasks_ section in the tasks tab - or something similar.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
There are some proposed workarounds:

1. We can extend task windows to display tasks for a very long time. But since there are often daily follow-ups, this is very confusing in the UI since there are multiple identical tasks with overlapping time windows.
2. We can create an experience for a "missed followup" action via the contacts tab. We can make calculations in the contact-summary to know "what was the last assessment", "which follow-ups were missed", etc and pass that data into the follow-up forms. The downside here is that a) it's kinda hard, and b) the task completion data isn't captured properly in task documents (task-completion statistics). 

Currently, @loukmantidjani @Fatoufall are in discussions with Muso for how to proceed.

**Additional context**
https://github.com/medic/config-muso/issues/235

title: CHT hosting improvements for App Developers
body:
### Describe the issue
CHT app developers, primarily App Services, currently use [CHT-Core Starter](https://github.com/medic/app-services-team/tree/master/cht-core-starter) (private repo) to do development for specific CHT deployments.  Starter's goal is to enable easy "one liner" deployments of CHT instances in a local dev environment.  

It, along with the complimenting [docker compose](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/tutorials/local-setup/) and [development](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/DEVELOPMENT.md) approaches, faces some challenges:
* Current docker-compose option doesn't start reliably - 403 errors, 404 errors, 
* Docker or bare-metal installs have large internet requirements to use ngrok to get around serviceworker limitations. This is slow b/c routes local traffic via internet
* Multiple projects at the same time are hard (either literally concurrent to compare configs side by side, or working on 3 different deployment serially through out a day)
* Starter can be overly aggressive in deleting ~/.horticulturalist/deployments every time :(
* Starter downloads specific version every time (eg downloading 3.10 w/i horti) 

As well, there's a number of problem tickets related to this (some are dupes of above):
* [One-line app developer experience](https://github.com/medic/app-services-team/issues/72) 
* [Local config: Docker failed to create couchDB account - 404 Not Found](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6456)
* [medic-os docker: Research nginx not starting causing 404s ](https://github.com/medic/medic-infrastructure/issues/293)
* [Cannot login on localhost as restricted user ](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6168)
* [Publish a dev version of the docker-compose.yml](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6455)

### Describe the improvement you'd like
We should offer a public facing, docker based solution for App Developers that:
* caches as much as possible to avoid re-downloading CHT versions & docker images.  This will help greatly for developers who might be bandwidth constrained. 
* supporting the trifecta of macOS* / Windows WSL 2 / Linux development environments (_* - watch out for M1_)
* Offer dockerized version of couchdb to avoid having to run in couchdb in bare-metal (in WSL2 for example)
* support CHT back to version 3.5 and up to any posted version in GH (releases, betas & alphas)
* **Added Apr 22 '21** - Work in Architecture V2 so App Developers are developing on near identical configuration as to what is running in product
*  **Added Apr 22 '21** - Permit access to Fauxton (see [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6455#issuecomment-637047221))
*  **Added Apr 22 '21** - Work on which ever ports are open to avoid port collision (see [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/6962#issuecomment-785606008) and [here](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/self-hosting/#port-conflicts))
*  **Added Apr 22 '21** - Offer Valid SSL support out of the box to support android development (see [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6168))

### Describe alternatives you've considered
Continue using starter, docker-compose and bare-metal installs as we do today.

title: Admin upgrade page shows all upgrades as potentially incompatible
body:
**Describe the bug**
The upgrade page shows all releases as potentially incompatible regardless of what the base version is.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Go to App Management > Upgrade instance

**Expected behavior**
- Final releases (version format `x.y.z`) that are less than the currently installed version are hidden.
- Final releases that are greater than the currently installed version are shown *without* a "potentially incompatible" warning.
- Other releases with unknown versions (eg: branch releases) are shown *with* a "potentially incompatible" warning.

For example, in the screenshot below, 3.11.0 should _not_ have the warning icon, because we know 3.11.0 is compatible with the currently installed 3.10.3.

**Logs**
None.

**Screenshots**
![Screenshot from 2021-04-21 14-54-29](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2064938/115623415-44fa5d80-a34d-11eb-983f-73e4ca8b3d4c.png)

**Environment**
- Instance: demo-cht.dev
- Browser: Firefox
- Client platform: Linux
- App: admin
- Version: 3.10.0, 3.11.0

**Additional context**

This warning is based on the `deploy_info` property in the `medic` ddoc. Before upgrading the value for this was...

```json
  "deploy_info": {
    "timestamp": "2021-03-24T15:33:58.070Z",
    "user": "medic",
    "version": "3.10.3"
  }
```

I debugged [this line](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/admin/src/js/controllers/upgrade.js#L121) in the Upgrade controller which checks for the `base_version` which is undefined above. We should either store the `base_version` when upgrading, or use the `version` when the `base_version` is undefined.


**Why Now?**
Partner(s): Internal
Reason(s): A partner will have CHWs/Supervisors with a detrimental experience, thus providing bad care

title: Single quotes escaping `'` rendered wrong
body:
**Describe the bug**
We use the library [npmjs.com/.../properties](https://www.npmjs.com/package/properties) in CHT core that is also used in other components like the [POE scripts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/scripts/poe) to import translations from POEditor, and the library [@medic/translation-checker](https://github.com/medic/translation-checker) that is used by medic-conf and the poe scripts mentioned. The "properties" library has a bug: it does not take into account [single quotes escaping](https://www.mscharhag.com/java/resource-bundle-single-quote-escaping) when there are `{{..}}` arguments in the text.

Although there is no clear specification about the .properties file format, most programs interpret the value of the following:

    sys.form_not_found = Fomu ''{{form}}'' haipatikani.

As:

    Fomu '{{form}}' haipatikani.

And POEditor is not the exception, when we write translations in the POE web editor, we don't care how to escape characters, so we write the value of a translation key like this:

![POEditor_translation_with_escaped_quotes](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1608415/115752982-08405d80-a371-11eb-9a79-cfff635568bc.png)

But the final result when we execute the poe script to import the translation from the POE API is:

    sys.form_not_found = Fomu ''{{form}}'' haipatikani.

Which is right, but again, the value rendered by Angular will be `Fomu ''{{form}}'' haipatikani.` instead of `Fomu '{{form}}' haipatikani.` (with the `{{form}}` replaced by the variable value).

**Environment**
- cht-core version: tested in master, v3.11 and bellow
- medic-conf version: tested in master, v3.5.0 and bellow
- translation-checker: v1.0.0 is the version linked in cht-core and medic-conf

**Additional context**
We could just leave in the .properties files the single quotes without escaping, is even more clear to read, but we relay on POEditor for translations that does the export following the format spec, and even if we add some changes in the poe scripts to post-process the content and remove the escapes, we shouldn't use "custom" made formats for any type of content.

A good solution would be to use another library, the one we use does not have new releases the last 7 years, and the project has a lot of bug not solved. Also has other limitations like the API does not provide "meta" info of the content parsed, like the line where each key / value pair was read, which could be useful to better highlight errors in the translations files.

However this is not a big issue, we should use double quote char `"` in our translations instead of the single one `'`.

Finally, it does not cause the CHT to crash, so I wouldn't consider the error important.

CC @garethbowen

title: Adds offline muting
body:
# Description

Muting is now be processed client-side, for offline users. To run transitions on the client, no config changes are required. However, it is possible to disable client-side muting by updating the config like: 
```json
"transitions": {
  "muting": { "client_side": false }
}
```

Also: 
Splits validation into own shared lib to be used from webapp.
Updates validation to be promise based (some QOL but kept changes to a minimum). 
Updates lineage to use all known docs when building subject lineages (so when we can have hydration for new reports + new contacts out of the box). 
Consolidates the get-message logic into message-utils to be used by validation and transitions.
Consolidates getLocale into message-utils.

Offline muting happens on the device, with the transition code running over docs before they are saved into the local database, following a few rules:
1. Only new docs are processed
2. When a batch contains both muting and unmuting forms, only unmuting forms will be processed, while the muting forms will be ignored.
3. The actions performed over docs are: 
 - when a muting / unmuting report is submitted, local relevant contacts are updated. This follows the same rules as server-side muting, where muting cascades downwards and unmuting cascades upwards.
 - when a new contact is added under a muted parent, it also becomes muted
 - reports get an "client_side_transitions" property to log which transitions have run over them
 - validation runs over reports, with invalid reports being ignored by the transition and validation errors saved in their json. Validation errors are generated in the user's selected language and are visible on the report's detail page. 
 - contacts get a "muting_history" property, to log every muting/unmuting event that has been processed on the device, and which "service" updated the muted state last (options are "server_side" or "client_side")
 - the "muted" property on the contact is still the property that determines if the contact is muted or not, so configs and queries don't require changes. 
4. Except the muting/unmuting reports and the relevant contacts (as described above), no other docs are edited directly -  registrations are not silenced and the config is still responsible with handling muted contacts (cancelling tasks, updating targets. contact summary and etc). 
5. It's necessary to process docs before they are saved, otherwise there is a high risk of generating conflicts on every muting event, if the device has a strong internet connection and Sentinel is up to date (and both device and Sentinel process the event at the same time). 


Server-side muting is updated to handle offline muting:
1. When a contact is processed, its "muting_history.last_update" is updated to "server_side" and an entry is added to the infodoc muting_history.
   If the contact is muted, the muted property is updated with the server's current date (for consistency).
   The contact's offline "muting_history" event log is left untouched and is **not** merged into the infodoc muting_history (to avoid adding complex logic around handling doc conflicts and ending up with muting_history events stored in infodocs that happened only for losing revs).
2. Muting/unmuting reports that were processed offline are always processed sever-side, even if their subjects are already in the correct state (because offline muting doesn't silence registrations, and offline devices don't have access to the whole hierarchy to perform correct muting).
   Additionally, for every contact that is updated, the offline "muting_history" event log is inspected and searched for the muting event corresponding to the currently processed report. If a matching event is found, every other following event is collected to be replayed. 
   After processing all contacts, the collected list of muting events to be replayed is sorted chronologically (this sorting is imperfect, as dates from devices are not reliable, but some sorting is necessary and this is the only data that is available). This results in a sorted list of report uuids. Muting is (re)run over every corresponding report, in sequence and in order, even if muting already ran. 
   Replaying events that were processed on the client (ideally in the same order they were submitted) is necessary because there are little chances for Sentinel to process these events in this ideal order (mainly because the changes feed is not ordered and the position of a doc in the feed is not correlated with when it was created, rather with when it was updated/synced/read from a shard).
3. When receiving a contact that was last_updated offline, Sentinel processes it - to solve the problem of the muting/unmuting report being deleted before it was synced. 
   

The code tries to handle most situations that might arise, in an effort to make the muting action idempotent:
- a composite form that creates a new place, + new persons in the place and mutes this new place (which should mute the new place and the new persons in the place)
- a composite form that creates a new place + new persons in the place and mutes the person (which should only mute the new person)
- a composite form that creates a new person under a muted parent and unmutes the person or any other ancestor (which should unmute all contacts under the topmost muted ancestor). 
- multiple muting/unmuting events processed on the client and then synced out of order. 
- deletion of muting/unmuting reports before syncing

However, there could be situations where muting client-side could yield inconsistent results: for example if settings are updated, so a device and Sentinel run muting over the same doc with different settings, could result in contacts being muted but registrations not silenced. Additionally, the behavior might not be consistent when reports are edited before they are synced (and one contact is muted on the client-side and another contact is muted server-side). 

medic/cht-core#6737

title: Store users' selected language in telemetry and feedback docs
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
As a consequence of https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7068, it's no longer possible to know what language users have selected, since it's no longer stored in the `user-settings` document.


**Describe the improvement you'd like**
I think the currently selected language should be stored in all feedback and telemetry documents. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None. 

**Additional context**
Given that plenty of bugs have been isolated when a specific language was used, with some of these critically affecting production instances, it's extremely important that this information is available, accurate and relatively fresh. 

Data analysis might also find it useful to have this information, but maybe could cope with more stale data.

Running transition end to end tests fails on MacOS. The bug was traced to the package we use to read logs

title: Can't submit forms against muted contacts
body:
**Describe the bug**
We show a modal when before opening an action against a muted contact in webapp: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/117460214-f35cf000-af54-11eb-99b9-f556ad80660f.png)

The modal should close and do nothing if user clicks "No", but should redirect to the form if user clicks "Yes". 
Clicking "Yes" does nothing. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Deploy 3.11. 
2. Mute a contact (quick is to just add a `muted` property in the doc's json)
3. Open the contact in webapp and click to open a form against them (make sure this is not an unmuting form). Click yes in the popup. 
4. You're not redirected when you click yes. 

**Expected behavior**
You should be redirected when clicking yes. 

**Logs**
No logs.

**Environment**
- App: Webapp
- Version: 3.11

**Additional context**
This is a regression in 3.11 and is a one liner fix.

title: Send form_not_found Notifications to Known Senders Only
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
In SMS or collect projects, we have users who are registered (known senders) in the system, but submit invalid forms to the system. We want to be able to send them [notifications to guide them in their form submissions](https://github.com/medic/config-cdc-mohke-dsru/issues/3). When the `forms_only_mode` is set to true, all valid and invalid messages are created as reports, with appropriate error codes issued, however, we still cannot send notifications to registered users **ONLY**. The notifications are sent to unregistered users as well, and we don't want that.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Possible solutions:
- Add a form code that represents the infinite set of form inputs that are not configured, so that a user is able to receive notifications through reminders or alerts.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Using `form validations`, `reminders`, `conditional_alerts` and `multi_report_alerts` all require that the forms be known (configured) in the system.

title: 6915  - Telemetry daily frequency
body:
# Description

Change telemetry frequency from monthly to **daily**.

medic/cht-core#6915

### Improvements

- Telemetry frequency changed from monthly to daily.
- The id of a telemetry record now looks like `telemetry-<year>-<month>-<day>-<username>-<uuid>`. Also in the `metadata` section a new field `day` is added with the day of the month the data belongs to.
- More test coverage in the telemetry spec.
- Minor improvements in the script to collect meta data from a terminal (`scripts/get_users_meta_docs.js`):
  - Output errors in the standard error stream to see the errors in the console while piping results to a JSON file.
  - Add Unix exec permission and header to execute the script without the `node ` prefix.

Please also review the documentation changes [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/pull/493).

### Bug fixed

It also fix the following ~bugs~ bug found in the current implementation:

When `record()` is called for the first time in the period (a period was a month, now is a day), the record is added to the telemetry DB and then the aggregation is executed with the data that was stored previously, so the aggregation process aggregates all the records from the previous period + a record that is actually from the current period. The last record shouldn't be taken into account in the aggregation submitted.

This represents a minor issue even for daily reports, and it is fixed in this PR just changing the order of the execution: executing first the aggregation if a new period started, and then add the new record.

### Backward compatibility

Systems that rely on telemetry data will need to adequate to the new frequency, but so far the data collected and the schema is the same, with the only addition of the new field `metadata.day`.

There is no special code to "migrate" existent data collected in the devices where the new version is installed: if a device was collecting telemetry data to send next month and then the new version is installed, the app will aggregate the data collected the same day the device is used, and send the aggregation when connection is available, but the record will look like a "daily" aggregation, not monthly, or more precisely "partially monthly". E.g.:

1. A device is in sync with a CHT v3.11 deployment and has been sending monthly aggregation for a while. Last time it sent an aggregation report was May 2nd with the data collected previous month (April). So the id of that reports is something like `telemetry-2021-4-greg-aaabbb1234`.
2. Now is May 12, so the device was recording telemetry data since May 2. All these records were not aggregated yet.
3. On May 13 CHT v3.12.0 is deployed, and the same day the app is synced. The new frequency algorithm is applied so data collected from May 2 to May 13 is aggregated and sent as it was data collected from the last recorded day May 2, the id of the record will be: `telemetry-2021-4-2-greg-aaabbb1234`.
4. Next day data sent will be truly daily aggregated. On May 14 the device will aggregate the data collected on May 13 and the record id will be: `telemetry-2021-5-13-greg-aaabbb1234`. Next day if there is data collected will be `telemetry-2021-5-14-...` and son on. Days that the devices is not used won't have telemetry recorded therefore no reports to send.

So once a upgrade of the CHT is rolled out, first reports will include data from many days, but should be easy to identify these reports because the month in the id (or the field `metadata.month`) will be from the past month, not the current month. If we want to implement a more smooth transition, like send one report for each day the telemetry data has not been aggregated, will require more changes, specially in the device webapp, and not sure if it worth the effort.

CC @helizabetholsen and @dianabarsan on this, let me know if is not clear enough.

### ~To-do~ in another app / issue

medic-couch2pg has a PG view [useview_telemetry](https://github.com/medic/medic-couch2pg/blob/master/libs/medic-users-meta/migrations/202102191153.do.54-create-couchdb-users-meta-table.sql#L20-L31) with the telemetry data, and there is a field field `period_start` that we need to adapt to support these changes. I've created a ticket to keep track of it: [medic-couch2pg#85](https://github.com/medic/medic-couch2pg/issues/85)  →  released in 3.3.0

- [x] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the [style guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/style-guide/), documented if necessary.
- [x] Documented: Configuration and user documentation on https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/pull/493
- [x] Tested: Unit and/or e2e where appropriate
- [x] Backwards compatible: Works with existing data and configuration or includes a migration. Any breaking changes documented in the release notes. --> discussion above.

title: Adds telemetry for replication requests
body:
# Description

The following telemetry records are added: 

| key | value | recorded | 
| --- | ------- | -------- | 
| `replication:user-initiated`  | 1 | when the user clicks "Sync now" | 
| `replication:<database>:<direction>:success` | number representing how long in took to replicate, in ms | when replication is successful | 
| `replication:<database>:<direction>:failure` | number representing how long in took to replicate, in ms | when replication is failed | 
| `replication:<database>:<direction>:failure:reason:offline:client` | 1 | replication fails because of connection error and the app detects the client is offline | 
|  `replication:<database>:<direction>:failure:reason:offline:server` | 1 | replication fails because of connection error and the app detects the client is online | 
| `replication:<database>:<direction>:failure:reason:error` | 1 | replication fails because of other errors |
| `replication:<database>:<direction>:docs` | number of replicated docs | For one-directional, stores number of "read" docs, for sync, stores sum of read docs for every direction. | 
| `replication:medic:<direction>:ms-since-last-replicated-date` |  number in ms representing the difference between now and when the client last replicated successfully | only recorded for medic database, every time replication is attempted | 
| `replication:medic:<direction>:denied` | 1 | when replication is denied | 

Unless otherwise specified, <database> and <direction> placeholders stand for any combination of:
| database | direction | 
| --- | --- | 
| `medic` | `from` or `to`  | 
| `meta` | `sync` |

title: Disable dynamic translation by fully loading translations before rendering UI
body:
**Describe the issue**
We attempt to follow best practice by using async translation so that if the translation file isn't yet loaded it'll block execution. However for various reasons we still do use instant translation and assume it'll be fine, and it usually is.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
If we block to guarantee we've loaded the translation file _before_ we render anything then we can use instant translation everywhere. This will clean up the code and make the current instant translations consistent and also provide some performance improvements. Potential downsides are slower first load time (make sure to profile the change before committing it), and potential regression in the ability to dynamically change the language (test this out and if necessary prompt the user to reload the page).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The latest best practice is to ship pre-translated templates but this is difficult with our configurable translations as they'd have to be dynamically translated on the server.

body:

title: Monitoring sentinel backlog values are wrong
body:
**Describe the bug**
The monitoring `sentinel.backlog` value is incorrect, as it counts changes depending on the value from the deprecated `_local/sentinel-meta-data` doc. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Load a 3.11 or 3.10 instance. Make sure you added some docs and Sentinel cleared the queue. The update a contact. Wait for Sentinel to clear the queue again. 
2. Request `api/v1/monitoring` and check the `sentinel.backlog`
3. Value is above 0. - the actual value can differ, if you just installed, it will be equal to the number of docs in the database, if you upgraded or you have an old `_local/sentinel-meta-data` doc, it will count changes depending on values stored in this doc. 

**Expected behavior**
The value should be correct.
Even if sentinel is "up to date", this value doesn't have to be 0. Sentinel skips from processing some docs and when a doc is skipped, the update_seq doesn't advance. 
To make sure that the value gets to 0, update a doc that will be processed, for example a contact or a report. 

**Environment**
- App: api
- Version: 3.10, 3.11, 3.12

**Additional context**
In `3.10` we [changed](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/6408) the doc where Sentinel keeps its transition update_seq from  `_local/sentinel-meta-data` to `_local/transitions-seq` but the monitoring service code was not updated with this change.

title: "Sync Now" should synchronize "meta" database when pressed
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
When users press **"Sync Now"** , only the device's main database is synchronized (the database with the reports, tasks, messages..). The "meta" database that contains feedback and telemetry documents is only synchronized by a _cron_ job each 30 min, and if there is no connection by the time, another 30 min of waiting are needed to successfully synchronize.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
When user clicks "Sync Now", the meta DB should also be synchronized. One synchronization shouldn't affect the sync of the another.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
This was not requested by any particular partner or user, but would be a nice to have now that we are increasing the quality and sync frequency of "meta" data. Also is a one line patch, that going to attach to the issue.


**Additional context**
The size of the request needed to do the synchronization is still little data, it won't affect data caps if the data is synchronized with a mobile data plan instead of WiFi, because taking into account compression used by the devices and that only new data is syncronized, only a few kilobytes are consumed. Moreover, because we put the user in control of when to synchronize, we avoid waste of data spend by requests made automatically by the app because the user can choose to do the sync when is connected to a WiFi connection.

title: Record device id in feedback docs
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently, feedback docs contain some key information which is useful for debugging purposes, like: the app version, users' roles, and the active url. However, in some cases, it's very useful to know for certain that multiple feedback docs were generated on the same device (since the same user could be logged in on multiple devices). 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Store the device Id in feedback docs. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

title: Tasks fail to load when priority labels are empty
body:
**Describe the bug**
ngx-translate (which is the tool we use to internationalize webapp) throws an error when it gets passed an empty string as a translation key. 
When using a nools-based config (non-declarative) there are no constraints on tasks priority labels. 
For declarative config, need to be undefined or be at least one character long: https://github.com/medic/medic-conf/blob/master/src/lib/validate-declarative-schema.js#L128
Having an empty string as a task priority label will stop the tasks list from loading. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Deploy 3.11 with a nools based config
2. Update a task and set its priority label to an empty string. 
3. Login as an offline user and trigger the task to generate. 
4. See error when loading tasks

**Expected behavior**
Tasks should load correctly. 

**Logs**
```
Error: Parameter "key" required
        at TranslateService.instant (projects/ngx-translate/core/src/lib/translate.service.ts:439:13)
        at RulesEngineService.translateProperty (_karma_webpack_/src/ts/services/rules-engine.service.ts:344:4)
        at http://localhost:9876/_karma_webpack_/src/ts/services/rules-engine.service.ts:390:4
        at Array.forEach (<anonymous>)
        at RulesEngineService.translateTaskDocs (_karma_webpack_/src/ts/services/rules-engine.service.ts:369:3)
        at apply (_karma_webpack_/main.js:298517:20)
        at ZoneDelegate.invoke (_karma_webpack_/node_modules/zone.js/dist/zone.js:400:30)
        at ProxyZoneSpec.onInvoke (_karma_webpack_/node_modules/zone.js/dist/zone-testing.js:301:43)
        at ZoneDelegate.invoke (_karma_webpack_/node_modules/zone.js/dist/zone.js:399:56)
        at Zone.run (_karma_webpack_/node_modules/zone.js/dist/zone.js:160:47)
```

**Environment**
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.11

**Additional context**
The workaround (thanks to @derickl ) is to set the task labels to be undefined. 
This bug might affect other areas of the app where we accept translation keys from configuration.

title: Require additional permission for accessing the upgrade page and/or upgrade api endpoint
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
At the moment, any user with "can_configure" permission can initiate an upgrade. The "can_configure" is a very broad permission with makes a user akin to an admin, and is required to enable users to make any config/app/users changes. However, more granularity would be desirable to reduce risk of accidental/unplanned upgrades. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Add an additional permission for accessing the upgrade page - or still permit access, but show a message that the user doesn't have the required permission to upgrade. Additionally, the same permission should be required to access the /upgrade api endpoint. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Leave everything unchanged.

title: Add more granularity to permissions scheme for the admin app
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently, the admin app access is not granular. 
There are three permissions that are used to access the admin app:
- `can_configure` enables the user to do everything
- `can_view_outgoing_messages` enables the outgoing messages tab only
- `can_export_all` enables the export tab only

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We should consider defining personas for users who access the admin app and add roles for each persona. For example: 
- a user that updates translations
- a user that can update the branding / partners / privacy policies / header tabs
- a user that creates/updates other users
- etc

Each persona should have their own permission(s) that are required to access various parts of the app. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
An alternative to personas would be to define a permission for each page, but that could be overkill.

title: Initial user creation fails when CouchDB admin username contains uppercase characters
body:
**Describe the bug**
When starting the services for the first time with a fresh (empty) CouchDB instance (particularly as described in the [DEVELOPMENT documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/DEVELOPMENT.md)), if the username for the initial admin user for CouchDB contains uppercase characters, that user will not be able to login to Medic.  All of the servers will start successfully, but the login for the existing admin user will fail.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Follow the [DEVELOPMENT steps](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/DEVELOPMENT.md) for starting the framework, except, instead of using the recommended `myadminuser` as the CouchDB admin username, use something with uppercase characters like `MyAdminUser`.
2. Once you have started the webapp and the API, navigate to `http://localhost:5988/medic/login` and try to login with your CouchDB admin username/password
3. The login will fail with a 401

**Expected behavior**
Under normal circumstances, [Medic does not allow](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/6e82151d120e57f2332d6cc1ea78da7a5bae69f9/api/src/controllers/create-user-db.js#L8) for creating users with usernames that contain banned characters (such as uppercase). Any old Medic users that happened to have invalid usernames should be corrected automatically by the [extract-user-settings](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/src/migrations/extract-user-settings.js) migration. So, normal users added via the API should not encounter this problem. It is just existing users from CouchDB. 

It seems like we should try to find a more graceful way to handle this situation. Perhaps if the lower case version of the username fails, we try the case as entered or if we want to still fail the login, at least fail with a more helpful message...

**Environment**
- Instance: local
- Browser: Chrome
- Client platform: Linux
- Version: 3.11.0 (master)

title: Fix missed jobs from schedules ahead of time less than 1 second
body:
# Description

Fix missed jobs from schedules ahead of time less than 1 second.

medic/cht-core#6634

- The issue was fixed replacing the use of `later.setTimeout` by the native `setTimeout` and the milliseconds ahead that is calculated before hand, taking into account the difference between "now" and the schedule to not be less than 1 second.
- Add regression tests.
- Minor refactor: method `getSchedule` was repeated in the code twice.

## About the error and how to test it

Doing some tests I found a bit different scenario of why this happen. Contrary to what we think, timers are likely to be executed in less than 1 seconds, here is a small test that can be executed under the `sentinel` folder (because it has the `later` dependency in the `node_modules`):

```js
$ sudo date --set="2021-06-09T14:59:59.900Z" && node -e "
  var later = require('later');
  console.log('Date from Node:', new Date());
  var cron = later.parse.cron('00 * * * *');
  var schedule = later.schedule(cron);
  console.log('Next 3 schedules:', schedule.next(3));
  later.setTimeout(()=> console.log('Schedule executed at', new Date()), cron);
"
```

The output:

```
Wed 09 Jun 2021 11:59:59 AM -03
Date from Node: 2021-06-09T14:59:59.923Z
Next 3 schedules: [
  2021-06-09T15:00:00.928Z,
  2021-06-09T16:00:00.928Z,
  2021-06-09T17:00:00.928Z
]
Schedule executed at 2021-06-09T15:00:00.932Z
```

Basically it crates a cron to be executed at 00 minutes of any hour, the process is launched 100 millis before 12:00 UTC, and it works (tried dozens of times, all them worked, and you have to have disable automatic Date & Time sync in your system).

Then if you try to do the same but milliseconds AFTER, despite an entry is created to be executed, the scheduling for that first entry is not executed (`2021-06-09T15:00:00.117Z`):

```
$ sudo date --set="2021-06-09T15:00:00.090Z" && node -e "
  var later = require('later');
  console.log('Date from Node:', new Date());
  var cron = later.parse.cron('00 * * * *');
  var schedule = later.schedule(cron);
  console.log('Next 3 schedules:', schedule.next(3));
  later.setTimeout(()=> console.log('Schedule executed at', new Date()), cron);
"
Wed 09 Jun 2021 12:00:00 PM -03
Date from Node: 2021-06-09T15:00:00.112Z
Next 3 schedules: [
  2021-06-09T15:00:00.117Z,
  2021-06-09T16:00:00.117Z,
  2021-06-09T17:00:00.117Z
]
```

However testing the bug with the application is almost impossible, because even configuring the system clock to a fixed time like the tests above don't warranty at what time the main loops starts, and how much it takes to reach the purging timer. The only way I could reproduce the error consistently was adding 2 regressions tests to this PR, both uses real timers instead of fake ones because was not possible to test it properly with the ones provided by the sinon mocking library.

I tried the following that only failed in master as expected one time, and at this point I'm not even sure whether the failure was because I did configure the cron wrong in the DB or was the perfect timing to reach the bug.

First setup the purge scheduling as described [here](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/performance/purging/) in Couch at http://localhost:5984/_utils/#database/medic/settings with something like:


```js
{
  ...
  "settings": {
    ...
    "purge": {
      "fn": "function(userCtx, contact, reports, messages) { const old = Date.now() - (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 365); return reports.filter(r => r.reported_date < old).map(r => r._id);}",
      "cron": "*/5 * * * *"
    },

  }

```

The purging is configured to run each 5 minutes on each minute that is multiple of 5: 0, 5, 10, ...

Then execute:


```
sudo date --set="2021-06-14T19:50:00.010Z" && node server.js
```

In `master` you won't see the purging process being executed, and after 5 minutes, it may not be executed either. But switching to this branch, you will see in the logs that the purging is executed both at the beginning and after 5 min:

```
2021-06-14 16:50:01 INFO: Running server side purge 
...
2021-06-14 16:50:01 INFO: Server Side Purge completed successfully in 0.0009530372333402435 minutes

```
