title: Release 4.2.0
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [ ] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`.
- [x] Raise a new issue called `Update dependencies for <version>` with a description that links to [the documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/guides/update-dependencies/). This should be done early in the release cycle so find a volunteer to take this on and assign it to them.
- [x] Write an update in the weekly [Medic Product Team call agenda](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AuJ7SerLuOPESBjQlJqpBtzwSAoVf5ykTT7fjyJBT0/edit) summarising development and acceptance testing progress and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have passed acceptance testing and have been merged into `master` release testing can begin.

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development using this template:
```
@core_devs I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag and when CI completes successfully notify the QA team that it's ready for release testing.
- [x] Announce the start of release testing on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*Release testing has started for {{version}} of {{product}}*

To get a sneak peak at this upcoming release, you can install `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` on your testing environment. We suggest you test your forms and workflows with this release candidate version and raise any issues that you experience. This helps to to discover any potential regressions that wouldn't otherwise be caught during release testing.

Keep an eye on the forum for the release announcement in the next couple of weeks!
```
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, that they're correctly labelled (in particular: they have the right Type, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate), and have human readable descriptions.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [x] Manually document any known migration steps and known issues.
  - [x] Provide description, screenshots, videos, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions) and update the EOL date and status of previous releases. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page.
  - [x] Assign the PR to:
    - The Director of Technology
    - An SRE to review and confirm the documentation on upgrade instructions and breaking changes is sufficient
- [x] Until release testing passes, make sure regressions are fixed in `master`, cherry-pick them into the release branch, and release another beta.
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds_4/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Execute the scalability testing suite on the final build and download the scalability results on S3 at medic-e2e/scalability/$TAG_NAME. Add the release `.jtl` file to `cht-core/tests/scalability/previous_results`. More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [ ] Upgrade the `demo-cht.dev` instance to this version.
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*We're excited to announce the release of {{version}} of {{product}}*

New features include {{key_features}}. We've also implemented loads of other improvements and fixed a heap of bugs.

Read the [release notes]({{url}}) for full details.

Following our support policy, versions {{versions}} are no longer supported. Projects running these versions should start planning to upgrade in the near future. For more details read our [software support documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions).

Check out our [roadmap](https://github.com/orgs/medic/projects/112) to see what we're working on next.
```
- [x] Add one last update to the [Medic Product Team call agenda](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AuJ7SerLuOPESBjQlJqpBtzwSAoVf5ykTT7fjyJBT0/edit) and use this meeting to lead an internal release retrospective covering what went well and areas to improve for next time.
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Use _all_docs to get forms documents in API
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
If installation is interrupted before view indexing is finished, API will start up immediately, without waiting for indexes to be up to date. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
I think this warrants a discussion. 

Some context: 
- this case can present when: 
  - CHT 4.x is being installed on an existing data-set - for example when upgrading from 3.x without pre-indexing views
  - an upgrade is staged, but finalized at a later date (and after a significant number of changes have been pushed to the database) 
- in this scenario, API has already started on the correct version, so we are passed the point of upgrade. where the old version of API would still be running
- we are facing potential downtime while views are not up to date, regardless of choice

The options are to:
1. Wait for all views to be indexed before starting API
- this means that the API startup page will be displayed for the duration of this process
- API will not respond to any requests 

2. Start API anyway
- depending on which views require indexing, API could be working partially, responding to some requests that don't require querying  these views, and timing out for others
- startup could be blocked because some views are required in startup steps: for example `medic-client/doc_by_type` is queried when getting forms: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/src/services/forms.js#L23

One thing to note is that most projects will not actively use all views. For example, some webapp projects might never use SMS views and vice versa. When installing or upgrading, **all views** will be indexed.

title: Export action isn't displayed when there is a child place and user doesn't have 'can_create_places' permission
body:
**Describe the bug**
There is currently a rule that if there are child places and the user doesn’t have 'can_create_places' permission, then the Export action is not displayed. The bug is in [this code.](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/aab4b89b2fb354c442f6fca0f6c795d929ca3ba8/webapp/src/ts/components/actionbar/actionbar.component.html#L41)

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Make a hierarchy 
2. Deactivate 'can_create_places', and activate 'can_export_all' or 'can_export_contacts' permission.
3. Go to contact tab
4. See how export doesn't display. 

**Expected behavior**
The export action should display if there are records to export and if the user has 'can_export_all' or 'can_export_contacts' permission. The 'can_create_places' isn't related to this action. 

**Environment**
- Instance: all
- Browser: chrome
- Client platform: MacOs
- App: webapp
- Version: [3.9.x](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/3.9.x/webapp/src/templates/directives/actionbar.html#L52) maybe even since before.

**Additional context**
I discover this while working on [More Options Menu](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/7965#:~:text=room%20for%20it.-,%237872,-Code%20review%20checklist). The issue is fixed in the More Options Menu but not in the action-bar component

body:
**Describe the bug**
`container_name` needs to be specified for couchdb docker-compose files when using clustered setup across different nodes. The other option is to make CLUSTER_PEER_IP variable configurable and not hardcoded.

When running couchdb nodes across different instances, you want to be able to address the container names using their exact names. Given the CLUSTER_PEER_IPs are hardcoded to couchdb.2 and couchdb.3, to way to get it working right now is by setting `container_name` property for the containers.

title: Credentials exposed in logs
Improve debounce when exporting reports
body:
**Describe the issue**
The export actions might take some seconds to start and finish downloading the CSV, we have [implemented a timeout to disable the action temporarily](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/6fb758e2997bd20bf4b896c2724495216cf5c414/webapp/src/ts/modules/reports/reports.component.ts#L346) but we can probably implement a debounce mechanism or a way to know when the export has started to download the CSV. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We can probably implement a debounce mechanism or a way to know when the export has started to download the CSV. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The server can set a cookie at the beginning of the process, `waitingToDownload`, then when [the data is ready to download](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/6fb758e2997bd20bf4b896c2724495216cf5c414/api/src/controllers/export-data.js#L133) the server can remove the cookie. The front-end enables the export action when the cookie value is falsy.

title: 7910 Fix issue where cancel confirm dialog not shown
body:
# Description

Manually set the `editStatus` of an Enketo form to `false` before rendering the form. During the form initialization, the re-evaluation of some `calculate`s can cause the form to be marked as edited before receiving any input from the user.  

Resetting the `editStatus` prevents this behavior from affecting the cancel confirmation dialog behavior.  After this change, the cancel confirmation dialog should always be shown when the user has input data into the form (regardless of what calculations are done while initing the form).

title: Move additive actions from the Action Bar to Floating Action Button
body: # Overview As a part of our [longer term goal](https://github.com/medic/cht-roadmap/issues/61) to align with material design standards, the "Action Bar" at the bottom of the app (left hand side AND right hand side) is being removed. This issue will **remove the Action Bar** (_see Notes below_), **introduce a [Floating Action Button (FAB)](https://m3.material.io/components/floating-action-button/overview)**, and **move additive actions** (creating reports, places, people, etc...) from the Action Bar to the FAB. This will affect single pane (mobile) and dual pane views (desktop) on the [Messages](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/features/messaging/), [Reports](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/features/reports/), and [People](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/features/contacts/) tabs. The Figma mockups can be found [here](https://www.figma.com/file/3wFzMcNEGxV6se1QWftckk/UX-Stages?node-id=230%3A9424&t=BsHuimIOqnExyorI-0). #### NOTES 1. The Action Bar will be temporarily available through a [feature flag](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/updates/feature-flags/) by enabling the `can_view_old_action_bar` [permission](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/app-settings/user-permissions/). Be aware that [#7778](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7778) **_uses the same permission_**. 2. Issue [#5962](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5962) will be worked on separately, _after_ the FAB update is released. This FAB issue will define a default order when multiple actions are in the FAB. # FAB Contents This table illustrates which actions are **currently** available based on what is selected and which device is being used. This is not changing. There are [permissions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/app-settings/user-permissions/) to control the visibility of the Call and Message actions on the Contacts tab. ![Screenshot 2023-01-19 at 2 47 50 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10096985/213544955-8e0ee7f1-08f9-419a-8f5e-f31bd4fca2e3.png) _In all cases, only show relevant actions based on `context`._ ## Mobile View The FAB options will show up as a drawer from the bottom with rows of actions, much like it looks today for Forms, but with the other options (Call, Message, Contact Forms) in this list as well. ![Screenshot 2023-01-19 at 2 39 49 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10096985/213543673-52da4e12-fe2e-4f5f-9925-78b5854bb92d.png) ## Desktop View There are two trigger buttons, one is located in the list's footer which only has a label (no icon), and the other one is located on the top right side and only has an icon (no label). ![Screenshot 2023-03-07 at 6 02 22 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/66472237/224626072-1881959a-2c4d-4b56-9e36-2afd343b8db7.png) The FAB options will show up as a modal window in the middle of the screen. The options will be in a list just like the mobile drawer mentioned above. If the option name is too long, then display it in two lines and use the ellipsis to trim the text. If the user clicks outside the modal or presses "Esc" from the keyboard, also if the user navigates to another page, then the modal should close. ## Trigger button The old action bar will be removed and tapping on the list footer's button (desktop) or in the FAB (mobile) will bring up the action list. FAB button: - No label - If there is more than one action: plus sign icon - If there is only one action, but the action's icon isn't Font Awesome: plus sign icon. - If there is only one action, and the action is a Font Awesome: action's icon. List footer's button: - No icon - Show label ## Order of items in the list Issue https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5962 will allow a custom order by for actions in the list, but the default will be as below. Reference the colorful table above to understand what is shown when. For example, you'll notice that there are never more than 3 "types" of things shown at once. 1. Call 2. Message 3. "Place" Contact Forms, in alphabetical 4. "Person" Contact Forms, alphabetical 5. App Forms, alphabetical # Messages Tab The only action available on this tab is `Send message`. The old action bar will be removed and tapping on the list footer's button (desktop) or in the FAB (mobile) will bring up the `Send Message` modal. # Contacts Tab The Contacts Tab has five possible actions: `Call`, `Send message`, `New place`, `New person`, and `New action` (report). ## Mobile View #### Left Hand Side (Top Level) - The only option available is `New place`. Move it to the FAB. When the search input has the focus and the soft-keyboard appears, then hide the FAB. #### Right Hand Side (Place) - There are three options: `New place`, 'New person', and `New action`. Move all these to the FAB. - Never skip the drawer if the one thing is a Form. #### Right Hand Side (Person) - There are three* options: `Call`, `Send message`, and `New action`. Move all these to the FAB. - Never skip the drawer if the one thing is a Form. _* `Call` only shows up if you are on a mobile device._ ## Desktop View #### Left Hand Side The action will be moved to the list footer's bottom. #### Right Hand Side Same as in mobile # Reports Tab The Reports tab has four main Actions: `Submit report`, `Send message`, `Update facility` and `Review`. ## Review action - This action is moved to the More Options menu. - When a user taps on it, shows a modal (desktop) or a bottom drawer (mobile) with two options: "Has errors" and "Correct". Show in one row, with "Has errors" on the left and "Correct" on the right. - The review badge is moved next to the form's name. ![Screenshot 2023-03-13 at 4 00 43 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/66472237/224654728-9bd83add-5aa0-408f-b6fc-c4fa0e774bae.png) ## Mobile View #### Left Hand Side The only option available is `Submit report`. Move it to the FAB. - Icon should always be a `+` - Always show the drawer, even if there is only one thing on the list - The FAB is hidden behind the Filter panel when it's open. - When the search input has the focus and the soft-keyboard appears, then hide the FAB if possible. - While in multiselect (bulk delete), hide the FAB #### Right Hand Side - There are two options: `Send message` and `Update facility`. Move it to the FAB - While in multiselect (bulk delete), hide the FAB ## Desktop View #### Left Hand Side - The only option is `Submit report`. title: Upgrade webapp's angular to v15
body:
# Description

Upgrading from v12 to v13:
- All @angular/XX libraries were upgraded to v13
- [Typescript was upgraded to v4.4.2](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-4-4.html) which is the minimum required by Angular 13
- Angular 13 now creates a `.angular/cache` directory [to improve build speed](https://blog.angular.io/angular-v13-is-now-available-cce66f7bc296#05df). This was added to the gitignore file.
- The ` MethodCall` from angular compiler [was deprecated here](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/42882/files#diff-1002bdc266028e1c303492a63ed5990124b8fd29a8f87098d07f86c0519d47f0R319), I've replaced it with `Call`
- Now there's an error when trying to build the app and when there's a `window.location.reload(true|false)` [this parameter isn't standard](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Location/reload), I've removed it.

Upgrading from v13 to v14:
- [Typescript was upgraded to 4.6](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-4-6/#breaking-changes) which is the minimum required for Angular 14.
- The typescript eslint libs were upgraded to support the new version of typescript.
- I fixed the unit tests, and now we need to reset the store in the `beforeEach`.
- Also, the new version of ngrx changed a bit how [tests are done](https://ngrx.io/guide/store/testing#testing-selectors) in selectors, that’s something I fixed.
- The [parser provider](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/providers/parse.provider.ts) was fixed, something changed in the [angular compiler classes](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/50f95f831e7da84e2b879dd4b9b7764ca07ef0e7/packages/compiler/src/expression_parser/parser.ts).
- At this point I can see an improvement in speed, when running `grunt unit-webapp` on `master branch` (angular v12) it takes 3m 31.3s to complete, while on my branch (angular v14) it takes 2m 7s
- Removed `polyfills-es5.js`, since angular **drop support for IE11**, see [End of IE11 support](https://blog.angular.io/angular-v13-is-now-available-cce66f7bc296)

Upgrading from v14 to v15:
- Removed `relativeLinkResolution` from app router module, [depracation](https://angular.io/guide/update-to-version-15#relativelinkresolution-is-not-configurable-in-the-router).
- Upgraded typescript to 4.8 min supported by Angular v15
- Upgraded typescript eslint libs to match the new version of typescript. (@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin: 5.43, @typescript-eslint/parser: 5.43)
- Upgraded NgRx libraries and the Ngx Translate Core lib to support Angular v15 (@ngrx/effects, @ngrx/store, @ngx-translate/core)
- Set the `tsconfig.base.json`'s target to ES2020 to support latest typescript, and fix the error: `Class constructor cannot be invoked without 'new'`
- Fixed unit test configuration to match how angular finds specs files. That's in angular.json and test.ts
- Fixed angular material styles and classes selectors, more in [mdc v15](https://material.angular.io/guide/mdc-migration).

**NOTE:**
Whenever we have the error below, it's likely that `@angular/compiler`, `@angular-devkit/build-angular`  or `@angular-builders/custom-webpack` aren't resolved properly in the `package-lock.json`. So, uninstall these 3, then install them again in that order.

![Screen Shot 2022-12-22 at 12 36 21 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/66472237/209088049-aaf33272-dd0c-4640-9917-a309c5782eea.png)

title: Error deleting documents on slow connection
body:
**Describe the bug**
Users get an error when bulk deleting documents. The message they see says "Error deleting document". 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Log in as an online user with the ability to bulk delete reports
2. Make your browser window small enough so that it is showing mobile view (single pane)
3. Go to the reports tab
4. Throttle your connection to "Slow 3G" or "Low-end mobile"
5. Go into "Select" mode
6. Select several (I did 4) reports 
7. Immediately tap on "Delete All"
8. Tap on "Delete" on the confirmation page
9. See the error

**Expected behavior**
The documents I have selected should be deleted without error OR don't give me the option to delete until you are actually ready to delete them. 

**Logs**

[127-0-0-1.my.local-ip.co.har.txt](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/files/10288574/127-0-0-1.my.local-ip.co.har.txt)


**Screenshots/Videos**

**3.17.0**

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10096985/209172384-ec306878-60f0-4872-9c4f-62a396afb0a9.mov

</details>

**4.1.0**

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10096985/209172437-9d5ff491-13a3-43be-a376-adcc9a95a240.mov




**Environment**
- Instance: demo-cht.dev (3.17.0) and local docker instance (4.1.0)
- Browser: Chrome
- Client platform: MacOS
- App: WebApp
- Version: I've verified it is an issue on 3.17.0 and 4.1.0. [Another user is experiencing it on 3.16.1](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/experience-with-bulk-deleting-reports/2142/3?u=michael).

**Additional context**
For me, this wasn't an issue on desktop in 3.17.0 because the "Delete All" action bar doesn't show up until everything it needs is loaded. On 4.1.0, the "Delete All" option shows up immediately so it is still an issue even on desktop. 

At time of writing this, there have already been a few other issues identified related to bulk delete: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7300 , https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7868 , https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7883

title: Bullets not displaying properly in form labels
body:
**Describe the bug**
In `3.x` versions of the CHT you could _simulate_ a bulleted list in a form label (e.g. a `note`) by using `-` or `*`.  Now, in `4.x`, after https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6345, the bullets are no longer properly displayed in the label.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a form with a note that has this label:
```
Do these bullets work:
- Hello 
- World

Or do these work:
– Hello 
– World

How about these:
* Hello 
* World
```
2. Open the form and view the note

**Expected behavior**
On `3.x`, the note looks like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8441903/209364499-65c8f4cd-a0af-427f-986c-bd4b397d1539.png)

**Actual behavior**
On `4.x`, though, it looks like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8441903/209364595-8b73b480-e939-4a87-a08f-25ef3e0c6894.png)

_(Note that the middle block "works" because the `–` character is not valid markdown syntax for a bullet point....)_

**Additional context**

The problem is that in `3.x` the [markdown processing](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/3.17.x/webapp/src/ts/services/markdown.service.ts) was basic and did not support bullet points.  So, these notes were evaluated as simple text and the bullet characters are preserved in the text.  

On `4.x`, the [markdown processing](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/69a0207d8c67e92ba625f9545e01c4c781779246/api/src/enketo-transformer/markdown.js#L65) is more advanced and can detect the bullet points in the question labels.  It then converts the bullets to unordered lists (`<ul>`).  The problem is that the CSS style that ends up getting computed for those unordered lists is `list-style: none`.  So, the end result is that the unordered lists are displayed in the labels without any bullet points.

I think we probably just need to tweak the CSS for these unordered lists to be `list-style: inside;`

_(This change was first noted by @binokaryg (and team) when upgrading a project's config to work with CHT `4.x`.)_

body: **Describe the bug** Bikram sambat date picker widget converts date even when user hasn't selected a Month. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. title: CI build fails for external contributors
body:
**Describe the issue**
The CI build steps for internal contributors are: 
1) build and test all services code (webapp, api, sentinel, etc)
2) build services docker images 
3) publish services docker images to private amazon ECR

For external contributors, step 3 would fail, since they do not have access to the private amazon ECR credentials (saved as a GH environment variable). Instead of publishing to amazon ECR, the images should be saved as artefacts and attached to the GH build. 
However, this path is not taken at the moment, and the CI is trying to push service images to ECR, and fails: 

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/runs/3888134996/jobs/6635149994

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Fix the build for external contributors.

title: Feature Release upgrades don't work on CHT 4.x
body:
**Describe the issue**
In 3.x you would upgrade using `horti` and then when you published a new FR (eg beta 2) it would show up in the admin UI.  This is no longer true in 4.x

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We should make it an easy way to upgrade after you have [installed the FR](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/pull/934).  

As well, we may consider making the latest version of every available FR for your current version visible in the admin GUI. For example if you were on `4.2.0`, we might show you all the FRs that were based on this version or later versions.  We would only show the latest (eg `beta3`) and not all prior versions (eg `beta1` and `beta2`)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
NA

**To Reproduce**

2. Login to admin app. Go to Images -> Branding.

4. Click Submit. Nothing happens.

**Expected behavior**
The UI should inform the user that the existing document is malformed. 
Even when the document is malformed, the user should have the possibility to "fix" it by editing from the Admin UI.

**Describe the bug**
A malformed `partners` doc will block the user from updating partners from the admin app and will throw an error in Webapp.

**To Reproduce Admin behavior**
1. Create a `partners.json` document in your config. Set the contents of this document to be `{}`. run `cht upload-partners`. 
2. Login to admin app. Go to Images -> Partners.
3. Add a new "partner".
4. Click Submit. 
5. See error `There was an error saving your settings, please try again.`. 

**Expected behavior**
The UI should inform the user that the existing document is malformed. 
Even when the document is malformed, the user should have the possibility to "fix" it by editing from the Admin UI. 

**Logs**
When loading the partners page:
```
angular.js:15697 TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object
    at Function.keys (<anonymous>)
    at resource-icons.js:111:24

    at images-partners.js:54:27

2. Load the About page and open dev tools. 
3. See logged error: 

```
main.js:1 Error fetching "partners" doc TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object
    at Object.keys (<anonymous>)
    at main.js:1:974376
    at H.invoke (polyfills.js:1:10944)

**Development steps**

- update [`images-partners` controller](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/5153b1916395bdee06220eecdc450e26dc6870b1/admin/src/js/controllers/images-partners.js#L60) to create the `resources` property if it does not exist

title: Add config to allow replicating primary contacts for places at max depth
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When using the `replication_depth` configuration, the _places_ at the max depth will be replicated, but not the _person_ associated with that place. For example, a CHW Supervisor may be configured to only have access to the CHW Areas (but not the actual CHW person contacts related to the areas).  

Pain points:

- The logged-in user has no information about the place-related contact they are monitoring.
- Users are forced to use a notebook to match the place with its primary or related contact.
- The place-related contact is not available when creating tasks or goals.

 Currently, the only way for the supervisor to have access to the CHW is to increase the replication_depth. However, that would also give the supervisor access to all the other contact children of the CHW Area (e.g. households) which could cause performance issues.  

**Describe the solution you'd like**

It would be useful to have a configuration option that will allow replicating primary contacts, using the same replication depth. So, if the config option is set, then the primary contacts for places at the max depth would also be replicated.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Another option is to just make this the default behavior so that primary contacts are always replicated whenever a place is replicated.

A separate approach would be to to support configuring separate replication depths for places and persons (e.g. `place_depth` and `person_depth`).  This would not be easy to implement because we use a view which is unaware of whether a contact is a place or person, since we can’t inject configurable hierarchy contact types in the view. This means that we’d need to edit the view to emit the contact type, and, in code, we would query for every contact type for every level instead of one query just by level. This adds complexity and potentially impacts performance because of the additional queries that are needed.

**Additional context**
Originally submitted [on the CHT Forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/enhancing-user-experience-by-allowing-place-to-be-replicated-with-their-direct-contacts/2395).

title: Update client-side purging to trigger task recalculation
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Task recalculation is triggered through a couple of mechanism:
- once every 7 days, automatically
- when reports and contacts are created/edited/deleted - the Rules-Engine service watches the local changes feed and marks affected contacts as dirty
- when the configuration is changed

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Purging implies deleting documents from the user's device. However, the deletion happens when booting, before any Angular service has started, specifically to avoid changes feeds from catching up with a large stream of changes (the purged documents being deleted). 
The consequence for this is that local mechanism that watch the changes feed will not be notified of the change, one of these examples is recalculating tasks when older documents are deleted. 

After purging, targets _will_ get recalculated by the other mechanisms, it will just take a while and the action that triggered the recalculation will not be obvious. 

To reproduce: 
- add a task configuration that will create a task when a report of type X is submitted
- login as an offline user and submit a report of type X 
- check that the task appears in your task list
- update purging rules to purge reports of type X and run purging on the server
- run purging on the client and refresh
- check that report X is gone from the report list
- got task list and observe that the task still exists! 
- completing the task does make it disappear, but if you check the task state afterwards, it will be cancelled, instead of completed! 

Ideally we would only force recalculation of relevant tasks, much like it would be as if the deletes happened while the Angular app was running and Rules-Engine would mark corresponding contacts as dirty.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Leave it as it is. 

**Additional context**
[Form post](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/task-are-going-to-cancelled-state-with-appliesif-true/2408/9) where a submission that was supposed to resolve a task ended up cancelling it after purging had changed the `appliesIf` result from `true` to `false`.

title: Allow users to report client-side crashes via screenshots
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently when a CHT application causes a crash, the user sees a basic error message with no actionable in distinguishable details.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9014751/213537506-df9be9ad-f1f4-4ae0-847e-391802b4478c.png)

Although the details of the crash are recorded via feedback documents - it would sometimes be useful for users to report their users via screenshot. 

Example: an app developer in an offline context is working beside a user who experiences a crash.
Example: a user experiences a crash which cannot be found in feedback docs
Example: an app developer is asked to help fix crashes in an app where they don't have access.

title: Incorrect form summary delivery date in default pregnancy form
body:
**Describe the bug**
When submitting a pregnancy form, and using the estimated delivery date input option, the displayed delivery date is different from the actually selected one. 

This might be only the case now, when selecting a delivery date in February, and on a GMT+ timezone. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Load default config. 
2. Load a pregnancy form. Select `Expected date of delivery (EDD)` as the gestational age calculation method. 
3. Set the expected delivery date to be one month from now (In my case Feb 25th). 
4. Go to next page, and see that EDD is one day before your selected date, Feb 24th. 
5. Continue filling the form, and notice that on the summary page the EDD is displayed incorrectly. 
6. Submit the form. On submission, the correct delivery date is saved! 

**Expected behavior**
Actually selected date should be displayed. 

**Logs**
No errors

**Video**

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/214503863-f30a679f-1d69-4211-8811-65b57c125be7.mp4


**Environment**
- Instance: local
- App: webapp
- Version: 4.1.0

**Additional context**
Discovered because an e2e test was failing locally. I should mention that I'm on GMT+2.

title: CHT 4.x Docker services fail to communicate in multi-nodes setup
body:
**Describe the bug**
Often, when I start my multi-node clustered CHT 4.x instance, I get errors in my API container and nginx containers and the CHT fails to start

**To Reproduce**
1. Set up 4 computers as a [multi-node clustered CHT 4.x instance](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/4.x/self-hosting-multiple-nodes/)
2. run `docker compose up -d` on the CHT Core node
3. Go to the browser and try and load the CHT

**Expected behavior**
The CHT shows a login  page and loads correctly

**Logs**

The API container has this error repeatedly:

```
RequestError: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.1.7:5984
    at new RequestError (/api/node_modules/request-promise-core/lib/errors.js:14:15)
    at Request.plumbing.callback (/api/node_modules/request-promise-core/lib/plumbing.js:87:29)
    at Request.RP$callback [as _callback] (/api/node_modules/request-promise-core/lib/plumbing.js:46:31)
    at self.callback (/api/node_modules/request/request.js:185:22)
    at Request.emit (node:events:513:28)
    at Request.onRequestError (/api/node_modules/request/request.js:877:8)
    at ClientRequest.emit (node:events:513:28)
    at Socket.socketErrorListener (node:_http_client:481:9)
    at Socket.emit (node:events:513:28)
    at emitErrorNT (node:internal/streams/destroy:157:8) {
  cause: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.1.7:5984
      at TCPConnectWrap.afterConnect [as oncomplete] (node:net:1247:16) {
    errno: -111,
    code: 'ECONNREFUSED',
    syscall: 'connect',
    address: '10.0.1.7',
    port: 5984
  },
  error: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.1.7:5984
      at TCPConnectWrap.afterConnect [as oncomplete] (node:net:1247:16) {
    errno: -111,
    code: 'ECONNREFUSED',
    syscall: 'connect',
    address: '10.0.1.7',
    port: 5984
  }
}
```

This, in turn, causes the the webserver (nginx) to fail to talk to API, so the browser to my instance gives a `502` error:

```
502 Bad Gateway
nginx/1.19.6
```

The nginx container of course has errors too, because API can't talk to HA Proxy:

```
CERTIFICATE MODE = SELF_SIGNED
Running SSL certificate checks
self signed SSL cert already exists.
Launching Nginx
/docker-entrypoint.sh: Configuration complete; ready for start up
10.131.161.1 - - [26/Jan/2023:23:33:51 +0000] "GET /medic/login?redirect=https%3A%2F%2F10-131-161-147.my.local-ip.co%2F HTTP/1.1" 502 157 "-" "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Ubuntu; Linux x86_64; rv:109.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/109.0"
2023/01/26 23:33:51 [error] 29#29: *1 connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream, client: 10.131.161.1, server: , request: "GET /medic/login?redirect=https%3A%2F%2F10-131-161-147.my.local-ip.co%2F HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.0.1.4:5988/medic/login?redirect=https%3A%2F%2F10-131-161-147.my.local-ip.co%2F", host: "10-131-161-147.my.local-ip.co"
```

**Screenshots**

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8253488/214974738-882076a9-d8b6-41e2-a503-0179fcd8e725.png)

**Environment**
- Instance: local dev
- Browser: all
- Client platform: ubuntu
- App: docker
- Version: any multi-node clustered 4.x instance

**Additional context**

When testing this, everything may work on the first try.  If that's the case try and run this 5 or 6 times on the CHT core node and check in a browser if it succeeds each time:

```
docker kill $(docker ps --quiet)
cd /home/ubuntu/cht/upgrade-service/
docker compose up -d
```

The semi-functional work around is to aggressively restart containers, with out changing anything and then some how it starts working again.  

There was [some speculation](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C02F2TAME90/p1674756143835159?thread_ts=1674694330.228769&cid=C02F2TAME90) (private slack thread) that the fix to this was:
* change all CouchDB names from `couchdb.1` -> `couchdb-1.local`
* in the CouchDB compose files (1 on each node), add an explicit name: `container_name: couchdb-1.local`

This is not the case.  I still get high occurrences of this error when I set my CouchDB servers in my CHT Core `.env` file to have the correct name: `COUCHDB_SERVERS=couchdb-1.local,couchdb-2.local,couchdb-3.local` and then set each of CouchDB compose file look like this node 1 in this example (below).  

```yaml
version: '3.9'
services:
  couchdb-1.local:
    container_name: couchdb-1.local
    image: public.ecr.aws/s5s3h4s7/cht-couchdb:4.0.1-4.0.1
    volumes:
      - ./srv:/opt/couchdb/data
      - cht-credentials:/opt/couchdb/etc/local.d/
    environment:
      - "COUCHDB_USER=${COUCHDB_USER:-admin}"
      - "COUCHDB_PASSWORD=${COUCHDB_PASSWORD:?COUCHDB_PASSWORD must be set}"
      - "COUCHDB_SECRET=${COUCHDB_SECRET}"
      - "COUCHDB_UUID=${COUCHDB_UUID}"
      - "SVC_NAME=${SVC1_NAME:-couchdb-1.local}"
      - "CLUSTER_PEER_IPS=couchdb-2.local,couchdb-3.local"
      - "COUCHDB_LOG_LEVEL=${COUCHDB_LOG_LEVEL:-error}"
    logging:
      driver: "local"
      options:
        max-size: "${LOG_MAX_SIZE:-50m}"
        max-file: "${LOG_MAX_FILES:-20}"
    restart: always
    networks:
      - cht-net
      - cht-overlay
volumes:
  cht-credentials:
networks:
  cht-net:
     name: ${CHT_NETWORK:-cht-net}
  cht-overlay:
     driver: overlay
     external: true
```

# Description

There was a [discussion on Slack](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C02F2TAME90/p1674141851263569) recently about having a script we could encourage folks to run who were having troubles running CHT 4.x's docker containers. The discussion was in response to [a forum post](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/error-502-when-running-local-cht-instance/2414).  We thought the script would gather up all the logs and create a .tar.gz file that could easily be posted.  This PR adds a bash script to do just that. 

To test:
* create a CHT 4.x instance using[ docker helper](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/4.x/app-developer/#cht-docker-helper-for-4x)
* clone the `cht-core` repo, and check out the `add-script-to-zip-docker-logs` branch
* Change directories into the `cht-core` repo: `cd cht-core`
* run the script `./scripts/compress_and_archive_docker_logs.sh`
* check the `support_logs` directory and ensure there's a zip file in there: `ls ~/.medic/support_logs/`
* uncompressing the tarball should yield one log file per container with the container name as the file name. Also a file for `docker ps` and `docker stats` should be saved as `docker_ps.log` and `docker_stats.log`respectively.
* check that the `*log` files have correct contents

title: Support for running Tasks.js and Targets.js without Nools
body:
### Description

This is a proposed change which allows CHT Application code to run without the Nools library.

- This provides a workaround for https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6506 and https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/issues/225
- Step in the direction of https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5906. When ready we can remove the nools.emitter
- Probable minor performance gains since nools is a weird box of mysteries. May improve https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5515 if that issue is correct about Nools holding target instances in memory.

### User Details
This proposes to introduce a new optional variable in `app_settings.json` at [tasks.disableNools](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/compare/noNools?expand=1#diff-ad9f410e750994f008b5e63e2b5587375a03000a3b3f5d004fe6f69930e48c4bR223). When this value is set to `true` then the nools library is not used to process tasks.js and targets.js application code.

### Code Details
- I've proposed to move `rules-emitter.js` into a folder which contains `index` and `emitter.nools` and `emitter.metal` (better name available?)
- The value from appSettings is piped down and the appropriate emitter is chosen and used by index.
- I've updated relevant unit tests to run for both emitters - their behaviors should be nearly identical for projects using declarative configuration
- There are some more significant changes in `shared-libs/rules-engine/test/integration.spec.js` because nools breaks how `sinon.useFakeTimers` works. Since this is no longer broken when nools is disabled, I've updated those tests so the test time is equal to the time in which the rules engine is initialized.

title: CouchDB entry point always saves `couch_httpd_auth` and `couchdb` to cluster-credentials.ini
body:
**Describe the issue**
The `docker-entrypoint.sh` does a check to ensure that `couch_httpd_auth` and `couchdb` are in `/opt/couchdb/etc/local.d/cluster-credentials.ini`. However, the check always fails, even when it shouldn't, so the credentials are always written to the file causing `cluster-credentials.ini` to endlessly grow.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
fix [the entrypoint](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/bbc99f92dbd936511281c718b163aaba65d5704e/couchdb/docker-entrypoint.sh) so the checks work as expected and only write the values to the ini file once

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
none

title: Add a way to easily access CouchDb when API is down
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
This is the lifecycle of a request that needs to reach CouchDb in the CHT: 
1. client creates the request
2. nginx receives, and forwards to API
3. API receives, filters and forwards to CouchDb
4. CouchDb responds
5. API forwards response
6. Nginx forwards response

Out of the 3 services above, only Nginx exposes ports to the outside web, so reaching API or CouchDb directly is not possible.

When API is down due to a configuration error or any other malfunction, CouchDb is only reachable from within the container / network, which is cumbersome and error prone, when having to debug and fix issues only by using curl (or other basic commands). 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Think of a way to short-circuit access to CouchDb thought Nginx when API is down, while maintaining security. 

**Additional context**
It was cumbersome and slow to debug a production CouchDb problem using curl only to make complex requests (that require headers, payloads and authentication).

title: Support filtering contact search in forms by descendants of the current contact
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
In a discussion about interoperability, this question came up: "How do I establish a relationship between two contacts?". For example, selecting the mother/father of a child in a contact create form. 

Right now, we only support db-object searches by doc type, not by parent. So users are left in searching the whole list of contacts of a certain type to find the correct selection. This can prove cumbersome with duplicate names - which is a common occurrence in our deployments. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add support for db-object searches by parent. This can be a compound search by type and parent as well. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Another idea is to inject the children of a place directly in the form (via contact summary for example). 

**Additional context**
Question came up in a session about interoperability with a partner, concerning an existing deployment. 


## Solution

- This feature is applied when using the appearance:`descendant-of-current-contact`
- The scope remains for forms that are opened in the contact tab; it takes the contact ID from the URL. 
- It uses the CouchDB view `contact_by_parent` in combination with the contact type.

**Usage**
| type | name | label:en | appearance |
|------|-------|------|------|
| string | a-person | select a person | select-contact type-person descendant-of-current-contact |

[CHT Docs PR](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/pull/1254)

title: Add wdio retries
body:
**Describe the issue**
Our e2e tests are flaky, to the point where it's more likely for a build to fail than pass. This means engineers continually have to retry builds in order to get a green tick and be allowed to merge. Our policy is to keep on top of these issues and resolve them as they come up but history has shown we never find the time to do it.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Investigate turning on WDIO retries so individual tests are tried again and the build is only failed if they repeatedly fail. In addition we need better test reporting so we can see if the retries are making the build slower, or obscuring other issues.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Turn off the requirement for a green build. That will reduce confidence in the testing and it's likely regressions will be committed by people who assume the failures are flakes.
- Deal with flaky tests with extreme prejudice. If a test flakes it should be immediately skipped, and if we get around to fixing it in the future it can be re-enabled. The problem is flakiness is very common so possibly too many tests would get skipped. This may be worth looking into if retries don't work for any reason.

title: Race condition: Tasks list briefly shows "No more tasks" before displaying available tasks.
body:
**Describe the bug**
When loading the tasks list, even if there are tasks to display, the LHS will display "No more tasks" momentarily, before actually rendering the list. 
This would point to a race condition somewhere in the tasks controller. 
The race condition becomes more evident on a slow device. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Login as an offline user with a large number of active tasks (mine had 440 tasks). 
2. If in a browser, Throttle your CPU in the performance tab:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/219869927-0aa3a12e-88f7-4826-bdce-9e151fa7d48e.png)
3. Load the tasks page.
4. See "No more tasks" before actually seeing the tasks list. This behavior is visible with every subsequent task list render, not only when there are tasks to be calculated.

**Expected behavior**
Keep showing the spinner until the task list can be rendered.

**Video (desktop browser with mobile resolution)**

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/219870147-7148c7a8-1531-4868-a153-22461a56a9b0.mp4

**Environment**
- Instance: local
- Browser: Chrome
- App: webapp
- Version: 4.2.0

title: Implement a way of restricting which users are allowed to replicate
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Be it for performance reasons (for example: needing to prioritize certain users for replicating quickly) or for data integrity reasons (for example users that have orphaned contacts after a move contacts or a rollback), restricting replication to only some users has been a go-to solution for CHT projects a few times in cht history. 

A few of the ways this has been implemented:
- socially, by instructing some users to stop using their devices
- hot-patching the instance to add custom code which will produce the same result
- IP blocking at load balancer level 

None of the solutions above are easy or guarantee results: the social solution becomes inefficient very quickly for large projects, hot-patching with custom code is very risky, ip blocking requires that the target users have "stable" IPs and technical knowledge and accessibility to change the config of the load balancer. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Find way to:
- stop specific users from replicating (have an exclusions "list")
- allow only specific users from replicating (have an inclusions "list")

The user selection should be flexible, some example of criteria for selecting users can be: role, permission, username, facility_id (or facility ancestor). 
When a user is denied replication, their replication endpoint calls should respond with a status and error message that will stop the client from progressing replication (no "denied" errors for example, which do not stop replication progression). 
Changing the list of users should be easy, but be restricted to certain users (maybe only admins?). 

**Additional context**
Restricting replication, implemented socially, was the solution chosen by a partner when mitigating effects of moving most of the contacts in a large deployment.

title: Caught errors do not generate feedback documents.
body:
**Describe the bug**
Feedback docs get generated automatically on unhandled exceptions. Webapp has been getting better and better at catching errors and displaying useful/actionable data to the user, and also missing the trigger to create a feedback doc. 
Other examples of issues where we added feedback docs deliberately for specific errors: 
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7363 - errors in task targets
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6629 - errors in contact-summary
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7525 - errors in loading forms

Feedback docs are essential for assessing app health, and are the easiest way to discover most common problems in deployments. 

This bug is about errors when saving reports (submitted through reports, contacts, tasks, training forms). 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior on saving a report:
1. Upload a form that should throw an error when saving. I picked one that I was already using in another issue: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8072 . If that gets fixed first, another bugged form is required. 
2. Submit this form. 
3. After submission fails, check generated feedback docs. 
4. See that no feedback doc was generated. 

**Expected behavior**
A feedback doc should be generated when a report cannot be saved. 

**Logs**
The error gets logged correctly. 

**Environment**
- App: webapp
- Version: 4.2.0 (has been the case for a long time, version TBD)

**Additional context**
There are probably more cases where we avoid feedback doc creation on potentially critical errors. 
**We should reconsider when automatic feedback doc generation is triggered.**

title: Extract form's instance code out from the Enketo Service in webapp
body:
**Describe the issue**

Currently, `webapp` can only display one Enketo form at a time; the enketo service is doing form's instance jobs like [unloading a form](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/ee964cba74e63c5263c703d7b715dd634153ddb1/webapp/src/ts/services/enketo.service.ts#L811), [setup form's buttons](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/ee964cba74e63c5263c703d7b715dd634153ddb1/webapp/src/ts/services/enketo.service.ts#L708), [force a form recalculation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/ee964cba74e63c5263c703d7b715dd634153ddb1/webapp/src/ts/services/enketo.service.ts#L699), etc. 

There is a risk of race condition between form instances; for example, the webapp loads a pregnancy form, then loads a pregnancy follow-up form (by changing the URL); the pregnancy form may have a delay and ends up calling the service to unload after the pregnancy follow up was loaded. The [unload](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/ee964cba74e63c5263c703d7b715dd634153ddb1/webapp/src/ts/services/enketo.service.ts#L811) function has code that affected the pregnancy follow up form. 

These race conditions are rare but can still happen. If we fix this, then maintenance and extensibility will be easier. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
- Extract the form's instance-specific code out of the Enketo Service. The service receives the form instance and executes support operations like extracting data for saving, fetching and setting attachments, etc. 
- Operations over a form instance shouldn't affect another form instance. 
- A form instance has a clear life cycle that the implementing page can control.

title: Prevent data loss through re-sync when restoring data from backup
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Data loss when restoring from backups is most likely unavoidable. 
However there is one mitigation we can deploy, with relatively little cost. 

First, follow these steps to reproduce how data loss happens now: 
1. Launch CHT (4.x is easiest, but this applies to every release since 2017) and create an offline user
2. Login as the offline user. 
3. Create a data backup. 
4. As the offline user, create some documents and sync. 
5. As the admin, check that the documents created on step 4 exist on the server. 
6. Overwrite live data with the backup (simulate a restoration from backup). 
7. Check that the documents created on step 4 don't exist on the server (this is expected, those docs were created AFTER the backup). 
8. Sync as the offline user. 
9. Check that the documents created on step 4 don't exist on the server. 

What happens on step 9 is caused by the way we save the replication checkpointer in Pouchdb: [at replication source](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/services/db-sync.service.ts#L88). This means that the document that holds the replication sequence for client uploads exists only on the client. The client doesn't know the server was restored from a backup, so it will keep uploading docs based on the locally stored sequence. This sequence is _after_ the docs created on step 4. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
PouchDb supports multiple settings for the `checkpoint`, and by default will save the checkpointer on both `source` and `target`. 
If the checkpointer is also saved on the target, when reaching step 9, PouchDb will check replication history on both checkpointers and choose the latest common seq. Because the server will have an older seq, the documents created on 4 will be re-uploaded. No data loss. 

With this approach, in case the server checkpointer becomes corrupted, is deleted, etc, the client will start replication from 0. This means that the local database is iterated over in batches and, for each batch, it will query a server endpoint (_revs_diff) to check whether the docs already exist. This endpoint is unfiltered, and requests are forwarded directly to CouchDb.  Only missing docs will be uploaded.
We should assess the performance impact of a client resetting replication, both for the client and for the server. 

When implementing this, we should also make sure that we somehow "start" by writing the server-side checkpointer, if possible, so we avoid all clients going through the process described above. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Don't change anything. 

**Additional context**
We recently restored a production  deployment from a backup due to server-side data corruption.

title: cht-core 4.1 and cht-android 0.x compability testing
body:
CHT Core 4.x was released recently. As part of CHT Core 4.2, partners will also have to upgrade their CHT-android to 1.0.

However, we want to support partners that can't upgrade to CHT-android 1.0 while still offering scalability and performance improvements from CHT-core 4. x

For this reason, we need to do a complete testing of CHT considering this configuration/parameters:

CHT-core version: 4.1
CHT-android: 0.8.5
Android version: 10 or lower. Lower than 10 is preferred.

This originated after a request from MoH Uganda. However, we intend to ensure the testing is valid for any partner with this kind of setup.

For now, some of the questions we have are:

1. What configs do they have?
2. Do they use widgets?
3. Can we get details on their hierarchy?
4. Are there more details we should consider?
5. Should we test only the combination requested or more? For example, cht core 4.1, with cht-android 0.5, and then with cht-android 0.6
6. Should we test with default values if we can’t get specific answers to these questions? (related to partner-specific configurations and hierarchy)

The programs team will help us get answers to those questions by CoB tomorrow (Wed, Feb 22).

Edit on Feb 22: We got answers from programs team [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1pcXCtFpj3DvrpWrftM2J9kMi-I7W2S5dRZTzVGUiXGM/edit)

The next step for QA engineers is to provide a high-level estimate for the work needed once the questions are answered. If you feel comfortable providing a high-level estimate even without the questions answered and then updating it, that is also valid.

title: Deprecate use of  `SSL_CERT_FILE_*` , `CERTIFICATE_MODE` & `SSL_VOLUME_MOUNT_PATH` for nginx image
body:
**Describe the issue**
Infrastructure team has decided that `CERTIFICATE_MODE` and `SSL_VOLUME_MOUNT_PATH` should be deprecated (see below). Additionally, after research, we decided we should also deprecate  `SSL_CERT_FILE_PATH` and `SSL_KEY_FILE_PATH`  per #7949.

* It's confusing and complicated
* It works fine just use `cht-ssl` volume for persistence and have CHT admins follow steps to copy in their cert.
* Default can safely be to always create a self signed cert on boot which can easily be overwritten
* For Let's Encrypt, we use another container which mounts `cht-ssl` volume - [recommend official certbot docker image
](https://eff-certbot.readthedocs.io/en/stable/install.html#id5)


**Describe the improvement you'd like**
* remove all code, docs and test for the `CERTIFICATE_MODE`  and `SSL_VOLUME_MOUNT_PATH`  environment variables

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
*  do nothing - it mostly works as is
* double down and try and get everything easier and less error prone by enhancing existing functionality.

title: Enable easy integration with certbot and nginx container
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Right now we're working on [deprecating the built in functionality](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8098) of our Let's Encrypt integration.  

After this, we should add in easy integration with an external to the CHT core  way to generate TLS certificates using Let's Encrpyt.  This will enable partners to easily set up TLS for self hosted deployments. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Using the [published certbot image](https://eff-certbot.readthedocs.io/en/stable/install.html#id5) we should:
* Make it easy for certbot to publish ` /.well-known/acme-challenge/*` by exposing this path  in `nginx` config and accessible via the `cht-ssl` volume 
* use `--deploy-hook` as needed to copy config/certs to where they need to after certificate is created

title: DNS queries for *.my.local-ip.com fail causing development instances to be unreachable
body:
**Describe the issue**
We have 3 projects that heavily rely on the *.my.local-ip.com TLS certs:
* [NGINX Local IP](https://github.com/medic/nginx-local-ip/)
* [CHT Docker Helper for 3.x](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/3.x/app-developer/#cht-docker-helper)
* [CHT Docker Helper for 4.x](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/4.x/app-developer/#cht-docker-helper-for-4x)

Because TLS requires DNS and because the DNS server for my.local-ip.com often fails, it feels like a developers instances is broken, when in fact DNS is failing to resolve for their my.local-ip.com IP.  

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Provide a new solution that offers the same conveniences as my.local-ip.com but has stable DNS. Either a commercial offering or a self hosted option based on open source

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
* Hope that my.local-ip.com resolves their DNS issue
* Stop offering a valid TLS cert from a real CA and revert back to only https://localhost self signed certs

title: Forms that use Enketo `format-date-time` fail to load in old versions of CHT-Android

title: Monitoring and Alerting for CHT 4 Self Hosting
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Right now there's no easy way to monitor and alert on your CHT instance for folks who are [self hosting](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/4.x/self-hosting-single-node/).

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Provide an out of the box solution that provides monitoring and alerting for [common monitoring metrics](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/monitoring/).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Using the [App Monitoring data ingest](https://github.com/medic/cht-app-monitoring-data-ingest/) coupled with [superset](https://superset.apache.org/docs/intro/) might work, but feel that an off the shelf time series database (TSDB) plus off the shelf dashboard that already works well together would be a better fit for this.  As well, SRE has indicated they could bring more metrics to this as they use a TSDB + dashboard already internally.

**Additional context**
The goal of this is that the alerts need to be both relevant and actionable.  To that end, this solution should:
* try to get as many P0's from "App Health Metrics" from [App Serv project](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Slr0Bs2oXg6uqX4XKma5c5jzQ1fMJYkwlIO_bRlJmvc/edit#heading=h.1u4z3n85mbaf) (private google doc) 
* hopefully get all of the monitoring API metrics for "free" with a cheap "get all the JSON" recipe from the which ever solution is chosen. 
* Cover key metrics from the [published monitoring doc](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/monitoring/)

**Describe the bug**

title: "Send Message" action shouldn't send message to user that is logged in
body:
**Describe the bug**
The [report doc’s `contact` property](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/4b3d35d124de56d899fe12fd0fe84f3632c00658/webapp/src/ts/effects/reports.effects.ts#L204) can be the user who created the report, not necessarily the patient. So when someone clicks on “Send Message,” it opens the Send Message modal with a pre-filled phone number of the user who created the report. 
With the current implementation, the person that wants to send the message can be the same as the one pre-filled in the Send Message modal.

There are some other considerations about this UX:
- For those using mobile, it can be confusing who they’re sending messages to because the default app for sms opens and does not always show right away the name of saved contacts in the phone. Perhaps we must improve this interaction and clarify to whom we’re sending the message.
- We know many CHWs use WhatsApp, not SMS or CHT in-app messaging.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. log in as a user with a phone number
2. Send a report where you don't need to select a patient.
3. Go to the Report list and select the report
4. Click on send message action.

**Expected behavior**
- If the report's contact is the same as the user's contact, then disable the button. 
- If we could find the patient by patient ID, consider replacing the button's label with a "message the patient".
- Consider launching WhatsApp and prepopulate the phone number from the app.

**Environment**
- Instance: local
- Browser: Chrome
- Client platform: MacOS
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.11.x to 4.2.0

**Additional context**
The action bar will eventually be deprecated, but this should still be fixed. [This action will be moved to a fast action button.](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7998)

title: Show confirmation message in training cards when navigating to another page
body:
**Describe the improvement you'd like**
When a user quits the training cards by clicking the "Cancel" button or the top-right "X" button, the app displays a confirmation message that says: `This training is not finished. You will lose your progress if you leave now. Are you sure you want to leave?`.

We should show this confirmation message when the user navigates to another page, for example:

1. The user logs in, and training cards show up.
2. The user clicks on the back button of the browser.
3. The app stops navigation and shows a confirmation message.
    3.1. The user confirms to quit training, and the app resumes navigation to the other page.
    3.2. The user prefers to stay, and the app resumes the training where it was interrupted. 

**Additional context**
The training cards were added to CHT Core as part of this [work](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6598).

title: Add hooks in nginx container for certbot
body:
# Description

* `enable_certbot_compatability()` function in [ssl-install.sh](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/8099-nginx-certbot/nginx/ssl-install.sh#L110) -  Creates  the directories to serve `certbot` validation HTTP GET requests
*  `enable_certbot_compatability()` function in [ssl-install.sh](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/8099-nginx-certbot/nginx/ssl-install.sh#L110) - Creates a `/etc/nginx/private/deploy.sh` script to run after `certbot` creates the certs to move them to the right location for `nginx` to see them.
* Note - this PR overrides the use of `AUTO_GENERATE`, as a preemptive re-use of it instead of deprecating it, as we're planning to do.  It also removes `generate_certificate_auto()` from [ssl-install.sh](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/8122/files#diff-1d142cadb0d352501f8ba0fa27b775e113f561125f67e52099cd8414d84cfe4fL67). This seemed less invasive, but I'm open to input!

medic/cht-core#8099

## To test

Assumes FQDN of `deleteme2-certbot-nginx-cht.plip.com` and a CHT SSL docker volume of `cht_cht-ssl`. Both are configurable in the `.env` file for certbot service. Use your own FQDN and verify volume name in `.env`.

Steps 7-11 will be the basis of the new documentation to [be added here.](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/4.x/adding-tls-certificates/)

1. provision Ubuntu 22.04 w/ Public IP and FQDN
   *NOTE* - you can not use auto created AWS EC2 names (eg `ec2-35-180-117-38.eu-west-3.compute.amazonaws.com`). You must create a FQDN outside of the  `*.amazonaws.com` domain.
3. install docker
    ```
    curl -fsSL get.docker.com -o get-docker.sh && sh get-docker.sh
    ```
4. Install CHT using compose files from this PR (per `curl` call), create dirs, env file, compose files per [the single node self hosted steps](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/4.x/self-hosting-single-node/). Note we set `CERTIFICATE_MODE=AUTO_GENERATE`:
    ```
    sudo apt-get install wamerican
    mkdir -p /home/ubuntu/cht/{compose,certs,upgrade-service,couchdb}
    couchdb_secret=$(shuf -n7 /usr/share/dict/words --random-source=/dev/random | tr '\n' '-' | tr -d "'" | cut -d'-' -f1,2,3,4,5,6,7)
    couchdb_password=$(shuf -n7 /usr/share/dict/words --random-source=/dev/random | tr '\n' '-' | tr -d "'" | cut -d'-' -f1,2,3,4,5,6,7)
    cat > /home/ubuntu/cht/upgrade-service/.env << EOF
    CHT_COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=cht
    COUCHDB_SECRET=${couchdb_secret}
    DOCKER_CONFIG_PATH=/home/ubuntu/cht/upgrade-service
    COUCHDB_DATA=/home/ubuntu/cht/couchdb
    CHT_COMPOSE_PATH=/home/ubuntu/cht/compose
    COUCHDB_USER=medic
    COUCHDB_PASSWORD=${couchdb_password}
    COUCHDB_UUID=${uuid}
   CERTIFICATE_MODE=AUTO_GENERATE
    EOF
    cd /home/ubuntu/cht/
    curl -s -o ./compose/cht-core.yml https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/medic:medic:8099-nginx-certbot/docker-compose/cht-core.yml
    curl -s -o ./compose/cht-couchdb.yml https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/medic:medic:8099-nginx-certbot/docker-compose/cht-couchdb.yml
    curl -s -o ./upgrade-service/docker-compose.yml https://raw.githubusercontent.com/medic/cht-upgrade-service/main/docker-compose.yml
    ```

5. start CHT services:
    ```
    cd /home/ubuntu/cht/upgrade-service
    docker compose up --detach
    ```

7. test `.well-known`  works inside the container CHT nginx container:
   ```shell
   echo "should show 'CERTIFICATE_MODE AUTO_GENERATE':"
   curl http://deleteme2-certbot-nginx-cht.plip.com/.well-known/acme-challenge/index.html
   ```
   
   **NOTE** If this fails, see note below. Do not proceed - it won't work!
   
8. create certbot compose and env file
   ```shell
   mkdir -p /home/ubuntu/cht/certbot
   cd /home/ubuntu/cht/certbot
   cat > docker-compose.yml << EOF
   version: '3.9'
   services:
     certbot:
         container_name: certbot
         hostname: certbot
         image: certbot/certbot
         volumes:
           - ssl-storage:/etc/nginx/private/
           - ssl-storage:/var/log/letsencrypt/
         command: certonly --debug --deploy-hook /etc/nginx/private/deploy.sh --webroot -w /etc/nginx/private/certbot/ --domain \$DOMAIN --non-interactive --key-type rsa --agree-tos --register-unsafely-without-email \$STAGING
   volumes:
     ssl-storage:
         name: \${CHT_SSL_VOLUME}
         external: true
   EOF
   
   cat > .env << EOF
   DOMAIN=deleteme2-certbot-nginx-cht.plip.com
   STAGING=
   CHT_SSL_VOLUME=cht_cht-ssl
   TZ=America/Whitehorse
   EOF
   ```
   
9. generate certs
   ```shell
   cd /home/ubuntu/cht/certbot
   docker compose up
   ```
   
10. reload `nginx`
    ```shell
    docker exec -it cht_nginx_1 nginx -s reload
    ```

11. confirm you have valid certs on domain

12. For a production instance, create a cronjob for once a week to renew certs:
    ```
    #!/bin/sh
    cd /home/ubuntu/cht/certbot
    docker compose up
    ```

### well-known/acme-challenge/index.html failing to show "CERTIFICATE_MODE AUTO_GENERATE"

This is likely because the CI build is not passing so the images on AWS aren't up to date :( The fix is to manually build the `nginx` container and update the image used in the compose file.  Follow these steps

1. stop all services 
   ```
   docker kill $(docker ps --quiet)
   ```
2. checkout cht-core, cd into it, build `nginx` image: 
   ```
   cd
   git clone https://github.com/medic/cht-core.git
   cd cht-core/nginx
   docker build -t nginx-8099 .
   ```
3. replace the image in the compose file with the one you just built:
   ```
   sed -i "s/image:\ public.ecr.aws\/medic\/cht-nginx:4.1.0-8099-nginx-certbot/image: nginx-8099/g" /home/ubuntu/cht/compose/cht-core.yml
   ```
4. go back to step `#5` above and start again ensuring the `curl` call succeeds.

title: Expose Prometheus-style metrics from API endpoint
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

As a part of https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8114 we are specifying Prometheus as the recommended time series database for real-time CHT metrics.  Unfortunately, Prometheus cannot directly consume our existing [`/monitoring` API endpoint](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/api/#get-apiv2monitoring) because the returned data is not in a format that Prometheus can ingest.

Our current solution is to run an extra service, [the `json-exporter`](https://github.com/prometheus-community/json_exporter), that handles taking data from our `/monitoring` API and maps it to a format that Prometheus can ingest.  The downside of this (besides just having the extra effort/complexity of an additional service) is that when new data is added to `/monitoring` and we want to record that data in Prometheus, the `json-exporter` config must be updated.  (And _every deployment_ of the monitoring stack will have to update their copy of the config.)

**Describe the solution you'd like**
[Many third-party software](https://prometheus.io/docs/instrumenting/exporters/#software-exposing-prometheus-metrics) expose metrics in a format that Prometheus can directly ingest (typically on the `/metrics` endpoint).  We could do the same in the CHT and allow Prometheus to directly pull the metrics.  This would eliminate the need for config changes when adding new metric values (since Prometheus can just discover the new metrics as the CHT server is updated).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could write our own exporter (instead of using `json_exporter`) which could be pre-configured to fetch metrics for a particular version of the CHT.  Then partners would only need to keep their version of the exporter in sync with their CHT version (and not worry about updating config files...).

title: Expose CHT API to extension libs at runtime
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
The [Extension Libs](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7824) feature introduced in 4.2.0.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
The Extension Libs are available via CHT API so they can be invoked from tasks, targets, contact summary, and enketo forms (and maybe others?). This is a big win for reuse, of business logic like determining if someone is high risk, _but_ you cannot currently call one extension lib from another.

Provide some way for an extension lib to access the CHT API and potentially call another extension lib for maximum reuse.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- have cht-conf bundle everything together, but then if a dev changes a single character in a lib then the user has to download all the js again not just the file that changed.
- expose common functions from cht-core, but it's impossible to predict all possible functions
