title: When unmuting parent do not cascade to contacts that were already muted before the parent
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently when muting/unmuting a parent contact (e.g. a household), the muting/unmuting will cascade down to the children of the contact (and so the household members will also be muted).  

However, consider the scenario where a CHW area contains a household, `H` that contains members: `A` and `B`.

- The CHW mutes `A` because they have temporarily left the area
- The CHW retires and so the CHW Supervisor mutes the whole CHW Area 
  - The muting cascades down to `H` and `B` (and technically `A`, but it is already muted)
- A new CHW is onboarded and so the supervisor unmutes the CHW Area.
  - The unmute cascades down to `H`, `A`, and `B` 
 
The undesirable behavior is that `A` is unmuted because the CHW Area was unmuted when, in fact, `A` has not yet returned to the area and should still be muted.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
From a behavior perspective, I think it would be preferable for unmuting to not cascade to contacts that were previously already muted.  The only thing that should unmute those contacts would be submitting an unmute form for them specifically.

**Additional context**
Originally raised in a conversation [on the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/new-documentation-available-re-muting/2476/3).

title: Refactor initial replication to not use PouchDb replicate
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
When performing initial replication, the user needs to download and save all documents from the server. 
Right now, initial replication uses the standard Pouch/Couch APIs and sequence of calls: 
- call _changes
- check local revs for existence of docs
- call _bulk_get or _all_docs to download missing docs
- repeat until _changes returns no results

The _changes feed request is expensive, because it requires calls to: 
- get all allowed doc ids, which is an expensive multi-key view request 
- get a batch of changes for these doc ids

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
I'm proposing we don't use PouchDb replicate at all, and instead:
- create an API endpoint that returns the list of doc_ids and their latest revs, along with the updated_seq of the database
- the client iterates over these docs_ids, checks local revs and calls a batched _bulk_get to get all missing docs
- call .replicate, passing the since equal to the updated_seq that the server sent to create the up to date checkpointer

**To Reproduce**
Steps to record the performance metrics:
TBD

title: Method for linking feedback docs to relevant telemetry docs
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
When analyzing feedback documents, I want to know what device the user is running, their doc_count, their available disk space. It'd be great to have all the telemetry stuff that we know about a user.

Currently, when doing this analysis there is no way to link a feedback doc and telemetry doc except for username and datetime. If a user has telemetry documents from multiple devices on the same day then we cannot know which device the error happened on and the analysis loses accuracy.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Telemetry documents have a [deviceId](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/performance/telemetry/#metadata) and a wealth of information about the user.  If the feedback document had the same `deviceId` then we can link the documents during in analysis.  

Very useful for Global Database Failures and other intermittent problems which happen project-wide.

title: PouchDb `Failed to execute 'transaction' on 'IDBDatabase'` due to device inactivity
body:
**Describe the bug**
This issue was reported numerous times, but became prominent more recently, after a big project upgraded to a newer version of the CHT, and started writing tasks to disk. 
Upon inspecting feedback documents generated by users reporting this problem, we've noticed that when a "global failure" was reported, the log list frequently also contained errors about IndexedDb timeouts.  
An example: 
```
\"Error getting tasks for all contacts\",{\"status\":500,\"name\":\"indexed_db_went_bad\",\"message\":\"unknown\",\"error\":true,\"reason\":\"TimeoutError\"}]"}
```

We followed this lead and found several Chromium bug reports about people seeing similar errors when laptops went to sleep while IndexedDB connections were open: 
https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=855624
https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=955470

@kennsippell 's excellent data analysis showed that:
- this is happening when users have a large number of documents
- issue is more frequent for older versions of Chrome but there are cases for newer versions as well. 

I managed to replicate this multiple times on my own device (Pixel 6a), on CHT-Core ~4.2.0, with a user with 26000 documents. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Replicate a user with a large number of documents (according to data, above 25000 docs)
2. Open the task page.
3.1. Put the phone to sleep for a few minutes
3.2. Switch to another activity for a few minutes (I had a whatsapp call which probably took a lot of device resources). 
4. Open CHT App again and see error. 

**Expected behavior**
Tasks should be displayed. 

**Logs**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/227868362-d7722875-bec7-4cdd-81a5-cf85eb23f3d9.png)

The last error seems to repeat ad-infinitum. I kept the tab opened for 30 minutes, and the console reports that 36.000 have been logged: 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/227868610-a07a0684-869e-4b44-83a1-a575117d8411.png)

This is a sample feedback document that was generated during one of these events: 

https://gist.github.com/dianabarsan/82c01f0c3331f7c85427151816c9cc3c

**Screenshots**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/227868161-65bf8401-ba3f-4e29-959f-949c9d00cfaa.png)

If I ignore the error and stay on the tasks page I see: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/227966337-6f44996f-3990-4d10-b6ec-a15dae60a60a.png)


**Environment**
- Browser: Chrome
- App: webapp
- Version: TBD based on data analysis

**Additional context**
This is definitely a race condition, so repro steps will most likely not trigger the error every time. 
Refreshing the app and keeping the screen on and the app in the foreground fixes the issue.

title: feat(#7462) add cht-form web component for standalone Enketo form support
body:
Closes #7462 

See the issue for more context/commentary, but ultimately this PR adds configuration and a minimal amount of code into `webapp` to allow for generating a custom web component that will allow for rendering/interaction with CHT forms outside of a formal CHT instance.  The web component is built from the existing Angular code in webapp, but is packaged into `.js`/`.css` files in such a way that it can be consumed externally by non-Angular webpages.  

See https://github.com/medic/cht-conf-test-harness/pull/245 for an example of how this web component will be used!

Also see https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/pull/12 for a super simple web page that uses the web component!

## contact-save service refactor

In the previous refactoring of the EnketoService/FormService (https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/8455) I missed the `contact-save.service` code.  This service owns all of the logic for _saving_ contact forms (the `form.service` is used for _rendering_ contact and app forms and for saving app forms).   The Web Component needs to depend on the `contact-save` service logic for processing the submitted contact form data into the expected contact documents.  However we do not want to also depend on the logic in the `contact-save` service for doing additional CHT things like running the client-side transitions.  

So, I have refactored the `contact-save` service to move all the CHT-specific logic to the `form.service` (similar to what we did with the `enketo.service` code).  Existing webapp code now will use the `form-service` for rendering/saving _both_ app and contact forms. Then, the Web Component can depend directly on the `contact-save.service` (as well as the `enketo.service`) without pulling in a ton of extra dependencies.

(Note that as with the EnketoService/FormService refactor, I have tried to achieve the best balance of high unit test coverage vs spending days refactoring the tests.  So, largely I duplicated the existing `contact-save` tests into the `forms.service` test file and made sure they all passed.  Then I did my best to de-dupe the tests between the `contact-save` and the `forms.service` test file so there was not too much redundancy. However, I did not update the new `forms.service` tests (the ones I copied in) to mock the `contact-save` service. For the sake of time, I left them as they were in the `contact-save` service test file. This is not ideal, but I think is an acceptable trade-off...)


## Caveats 

~~@tatilepizs is adding proper e2e tests [in a separate PR](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/8601) that will eventually be merged into this one. So, what you currently see in the `tests` directory just represents a prototype of future tests.~~

~~The contents of `webapp/web-componenets/example` are also just a prototype of a site that actually uses the web component.  This directory will not be included when merging to `master`, but I am keeping it in here for now because it is useful when manually testing the web component.~~

title: Race condition during sentinel startup
PouchDb `indexed_db_went_bad` due to device inactivity
body:
**Describe the bug**
This is similar to https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8149
Except the error is different. It is also triggered differently, as it happens when an attempt to write times out, compared to the other error that happens on a read. 

Please insert statistics @kennsippell 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Replicate a user with a large number of documents (according to data, above 25000 docs)
2. Create a script that takes 100 documents that the user should see, deletes all doc attachments and adds lots of keys to the docs. I added ~5000 uuid keys and values. The purpose is to make the bulkDocs payload large enough that there is enough of a time span to put the phone to sleep. 
3. Connect phone to desktop and use `chrome://inspect` in order to track network requests on the device. 
4. Run the script that updates/creates 100 ultra large docs.
5. Sync. Watching the network tab, put the phone to sleep immediately after you see the outgoing `_bulk_get` request finish. 
6. Put the phone to sleep immediately. Wait for a few minutes. 

**Logs**

The logs will be riddled with `Failed to execute 'transaction' on 'IDBDatabase` errors, most likely. Scroll through the errors until you see the `indexed_db_went_bad` error. 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/228361807-a28a6310-b78a-4531-8708-b6af2e9f558f.png)

Example feedback doc created during event: https://gist.github.com/dianabarsan/8d4ca724f5833df8c602d89d045468a6

**Screenshots**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/228361734-6d704c2e-1471-4e11-ab61-73302233b8b0.png)

**Environment**
- Instance: local
- Browser: Chrome
- App: webapp
- Version: 4.2.0

**Additional context**
This was a lot trickier to replicate than https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8149. I think I only saw these errors in the 5th or 6th try, after I had reduced CPU performance on the phone by 4x. 
Just as with the other issue, reloading the app and keeping the phone screen on fixes the issue.

title: Duplicate outbound requests are sent when a document matches multiple config options
body:
**Describe the bug**
Described very aptly on the forum: https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/outbound-destination-property/2485/5 and https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/outbound-destination-property/2485/3

> However, we are seeing one object outbound being executed twice for the same form. Never the first one and it works if it’s only one outbound object, but if we have two outbound objects, the second one is executed twice. If there are three the second and the third one are executed twice as well.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create two identical outbound configs (they need different names, but everything else should be identical)
2. Submit a document that matches the relevancy condition
3. Wait for the document to be processed and for the outbound queue to clear (could take up to 10 minutes)
4. Check outbound recipient requests and notice there were three calls, instead of 2. 

**Expected behavior**
Only two requests should be executed. 

**Logs**
No errors in the logs

**Environment**
- App: sentinel
- Version: 3.9+ 

**Additional context**
In order to figure out what was going on, I had to add debug messages all over the outbound code, and I ended up with logging the error that we received here: 
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/mark_for_outbound.js#L47

and it is: 
```
{
  error: 'conflict',
  reason: 'Document update conflict.',
  status: 409,
  name: 'conflict',
  message: 'Document update conflict.',
  stack: 'Error\n' +
    '    at Object.generateErrorFromResponse (/sentinel/node_modules/pouchdb-errors/lib/index.js:104:18)\n' +
    '    at /sentinel/node_modules/pouchdb-adapter-http/lib/index.js:254:33\n' +
    '    at runMicrotasks (<anonymous>)\n' +
    '    at processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:96:5)',
  docId: '41ac853d-9e76-479b-ac6a-1dd2dea52969-info'
}
```
This is because the same infodoc gets updated when outbound succeeds, but we don't bother updating the rev to allow successive edits. https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/mark_for_outbound.js#L44

This causes every following outbound "block" to throw an error and generate a task - that would trigger another outbound request on a schedule - even if the initial request was actually successful.

title: fix(#8166): Update tune.bufsize and remove rsyslog from haproxy image
body:
# Description

According to documentation, when increasing `tune.bufsize`, `maxconn` should be decreased by the same factor, otherwise there is a risk of OOM. 
> values larger than default size will increase memory usage, possibly causing the system to run out of memory. 

https://www.haproxy.com/documentation/hapee/latest/onepage/#3.2-tune.bufsize

In our config, we both increased maxconn and tune.bufsize by x 100. This caused the haproxy memory footprint to increase to up to 18GB. This memory is not released when connections are dropped and crashed instances that had a lower amount of available memory than this. 

Additionally, this PR removes `rsyslog` from haproxy image. It was no longer needed, since docker logs are already enough for funnelling haproxy logs, and having the service running prevented the container from restarting when the main haproxy process ran out of memory. 
The container automatically restarts now, so setting a default resource limit to the container becomes an option. 

medic/cht-core#8166

body:
**Describe the bug**
I believe this is a race condition, as it has been only reported twice, as far as we know. 
Once was [on the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/404-error-on-model-xml/2455/11) and once on [slack](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C024KTGRW/p1680869810577819). 
On slack, I was able to log into the instance and personally checked this was happening. I updated a form document and saw nothing appear in the api logs about receiving a change. 
Restarting API fixed the issue. 

I believe this is a race condition. I'll examine the instance logs for clues and update with findings. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Load CHT 4.1.0
1. Wait 10 seconds. 
1. `docker restart <your haproxy container>` or `docker restart <your couchdb container>`
1. Upload a new form
1. Load the new form in webapp and see error. When checking the console, you'll see a request to get `model.xml` and `form.html`, and both would fail with a 404. 

**Expected behavior**
Form attachments should be generated by changes watcher on the fly. 

**Logs**
No logs. no errors.

title: Upgrade Webapp to use Bootstrap 4 or 5
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
We use a very old version of `ngx-bootstrap@^7`, which can no longer be installed without passing `legacy-peer-deps`, because it lists an older Angular version as a peer dependency - it supports up to Angular 12.

At the same time, we use [Bootstrap 3 in webapp](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/a30c1649e129cca54a42cc4e60976ce73a314af9/webapp/src/ts/app.component.ts#L146).  
[Support for `bootstrap3` was dropped in `ngx-bootstrap@10`](https://github.com/valor-software/ngx-bootstrap/blob/development/CHANGELOG.md#breaking-changes). 
The latest version of `ngx-bootstrap` still supports bs3 is `9.0.0`, which supports up to Angular 14.  

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Update webapp to use a newer version of Bootstrap. Bootstrap 4 might be the easiest migration, with minimal changes required. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Drop `ngx-bootstrap`?
- We're fine with installing with `legacy-peer-deps` and ignore compatibility mismatches

**Additional context**
I wanted to remove the need for installing with `legacy-peer-deps`, this was the only true blocker.

title: nginx and haproxy should respect `Accept` headers when responding with error templates
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?** Both nginx and haproxy use the default error templates for 4xx and 5xx responses. These templates are html. Respecting the `Accept` header would standardize the behavior of the CHT, and this is important since we expect third party software to call CHT APIs. To reproduce: - start CHT 4.x - stop your api container `docker stop ` - request a JSON response from API: ```shell curl -k https://localhost -H 'Accept: application/json' ``` ``` 502 Bad Gateway

502 Bad Gateway

nginx/1.19.6
``` If you are logged into webapp, you will see a JSON parse error spammed in the console: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/232050203-f0b152b0-fe75-4156-bece-2765155dc3b0.png) **Describe the improvement you'd like** We should change nginx and haproxy configs to respond with JSON when the `Accept: application/json` header is passed. **Describe alternatives you've considered** Leave it as it is. **Additional context** I had a script that passed the result of an API call to `jq`. Because the response was html, my `jq` call failed. Similarly, we've seen reports of feedback docs being generated that feedback docs get generated in webapp when with `Unexpected token < in JSON at position 0`: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6412 https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7782

title: Haproxy logs - serving as audit trail - truncate logged body when encoding is chunked
body:
**Describe the bug**
We are using `haproxy` logs as an auditing tool. However, `haproxy` has a severe limitation where it will not log the full body of a long post request. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Load up a 4.x instance (All containers) with seed data from scalability test. 
2. Login as an offline user. 
3. Set yourself as offline. 
4. Use the bulk delete feature to delete 20 reports (number is random, but make sure payload is considerable). The deletion in bulk only serves as a quick way of creating a large-ish payload to send to the server. You could equally create many docs or edit many docs, the used endpoints will be the same. 
5. [Wait until process is complete](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8180)
7. Start watching haproxy logs. 
8. Reload the webapp page, set as offline and sync. 
9. Inspect the haproxy logs for `_bulk_docs` requests. Look at the body that is logged. Copy the body and load it up in a JSON parser. 
10. See that JSON is incomplete. 

**Expected behavior**
We rely on haproxy logs as an audit trail. This means that the whole body of the write request should be logged. It is not. 

**Logs**
Example of logged haproxy `_bulk_docs` that truncates body: 
https://gist.githubusercontent.com/dianabarsan/205d23ef1761812ef880c4a6990ecdd6/raw/f1f3e644791d2977aa4ff94597838094a9dead51/gistfile1.txt


**Environment**
- App: haproxy
- Version: 3.0+

**Additional context**
This is related to haproxy logging on request received, not on request complete. If the request body is chunked, only the first chunk will be logged. 

https://docs.haproxy.org/2.0/configuration.html#7.3.6-req.body
> This returns the HTTP request's available body as a block of data. It requires that the request body has been buffered made available using "option http-buffer-request". In case of chunked-encoded body, currently only the first chunk is analyzed.

title: Add visibility to documents that were denied from upwards replication
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When an offline user syncs up (uploads documents), API checks whether that specific user has access to create / update those documents. When a user pushes a doc they should not be allowed to create or edit, the doc is not saved in the main `medic` database, and the request returns a `denied` response for that doc. Upload is retried 3 times for each denied document. A telemetry entry is recorded every time a denied event happens. 
There is no visibility, however, on what the these docs are, as they never get stored on the server, and POST bodies are not logged in nginx or API. 

Reasons for denied docs to exist are (not comprehensive): 
- move contacts produces docs with incorrect lineages
- supervisors submitting reports for subjects they can't see and the reports lack `needs_signoff` property
- reports with incorrect fields (form/task issues), not linking to the correct subject
- config changes that affect previously created docs
- incorrect replication (user device having docs they shouldn't have)

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Discuss ways to make the contents of these docs available for analysis. 
These can include: 
- storing the docs in a separate database (this requires a separate sync mechanism)
- storing the docs in the users meta database and possibly coalescing into `medic-users-meta`
- ??? 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
If these events are sufficiently rare, as we initially believed, we could choose to continue to ignore these docs. 

**Additional context**
[The issue](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6103) where denied replication was initially addressed.

title: Remove configuration wizard
body: **Describe the issue** Related [forum post](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/configuration-wizard/2670). The configuration wizard will be displayed the first time a user logs in if the user has the `can_configure` permission and the `setup_complete` property in `app_settings` is `false`. Closing this screen (even without setting anything) updates `setup_complete` to `true` and the screen does not show up again (but is still accessible from the hamburger menu). **Step 1** The modem setup, is only needed if you’ll be sending SMS which isn’t the first concern for most projects anymore. **Step 3** The language preference, is mostly useful for translating SMS messages, now users on smartphones pick their own language when they log in. **Step 2** ( Identify Care Coordinators) and **Step 4** (Registration form) aren't being used anywhere. it was probably useful in the DIY days, but less so today. **Describe the improvement you'd like** Remove the configuration wizard from webapp **Describe alternatives you've considered** Leave it there and fix the UI to explain better the steps and make it more friendly.

# Description

In versions prior to 4.3, training cards would appear on top of privacy policies for instances with an active training an a privacy policy enabled. This was partially due to training cards being displayed via the `initForms` method in `app.component.ts`, independent of the status of other elements of the user's session.

This PR presents a solution in which training cards are initialized and displayed alongside the startup modals in `startup-modals.service.ts` (as per @latin-panda's suggestion). In order to display training cards in sequence with the other startup modals, rather than directly above them. 

Like the startup modals, training cards are displayed by `ModalService.show`, and returning this promise to be used in `startup-modals.service.ts` allows for trainings to be displayed in sequence with the other startup modals.

To achieve this, the method `TrainingCardsService.showTrainingCards` was added, which calls `TrainingCardsService.initTrainingCards` and returns a promise that resolves to the "shown" training cards once they are available.

The resulting behavior can be seen below:

title: Add a way to know whether an offline user successfully synced
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Knowing whether a user has successfully managed to upload all of their pending documents is important in many situations. To list a few: 
- before changing hierarchies
- before moving contacts
- before an upgrade
- before disabling an account

This is a temporary knowing, of course, because once the user is offline, they could make as many edits as they desire, while the server gets no information about this. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We already store the upwards replication checkpointer on the serverside. This checkpointer document contains the local sequence of the last document that was uploaded. 
If we could store the generic `update_seq` of the local database along with this seq, we could compare the two to determine whether sync-ing is in progress or was interrupted before all documents were uploaded. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The checkpointer document is right now a byproduct if PouchDb replication, which PouchDb doesn't provide direct access to. 
We could either choose the direction of gaining access to it or build our own structure to store this information. 

**Additional context**
[Recent request on the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/how-to-be-sure-that-all-users-synced-on-a-specific-date/2678)

title: Nginx can't connect to API after container restarts because of dynamic IP allocation
body:
**Describe the bug**
Docker allocates dynamic IPs within a network. When a container restarts, there's a chance the IP changes. However nginx caches DNS queries to backend servers and never tries them again. 
As a result, after an API restart and IP change, nginx fails to connect. 

This is a known issue: 
https://github.com/docker/compose/issues/3314
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/27912917/how-to-configure-docker-port-mapping-to-use-nginx-as-an-upstream-proxy
https://serverfault.com/questions/722438/nginx-refresh-upstream-server-ip
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/63154521/connect-failed-113-host-is-unreachable-while-connecting-to-upstream-nginx-f

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Start CHT 4.
1. Run `docker network inspect <your network name>` and check API's IP
1. Restart some containers to get IPs to swap. I used: 
```docker stop <haproxy> -t 0 && docker stop <api> -t 0 && docker start <haproxy> && docker start <api>```. 
For some reason, when restarting a single container, I never got an IP change, but did get it quite consistently when restarting two. 
1. Wait for one minute - or make sure everything is up and running by checking container logs. Make a request to the server. 
1. Get 502. 


**Expected behavior**
nginx should be able to remap backends ips. 

**Logs**
```
2023/04/27 21:19:33 [error] 41#41: *8603 connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream, 
client: 172.30.0.1, server: , request: "GET /api/info HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://172.30.0.7:5988/api/info", 
host: "localhost"
172.30.0.1 - admin [27/Apr/2023:21:19:33 +0000] "GET /api/info HTTP/1.1" 502 157 "-" "-"
```

The IP of api was `172.30.0.6` at this point. 

**Environment**
- App: nginx
- Version: 4+

**Additional context**
I discovered this when working on https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8173, after adding an e2e test that restarted haproxy, which resulted in an expected API restart as well. Once API was up, nginx could not connect. 
Restarting nginx fixes this issue.

title: Contact and Messages Tab:  footer button scrolls with content, not staying pinned
body:
## Describe the bug

_Originally reported on the forum [here](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/change-of-button-position-after-a-given-number-of-entries/2708)._

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7998 Introduced a Floating Action Button and a list footer button (on desktop). The list footer button on desktop is supposed to stay pinned to the bottom of the list at all times. On the Contacts tab, when there are many rows in the list (basically once a scrollbar shows up), it becomes "unpinned" and scrolls with the content. It seems to work fine on the Reports tab, I didn't test the Messages tab, and it's not applicable to the Tasks tab (there is no button on the LHS on Tasks tab).

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Go to the Contacts tab on desktop
2. Make sure you have more places than can fit on the screen by creating a bunch of test places. 
3. Scroll down
4. Notice that the list footer button scrolls with the content

**NB** - the same thing happens on messages tab too

## Expected behavior
List footer button should stay pinned in all circumstances.

## Screenshots

Animated GIF (say "Jiff!!!") showing reports tab working, but people tab not working
![bottom button](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10096985/236032562-872f0b43-2ffa-4195-a361-26a2f181ccfe.gif)

Video showing people tab fixed #8219, but messages tab is broken: 

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8253488/236578298-48eede77-7cf0-4f01-b3af-02c5e7efaa02.mov

- Instance: Local docker
- Browser: Chrome
- Client platform: MacOS
- App: WebApp
- Version: `master`

title: Align nginx and ALB timeout values
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
In k8s medic-hosted deployments, we use AWS ALB as a proxy to API. 
In 4.x deployments, we use nginx. 

ALB has a configured timeout on 1h, however our nginx configured timeout is 10 minutes: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/nginx/nginx.conf#L14

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
I think should align these values. 
We should evaluate: 
- which requests we expect to be lengthy
- how long we expect them to be

**Additional context**
CouchDb has an internal default timeout of 5 minutes. We have seen this timeout get set with large requests to get purged docs.

title: Upgrade Message in Clustered Mode Should Include CouchDB containers (couchdb.1, couchdb.2, etc) - for use by kubernetes upgrade service
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**

When using the CHT in a cluster, the upgrade message should include a list of the couchdb containers to be upgraded by the upgrade service. This is important when dealing with the [kubernetes upgrade service](https://github.com/medic/upgrade-service-kubernetes) since it can upgrade couchdb even in a cluster on different nodes.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

The upgrade message includes a list of all couchdb containers (couchdb.1, couchdb.2, couchdb.3, etc) - possibly by querying couchdb for the cluster nodes.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Alternative is that the upgrade has to be done manually by editing the deployment manifest. This is not ideal. Especially, since the Kubernetes upgrade service already supports this.

title: Propagate request uuid from API to audit logging layer
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
When API receives a request from a client, we assign a unique ID to it, which gets logged along with some basic request / response information. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Propagate this unique UUID to the audit layer (right now haproxy, but this is likely to change) as a header, and include it in the log. This should also apply for requests that compound and not directly proxied - for example an offline user request to changes ends up generating multiple requests to CouchDb, and these requests should have the same uuid as the original client request. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None. 

**Additional context**
This is extremely helpful when analyzing logs. Without this, the correlation between the API incoming request and the cascade of couchdb requests is loose and sometimes impossible to determine.

title: Support ODK guidance_hints in forms
body:
[Guidance hints](https://xlsform.org/en/#guidance-hints) are collapsible (and collapsed by default) hint texts that can be added to questions in a form.  Normal hints are always displayed and so are always taking up screen space.  This is not great for extensive information that might not always need to be referenced but still is important to have available to the user.  Reference information could be embedded in a guidance hint that the user could reference when needed, but otherwise would not affect their workflow (they would not have to scroll past a bunch of text they are not going to read....).  

These guidance hints are already supported in enketo-core `5.5.2`+ so cht-core 4.x technically already has built-in support.  However, our verison of [pyxform](https://github.com/medic/pyxform) does not support including these in the form xml when converting the xlsx. So, that would need to be upgraded to be able to use the functionality.  Also, cht-core needs a new translation and probably some css tweaking to make stuff look nice.  

_[Related forum post](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/collapsible-form-section/2713/7?u=michael)_


I kinda manually compiled an xml for a form with a guidance hint and loaded into the CHT and this is what it looks like currently:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8441903/236497325-a0cc6aaf-2958-4ca5-8622-2712dc226804.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8441903/236497350-043d923c-6ac4-4c54-b0a8-927236ebdab2.png)

```.xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<h:html xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2002/xforms" xmlns:h="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:ev="http://www.w3.org/2001/xml-events" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema" xmlns:jr="http://openrosa.org/javarosa" xmlns:orx="http://openrosa.org/xforms">
  <h:head>
    <h:title>Enketo Widgets</h:title>
    <model>
      <itext>
        <translation default="true()" lang="en">
          <text id="/enketo_widgets/my_group/name:hint">
            <value form="guidance">This is a guidance hint!</value>
          </text>
        </translation>
      </itext>
      <instance>
        <enketo_widgets id="enketo_widgets" prefix="J1!enketo_widgets!" delimiter="#" version="2023-05-05 00:00:00">
          <my_group>
            <age/>
            <name/>
          </my_group>
          <meta tag="hidden">
            <instanceID/>
          </meta>
        </enketo_widgets>
      </instance>
      <instance id="contact-summary"/>
      <bind nodeset="/enketo_widgets/my_group/age" type="string"/>
      <bind nodeset="/enketo_widgets/my_group/name" type="string"/>
      <bind nodeset="/enketo_widgets/meta/instanceID" type="string" readonly="true()" calculate="concat('uuid:', uuid())"/>
    </model>
  </h:head>
  <h:body class="pages">
    <group appearance="field-list" ref="/enketo_widgets/my_group">
      <input ref="/enketo_widgets/my_group/age">
        <label>Age?</label>
        <hint>this is a regular hint</hint>
      </input>
      <input ref="/enketo_widgets/my_group/name">
        <label>Name?</label>
        <hint ref="jr:itext('/enketo_widgets/my_group/name:hint')"/>
      </input>
    </group>
  </h:body>
</h:html>
```

title: Support collapsible form groups
body:
Currently there is no way to show/hide sections of a form except via `relevant` logic.  This does not work for all use-cases since values in the non-relevant part of the form will not be saved at the end. ([Forum conversation](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/collapsible-form-section/2713/7?u=michael))

The default Enekto webapp supports being able to just collapse groups (that do not have the `field-list` appearance).  

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8441903/236499737-6fc095b4-d9c1-422f-9333-23528346360e.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8441903/236499821-dc413d6a-0a13-4dc4-be52-992158ab1640.png)

We could support similar functionality in the CHT, though we may want to make it opt-in. So if you added the `collapsible` appearance to a group it would make this happen. title: Docker image build fails for branch names with reserved characters
body:
(Update from @jkuester 2025-08-04)

I think the core of this issue (as noted in [this comment](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8220#issuecomment-1536837985)) is that the Git branch name is used as the "tag" for the docker images that are built locally when the `npm run local-images` script is executed.  This is to allow for having different versions of the CHT images in your local Docker context (one version/tag for each branch) when doing development and testing. 

Unfortunately, git is very permissive when it comes to what characters you can use in the branch name.  On the other hand, Docker is much more picky about the characters that are [allowed in the image tag](https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/image/tag/#extended-description).  Specifically, it seems that Docker uses the [Go package format](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/distribution/reference#pkg-overview) for its Docker image registry and so your image tag needs to match the pattern: `/[\w][\w.-]{0,127}/`.  

## Needed changes

The simple fix for this seems to be to just strip the unsupported characters from the git branch name before using it as a docker tag.  

The build scripts (including `local-images`) are already using [this function](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/f1bdfc07c0f4b1170e0d8be671cd27aa105baff4/scripts/build/versions.js#L13) to "escape" the branch name before using it.  Unfortunately this function currently only converts `/[/|_]/` chars.  (Notably the `(` char is absent which is why the `fix(8213)-contact-new-not-scroll` branch name still fails.)  

I think we should update that `escapeBranchName` function to replace all unsupported characters (basically anything that does not match: `/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]/`).  

To test your changes to the script you will need:

- A [working cht-core development environment](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/community/contributing/code/core/dev-environment/)
- Checkout an "invalid" branch name in git: `git checkout -b fix(8213)-contact-new-not-scroll`
- Run `npm ci && npm run build-dev` to build the assets
- Build the docker images with `npm run local-images`.

If your logic is correct, the `local-images` script should complete without errors. 👍 


---
(Original issue description)

**Describe the issue**
Since yesterday (May 4th 6pm Pacific), none of the "Publish for testing" CI has passed.  You can see all the [failed tests here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/workflows/build.yml). Following the CI down to the to the line that errors, I _believe_ (but I'm not 100% sure!)  it's:

1. in `build.yml` we call `node grunt build-service-images` in the ["Publish For Testing" section](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/.github/workflows/build.yml#L64)
1. In the `Gruntfile.js` it's failing in the `build-service-images` [call here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/58f23a8db0651faeb8c9fdeb7a00a288e05950cf/Gruntfile.js#L296).

The [full error is here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/runs/4895891000/jobs/8745289588) and the output is:

>> /bin/sh: 1: Syntax error: "(" unexpected

```

title: Cannot use db-object-widget to load contact data in non-relevant `inputs` group
body:
**Describe the bug**
If the `inputs` group in a form is never relevant, then the `select-contact` feature from the db-object-widget cannot be used to load contact data into a sub-group of the `inputs` group.

Take the following form:

type | name | label::en | relevant | appearance | calculation
-- | -- | -- | -- | -- | --
begin group | inputs | NO_LABEL | ./source = 'user' | field-list |  
begin group | contact | NO_LABEL |   | field-list |  
begin group | parent | NO_LABEL |   |   |  
hidden | _id | Parent ID |   |   |  
end group | parent |   |   |   |  
end group | contact |   |   |   |  
begin group | my_parent_data |   |   |   |  
string | _id |   |   | select-contact | ../../contact/parent/_id
string | name |   |   |   |  
end group | my_parent_data |   |   |   |  
end group | inputs |   |   |   |  

This does not work in situations where `./source = 'user'` is false (does not work when opening the form from the "People" tab with a contact in context.  

I think this behavior is the result of some incomplete [patching](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/webapp/patches) of the `enketo-inputs-always-relevant` situation where Enketo is still not actually evaluating the calculations in the non-relevant `inputs` group.  [Other `inputs` data](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/forms/form-inputs/) (such as `inputs/contact`) will show up just fine since it is pre-loaded into the form.  All of this kind of makes sense from the Enketo logic perspective, but is _really confusing_ for any consumer trying to get their form to work!
�
The whole `inputs` functionality probably needs to be re-thought in `5.0`, but for now, it might be enough to just add an additional patch(es) in enketo-core for places [like this](https://github.com/enketo/enketo-core/blob/b83271e8cc88fb79ddeb4f79fb1194d2aac9f421/src/js/calculate.js#L199) that would allow for calculations to run inside the non-relevant `inputs` group. 

**Environment**
- Version: `master` (`4.1.x`)

**Additional context**

The work-around here is to not try to use the `select-contact` in the `inputs` group unless you know that it is going to be relevant when you need it.

[forum thread](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/query-parent-contact-place-data-in-child-form/2711/4)

title: Do not display a form page when all the contents are "hidden"
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**

Basically, what I am trying to achieve is to support loading contact data via the db-object-widget into a "hidden" top-level group.

It is possible to use the `select-contact` functionality to transitively load data about a tangentially related contact into a form. For example, if you want to get the `name` value of the _parent_ of the current contact in context, you could have a group like this:

type | name | label::en | appearance | calculation
-- | -- | -- | -- | --
begin_group | parent_data | NO_LABEL | field-list |  
string | _id | NO_LABEL | select-contact | …/input/contact/parent
calculate | name | NO_LABEL |   | ""  
end_group

Unfortunately, doing it this way will still cause a question to be displayed in the form for `parent_data/_id` (which is not what we want if we are just trying to transitively load data from the parent).  

Adding the `hidden` appearance to the `parent_data` group (or both fields) will prevent the fields from actually showing in the form, but you still end up with an empty page in the form (caused by the group).  

You cannot always put the `select-contact` load inside the `inputs` group because of https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8225.

You cannot use `calculate`s for all the fields in the `parent_data` group. `_id` needs to have `appearance` values (for the db-object-widget to see), but `appearance` values are not set on `calculate` fields.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
I _think_ the most straight-forward way to achieve what I am looking for is to just not render (skip) any pages where everything is `hidden`.  

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
If the db-object-widget could work with `calculate` fields, we probably would not need to do anything here since groups with nothing but calculates are already not rendered.

([original forum thread](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/query-parent-contact-place-data-in-child-form/2711/4))

title: Add debugging options to wdio tests
body:
**Describe the issue**
At the moment, as in this [documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/TESTING.md), debugging involved going into the conf file and changing stuff like the `--headless` arg and the mochaOpts/timeout. This is not ideal, as one is changing files unnecessarily which could lead to unintentionally checking in those changes- plus this option does not s till give us the full advantage of debugging, we cannot interact with the test run, just observe.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

- Add a DEBUG environmental variable that can be used when the dev wants to use the debug mode
- If DEBUG, tests will run headful and the timeout is increased to allow time for interaction
- See [documentation](https://webdriver.io/docs/api/browser/debug/)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
As above, do manual modifications to the conf file

title: Figure out a different way to use purged docs cache
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Right now, purged docs are cached for a very short interval (5 minutes) - for considerations of memory management. 
Recent research has shown that: 
- users end up having a very large number of documents before purging - with 40k being common, growing up to 100k docs
- cache is used in 40% of requests

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Experiment with increasing TTL, and only bust cache when purging has run again. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
If experiments show that the memory footprint of the cache for a large project (suppose 4000 users each with 60k pre-purge docs, cached), investigate whether cache can be saved on disk.

**Additional context**
@kennsippell has been analyzing production logs and observing request behavior. Querying for purged docs in this project, which has  very aggressive purging and high number of pre-purge docs, the purging requests take up to 40% of server time.

title: Can't turn off permissions for `national_admin` role in admin app
body:
**Describe the bug**
A user with the `role` of national admin will always have all permissions enabled in webapp. 
[This was reserved solely for db admins](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blame/1edc93a9555737e2734fb37f4d7883a2fe3c400d/webapp/src/ts/services/auth.service.ts#L33) (user with the reserved couchdb role `_admin`) but was changed when adding the [CHT script API](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/commit/869fd7103723730f9f7a7a990c058687c8c3cbf5).

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Disable UHC (delete the `uhc` property in `settings` and uncheck the permission `can_view_last_visited_date` for all roles)
2. Create an online user. Give them the `national_admin` role. You can either configure this role or just leave it unconfigured and just add it manually to the `user` doc in `_users` db. Assign this user to a contact that would see places that have [`count_visits` enabled](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/config/default/app_settings.json#L335).
3. Login with this user and load the contacts tab.
4. See that the contacts list shows UHC last visited dates. 

**Expected behavior**
It should be possible to not display `last_visited` for `national_admin` role, but currently we only exclude that for `_admin`. 

**Logs**
Not applicable. 

**Screenshots**
![image](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/35681649/851e1bef-8a41-4156-bd83-2f4ed5d5e415)


**Environment**
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.12+

**Additional context**
Reported [on the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/seeking-clarity-on-the-national-admin-role-and-mm-online-role/2746/3?u=diana) after logs for a live instance were analyzed and observing very long view queries made by `national_admin`s loading the contact page, even though they did not have permissions to view last visited dates.

title: Updating contact information through the API
body:
This is a request for an update in relation to the feature request below:
Organization: International Training and Education Center for Health (I-TECH)
Organization Type: Technical
What Other Organizations Would Benefit From This Feature: All

**Describe the Feature:** As an engineer working with the API, I would like to be able to update contact information so that I can easily update certain bits of information about the contact.

**What “Pain Point” Does The Proposed Feature Address:** Currently there is no way to update contact information through the API. For instance, if I need to update a client’s phone number from another platform then I’d need to directly write to CouchDB. As far as I can tell, CouchDB does not support partial updates to documents as well. The current solution creates implementation leaks and room for error.

**Proposed Solution**: Open up a route under the contacts/people resource that allows one to supply some data points about the contact they’d like changed. For example a PUT request to /contacts/:id that accepts a JSON payload with the data points to update. This given that contact’s identifier is supplied.

Links To Supporting Information / Uploads: (https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/updating-contact-information-throught-the-api/2692)
Link to previous GH ticket: [Updating contact information through the API](https://github.com/medic/config-itech/issues/1501)

title: Working with messages between RapidPro and CHT using code: making automated messages from Rapidpro to CHT and clients visible on the message tab
body:
[Working with messages between RapidPro and CHT contacts using code](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/working-with-messages-between-contacts-using-code/2691)
Your Organization: Medic/University of Washington – CHV-NEO
Organization Type: Technical
What Other Organizations Would Benefit From This Feature: interventions with an interactive messaging component
Describe the Feature: CHV-NEO is an app that integrates the CHT (eCHIS) with RapidPro to provide direct to client communication between community Health volunteers (CHVs) and their clients (specifically peri-partum women). Part of this intervention includes sending automated messages to clients, and clients sending back unstructured conversational responses, which CHVs respond to manually. We would like the automated messages sent from RapidPro to clients to also appear in the Messages tab. We want them to appear as being sent from the community health volunteer (CHV) to the client. This so that the CHV is able to make sense out of the messaging history and respond to their clients appropriately and on time.
What “Pain Point” Does The Proposed Feature Address:  Currently on CHT, only manual interactive messages between the CHV and the client are visible on the message tab chat thread. Clients are also receiving daily/weekly automated messages – visit reminders and educational messages – most of which end with a question, but these are not visible in the messages tab. When clients send messages in response to automated messages, the client messages’ meaning cannot be easily understood without the automated message as context. We would like CHVs to be able to see the automated messages so they can follow the conversation, but have automated messages appear as read so that CHVs can prioritize interactive messages from the client that need a prompt response. This feature is essential for launch of the CHV-NEO program June 1.
Proposed Solution: 
We explored the following ways of doing this through RapidPro webhooks:
POSTing to /api/sms and specifying “from” and “to” properties in the payload. This did not seem to work.
Creating an sms_message data record for the contact directly in CouchDB. This worked. However, we noted that since these automated messages will show up as new messages for the CHV, it would create spam and make it difficult to discern these automated messages from actual client interactions.
Directly write the message to the database (should not trigger unread message notification)
Where we need help:
Alternatives to achieving this that may be easier and less complicated
How to mark the sms_message data record as already read so that we avoid spamming the CHV. This in the case that there are no better ways of achieving what we need.
Do you have funding to cover external developers? Yes with technical support from the product team
Do You Have Resources (Designers, Developers, PMs) Available: we have a designer, PM and developer
Links To Supporting Information / Uploads: forum post is here [Working with messages between RapidPro and CHT contacts using code](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/working-with-messages-between-contacts-using-code/2691) additional information on MobileWACh is in the description below
The messaging strategy used in CHV-NEO is adapted from a previous intervention named Mobile WACh (Publications can be found [here, ](https://bmjopen.bmj.com/content/11/12/e056062.long)[here](https://dl.acm.org/doi/epdf/10.1145/2702123.2702124) and [here](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29924912/)). In this strategy, clients receive automated messages grounded in behavioral theory and covering a range of health education topics. Automated messages end with a question to promote engagement and behavior change. Clients are encouraged to respond to messages with unstructured messages, which CHVs then respond to in an ongoing conversation. Note that unlike previous 2-way texting projects using the CHT, in our messaging strategy we are not expecting structured responses (eg 1/0) and we are not asking the same question in every message (eg do you need help). In our previous implementations of Mobile WACh across 7 studies in Kenya we have seen that clients message conversationally, including responses that cannot be understood without reading the prior system message (eg. “Yes”, “No”, “A little”). It is therefore necessary for CHVs to be able to read the automated messages when reading client messages. It is also necessary for the messaging tab of CHT to only indicate unread messages when there are unread client messages for the CHV to respond to (not automated messages that do not need the CHV’s attention). See the screenshots below for examples of the types of messages clients send and how the desired functionality was facilitated in a different messaging system.

title: UHC mode features not usable in some hierarchy configurations
body:
## Problem

CHWs don't know how to prioritize household visits because UHC mode does not work with some hierarchy configurations. When there are 1 or more hierarchy levels between CHW Area and Household, "Days since last visit" and "Number of Visits" are not viewable in household lists and it's not possible to sort households by last visit date. 

## Context

[UHC mode](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/forms/uhc-mode/) is based on household level activities. When UHC mode was originally [released](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/2.18.0/), the CHT only supported 3 place types and households were expected to be directly below CHW Area.  When CHWs accessed the Contacts tab, they always saw households in the LHS (left hand side) list, UHC related information was shown in the list, and CHWs could specify what value to sort on.

In [3.7.0](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/3.7.0/#configurable-hierarchies) we released [configurable hierarchies](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/concepts/hierarchy/). This did not break UHC Mode, it still works fine if households are configured directly below CHW Areas, but if there are 1 or more levels **_between_** the CHW Area and Household, CHWs no longer see households in the LHS list so UHC mode can no longer be used the way it was intended.

## Example 
If the hierarchy has the following [contact_types](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/app-settings/hierarchy/): `District -> Supervisor Area -> CHW Area -> Village -> Household`, CHWs see Villages in the LHS list not Households, so UHC information is not shown in the list and the list is not sortable.

![Screenshot 2023-05-16 at 5 26 52 PM](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/10096985/bb0091e0-65ef-471d-bafb-89f2bd29965c)

title: Replace local-ip.co in CHT 3.x Docker Helper, ensure certs get installed.
body:
**Describe the issue**
We did a lot of work around #8100 to improve DNS and TLS for app developers.  This work was not back-ported to [Docker Helper for CHT 3.x](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/3.x/app-developer/#cht-docker-helper) so it still uses the problematic `local-ip.co`.  As well, it looks like the cert isn't actually installed and users need to run the [add-local-ip-certs-to-docker.sh](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/add-local-ip-certs-to-docker.sh) script and specify the name of their container.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Have CHT 3.x Docker Helper default to using `local-ip.medicmobile.org` and ensure cert installs correctly.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
leave as is

title: Medic-api-log indicating empty responses during periods of high load
body:
I'm analysing production medic-api-logs to monitor a CHT production instance. I'm seeing intermittent drops in [yield](https://sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives/) where large numbers of requests are "unsuccessful" for sustained periods (1% of total requests are unsuccessful, and the worst minutes have ~35% of requests unsuccessful).

Looking at request logs during these periods of low yield, some are due to 500 errors due to overload at CouchDB. But it is 10x more common to see logged response events which look like this:

```
[2023-04-17 11:45:42] RES 0a90537d-6101-4510-ace7-42714ce05b0b 197.155.150.209 - GET /medic/form%3Atb_followup_weekly/form.html HTTP/1.1 - - - ms
[2023-04-17 11:45:42] RES 0dfa85c6-2559-4c7c-b639-5032b4257ecd 197.155.150.209 - GET /medic/form%3Acontact%3Ac30_supervisor_area%3Acreate/model.xml HTTP/1.1 - - - ms
[2023-04-17 11:45:42] RES 11c38315-f93d-4fbf-ba4e-e6ca0335b866 197.155.150.209 - GET /medic/form%3Aanc_followup/form.html HTTP/1.1 - - - ms
```

The `- - -` is indicating that the response from Medic-API has no status code, no response time, etc. We use morgan for these logs, and according to [this morgan issue](https://github.com/expressjs/morgan/issues/121) the cause of logging events like this is:

> This happens when you do not write a response and allow the app to just hang. The reason you get the dashes is because since you didn't write a response, there is no response code, there is no response time, there is no response size, etc. Basically you are seeing all the properties of the response as dashes (i.e. unknown) and the properties of the request populated in that log.

During a period of ~20 days, this affected >1% of all responses. These drops in yield usually coincide with periods of high load. This happened multiple times every day with the worst day having ~5000 responses like this. This affects many different url paths (list below).  The majority of these responses are logged within 10 minutes of the request, but many (~10%) are after 10-20 minutes, and many (~10%) are after 60-70 minutes. 

url_bucket | count
-- | --
medic/form%3.* | 2400
/medic/_changes w/o longpoll | 2161
/medic/_design/medic-client | 2009
/purging/changes | 1992
/medic/_bulk_docs | 1128
/_session | 625
/dbinfo | 426
/medic/_revs_diff | 210
/medic/_all_docs | 170
medic-user-.*-meta/_local.* | 138
/medic/[a-zA-Z0-9\-]{36} | 130
/medic/login | 125
medic-user-.*-meta | 104
/api/v2/monitoring | 104
/medic/_design/medic-client/_view/doc_by_type | 103
/api/v1/users-info | 91
/api/info | 84

title: Set default CouchDb log level to `info` or `debug`
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently, our default log level for CouchDb set in our docker-compose files is `error`. 
When debugging issues in production, especially related to performance, or load, having more logs is instrumental in understanding server activity. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Make default log level more inclusive, to get more information. If this becomes too noisy for some, they can opt off. 

**Additional context**
In recent outage log analysis, we ended up requiring CouchDB access logs to work out the duration of certain requests.

title: Usage Analytics to understand how health workers are using the CHT
body:
Initial goal is to understand how users (CHWs and Supervisors in particular) are interacting with the app today so that we can establish a baseline understanding of how certain actions are being completed. The goal of this initiative is not about identifying performance issues, errors, etc… like our [telemetry data provides](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/performance/telemetry/#performance-data). We want to understand how users are navigating while they are using the app, if/when they are using certain features.

_Here's the initial [Brainstorm doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xlV2b-y3_9WLxkhiys5ItWq7AkHB4Y2R2WfPrLGRDso/edit#), [Related Forum Post](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/what-would-you-like-to-know-about-how-health-workers-use-the-cht/2775), and a review of [platforms](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1EUvVCAGowNwmjGSc--J6jb1nPuo026QtV_PLjbzefpM/edit#gid=0)._

### Types of insights to uncover

1. What path did they take (ie what screens did they visit) to get to a specific screen/action?
2. How long did it take from start to finish?
3. How much time elapsed between each action?
4. What actions did they take on each screen (scrolling, tapping, etc…)?

### Types of questions we seek to answer

1. Are tasks being completed from the contacts tab or the tasks tab?
2. When completing a task from the tasks tab, where was the task in the list? Are CHWs coming here to find out what they should be doing or simply coming here to complete something they knew they had to do?
3. What are they doing after they complete a task?
4. How many key actions are happening within a single session?
5. Which actions are being “abandoned” often (ie opening a screen but not completing any actions)?
6. Are users accessing the targets tab throughout the month or only during meetings/at the end of the month? 
7. Do users take a direct route to specific pages or is there a lot of back and forth? How long do they spend looking for information on the screen? What are their scroll activities?
8. Do paths differ based on the type of form or task?
9. What % of time is spent on each tab?
10. Where and how often are [rage clicks](https://www.fullstory.com/blog/rage-clicks/) happening?
11. How many times per day/week/month are users even opening the app?
12. Which validation errors are they seeing most often and when?
13. How often CHWs edit reports/contacts and which are the most edited fields.
14. Etc...


### Other considerations

1. Segmentation of users
2. Who will be using this data
3. How will it be accessed
4. Turning recording on/off
5. Relationship between telemetry and usage analytics?
6. When will this data sync
7. How "heavy" will the data be
8. Environments configuration/customization

### Initial Approach

1. Prepare a Proof of Concept (PoC)
2. The PoC...
3. ...is meant to help us learn more about what UA will look like for the CHT and how useful it will be
4. ...should be quick and dirty / not take much time to develop or integrate
5. ...will not be concerned with performance, data usage, etc...
6. The PoC will be developed on a branch and installed on a server that others can access
7. We'll organize a day where we get a bunch of teammates together to use the app while we are recording UA
8. We'll review the data to assess it's ability to answer the questions we have
9. We'll agree on a path forward

### Assumptions / Decisions

1.

title: local-ip.medicmobile.org doesn't resolve on Google's DNS (8.8.8.8)
body:
**Describe the issue**
When using the [local-ip.medicmobile.org](https://local-ip.medicmobile.org/) service with nginx-local-ip or CHT Docker Helper, the `1-2-3-4.local-ip.medicmobile.org` URLs fails to resolve to embedded IP (eg `1.2.3.4`) when using [Google DNS](https://developers.google.com/speed/public-dns/)  (`8.8.8.8`)

```shell
// fails on Google's DNS:
ubuntu@local-ip:~$ dig  192-168-8-8.local-ip.medicmobile.org +short @8.8.8.8

// works on Quad9, Cloudflare, OpenDNS, Cleanbrowsing and Comodo
ubuntu@local-ip:~$ dig  192-168-8-8.local-ip.medicmobile.org +short @9.9.9.9
192.168.8.8
ubuntu@local-ip:~$ dig  192-168-8-8.local-ip.medicmobile.org +short @1.1.1.1
192.168.8.8
ubuntu@local-ip:~$ dig  192-168-8-8.local-ip.medicmobile.org +short @208.67.222.222
192.168.8.8
ubuntu@local-ip:~$ dig  192-168-8-8.local-ip.medicmobile.org +short @185.228.168.9
192.168.8.8
ubuntu@local-ip:~$ dig  192-168-8-8.local-ip.medicmobile.org +short @8.26.56.26
192.168.8.8
```

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Ensure that all the major DNS providers, specifically Google, work with the Medic hosted service.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Don't fix it

**Related Info**
While this could/should be filed in [medic-infrastructure repo](https://github.com/medic/medic-infrastructure/), that repo is private, so deferring to this public repo

title: Refactor downwards continuous replication following the Nairobi protocol
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
The continuous replication algorithm currently uses a mix between a custom filtered replication (via two view requests + one changes request) and standard CouchDb endpoints. 

This means that: 
- we can't use multiple replicas, because we can't reliably use sticky sessions for the view requests + the changes request
- we require 2 potentially very expensive queries (one view request + changes request with many doc ids)
- the need for tombstones

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
The Nairobi protocol replaces downwards continuous replication, and instead uses an API endpoint that was added as part of the [initial replication improvement](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8134).  

Rough steps:
- Client uploads all their locally changed docs; this will still use the existing PouchDb replication. 
- Client makes a request for all doc ids and revs they should have
- Client compares with ids and revs in the pouchdb
 - Download and store all docs that don't exist in pouch or have been updated
- For docs that exist in pouch but not couch, query the server to find out if they have been deleted or purged, and if so remove from pouch

The advantages are:
- potentially no longer requires tombstones to exist
- allows for shard replicas because no more changes feed requests
- lots of complex code removed

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
[Alternatives have been described here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Jz6QDYDJiICz5lLEeFB3odh-YoI_0c_AKHJvoVE-Exo/edit#).

title: Release 4.2.1
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create an GH Milestone and add this issue to it.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.
- [x] Ensure that all issues are labelled correctly, particularly ensure that "Regressions" are labelled with "Affects: <version>" labels. The "Affects" label is used in a link in the Known Issues section of the release notes of that version so it has to match exactly. To make sure the label is correct go to the [release notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) and ensure the issue is listed.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR to the release branch. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version patch`.
- [x] Ensure that issues from merged commits are closed and mapped to a milestone.
- [x] Write an update in the #product-team Slack channel summarising development and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The Release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have been merged into `master` then the release process can start:

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`).
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the team by writing a message in the #product-team Slack channel:
```
@product_team, I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag. 
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make. 
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
    - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
    - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, that they're correctly labelled (in particular: they have the right Type, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate), and have human readable descriptions.
    - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes) to export the issues into our release note format.
    - [x] Manually document any known migration steps and known issues.
    - [x] Add a link to the new release page in the [Release Notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) section.
    - [x] Assign the PR to:
        - The Director of Technology or a developer
        - An SRE to review and confirm the documentation on upgrade instructions and breaking changes is sufficient
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Ensure the release notes PR above is merged. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds_4/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*Announcing the release of {{version}}*

title: "Sync Now" reports success even if the replication fails due to timeout
body:
**Describe the bug**
When user clicks "Sync Now," a request is sent to API which times out if it takes >10 minutes. If this request fails due to timeout, no files are moved and the replication is not successful. Despite the timeout, the user sees a success message: "All reports synced".

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Login as a heavy user on a congested server. Alternatively, prepare a custom build of cht-core which reduces the timeout from 10minutes to something short (eg. <1 second).
2. Fill some forms on the device which should replicate up. Create some forms on the server which should replicate down.
3. Click "sync now".  
4. The _changes request needs to take longer than the timeout value to reproduce this issue. You can test if the timeout happened because the files you created will not have synced.
5. Observe the sync status in the hamburger menu - you will see "All reports synced" in green.

**Expected behavior**
Users should be see a failure message for syncronizations which timeout.
It is good these timeouts are not retrying on failure - we likely shouldn't change that

**Logs**
`/medic/_changes` requests which fail in this manner return a mostly empty result with `200` status code

**Environment**
- Instance: dev
- Browser: Chrome
- App: webapp
- Version: main (4.3)

**Additional context**
Based on recent analysis, ~10% of requests to `/medic/_changes` timeout in production for Muso-Mali over a period of 23 days.

title: Add support for Signature Widget in forms
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
As noted on [this forum thread](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/signature-drawing-widget/2176/3) there is a need to collect signatures within Enketo forms.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
An [Enketo Widget](https://docs.getodk.org/form-question-types/#signature-widget) already exists for doing this, but is not one of our [currently enabled widgets](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/js/enketo/widgets.js). During the uplift to Enketo 5.x, I did briefly test that widget, but it was ultimately not included. At the time we did not have any usecases where it was needed and so there was not much to justify the increase to the bundle size for the webapp (the drawing libs associated with the widget are not small),

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could roll our own drawing widget. This might result in a more lightweight solution, but would be extra code to maintain.  

Another alternative would be to see if the use-cases for the signature widget could be covered by just using the [trigger widget](https://docs.getodk.org/form-question-types/#trigger-acknowledge-widget) (I know a lot of "official" online forms that let me "sign" just by checking a box...).

title: Export messages does not export incoming messages
body:
**Describe the bug**
Our [message export](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/api/#get-apiv2exportmessages) is advertised as being able to export _all_ messages in the system, both incoming and outgoing. However this is untrue for incoming messages, because of how the mapping view works, where it only indexes docs that have [outgoing messages associated with them](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/ddocs/medic-db/medic/views/messages_by_state/map.js#L29-L30C36). 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Disable all transitions. 
2. Simulate receiving an SMS - easily done through the admin app: SMS -> Test message
3. Check the messages tab to see that your message was successfully registered.
4. Export messages from the admin app. 
5. Notice that your SMS is not exported. 

**Expected behavior**
The admin app advertises: `Download all messages that have ever been sent or received in CSV format.`

**Environment**
- Instance: any
- App: api
- Version: any

**Additional context**
Originally reported through the [forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/received-and-forwarded-messages/2824/2)

title: feat(#8296): the Nairobi replication protocol
body:
<!--

|
+ -------------- > type: chore, feat, fix, perf.

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

Refactors continuous downwards replication to: 
- not use PouchDb replication
- use same design as initial replication, downloading a list of all doc ids, and comparing them with existent data set
- if a doc is updated or new, it gets downloaded
- if a doc is missing, we check whether it should be deleted. This leverages a new endpoint that, provided a list of docs ids, returns a list of ids that are deleted or purged. The client deletes the documents that this endpoint returns.
- purging for the client is no longer necessary, deleting purged docs occurs when calling the endpoint above, this PR removes all purging endpoints
- tombstones are no longer necessary, Sentinel no longer generates tombstones. Existent tombstones will not be removed. 
- when contacts are deleted, their associated reports are orphaned
- restricted _changes requests and _all_docs requests always return "default" changes and docs (ddoc, settings, user-settings and serviceworker) to allow for restricted users to receive upgrades after this change

title: Automated penetration testing
body:
**Describe the issue**
Currently we aren't made aware of any regressions in our security.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Have an automated script to run a penetration test suite. This could be with the Rapid7 account that's already set up (credentials in 1pass), or some other test suite, or multiple solutions. Depending on the suite this may be run every commit as part of CI, or more likely periodically (monthly, or on beta) because it may be a long running task and potentially expensive. Make sure the results are recorded somewhere.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Manual security testing, but much of the work is repetitive.

title: Split up the ci-webdriver-default action
body:
**Describe the issue**
Now that we've converted e2e tests from protractor to wdio the run takes about 50 minutes to complete. This is too long.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Break up the suite into smaller test suites that can run in parallel. These suites should be broken up into functional groups, eg: all the enketo tests, all the contacts tests, all the admin tests, etc.

It doesn't matter terribly much how many suites we end up with but there will be a sweet (no pun intended) spot - if broken down too far then the build will take a long time to complete because there's a limit on how many runners we can have in parallel and there is a one-off cost for starting the suite. Use your judgement about where this limit should be but somewhere between 4-10 suites should work.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Reducing test coverage (obviously bad).
Finding other ways to speed tests up (bigger effort).

title: Verify PWA installation option
body:
**Describe the issue**
The CHT webapp is a valid PWA, and as an installation pattern PWA has many advantages over apk.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Do sufficient testing to ensure that PWA meets the requirements as a recommended installation method.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Stick with apks.
- Find other workarounds like fdroid
- Find a suitable MDM
