title: Low performance in Reports tab for users with thousands of places
body:
<!--
**Important**: This is a public repository. Anyone in the world can see what's posted here. If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the bug**
Report tab is slow on instances with thousands of places, some numbers:
```
training-2: 72k takes 20s
training: 1.9M takes 2min
```

**To Reproduce**
1. Log in as admin (desktop, browser)
2. Load the reports tab
3. Load the people tab
4. Load the reports tab
On the second load, the reports tab is very slow, maxes out a CPU, and eventually logs in the browser console `Uncaught RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. 

**Expected behavior**
Should not be slow.

**Environment**
- Instance: chis training instances
- Browser: Firefox & Chrome
- Client platform: MacOS
- App: webapp
- Version: verified in 4.2.0 and 4.4.0, possible also in 3.17

**Additional context**
Angular seems to have infinite recursion from internal calls from `refreshView(tView, lView, templateFn, context)` to refreshEmbeddedViews(lView) and back again.

title: feat(api, sentinal): adds servername and proxy origin switch for sni …
body:
# Description

Have designed a unified wrapper for `request-promise-native` to centralise global options and to add a `servername` by default. It's overridable in the case that you ever want to have a different `servername` or an empty one.

When proxying to HTTPS from HTTP (for example where an ingress does TLS termination), not including a 'servername' for a request to the HTTPS server (eg, def.org) the request produces the following error (where `abc.com` is the calling server):

 ```
'ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID'
"RequestError: Error [ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID]: Hostname/IP does not match certificate's altnames:
 Host: abc.com. is not in the cert's altnames: DNS:def.org"
```

The addition of `servername` as an option passed to the HTTP agent resolves this error. 

See docs for `tls.connect(options[, callback])` (https://nodejs.org/api/tls.html): "Server name for the SNI (Server Name Indication) TLS extension.  It is the  name of the host being connected to, and must be a host name, and not an IP address.".

Have written unit tests and have run other tests with the changes included. Relying on your CI for E2E and other tests.

**Note:** Have not changed the use of `request-promise-native` outside of calls to Couch.

title: When using Git BASH, Docker Helper doesn't add TLS certs for local-ip.medicmobile.org
body:
**Describe the issue**
If you're using [Git BASH](https://gitforwindows.org/) on windows and are using the [CHT Docker Helper 4](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/4.x/app-developer/#cht-docker-helper-for-4x), while the CHT instance will start, the instance will still have the self signed TLS cert, so you'll see errors in the browser:

![image](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/8253488/bd0cdddd-c545-40f5-8876-b8822dd50a23)

![image](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/8253488/f1402219-a578-48e2-9f3b-1da41a1fa4d0)

Additionally, there's some error output in the script itself:

```
Container test_vs_code_container-dir-cht-upgrade-service-1 Running
Starting project “test_vs_code_container”. First run takes a while. Will try for up to five minutes…
the input device is not a TTY. If you are using mintty, try prefixing the command with ‘winpty’
the input device is not a TTY. If you are using mintty, try prefixing the command with ‘winpty’
the input device is not a TTY. If you are using mintty, try prefixing the command with ‘winpty’
```

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
When using git BASH on windows the wildcard `*.local-ip.medicmobile.org`  cert should correctly install

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

You can manually install the cert by:

1. finding the name of the `nginx` container with: `docker ps|grep nginx`
2. entering the container with this (being sure to replace `CONTAINER_NAME` with the value form above): `winpty docker exec -it   CONTAINER_NAME bash`
3. and then running these 3 commands:
   ```
   curl -s -o /etc/nginx/private/cert.pem https://local-ip.medicmobile.org/fullchain
   curl -s -o /etc/nginx/private/key.pem https://local-ip.medicmobile.org/key
   nginx -s reload
   ```

2023/09/23 00:03:13 [warn] 47#47: the "listen ... http2" directive is deprecated, use the "http2" directive instead in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf:38
nginx: [warn] the "listen ... http2" directive is deprecated, use the "http2" directive instead in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf:38
2023/09/23 00:03:13 [notice] 47#47: signal process started

Per the note, we should use the non-deprecated config syntax to listen for `http2` requests.

This is just a warning (not an error or fatal), but was introduced in #8451

title: Asterisk for required field in form located on new line when in `summary` group
body:
**Describe the bug**
Originally reported [on the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/alignment-of-labels-with-asterisks-in-app-forms/3057/1).  If you have a `required` field in your form, you will see an asterisk (`*`) at the end of the label to indicate the question is required.  However, if that field happens to be in a group with the `summary` appearance, then the asterisk will be shown on a new line below the label (instead of just being appended to the same line as the label).  

**Expected behavior**
![image](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/8441903/20867cc2-ffa2-4c7f-b2b6-e94adcd70bb8)


**Actual behavior**
![image](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/8441903/b000b735-822a-482a-94e7-cb3b4e5cc428)

**Additional Information**
I have confirmed this behavior from `master` back to `3.17.1`, but I image it goes back much further than that.

title: Add SNI details for use in e2e HTTPS environment with TLS termination external to server (eg, kubernetes pod)
body:
When proxying to HTTPS from HTTP (for example where an ingress does TLS termination), not including a 'servername' for a request to the HTTPS server (eg, def.org) the request produces the following error (where abc.com is the calling server):

```
'ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID'
"RequestError: Error [ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID]: Hostname/IP does not match certificate's altnames:
Host: abc.com. is not in the cert's altnames: DNS:def.org"
The addition of servername as an option passed to the HTTP agent resolves this error.
```

See docs for tls.connect(options[, callback]) (https://nodejs.org/api/tls.html): "Server name for the SNI (Server Name Indication) TLS extension. It is the name of the host being connected to, and must be a host name, and not an IP address.".

This pull request represents the current state of the work: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/8579

As of writing, I need to figure out why the e2e tests are failing.

**Note**: Have not changed the use of request-promise-native outside of calls to Couch.

For us this resolves the breakdown between node and haproxy. The Azure equivalent of ELB which medic uses is not an option for termination for a few reasons:
- We're going to be offboarding our data through a Databricks instance so HTTPS to the haproxy instance is critical.
- Deploying into a much larger network with a lot of access via VPN, so HTTPS as much as possible is useful as defense in depth strategy -- I'm more worried about attacks from inside the network than at my ingress.
- Deploying sentinel, the api, an nginx (+modsec) proxy and a config container for cht-conf (using [container jobs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/jobs?tabs=azure-cli) for being able to run the conf in network on changes) into an [Azure Container App](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/overview) (managed kubernetes) environment. It has a lot of really nice benefits, but it does (as is a good idea, tbh) wrap each container in an HTTPS ingress termination. So while the haproxy instance isn't running in this env, eventually if we want to add sidecars this will be an issue.

title: Release 3.17.2
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create an GH Milestone and add this issue to it.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.
- [x] Ensure that all issues are labelled correctly, particularly ensure that "Regressions" are labelled with "Affects: <version>" labels. The "Affects" label is used in a link in the Known Issues section of the release notes of that version so it has to match exactly. To make sure the label is correct go to the [release notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) and ensure the issue is listed.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR to the release branch. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version patch`.
- [x] Ensure that issues from merged commits are closed and mapped to a milestone.
- [x] Write an update in the #product-team Slack channel summarising development and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The Release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have been merged into `master` then the release process can start:

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`).
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the team by writing a message in the #product-team Slack channel:
```
@product_team, I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag.
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make.
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
    - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
    - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labelled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
    - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our release note format.
    - [x] Manually document any known migration steps and known issues.
    - [x] Add a link to the new release page in the [Release Notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) section.
    - [x] Assign the PR to:
        - The Director of Technology or a developer
        - An SRE to review and confirm the documentation on upgrade instructions and breaking changes is sufficient
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, and change the Target dropdown to the release branch (eg: `4.4.x`). This will create the git tag automatically. Ensure the release notes PR above is merged. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*Announcing the release of {{version}}*

This release fixes {{number of bugs}}. Read the [release notes]({{url}}) for full details.
```
- [x] Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label.
- [ ] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Docker helper 4.x fails to install TLS certs on first run
body:
**Describe the issue**
When you are starting a CHT Core instance using Docker Helper 4.x  and don't have any containers created, images downloaded, or storage volumes created - the `*.local-ip.medicmobile.org` TLS certificate fails to install.  Restarting it via docker helper fixes it. Here's a video showing deleting all docker assets with:

```
docker kill $(docker ps -q); docker rm 4_4_test_api_1 4_4_test_couchdb_1 4_4_test-dir-cht-upgrade-service-1 4_4_test_haproxy_1 4_4_test 4_4_test_haproxy_1 4_4_test_healthcheck_1 4_4_test_nginx_1 4_4_test_sentinel_1;docker image rm -f public.ecr.aws/medic/cht-nginx:4.4.0 public.ecr.aws/medic/cht-haproxy-healthcheck:4.4.0 public.ecr.aws/medic/cht-haproxy:4.4.0 public.ecr.aws/medic/cht-couchdb:4.4.0 public.ecr.aws/medic/cht-sentinel:4.4.0 public.ecr.aws/medic/cht-api:4.4.0;docker volume rm -f 4_4_test_cht-ssl;docker volume rm -f 4_4_test_cht-credentials;
```

and starting a new instance.  The certs fail to install and then a restart fixes it:

[video](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/94494491/965c4372-2b5d-4768-8676-f0ca4ab35b96)

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
TLS cert should be installed on first run

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
restart per above or  to do a one off cert update:

1. First, find the name of the `nginx` container with: `docker ps --filter "name=nginx" --format '{{ .Names }}'`
2. After cloning the [CHT Core repo](https://github.com/medic/cht-core), cd into the scripts directory: `cd ./cht-core/scripts`
3. now using the container name from the first command, call the script to update the cert: `./add-local-ip-certs-to-docker-4.x.sh CONTAINER_NAME`

These three steps look like this:

```
$ docker ps --filter "name=nginx"  --format '{{ .Names }}'
4_3_0_is_here_yay_nginx_1

$ cd Documents/MedicMobile/cht-core/scripts/   

scripts $ ./add-local-ip-certs-to-docker-4.x.sh 4_3_0_is_here_yay_nginx_1
4_3_0_is_here_yay_nginx_1

If just container name is shown above, a fresh local-ip.medicmobile.org certificate was downloaded fresh local-ip.medicmobile.org.
```

title: fix(#7670): do not cache generated patient ids
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

feat(#1234): add hat wobble
^--^(#^--^): ^------------^
|     |      |
|     |      + - > subject
|     |
|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: chore, feat, fix, perf.

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

This is the minimal fix... I resisted refactoring more to keep the backport easy and safe.

The DB call is quick against a warm view, so I think this is safe to do. If we find it's a limitation we can cache it in a way that's safe in a distributed environment.

An alternative approach would be to keep the ID cache but still check against the DB every time, which would save regenerating IDs every call, but that's the fast bit so I didn't think that optimisation was necessary.

Because we're going to request to the DB every request instead of every 100 requests the chance of finding 0 unused IDs has increased. This means the length of the ID would be increased more frequently which is bad for the user. To compensate I raised the generation size to 200. It's theoretically possible the length will get bumped on the nth request (where n is the size of the set) if it happens to generate random IDs that are already in use. I would prefer this was changed to be deterministic, and the length was bumped only when the total used IDs reached some percentage of available IDs, but I've left this as an exercise for the future.

medic/cht-core#7670

title: Contact summary page doesn't support svg icons
body: **Describe the bug** CHT suggests use of [SVG over png](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/design/icons/) icons, however it appears that not all pages of CHT support svg images. Certain section on contact page (contact-summary.templated.js) doesn't suport SVG icons, but supports png images. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Define the icon to be used on your contact-summary-templated.js and set it to `icon-delivery`. 2. On resource.json, set `icon-delivery` [png icon](https://github.com/medic/icon-library/blob/master/forms_tasks_targets/PNGs/icon-delivery%402x.png) from CHT library icons. This is just a link, ensure you've this file inside resources folder. 3. Compile and upload CHT, upload resources and go to contct page for a patient. Observe the icon before Expected Delivery Date. 4. On step 2, point `icon-delivery` to svg icon from CHT icon library and compile again. 5. Go to contact page, you won't see the icon now. See the icon missing before Expected Delivery Date. **Expected behavior** All section of contact page should support svg icons too. **Environment** - Instance: Any - Browser: Chrome - Client platform: MacOS - App: webapp - Version: 4.4

title: Selecting a contact with many children is very slow
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
In this [forum post](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/cht-app-slowing-down/3041/10), performance experiments took ~57seconds to load a place's contact summary but then took another ~55seconds to render the contact list.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Consider pagination of the contacts list in the selected contacts tab

**To Reproduce**
Steps to record the performance metrics:
1. Create a place with 5500 contacts under it
1. Load the contact

**Measurements**
Contacts load at 0:07s
Contact summary loads at 0:57s
When I scroll down, I just see white. The list of contacts actually renders at 1:51s

Hamburger is very slow to open
Tab takes ~4 seconds to unload

**Environment**
- Instance: https://itechcares-malawi.dev.medicmobile.org/
- Browser: Chome117
- Client platform: Ubuntu
- App: webapp
- Version: 4.4.1 prerelease

title: CVE-2023-44487: Research and fix if needed CHT Core use of nginx
body:
**Describe the issue**
[CVE-2023-44487](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-44487) is a [Denial of Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denial-of-service_attack) attack on `nginx` using the HTTP/2 protocol. [As of CHT 4.4.0](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8451), we now support HTTP/2 by default in `nginx`. All earlier version before 4.4.0 are not vulnerable to this attack. 

While it's still unknown if CHT Core is affected, it's important to know  **there is no risk of PII/PHI being leaked**. The worst case is that the attack knocks the deployment offline because of TCP resource depletion.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We should research if we're vulnerable and make updates accordingly if we are.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
While CHT Core's use of `nginx` may not be vulnerable, immediate remediation can be made. The impact of these remediations on CHT Core performance is not yet known. Excerpt below taken from "[Steps for Mitigating Attack Exposure](https://www.nginx.com/blog/http-2-rapid-reset-attack-impacting-f5-nginx-products/)":

>  It is [nginx's] recommendation that the following updates are made to NGINX configuration files, minimizing the server’s attack surface:
> * [keepalive_requests](http://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_core_module.html#keepalive_requests) should be kept at the default setting of 1000 requests
> * [http2_max_concurrent_streams](http://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_v2_module.html#http2_max_concurrent_streams) should be kept at the default setting of 128 streams
> * [limit_conn](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_limit_conn_module.html) enforces a limit on the number of connections allowed from a single client. This directive should be added with a reasonable setting balancing application performance and security.
> * [limit_req](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_limit_req_module.html) enforces a limit on the number of requests that will be processed within a given amount of time from a single client. This directive should be added with a reasonable setting balancing application performance and security.

title: Allow schedule to start with multiple fields
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We need to create one schedule based on multiple forms and SMS. And sadly, not all forms and reports create a field at the same level or name. [`start_from` in schedules.json](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/app-settings/schedules/) currently accepts only one field. Problem ius explained here in the [forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/adding-form-field-outside-of-fields-section/2998). This means we need to repeat the same schedule for different forms for which a field name is different. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Allow `start_from` to accept multiple date fields and create schedule best on first non-undefined value.

title: Rework how we flag time-travelling users
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
We have a service that polls a specific server API, grabs the Date header and compares it to the local time. If there's a large enough difference, we add a telemetry entry. 
This has one bug: the service runs on startup, which means that if the device has no connection when the app is started, no telemetry will be logged. In addition, the service makes an additional request, despite all requests having the Date response header present and available for comparison. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
- add a hook to existing network requests to the server and compare the Date header every time
- reconsider how we log this in telemetry, from having a metrics entry to having a metadata field
- store the delta in local storage and save a best-effort server-time equivalent `reported_date` for every created doc.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Leave it as it is. 

**Additional context**
@garethbowen and I randomly stumbled on a telemetry entry dated 2009, and upon investigation discovered that the existent time-travelling feature didn't work as expected - the telemetry documents lacked the metric for time differences because of the above mentioned issues. 

A similar feature was discussed here: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6284

title: Release 4.4.1-FR-ENKETO
body:
When development is ready to begin on a [Feature Release](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/feature_releases/#release-names), an engineer on the appropriate Care Team or Allies should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are followed, though not necessarily doing the work themselves.

# Planning

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release.
- [ ] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.
- [ ] Have an actual named deployment and specific end user that will be testing this Feature Release. They need to test in production, on the latest version. No speculative Feature Releases.
- [ ] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development

- [ ] Create a new release branch in `cht-core` from the most recent release and call it  `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-FR-<FEATURE-NAME>`. If latest is `3.15.0` and the feature is to "allow movies to be uploaded", call it `3.15.0-FR-movie-upload`. Done before the release so all PRs can be set to merge to this branch, and not to `master`.
- [ ] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <feature-release>`.
- [ ] Ensure QA is briefed and is partnering with the Trio to ensure early and often checks of the feature are on track to be of production quality from the start.

# Releasing

This is an iterative process and it's assumed there will be multiple numbered releases throughout development of the Feature Release.

- [ ] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-FR-<FEATURE-NAME>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag. If an updated Feature Release is needed, increment the last `1` by calling it `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-FR-<FEATURE-NAME>-beta.2` etc.

# Close-out

- [ ] Validate with the actual end user that this Feature Release delivers a quantifiable improvement. If yes, plan on adding the feature to the next minor release by creating a new ticket to merge the code to `master`. If no, we leave the code dead in this branch, never to be merged to `master`, but still loved all the same.
- [ ] Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label. 
- [ ] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Form questions not rendered with values loaded by db-object-widget
body:
**Describe the bug**
When using the db-object-widget to [load contact data](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/forms/form-inputs/#loading-additional-contact-data) into a form, data from the contact is populated into the fields in the form that are in the same group as the `select-contact` field.  However, if one of those fields is a question that should be visible to the user (and not just a `hidden`/`calculate`) that question will be shown to the user, but the value loaded by the db-object-widget will not be displayed.  The question will show up as blank/unanswered, but there is actually a value in the data-model and when the form is submitted, a value will be saved for the question.

**To Reproduce**

Load a form with the following fields (make sure to set the `_id` value to be a contact accessible to the user):
type | name | label::en | calculation | appearance
-- | -- | -- | -- | --
begin group | prev_respondent |   |   |  
string | _id | HHM ID | “35c5877c-2dbe-44c9-ad51-bf6d74ae504d” | select-contact type-person
string | name | Name |   |  
end group | prev_respondent |   |   |  
string | adjacent_name | Adjacent Name | ../prev_respondent/name |  

When you open the form you will see that the `Name` question is not pre-populated with the name of the contact, but the `Adjacent Name` question is pre-populated with the name of the loaded contact.  

**Expected behavior**
It appears that the question fields that are _directly populated by the db-object-widget_ do not get re-rendered in the form when the contact data is loaded.  

It is possible to work-around this issue by just using separate fields for loading the contact data vs accepting input from the user.  However, the current behavior is confusing and unintuitive. 

**Environment**

I believe this issue was caused by the Enketo uplift in `4.0.0`.  I cannot recreate the issue in `3.9.0` - `3.17.0`, but it does appear in `3.17.0-FR-enketo-upgrade-beta.1` as well as `master` (`4.4.1`+).

**Additional context**
Originally reported [on the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/unable-to-load-additional-contact-data-in-app-form/3111).

title: db-object-widget not re-triggered when field becomes relevant
body:
**Describe the bug**
A `select-contact` field can be pre-populated by setting its `calculation` value to the Id of a contact to load.  However, when the field is non-relevant, no data is loaded for the contact.  Then, if the field does become relevant later, the db-object-widget code does not get triggered and so no data gets loaded. 

**To Reproduce**
Use a `select-contact` field in a group to load data for a pre-populated contact id.  If the group is relevant when the form loads, then the data for the contact is loaded as expected.  However, if the group is non-relevant when the form loads and then later becomes relevant, no data will be loaded for the contact (and the contact's name will not be shown in the question widget).  

**Expected behavior**
When a  `select-contact` field becomes relevant, it should evaluate the db-object-widget logic when there is a pre-populated id value.  

**Environment**
Happening on `master` (`4.4.1`+) and on `3.9.0`.

**Additional context**

Note that a non-relevant `select-contact` field that becomes relevant behaves just fine when the value is _selected by the user_. It is just the case where the value is pre-populated that results in the logic not getting triggered.

This issue seems related to https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8225, but is not exactly the same since it is not specific to `inputs`.

Originally reported [on the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/a-select-contact-question-displays-blank-when-the-containing-group-is-conditionally-shown-in-an-app-form/3112).

# Description

This PR enables partners who are running out of support CHT 3.x versions to upgrade their node versions in the container.  Node binary is written to `/srv` when upgraded, so persist across reboots.  The script existed before to help with #7957, but a partner wanted to ugprade to latest node `8.x`, so this PR expands the script to support both Node 12 and node 8, with backwards comparability to default to `12`

## To test
* deploy CHT3.x [locally](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/3.x/app-developer/)
* List running containers with `docker ps` - look for the `medic-os` one you just started. 
* Assuming it's called `cht3x-docker-medic-os-1`, you can get shell by calling `docker exec -it  cht3x-docker-medic-os-1 /bin/bash`
* download the script from this branch: `curl -o /srv/upgrade.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/medic/cht-core/node-8-upgrade-script/scripts/cht-3x-node-upgrade/upgrade.sh`
* make it executable: `cd /srv/;chmod +x upgrade.sh`
* On line `27` change `BRANCH` to be the branch `node-8-upgrade-script` as it's not yet merged to `master` yet
* run the script 3 times:
   1. once with no input (`./upgrade.sh`) ensuring it upgrades to Node 12 - backwards compatible
   2. once with `12` input (`./upgrade.sh 12`) ensuring it still upgrades to Node 12
   3. Once with `8` input (`./upgrade.sh 8`)  to ensure it upgrades to 8
* After each upgrade ensure web UI works and all services are nominal

title: Link to Contact's Profile from Messages tab
body:
_This originally came from the [forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/having-a-link-to-the-client-profile-page-on-the-message-tab/3088)._

When viewing messages on the Messages tab, users will often want to navigate to the message recipient's profile on the Contacts tab. They should be able to do this just by tapping on the message recipient. Currently, users would have to tap on the parent place (in the breadcrumbs) and then scan the list of contacts for that place. If the message recipient has many "peers" (ie contacts at the same level), this becomes very inconvenient and there is no ability to search.  

We should hyperlink from the message recipient to the specific contact's profile on the Contacts tab, just like we do on the Reports tab.

title: Changing a role from being "online" to "offline" does not also change behavior of existing users having this role
body:
**Describe the bug**
Users can have a specific role flag `mm-online`, which determines whether they are online or offline users. This role is added or removed when the user is created or edited, depending on the list of roles that is provided for them. 
If a user is assigned to an role that is `online`, they will also be assigned this `mm-online` role. 
If the user's primary role is later changed, from being online to offline, any user that has this role will still be treated as `online`, because of the `mm-online` flag. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a new online role. 
2. Create a user with this online role. 
3. Edit the role and make it offline. 
4. Log in with the user and observe they are treated as an online user: they have access to all documents and do not have the app available when they are offline. 

**Expected behavior**
It should be clear that simply editing the role is not sufficient to changing the behavior of users that are assigned to this role. 
An alternative would be to edit the users every time a role is changed. 

**Environment**
- Instance: self hosted partner
- Version: all

**Additional context**
This came in through the forum: https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/scope-report-viewing-to-specific-top-level-place/3092/9

title: Enketo labels are not interactable
body:
**Describe the bug**
Due to labels now having `display: contents`, they are no longer interactable. This means they are visually rendered correctly, but they cannot receive clicks or other actions from the user. 
Latest version of WebdriverIO [requires elements to be interactable](https://webdriver.io/docs/api/element/getText/) in order to get or receive values from. This behavior can be also viewed in Chrome dev tools when hovering over elements. 

**To Reproduce**

**Expected behavior**
The user should be able to interact with elements that are visible on the page. 

**Logs**
Sample of wdio logs when trying to get text from labels: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/runs/6649138918/job/18067409025#step:16:626

**Describe the bug**
I used the [places api](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/api/#post-apiv1places) to create a place and contact as shown in the docs. 

```json
{
  "name": "County",

    "name": "Paul",
    "phone": "+254883720611",

}

That worked but i cannot create a user for the created contact

![Screenshot from 2023-11-01 04-41-02](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/10602047/3ad8959e-4c73-49b9-804d-b1d735532c53)

}

The pattern used in the API explains the behavior but it'd be cool if we could assign the place as the person's parent and also include the person id in the response

title: Release 4.4.1-FR-ENKETO-NO-CALCULATE
body:
When development is ready to begin on a [Feature Release](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/feature_releases/#release-names), an engineer on the appropriate Care Team or Allies should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are followed, though not necessarily doing the work themselves.

NB - this release should hard code the removal of [forced calculations](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/ce80d1234561807474c8853d9f2a1aa783c96202/webapp/src/ts/services/enketo.service.ts#L753)

# Planning

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release.
- [ ] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.
- [ ] Have an actual named deployment and specific end user that will be testing this Feature Release. They need to test in production, on the latest version. No speculative Feature Releases.
- [ ] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development

- [ ] Create a new release branch in `cht-core` from the most recent release and call it  `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-FR-<FEATURE-NAME>`. If latest is `3.15.0` and the feature is to "allow movies to be uploaded", call it `3.15.0-FR-movie-upload`. Done before the release so all PRs can be set to merge to this branch, and not to `master`.
- [ ] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <feature-release>`.
- [ ] Ensure QA is briefed and is partnering with the Trio to ensure early and often checks of the feature are on track to be of production quality from the start.

# Releasing

This is an iterative process and it's assumed there will be multiple numbered releases throughout development of the Feature Release.

- [ ] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-FR-<FEATURE-NAME>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag. If an updated Feature Release is needed, increment the last `1` by calling it `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-FR-<FEATURE-NAME>-beta.2` etc.

# Close-out

- [ ] Validate with the actual end user that this Feature Release delivers a quantifiable improvement. If yes, plan on adding the feature to the next minor release by creating a new ticket to merge the code to `master`. If no, we leave the code dead in this branch, never to be merged to `master`, but still loved all the same.
- [ ] Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label. 
- [ ] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Release 4.5.0
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [x] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`.
- [x] Ensure that issues from merged commits are closed and mapped to a milestone.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have been merged into `master` then the release process can start:

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development Slack channel using this template:
```
@core_devs I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`).
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the team by writing a message in the #product-team Slack channel:
```
@product_team, I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag. 
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make. 
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [ ] The beta tag will automatically trigger the scalability build. Once it passes, download the scalability results on S3 at medic-e2e/scalability/$TAG_NAME. Add the release `.json` file to `cht-core/tests/scalability/previous_results`. More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labelled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [x] Collect known migration steps, descriptions, screenshots, videos, data, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. This information should already be on the issue, but if not, prompt the change author to provide it.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions) and update the EOL date of the previous release. Update the status of any releases that are past their End Of Life date. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page.
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, and change the Target dropdown to the release branch (eg: `4.4.x`). This will create the git tag automatically. Ensure the release notes PR above is merged. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Upgrade the [demo](https://demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org/) instance to this version.
- [x] Use cht-conf to upload the configuration from the `/config/demo` folder to the `demo-cht.dev` server.
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*We're excited to announce the release of {{version}} of {{product}}*

New features include {{key_features}}. We've also implemented loads of other improvements and fixed a heap of bugs.

Read the [release notes]({{url}}) for full details.

Following our support policy, versions {{versions}} are no longer supported. Projects running these versions should start planning to upgrade in the near future. For more details read our [software support documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions).

Check out our [roadmap](https://github.com/orgs/medic/projects/112) to see what we're working on next.
```
- [x] Add one last update to the #product-team Slack channel and use the thread to lead an internal release retrospective covering what went well and areas to improve for next time.
- [x] Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label.  
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Support making countdown-widgets `required` in forms
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, when including the [`countdown-widget`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/js/enketo/widgets/countdown-widget.js) in a form, there is no way to ensure that the widget was actually _used_ when filling out the form.  Users can simply skip the widget and continue to fill out the form without waiting for the timer to run.  

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It seems like the cleanest way to proceed would be to have the `required` value be respected for fields with the `countdown-timer` appearance.  This way, a form designer could control whether or not the user has to use the timer by setting the `required` expression (and, by default, the behavior would remain the same as now where a user is not required to wait on the timer).  

**Additional context**
This is a feature request from a partner.

Implementing this could be tricky since currently the `countdown-widget` operates as a `note` field in the form.  The `note` fields actually cannot be `required` in recent versions of Enekto (since objectively it does not really make sense to require a note).  So, we may need to support using the `countdown-timer` appearance on a different type of question besides `note`.  Options off the to of my head are: `boolean` field that is set to `true` when the timer completes, or `integer` field that contains the number of seconds remaining on the timer.

body:
<!--

# Description
Nb. This will be delivered in 4 different PRs:
- Search by barcode (this PR)
- Enketo widget to read barcode 
- Autoselect if search by barcode returns 1 result
- Automation test coverage

This work uses the native [Barcode Detector API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Barcode_Detection_API) from the browser by using a hidden input type `file` to natively open the camera in Android devices. This avoids custom code in the CHT Android and allows more accessibility since the feature can be used in CHT Android, PWA, and Android browsers. 

[See Figma design](https://www.figma.com/file/klZKCYWVkXxu8ZzrIwGXXz/Barcode?type=design&node-id=0-1&mode=design&t=fWzRYLKl7juYloh4-0)

**It works the following way:** 
- The user clicks on the barcode scanner icon
- Prompt is displayed by the OS to take a picture or pic from the gallery 
- User takes a picture
- CHT loads the image and then uses the Barcode Detector API to read the barcode. 
- CHT enters that code into the search input field and triggers the search. 

**More considerations:**
- It works in Android Chrome, PWA, and CHT Android app. 
- This feature is enabled by using `can_use_barcode_scanner` permission 
- This feature isn't supported on desktops and in browsers older than Chrome/Wedview v90.
- When clicking on the barcode icon to scan, the OS will open an option to take a picture or pick from the gallery. This is fully managed by the OS, and we can't limit these options (like preventing from selecting from the gallery) 
- The user needs to grant permission to use the camera, sometimes it's already granted, but they can remove it. We can't force it, and we can't know if they have removed the camera access since we are using the native browser APIs. 
- Some browsers might not support all the [barcode types](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Barcode_Detection_API#supported_barcode_formats).  Supported barcodes are printed in the console from the browser's developer tools.
- The DB Admin user doesn't have access to this feature. Otherwise, they will always have access to this.

**Telemetry:**
- `search_by_barcode:open` -> When a user clicks on the barcode scanner icon
- `search_by_barcode:not_supported` -> When the feature isn't supported because the device is a desktop or the Barcode Detector API isn't available in the browser. 
- `search_by_barcode:scan` -> When the user has taken the picture.
- `search_by_barcode:trigger_search` ->  When Barcode Detector gets the code from the image and triggers the search.
-  `search_by_barcode:barcode_no_detected ` -> When Barcode Detector couldn't detect the code from the image.
- `search_by_barcode:failure ` -> Any system failure when the Barcode Detector tries to get the code from the image.

**Snackbar messages:**
-  On error when the feature is enabled and the picture is loaded but cannot read the barcode: `Failed to read the barcode. Retry`

**Videos**
- Happy path: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/66472237/17bfa6a9-f1ae-4632-b213-83d80a329899
- Errors: When a picture is bad quality (distorted) and it can’t detect the barcode: see snackbar message: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/66472237/8354f530-b82f-4bff-9f53-4ac276dc8d27
- Error: Barcode Detector API no supported / Desktop machine (see snack bar and absence of icon to scan): https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/66472237/e9c3f442-7070-4c4f-ae6a-2e94afd25bfc

**Describe the bug** When calling `/api/v1/users` or `/api/v2/users` it does not respond. **To Reproduce** 1. make a call to download users: `curl https://USER:PASS@DOMAIN/api/v2/users > ~/Documents/users.json` **Expected behavior** API call completes **Logs** ``` curl https://medic:PASSWORD-HERE@CHT_URL_HERE/api/v2/users > ~/Documents/users.json % Total % Received % Xferd Average Speed Time Time Time Current Dload Upload Total Spent Left Speed 100 160 0 160 0 0 0 0 --:--:-- 1:00:01 --:--:-- 40 cat ~/Documents/users.json 504 Gateway Time-out

504 Gateway Time-out

nginx
``` **Screenshots** NA **Environment** - Instance: National deployment - Browser: NA - Client platform: NA - App: NA - Version: 4.3.1 **Additional context** In testing, this API seems to work fine with 100s of users. The instanced that we found the problem with has over ~8400 documents in the `_users` database and 4,624,973 documents in the the `medic` database. A work around was used instead: 1. get sets 100 users (`limit=100`) and start at the 1st (`skip=0`) and then start at the 100th (`skip=100`) . You would do this in a loop until you got all users : `/_users/_all_docs?limit=100&skip=100 ` 2. Then to get the contact their linked to, query the `/medic/org.couchdb.user:USERNAME` endpoint

title: Re-add support for running e2e tests via Chromium (instead of Chrome)
body:
**Describe the issue**
Previously, the e2e tests would run on Linux if only the `chromium` binary was available. [Recent updates](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/commit/cf5b72532cb9df1d7bd059b8e470450f57b5cc86) to the `wdio` dependency have made it so that you get the following error if you do not have a `google-chome` binary available.


> Error: Error: Command failed: which google-chrome

There is a currently open wdio ticket (https://github.com/webdriverio/webdriverio/issues/11250) related to this and perhaps this will be resolved in a future version of wdio.

Additionally, wdio has recently added support for specifying `chromuim` as the actual target for the tests (instead of chrome). https://github.com/webdriverio/webdriverio/issues/11472  Perhaps there is some config we could leverage that would allow running against either one....

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Ideally, we could get back to the original functionality where the e2e tests will run on either chrome or chromium.


**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could just commit to supporting one or the other (and document this requirement).  In that case, developers would need to install the required browser to run the tests.

For the record, if you have `chromium` installed, one workaround to get the current tests to run is to symlink your `chromium` binary to a new `google-chrome` binary:

```sh
ln /usr/bin/chromium /usr/bin/google-chrome
```

title: Speed up build execution by breaking up longest running jobs
body:
**Describe the issue**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. -->
A successful CI build takes 40-50 minutes which is too long.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to change. -->
Identify the longest running jobs and split them up to see if with parallelisation this improves the overall build time.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->
- Reduce the number of tests but this would cause a reduction in coverage (unless we're doing something silly)
- Investigate making tests faster but this is likely a high effort low reward task
- Pay for more runners but this costs money

title: Make update compose URLs action more reliable
body:
**Describe the issue**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. -->
The compose URLs in the PR templates have 3 stages...
1. A place holder value before the `Update compose URLs` has run.
2. A link to a URL after the `Update compose URLs` that 404s until the publish is complete.
3. The link that actually works.

The first two are not useful states.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to change. -->
Instead of having a separate action for the URLs this would be better as a job that runs after publishing has succeeded, that way step 2 never happens.

I think it would also be better to add a comment to the PR rather than find and replace content in the PR description. This is less fragile because it doesn't rely on finding a specific string, removes the step 1 above, and by using [standard GH commands](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/58066966/commenting-a-pull-request-in-a-github-action) also allows for removing a lot of code.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->
Alternatively we could remove it altogether. With docker helper does anyone use docker compose files manually any more?

title: Remove separate action for "Test nginx and haproxy"
body:
**Describe the issue**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. -->
We have a "Test nginx and haproxy" action which runs unit tests on our nginx and haproxy code, but it's not required so doesn't block merging, and is not part of the main "Build and test" action so it doesn't block the rest of the testing from running.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to change. -->
Make the unit tests run with the rest of the unit tests in the "Compile the app" job in the "Build and test" action. This will make them required and skip the rest of the build if they fail.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->
- We could just mark the "Test nginx and haproxy" action as required, but that doesn't stop the e2e tests from running which is very expensive.
- One downside of this approach is it'll slow down the "Build and test" action by maybe 1 minute. Another option is to make the action a new step that runs in parallel with "Compile the app" which is a little wasteful in terms of firing up two GH runners and checking out the code twice, but would be faster. If we go down this route there are other parts that could be split out from "Compile the app" which would save even more time.

title: Release 4.4.1-FR-barcode
body:
When development is ready to begin on a [Feature Release](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/feature_releases/#release-names), an engineer on the appropriate Care Team or Allies should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are followed, though not necessarily doing the work themselves.

# Planning

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.
- [x] Have an actual named deployment and specific end user that will be testing this Feature Release. They need to test in production, on the latest version. No speculative Feature Releases.
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development

- [x] Create a new release branch in `cht-core` from the most recent release and call it  `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-FR-<FEATURE-NAME>`. If latest is `3.15.0` and the feature is to "allow movies to be uploaded", call it `3.15.0-FR-movie-upload`. Done before the release so all PRs can be set to merge to this branch, and not to `master`.
- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <feature-release>`.
- [x] Ensure QA is briefed and is partnering with the Trio to ensure early and often checks of the feature are on track to be of production quality from the start.

# Releasing

This is an iterative process and it's assumed there will be multiple numbered releases throughout development of the Feature Release.

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-FR-<FEATURE-NAME>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag. If an updated Feature Release is needed, increment the last `1` by calling it `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-FR-<FEATURE-NAME>-beta.2` etc.

# Close-out

- [ ] Validate with the actual end user that this Feature Release delivers a quantifiable improvement. If yes, plan on adding the feature to the next minor release by creating a new ticket to merge the code to `master`. If no, we leave the code dead in this branch, never to be merged to `master`, but still loved all the same.
- [ ] Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label. 
- [ ] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Check if a phone number is mobile or fixed line
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Allow an option to validate if given phone is Fixed line or Mobile number. Most of the time, when phone is registered on CHT, they're used for reporting or sending SMS. CHT currently allows user to input valid phone numbers

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
If we're allowing to input fixed line numbers, to which messages can not be delivered, gateway phone tries and will fail. This impacts CHT performance, caused gateway to send messages to phones where message can not be sent or delivered at all. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Allow a validation to be passed when `tel` input is used. Or, introduce a new type `mobile` which accepts only mobile phone numbers. 

**Additional context**
medic/config-moh-nepal#1067

title: Capture contact creator by default
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. I'm always frustrated when [...] -->

It'd be good to have CHT automatically record the uuid of the user who created a particular contact type. Given some of the CHT deployments focus most of the early time in creating and registering households and household persons and do not start reporting, we can not currently account this as CHT caring action since there's no default way of knowing which user created users. Now, we are including contact creation as caring action and CHT users creating contact as Active CHW, we need to support this by default on CHT. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**

In a contact document, capture the uuid of the user who created. Any additional information is helpful but not necessary. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
CHT currently supports [manually capturing this information](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/forms/form-inputs/#example-of-saving-user-data-as-metadata-on-a-report) if users configured it on the contact form. However, not all deployments configure it and this information is missing.

**Additional context**
[Slack thread](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C05C9UTT7CN/p1699296710125359) (private).

title: Use AuthSession cookie for querying instead of basic auth in healthcheck
body:
**Describe the issue**
We're discussing increasing [pbkdf2 iterations](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8338) for CouchDb. 
This will mean that computing the hashed password every time basic auth is used will become a costly server-side operation.  
`haproxy-healthcheck` polls `_membership` with basic auth every 5 seconds. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Instead of using basic auth for every request, make one initial _session request, and use the provided AuthSession cookie to authenticate all following requests within one conf run. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None.

title: 7462 forms module uplifted enketo
body:
# Description

Includes patches for the date picker and date-time picker Enketo widgets to avoid auto-popping open the pickers when they are the first question on a page.  See https://github.com/enketo/enketo-core/issues/1002

Also sets `'excludeNonRelevant': true` in the Enekto config (see https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7674).  This change required an update to our patch for the enekto-core `relevant.js` file to keep our custom functionality with the `inputs` group working.  Basically, for CHT forms we want all the fields in the `inputs` group to be accessible to expressions _even if the `inputs` group is non-relevant_.  To make this work with `excludeNonRelevant` we just need to make sure we are not clearing the value from the `inputs` group fields if they are non-relevent.

title: Support `computeAsync` Enketo functionality
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Enketo has [recently added](https://github.com/enketo/enketo-core/pull/881) support for running the expression computations in a form asynchronously such that the form rendering would not block waiting for all the expressions to finish being computed (more details in the linked PR).  The perceived advantage here is that large forms with many expressions to evaluate should not lag as bad when the user interacts with them.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
See [this slack thread](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C02FMC810UE/p1700090394934849) for more contact, but there is some concern of unintentionally breaking things or running into indeterminate form outputs due to this behavior.

It is worth considering if we should include some way for a partner to easily _disable_ the config on their instance if they run into an unforeseen issue.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could just not use this flag (or wait for it to no longer be experimental!).  It sounds like the ODK team is interested in this becoming the standard Enketo behavior, though, so it probably makes sense to try and get out ahead of this!

title: error.loading.form.no_authorized when opening a form from tasks tab because context evaluates to false
body:
**Describe the bug**
There is a form with `context: "false"` in form.properties.json because this form should never appear on the contacts tab.  In 3.x I am able to open this form via the tasks tab but in 4.x this throws error `error.loading.form.no_authorized`

**To Reproduce**
1. Create a form with `form.properties.json` with `context: "false"`
2. Create a task to trigger the form
3. Trigger the task and click on it

**Expected behavior**
Form should open

**Observed behavior**
error.loading.form.no_authorized

**Environment**
- Instance: CARES
- App: webapp
- Version: 4.4

body:
Now that we are done with #7599, it seems like a good idea to start preparing for updating to the next Enekto version!  :laughing: 

As @m5r pointed out [on Slack](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C02FMC810UE/p1700518578709929), the enketo-core repo has been moved into the big Enketo monorepo: https://github.com/enketo/enketo/blob/main/packages/enketo-core and version `8.0.0` has been released:

> - Breaking change: in the move to a monorepo, some paths in Sass styles have been updated to reflect the new file structure. The impact should be minimal, but custom themes may need to be updated. Generally, paths which cross package boundaries (i.e. imports from Enketo Express to styles in Enketo Core, or imports of third party styles from NPM packages) should use absolute paths from the monorepo root. You may refer to existing theme styles for examples.
> - Breaking change: Support Node 18 and 20, drop support for older versions


It may make sense to try to address this issue at the same time: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8741

title: Users can't login because data loss during creation via API
body:
<!--
**Important**: This is a public repository. Anyone in the world can see what's posted here. If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the bug**
In the MoH KE deployment, we've seen users that were  created via `/api/v1/users` endpoint via  `cht-conf`.  They're initially created without error, but then are missing in the CouchDB `_users` database:

> At some point, it is claimed that there is a period of downtime after which users are not able to log in.  Upon investigation, app devs find that the `_user` docs are "missing" - people use words like "corrupt", "deleted", etc.  w/e... They are just "missing".
>
> Evidence from CouchDB shows these docs "never existed."  But if these docs are created and then being lost, we have a very serious cht-core bug on our hands or an issue with how eCHIS is hosted, other? 

While the issue may indeed be with "how eCHIS is hosted", I'm filing this bug with an abundance of caution, as they say, to capture details in case we verify it is indeed an issue with CHT Core.

**To Reproduce**
So far this hasn't been reproducible every time, but this is the closest I know of:
1. create a CSV file with users
2. run `cht csv-to-docs` to create the JSON file
3. run `cht upload-docs` to upload the JSON file to the CHT instance

**Expected behavior**
Users get created via `cht-conf` and can login fine.  Their login continues to work over time with out issue.

**Logs**
<!-- If applicable, include the server or browser logs. -->

**Screenshots**
<!-- If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem. -->

**Environment**
- Instance: siaya.echis.go.ke, echis.health.go.ke, migori-echis.health.go.ke
- Browser: NA
- Client platform: Linux
- App: CHT Core
- Version: 4.2.2

**Additional context**


The [users file mentioned in Slack](https://medic.slack.com/archives/CHYAGKHN2/p1702648685287979?thread_ts=1702472824.421589&cid=CHYAGKHN2) was the source CSV file which was converted to JSON with `cht-conf` and then uploaded to `siaya.echis.go.ke` also with `cht-conf`.

Related URLs/incidents:
* https://github.com/moh-kenya/config-echis-2.0/issues/1650
* https://github.com/moh-kenya/config-echis-2.0/issues/1770
* [slack thread after (unrelated) power outage](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C042D6TPC3Y/p1698130551344359)
* [another slack thread](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C042D6TPC3Y/p1702632855926239?thread_ts=1698130551.344359&cid=C042D6TPC3Y)
* [Lwala slack thread](https://medic.slack.com/archives/CHYAGKHN2/p1699355666521429?thread_ts=1698130720.826469&cid=CHYAGKHN2)

@kennsippell  reported this about the `siaya.echis.go.ke` instance:

> I just did a quick scan. There were 819 users with `user-settings` docs and without `_user` docs as-of today when I investigated this Siaya issue. Of these, 376 of them are listed in the `connected-users` log.  There are only 19 deletion entries in the `_users/_changes` feed.  This definitively confirms dataloss within the CouchDB `_users` database.

body:
**Describe the performance issue**
Premises: 
1. Task emissions expire after 7 days, and require to be recalculated. 
2. When contacts are already loaded into rules-engine, only emissions that are associated to "dirty" contacts are recalculated - for performance reasons
3. When a large amount of contacts become dirty (after 7 days since last recalculation), existent view queries which use `keys` become very inefficient due to implementation details in the PouchDb adaper

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Update the queries to not use `keys` param when recalculating emissions for a large number of contacts (200+). It's more performant to 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Drop task recalculation entirely - more complex. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to record the performance metrics:
1. Load an user with a large number of contacts - I used one with 6000 contacts
2. Calculate tasks. Check telemetry entry: `rules-engine:tasks:all-contacts` and record value. 
3. Advance clock by 8 days. Reload task tab. Check telemetry entry: `rules-engine:tasks:all-contacts` and record value. 
4. Repeat step 3, adjusting clock back and forth to get multiple measurements. 

**Measurements**
| contacts | reports | Query style                   | duration | duration | duration | duration | AVG    | IDB Crashes |
|------------| ------ |-------------------------------|----------|----------|----------|----------|--------|-------------|
| 6661       | 10000 | keys (current)                | 293s   | 276s  | 270s   | 293s   | 283s | 3           |
| 6661       | 10000 | all rows (proposed)           | 64s    | 63s    | 66s   | 58s    | 63s  | 0           |
| 6661       | 10000  | start_key + end_key (attempt) | 100s   | 95s    | 92s    | 92s    | 95s  | 0           |

**Environment**
- Instance: local
- Browser: Chrome
- Client platform: Android
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.9+

**Additional context**
Instances that have offline users with a large number of contacts have very poor loading times sometimes.

title: perf(#8771): improve performance of task recalculation for many contacts
body:
<!--

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

PouchDb is notoriously slow to query views with a large number of keys. This is what happened when task recalculation was triggered. For users with large numbers of contacts, these requests became so heavy it took minutes to complete, sometimes crashing PouchDb entirely. 

This adds a short-circuit to the key loaded query, when there are more than  500 keys, and instead gets all rows and filters them. 
The limit of 500 can be changed. In my sample test with ~10000 reports, it took roughly the same time to get all rows vs query with 500 keys. 

Performance difference: 
| contacts | reports | Query style                   | duration | duration | duration | duration | AVG    | IDB Crashes |
|------------| ------ |-------------------------------|----------|----------|----------|----------|--------|-------------|
| 6661       | 10000 | keys (current)                | 293s   | 276s  | 270s   | 293s   | 283s | 3           |
| 6661       | 10000 | all rows (proposed)           | 64s    | 63s    | 66s   | 58s    | 63s  | 0           |
| 6661       | 10000  | start_key + end_key (attempt) | 100s   | 95s    | 92s    | 92s    | 95s  | 0           |

[0-22] PASSED in chrome - file:///tests/e2e/default/targets/target-aggregates.wdio-spec.js

The CSS selector is invalid probably because it has a `!` in it, but I think it's a bad selector anyway. Even if we remove the `!` you're still left with ".cell.what a target label" which is weird at best. The generated label for this target is "what a target!" so I suspect the selector should be more like `.cell label["what a target!"]` or something.

Figure out why the test is failing, and fix the CSS selector to not throw this error.

title: feat(#8462): support exporting users devices details
body:
# Description

#8462

Docs PR: medic/cht-docs#1290

As per https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8462#issuecomment-1878008807, this PR adds a way for admins to export user devices details to CSV. It builds on the data exporter already present in the API that comes with streaming and pagination built in.  
I added the minimum amount of code in the admin app to let admins use it, they will find in the "User devices" tab of the export page.

There was some [discussion](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8462#issuecomment-1876793922) about this in the issue but the new CouchDB view used to get every user's most recently used device's telemetry entry is kind of slow. It's not terrible but it's not ideal either and I don't see a faster way to do it, let me know if you have some ideas!
Side note about couchdb views DX, they [shipped a new JS engine with couch 3.0](https://blog.couchdb.org/2020/02/26/the-road-to-couchdb-3-0-update-to-javascript-engine/) that supports ES6 so I reflected that in our eslint config.

Note: I wanted to implement an e2e test that generates telemetry entries and then export users devices from the admin app but users telemetry data gets saved to their own `medic-${username}-meta` db before getting replicated to the common `medic-users-meta` db, where the exporter gets its data from. This replication process happens once a day at 2am and I couldn't come up with a proper way to make that happen within a testable timeframe.
The closest I got to a "proper solution" is by duplicating some code from [sentinel](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/8462-export-user-devices-details-to-csv/sentinel/src/schedule/replications.js#L123-L142) into our test to force a replication before exporting the csv.
Since this feature is planned to evolve towards a smarter way to tell admins "that user needs to upgrade this thing", we will revisit how/what we test this feature.

To do before merging:
- [] make sonar accept the "5.3% duplication on new code" it caught, it's only admin-related code for the new tab
- [] add a new `can_export_devices_details` permission - still open to suggestions for a different permission name

title: Shared libs unit test failures are a chore to debug
body:
**Describe the issue**
This is due to us implementing shared libs with npm workspaces and workspaces having a known issue of not short circuiting on a script failure: https://github.com/npm/rfcs/issues/575

Right now, if a unit test in a shared lib fails, the dev must scour the whole log to find which test failed, which is cumbersome and very annoying. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Figure out a way to show a generic error when any of the shared libs unit tests fail at the end of the suite.

title: Multiple validation functions in rule doesn't work
body:
**Describe the bug**
If you apply Logical operation to multiple [cht validation functions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/app-settings/#cht-validation-functions) it doesn't work. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Prepare an app settings with forms for validations. 
2. On config, ensure that two validations are combined together, for example we are trying to check whether L or G form has been submitted previously before f1 form is submitted. Add following validation property in `f1` form. 

```js
validations = [
      {
        property: 'parent_id',
        rule: '"exists('L','patient_id') || exists('G','patient_id')',
        message: [
          {
            content: 'Pregnancy not registered already',
            locale: 'en',
          },
        ],
      }
```
3. Compile app setting, upload to instance. 
4. Ensure patient doesn't have `G` or `L` form submitted already.
5. Submit `f1` form. Since `L` or `G` form doesn't exist, it will work properly and report `Pregnancy not registered already`. This is expected. 
6. Now, submit `G` form for this patient. 
7. After submitting G form, submit `f1` form again. 
8. This will again throw error `pregnancy not registered already`.

**Expected behavior**
1. In step 8 above, it should not throw an error since `G` form is already submitted. 

**Environment**
- Instance: Any
- Browser: Any
- Client platform: Any
- App: Sentinel
- Version: 4.5.0, but this likely exists in all previous supported versions. 

**Additional context**
If this issue is fixed, we won't need to work on #8402 .

# Description

<!-- DESCRIPTION -->
Sticking with python to reuse existing code as much as possible

Addressing my main concerns for this app

Supports more than one concurrent connection
originally this app could hang if a connection wasn't closed properly
