title: Only last 50 reports for contact are provided to contact-summary calculation
body:
**Describe the bug**
The `contact-summary` calculation logic is provided with an array of the reports associated with the contact (and any of the contact's `person` children).  Unfortunately, because of the way the code was implemented (at least as far back as `3.9`) the number of reports that would be retrieved for the contact and passed to the `contact-summary` calculation was [capped at 50](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/3e126356afba2c75e68a5c70dab2eb8bf60e65c5/webapp/src/ts/services/search.service.ts#L133).  So, the `contact-summary` for contacts associated with >50 reports, would not have the full context of all that contacts reports.

**To Reproduce**
1. Register a pregnancy for a contact
2. See that a pregnancy card is shown for the patient based on their contact-summary calculation
3. Submit 50 more reports for the contact
4. See that the pregnancy card is no longer shown

**Expected behavior**
The `search.service` gets used in a number of situations where it probably makes sense to have the 50 report limit (e.g. when displaying reports for the contact on the contact's profile page, we probably do not need to show an unlimited number of reports).  However, for the `contact-summary` calculation, for the sake of accuracy, we should be providing all the reports associated with that contact.

Also, the [contact-summary docs](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/contact-page/) should be updated to note which version lifted the 50 report limit.

**Additional context**
https://github.com/medic/config-muso/issues/1050
[Forum thread](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/is-contact-reports-limited-to-a-certain-number-of-documents/3247/3)

## Fixed 6-April-2024 

The fix for this issue was [merged](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/8984). 

- Now the calculation of the contact-summary fetches and uses [500](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/8334a596ff18969204eb86a9e868733c69a9892f/webapp/src/ts/services/contact-view-model-generator.service.ts#L38) reports.
- However, only 50 reports are displayed in the contact detail page (For performance reasons, we don’t want to app freezing as it fetches the max number of reports (500) all at once).

title: Fragile text search can invalidate CouchDb admins on container restart
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Referencing [this code](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/aef8973a0f184f5e511bae7897f6b6a3e83eed2d/couchdb/docker-entrypoint.sh#L83)

```
if [ "$COUCHDB_USER" ] && [ "$COUCHDB_PASSWORD" ] && [ -z "$COUCHDB_SYNC_ADMINS_NODE" ]; then
        # Create admin only if not already present
        if ! grep -Pzoqr "\[admins\]\n$COUCHDB_USER =" $CLUSTER_CREDENTIALS; then
            printf "\n[admins]\n%s = %s\n" "$COUCHDB_USER" "$COUCHDB_PASSWORD" >> $CLUSTER_CREDENTIALS
        fi
    fi
```

This code requires that the env user is the first user entry in the admins section of the config file. 
If the section already exists, but does not match this text search, either because another admin is listed first or there are additional spaces (??), a new admin section will be created at the bottom of the file, invalidating the existing section - apparently CouchDb doesn't merge config, at least not within the same file.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Improve the user detection to handle:
- multiple admins in the section
- the admin not being the first admin

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Leave it as it is, and document that you can't (reliably) create another admin that you use as the default Docker user. 

**Additional context**
This came about while debugging an instance where data corruption (caused by two couchdbs running in parallel over the same data) invalidated existing users. We noticed a new [admins] section being created after we added the new couchdb user and restarting the container.

title: Release 4.6.0
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [x] @jkuester Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x]  @jkuester Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`.
- [x]  @jkuester Ensure that issues from merged commits are closed and mapped to a milestone.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have been merged into `master` then the release process can start:

- [x] @sugat009 Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development Slack channel using this template:
```
@core_devs I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] @sugat009  Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`).
- [x] @sugat009 Once the CI completes successfully notify the team by writing a message in the #product-team Slack channel:
```
@product_team, I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag. 
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make. 
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [ ] @jkuester The beta tag will automatically trigger the scalability build. Once it passes, download the scalability results on S3 at medic-e2e/scalability/$TAG_NAME. Add the release `.json` file to `cht-core/tests/scalability/previous_results`. More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [x] @jkuester Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] @jkuester Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] @jkuester Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labelled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
  - [x] @jkuester Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [x] @jkuester Collect known migration steps, descriptions, screenshots, videos, data, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. This information should already be on the issue, but if not, prompt the change author to provide it.
  - [x] @jkuester Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] @jkuester Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions) and update the EOL date of the previous release. Update the status of any releases that are past their End Of Life date. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page.
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, and change the Target dropdown to the release branch (eg: `4.4.x`). This will create the git tag automatically. Ensure the release notes PR above is merged. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Upgrade the [demo](https://demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org/) instance to this version.
- [x] Use cht-conf to upload the configuration from the `/config/demo` folder to the `demo-cht.dev` server.
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*We're excited to announce the release of {{version}} of {{product}}*

New features include {{key_features}}. We've also implemented loads of other improvements and fixed a heap of bugs.

Read the [release notes]({{url}}) for full details.

Following our support policy, versions {{versions}} are no longer supported. Projects running these versions should start planning to upgrade in the near future. For more details read our [software support documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions).

Check out our [roadmap](https://github.com/orgs/medic/projects/112) to see what we're working on next.
```
- [x] Add one last update to the #product-team Slack channel and use the thread to lead an internal release retrospective covering what went well and areas to improve for next time.
- [x] Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label.  
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Restrict which contacts can be deleted by a user with `can_delete_contact` permission
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Users with the [`can_delete_contact` permission](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/app-settings/user-permissions/#system-defined-permissions) have an entry shown in the "more options" context menu for a contact that allows them to delete that contact.  However, there is no way (as far as I can tell) to limit which contacts can be deleted by the user. (Basically, they can remove any of the contacts they have access to.)

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/3c3accebdfba8db7ad2c5261eeb75da79e7ad56c/webapp/src/ts/modules/contacts/contacts-more-menu.component.ts#L113

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
There needs to be some way to be able to specify which which contacts a user can (or cannot) delete.  Perhaps this is a boolean evaluation (similar to a [form `expression`](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/forms/app/#formsappform_namepropertiesjson)?  At the very least, user's should _never_ be allowed to delete their own contact (since this will render them unable to submit any `app` forms).  

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Currently, I logged this as an Improvement, but since user's can actually break themselves by deleting their own contact, it might make sense to re-label this as a bug....

**Additional context**
Originally reported [on the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/restrict-can-delete-contact-permission-to-specific-hierarchy-for-role/3290) where it was noted:

> Unfortunately, we have encountered a scenario where a CHW accidentally deleted themselves. There is also a real possibility of accidentally deleting other CHWs and impacting their work.

title: feat(#8591): adds option for enabling server name indication
body:
# Description

Have designed a unified wrapper for `request-promise-native` to centralise global options and to add a `servername` by default. It's overridable in the case that you ever want to have a different `servername` or an empty one.

When proxying to HTTPS from HTTP (for example where an ingress does TLS termination), not including a 'servername' for a request to the HTTPS server (eg, def.org) the request produces the following error (where `abc.com` is the calling server):

 ```
'ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID'
"RequestError: Error [ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID]: Hostname/IP does not match certificate's altnames:
 Host: abc.com. is not in the cert's altnames: DNS:def.org"
```

The addition of `servername` as an option passed to the HTTP agent resolves this error. 

See docs for `tls.connect(options[, callback])` (https://nodejs.org/api/tls.html): "Server name for the SNI (Server Name Indication) TLS extension.  It is the  name of the host being connected to, and must be a host name, and not an IP address.".

Have written unit tests and have run other tests with the changes included. Relying on your CI for E2E and other tests.

**Note:** Have not changed the use of `request-promise-native` outside of calls to Couch.

Some prior discussions under this PR (branch name was throwing an error): https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/8579

Closes this issue: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8591

title: Consider re-enabling the Erlang Query Server on Couch to improve performance of server-side views
Consider enabling Couch ast-bypass script to improve performance of custom reduce functions in JS views
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
Couch `3.0.0` [introduced a performance regression](https://docs.couchdb.org/en/stable/config/query-servers.html#query-servers-definition) in the processing of custom JS `reduce` functions in views.  View queries for views that have custom reduce functions take longer than necessary.  Currently this affects the following views (the only ones with custom `reduce`):

- `medic-client/messages_by_contact_date` 
- `medic-client/reports_by_form`
- `users-meta/device_by_user` (being added by https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/8797)

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
[Testing locally](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C02FMC810UE/p1706672125231989) with the `users-meta/device_by_user` view with a data set of `200,000` total documents for `1000` users, I measured a `48%` improvement in the query response time. With the experimental ast-bypass fix, the query returned in `~19sec` (vs a baseline of `~36sec`).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Interestingly, I guess this could be enabled on a case-by-case basis since all you need is to set the envar for your Couch container.  Does not require any code change.  (Though we could make it default by setting the envar in our Dockerfile/docker-compose.)

**To Reproduce**
1. Set the following envar for your CouchDB docker container: `COUCHDB_QUERY_SERVER_JAVASCRIPT="/opt/couchdb/bin/couchjs /opt/couchdb/share/server/main-ast-bypass.js"`
2. Down/up your Couch container
3. See your view query run twice as fast as before...

**Measurements**
The main measurable here is the raw performance of the view query in Couch. Just running a GET request against the view endpoint (e.g. `medic-users-meta/_design/users-meta/_view/device_by_user?group=true`)

**Environment**
- Version: `4.5+`

title: Telemetry date not logged on telemetry documents
body:
**Describe the bug**
It has been observed that for many users, a telemetry document is captured without a proper date.

Look at this example telemetry doc: 
```json
 "metadata": {
    "year": null,
    "month": null,
    "day": null,
    "user": "_sample_",
    "deviceId": "d496ea42-b24f-4864-8f99-0aa7bcda5179",
    "versions": {
      "app": "4.5.0",
      "forms": {
        "contact:clinic:create": "8-cf7d43ccfbaf887faf1b6550ecde6d8f",
```

**To Reproduce**
There's no particular way to reproduce this, but these documents can be seen in many 4.5.0 production instances. I'll share the link to these documents in slack. 

**Expected behavior**
Proper date should be logged for year, month, day field. 

**Environment**
- Instance: achham, bardiya, and other 4.5 instances
- App: Webapp
- Version: 4.5.0

**Additional context**
This might have been caused after [this fix](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7616). Issues related to missing days in telemetry document was fixed in that issue. 

This issue has adverse effect in data reporting since we sync telemetry documents by couch2pg and since couch2pg [view](https://github.com/medic/cht-couch2pg/blob/main/libs/medic-users-meta/migrations/202304140052.do.telemetry_devices.sql) doesn't proper date, the couch2pg fails causing entire data transfer failing for all instances running 4.5.0.

```

```

If the persistent storage permission is not granted, the browser will evict data stored in IndexedDB. We are requesting [this here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/dac993b4529cd70fea76cf9678f0c2e02705e7e5/webapp/src/ts/app.component.ts#L334).

https://web.dev/articles/persistent-storage
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/StorageManager/persist

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Prompt the permission request to the user if it was not granted before. We can do this in the telemetry service.

title: Release 4.5.2
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create an GH Milestone and add this issue to it.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.
- [x] Ensure that all issues are labelled correctly, particularly ensure that "Regressions" are labelled with "Affects: <version>" labels. The "Affects" label is used in a link in the Known Issues section of the release notes of that version so it has to match exactly. To make sure the label is correct go to the [release notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) and ensure the issue is listed.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR to the release branch. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version patch`.
- [x] Ensure that issues from merged commits are closed and mapped to a milestone.
- [x] Write an update in the #product-team Slack channel summarising development and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The Release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have been merged into `master` then the release process can start:

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`).
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the team by writing a message in the #product-team Slack channel:
```
@product_team, I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag.
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make.
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
    - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
    - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labelled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
    - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our release note format.
    - [x] Manually document any known migration steps and known issues.
    - [x] Add a link to the new release page in the [Release Notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) section.
    - [x] Assign the PR to:
        - The Director of Technology or a developer
        - An SRE to review and confirm the documentation on upgrade instructions and breaking changes is sufficient
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, and change the Target dropdown to the release branch (eg: `4.4.x`). This will create the git tag automatically. Ensure the release notes PR above is merged. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*Announcing the release of {{version}}*

This release fixes {{number of bugs}}. Read the [release notes]({{url}}) for full details.
```
- [x] Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label.
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Add MVP OAuth 2.0 Support
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When deployments need to add a feature to the CHT, or want to host a related services like an external dashboard, one of the main challenges is that there is no way to authenticate against CHT itself.  

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be great if the CHT could implement [OAuth 2.0](https://oauth.net/2/) to enable remote systems to use the CHT for credentials. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
As a work around today,  systems can ask the user to enter their CHT Credentials anew on their own site and proxy over their requests as the [User Man. Tool does today](https://github.com/medic/cht-user-management/).

**Additional context**
This should be a minimum viable product (MVP) effort to support a "plugin" of sorts that allows external developers to specifically build the  [User Man. Tool does today](https://github.com/medic/cht-user-management/). This means if there's other parts of the OAuth 2.0 spec that take more time to implement but will not be used right, we shouldn't do that part.

title: Add MVP OIDC Support
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
After we add [OAuth 2.0 support](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8849), we'll need to add [OpenID Connect](https://openid.net) (OIDC) which will enable  authentication on top of the authorization that OAuth offers.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
MVP OIDC On the cheap ;)

**Additional context**
This should be a minimum viable product (MVP) effort to support a "plugin" of sorts that allows external developers to specifically build the  [User Man. Tool does today](https://github.com/medic/cht-user-management/). This means if there's other parts of the OIDC spec that take more time to implement but will not be used right, we shouldn't do that part.

title: "Maintenance Mode" for user accounts
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
_Loss of Health Data_ - Today, there is risk of data loss any time an user manager: 1) moves a user's area to a different spot in the hierarchy, 2) disables a user account, 3) replaces a user with another.  You can see data-loss happening for live projects in issues like https://github.com/medic/config-pih/issues/719 where hundreds of denied replications are happening for this month-long period.

_Burdensome Human Coordination_ - In our [documentation for move-contacts](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/updates/moving-contacts/), we require that "users must be encouraged to clear cache and resync!" to avoid this sort of dataloss. Users need to do this before the move-contacts command is executed and coordinating these sorts of activities with users/devs is very time consuming.  

Also - when you run multiple move-contacts commands, you can take down a server like in https://github.com/medic/config-muso/issues/932 where the server was down for 12 days.  This makes coordination even more difficult. For Uganda eCHIS where the entire nation is on one instance, how do you ensure that everybody who is moving contacts is talking to everybody else? 

These programmatic steps required to do user management safely are becoming increasily difficult with scale. Without the availability of better tooling, project teams do not have time to coordinate these activities and have no option but to accept the risk of data loss.  

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We are creating automation to improve user management scenarios with [cht-user-management](https://github.com/medic/cht-user-management). A noteworthy example on the roadmap, is a UI and cloud-based execution of move-contacts commands which aims to execute move-contact commands safely. https://github.com/medic/cht-user-management/issues/12

This issue tracks a request to create some sort of "maintenance mode" for user-accounts which will allow automation to perform operations on them without dataloss.

Something like: 

1. Automation can set a flag on a user to "put into maintenance mode" 
2. Next time user syncs their data, the user is automatically logged out after the sync complete successfully
4. All data is cleared from the user's device
5. User cannot login, should see an error like "Your account is in maintenance mode"
6. The user's account is flagged so automation knows the user has synced (account maintenance is now safe).  
7. In the example above, this is when move-contacts could be safely executed.
8. Automation removes the flag keeping the account in maintenance mode
9. User can now login.  Maybe with their original credentials, maybe with a resent magic link, etc.

title: Split up webapp JS into multiple smaller bundles
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. It is slow when I [...] -->
When upgrading the service worker refreshes the asset cache, which tells the browser to download all JS. The browser then checks its cache and only downloads resources that have changed. With all the JS bundled into one module, the browser always downloads the entire JS again. This discourages frequent upgrading and can incur a cost on the CHW or program due to downloading a large JS bundle. Furthermore if the download is interrupted it has to redownload the entire JS bundle. Bundling all JS together was best practice 10 years ago before improvements in the http spec (ie: multiplexing in http2).

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->
Use Angular modules to split the one large bundle into a series of small bundles. These bundles should be defined logically with coupled code being together in the same module because this code is likely to be updated in the same release.

There will likely be a tradeoff between having too few modules which cause excessive downloads, and having too many causing many requests and overall complexity.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->
Drastically reducing the size of the JS, but previous audits haven't shown any low hanging fruit here.

**To Reproduce**
<!--
Steps to record the performance metrics:
1. Go to '...'
2. Click on '....'
-->
1. Clear your service worker cache
2. Open the network tab in the dev console
3. Load the login page (no login necessary)
4. Record the number and size of the JS assets downloaded
5. Record the time it takes to download all the assets
6. Upgrade the CHT (In development, just modify one JS file. In a production like environment do the smallest possible upgrade.)
7. Wait for the service worker to realise there's a new version
8. Record the number and size of the JS assets updated

**Measurements**
<!-- Record at least one measurement that you think should be improved. Ex. 5 seconds, 200MB memory usage, etc -->
- Compare the results in step 4 and step 8 to verify that only the module that changed has to be downloaded
- Compare the results in step 5 with `master` to make sure there's no significant change in load time
- Evaluate the bundle sizes in step 4. Ideally there would be 5-10 bundles of approximately equal size, but it's not completely under our control.

title: Make upgrades smooth for users
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. It would be better to [...] -->
When webapp detects a new version is available it downloads the db docs and refreshes the service worker cache and then prompts the user to reload. This happens in the background so the prompt can pop up at inconvenient times like during a household visit halfway through filling in a form. We know there's a long tail of users not upgrading so we added a reminder that prompts every 2 hours. This is annoying for users, and trains them to ignore the upgrade dialog.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->
Instead of prompting the user at an random...
1. Update the UI subtly that an upgrade is available (eg: a notification dot, or a menu item in the hamburger near the sync status). If someone is waiting on an upgrade this lets them know it's ready.
2. The next time the user navigates to a new page (submits a form, selects a new tab, etc), instead of doing the usual single page navigation, do a full page load which brings in the new code. This ensures the reload happens at a convenient time and users aren't distracted. Before doing this ensure that the page reload time is acceptable so the users don't unexpectedly get a long running spinner!

The result should be a better experience for CHWs who won't get interrupted with prompts.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->
Instead of automatically reloading we could just move the prompt to after the page navigation but most people in the world including our users have been trained to dismiss popups like this, so smoothly applying the upgrade without bothering the user is preferable.

**Additional context**
<!-- Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here. -->

body:

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

This PR updates the existing `bulk-password-update-export.js` [script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/bulk-password-update-export.js)  to 
* not allow changing passwords for users `medic` or `admin`.  While `4.6.0`+ [defend against](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8096) this already, earlier 4.x versions do not.
* allows you to specify CSV input of users so they can have their passwords specified instead of randomly added
* adds the same warning to both scripts "ARE YOU SURE YOU WANT TO CONTINUE!" 
* removes `bulk-password-functions.js` 

per #8862

###  `bulk-password-update-export.js` 

Now supports the `--use_passes` flag.  If you pass it `false` it will generate random passwords via `generatePassword()`. If you pass it `true` it will read the CSV.  Passwords that are insifiently complex will get refused with a `400` response and `The password is too easy to guess. Include a range of types of characters to increase the score.` message.

Here's the help text:

```
Change passwords of users in user-password-change.txt, show results on screen 

Usage:
      node bulk-password-update-export.js -h | --help
      node bulk-password-update-export.js --url https://localhost --user medic --password adminPass

Options:
    -h --help     Show this screen.
    --url         The url for the instance being changed
    --user        The admin user this operation is run as
    --password    The password for the admin user 
    --use_passes  The passwords are in user-password-change.txt in or not. 
                  "true" - yes they're there in USER, PASSWORD format
                  "false" - no, no password, just usernames, one per line. Generate a random password for me.
```


###  `bulk-password-functions.js` 

this script has been removed as it's been deemed too dangerous.  At a later date, we can add in an `--all` flag on  `bulk-password-update-export.js`  if needed

title: Block users from editing important fields in user settings docs
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. It would be better to [...] -->
Currently users can edit their own user settings doc in the medic db. This is usually not a big issue because on the server we only trust the data in the _users database, but it would be easy to regress and use the wrong one by mistake, but also it would be useful to allow read only access at times ([recent example](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8877#issuecomment-1948039024)). Also if the medic version gets out of sync with the users version then the application can [behave in unexpected ways](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8337).

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->
Disallow editing of the user settings doc except by API or db admin users.

There are two ways I can think of that this doc may get modified - either directly to couchdb by a malicious user with curl, or unintentionally by a well meaning developer storing the doc in pouchdb and replicating.

The final gatekeeper for the database is `validate_doc_update` which will block both approaches, but I think this will permanently block upwards replication for anyone who has an update (needs testing). If we can couple this with a client side check to stop pouchdb getting in an inconsistent state then it may work.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->
Long term we should block direct access to the db, and use APIs for everything which would allow us to perform custom validations on writes, but this would be a breaking change so doesn't solve the problem in the near term. It also doesn't solve for accidental updates by well intentioned developers.

**Additional context**
<!-- Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here. -->
There may be legitimate reasons for updating this doc (eg: "known" and "privacy policies") either in use, or historically used. The historical part is important because if the server is upgraded and gets the new gate, but there's an old doc sitting on a phone, we need to make sure they can recover.

### Severity

**Low** because the user can only edit the shadow of the permissions. We should only use the permissions in the `_users` db on the server so the medic copy isn't especially important.

title: Provide API access for online users
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. It would be better to [...] -->
For performance online users don't download data to their device. When this was first implemented the simplest approach was to use PouchDB with online users having the http adapter. This means that the webapp can query a single API and PouchDB handles whether the data comes from IndexedDB or CouchDB over http. To enable this proxied all their requests direct to couch which in turn means we've exposed the entire CouchDB API for administrators to use. While this works, it means we're exposing implementation details without any guarantee of backwards compatibility which can get implementers in to trouble.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->
Instead we should block direct access to CouchDB and provide a complete set of APIs to allow implementers access with a guarantee of backwards compatibility. For this issue specifically, target online users of the webapp. This will provide a lot of APIs for common requests.

To achieve this will require significant changes to webapp to remove direct access to PouchDB. Specifically, create a DB service which exposes a strongly typed API that is called everywhere PouchDB is currently called. This API will return specific types (eg: Patient, Report, Form) and abstract away the access method. The implementation of the API on the webapp will either issue queries to PouchDB or issue requests to APIs depending on whether the user is online or offline. The implementation of the API will ultimately make the same requests to CouchDB as the webapp makes to PouchDB so this should be a shared lib.

This architecture gives us a client side API and a server side API that are identical and abstract away the underlying database and schema, making it easier for Core and App developers to work with, as well as allowing for schema changes without disruption, and even replacing Pouch or Couch if necessary in future.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->

title: chore(#8612) Fix docker helper to have valid TLS on 1st run
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

feat(#1234): add hat wobble
^--^(#^--^): ^------------^
|     |      |
|     |      + - > subject
|     |
|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: chore, feat, fix, perf.

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

### This PR

Fixes docker helper 4.x to have valid TLS on 1st run:
* refactors `get_is_container_running()` to be called `nginx_is_running()` (only nginx is ever used with it)
* adds an extra check that `nginx` returns a `301` as opposed to `000` or other failure, ensuring it is up and running

Per #8612


### Background

I narrowed down the bug to these three lines being called before `nginx` container was fully running:

```
docker exec -it $nginxContainerId bash -c "curl -s -o /etc/nginx/private/cert.pem https://local-ip.medicmobile.org/fullchain"  2>/dev/null
docker exec -it $nginxContainerId bash -c "curl -s -o /etc/nginx/private/key.pem https://local-ip.medicmobile.org/key"  2>/dev/null
docker exec -it $nginxContainerId bash -c "nginx -s reload"  2>/dev/null
```

By adding a `sleep 5` above these, I could get it to work giving `nginx` container more time to boot.  However, this was non-deterministic and may still fail.  I settled on explicitly waiting for a `301` redirect from the `/` path on `http` to the `https` port.   


### Testing

Test these steps on `master` to ensure they fail and then test on `8612_no_tls_1st_start_nginx` branch to ensure they succeed.   Before starting, create a new docker helper project called `8612_no_tls_1st_start`. Then:

1. run this one liner to reset the instance: `docker rm -f 8612_no_tls_1st_start_nginx_1; docker volume rm -f8612_no_tls_1st_start_cht-ssl;docker kill $(docker ps -q);./cht-docker-compose.sh 8612_no_tls_1st_start.env`
2. open the URL output in docker helper script  in a new incognito tab = remember offline first - stuff gets cached!  using a **new** incognito tab ensure no cache
3. see if TLS is invalid (self signed cert) or valid (let's encrypt)

Make sure there's no regressions and these work on `8612_no_tls_1st_start_nginx` branch:
* can start existing docker helper project
* can start a new   docker helper project
* can  `stop` a running docker helper project

Run all e2e tests over k8s.

2.12.1 (2024-02-22)

  • Do not parse sourcemaps in post-css. This fixes a vulnerability in which information about the existence or non-existence of files on a server could be disclosed via properly crafted HTML input when the style attribute is allowed by the configuration. Thanks to the Snyk Security team for the disclosure and to Dylan Armstrong for the fix.

2.12.0 (2024-02-21)

  • Introduced the allowedEmptyAttributes option, enabling explicit specification of empty string values for select attributes, with the default attribute set to alt. Thanks to Na for the contribution.

title: Support Android validation URL endpoints for registering an intent
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
In Android 12+ you can't just register a URL as an intent and have it work.  You now need to have the domain you're pointing to [be able to validate](https://doordash.engineering/2022/01/25/your-deep-links-might-be-broken-web-intents-and-android-12/) it is knowingly participating with the app. Otherwise, these URLs won't register in the app without manual intervention.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Allow the CHT Core to have an API endpoint that can be configured with the correct response to validate URLs that are in the corresponding CHT Android app.  Presumably this will be in the app settings file, but TBD.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
You can [manually approve URLs](https://github.com/medic/cht-android/issues/308#issuecomment-1560074617), but this scales poorly with non-technical users and may only work for side-loaded apps.

**Additional context**
With out this feature, all token login [links are broken](https://github.com/medic/cht-android/issues/308).

body:
Bumps the pouchdb group with 4 updates: [pouchdb-adapter-http](https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/tree/HEAD/packages/node_modules/pouchdb-adapter-http), [pouchdb-adapter-memory](https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/tree/HEAD/packages/node_modules/pouchdb-adapter-memory), [pouchdb-core](https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/tree/HEAD/packages/node_modules/pouchdb-core) and [pouchdb-mapreduce](https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/tree/HEAD/packages/node_modules/pouchdb-mapreduce). Updates `pouchdb-adapter-http` from 7.3.1 to 8.0.1
Release notes

Sourced from pouchdb-adapter-http's releases.

8.0.1

The first release of the year! This is a patch release, it fixes a bug we introduced during a refactor made in the last release and sets Node 14 in our CI. For a full changelog from 8.0.0 to 8.0.1, please see the releases page or view the latest commits.

Fix this of changesHandler

#8583 #8581 We introduced a bug in the #8450 refactor that has been fixed now.

Use Node 14

#8570 We were testing our CI in GHA against Node 12, which is EOL. Now we are testing against Node 14.

Changelog

Bugfixes

  • da5069df (pouchdb#8581) - Fix this of changesHandler

Documentation

  • 4dcaac82 docs: release post for 8.0.0
  • 0bdb3423 feat: add mastodon verification link
  • 40ac7a26 feat(site): faster website uploads, rsync skips files that are already on the server
  • ae69d4fb fix(blog): title case
  • 3728f020 Update 2022-12-14-pouchdb-8.0.0.md
  • c90a0208 Update 2022-12-14-pouchdb-8.0.0.md
  • e9bf059c docs: update to version 8.0.0
  • 7484e245 docs: update 2022-12-14-pouchdb-8.0.0.md

Testing

  • 06bfe891 (pouchdb#8581) - Fix test - Reorder for confirming equal(7)
  • 2c81da46 (pouchdb#8581) - Fix test Fix format issues.
  • 3d36d2d8 (pouchdb#8581) - Fix test - Rewrite the function to callback-style. - Fix for timings.
  • 6a7fd466 (pouchdb#8581) - Fix test.
  • ff81fa35 ci: use node 14

Get in touch

As always, we welcome feedback from the community. Please don't hesitate to file issues, open discussions or get in touch. And of course, a big thanks to all of our new and existing contributors!

8.0.0

We are thrilled to announce the release of PouchDB's new major version 8.0.0. For a full changelog from 7.3.1 to 8.0.0, please see the releases page or view the latest commits. Here are the highlights:

Embracing modern ES6+ JS syntax

We have started the process of moving to ES6+ syntax. We made refactors to use native JS classes instead of prototypes, deprecated some packages that implemented features that are now built in the language (inherits, argsarray), and started in packages such as pouchdb-abstract-mapreduce and pouchdb-adapter-http. We encourage you to embrace the syntax in your new contributions and, if you can, contribute to the refactoring effort.

This might mean a potentially breaking change, therefore we bump the major version. If you need to support ES5 we recommend you use a transpiler.

title: fix(#8868): don't forward all headers for get requests
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

feat(#1234): add hat wobble
^--^(#^--^): ^------------^
|     |      |
|     |      + - > subject
|     |
|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: chore, feat, fix, perf.

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

Node 19 adds keep-alive header to requests by default. This makes the `content-length` header very significant **and** important because it enables the server to know when one request has been fully received and another one is sent through the same connection. 
When authenticating a user, we take all headers from the original user's request and pass them to a GET /_session request, presumably so we don't have to filter out all the ways through which the user can authenticate (cookie, authorization etc). This meant that if the original request was a POST, and it had a `content-length` header, this header was also forwarded. This meant that when the connection would later be reused, the server (haproxy in this case) would truncate the previous's request `content-length` number of characters from the next request, believing the previous request was not finished. Obviously, this new truncated request was invalid and generated a 400 status code. 

This only seems to happen when accessing API directly or through the AWS load balancer, and never when running requests through nginx. 

To avoid next request truncation, I am no longer forwarding `content-length` headers in the session request. 

#8868

title: `xml2sms` functionality broken
body:
**Describe the bug**
It seems like the [`xml2sms` functionality](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/forms/app-form-sms/) for sending an SMS when a report is created has been broken for awhile.

**To Reproduce**
Follow the documented steps to configure sending report data via SMS:

- In your `app_settings.json` set a value for the `gateway_number`.
- In  your form properties.json, set `"xml2sms": true`
- Assemble a cht-android apk with the `SEND_SMS` permission
- Use the Android app to submit a report
- See that you are not prompted for SMS permissions
- See `Form2Sms failed` error in the console logs

**Expected behavior**
When everything is properly configured, the user should be prompted to allow SMS permission (so the report can be sent).  But, on newer cht-core versions, this never happens.  Basically, the webapp fails to create an SMS message to send and so it never tries to trigger the permission.  

**Logs**

<details>
<summary>APK Logs</summary>
```
2024-03-13 11:21:46.511 19293-19293 MedicMobile             org.medicmobile.webapp.mobile        D  org.medicmobile.webapp.mobile.EmbeddedBrowserActivity$3 :: onConsoleMessage() :: https://192-168-1-33.local-ip.medicmobile.org:10443/main.js:1 | Form2Sms failed:  [object Object]
2024-03-13 11:21:46.512 19293-19293 MedicMobile             org.medicmobile.webapp.mobile        D  org.medicmobile.webapp.mobile.EmbeddedBrowserActivity$3 :: onConsoleMessage() :: https://192-168-1-33.local-ip.medicmobile.org:10443/main.js:1 | Unhandled Promise rejection: missing ; Zone: <root> ; Task: Promise.then ; Value: [object Object] Error
                                                                                                        at new fe (https://192-168-1-33.local-ip.medicmobile.org:10443/main.js:11:494301)
                                                                                                        at Ti (https://192-168-1-33.local-ip.medicmobile.org:10443/main.js:11:494382)
                                                                                                        at wi.objectStore.get.onsuccess [as __zone_symbol__ON_PROPERTYsuccess] (https://192-168-1-33.local-ip.medicmobile.org:10443/main.js:11:545424)
                                                                                                        at IDBRequest.ke (https://192-168-1-33.local-ip.medicmobile.org:10443/polyfills.js:1:15728)
                                                                                                        at G.invokeTask (https://192-168-1-33.local-ip.medicmobile.org:10443/polyfills.js:1:11385)
                                                                                                        at Q.runTask (https://192-168-1-33.local-ip.medicmobile.org:10443/polyfills.js:1:6758)
                                                                                                        at F.invokeTask [as invoke] (https://192-168-1-33.local-ip.medicmobile.org:10443/polyfills.js:1:12437)
                                                                                                        at q (https://192-168-1-33.local-ip.medicmobile.org:10443/polyfills.js:1:25168)
                                                                                                        at ee (https://192-168-1-33.local-ip.medicmobile.org:10443/polyfills.js:1:25477)
                                                                                                        at IDBRequest.ye (https://192-168-1-33.local-ip.medicmobile.org:10443/polyfills.js:1:25760)
```
</details>

The problem is in the [form2sms.getFormModel function](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/e8d88accb607f5ae5060f9bb4a988d91dc615812/webapp/src/ts/services/form2sms.service.ts#L45).  It tries to get the form model attachment, but it is not passing the correct parameters.  It should look like the [forms service code](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/e8d88accb607f5ae5060f9bb4a988d91dc615812/webapp/src/ts/services/form.service.ts#L97) with will pass the form doc id (e.g. `form:pregnancy`) and `model.xml`.  Instead, the form2sms service code is passing the form name (`pregnancy`) and `model`.  As far as I can tell, there is no way this code will ever succeed.  

I think this issue was introduced  in https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/7596 and shipped on `4.0.0`.

title: fix(#8085): fix spinner race condition in tasks and contacts components
body:

|
+ -------------- > type: chore, feat, fix, perf.

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description
- When visiting the tasks component, `No more tasks` is briefly displayed because of the momentary state where `loading` is false, `hasTasks` is false (because `refreshTasks` hasn't completed yet). The fix is adding a new `tasksReady` flag, which is set to true at the very end of refreshTasks. The new flag synchronizes the visibility of the spinner and the display of tasks with the actual completion of task loading.

- Similar, when visiting contacts component, you see `No more people`. The fix is adding a new `contactsReady` flag  to accurately represent when the contacts are fully loaded and the component is ready to update the view. The flag is initially set to false and only set to true when contacts have been completely loaded.

### Video showing the race condition 
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/2597305/72bbb53d-e1a7-43ae-ac5f-83952cbc7c41

### Video showing the race condition fixed by this PR

title: Select question grid display in forms broken
body:
**Describe the bug**
In Enekto forms, you can create a [grid of select questions](https://docs.getodk.org/form-question-types/#grid-of-selects-on-the-same-screen) that all have the same choices so that the choice labels are only displayed once.  

Unfortunately. the CSS to hide the subsequent choice labels in the matrix seems to have been broken with these changes: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/8672

**To Reproduce**

Create a form with either of the following select matrix patterns (note that Enekto supports both the `table-list` and the `list-nolabel` appearance patterns, but only the `list-nolabel` pattern is included in the ODK docs):

type | name | label::en | appearance
-- | -- | -- | --
begin_group | table_list_test | Table | field-list
select_one yes_no | table_list_test_label | Table | label
select_one yes_no | table_list_1 | Q1 | list-nolabel
select_one yes_no | table_list_2 | Question 2 | list-nolabel
end group |   |   |  
begin group | table_list_test2 | Table (alternative method) | table-list
select_one yes_no | table_list_3 | Q1 |  
select_one yes_no | table_list_4 | Question 2 |  
end_group |   |   |  

Open the form on a CHT instance `>=4.5.0` and see that the labels for the matrix choices are not hidden as expected.

**Screenshots**
This is the expected behavior:
![image](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/8441903/efa68a9f-8ed1-4e66-88fa-c5ce8e083e19)

This is how it looks now:
![image](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/8441903/950b9e2d-8903-43a5-951d-43f05d69a83c)


**Additional context**
Originally reported [on the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/changes-in-table-list/3384)

title: Admin app shows error after successful upgrade
body:
**Describe the bug**

When using the Admin app to upgrade a CHT instance to the latest tagged version (e.g. `4.6.0-beta.3`), the installation will complete successfully, but the UI will still display the installation error card.  

**To Reproduce**

Deploy a CHT instance that can be upgraded via the Admin app (I used EKS)

In the Admin app on the Upgrades tab, select "Install" for the `4.6.0-beta.3` tag.  Wait for the install to complete and see the error message (even though the installation succeeded).  

![image](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/8441903/96547788-fbd9-4881-9546-bfb1989a6a03)

Alternatively, instead of selecting "Install", select "Stage".  Then, once the installation is staged, click "Install" and see the error (note that, for me, the page automatically updates after ~30sec to clear this screen and take me back to the normal Upgrades tab.  I never see the "Deployment Complete" card, but at least the error goes away....):

![image](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/8441903/e4859223-25b7-43c3-82a7-96c28ca6d25c)

**Expected behavior**

Either way, when the installation succeeds, I expect to see "Deployment complete.":

![image](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/8441903/969fa609-454e-4a67-8b19-d1db4883f160)


**Logs**

There are lots of errors in the console log, but I think most of them are normal while polling for the updated api server to come back online.  However, as the error card appears at the end of the upgrade, I do see: `main.js:1 Error triggering update instance.upgrade.error.deploy`

**Additional context**

This behavior only seems to be happening for the `4.6.0` beta tags.   If I start from an older CHT version,  such as `4.3.0`, and then try upgrading to `4.5.2-beta.1`, I do not see any problems.  Then if I upgrade to `4.6.0-beta.3`, I see the error card being displayed.

title: Outbound push cron config error
body:
Job commented on the [forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/configure-cronjob-or-batch-processing-for-cht-outbound/2641/31?u=njuguna) that outbound push tasks are failing with `Unable to push ***** for ped_benchmark_outbound because this outbound config no longer exists, clearing task`.

The steps for reproduction are:

1. Configure outbound as seen below:

![Image](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/141340177/741ac868-edcc-40f7-a2bf-79b875e77e93)

2. Create records and trigger outbound at minute 11 all the way to 20. You will notice that your records will be saved and not pushed, see the above logs. An outbound task will be generated
3. Within the same timeframe you will see a message `Unable to push ***** for ped_benchmark_outbound because this outbound config no longer exists, clearing task`

title: Scalability tests broken

**Describe the issue**
[Noticed this](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C024KTGRW/p1711040146261659) during the `4.6.0` release process.  The scalability test suite appears to be broken and all the tests are failing (even though the CI job succeeds).  

The tests all fail with an error like:
```

(Use `node --trace-warnings ...` to show where the warning was created)

    errors: [],
    status: 'aborting',
    end_time: '2024-03-21T15:42:33.885Z',
    last_seq: 0
  }
}
```

The JSON results from the run look like:

```

```

Note the `"errorPct" : 100.0`.

title: Support getting the difference between two dates in various time formats
body:
Retroactively logging this issue for the functionality already in PR: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/8949

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
See https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5468, but basically doing logic around dates in xforms can be tricky and error prone since it is mostly manual calculations. It would be much nicer to have proper XPath functions that could do the generic heavy lifting around date calculations.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Contained in the PR are 4 new functions that add functionality similar to the existing [`difference-in-months` function](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/forms/app/#difference-in-months).

- `cht:difference-in-days`
- `cht:difference-in-weeks`
- `cht:difference-in-months`
- `cht:difference-in-years`
- ~~`days-remaining-in-week`~~

Most of these are pretty self-explanatory, but @ChinHairSaintClair, I was hoping you could provide some more context here for `days-remaining-in-week`.  Looking at the code, it seems to calculate the value by `totalDiffDays % 7;`.  This seems like a pretty simple calculation that could be done in the form via just getting the modulo of the `difference-in-days` value.  Am I missing something here?  (Have not actually tried calculating modulo in an xform....)  Depending on the circumstances here and how common the use-cases would be for this functionality, we might not need this function.

The rest of these functions seem super valuable and hard to manually code within the form logic (because of all the weird date edge cases).  

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
One alternative would be to try and up-stream these functions into the ODK spec (and then into the Enketo code-base). The functionality here is genericish since it just deals with date values, but maybe is not very useful in typical data-collection contexts...  One point of context is that the `difference-in-months` function was actually [removed from the Enekto code base](https://github.com/enketo/enketo/issues/911). I imagine any functions that are actually accepted into the spec would be welcome in Enekto.  @garethbowen you probably have more context here regarding the history of trying to put this kind of thing into the xform spec.  What do you think?

My current thinking is that regardless we should move forwards with adding these functions to the CHT. It will not be hard to migrate the code to Enketo later if needed.

**Additional context**
Originally discussed in [this forum thread](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/mitigate-duplicate-data-capture/3313/6?u=anro).

title: Form `end` meta field not correctly populated when the form ends
body:
**Describe the bug**
CHT forms support several [meta fields](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/forms/app/#supported-xlsform-meta-fields) including `start` and `end` that are supposed to record the exact time the form began and the form ended.

Unfortunately, the `end` value is always just recorded as (almost) the exact same value as the `start` regardless of how long the user takes to fill out the form.

**To Reproduce**
Create a form that contains:

| type | name |
| --- | --- |
| start | start |
| end | end |

1. Begin the form
2. Wait a bit of time (at least a few seconds)
3. Submit the form
4. See that the different between `start` and `end` do not match the time waiting before submitting the form.

**Expected behavior**
The `end` value should contain the time that the form was submitted.

**Additional context**
Originally reported [on the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/start-end-xlsform-meta-fields-returns-same-value/3416).

It appears this is a regression that happened as a result of the [Enekto Uplift](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6345) in `4.0.0`.  I tested and confirmed everything works as expected in `3.17.2`, but it is broken in `4.0.0`.

Debugging through the Enekto code flow, it appears the `start` and `end` values [are preloaded correctly](https://github.com/enketo/enketo/blob/37a7af1886743c7e20ddcb9f3b0f8708d184cd88/packages/enketo-core/src/js/preload.js#L75), but the `BeforeSave` event is never triggered for the form.

title: Cannot use /api/v1/people to create a person if any place in the lineage has an invalid primary contact
body:
**Describe the bug**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the bug is. -->

**To Reproduce**
1. Create a grandparent place with no primary contact
2. Create a parent place with a primary contact
3. Attempt to use the `POST api/v1/people` API to create a person within the parent place
 
**Expected behavior**
In 4.4, you could create this person. In 4.6, you see the error `Wrong type, this is not a person.` 
There is no UUID of the affending contact or place, no hints for a targeted followup. I thought the problem was in my payload; but it is in the hierarchy. 

**Environment**
- Instance: test
- App: webapp
- Version: 4.6.0

**Additional context**
For our Uganda eCHIS app: regions, districts, subdistricts, counties, subcounties all do not have primary contacts. This currently may block cht-user-management from using cht 4.6 via API. 

I believe this was [changed here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/8682/files#diff-847864fa7d0eecc88050c831b2b0b83933bf7bef90143e48810d7aec0b85a0d9R78)

I'll just note that in the real world it's sometimes quite annoying to need a 100% valid hierarchy in order to complete  task.  When county-level ICT team staff get an error like this and are blocked from creating a user at this place, what are they supposed to do? It's quite burdensome to train every single person creating users in eCHIS to also manage the hierarchy - this app doesn't have forms to create/edit these places or their primary contacts.

title: chore(#8987): validate commit milestones for release
body:
# Description

#8987

Adds validation to the release-notes generation script to validate that all of the commits in the release have an associated milestone.  This is done by checking for a milestone on:
- Any PR associated with the commit
- Any issue closed by a PR associated with the commit
- Any issue/PR whose number is included in the commit message

It is not absolutely air-tight validation, but it is probably more thorough/accurate than any kind of manual validation of the commits (e.g. the release engineer going through each commit to validate it has a milestone). The actual _milestone values_ are not checked. This logic just ensures that each commit is somehow associated with a milestone.

I also added a new `--skip-commit-validation` flag as a backstop so this validation logic will not block the main functionality of the script.  (Maybe there is a commit that we do not care about having in a milestone and it is not worth going back to fix it.)

title: Improve Apdex score in contact details page
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
[Care Teams KR](https://github.com/medic/care-teams/issues/22)
[Initial research done](https://github.com/medic/care-teams/issues/74#issuecomment-2039384512)

I found out that load_reports ([code](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/679b7051aa15488b6c9f3e872145a3b0d433aba8/webapp/src/ts/effects/contacts.effects.ts#L150)) is requesting the reports' docs twice, the tech explanation is:

- We use the search feature to return the reports (and docs) from the selected contact and its descendants ([code](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/679b7051aa15488b6c9f3e872145a3b0d433aba8/webapp/src/ts/services/contact-view-model-generator.service.ts#L312))
- The search feature uses the data record service ([code](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/679b7051aa15488b6c9f3e872145a3b0d433aba8/webapp/src/ts/services/search.service.ts#L159)) to get the docs. Makes a request to the [user's local db](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/679b7051aa15488b6c9f3e872145a3b0d433aba8/webapp/src/ts/services/get-data-records.service.ts#L38)
- Then we take the ids from the search result and build the data for the report's header ([code](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/679b7051aa15488b6c9f3e872145a3b0d433aba8/webapp/src/ts/services/contact-view-model-generator.service.ts#L334))
- To build that header, we are retrieving the reports' docs again by using the [data record service](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/679b7051aa15488b6c9f3e872145a3b0d433aba8/webapp/src/ts/services/contact-view-model-generator.service.ts#L292C12-L293C22) that also request the [user's local db](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/679b7051aa15488b6c9f3e872145a3b0d433aba8/webapp/src/ts/services/get-summaries.service.ts#L118) (but somewhere else in the code)

Instead of retrieving the same information twice, reports' docs, we can find a way to pass that information to the process that generates the reports' headers and void querying the user's local DB twice. And make sure we are not breaking anything else using the same processes.

title: Possibly improve freetext search by using Mango Index instead of view
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
[This blog post](https://reintech.io/blog/efficient-full-text-search-couchdb-mango-queries) notes that [Mango queries](https://pouchdb.com/guides/mango-queries.html) (aka [`_find` requests](https://docs.couchdb.org/en/stable/api/database/find.html)) can be leveraged with pre-built indexes to provide performant full-text search.  

It might be worth investigating if this is true and if it can provide better performance/functionality than our current "freetext" search approach (which is very brute-force TBH).  

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

Currently doing freetext searches (e.g. searching for a contact by name) requires some [nasty views](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/dac993b4529cd70fea76cf9678f0c2e02705e7e5/ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/contacts_by_freetext/map.js#L7) that do not index words `< 3` characters.  See https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8832 for the UX challenges this poses to users. 

A more functional full-text search would be useful to users and perhaps Mango indexes could get us that without sacrificing much in terms of performance, complexity, or DB index/view size.  The [`_find` docs](https://docs.couchdb.org/en/stable/api/database/find.html#db-index) note: 

> Mango wraps several index types, starting with the Primary Index out-of-the-box. Mango indexes, with index type json, are built using MapReduce Views.

I expect this means that Mango indexes on the Couch server leverage Erlang views, which [could be more performant](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8835).  But we would need to measure the performance impacts for both the server and the offline Pouch implementation (since that will not be built on Erlang).

**Additional context**
@ChinHairSaintClair this might be of interest to you since it touches on things we discussed [in this thread](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/mitigate-duplicate-data-capture/3313)!

title: Report sent and delivered message count separately in api
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Reporting of the message status on api

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
The `messaging/outgoing/total` section in `/api/v2/monitoring` currently combines both `sent` and `delivered` messages as a `delivered` and is reported accordingly. For example: 

```json
  "messaging": {
    "outgoing": {
      "total": {
        "due": 275827,
        "scheduled": 13856,
        "muted": 172372,
        "failed": 9064,
        "delivered": 192303
      },
```

Instead of this, report `sent` and `delivered` separately since they mean different things. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Instead of combining, report sent and delivered separately. This is already available in `medic-admin/message_queue` view. Updating this view would allow us to report sent and delivered separately. The expected output can be something like this:

```json
  "messaging": {
    "outgoing": {
      "total": {
        "due": 275827,
        "scheduled": 13856,
        "muted": 172372,
        "failed": 9064,
        "sent": 100000,
        "delivered": 92303
      },
```

**Additional context**
We saw many messages remained in Sent state forever and saw that FCHVs never got those messages and they kept on sending new message to the system, resulting in duplicate activities. (More on this medic/config-moh-nepal#1212).  If we report `sent` and `delivered` separately, it'll be easy to see this in grafana and be more actionable.

title: Freetext search for a keyword which is also a common field name returns all records

**Describe the bug**

title: Improve Apdex score of contact_list
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
[Care Teams KR](https://github.com/medic/care-teams/issues/22)
[Initial research done](https://github.com/medic/care-teams/issues/91#issuecomment-2049084781)

In the first cycle of performance optimisation I did not find any glaring performance bottlenecks. In this issue I suggest two refactors that might improve performance or at least better maintainability that could lead to potentially improved performance. 

### contactsComponent
1. In [contacts-component.ts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/modules/contacts/contacts.component.ts), the `ngOnInit` method mixes synchronous and asynchronous logic ([code](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/c4c3114ed8e17f49a78e1f803a643792b71f2c8e/webapp/src/ts/modules/contacts/contacts.component.ts#L124)) which can be refactored to use `async - await`
2. The initialization of the contacts Component can also be wrapped in a `try - catch` block to allow for centralized error handling instead of error handling in each promise. 
3. The subscription management ([code](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/c4c3114ed8e17f49a78e1f803a643792b71f2c8e/webapp/src/ts/modules/contacts/contacts.component.ts#L92)) can also be refactored into a separate method. This wont particularly lead to a performance gain but it improves the separation of concerns. 

### searchService
In looking for ways to optimize the `contact_list:query` I reviewed the search library and there could be possible optimization by avoiding redundancy of [responses.map](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/c4c3114ed8e17f49a78e1f803a643792b71f2c8e/shared-libs/search/src/search.js#L46C30-L46C43)

Is it the case the this move is seamless from a migrations perspective? 

Ie, given the data replicated into a new couchdb cluster upgraded in lockstep with the first version of CHT Core to use that version of couchdb, will CHT Core migrate what it needs to?

If so, it would be great to get that explicitly stated in the docs. 

If not, what would one need to be aware of? If there are dragons there it would also be good for them to be noted in a doc.

If I've just missed some documentation, please let me know.

title: Update patient_id for reports after it is generated
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
When CHT is used in offline mode and CHWs perform multiple functionalities in a row. For example, register a patient, register pregnancy for them and send pregnancy visit form. Patient id is populated when a report is synced to server and sentinel picks it and generates patient id. This then updates the patient's document. However, it doesn't check or update any reports that were filled out for this patient before the document got patient id. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
When patient_id is generated, update other reports that were filled for patient. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
For analytics, since we can't rely on patient_id being populated always because of this issue, we've been using patient_uuid and joining it against the person registration to link documents.

title: Reduce loops when processing tasks and reports
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
[Research 1](https://github.com/medic/care-teams/issues/74#issuecomment-2039481418)
[Research 2](https://github.com/medic/care-teams/issues/99#issuecomment-2060711839)

- Add all the tasks' [emissions fields in the rule engine](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/679b7051aa15488b6c9f3e872145a3b0d433aba8/webapp/src/ts/services/rules-engine.service.ts#L293) to avoid going through the list of data twice. [Tasks list adds](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/679b7051aa15488b6c9f3e872145a3b0d433aba8/webapp/src/ts/modules/tasks/tasks.component.ts#L129): date, overdue and owner. While [contact detail adds](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/679b7051aa15488b6c9f3e872145a3b0d433aba8/webapp/src/ts/services/tasks-for-contact.service.ts#L66) overdue, the calculation is the same.

- Pass the selected contact ID and the descendants' IDs to the service that loads the breakdown of tasks to avoid going through the list of data twice.

- There is a micro improvement [to avoid looping twice a list of tasks](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/04491c9f93c4689c4207928a339347e863c1d52f/webapp/src/ts/reducers/contacts.ts#L119), but it is likely not noticeable by the user.

title: Remove server check for node version
body:
**Describe the issue**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. -->
The server checks code checks a few things to make sure the server is correctly set up so it can fail early with a clear error message if it's not. One of the things it checks is the node version, but because we publish docker images with a node dependency it should never be wrong in prod.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to change. -->
Remove the node check. Keep the code that logs the version because that's useful. Consider _adding_ a check for CouchDB version which is more likely to get out of sync because the CouchDB version is defined in a separate docker image.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->
Keep it as a sanity check, and to protect devs who are running outside of docker from silly mistakes.
Due to an oversight on my part it didn't get updated when we bumped to Node 20 so update it and move on.

title: Add pagination when loading All reports associated with a contact in contact detail page
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. It would be better to [...] -->

We recently fixed a [bug](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8815) where only the last 50 reports for contact were provided to contact-summary calculation. The fix to use max fetched reports (500 reports) for contact-summary calculation was [merged](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/8984). 

However, currently loading reports in the contact detail page does not have any pagination or lazy loading implementation. Since there is a possibility that a contact might have 500 reports, the app might freeze as it loads all 500 Reports at once. To mitigate that, we set the max number of reports you can view in the contact detail as 50.

That means when you click the `View all` tab in the Reports section you see only 50 instead of literally `All Reports` associated with that contact.
![Screenshot 2024-04-20 at 14 24 17](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/2597305/e2046e4f-bbe0-4cd4-a78a-180a62586898)


**Describe the improvement you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->
Implement lazy loading / pagination similar to how its implemented in the Reports Tab to load reports in batches but ensure someone can view `All Reports`associated with a user.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Save artifacts with unique names. 
The same applies to allure history.
