title: Release 4.7.2
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create an GH Milestone and add this issue to it.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.
- [x] Ensure that all issues are labelled correctly, particularly ensure that "Regressions" are labelled with "Affects: <version>" labels. The "Affects" label is used in a link in the Known Issues section of the release notes of that version so it has to match exactly. To make sure the label is correct go to the [release notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) and ensure the issue is listed.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR to the release branch. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version patch`.
- [x] Ensure that issues from merged commits are closed and mapped to a milestone.
- [x] Write an update in the #product-team Slack channel summarising development and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The Release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have been merged into `master` then the release process can start:

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`).
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the team by writing a message in the #product-team Slack channel:
```
@product_team, I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag.
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make.
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
    - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
    - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labelled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
    - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our release note format.
    - [x] Manually document any known migration steps and known issues.
    - [x] Add a link to the new release page in the [Release Notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) section.
    - [x] Assign the PR to:
        - The Director of Technology or a developer
        - An SRE to review and confirm the documentation on upgrade instructions and breaking changes is sufficient
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, and change the Target dropdown to the release branch (eg: `4.4.x`). This will create the git tag automatically. Ensure the release notes PR above is merged. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*Announcing the release of {{version}}*

This release fixes {{number of bugs}}. Read the [release notes]({{url}}) for full details.
```
- [x] Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label.
- [ ] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Admin upgrade page incorrectly shows "Error triggering upgrade" even if upgrade was successful
body:
<!--
**Important**: This is a public repository. Anyone in the world can see what's posted here. If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the bug**
This only affects older versions of the CHT installing newer versions, and it's caused by a change in the `api/deploy-info` interface: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8790

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Install 4.2.4
2. Upgrade to 4.6.0. Wait until upgrade is complete. 
3. Notice that the upgrade page says "Error triggering upgrade" but the version displayed is 4.6.0.

**Expected behavior**
The upgrade was successful, so the admin page should not report that upgrade was not. 

**Environment**
- App: admin
- Version: 4.2.x -> 4.5.0

**Additional context**
This only affects upgrades from versions lower than 4.6.0 to versions higher than 4.6.0

title: Upgrade from latest release test fails for patch releases
body:
**Describe the issue**
Because we don't support rollbacks, the admin upgrade page doesn't show releases that are semver older than the currently installed release. The upgrade test will fail because it can't find the button to install the desired patch release: \

In this image, I was running the upgrade test for `4.7.1`, while the latest release is `4.8.0`. 

![image](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/35681649/36c7724f-13f7-432b-bf1b-6b6c2b7d5e8f)

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Either skip the test, to avoid confusion - the test will still run for betas and branches, or make the test smarter to not install latest release, but instead the release previous to the installed tag.

title: API Endpoints for getting contacts by type
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
As noted in https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8889, getting the contacts of a specific type is needed for cht-user-managment.  

**Describe the solution you'd like**

```
HTTP GET api/v1/person

HTTP GET api/v1/place?type=clinic
```

Endpoints should also accept the following query parameters to allow for paging through the data: 
- `limit` - default is `100`
- `skip` - default `0`

When it comes to the cht-datasource api, things will be a bit interesting.  On one hand, _most_ consumers of the lib will not want to manually deal with paging, but instead we should return something like an `async Iterable` so the paging it completely abstracted away.  However, the api code will need to be able to make a targeted request for a specific limit/skip since that is what it will be receiving as a request and for best performance we will need to be able to pass those though directly to the Couch view query... Perhaps we just provide both functions in cht-datasource:

- One that takes `limit/skip` and returns an array of values.
- One that just returns an Iterable - Under the hood, this would probably just use the first function, but wrap it up with a generator function or something.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Other ways to structure the API include:
- `api/v1/clinic`
- `api/v1/place/clinic`

However, these do not seem any more clear than just using a query parameter and are definitely less flexible.

body:

title: Increase ecmaversion linting for ddocs
body:
**Describe the issue**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. -->
CouchDB 3 increased their supported JS engine version which meant more modern features could be used in code such as map/reduce view definitions. However due to the way we warm views before upgrading this caused [a bug](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9166) where releases were blocked because the view warming on CouchDB 2 failed. This only impacts upgrades from a version of CHT with CouchDB 2. The fix for 4.x is to not use modern JS features.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to change. -->
In the next major, we can safely bump [the ecma version](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/8ce2fd08c11bf1e283c2db4af2ecf29a3d1c1896/ddocs/.eslintrc#L10) and list this as a breaking change when upgrading from 4.4. The workaround is to upgrade to the latest 4.x release before upgrading to 5.x.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->
- We could document the broken backwards compatibility but it's hard to make it clear without also bumping the major
- We could disable view warming or skip over if it fails for some reason - this risks taking a production instance out for days

title: API Endpoint for getting generic contact data
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Based on [this discussion](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9065#issuecomment-2186704076) we should add a `api/vi/contact` endpoint (in addition to `person` and `place`) that will return return generic contact data (given the identifier for either a person or a place).  

There are a number of situations in the CHT data model where one might have a contact identifier, but not know what type of contact it is associated with. (E.g. a report can be associated with a contact, but there is no guarantee if the contact is a person or a place). 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The `api/vi/contact` endpoint should support returning the full data for the person/place (implemented via cht-datasource) but under the generic Contact interface.

In cht-datasource we should move the `Contact` interface into a `v1` namespace since it will be exposed as a first-class data type.  We should also look at exporting some type assertion helper functions to confirm if a `Contact` is a `Person` or a `Place`.  

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Just not supporting getting generic contacts and trying to update the various places in the data-model to always know the type.
- Add an endpoint for just getting the _type_ of a contact (so you knew whether to get the entity from the person/place endpoint).

title: API endpoint for getting generic entity data
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Based on [this discussion](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9065#issuecomment-2186704076) we should add a REST endpoint that will return return data from a generic DB document. 

While this may be undesirable from an encapsulation perspective, it will be incredibly useful as a stop-gap solution for a number of workflows.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I am thinking an endpoint like `api/v1/entity` that supports GET with an id. The main open question I have right now is if we need to consider handling different DBs besides just `medic`?  

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
One school of thought is that this would prove to be a loophole that could be used to get document data that we actually do not want to expose via other apis.  The counter to this is that it is unreasonable to expect that we can make it to 100% API coverage via our REST apis (since that will be something of an always moving target anyway). This functionality will allow the eventual locking down of Couch access even without perfect coverage of all use cases.

title: Evaluate performance of PouchDB indexeddb adapter
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. It is slow when I [...] -->
PouchDB 9.0 has [just been released](https://pouchdb.com/2024/05/24/pouchdb-9.0.0.html) with significant improvements to the `indexeddb` adapter which _should_ make it perform better than the `idb` adapter we currently use.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->
Upgrade to Pouch 9.0 and run a suite of client side performance tests with representative data on the old adapter and the new adapter and publish the results. There is currently no migration from one to the other so you will have to completely reset the browser data when you switch adapter.

**Measurements**
<!-- Record at least one measurement that you think should be improved. Ex. 5 seconds, 200MB memory usage, etc -->
- Most important will be client side apdex or similar to measure user satisfaction with the new adapter
- But we should also measure cpu, memory, and disk usage to make sure we don't incur unintended costs

**Additional context**
<!-- Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here. -->
Once we've determined if and how much this improves performance we can decide which of several options to take next (in a separate issue):
1. Do nothing
2. Use the `indexeddb` adapter for new clients, but keep the `idb` adapter around for existing clients. I like this option because it's not a breaking change, and allows for progressive rollout. This could also be used as a workaround for heavy users to do a sync, wipe, initial replication to get the improved performance.
3. Write code to migrate between adapters, and drop support for the `idb` adapter. This is difficult because we have to be careful about not exhausting disk space during the migration, and may take a while to execute which would block CHWs from doing work until it's finished. For this reason it's probably a breaking change and would be delayed until the next major release.

title: Release 4.10.0
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [x] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Checkout to a new `<issue>-update-version` branch (eg: `1234-update-version`) and set the version number in the `package.json` and `package-lock.json`. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`. Once the version is updated, submit a PR to `master` branch.
- [x] Ensure that issues associated with commits merged to `master` since the last release are closed and mapped to the milestone.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once the PR has been merged into `master`, and the `master` branch has the new version number, then the release process can start:

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development Slack channel using this template:
```
@core_devs I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by creating a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`) and then push the created tag.
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the team by writing a message in the #product-team Slack channel:
```
@product_team, I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag. 
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make. 
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [ ] The beta tag will automatically trigger the scalability build. Once it passes, download the scalability results on S3 at medic-e2e/scalability/$TAG_NAME. If you do not have access to the scalability results ask someone in the #product-team who has access. Add the release `.json` file to `cht-core/tests/scalability/previous_results`. More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labelled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [x] Collect known migration steps, descriptions, screenshots, videos, data, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. This information should already be on the issue, but if not, prompt the change author to provide it.
  - [ ] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions) and update the EOL date of the previous release. Update the status of any releases that are past their End Of Life date. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page.
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. In the releases tab, you select the "Choose a tag", type tag in the search box, then create a tag for the release `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. Next, change the Target dropdown to the release branch (eg: `4.4.x`). Ensure the release notes PR above is merged. Add a link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Once you publish the release, confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Upgrade the [demo](https://demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org/) instance to the newly released version.
- [x] Use cht-conf to upload the configuration from the `/config/demo` folder to the `demo-cht.dev` server.
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*We're excited to announce the release of {{version}} of {{product}}*

See below for some highlights, read the [release notes]({{<paste-url>}}) for full details.

Following our support policy, versions {{versions}} are no longer supported. Projects running these versions should start planning to upgrade in the near future. For more details read our [software support documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions).

Check out our [roadmap](https://github.com/orgs/medic/projects/112/views/21) to see what else is currently being working on.

## {{version}} Highlights

### [{{Highlight 1}}]({{<paste-url to section>}})

{{description of highlight section}}

### ### [{{Highlight 2}}]({{<paste-url to section>}})

{{description of highlight section}}

### [And more...]({{paste-url to section}})

We’ve also implemented loads of other improvements and fixed a heap of bugs.

```
- [x] Add one last update to the #product-team Slack channel and use the thread to lead an internal release retrospective covering what went well and areas to improve for next time.
- [x] Go to the [Issues tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues) and filter the issues with `is:issue label:"Affects: 4.x.x" ` , replace `4.x.x` with the previous version number. Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label.  
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: feat(#9227): add validation function for luhn algorithm
body:
# Description

#9227

The Luhn algorithm is classified as:
> designed to protect against accidental errors, not malicious attacks. Most credit cards and many government identification numbers use the algorithm as a simple method of distinguishing valid numbers from mistyped or otherwise incorrect numbers. 

It has several applications, as shown below. Specifically, we use it to validate South African ID numbers.

Other uses:
* Credit card numbers
* IMEI numbers
* National Provider Identifier numbers in the United States
* Canadian social insurance numbers
* Israeli ID numbers
* South African Tax reference numbers
* Swedish national identification numbers
* Swedish Corporate Identity Numbers (OrgNr)
* Greek Social Security Numbers (ΑΜΚΑ)
* ICCID of SIM cards
* European patent application numbers
* Survey codes appearing on McDonald's, Taco Bell, and Tractor Supply Co. receipts
* United States Postal Service package tracking numbers use a modified Luhn algorithm

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luhn_algorithm

The [Luhn algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luhn_algorithm) provides for checkbits to detect typos on the client side, but right now there's no way to run this validation in enketo forms.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Include a custom xpath function to validate the given number is valid.

title: CHT Docker Helper for 4.x fails to install the TLS certificate
body:
**Describe the bug**
When using cht-docker-helper from a Node.js script, it fails to install the TLS certificate from local-ip installed. [These three commands](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/987947839f1a01538c7abecbfb9ca5b410a60e41/scripts/docker-helper-4.x/cht-docker-compose.sh#L461-L463) fail with `the input device is not a TTY` when spawning a process to run the script with any `stdio` setting other than `inherit` `child_process.spawn('cht-docker-compose.sh', { stdio: 'inherit' })`.

This makes the CHT instance unusable because browsers reject the self-signed certificate nginx generated instead of the expected certificate from https://local-ip.medicmobile.org

**To Reproduce**
```js
const { spawn } = require('child_process');

const childProcess = child_process.spawn('cht-docker-compose.sh', { stdio: 'pipe' });
childProcess.stdout.on('data', data => console.error(data.toString()));
childProcess.stderr.on('data', data => console.log(data.toString()));
childProcess.stdin.write('y\n');
childProcess.stdin.write('y\n');
childProcess.stdin.write('project_name\n');
```

**Expected behavior**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen. -->

**Logs**
```
...
Starting project "project_name". First run takes a while. Will try for up to five minutes.......

the input device is not a TTY

the input device is not a TTY

the input device is not a TTY

out   Success! "project_name" is set up:

    https://192-168-1-29.local-ip.medicmobile.org:10443/ (CHT)
...
```

**Additional context**
The only workaround I found was to spawn the process executing the script with `{ stdio: 'inherit' }` but this prevents the script from writing to stdin to answer to cht-docker-helper prompts to set up a new project

title: Improve Bikram Sambat date picker
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
The [Bikram Sambat date picker](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/bikram-sambat/) we currently have for [the forms](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/forms/app/#bikram-sambat-datepicker) provides an easy way to enter dates in Bikram Sambat calendar. However, it lacks many features of a complete date picker.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

Some of the features missing in the Bikram Sambat date picker compared to its Gregorian counterpart:
- Proper calendar view (Month and Weeks)
- Option to jump to Today
- Option to clear
- Option to go to next and previous month
- Option to select the year and date

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None

**Additional context**
Screenshot from the [CHT docs](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/bikram-sambat/):
![image](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/20041732/373d3e8d-b85f-4f2c-9177-c15d8dab5328)

A public repo that has better date picker: https://github.com/opensource-nepal/nepali-date-picker
Demo: https://leapfrogtechnology.github.io/nepali-date-picker/demo/

title: Annotate image not properly loaded by form draw widget
body:
**Describe the bug**
The draw/signature form functionality added in https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8308 included support for "annotating" an image. Basically you upload an image into the form and then you can draw/annotate the image and save the updated file as a report attachment.

Unfortunately, if the annotation question is on the first page of the form, when the image is initially loaded, it actually shows up in the canvas zoomed too far out (instead of being properly fitted within the canvas:

| Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- |
| ![image](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/8441903/95024f5c-6cd5-401f-8b68-bd7d34915ba2)  |  ![image](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/8441903/97cb8318-81ab-4035-b4a0-ff4055d32326) |

**To Reproduce**

- Use the [draw_widget form](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/integration/cht-form/default/forms/draw-widget.xlsx) and upload an image into the "Annotate image widget" question.  
- See that the image is zoomed out.
- Use the reload button to clear the image
- Upload the image into the question again
- See that it is zoomed as expected

**Expected behavior**
The image should be loaded into the canvas at the right size the first time it is loaded.

**Additional context**
After doing some debugging, it appears to be a problem with how we only display the loading indicator while initializing the form.  This means that the `canvas.offsetWidth` property is `0` until we finish initializing the for (and its widgets).  Then we hide the loading indicator and display the form.  

This is a problem because [when the draw widget is enabled](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/e6d184946affc62773d569168216a5b913f38a30/webapp/src/js/enketo/widgets/draw.js#L648) it tries to initialize the size of the canvas [based on the `offsetWidth/height`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/e6d184946affc62773d569168216a5b913f38a30/webapp/src/js/enketo/widgets/draw.js#L600). This, of course, does not behave as expected since the `offsetWidth` is still `0`.  The result is that the various downstream calculations [in `fromObjectURL`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/e6d184946affc62773d569168216a5b913f38a30/webapp/src/js/enketo/widgets/draw.js#L40) do not work properly and the result is a zoomed out image.  

This problem behavior does not happen if the annotation question _is not on the first page_. This is because the `_resizeCanvas` function is re-triggered when changing to a new page. At that point the loading screen is gone and `canvas.offsetWidth` is valued.

I am going to see if I can cook up a fix for this as part of https://github.com/enketo/enketo/issues/1323, but it might require custom handling in cht-core...

title: Organize the upgrade test suite
body:
**Describe the issue**

We want to run the upgrade test suite in a specific order and stop the execution of the other tests if the upgrade to the current branch fails.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

We want to run the upgrade test in this order:
- upgrade from latest to current branch
- run admin-user and webapp
- upgrade to master

And stop the execution of the test suite if the upgrade to the current branch fails. To do that we can consider:
- using `bail` in the `wdio.conf` file -> [wdio config file ](https://webdriver.io/docs/configurationfile/)
- Or maybe adding a condition in the `afterTest` method

```.js
afterTest: (test, context, { error }) => {
        const specificTestName = 'specific test name'; // The name of the specific test
        const specificTestFile = 'specificTestFile.spec.js'; // The specific test file name
        
        if (test.title === specificTestName && test.file.includes(specificTestFile) && error) {
            console.error(`Test "${test.title}" in file "${test.file}" failed. Stopping the test suite.`);
            process.exit(1); // Exit with a non-zero status to indicate failure
        }
    },
```

title: Make Docker Helper more scripting friendly
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
The docker-helper script is great for spinning up test CHT instances.  However, it only works via a prompt-based CLI.  As discussed in https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/pull/620#discussion_r1672578547, it would be nice to update the docker-helper to make it easier to script with.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

More discussion/investigation is needed to determine the best approach, but some of the proposed ideas are:

- Add support to the script for passing some arguments to the initial call that will bypass the prompts
- Break out certain functionality into into well-defined sub-scripts that could be independently consumed
- Rewrite into JavaScript
- Move the whole docker-helper into cht-conf

title: Contact Details load facilities when user has one home place assigned
body:
**Describe the bug**
When the user only has 1 home place assigned, the contact details should not load the descendant facilities. For example, a CHW Area that is the user's home place should not load households. 

But if the user has more than 1 home place assigned, it should load them.  

The bug is when the user has 1 home place, it's loading the facilities on reload.

title: Geopoint Widget map rendering issue when on first page of the form
body:
**Describe the bug**
As noted in [this forum thread](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/conditional-relevant-geopoint-omits-calculate-value/3672/7), there appears to be a rendering problem with the geopoint widget when it is located on the first page of a form.  Basically, the rendered part of the map is off-center and most of what is visible is grey-ed out.

| Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- |
| ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1c298489-26df-4ae1-aca0-6ca26f839c5b) | ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bb9519f5-a516-4612-9eea-627b4583be8e) |

These rendering issues can be fixed when the window is resized and do not happen at all if the widget is located on subsequent form pages.  

**To Reproduce**

1. Create a form with a field that has `type: geopoint` and `appearance: maps` on the first page
2. Open the form and see the map rendering issue.

**Expected behavior**
The map should render properly regardless of which form page it is located on.

**Environment**
I have recreated this behavior on `4.3` and `4.9` code.  

**Additional context**
I have a theory that this behavior is related to what is causing https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9252.  For that issue, the root cause seems to be that Enketo is initializing the widget while the loading spinner is still displayed (and the form is hidden).  This causes weird things to happen for the canvas calculations since the canvas size is wrong (offsetWidth/Height is `0`). Perhaps this is related.

title: Expose the user's target documents into the contact summary
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Automated payment workflows and stock monitoring workflows are often limited in their functionality because of the data that is available to the contact summary and data which is available to forms. A contact summary can only see data directly associated with a single place and even after 3.7.x the data is limited to 500 reports which can be insufficient when reviewing all data created by a CHP in a month. 

We are seeking a performance way to expose more data to contact summaries and to forms.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Targets have full access to all data on a user's device. Targets are efficient because 1) the data is not exposed at once and 2) the results target computations are efficiently cached. `targetDocs` store the computed results of targets.  If we were to expose the user's current and recent target docs to the contact summary, this would be fast, powerful, and performant way to allow contact summaries and forms to effectively access the results of computations which requirei all data on the device. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->

**Additional context**
eCHIS Kenya Digital Payments go-live is awaiting this feature

Deprecations

material

  • Tree controller deprecated. Use one of levelAccessor or childrenAccessor instead. To be removed in a future version.

    • BaseTreeControl, TreeControl, FlatTreeControl, and NestedTreeControl deprecated
    • CdkTree#treeControl deprecated. Provide one of CdkTree#levelAccessor or CdkTree#childrenAccessor instead.
    • MatTreeFlattener deprecated. Use MatTree#childrenAccessor and MatTreeNode#isExpandable instead.
    • MatTreeFlatDataSource deprecated. Use one of levelAccessor or childrenAccessor instead of TreeControl.

    Note when upgrading: isExpandable works differently on Trees using treeControl than trees using childrenAccessor or levelAccessor. Nodes on trees that have a treeControl are expandable by default. Nodes on trees using childrenAccessor or levelAccessor are not expandable by default. Provide isExpandable to override default behavior.

  • Setting tabindex of tree nodes deprecated. By default, Tree ignores tabindex passed to tree nodes.

    • MatTreeNode#tabIndex deprecated. MatTreeNode ignores Input tabIndex and manages its own focus behavior.
    • MatTreeNode#defaultTabIndex deprecated. MatTreeNode ignores defaultTabIndex and manages its own focus behavior.
    • MatNestedTreeNode#tabIndex deprecated. MatTreeNode ignores Input defaultTabIndex and manages its own focus behavior.
    • LegacyTreeKeyManager and LEGACY_TREE_KEY_MANAGER_FACTORY_PROVIDER deprecated. Inject a TreeKeyManagerFactory to customize keyboard behavior.

    Note when upgrading: an opt-out is available for keyboard functionality changes. Provide LEGACY_TREE_KEY_MANAGER_FACTORY_PROVIDER to opt-out of Tree managing its own focus. When provided, Tree does not manage it’s own focus and respects tabindex passed to TreeNode. When provided, have the same focus behavior as before this commit is applied.

-->

# Description

This PR includes the following, for more details, see the comments below in the code. 

- New settings: 
   - Relaunching the app is now optional, and we can specify it on any page. 
   - Search is now defined at page level, so we can search in contact list or report list or any other page in the future.
   - Now, we define the path of the APK file in the computer. Not hardcoded anymore. 
   - Option to start faster by skipping the APK installation and the login: `skip.login` and `capabilities.noReset`, especially useful when building the tests for a new config and want to test if they run fine. 
   - Skip test cases from the settings file. 
- Small refactors
  - one of them is to have a `clickButton` utility function that uses our wait mechanism with automatic retries.  
  - Renaming to follow conventions
    -  `performance.page.js` file to `targets.page.js`
    - `test.apdex.js` to `test.spec.js`
    -  `searchPatient` to `searchContact`
    - `contact-list`, `messages`, `reports` and other labels to follow same convention: `contactList`, `messageList`, `reportList`, etc.
- Separated task load and task submit test cases
- Added report search test case.

The user's facility ID is saved in the store by the contact list. The contact detail also needs it to load the descendants. The problem is when reloading the app, the contact details get an empty facility ID, therefore loading the descendants. 

The fix is to subscribe in the contact's effect constructor to get the facility ID, so it's ready before. 

The contact details should not display the descendants if the user has 1 assigned facility. 
It's fine to display it if the user doesn't have descendants or has more than one descendant. The later is because when the user has more than one facility, the contact list doesn't load descendants, and the contact details is the only way to navigate down the hierarchy. 

This also contains some minor fixes to use plurals for variables containing many items 😬 

#9265

**Describe the bug**
A couchdb restart in single node docker takes down the whole instance. 
I believe this is due to couchDb receiving a new IP in the docker network after restart - this is a fact, but I have not definitively proven this is the cause of the faulure, 

**To Reproduce**

1. Launch single node couchdb 4.9.0 in docker 
2. run `docker stop cht_couchdb_1`

title: Default config: Delivery report is not considered when deciding to show pregnancy report
body:
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/88f9e463abcdd1944a62ced090e9ce870bdf9fb0/config/default/contact-summary-extras.js#L284-L288

Based on the code comment on line 284, it should decide on the basis of a delivery report on whether the contact is ready for a new pregnancy. But the delivery report is not being checked here.

Instead, it checks for abortion and miscarriage, which are already checked above:
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/88f9e463abcdd1944a62ced090e9ce870bdf9fb0/config/default/contact-summary-extras.js#L276-L279

It is probably stopping the users from registering a new pregnancy for a woman who has already delivered some time ago.

```

**Environment**
- Instance: production instance
- App: CouchDb & Haproxy
- Version: 4.2.2 - guessing it will affect 4.3.x, since this uses the same version of couchDb 

**Additional context**
Everytime this happens, I've restarted both haproxy and couchdb - I believe this is also happening: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9284

Eventually I just abandoned using the upgrade API and started indexing process manually (by navigating to the views one by one). This seems to not trigger the same behavior. 

I'm suspecting we're ending up queuing too many requests because of the 2 minute timeout we set in API: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/4.2.x/api/src/services/setup/view-indexer.js#L69
I believe this timeout doesn't end up cancelling the request at CouchDb level, so it's possible we're running out of file descriptors or something (???). Because there are no logs, it's not possible to know.

title: Update add-contact-id-to-user-docs migration to not use medic-client view
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
We've been making efforts to remove calls to medic-client in api startup, but this call crept in in a recent update: 
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/src/migrations/add-contact-id-to-user-docs.js#L6

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
It would be super easy to change this to an _all_docs request with a start_key and end_key to get user-settings docs, which always follow a preset format of `org.couchdb.user:<username>`. 

**Additional context**
This is blocking a complicated and lengthy upgrade of a production instance, where we don't have the luxury to wait for medic-client indexing before launch.

title: Research freetext view use to inform hosting TCO reduction
body:
**Describe the issue**
it's been decided that storage is the highest cost for hosting total cost of ownership (TCO).  It's suspected that CHT's use of CouchDB freetext views cause a large amount of disk space.  But how much? How might the size of the view be reduced? Where does the UI surface the use of these views?

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
research and document use of freetext views so we know how to safely reduce the disk use caused by using them

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
na

-----------------------

**Next Steps:**

 * [x] Check Couch/HAProxy logs for instances of the views being used
 * [ ] [community research](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9365)
 * [ ] Remove views and run e2e tests and see what happens
 * [ ] Add logging for the view and manually poke around the app

Open Questions:
* Where are the views being used programmatically?
* What fields are being searched for?
* What are users actually searching for?

----------------------------------

**CouchDB views for freetext searching**
* [contacts_by_freetext](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/67bb273e2d20b775b27a6c0bdf20b169284aff1d/ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/contacts_by_freetext/map.js#L11)
* [contacts_by_type_freetext](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/contacts_by_type_freetext/map.js)
* [reports_by_freetext](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/reports_by_freetext/map.js)

These get queried by the @medic/search shared lib:
* code that generates queries against the 2 contact-related views: [shared-libs/search/src/generate-search-requests.js](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/shared-libs/search/src/generate-search-requests.js#L264-L276)
* code that generates queries against the report-related view: [shared-libs/search/src/generate-search-requests.js](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/shared-libs/search/src/generate-search-requests.js#L251)

These generated queries are then executed one level higher in [shared-libs/search/src/search.js](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/shared-libs/search/src/search.js#L124-L129)This is then imported and ran by:

* the contact exporter in the API: [api/src/services/export/contact-mapper.js](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/src/services/export/contact-mapper.js)
* the report exporter in the API: [api/src/services/export/report-mapper.js](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/src/services/export/report-mapper.js)
* the search service in the admin app: [admin/src/js/services/search.js](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/admin/src/js/services/search.js)
    * which is used by [this other service](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/admin/src/js/services/select2-search.js#L96) to filter through contact types and places types when editing a user in [admin/src/js/controllers/edit-user.js](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/admin/src/js/controllers/edit-user.js#L151-L157)
* the search service in the webapp: [webapp/src/ts/services/search.service.ts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/services/search.service.ts#L19)
    * contacts => [webapp/src/ts/modules/contacts/contacts.component.ts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/modules/contacts/contacts.component.ts#L439)
    * contacts => [webapp/src/ts/services/contact-view-model-generator.service.ts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/services/contact-view-model-generator.service.ts#L294)
       * [webapp/src/ts/modules/contacts/contacts-deceased.component.ts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/modules/contacts/contacts-deceased.component.ts)
       * [webapp/src/ts/services/contact-view-model-generator.service.ts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/services/contact-view-model-generator.service.ts)
       * [webapp/src/ts/modules/messages/messages-content.component.ts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/modules/messages/messages-content.component.
       * [webapp/src/ts/modules/contacts/contacts-content.component.ts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/modules/contacts/contacts-content.component.ts)
    * contacts => [webapp/src/ts/services/target-aggregates.service.ts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/services/target-aggregates.service.ts#L211)
       * [webapp/src/ts/modules/analytics/analytics-target-aggregates.component.ts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/modules/analytics/analytics-target-aggregates.component.ts#L73)
   * contacts => [webapp/src/ts/services/select2-search.service.ts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/services/select2-search.service.ts#L78)
       * [webapp/src/ts/modals/edit-report/edit-report.component.ts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/modals/edit-report/edit-report.component.ts#L50)

   * reports   => [webapp/src/ts/modules/reports/reports.component.ts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/modules/reports/reports.component.ts#L290)
    * reports   => [webapp/src/ts/modules/reports/reports.component.ts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/modules/reports/reports.component.ts#L470-L474) again
    * reports   => [webapp/src/ts/services/form.service.ts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/services/form.service.ts#L131)

title: No feedback document recorded on PouchDb crash
body:
<!--
**Important**: This is a public repository. Anyone in the world can see what's posted here. If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the bug**
When a PouchDb crash happens, we display a modal saying that the app needs to be reloaded, and we log the error on screen on the tasks tab. However, such an error does not record a feedback document, because saving the feedback document fails. 

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Login as an offline user. 
2. Open the console 
3. type `CHTCore.dbService.get().close();`. This will close the connection to the main database -  but theoretically not to the meta database.
4. Navigate to the tasks page. 
5. Observe the error being visible in the UI and `Error getting tasks for all contacts` getting reported in the console. 
6. Observe a warning `Error while trying to record error` in the console. 
7. Reload the page and sync. 
8. Check the server and see that there is no feedback doc recorded for the event. 

**Expected behavior**
We should have a workaround in place to record feedback docs when PouchDb cannot write. 

**Logs**

title: CouchDb error on indexing telemetry documents
body:
<!--
**Important**: This is a public repository. Anyone in the world can see what's posted here. If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the bug**
Checking logs from an instance upgrading from `4.2.2` to `4.8.1`, I'm seeing lots of errors logged about failing to index certain telemetry documents: 
```
[info] 2024-07-24T22:47:37.208456Z couchdb@127.0.0.1 <0.26440.0> -------- OS Process #Port<0.9087> Log :: function raised exception (new TypeError("number.toString().padStart is not a function", "undefined", 12)) with doc._id telemetry-2024-2-13-plucygaren-5ddd3d91-56b1-48ad-a11f-8f0e97f813fd
[info] 2024-07-24T22:47:37.208835Z couchdb@127.0.0.1 <0.26439.0> -------- OS Process #Port<0.9086> Log :: function raised exception (new TypeError("number.toString().padStart is not a function", "undefined", 12)) with doc._id telemetry-2024-2-16-bmargaretitauc-022087c6-d91c-4f8a-b3f0-14b9bf787784
[info] 2024-07-24T22:47:37.210019Z couchdb@127.0.0.1 <0.6689.1> -------- OS Process #Port<0.9887> Log :: function raised exception (new TypeError("number.toString().padStart is not a function", "undefined", 12)) with doc._id telemetry-2024-2-6-vvictorhumax-2367c8bf-1508-4eb1-bdbb-c210356d25e9
[info] 2024-07-24T22:47:37.210751Z couchdb@127.0.0.1 <0.6670.1> -------- OS Process #Port<0.9882> Log :: function raised exception (new TypeError("number.toString().padStart is not a function", "undefined", 12)) with doc._id telemetry-2024-2-10-hleahwasif-a07b0c8a-1c08-4b8c-bc90-8ce228ed86ab
```

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Install 4.2.2
2. Create an offline user and do some actions, change the date to generate a telemetry document. 
3. Upgrade to 4.8.1
4. Check logs. 

**Expected behavior**
Ideally no views should throw errors. 

**Logs**
As above. 

**Environment**
- Instance: production instance
- App: couchdb
- Version: 4.8.1

**Additional context**
We had fixed the view to be backwards compatible with the Javascript engine that runs on CouchDb 2, so the view can be warmed, but it appears that some documents can still throw errors when being indexed.

title: Expose user's contact summary when filling out forms
body:
@mrjones-plip summarized Philip's issue as: Some deployments of CHT will store a lot of information in the contact summary for a CHW's user when using stock monitoring.  When the user then goes to fill out a form that needs this information, say to administer medication from their stock, deployments would like the form to have logic to know if the medication is in stock or not.

From [the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/how-to-access-parents-summary-information-from-an-app-form/3287) post on the same topic summarized it this way:

> Suppose we have a Place A which keeps stock records in its contact summary.
> 
> In a form linked to Place A, to access the stock of Albendazol 200, we use the following calculation code: `instance('contact-summary')/context/stock_monitoring_albendazol_200_qty` and it works perfectly.
> 
> Under Place A, we have a household with many people. My question is as follows:
> In a form linked to a household member, how do I access the stock of Albendazol 200?
> 
> As you know `instance('contact-summary')/context/stock_monitoring_albendazol_200_qty` wouldn’t work, because it would mean searching for that quantity on that household member’s contact. summary 

@jkuester and @dianabarsan replied:

> there is no way...to access the contact-summary of a different contact.

and

> I don’t believe it’s possible to access to contact summary of another contact. Is there any way that you can persist certain fields or data across multiple contacts to help you achieve the same result?

@PhilipNgari  originally wrote this when opening the ticket, in the context of eCHIS KE:

> The supply chain module in eCHIS has run into a deadlock per these two scenarios;
> 1. When CHAs supply CHPs with commodities the CHP's balances are updated but this does not happen to CHAs
> 2. CHAs and CHPs can supply even when they have negative balances
> 
> This has been explored by  devs via https://github.com/moh-kenya/config-echis-2.0/issues/905 and currently, all combined in #https://github.com/moh-kenya/config-echis-2.0/issues/2410.
> 
> This capability is urgent as all users must account for commodities but are blocked by this. 
 cc @garethbowen @craig-landry  per our conversation.  I am tagging @christinawere  @JenniferMuli  for additions where need be.

title: Consolidate angular dependencies
body:
**Describe the issue**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. -->
Currently angular dependencies are split between webapp and root package.json files, which means if you update one and not the other you're going to have a bad time ([comment](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/9300#discussion_r1703832846)). This follows on from #9106

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

Move all angular dependencies to webapp - it's the only directory that uses angular currently so it makes sense to put everything in there.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->
Move all angular dependencies to root, but this means they will get bundled in to api and sentinel which is completely unnecessary. Also there's a risk of somehow conflicting with angularjs needed by admin.

title: Upgrade to CouchDb 3.4.x
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
CouchDb 3.4.0 will be released soon. 
It includes some changes that could improve things for the CHT significantly such as: 
- [#4736](https://github.com/apache/couchdb/issues/4736): Stop client process and clean up if client disconnects.
- [#4503](https://github.com/apache/couchdb/issues/4503): Make timeouts for _view and _search configurable.
- [#4627](https://github.com/apache/couchdb/issues/4627): Add [QuickJS](https://bellard.org/quickjs/) as a JavaScript engine option.

Full release notes: https://docs.couchdb.org/en/latest/whatsnew/3.4.html

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Upgrade CHT to use CouchDb 3.4.0

title: warnings output on command line with docker helper
body:
**Describe the issue**
When you run [docker helper](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/hosting/4.x/app-developer/#cht-docker-helper-for-4x) and opt to create a new project there's some warnings output:

```bash
Would you like to initialize a new project [y/N]?y
grep: warning: stray \ before :
grep: warning: stray \ before :
```

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
These should not be output

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
they're benign, so could leave as is

## Good first issue

To succeed on this ticket, please:

1. Set up your [development environment](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/community/contributing/code/core/dev-environment/) and ensure it works by logging in to your CHT instance
1. The file to fix is [`scripts/docker-helper/cht-docker-compose.sh`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/docker-helper/cht-docker-compose.sh). Open it and look at the `grep` calls on the following lines:
   - **Line 59** (`get_all_known_versions`): `grep -o "medic:medic:[A-Za-z0-9\.\_\/\-]*"` contains unnecessary backslash escapes inside the `[...]` bracket expression (e.g. `\.`, `\_`, `\/`). Inside bracket expressions, most characters are literal and do not need escaping. Newer versions of `grep` warn about these stray backslashes
   - **Line 63** (`get_latest_version_string`): `grep -o 'medic:medic:[0-9\.]*'` has the same issue with `\.` inside brackets
   - **Line 200** (`get_image`): `grep "${service}:" "${compose_path}"` may also be relevant depending on what `$service` resolves to
1. To understand the root cause: in POSIX regex, a backslash inside a bracket expression `[...]` has no special meaning. So `[A-Za-z0-9\.\_\/\-]` should be `[A-Za-z0-9._/\-]` (only `-` needs escaping or placing at the end). Modern `grep` versions emit a warning for each unnecessary backslash escape it encounters
1. Reproduce the issue by running the docker helper script (`scripts/docker-helper/cht-docker-compose.sh`) and choosing to initialize a new project. Confirm you see the `grep: warning: stray \ before :` warnings
1. Fix the grep patterns by removing the unnecessary backslash escapes from inside the bracket expressions. Make sure the regex still matches the same strings after your changes
1. Run the docker helper script again after your fix and confirm the warnings are gone and the script still behaves correctly (versions are listed, project initializes successfully)

Release notes

Sourced from pouchdb-generate-replication-id's releases.

9.0.0

The PouchDB developers are delighted to announce the immediate availability of PouchDB 9.0.0. This is a major release with 202 PRs merged since the last version.

For a full changelog from 8.0.1 to 9.0.0, please see the releases page or view the latest commits.

The PouchDB developers would like to thank all contributors for their hard and diligent work.

Highlights

  • Massively improved the stability and performance of the indexeddb adapter. Special thanks to @​alxndrsn, Medic, and the Google Advanced Web Apps Fund.
  • Introduce a default limit (of 25) to the .find() method. This constitutes a backwards incompatible change and is the reason for the major version bump.
  • Streamline the automated test suites and move in-browser testing to Playwright resulting in much more reliable test runs.
  • Continue to update the codebase to ES6.

title: Generated docs are published when building dev branches
body:
**Describe the issue**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. -->
The documentation is being updated way more often than it should be.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to change. -->
The documentation should only be updated when the main branch is built. Not only is this less spammy, but it also means the docs are only updated when reviewed, the docs aren't revoked when out of date branches run, and finally the build won't run and fail for external contributors.

The easiest way is just to skip the step when not on `master`.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->
Maybe it should be a cron build instead of complicating the build workflow further.

**Other**

- It looks like this was the intention because the build is named "Main Branch Only - Deploy to GH pages"
- Too many commits in the repo: https://github.com/medic/cht-datasource/commits/main/

title: Release 4.11.0
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [x] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Checkout to a new `<issue>-update-version` branch (eg: `1234-update-version`) and set the version number in the `package.json` and `package-lock.json`. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`. Once the version is updated, submit a PR to `master` branch.
- [x] Ensure that issues associated with commits merged to `master` since the last release are closed and mapped to the milestone.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once the PR has been merged into `master`, and the `master` branch has the new version number, then the release process can start:

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development Slack channel using this template:
```
@core_devs I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by creating a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`) and then push the created tag.
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the team by writing a message in the #product-team Slack channel:
```
@product_team, I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag. 
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make. 
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [x] The beta tag will automatically trigger the scalability build. Once it passes, download the scalability results on S3 at medic-e2e/scalability/$TAG_NAME. If you do not have access to the scalability results ask someone in the #product-team who has access. Add the release `.json` file to `cht-core/tests/scalability/previous_results`. More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [x] Go to the [Issues tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues) and filter the issues with `is:issue label:"Affects: 4.x.x" ` , replace `4.x.x` with the previous version number. Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label.  
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labelled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [x] Collect known migration steps, descriptions, screenshots, videos, data, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. This information should already be on the issue, but if not, prompt the change author to provide it.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions) and update the EOL date of the previous release. Update the status of any releases that are past their End Of Life date. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page.
- [x] Create a [new release](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases/new) in GitHub, with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, from the release branch created above as the target branch. Click on the "Choose a tag" dropdown and create a tag for the release with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. Ensure the release notes PR from above are merged. Add a link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Once you publish the release, confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Upgrade the [demo](https://demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org/) instance to the newly released version.
- [x] Use cht-conf to upload the configuration from the `cht-core/config/demo` folder to the `demo-cht.dev` server.
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*We're excited to announce the release of {{version}} of {{product}}*

See below for some highlights, read the [release notes]({{<paste-url>}}) for full details.

Following our support policy, versions {{versions}} are no longer supported. Projects running these versions should start planning to upgrade in the near future. For more details read our [software support documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions).

Check out our [roadmap](https://github.com/orgs/medic/projects/112/views/21) to see what else is currently being working on.

## {{version}} Highlights

### [{{Highlight 1}}]({{<paste-url to section>}})

{{description of highlight section}}

### ### [{{Highlight 2}}]({{<paste-url to section>}})

{{description of highlight section}}

### [And more...]({{paste-url to section}})

We’ve also implemented loads of other improvements and fixed a heap of bugs.

```
- [x] Add one last update to the #product-team Slack channel and use the thread to lead an internal release retrospective covering what went well and areas to improve for next time.
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently the logic for the custom phone widget for collecting phone numbers in forms, will [automatically format](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/1b9b6527c77d8668ca4963ddc7a2d5e6aa6b7273/webapp/src/js/enketo/widgets/phone-widget.js#L54) the number value before saving the data into the form's model.  However, the value _displayed to the user_ in the form does not change (the input text box still just contains the exact value entered by the user).  

**Describe the solution you'd like**
More UX consideration here is needed to decide what would be most helpful (and least surprising) to users, but the original phone widget code included a TODO that suggested updating the displayed phone number value in the form to also be the formatted value stored in the model.  

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
One reason we may not want to do this is because it would result in the user seeing the value change _after they enter it_.  This could result in user confusion as to what happened with the value the entered.  (Note that the only automatic changes that could happen to the value would be with regards to its formatting. The actual number, itself, would not be automatically updated.)

**Additional context**
I am logging this issue now for better visibility and discussion of the feature. I plan to remove the TODO comment from the code.

title: feat(#6390): update phone widget to allow not checking for dupes
body:
# Description

Closes #6390

https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/pull/1498

This PR add support for a new way to configure a phone number field in a form.  Previously, the phone widget was configured in an xlsxform field by setting `type: tel`.  By default, the phone widget both validates the phone number value and checks for existing contacts that have the same number.  

With these new changes, the existing (now deprecated) functionality stays the same, but going forwards, phone number fields should be configured in an xlsxform by setting `type: string` with `appearance: number tel`.  Fields with this new configuration will always validate the phone number value, but by default they will _not_ check for existing contacts with the same number.  To enforce a unique phone number with the new style of field, you should add a new column with `instance::cht:unique_tel: true`

## Testing considerations

We had some existing coverage of the phone widget in the enekto_widgets tests both in `e2e` and `integration/cht-form`.  However, as we determined when we did the countdown timer feature, it seems more sustainable to break out tests/forms for specific widgets instead of trying to cram everything into the `enketo_widgets` tests.  So, I have created a new `phone_widget` form and added tests for that, both in `e2e` and `integration/cht-form`. I covered as much as possible in the cht-form tests, but part of the phone-widget functionality involves querying the database to check for other contacts with the same phone number.  This functionality cannot be properly validated in the cht-form tests, so I added a few cases to the `e2e` tests.

title: Strip invisible characters from the fields bsYear, bsMonth, bsDay
body:
With issue #7654 (PR #7656), we solved the problem of zero-width (invisible) characters ruining the SMS forms.

With #7676 (PR #7718), we made it less strict and allowed the zero-width characters in strings.

9.0.0

The PouchDB developers are delighted to announce the immediate availability of PouchDB 9.0.0. This is a major release with 202 PRs merged since the last version.

For a full changelog from 8.0.1 to 9.0.0, please see the releases page or view the latest commits.

The PouchDB developers would like to thank all contributors for their hard and diligent work.

Highlights

body:
Bumps [redux](https://github.com/reduxjs/redux) from 4.2.0 to 5.0.1.
Release notes

Sourced from redux's releases.

v5.0.1

This patch release adjusts the isPlainObject util to allow objects created via Object.create(null), and fixes a type issue which accidentally made the store state type non-nullable.

What's Changed

  • fix(isPlainObject): support check Object.create(null) by @​zhe-he in reduxjs/redux#4633
  • fix(types/store): Unexpectedly narrowed return type of function Store['getState'] by @​exuanbo in reduxjs/redux#4638

Full Changelog: https://github.com/reduxjs/redux/compare/v5.0.0...v5.0.1

v5.0.0

This major release:

  • Converts the codebase to TypeScript
  • Updates the packaging for better ESM/CJS compatibility and modernizes the build output
  • Requires that action.type must be a string
  • Continues to mark createStore as deprecated
  • Deprecates the AnyAction type in favor of an UnknownAction type that is used everywhere
  • Removes the PreloadedState type in favor of a new generic argument for the Reducer type.

This release has breaking changes.

This release is part of a wave of major versions of all the Redux packages: Redux Toolkit 2.0, Redux core 5.0, React-Redux 9.0, Reselect 5.0, and Redux Thunk 3.0.

For full details on all of the breaking changes and other significant changes to all of those packages, see the "Migrating to RTK 2.0 and Redux 5.0" migration guide in the Redux docs.

[!NOTE] The Redux core, Reselect, and Redux Thunk packages are included as part of Redux Toolkit, and RTK users do not need to manually upgrade them - you'll get them as part of the upgrade to RTK 2.0. (If you're not using Redux Toolkit yet, please start migrating your existing legacy Redux code to use Redux Toolkit today!)

# RTK
npm install @reduxjs/toolkit
yarn add @reduxjs/toolkit

Standalone


npm install redux
yarn add redux

Changelog

ESM/CJS Package Compatibility

The biggest theme of the Redux v5 and RTK 2.0 releases is trying to get "true" ESM package publishing compatibility in place, while still supporting CJS in the published package.

The primary build artifact is now an ESM file, dist/redux.mjs. Most build tools should pick this up. There's also a CJS artifact, and a second copy of the ESM file named redux.legacy-esm.js to support Webpack 4 (which does not recognize the exports field in package.json). Additionally, all of the build artifacts now live under ./dist/ in the published package.

title: Research community use of search
body:
**Describe the issue**
We don't know how search is used, so we're not sure how hosting TCO efforts to reduce free text search might impact search.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
UXR team to decide best how to validate search use, but: We should reach out to App Services, program managers, 3rd party app devs and anyone else we think would help inform us of how search is used.  Are there workflows that CHWs are trained on that use search?  Are there deployments where reports tab is hidden so this search doesn't work? 

Some info to inform our research is:

### update from Care Teams

Excerpt from a [slack thread](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C02GME3BQE6/p1722904248162379?thread_ts=1722887181.632989&cid=C02GME3BQE6):

> > which ones use it?  (telemetry?)
> 
> Here are two posts re: search on [Reports](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/telemetry-questions-about-the-reports-tab-search/2018) and [Contacts](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/telemetry-questions-about-the-contacts-tab-search/2651) pages.  I [just pulled some data](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1LZhRpnC1R3YRmkhDgPNA3cEgrCNLQuTidgSEltBRuo8/edit?gid=427600872#gid=427600872) based on the search:contacts:search and search:reports:search keys for a handful of projects. I can't guarantee that these keys only count freetext searches but I believe so.  We can chat tomorrow about the details if you like.

> > how many hide it? (eg hide reports tab)
> 
> Also included in the same spreadsheet as above. Pretty much everyone has access to the Contacts Page, some users don't have access to Reports, but most do.
> 
> Worth noting that there's a difference between (a) being able to see the page at all, and (b) whether it shows up as a tab or in the hamburger menu. The data I pulled relates to being able to see the page at all
> 
> > train on it?
> 
> Not sure. 

Another excerpt from the same thread:

> Looking at [telemetry](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1LZhRpnC1R3YRmkhDgPNA3cEgrCNLQuTidgSEltBRuo8/edit?gid=427600872#gid=427600872) ,percentage of total CHWs is between   0.07% and 50%  - search is very much being used!

### Fields we're planning on indexing

Contacts
* name
* notes
* patient_name

Reports:
* ? TK ?

### Search results analysis
* ? TK google doc link (private) ?

### Care Teams Updates

Currently [releasing](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/releasing/#cht-core) takes 2-3 days of manual effort, which costs in productivity. It also means there's a limit on how quickly and frequently releases are done, so in some cases code is approved and merged but projects still have to wait before it can be deployed into production.  It also means that Medic is the gatekeeper on when releases are made available for community contributed code.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to change. -->
Use Continuous Delivery to automatically release every time a non-chore commit is merged. This should work much like cht-conf which automatically releases using semantic-release to npm. This will include...

- updating the semver version
- publishing the artifacts
- generating and publishing the release notes
- sending appropriate notifications

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->
- Doing releases _less_ often - this would reduce the workload but increase the time partners have to wait for changes that are ready

**Steps to achieve this**

Preparation steps - these can be done while still using the manual process.

- [ ] Automatically generate and publish release notes on [docs site](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/). This might include the PR contributor including release note details (like highlights, screenshots, links to documentation, etc) in the issue or PR so that the script can publish these during release.
- [ ] Updating the release notes so you can aggregate changes between two versions. Ideally find a 3rd party solution for this, but implementers need to be able to see all the changes that will be applied from their current version to the desired upgrade version. This is really useful today, but will be critical when we increase the number of releases drastically. The old release notes will need to be updated in this new format so it still works if comparing back to 3.10 (approx). Releases notes earlier than that can just be archived.
- [ ] Improve how we label regressions and known issues. Right now we label every regression with an "Affects" label for every release between when it was introduced and when it was resolved. This is already unwieldy but will become more so with more releases. Mostly this label is used so the release notes can include "known issues" but searching on GH. With the new release notes format (above) this can be replaced with a better system, for example, just label when the regression was introduced, and the release notes can scrape all labels.
- [ ] Re-evaluate our supported versions policy. It was designed for when releases happened infrequently. With releases happening all the time does this change the support duration? How will fixes be backported to dozens of old branches anyway? If we guarantee no backwards compatibility issues, is it reasonable to expect people to upgrade to the latest minor?
- [ ] Announcing the release on the forum. The forum posts are very formulaic, mostly just linking to the release notes. Set up GH > Forum integrations and it should be straightforward.
- [ ] Automatically update the demo instance with a new release.  See [earlier effort on this work](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8270).
- [ ] Fully [automate the scalability suite](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7526) and execute it on a weekly schedule so it doesn't block the release but doesn't run too often.

Finally, in one go...

- [ ] Use semantic-release to automate kicking off the release
- [ ] Update [documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/releasing/#cht-core), [issue templates](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE), etc
- [ ] Communicate new process and policies on the forum, with teammates, and with key partners

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

Added functionality of getting places using pages or as `AsyncGenerator` using `cht-datasource` along with the addition of REST endpoint `/api/v1/person` which provides people as pages.

<!-- ISSUE NUMBER -->
Issues: #9239 , #9240 , #9242

Usage:
1. Pagination API
```typescript
Place.v1.getPageByType(Qualifier.byContactType(placeType), cursor, limit); // limit and cursor are optional with defaults as 100 and "0" respectively
```
2. Async Generator API
```typescript
const getAllIterator = Place.v1.getByType(ctx)(Qualifier.byContactType('place'));
```
3. REST API endpoint
```
HTTP GET api/v1/place
```
Query Params:
- placeType - the `contact_type` of the place to fetch
- limit - default is 100
- cursor - default is 0
