title: Add dedicated field to freetext search indexes for recording custom search keywords for reports and contacts
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
As a part of https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9293 we are dramatically reducing the contacts/reports fields that will be indexed for freetext searching (e.g. using the search bar on the Reports or People tabs).  Instead of indexing data from nearly all top-level fields on the docs, we will instead be indexing a specific hard-coded set of fields (e.g. `name`, `person_id`, etc).  

However, it is possible that for some deployments there is a need to be able to search for data that is recorded in a custom field on the contact/report.  

**Describe the solution you'd like**

The proposal here is to add an additional `search_keywords` field to be indexed by the freetext search views.  This field would be empty by default, but can be auto-populated in the form when creating new reports/contacts.  The data in the `search_keywords` just needs to be space-separated to be able to make the freetext search work so the forms could even be configured to combine data from multiple input fields and make it all searchable.  

One known downside to this is that it would not be retroactive.  If a project decides they want to index the `phone` field of a contact, they can update their forms to copy the `phone` value to `search_keywords`, but this will not affect the existing contacts.  You would need a script to go copy the field for each existing contact.

title: accept_case_reports transition broken - report not updated
body:
**Describe the bug**
So, this is some ancient history (and I do not fully understand the workflow). But, I was trying to manually configure and test `case_id` functionality by using the `accept_case_reports` transition to set the `place_uuid` field on a report based on its `case_id` value.

Unfortunately, I could not get this to work. The transition code would get triggered as expected, but the `onMatch` function [returns the result of `silenceRegistrations`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/53439767aa828c8bd7e5513ab59f1461ae7a741f/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/accept_case_reports.js#L97). In order to trigger the updates to the doc to be written to the DB, the `onMatch` function should resolve a truthy value.  However, the `silenceRegistrations` function [does not seem to ever resolve something truthy](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/53439767aa828c8bd7e5513ab59f1461ae7a741f/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/accept_patient_reports.js#L175).  

**To Reproduce**

Once again, I am not super familiar with the "proper" case_id workflow, so maybe I am just doing something wrong here....  

I started with a `register_case` app form that is associated with a contact when it gets saved. With this form, I enabled the `registration` transition and added the following app_settings config:

```json
  "registrations": [{
    "form": "register_case",
    "events": [{
      "name": "on_create",
      "trigger": "add_case"
    }]
  }],
```

When I submitted a `register_case` form, the transition would automatically update the report with a generated `case_id`.

Then I created a `case_event` form that contained nothing but a field to set the `case_id` (no linkage to any kind of contact).  I enabled the `accept_case_reports` transition with the following config:

```json
  "accept_case_reports": [{
    "form": "case_event",
    "validations": {},
    "messages": []
  }],
```

When I submit a `case_event` report (with the case_id assigned to my previous `register_case` report), I can see the `accept_case_reports` transition is triggered. It finds the existing case registration and sets the expected `place_uuid` field onto the `case_event` doc.  However, since the `silenceRegistrations` function resolves `undefined`, this doc update is not persisted to the DB.   

**Expected behavior**
I was expecting the `case_event` report to be assigned to the place associated with my `register_case` report.

**Additional context**

It seems like this workflow was broken in `3.9.0` :sweat: with [these changes](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/commit/32f501134ebde24e81075af56018971d1649f28d#diff-3cb63b4eca753069d70e238b3bb489a4857b55751231efd4bd9ffcd47f846b9fL191) to the `accept_patient_reports.silenceRegistrations` logic. Previously that function resolved `true` when it successfully completed. Afterwards, it resolves `undefined`.

title: fix(#8225): fix handling of `inputs` group with contact selector
body:
# Description

Closes https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8225

This PR updates our patch for the Eneketo relevant logic to make it so that the `inputs` group never can get set to non-relevant (and so calculations and widgets and things involving `inputs` all work as expected even when the `inputs` fields are not _shown_ in the form).  

## Testing considerations

I have expanded our db-object widget e2e tests to cover using the widget to load contact data inside the `inputs` group.  Also, the other existing tests all work as expected.  The risk here is that the new Enekto patch somehow breaks Enekto code in other unexpected ways.  I have done some manual testing to try to shake out any issues, but everything has worked as expected.

It would be good, though, to perhaps do more manual testing of any workflows that involve passing `inputs` data to forms (e.g. forms triggered from tasks).

**Describe the issue**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. -->
We have a package.json in `/scripts` and `/scripts/generate-form-attachments` which seldom get updated because they're out of the way. These are now firing dependabot alerts for serious vulnerabilities.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to change. -->
1. Remove unused packages.
2. Remove packages that are already installed at the root level.
3. Move remaining dependencies to the root level.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->
I thought about keeping the script package.json separate, but decided to add all dependencies as root devDependencies because that's literally what that's for.

title: Update `api/v1/person` endpoint to not use camel-case `personType` query parameter
body:
We do not have a ton of consistent conventions for our [REST api](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/api/), but one that we do have is that all our current query parameter names are _snake-case_ and not _camel-case_.  

For the [recently added](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/9311) (and as of yet unreleased) support for getting persons by type, I missed in the code review that the query parameter was named `personType`.

We should just change this to be `type` since semantically the "person" part is redundant: `api/v1/person?type=my-person-type`.

title: Prototype for Documenting UI State - Contacts Page | List View (Access)
body:
**Describe the issue**
We need to create documentation for the UI State by Config because the CHT has complex configurations that significantly impact how the user interface appears and functions. By documenting these configurations, we provide valuable guidance to the QA team to ensure they can accurately test the UI under various configurations. It also helps new team members quickly understand how the system is set up and how different configurations affect the UI. For first-time users, clear documentation makes navigating and using the tool easier, minimizing confusion and improving overall user experience.

This issue aims to prototype one feature (for the Contacts Page | List View (Access)) to identify unknowns and create a workflow for documenting UI States.

**Tasks already done**

- [X] Decide on the Feature:

We will use "Contacts Page - Access" as our first example.

- [X] Confirm Individual Scenarios:

We will use [this](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ucVVVVv7BR7C9AmTVgYm4H4OLSX2pmtXojvUElX00tc) list of scenarios required for the "Contacts Page - Access."

- [X] Design Configuration and Data:

Design the necessary configuration and data, including roles and names for households and other entities. We will start with [this](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ucVVVVv7BR7C9AmTVgYm4H4OLSX2pmtXojvUElX00tc). As part of this work, we will improve the design if needed.

**Tasks included in this issue**
- [x] Create Tests for Screenshots:

    - [x] Verify if existing end-to-end (e2e) tests cover the scenarios. If not, create new tests.

    - [x] Update test data to be more realistic ("nice" data) if necessary for documentation purposes. If necessary, improve the design of the necessary configuration and data.

    - [x] Run the tests to generate the required screenshots: Ensure the data and screenshots are consistent and realistic for documentation.

**Tasks not included in this issue**
- [ ] Draft Documentation Pages:

Begin drafting the page(s) for the cht-docs repository.
Include screenshots and detailed descriptions of each scenario.

- [ ] Deploy to Docs Site:

Manually deploy the updated documentation and screenshots to the docs site.

title: Streamline /config dependencies
body:
**Describe the issue**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. -->
Having dependencies defined in the /config directories makes managing updates difficult. Currently these packages are triggering 65 of 118 dependabot warnings, which at worst mean there is a vulnerability, but at best is hiding the signal in the noise of overreporting.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to change. -->
Remove unnecessary dependencies, remove dependencies that are already defined at the root, and move dependencies needed to the root devDependencies

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->
We could add monitoring to each subdir and do the updates but because most packages are duplicated at the top level this would just be duplication of effort.

title: Create a Apdex settings file to test form flows
body:
**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We have [a settings file to test navigation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/tests/performance/apdex-score/sample-settings-files) across the app when using the default config 

Now we need another one to test performance when:
- Creating patients, 
- Creating reports, 
- Submitting tasks, 
- Closing and reopening the app

**Additional context**
This is something we need to assess the current performance of CHT and also to test migrations, for example a new version of Angular or Pouchdb v9

title: Default delivery form fails when selecting two healthy children
body:
<!--
**Important**: This is a public repository. Anyone in the world can see what's posted here. If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the bug**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the bug is. -->
On the latest cht-core the default delivery form fails with a fatal constraint validation when selecting 2 healthy children.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Load the default config (or use demo-cht)
2. Select a person who can deliver
3. Start a delivery form 
4. Select "Alive and well" 
5. Click Next
6. Select "No" for all danger signs
7. Click Next
8. Select 2 babies delivered
9. Select 2 babies alive
10. See error

**Expected behavior**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen. -->
No constraint violation.

**Logs**
<!-- If applicable, include the server or browser logs. -->

**Screenshots**
<!-- If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem. -->

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c90537f6-a151-4d5d-9739-46c632538460)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aca91f10-d397-4b4f-9165-a435dc08b68d)

**Environment**
- Instance: localhost
- Browser: Chrome
- Client platform: linux
- App: webapp
- Version: 4.11.0

**Additional context**
<!-- Add any other context about the problem here. What have you tried? Is there a workaround? -->

I think this is a regression, probably due to an enketo-core upgrade. It's not helped by our form being incredibly complex.

title: Provide config translations for all supported languages
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. It would be better to [...] -->
The `default` and `demo` configs only have English translations, but CHT also supports Nepali, French, Swahili, and Spanish out of the box. This is a bad experience out of the box.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->
1. Clean up duplicates between `api/resources/translations/*` and `config/**/translations`. There are some translations that are overwritten in the default config - pick the winner and set it in the `api` version and remove the key from the `config` version. 
2. Move translation keys to the appropriate translation file. Ideally the `api` version would have all translation keys that are needed for cht-core and the `config` version would have keys for the forms, targets, etc for that specific config. Right now it's mixed up so it's complicated to trace where the key is used.
3. Provide 100% of the translations for supported languages.
4. Extend the translation linting to also verify translations for `demo` and `default` configs so support isn't accidentally dropped in future.

title: chore: bump webpack from 5.90.3 to 5.94.0

Bumps [webpack](https://github.com/webpack/webpack) from 5.90.3 to 5.94.0.
Release notes

Sourced from webpack's releases.

v5.94.0

Bug Fixes

  • Added runtime condition for harmony reexport checked
  • Handle properly data/http/https protocols in source maps
  • Make bigint optimistic when browserslist not found
  • Move @​types/eslint-scope to dev deps
  • Related in asset stats is now always an array when no related found
  • Handle ASI for export declarations
  • Mangle destruction incorrect with export named default properly
  • Fixed unexpected asi generation with sequence expression
  • Fixed a lot of types

New Features

  • Added new external type "module-import"
  • Support webpackIgnore for new URL() construction
  • [CSS] @import pathinfo support

Security

  • Fixed DOM clobbering in auto public path

v5.93.0

Bug Fixes

  • Generate correct relative path to runtime chunks
  • Makes DefinePlugin quieter under default log level
  • Fixed mangle destructuring default in namespace import
  • Fixed consumption of eager shared modules for module federation
  • Strip slash for pretty regexp
  • Calculate correct contenthash for CSS generator options

New Features

  • Added the binary generator option for asset modules to explicitly keep source maps produced by loaders
  • Added the modern-module library value for tree shakable output
  • Added the overrideStrict option to override strict or non-strict mode for javascript modules

v5.92.1

Bug Fixes

  • Doesn't crash with an error when the css experiment is enabled and contenthash is used

v5.92.0

Bug Fixes

  • Correct tidle range's comutation for module federation
  • Consider runtime for pure expression dependency update hash
  • Return value in the subtractRuntime function for runtime logic

title: Deprecated mutation event
body:
We've experienced an new test failure in our pipeline (where we run many of your tests) without a change in code which we think may be related to removal of support for the mutation event `DOMSubtreeModified` https://developer.chrome.com/blog/mutation-events-deprecation from Chrome 127, which appears in the following file: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/js/enketo/widgets/dynamic-url.js. 
This file is identical in the version (`"enketo-core": "^5.18.1"`) we're running.

`should set the href to the dynamically generated URL even when the dynamic value is empty`. outputs:
```
+ expected - actual
-[[http://google.com?q=helloWorld](http://google.com/?q=helloWorld)](http://google.com/?q=helloWorld](http://google.com/?q=helloWorld))
+[[http://google.com?q=worldHello](http://google.com/?q=worldHello)](http://google.com/?q=worldHello](http://google.com/?q=worldHello))
```
This only fails in the pipeline and does not fail locally.

The failures starting loosely align with an update to the runner image: https://github.com/actions/runner-images/commit/0d632219e5a750d8d1b9974d1e8713a2fa111ce9

We have looked at your pipelines and don't see failures with the same Chrome version, but we're a bit out of ideas otherwise.

In support of this theory, using the following to ensure that the assert occurs as the last action on the macro-task queue seems to resolve the issue.
```
setTimeout(() => {
   expect($(DynamicUrlWidget.selector).attr('href')).to.equal(`[http://google.com?q=${dynamic}](http://google.com/?q=${dynamic})`);
}, 0);
```

If there is a polyfill using MutationObserver (something like https://github.com/mfreed7/mutation-events-polyfill) buried somewhere in the dependency tree (shadydom may be adding one), then this may have changed the behaviour from sync to async and scheduled on the micro-task queue.

That said, we're not sure why this issue wouldn't be affecting your pipelines. However, because `DOMSubtreeModified` is being removed, we thought it useful to let you know about it.

We understand this isn't your bug, so our PR with the setTimeout is just a suggestion, but it might be something of a minor future proof for you and this issue is in part just a note that a breakage may be coming down the pipe.

Otherwise, we're hoping you may know something about it.

**Additional context:**

title: Replace pupil for rule evaluation
body:
**Describe the issue**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. -->
The [pupil lib](https://github.com/Dragory/Pupil) is abandoned and 11 years out of date. Because it's no unpublished from npm we have inlined it in the [validation shared-lib](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/shared-libs/validation/src/pupil). Furthermore we made some changes to the source so it's a custom medic implementation. Because it's so old dependabot is reporting 12 errors.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to change. -->
- Ensure there's enough testing coverage to guarantee backwards compatibility
- Move the pupil src into a regular directory and give up on any pretense that it's an npm dependency and delete unnecessary artifacts (package-lock.json, readme.md, dist, etc)
- Update it pass our linting and style guide
- Merge our custom `extra_validations` into pupil to reduce complexity - this may also solve https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8806

title: feat(#9327): add tabs navigation in desktop display

# Description Adds back the tabs navigation for desktop display. The intention is to smooth the transition to the new navigation, the plan is to eventually remove the tab navigation bar from the desktop, so CHWs can access the tabs using the sidebar menu. title: Prevent creating contacts under facilities that are not the direct parent
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
It's possible to create a contact under another that is not its direct parent. 

In app-settings, we define the hierarchy. Take the one in the `default` config as an example, [where `clinic` direct parent is the `health_center`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/488bbd6148075ea8cbc575729061e019ecda7004/config/default/app_settings.json#L331). It's possible to create a `clinic` under `district_hospital` by changing the URL like this: 
`#/contacts/[district-hospital-id]/add/clinic`

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
The Contact Edit component can validate that the parent_id in the URL is a contact type directly associated of contact_type form. 

**Additional context**
It can help preventing errors [like this one reported in the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/bizarre-recursive-place-case/3825/9)

title: Add additional storage data to monitoring API
Only 50 reports are passed to the contact summary which is passed to enketo
body:
**Describe the bug**
After https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8815 (4.7),  the contact-summary.templated.js code is passed the contact's latest 500 reports.  But in this specific scenario, the contact-summary is passed only 50 reports.

**To Reproduce**
1. Create a CHT place
2. Create 100 reports at this place
3. Create a contact-summary.templated.js which outputs the value of `console.log(reports.length);`
4. Navigate to the CHT place and view the value of reports. You see `100` (good)
5. Complete an action at the place
6. When the action loads, contact-summary is calculated again with the result passed to enketo and this time says `50` (bad)

**Expected behavior**
The data passed to the contact-summary should be consistent every time it is calculated

**Environment**
- Instance: eCHIS Kenya
- App: webapp
- Version: master 4.11

**Additional context**
This is causing data quality problems for eCHIS Kenya digital payments work. If a CHP completes more than 50 forms between their performance-assessment and their performance-verification, then their supervisor sees that their performance-assessment was not completed (not found).

title: Improve accuracy of target document after interval turnover
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Target documents have a monthly interval. Because target documents are not always written (max of once per day, and only when viewing targets tab) they can be stale.  When the interval ends, there is some "lazy best effort" to ensure that the previous interval's data is updated. 

The digital payment system relies on the data in the previous month's target document. This month, there was a lot of variance between the "ideal" result (what would actually be calculated by targets.js for the month) vs the "actual" data written to the target document (the result of this interval turnover).

This feature suggests improvements to target documents so at least the previous month's target document is guaranteed to be the result of some deterministic predictable calculation.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Can we recalculate all emissions during the interval turnover process before writing the values?
Can we run the interval turnover function even if the previous month's target document doesn't exist?
Or could we update the target document every time rules emissions are updated instead of daily when targets are viewed?
 
**Additional context**
Some scenarios
1.  Does activity on 24th of the month. Then views a different contact on 1st of next month without going to tasks tab. Their activity is not included in the target document.
2. User does activity on 30th of the month. Views the tasks tab. This will work great! Except user changes devices on the 1st of the month and interval turnover happens on the new device (actual scenario from telemetry)

title: Merge ensureTaskFreshness and  ensureTargetFreshness into single event
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
In `rules-engine.service.ts` there are two background events which trigger after 120seconds. One of these background events (ensureTaskFreshness) refreshes tasks, and the other (ensureTargetFreshness) refreshes targets.  

Under the covers, refreshing tasks and targets is mostly the work to `refreshRulesEmissionForContacts` + some minor task/target specific things. 

Can we avoid redundant calls to refreshRulesEmissionForContacts?

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Probably just a single call to new interface like `fetchAll` which writes task docs and target doc. Also, there is some evidence to suspect that this may be linked to an intermittent unreproduced functional bug: 

1. There are numerous reports of users who navigate to the analytics tab and intermittently experience all zeros.  
2. When analyzing a set of two users who have targetDocs in the erroneous state of having all 0s (not representative of correct target calculations), both user's telemetry docs had `rules-engine:ensureTargetFreshness:cancel` events their telemetry events the day the target doc was written.

So there are maybe some problems introduced by these async managed and _concurrent_ calls to `refreshRulesEmissionForContacts`.  Don't know how rules-engine handles multiple concurrent calls (?)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could remove these background threads completely since it isn't clear how they impact the user experience or freshness and it's somewhat risky&complex to do this kind of thing. Or we could reconsider when they happen - like it may be preferrable to run these after launching an enketo form; it is more likely no other heavy activity is happening then vs just a random 120seconds.

**Measurements**
Unknown

**Environment**
- App: webapp
- Version: 4.11 master

**Additional context**

title: Docker helper failing to run cht on later versions
body:
**Describe the bug**
We are not able to run docker-helper-4x on latest version of CHT as it fails to pull required images. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Run docker helper.
2. When prompted if you want to start new project, say yes. 
3. When prompted if you want to run latest version of CHT Core (4.10.0), say yes. 
4. Give your project a name. 
5. Wait for your project to fail. 

**Expected behavior**
Docker helper should successfully start the instance. 

**Logs**
<!-- If applicable, include the server or browser logs. -->

If you inspect the upgrade service logs, you would see that docker helper is unable to pull required manifests. 

This is the log I got from trying to start 4.10.0 instance:

body:

If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the bug**
For developers, the CHT allows to upgrade to new versions of the same branch. However these upgrades seem to become stalled after the new images are downloaded, and after API restart, because API can't tell that it needs to upgrade. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Made a branch. Install this branch with docker-compose and the docker upgrade service. (using docker is important)
2. Push a new change to the branch and wait until build is successful.
3. Upgrade to the same branch. 
4. After a while, you see that the upgrade page is stuck on "completing upgrade" but API is up and running. 

**Expected behavior**
Upgrade should complete after new images got downloaded. 

**Environment**
- App: api
- Version: 4.11

**Additional context**
Since this only applies to development, I'm marking this as low priority.

Release notes

Sourced from express's releases.

4.20.0

What's Changed

Important

  • IMPORTANT: The default depth level for parsing URL-encoded data is now 32 (previously was Infinity)
  • Remove link renderization in html while using res.redirect

New Contributors

  • @​mertcanaltin made their first contribution in expressjs/express#5627

4.21.0 / 2024-09-11

  • Deprecate res.location("back") and res.redirect("back") magic string
  • deps: serve-static@1.16.2
    • includes send@0.19.0
  • deps: finalhandler@1.3.1
  • deps: qs@6.13.0

4.20.0 / 2024-09-10

  • deps: serve-static@0.16.0
    • Remove link renderization in html while redirecting
  • deps: send@0.19.0
    • Remove link renderization in html while redirecting
  • deps: body-parser@0.6.0
    • add depth option to customize the depth level in the parser
    • IMPORTANT: The default depth level for parsing URL-encoded data is now 32 (previously was Infinity)
  • Remove link renderization in html while using res.redirect
  • deps: path-to-regexp@0.1.10
    • Adds support for named matching groups in the routes using a regex
    • Adds backtracking protection to parameters without regexes defined
  • deps: encodeurl@~2.0.0
    • Removes encoding of \, |, and ^ to align better with URL spec
  • Deprecate passing options.maxAge and options.expires to res.clearCookie
    • Will be ignored in v5, clearCookie will set a cookie with an expires in the past to instruct clients to delete the cookie

# Description

In the forums folks have [had issues](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/using-sudo-with-docker-helper-installing-tls-certs/3979/9?u=mrjones) getting TLS certs downloaded in docker helper.  This PR:
* updates [add cert script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/add-local-ip-certs-to-docker-4.x.sh) and [docker helper](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/docker-helper-4.x/cht-docker-compose.sh) to move the `curl` calls to be on `localhost` instead of inside `nginx` container.
* be extra defensive about `curl` calls to output user facing errors in case of DNS or `404` errors
* add an explicit check for valid TLS after we install the cert
* unchanged: we re-install the cert every time clean
* updates docs URLs to not be redirects

Closes  #9485 

## Testing
* test on a new install of CHT `4.10` in docker helper - ensure valid cert
* on the instance you just created, use the [add cert script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/add-local-ip-certs-to-docker-4.x.sh) to install a self signed cert and re-install  - ensure valid cert
* on an existing docker helper instance created not in this branch - re-run docker helper  - ensure valid cert

This is is what it looks like when TLS installation fails.  This was achieved by [changing the local-ip cert](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/57f8ed2b7672f334fbf125b015570de4d4b489a8/scripts/docker-helper-4.x/cht-docker-compose.sh#L274) to be a `404` URL

title: Release 4.12.0
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [ ] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [ ] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [ ] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo.
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Checkout to a new `<issue>-update-version` branch (eg: `1234-update-version`) and set the version number in the `package.json` and `package-lock.json`. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`. Once the version is updated, submit a PR to `master` branch.
- [x] Ensure that issues associated with commits merged to `master` since the last release are closed and mapped to the milestone.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once the PR has been merged into `master`, and the `master` branch has the new version number, then the release process can start:

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development Slack channel using this template:
```
@channel I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by creating a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`) and then push the created tag.
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the team by writing a message in the #development Slack channel:
```
@channel, I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag. 
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make. 
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [x] The beta tag will automatically trigger the scalability build. Once it passes, download the scalability results on S3 at medic-e2e/scalability/$TAG_NAME. If you do not have access to the scalability results ask someone in the #product-team who has access. Add the release `.json` file to `cht-core/tests/scalability/previous_results`. More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [x] Go to the [Issues tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues) and filter the issues with `is:issue label:"Affects: 4.x.x" ` , replace `4.x.x` with the previous version number. Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label.  
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labelled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [x] Collect known migration steps, descriptions, screenshots, videos, data, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. This information should already be on the issue, but if not, prompt the change author to provide it.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions) and update the EOL date of the previous release. Update the status of any releases that are past their End Of Life date. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page.
- [x] Create a [new release](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases/new) in GitHub, with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, from the release branch created above as the target branch. Click on the "Choose a tag" dropdown and create a tag for the release with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. Ensure the release notes PR from above are merged. Add a link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Once you publish the release, confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Upgrade the [demo](https://demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org/) instance to the newly released version.
- [x] Use cht-conf to upload the configuration from the `cht-core/config/demo` folder to the `demo-cht.dev` server.
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*We're excited to announce the release of {{version}} of {{product}}*

See below for some highlights, read the [release notes]({{<paste-url>}}) for full details.

Following our support policy, versions {{versions}} are no longer supported. Projects running these versions should start planning to upgrade in the near future. For more details read our [software support documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions).

Check out our [roadmap](https://github.com/orgs/medic/projects/112/views/21) to see what else is currently being working on.

## {{version}} Highlights

### [{{Highlight 1}}]({{<paste-url to section>}})

{{description of highlight section}}

### ### [{{Highlight 2}}]({{<paste-url to section>}})

{{description of highlight section}}

### [And more...]({{paste-url to section}})

We’ve also implemented loads of other improvements and fixed a heap of bugs.

```
- [x] Add one last update to the #product-team Slack channel and use the thread to lead an internal release retrospective covering what went well and areas to improve for next time.
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Remove "version" from compose files
body:
**Describe the issue**
Per the [compose spec](https://github.com/compose-spec/compose-spec/blob/main/04-version-and-name.md):

> The top-level version property is defined by the Compose Specification for backward compatibility. It is only informative you'll receive a warning message that it is obsolete if used.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We should remove `Version:` from the top of the compose files

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
leave it until compose gives a fatal error and fix it then.

Bumps [express](https://github.com/expressjs/express) from 4.19.2 to 4.21.0.
Release notes

Sourced from express's releases.

4.21.0

What's Changed

  • Deprecate "back" magic string in redirects by @​blakeembrey in expressjs/express#5935
  • finalhandler@1.3.1 by @​wesleytodd in expressjs/express#5954
  • fix(deps): serve-static@1.16.2 by @​wesleytodd in expressjs/express#5951
  • Upgraded dependency qs to 6.13.0 to match qs in body-parser by @​agadzinski93 in expressjs/express#5946

New Contributors

  • @​agadzinski93 made their first contribution in expressjs/express#5946

Full Changelog: https://github.com/expressjs/express/compare/4.20.0...4.21.0

4.20.0

What's Changed

Important

  • IMPORTANT: The default depth level for parsing URL-encoded data is now 32 (previously was Infinity)
  • Remove link renderization in html while using res.redirect

Other Changes

  • 4.19.2 Staging by @​wesleytodd in expressjs/express#5561
  • remove duplicate location test for data uri by @​wesleytodd in expressjs/express#5562
  • feat: document beta releases expectations by @​marco-ippolito in expressjs/express#5565
  • Cut down on duplicated CI runs by @​jonchurch in expressjs/express#5564
  • Add a Threat Model by @​UlisesGascon in expressjs/express#5526
  • Assign captain of encodeurl by @​blakeembrey in expressjs/express#5579
  • Nominate jonchurch as repo captain for http-errors, expressjs.com, morgan, cors, body-parser by @​jonchurch in expressjs/express#5587
  • docs: update Security.md by @​inigomarquinez in expressjs/express#5590
  • docs: update triage nomination policy by @​UlisesGascon in expressjs/express#5600
  • Add CodeQL (SAST) by @​UlisesGascon in expressjs/express#5433
  • docs: add UlisesGascon as triage initiative captain by @​UlisesGascon in expressjs/express#5605
  • deps: encodeurl@~2.0.0 by @​blakeembrey in expressjs/express#5569
  • skip QUERY method test by @​jonchurch in expressjs/express#5628
  • ignore ETAG query test on 21 and 22, reuse skip util by @​jonchurch in expressjs/express#5639
  • add support Node.js@22 in the CI by @​mertcanaltin in expressjs/express#5627
  • doc: add table of contents, tc/triager lists to readme by @​mertcanaltin in expressjs/express#5619
  • List and sort all projects, add captains by @​blakeembrey in expressjs/express#5653
  • docs: add @​UlisesGascon as captain for cookie-parser by @​UlisesGascon in expressjs/express#5666
  • ✨ bring back query tests for node 21 by @​ctcpip in expressjs/express#5690
  • [v4] Deprecate res.clearCookie accepting options.maxAge and options.expires by @​jonchurch in expressjs/express#5672
  • skip QUERY tests for Node 21 only, still not supported by @​jonchurch in expressjs/express#5695
  • 📝 update people, add ctcpip to TC by @​ctcpip in expressjs/express#5683
  • remove minor version pinning from ci by @​jonchurch in expressjs/express#5722
  • Fix link variable use in attribution section of CODE OF CONDUCT by @​IamLizu in expressjs/express#5762
  • Replace Appveyor windows testing with GHA by @​jonchurch in expressjs/express#5599
  • Add OSSF Scorecard badge by @​UlisesGascon in expressjs/express#5436
  • update scorecard link by @​bjohansebas in expressjs/express#5814
  • Nominate @​IamLizu to the triage team by @​UlisesGascon in expressjs/express#5836
  • deps: path-to-regexp@0.1.8 by @​blakeembrey in expressjs/express#5603

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from express's changelog.

4.21.0 / 2024-09-11

  • Deprecate res.location("back") and res.redirect("back") magic string
  • deps: serve-static@1.16.2
    • includes send@0.19.0
  • deps: finalhandler@1.3.1
  • deps: qs@6.13.0

4.20.0 / 2024-09-10

  • deps: serve-static@0.16.0
    • Remove link renderization in html while redirecting
  • deps: send@0.19.0
    • Remove link renderization in html while redirecting
  • deps: body-parser@0.6.0
    • add depth option to customize the depth level in the parser
    • IMPORTANT: The default depth level for parsing URL-encoded data is now 32 (previously was Infinity)
  • Remove link renderization in html while using res.redirect
  • deps: path-to-regexp@0.1.10
    • Adds support for named matching groups in the routes using a regex
    • Adds backtracking protection to parameters without regexes defined
  • deps: encodeurl@~2.0.0
    • Removes encoding of \, |, and ^ to align better with URL spec
  • Deprecate passing options.maxAge and options.expires to res.clearCookie
    • Will be ignored in v5, clearCookie will set a cookie with an expires in the past to instruct clients to delete the cookie

title: Improve Sidebar Menu's button and label placement
body:
**Describe the issue**
During exploration testing we got 2 feedback for improving the Sidebar Menu. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
1.. It would be nice to be able to close the hamburger menu from the same position without having to move the cursor to the left. 
 - Make the clickable area of the close icon bigger, that way, we don't need to change the alignment of the close icon and other icons in the sidebar. 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/752aa77f-b94f-47e2-917b-751b486829b3

2.. When I chose Bamanankan (Bambara) , on Desktop, the word for messages is too long, and it needs to be cut. I think it is great that nav bar still looks the same, but I was wondering if it ok to cut the work/phrase?
  - Maybe wrap the label to second line and also add ellipsis if it still doesn't fit on second line (we do this with breadcrumbs) 
  
![image (4)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f61cad5c-90a9-4c50-8b5e-4f19aae37589)

title: Add telemetry for offline freetext searching
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

During our research for https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9293 it has become clear that we currently cannot make any changes to the offline freetext search experience without potentially affecting user workflows because we simply have no way to be sure how users are actually interacting with the freetext search (for both contacts and reports).

For example, in interviews with users, they mention searching by contact name.  However, in practice we know that contact names are often de-normalized into various custom fields on both contacts and reports.  So, simply indexing the `name` fields on contacts may not be enough to support user workflows.  Most importantly, we just do not have any way to know the answer here one way or the other.  The users, themselves, are probably not aware of the exact field structure on the documents they are searching for.  

**Describe the solution you'd like**

One reason we are not currently collecting any search telemetry data is because it is likely that the search terms provided by the user will contain PII and we want to avoid logging PII in telemetry docs.

The proposal here is to add telemetry that is more holistically focused on _the search workflow_.  Instead of merely logging what terms the user searches for, we want to focus on the whole process whereby a user searches for something _and then actually selects ones of the filtered reports/contacts._  Once a user chooses a report/contact to navigate to, we do a comparison between the contents of the report/contact with the user's search term and find the _doc fields_ that were matched by the search query.  Then we can log telemetry indicating a search happened (but do not  include the exact search terms).  Instead we can include information about the report/contact that the user ended up selecting and espeically _the names of the doc fields that were matched by the search query_.  In this way, we avoid including PII in the telemetry, but can still construct an (imperfect) image of the kinds of things users are searching for....

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Not collecting any telemetry means that any changes we make to offline freetext search functionality will be done without any way of realistically quantifying their impact.

OTOH, if we log PII in telemetry, it would make it more difficult to collect telemetry data from partners.  Extra care must be taken when storing/transmitting this kind of info.

title: e2e tests should fail gracefully if the ports are not available (or find a new port)
body:
**Describe the issue** The e2e tests use docker compose to spin up the CHT containers to run the tests against. The nginx container tries to bind to the default ports `80/443` and the e2e tests running on the host machine will communicate with the containers via these ports. However, if those ports are not available (e.g. something else like the https://github.com/medic/nginx-local-ip service is already bound to them) the nginx container will fail to start. The way this gets presented to the end user (when running `npm run wdio-local`) is very confusion, though (as noted in https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/9422). The tests start the containers in the background and then poll until the api server is available. But if the nginx container fails to start the e2e tests will just continue polling forever with the error: ``` Checking API API check failed, trying again in 1 second 502 - "\r\n502 Bad Gateway\r\n\r\n

502 Bad Gateway

\r\n
nginx/1.19.10
\r\n\r\n\r\n" ``` **Describe the improvement you'd like** One solution would be to simple end the e2e test run (with a helpful error message) if any of the docker containers fail to start. Alternatively, I do not think there is any hard requirement that the e2e tests use `80/443`. Instead it seems like we might be able to use custom ports that we determine at runtime are available.

We want to add screenshot-generator tests for the Messages page. This will help us update the [Messaging overview section in the Docs site](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/messaging/overview/) with consistent and up-to-date UI images.

This work is part of the [UI screenshots generation initiative](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22project%3A%20Screenshots%22), where we generate screenshots under known configurations to help document what users see in the app.

💡 **Note:** These tests are only meant to generate screenshots. They are not yet used for visual comparison or automated visual testing. This will be a future effort.

This issue will cover the images for the [Messaging Overview](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/messaging/overview/) page.

▶️ How to run your test?
- Modify the suite property of [wdio.conf.js](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/b58c1a7de95577fa92a75397742bd3d412007106/tests/e2e/visual/wdio.conf.js#L30) so it only finds your test.
- For desktop use the [wdio-visual-desktop script ](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/b58c1a7de95577fa92a75397742bd3d412007106/package.json#L56C6-L56C25), running `npm run wdio-visual-desktop`
- For mobile use the  [wdio-visual-mobile script ](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/b58c1a7de95577fa92a75397742bd3d412007106/package.json#L57) , running `npm run wdio-visual-mobile`
- If you are also running the test for mobile, consider that you must be careful with mobile selectors if they differ from the desktop.
- When you are happy with the screenshots generated, share them on a public drive.

📁 Where to add the test?
- Add your tests in: [tests/e2e/visual/](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/tests/e2e/visual)
- You can create a new folder called `messages`
- You can organize the tests in different .`wdio-spec.js` files as you see fit. 
- You can use the files in [tests/e2e/visual/contacts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/tests/e2e/visual/contacts) as an example. 

🧱 Implementation Notes
- You might need to add some configurations to get the desired thing to show in messages. Please read the complete [Messaging](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/messaging/) section to know how to configure it so you can send messages. 

🧠 Why is this a good first issue?
- You’ll get hands-on experience writing a real WebdriverIO test.
- You’ll learn how to work with the CHT’s visual testing structure.
- You'll learn about [Users](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/concepts/users/), [Messages](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/messaging/) and [Gateways](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/messaging/gateways/) in the CHT.
- Your contribution will improve the experience for everyone viewing our documentation.
- Your contribution will be the foundation for future automated visual testing in the CHT.

🧭 Important References
[First Time Contributors Guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/community/contributing/first-time-contributors/)
[Development Workflow](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/) 
[Coding Style Guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/style-guide/) 
[Automated Tests - E2E](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/core/automated-tests/#e2e-tests)
[Style Guide for Automated tests](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/core/style-guide-automated-e2e-tests/)

title: UI Navigation: Screenshot Generation for Reports Section
body:
We want to add screenshot-generator tests for the Reports page. This will help us update the [Reports section in the Docs site](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/features/reports/) with consistent and up-to-date UI images.

This work is part of the [UI screenshots generation initiative](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22project%3A%20Screenshots%22), where we generate screenshots under known configurations to help document what users see in the app.

💡 **Note:** These tests are only meant to generate screenshots. They are not yet used for visual comparison or automated visual testing. This will be a future effort.

This issue will cover the images for [Reports](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/features/reports/) page.
To ensure smooth collaboration and avoid overlapping work:
👉 Please claim and work on only one sub-issue at a time. You can find the sub-issues below.
Once you've finished and submitted a PR for your sub-issue, feel free to pick another that's still available.

🧪 What’s the task?
_Using as an example Report list - mobile & desktop view_ 
Create a test that:
- Create reports and a user before the test starts
- Logs in as the user with access to the Reports tab
- Navigate to the Reports page
- Waits for the reports list to load fully
- Using the [generateScreenshot](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/b58c1a7de95577fa92a75397742bd3d412007106/tests/utils/screenshots.js#L45) method from [screenshots.js](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/utils/screenshots.js) utils, takes a screenshot and saves it with a meaningful filename (for example [this](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/b58c1a7de95577fa92a75397742bd3d412007106/tests/e2e/visual/contacts/list-view-login-visual.wdio-spec.js#L42C11-L42C29) one)

▶️ How to run your test?
- Modify the suite property of [wdio.conf.js](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/b58c1a7de95577fa92a75397742bd3d412007106/tests/e2e/visual/wdio.conf.js#L30) so it only finds your test. (⚠️ Please be careful not to commit this change, this is only to isolate your test when running locally)
- For desktop use the [wdio-visual-desktop script ](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/b58c1a7de95577fa92a75397742bd3d412007106/package.json#L56C6-L56C25), running `npm run wdio-visual-desktop`
- For mobile use the  [wdio-visual-mobile script ](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/b58c1a7de95577fa92a75397742bd3d412007106/package.json#L57) , running `npm run wdio-visual-mobile`
- If you are also running the test for mobile, consider that you must be careful with mobile selectors if they differ from the desktop.
- When you are happy with the screenshots generated, share them on a public drive.

📁 Where to add the test?
- Add your tests in: [tests/e2e/visual/](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/tests/e2e/visual)
- You can create a new folder called reports
- You can organize the tests in different .`wdio-spec.js` files as you see fit. 
- You can use the files in [tests/e2e/visual/contacts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/tests/e2e/visual/contacts) as an example. 

🧱 Implementation Notes
- You might need to add some specific configurations or forms to get the desired thing to show in reports.
- You can look at how the [tests/e2e/visual/contacts/forms](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/tests/e2e/visual/contacts/forms) is used in the tests to see how this can be done.

🧠 Why is this a good first issue?
- You’ll get hands-on experience writing a real WebdriverIO test.
- You’ll learn how to work with the CHT’s visual testing structure.
- You'll learn about [Users](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/concepts/users/), [Reports](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/features/reports/) and [Forms](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/forms/) in the CHT.
- Your contribution will improve the experience for everyone viewing our documentation.
- Your contribution will be the foundation for future automated visual testing in the CHT.

body:
**Describe the issue**
Following the work initiated in [#8159](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8159), we need to continue adjusting the end-to-end (e2e) tests to ensure compatibility with the minimum supported browser version, Chrome 90.

This issue addresses explicitly:
Ensuring that all tests in the default `workflow` suite are functioning as expected in this browser version.

body:

If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the bug**
The sidebar menu stays open when trying to access the same page as the one that is currently opened. This is really confusing, especially since the sidebar menu obscures the current page title, so you're not actually aware of what is happening. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Open sidebar menu. 
2. Go to the about page. 
3. Open sidebar menu and click the about page again. 
4. Nothing happens, sidebar menu is still visible and you don't see that you're actually already on the about page. 

**Expected behavior**
Sidebar menu should close regardless of the link clicked. 

**Screenshots**
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/439937cc-2aa2-4ccb-b4ee-73c1d8f64fca)


**Environment**
- App: Webapp
- Version: 4.12

title: chore: bump webpack from 5.90.3 to 5.95.0
body:
Bumps [webpack](https://github.com/webpack/webpack) from 5.90.3 to 5.95.0.
Release notes

Sourced from webpack's releases.

v5.95.0

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed hanging when attempting to read a symlink-like file that it can't read
  • Handle default for import context element dependency
  • Merge duplicate chunks call after split chunks
  • Generate correctly code for dynamically importing the same file twice and destructuring
  • Use content hash as [base] and [name] for extracted DataURI's
  • Distinguish module and import in module-import for externals import's
  • [Types] Make EnvironmentPlugin default values types less strict
  • [Types] Typescript 5.6 compatibility

New Features

  • Add new optimization.avoidEntryIife option (true by default for the production mode)
  • Pass output.hash* options to loader context

Performance

  • Avoid unneeded re-visit in build chunk graph

v5.94.0

Bug Fixes

  • Added runtime condition for harmony reexport checked
  • Handle properly data/http/https protocols in source maps
  • Make bigint optimistic when browserslist not found
  • Move @​types/eslint-scope to dev deps
  • Related in asset stats is now always an array when no related found
  • Handle ASI for export declarations
  • Mangle destruction incorrect with export named default properly
  • Fixed unexpected asi generation with sequence expression
  • Fixed a lot of types

New Features

  • Added new external type "module-import"
  • Support webpackIgnore for new URL() construction
  • [CSS] @import pathinfo support

Security

  • Fixed DOM clobbering in auto public path

v5.93.0

Bug Fixes

  • Generate correct relative path to runtime chunks
  • Makes DefinePlugin quieter under default log level
  • Fixed mangle destructuring default in namespace import

title: Release 4.13.0
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [ ] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [ ] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo.
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Checkout to a new `<issue>-update-version` branch (eg: `1234-update-version`) and set the version number in the `package.json` and `package-lock.json`. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`. Once the version is updated, submit a PR to `master` branch.
- [x] Ensure that issues associated with commits merged to `master` since the last release are closed and mapped to the milestone.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once the PR has been merged into `master`, and the `master` branch has the new version number, then the release process can start:

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development Slack channel using this template:
```
@channel I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by creating a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`) and then push the created tag.
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the team by writing a message in the #development Slack channel:
```
@channel, I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag. 
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make. 
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [ ] The beta tag will automatically trigger the scalability build. Once it passes, download the scalability results on S3 at medic-e2e/scalability/$TAG_NAME. If you do not have access to the scalability results ask someone in the #product-team who has access. Add the release `.json` file to `cht-core/tests/scalability/previous_results`. More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [x] Go to the [Issues tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues) and filter the issues with `is:issue label:"Affects: 4.x.x" ` , replace `4.x.x` with the previous version number. Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label.  
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labelled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [x] Collect known migration steps, descriptions, screenshots, videos, data, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. This information should already be on the issue, but if not, prompt the change author to provide it.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions) and update the EOL date of the previous release. Update the status of any releases that are past their End Of Life date. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page.
- [x] Create a [new release](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases/new) in GitHub, with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, from the release branch created above as the target branch. Click on the "Choose a tag" dropdown and create a tag for the release with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. Ensure the release notes PR from above are merged. Add a link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Once you publish the release, confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Upgrade the [demo](https://demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org/) instance to the newly released version.
- [x] Use cht-conf to upload the configuration from the `cht-core/config/demo` folder to the `demo-cht.dev` server.
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*We're excited to announce the release of {{version}} of {{product}}*

See below for some highlights, read the [release notes]({{<paste-url>}}) for full details.

Following our support policy, versions {{versions}} are no longer supported. Projects running these versions should start planning to upgrade in the near future. For more details read our [software support documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions).

Check out our [roadmap](https://github.com/orgs/medic/projects/112/views/21) to see what else is currently being working on.

## {{version}} Highlights

### [{{Highlight 1}}]({{<paste-url to section>}})

{{description of highlight section}}

### ### [{{Highlight 2}}]({{<paste-url to section>}})

{{description of highlight section}}

### [And more...]({{paste-url to section}})

We’ve also implemented loads of other improvements and fixed a heap of bugs.

```
- [x] Add one last update to the #product-team Slack channel and use the thread to lead an internal release retrospective covering what went well and areas to improve for next time.
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: feat(#9489): collect telemetry for offline freetext searching
body:
# Description

#9489 

This PR adds telemetry collection for searches without storing any PII/PHI by storing only the properties that matched against the query.
It would have been more straightforward to edit the views and make it emit the property that matched but that meant re-indexing `medic-client` for 0 immediate benefit to the end users. So instead I hooked into webapp code to record a telemetry entry after the user selected a contact/report from the search results.

title: API logs error when privacy policies doc contains no privacy policies
body:
**Describe the bug**
When the privacy policies doc lacks the `privacy_policies` property, API logs an error. However this error is not critical and does not inform the user of what they should do. 
An empty privacy policies doc can come from an incomplete, but not incorrect configuration. 

This creates noise and confusion, and gets reported as the reason why API crashed. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. In your config folder, create a `privacy-policies.json` file, but leave it empty. 
2. Upload thid config. 
3. Relaunch API. 
4. See error

**Expected behavior**
This should be logged as a warning, or inform the user on what to do. 

**Logs**
```
2024-10-11T08:30:29.645 ERROR: Error retrieving privacy policies: Error: Invalid privacy-policies doc: missing required "privacy_policies" property
    at /service/api/src/services/privacy-policy.js:25:15

- Version: 4.0.0

title: chore: bump express from 4.19.2 to 4.21.1
body:
Bumps [express](https://github.com/expressjs/express) from 4.19.2 to 4.21.1.
Release notes

Sourced from express's releases.

4.21.1

What's Changed

  • Backport a fix for CVE-2024-47764 to the 4.x branch by @​joshbuker in expressjs/express#6029
  • Release: 4.21.1 by @​UlisesGascon in expressjs/express#6031

Full Changelog: https://github.com/expressjs/express/compare/4.21.0...4.21.1

4.21.0

What's Changed

  • Deprecate "back" magic string in redirects by @​blakeembrey in expressjs/express#5935
  • finalhandler@1.3.1 by @​wesleytodd in expressjs/express#5954
  • fix(deps): serve-static@1.16.2 by @​wesleytodd in expressjs/express#5951
  • Upgraded dependency qs to 6.13.0 to match qs in body-parser by @​agadzinski93 in expressjs/express#5946

New Contributors

  • @​agadzinski93 made their first contribution in expressjs/express#5946

Full Changelog: https://github.com/expressjs/express/compare/4.20.0...4.21.0

4.20.0

What's Changed

Important

  • IMPORTANT: The default depth level for parsing URL-encoded data is now 32 (previously was Infinity)

title: Upgrade to latest version of PouchDB (current adapter)
body:
**Describe the issue**
PouchDB recently released v9.X, upgrade CHT's PouchDB from v7.x to 9.x.

title: Create minimal GET Patient Endpoint for a FHIR API
body:
**Describe the solution you'd like**
Create a simple FHIR endpoint that returns a patient record given its ID.

{base_url}/api/fhir/v1/patient/{patient_id}/

and returns a valid patient FHIR

For this issue, ignore FHIR boilerplate including pagination, querying by attributes other than id, capability statements, etc..

include
- [ ] ability to configure which documents are patients
- [ ] mapping the required fields for FHIR patients from a document where they may have different names
- [ ] name (in FHIR format)
- [ ] sex
- [ ] date of birth
- [ ] phone

title: Minimal FHIR Facade
body:
**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add boilerplate for a FHIR API in CHT Core
Using version 5.0.0 [R5](https://hl7.org/fhir/R5) 
See the FHIR standard for [resource](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/resource.html)
The FHIR standard for a [REST API](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/http.html)
And the FHIR standard for [security](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/security.html)

Not everything in those standards will be possible or desirable for CHT core to implement.

A minimal implementation should include the following from the [REST API](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/http.html)
- [ ] Authentication with HTTP Basic Authentication
- [ ] [read](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/http.html#read) (for all types supported)
- [ ] [search](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/http.html#search) (for all types supported)
- [ ] [capabilities](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/http.html#capabilities)

This requires 
- [ ] [pagination](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/http.html#capabilities)
- [ ] [filters](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/resource.html) (as much as possible, not everything will be)
- [ ] [metadata](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/resource.html#Meta) (as much as possible, not all attributes will be available)
- [ ] [conformance](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/conformance-rules.html) layer including auto-generated [capability statements](http://hl7.org/fhir/capabilitystatement.html) 

Notable items to EXCLUDE from the first version

- updating and creating resources
- authorization (for now assume a system user with access to everything)
- OAuth (basic authentication is fine for now)
- [references between relationships](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/references.html)

There are some node [FHIR servers](https://github.com/bluehalo/node-fhir-server-core) existing, and some functionality may overlap with cht-datasource.
Part of this issue will be investigating these solutions and see what can be used or re-used, and what should be implemented from scratch

title: Investigate adding more shards for increased performance for single node deployments
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
Checking an additional path for options for vertically scaling a CHT instance by adding more cores and using a single node CouchDb, since certain processes (like view indexing) are limited by shard count.  
We have not seen an obvious performance improvement when vertically scaling single node couchdb without adding multiple shards. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Check whether doubling shard count and doubling CPU count increases performance when querying while documents are pushed to the instance. 

**Measurements**
TBD.

title: feat(#9857): implement CouchDB Nouveau
body:
# Description

Closes #9857

Adds Nouveau indexes for freetext contact/report searching.  Updates `shared-libs/search` to call Nouveau indexes or offline freetext views.

## Usage

### Building locally

You need to build/run the new Couch+Nouveau images for your local Couch instance.

- `npm run local-images`
- Put this into `./local-build/cht-couchdb-override.yml`: 
	```yaml
	services:
	  couchdb:
	    ports:
	      - "5984:5984"
	      - "5986:5986"
	```
- `COUCHDB_USER=admin COUCHDB_PASSWORD=pass docker compose -f ./local-build/cht-couchdb.yml -f ./local-build/cht-couchdb-override.yml up -d`

Once Couch/Nouveau are running, start the api server (`npm run dev-api`) to deploy the updated design docs.

### Querying

Query the indexes like so:

#### contacts by freetext:

The `sort_order` field ensures the order of the returned hits matches the original freetext view.

```
POST {{url}}/medic/_design/medic/_nouveau/contacts_by_freetext
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "q":malcolm*",
  "sort":"sort_order"
}
```

#### contacts by type freetext

Uses the `contact_type` facet to only return hits for the given contact type.

```
POST {{url}}/medic/_design/medic/_nouveau/contacts_by_freetext
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "q":"contact_type:\"person\" AND malcolm*",
  "sort":"sort_order"
}
```

#### reports by freetext

Sorted by the `reported_date` to match the original freetext view.

```
POST {{url}}/medic/_design/medic/_nouveau/reports_by_freetext
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "q":"malcolm*",
  "sort":"reported_date"
}
```

#### key:value query

Use the `exact_match` field to ensure the query only resolves on an exact match.  By default Nouveau will do an "includes" match even when targeting a specific field.

```
POST {{url}}/medic/_design/medic/_nouveau/contacts_by_freetext
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "q":"exact_match:\"name:malcolm\"",
  "sort":"sort_order"
}
```

title: Reduce disk space with CouchDB Nouveau (TCO v1)
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Reduce total disk space that CHT takes up, thus reduce the total cost of ownership  (TCO)

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Use [Nouveau search](https://docs.couchdb.org/en/stable/ddocs/nouveau.html) instead of existing CouchDB search

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
[refactoring/removing freetext views](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9293#issuecomment-2412188631)

**Additional context**
We should answer how viable it will be to use CouchDB's [Nouveau search](https://docs.couchdb.org/en/stable/ddocs/nouveau.html) to both improve search but to also reduce disk use of the indexes. This should include, but not be limited to:
* how fast is it to index?  
* how hard will it be to bifurcate offline search using the old view from online search using this new search
* how hard will it be to package up and maintain the java file which powers Nouveau
* how hard will it be to measure database  disk use?
* how hard will it be to upgrade the index?
* how much disk savings do we see? 
* what else are we forgetting?

title: Make freetext search view indexes "offline only"
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
If we move to Nouveau for freetext searching on the Couch server (aka "online" use), then we still need a solution for freetext searching "offline" (what offline users would experience via their local Pouch instance).  

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The most straightforward approach should be to just have a design doc that is "client-only" similar to how we have docs that are currently "server-only".  This design doc will be indexed by PouchDB clients, but will not be indexed by the Couch server.  

Since we are likely going to require a complete re-indexing of these views on the client devices one way or the other, we should take this opportunity to remove the unused `key:value` emissions from the freetext views [as originally proposed](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9293) for the "freetext-lite" views. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
One interesting alternative would come [after our upgrade to Pouch `9`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9208) and the `indexeddb` adapter.  IIRC, Mango queries should be more performance on Pouch with `indexeddb`. If that is the case, then we could evaluate possibly using Mango queries for freetext searching.  [This one blog post](https://reintech.io/blog/efficient-full-text-search-couchdb-mango-queries) suggests it works well... 😅

title: Change password on first login
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
System admin users create accounts for CHWs and then share the password with them. To enhance the security of these accounts, there should be a way to prompt a password change on the first login. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
On the login page, create a feature to change the password with the following considerations: 
- All UI texts should be translatable in CHT's supported languages
- This feature is enabled by default but it can be disabled for user roles based on the `can_skip_password_change` permission
- Only new users will be prompted to change their password on the first login when the permission is enabled.
- Subsequent logins won't require a password change. 
- Users will be prompted to change their password on their next login when the admin manually updates the user password 
- Changing the password in this step is an online action (they need internet)
- If the CHW can't change the password for some reason, they can't access the app
- If CHW logins for first login and closes the app before changing password, the next time they login (even though it is not technically first login) they are prompted to change password.

[Figma design](https://www.figma.com/design/3S7e2khzFNkdT7PLlf153H/Cybersecurity?node-id=202-92&node-type=canvas&t=J1kyJfBTdPxJmCUP-0)

The scope of this work is to enable changing the password on the first login. It doesn't include changing the password rules or current authentication mechanisms.
