# Planning - CHT Community 

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [x] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo.
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label.

Update the status of any releases that are past their End Of Life date. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page.

title: Refactor to use `cht-datasource` for reading contacts by id (both with and without lineage)
body:
## Ticket Contents

Throughout much of the cht-core code-base contact (persons/places) documents are read directly from the database via the [PouchDB library](https://pouchdb.com/). Persons/places exist within a particular hierarchy (places can belong to other places, people can belong to places).  Contact docs in the database will reference their associated lineage _by `_id`_, but the complete data of the lineage (e.g. the ancestor contacts) are not de-normalized into each document.  However, within the application logic there is often a need for this de-normalized contact data.  The [`shared-libs/lineage` library](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/shared-libs/lineage) supports some a number of ui-focused workflows around loading and structuring this contact/report data along with lineage information.

More recently, the [`cht-datasource` library](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/shared-libs/cht-datasource) has been introduced as a general purpose library for interacting with contact/report data (instead of having to load it straight from Pouch).  `cht-datasource` includes support for loading a contact along with their lineage data.

We need to streamline and centralize all our logic for reading contacts _by id_ so that it goes through `cht-datasource`.  When possible, code that is currently using `shared-libs/lineage` should be refactored to use `cht-datasource` directly.  Any code logic that remains used in `shared-libs/lineage` (presumably because it is supporting some common ui-workflow) should be refactored to itself use `cht-datasource` instead of directly calling Pouch.

## Goals

- [ ] Update code that is loading contacts _by id_ directly from Pouch to use cht-datasource to load the contact data instead
- [ ] Refactor code that is loading contacts via `shared-libs/lineage` to use cht-datasource when possible (additional common logic around structuring the contact data should remain in `shared-libs/lineage`)
- [ ] Update `shared-libs/lineage` to use cht-datasource to load contact data
- [ ] Implement any additional necessary contact read APIs in cht-datasource

## Expected Outcome

The end result is that all contact-by-id reads in cht-core will be done via the cht-datasource library and any unnecessary/unused logic is removed from shared-libs/lineage.

## Implementation Details

[Technical Design Doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1EdAm_G2m_99IOLhUWamYzDMD73wWGiktNSZDcif2B04/edit?tab=t.0)

One important note is that in addition to loading it _by id_, contact data can also be loaded as the result of various view queries.  It is out of the scope of this issue to replace these view queries.  This issue is focused on updating the code associated with loading contact data directly _by id_.

title: Use latest bikram-sambat release (1.8.0)
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Update to latest `bikram-sambat` version (1.8.0)

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We use [`bikram-sambat`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bikram-sambat) and [`bikram-sambat-bootstrap`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bikram-sambat-bootstrap) packages to convert dates between Gregorian and Bikram Sambat. Recently, a new version of `bikram-sambat` has been released that [fixes some incorrect days](https://github.com/medic/bikram-sambat/pull/27). We need to use them so that CHT users do not get the wrong dates in the UI and the data.

title: Add support for cht-form for using extension-libs in forms
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**

https://github.com/medic/cht-conf-test-harness/issues/275

The cht-form web component currently does not support using `extension-libs` in the loaded forms (as detailed by the linked harness issue).

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We should add the ability to inject extension-lib functions that can be used from within the forms.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Alternative approaches:

- Just stub out the extension-lib functionality so that a default value (e.g. empty string) is always returned
- Support mocking answers to extension-lib calls from within the forms (e.g. to return pre-injected answers)

While these approaches may be more convenient in some situations (e.g. unit testing forms with the test-harness), I think that the cht-form code should be as generic as possible. If we just allow injecting extension functions, then consumers of cht-form (like the test-harness) can build whatever kinds of abstractions they need on top.

title: Duplication in outbound push
body:
<!--
**Important**: This is a public repository. Anyone in the world can see what's posted here. If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the bug**
When configuring more than one out bound pushes without a cron configuration eg obp1 and obp2 the second configuration (obp2) will be pushed twice. Once immediately and another after about 5 mins

**To Reproduce**
- create out bound push with atleast 2 configurations to 2 target end points eg `push-target1` and `push-target2`
- Configure both outbound pushes to be triggered by the same form type i.e `relevant_to: doc.form === malaria_screening`
- Leave the  "cron" empty so pushes occur immediately as soon as the report is submitted
- Login as a user and submit the sample form (malaria_screening)
- Outbound push will push records to both `push-target1` and `push-target2` and create another  task:outbound for `push-target2`
- After about 5 mins the push-target2 task will be executed and the same payload will be pushed to target2 again 
**Expected behavior**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen. -->
- Target2 task shouldnt be created as it causes payload to be pushed twice

**Logs**
<!-- If applicable, include the server or browser logs. -->

**Screenshots**
<!-- If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem. -->

**Environment**
- Instance: dev instance on v4.9.0, local environment with v4.18.0
- Browser: Firefox and Chrome
- Client platform: Linux
- Version: 4.9.0 and the latest code 4.18.0

**Additional context**
<!-- Add any other context about the problem here. What have you tried? Is there a workaround? -->

# Description
When two out bound pushes running against the same document (same doc id) there is an uncaught error as shown below while writing to the sentinel info doc that leads to duplication in the push.

while looping thru the outbound keys eg push-1 and push-2, 
push-1 will successfully write the info doc for the report
when it get to push-2 it attempts to `put` the info doc but runs into a conflict error
This will lead to creation of an unnecessary task:outbound which leads to push-2 being pushed again.

title: Add server-check that verifies that the system is using the CHT version of CouchDb
body:
**Describe the issue**
The CHT API will start even when it runs with an incompatible version of CouchDb, for example the default CouchDb image. There are a number of CouchDb configs that we know are incompatible with the CHT (multi replica, other js engines, etc - this is a non-exhaustive list). 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Add a server-check that verifies the version of CouchDb that is running, to make sure that we're on the correct version. I believe that we also need to add some sort of endpoint to the CouchDb image that returns the actual version, and compare that to the expected version. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Leave it as it is. 

A recent forum support request revealed that a partner was using a default CouchDb image instead of the CHT one and they had issues with users getting logged out: https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/extending-session-timeout-duration/4794/3

We have also had unfortunate cluster upgrades where only one node in the cluster was upgraded - these faulty upgrades were due to a bug in the upgrade script, and it left the instance running in an inconsistent state until something broke. Having a check like this can prevent data-loss through data corruption if a similar event happens.

title: Bug Fix: Missing Dependencies for Default Config Compilation
body:
### Problem:
After removing inline dependencies from the default config, we're unable to recompile app settings because not all required dependencies were added to the parent package.json. The compilation fails with:

ERROR in Entry module not found: Error: Can't resolve 'eslint-loader'

**Steps to Reproduce:**

Run npm ci at root level

Navigate to config/default

Run cht compile-app-settings

Observe the eslint-loader resolution error

### Solution:
We need to add the missing dependencies to the root package.json since this is a monorepo-style project. Specifically:

Add eslint-loader@^3.0.0 as a devDependency (compatible with our webpack 4.x)

Ensure cht-conf is properly listed as a dependency

**_npm install --save-dev eslint-loader@^3.0.0 cht-conf_**

**Verification Steps:**

Apply the changes

Run clean install: npm ci

Verify compilation works: cd config/default && cht compile-app-settings

title: Allow docker multi-node to be easily run, but for developer, non-production
body:
In a [recent forum post](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/trouble-with-multi-node-docker-instance-error-while-creating-mount-source-path/), we discovered it's hard to run a multi-node couch instance in docker for development.  A while ago we supported this for production in docker swarm, but this has been deprecated.  However, we should still enable developers to run this locally, easily.  

This ticket tracks making a few changes to make this easier should a developer go looking for it.

Aside from downloading [the multi-node compose file](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/medic:medic:4.11.0/docker-compose/cht-couchdb-clustered.yml), from the post you need to:


1. Add 3 extra variables to `cht-upgrade-service` compose file in the `environment` section:
   ```yaml
      - DB1_DATA
      - DB2_DATA
      - DB3_DATA
   ```
2. Add 3 correct paths for each of the above env vars in your `.env` file.  For me this was as shown below, but it will be unique to each deployment:
   ```env
   DB1_DATA=/var/home/mrjones/Documents/medicmobile/multi-couch-test/couchdb/srv1
   DB2_DATA=/var/home/mrjones/Documents/medicmobile/multi-couch-test/couchdb/srv2
   DB3_DATA=/var/home/mrjones/Documents/medicmobile/multi-couch-test/couchdb/srv3
   ```
3. Define each of the three couch nodes, also in the `.env` file:
   ```env
   COUCHDB_SERVERS=couchdb-1.local,couchdb-2.local,couchdb-3.local
   ```

After all that is set up, you should just need to do `docker compose up -d` and away you go!

title: Add user storage usage to user-devices API
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
CHWs can run out of disk space and not know why their device is not performing as expected.  Giving administrators an easy way to monitor this would be really helpful

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Right now there's a [user-devices API](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/reference/api/#get-apiv2exportuser-devices) which has per user information, but does not include used and total storage space on the device.  If we add this to this report, it would make an easy way to find this data!

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Administrators could either manually check telemetry documents per user in Couch ([see](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/guides/performance/telemetry/#metadata) `deviceInfo.storage.free`) or they could set up a process like CHT Sync or couch2pg to sync this data to a Postgres database.

These are either slow (manually checking) or hard to set up (syncing data), where as the API is built in.

**Additional context**
* [Forum discussion](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/storage-pressure-indicator/4795/12). 
* [Original work](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8462) on user-devices API

### Good first issue 

This ticket has the [Good first issue label](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22Good%20first%20issue%22)! This means it's been especially curated by other CHT contributors to be easy to work on for first time contributors.

To succeed on this ticket, please:
1. set up your [development environment](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/core/dev-environment/) - and ensure it works by logging in to you CHT instance
2. create an offline user called `test` in the administrative interface
3. log in as this user to ensure a unique device ID in the CHT  is created
4. go to [fauxton](http://localhost:5984/_utils/#database/medic-users-meta/) and create a document based on the JSON below
5.  do a `curl` call to the user-devices API and not it's output: `http://medic:password@localhost:5988/api/v2/export/user-devices` - ensure you see the values from the document you created above
6. review the code changes made when the original [User Devices API](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/8797/files) was added:
   * while 35 files were edited (a lot!) - check out the changes to `api/src/services/export/user-devices.js` and `ddocs/users-meta-db/users-meta/views/device_by_user/map.js`
   * how might you extend these two files to include two new values based on the earlier work in this PR?

title: Provide offline user device storage info at a glance
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, there appears to be no built-in UI mechanism for offline users to view app storage usage.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The available storage space should be displayed to offline users in a clear, easy-to-find, and easy-to-understand manner. **Describe alternatives you've considered**

title: Remove body logging from Haproxy
body:
**Describe the issue**
Haproxy doesn't support logging full bodies. It is limited to 65k characters AND only logs the first chunk of a chunked body. 
Logging the body partially provides no benefit for auditing, and just increases the size of stored and parsed logs. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Update haproxy config to not log request bodies anymore. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Switch to nginx (this might be done anyway in another ticket).

title: Support selecting from external dataset in forms
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Sometimes in a form you want to allow the user to [select from very large set of choices](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/select-choice-question-type-with-a-lot-of-choices/3261/9).  Currently, the only way to do this is by adding all the choices to the `choices` tab (aka the "internal" dataset).  

This approach does not scale well for a number of reasons:
- It can be hard to maintain the list of data, particularly keeping the data in sync across multiple different forms that use the same dataset.
- The `xlsx` files can become large and unwieldy to edit
- The form `xml` file produced by cht-conf is very large and cht-conf's form validation logic will not perform well.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Enketo supports a [`select_*_from_file` question type](https://docs.getodk.org/form-question-types/#select-from-external-dataset) that allows for specifying that the data to select from is coming from an [external dataset](https://docs.getodk.org/form-datasets/#form-datasets).  We should add support to the CHT for this question type.  External data files could be uploaded to the server as attachments on the form doc and then injected into the form model when initializing the Enketo form.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I did spend some time exploring the possibility of using the `extension-libs` to do something here.  Unfortunately, the intricacies/functionality of `select_*` questions are so closely integrated with the Enekto form lifecycle (which requires that the form-model data be completely initialized _when creating the form_ that I could not find any feasible approach from that angle.

**Additional context**

The `select_*_from_file` question type basically causes the select widget to look for an external `instance` in the form model. We are already adding an external `instance` to forms [containing contact-summary data](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/e73d2e3036c34f2936f4b92d387300650262926c/webapp/src/ts/services/enketo.service.ts#L162).  I think it should be fairly straightforward to extend this code to include more xml instances in the `options.external` list that gets passed to the `EnketoForm` constructor.

The MVP here would seem to be including an xml file that exists as an attachment to the form doc.  For completeness, this would also probably include changes in cht-conf and the api server to upload/save the attachment to the doc.

title: Create separate analyzer.report.html for cht-form component
body:
**Describe the issue**
Twice now I have wasted a ton of time while investigating webapp bundle sizes because I did not realize that the `webapp/analyzer.report.html` file that gets created when running `npm run build` will be populated with data about the `cht-form` build since that runs after the actual `webapp` build.  Basically the `webapp/analyzer.report.html` file from the `webapp` build gets overwritten by the `cht-form` one.

(Yes a wiser person would have logged this issue after the _first_ time this happened... :🤦)

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
I _think_ it should be fine if we can just write a separate report file for `cht-form`.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Alternatively, we could just not write a report for `cht-form`  since we are not so sensitive about its bundle size...

title: Implement metadata audit log
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Historically, the CHT has always had (or tried to have) an audit log. 
An older implementation involved a secondary database that stored, for each document, a copy of the current body along with metadata of when the change happened. 
This solution became very problematic with documents with large bodies or that were saved frequently. 

We had an issue where an SMS service would infinitely update a certain document, every time it was processed. This should not be an issue normally, but the audit log saved copy after copy of the same document in the same audit document, creating absurdly large docs that eventually overwhelmed CouchDb. 

A second iteration of the Audit log was haproxy. However this solution had another issue, where haproxy would not log whole payloads of requests (makes sense, since payloads can be gigantic! and logging them in text can be overwhelming for the I/O system), but limit the size to a maximum of 65k characters and only log first body chunk. 

More details in the parent issue. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Iterating back on the solution where audit logs are stored in the database, except: 
- only metadata should be saved
- Make sure that we never get too large documents, this might mean that there should not be a 1-1 ratio between audit doc and medic doc (think of this as a log rotation, where once an audit doc is large enough, a new one is created)
- access should be fast and writing the audit should not be blocking

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Continue to log to STDIO. Because we can only add this to API, it would mean that API would log every document change. In my opinion, this would pollute API logs significantly, especially in periods of high load. 
Another option is to stream this log through another service.

title: Fix local ddoc versioning so changes to local ddocs are deployed during development
body:
**Describe the issue**

##### Summary

Previously, when running a local development instance of the CHT (e.g. via `npm run dev-api`), if you made changes to the design document code in the `ddocs` directory and then ran `npm run build-ddocs` the updated design documents would be automatically deployed to your local Couch instance by the running api server.

Unfortunately, I think changes made in https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/9674 to the local versioning logic have broken this workflow.  Now, if you update the design doc code and run `npm run build-ddocs`, it will properly compile the design document, but the api server will not deploy design document to the server. This is because the api server only uploads the new ddoc when it detects a change in the `version` property. Previously, this version changed on each execution of `npm run build-ddocs` because it included the current timestamp.  Now, however, the version used when building locally is just the current branch version (and so does not change between executions of `npm run build-ddocs` unless you change branches).  

##### Background

The CHT uses [CouchDB Design documents](https://docs.couchdb.org/en/latest/ddocs/ddocs.html) to store the code used by Couch for building the map/reduce views needed for querying data.  The code for each design-doc/view is stored in the sub-directories of [`./ddocs`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/b3cee4acc8bfe909df2b6eed70264138cfaf8c76/ddocs).  During CHT development we occasionally have to make changes to this view code and/or add new views to the design documents. When doing this, the proper way to compile the new design documents (from all the code in the `ddocs` directory) is to run `npm run build-ddoc`. This will put the built ddocs into the `build/ddocs` directory, but will not automatically upload them to Couch.

The `npm run dev-api` command is supposed to run the CHT api server in development mode so that changes to local files are automatically detected and reflected in the locally running development instance. This is a convenience for the developer so they can quickly iterate on code changes. Unfortunately, it is currently not possible to easily/automatically upload new versions of these design docs to Couch (see the workaround mentioned down below). Restoring that functionality is the goal of this issue.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

The fix should here should be pretty simple: 

- [ ] Update [`setDdocsVersion` function in scripts/build/index.js](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/b3cee4acc8bfe909df2b6eed70264138cfaf8c76/scripts/build/index.js#L193) to check the existence of the `TAG` environment variable.
    - If `TAG` exists, it means a release build is being performed and we should do nothing.  The `version` variable should just be set to the value returned by `versions.getVersion()`.
    - If `TAG` does not exist, we should append `new Date().getTime()` to the end of the `version` variable to ensure a new ddoc version gets set each time this runs.
- [ ] Ensure the change was successful by doing the following manual test:
    - Start the api server: `npm run dev-api`
    - Make an update to one of the design documents (e.g. update the [contacts_by_depth map function](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/80760a6d2155e5f77cb5278651b0fe63de7ed0fc/ddocs/medic-db/medic/views/contacts_by_depth/map.js) to include `console.log('hello world');`
    - Run `npm run build-ddocs`
    - Use Fauxton to verify the new version of the design doc was automatically uploaded to the server:
        - Open `http://localhost:5984/_utils/#database/medic/_design%2Fmedic` in your browser
        - Verify the document contents contains `hello world`.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

One alternative would be to update the api server logic to actually compare the ddoc _contents_ (local vs server) instead of just looking at the `version`.  However, in production the only time the ddoc should actually change is during an upgrade. So, it feels like a lot of unnecessary logic in the production code to support what is really only relevant in a development environment.  I think it is best to keep the API version check the same and just restore our previous behavior of time-stamping the local ddoc version when building the docs locally.

Also, just noting that with the current functionality the most convienient workaround that I have found to deploy new versions of the ddocs when doing local development is:

- Run the api server `npm run dev-api`
- Use Fauxton (or curl) to completely delete the design doc in question from Couch
    - This will cause the api server to crash and wait for local file changes before continuing
- Run `npm run build-ddocs` to re-build the ddocs. When this finishes, the api should should automatically upload the "new" ddoc to Couch.

title: Ensure proper mapping for SSO users to Couch users
body:
Couch usernames have some strict requirements (most significantly that you cannot use `@`).  However, many SSO providers may use _email_ as the unique identifier for their users (included in the id_token provided in the OIDC flow).

There are a number of possible resolutions here, but we should focus on doing the MVP to get things working with Microsoft Entra ID.

title: Allow setting background color for form questions
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Originally proposed [on the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/custom-css-for-custom-appearance/4838/7).

In our Enekto forms. we already have a (poorly documented) feature that lets you set specific background colors for `note`s that are within a `summary` group by setting a header _appearance_ (e.g. `h2`) and a color _appearance_ (e.g. `red`).  This feature is intended to support formatting the "summary" page at the end of the form where the user can review the details of the data they have captured before submitting it.  The header appearances affect the size/alignment of the text and the colors allow for setting the background for that header.

Unfortunately, this functionality is not flexible enough to support all the desired use cases. Specifically, there is no way to set the color without also setting the header and setting the header really only "works" for `note` fields. If you set the header appearances on other types of questions, it can cause undesired layout issues.  This ticket proposes expanding the color functionality in the css to allow for setting a background color on all types of questions

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Enketo already automatically supports setting the values from the `appearance` column in the xlsx as classes on the HTML element for that form question.  This is how the [`summary` stuff](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/a2682caf70f2bf0a5e2ca870ad7adeb99f2a57df/webapp/src/css/enketo/medic.less#L306) works currently.  We can target these appearance classes in our css and provide styling that can be toggled on by setting the appearance. 

My proposal is that we add a new set of supported classes directly under `.enketo` that will allow for targeting specific background colors for any question:

- `.or-appearance-background-red`
- `.or-appearance-background-green`
- `.or-appearance-background-blue`
- `.or-appearance-background-yellow`
- `.or-appearance-background-lime`

To use these, you would just set something like `background-blue` in the _appearance_ column in the xlsx form config.  

For backwards compatibility, we should retain the existing `.or-appearance-red/blue/...` classes, but I think they should be considered deprecated in favor of the more general-purpose `.or-appearance-background-red/blue/...` classes. We could even add a [form validation warning](https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/tree/main/src/lib/validation/form) to cht-conf to prompt app devs to update their form configuration to the new appearances.

I do not think there is much we can do here in the way of having automated tests for these changes, but we will want to thoroughly manually test these background colors (particularly with the [enketo_widgets_test.xlsx form](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/e2e/default/enketo/forms/enketo_widgets_test.xlsx) since that will let us catch any unintended impacts to all the various enketo widgets we support).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

One discussed alternative is to simply allow for injecting a custom stylesheet as part of the branding assets configurable for the CHT.  While I think that could be used for to achieve much more dramatic customization, I remain concerned about the long-term maintainability of that approach.  At the very least, I would want to have some kind of set list of things that are officially supported for styling in this way. (AKA some kind of theming structure that would allow for deeper configuration of the CHT styles, but could still be guaranteed not to break/change unexpectedly. One big draw-back of that kind of approach is that it is pretty heavy-handed/technical for achieving something simple like coloring form questions. Thinking as an app developer, if I want to set a background color on a form question, it is much more convenient/straightforward to just be able to set an `appearance` value right in my form xlsx instead of trying to figure out my own custom css....

title: fix(#7990): prevent credentials exposure in error response
body:
# Description

   This PR fixes a security vulnerability where credentials were being exposed in error logs when there was an error in the URI or other request parameters.

   The fix adds a sanitization function that:
   1. Detects and redacts sensitive fields (like passwords, usernames, auth tokens) in error objects
   2. Uses regex to find and replace credentials in string error content
   3. Preserves the error message format while ensuring credentials are masked

   Fixes #7990

   # Code review checklist

body:

### feat(#9492): fix Angular Material icon registration in unit tests with MaterialTestModule

## Description

Closes #9492 

We identified an issue where unit tests using Angular Material icons were failing due to the icon `:icon-back` not being properly registered in the test environment. This caused errors in multiple test files that relied on this and potentially other custom icons.

## ❌ Error: The icon "icon-back" was not found in the registry

### Why does this happen?

Because Angular needs icons to be **explicitly registered** using the `MatIconRegistry`.

### Solution

To resolve this, we introduced a consistent testing setup using a shared testing module. Here's what we did:

- **Created a `MaterialTestModule`** in `test-utils/material-test.module.ts` that:
  - Properly registers Angular Material icons such as `:icon-back`
  - Optionally sets up FontAwesome if required by the components
- **Added a utility function** to simplify and standardize test module setup using this shared module
- **Updated individual test files** to replace direct usage of `MatIconModule` with the new shared module:
  
  **Before:**
  ```ts
  import { MatIconModule } from '@angular/material/icon';
  
 **After:**
  ```ts
  import { MaterialTestModule } from '../../test-utils/material-test.module';

title: Add release date to scripts so docs have dates
body:
**Describe the issue**
We're [adding dates to all releases](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/issues/1843) in the docs, but they'll not be added automatically for future releases. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Update the [release notes generation script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to include the include the date of the release as a part of the page markdown content. 

### Background

As a part of the cht-core [release process](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/z_release_patch.md#releasing---release-engineer) we use the release notes generation script to automatically generate the base release notes content to be [included on our Docs site](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/releases/).

title: Handle situation where CHT user does not exist for SSO user
body:
What should we do when the SSO user authenticates successfully with the OIDC provider, but once they are redirected back to the CHT, the api server cannot find any existing CHT user for the SSO user?

It seems like a good default action is just to redirect them back to the login page.  It would be even better if they ended up on the login page AND were shown some helpful message indicating the issue.  

My main concern is that an SSO login failure like this could be really hard for the personnel in the field to understand/troubleshoot without some kind of error message that helps you understand why it is that you "logged in" to the OIDC provider successfully, but still cannot access the CHT....

title: feat(#9885): adds new meta audit database
body:
<!--

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

Adds new mechanism to audit document changes, through a new shared library, `audit`. The library is injected into every call that handles requests (PouchDb `fetch` and `couch-request`). 
When a monitored API is called (POST to create a doc, PUT to update a doc or _bulk_docs), the response is analyzed and entries are added into a new database `medic-audit`. 
In `medic-audit`, each document has an audit doc which contains the last 10 entries of received changes. Each entry includes the `rev` of the change in question, the user that made the change, the `request_id` (in case this was a direct client request), the service that made the change (api or sentinel) and the date when the change was registered. 
When an audit doc has 10 history entries, a rotation mechanism will save the old audit entry in a new doc, and the existing document trail will only contain the new change. 

Moves `getDeployInfo` into its own shared library to avoid circular dependencies. 

closes #9885

title: Replace usage of `db-object` appearance with `select-contact`
body:
<!--
**Important**: This is a public repository. Anyone in the world can see what's posted here. If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the bug**
We should replace the `db-object` appearance  and use `select-contact` instead which supports multiple types of contacts as a follow-up to: https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/issues/502.

`db-object` instances in the XML forms in `/config` : https://pastebin.com/0pB1PmTN


Additional tip by @jkuester, originally mentioned [here](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/warn-when-using-deprecated-db-object-appearance/4890/4?u=apoorvapendse):

Just one tip when it comes to uplifting forms to use `select-contact`, you can find the docs [here](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/forms/configuring/form-inputs/#contact-selector). But basically for the form to work you will need to update both the `appearance` column (from `db-object` to `select-contact`) AND the `type` column. The type changes from `db:{{contact_type}}` to just be `string`. *Then*, you need to add an additional value in the `appearance` column (it is a space-separated list) that is `type-{{contact_type}}`. 

For example, if you start with:

|type|appearance|
| --- | --- |
|db:person|db-object|

This should be updated to:

|type|appearance|
| --- | --- |
|string|select-contact type-person|


**To Reproduce**
Using the branch in https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/pull/682 might be a good start, as that branch introduces the `db-object` deprecation warnings.

The steps will be similar to the ones mentioned in https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/issues/502
We should ensure that the `db-object` warnings are not displayed on running for the applicable forms.
```
cht --url=$(chtx instance ls <instance_name>) upload-app-forms -- <form_name>
```

**Expected behavior**
`db-object` usage is replaced with `select-contact` which can be tested running the form validation using a `cht-conf` version that introduces the `db-object` warning.


**Additional context**
Related Discussion: https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/warn-when-using-deprecated-db-object-appearance/4890

title: chore(#9523): upgrade WebdriverIO to v9
body:
<!--

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

This PR upgrades WebdriverIO from v8 to v9
closes https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9523

**Main Changes**
- WebdriverIO version updates
- Removed `waitForClickable` before `.click()` calls, as WebdriverIO v9 now automatically waits for elements to become interactable. [Reference](https://webdriver.io/blog/2024/08/15/webdriverio-v9-release#automatic-waiting-for-elements-to-become-interactable)
- Simplified element access by removing double `await`, following the updated approach for accessing element properties. [Reference](https://webdriver.io/blog/2024/08/15/webdriverio-v9-release#accessing-element-properties)
- Replaced `isDisplayedInViewport` with `isDisplayed({ withinViewport: true })` as the former has been removed. [Reference](https://webdriver.io/blog/2024/08/15/webdriverio-v9-release#removal-of-isdisplayedviewport)
- Using WebDriver Classic mode by setting `'wdio:enforceWebDriverClassic': true` in capabilities, as BiDi support is currently unstable. I'm getting [this](https://github.com/webdriverio/webdriverio/issues/14430) error.

# Code review checklist
<!-- Remove or comment out any items that do not apply to this PR; in the remaining boxes, replace the [ ] with [x]. -->

title: Release 4.19.0
body:
# Planning - CHT Community 

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [x] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo.
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Checkout to a new `<issue>-update-version` branch (eg: `1234-update-version`) and set the version number in the `package.json` and `package-lock.json`. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`. Once the version is updated, submit a PR to `master` branch.
- [x] Ensure that issues associated with commits merged to `master` since the last release are closed and mapped to the milestone.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once the PR has been merged into `master`, and the `master` branch has the new version number, then the release process can start:

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development Slack channel using this template:
```
@channel I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by creating a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`) and then push the created tag.
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the team by writing a message in the #development Slack channel:
```
@channel, I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag. 
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make. 
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [x] The beta tag will automatically trigger the scalability build. Once it passes, download the scalability results on S3 at medic-e2e/scalability/$TAG_NAME. If you do not have access to the scalability results ask someone in the #product-team who has access. Add the release `.json` file to `cht-core/tests/scalability/previous_results`. More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [x] Go to the [Issues tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues) and filter the issues with `is:issue label:"Affects: 4.x.x" ` , replace `4.x.x` with the previous version number. Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label.  
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labelled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [x] Collect known migration steps, descriptions, screenshots, videos, data, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. This information should already be on the issue, but if not, prompt the change author to provide it.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions) and update the EOL date of the previous release. Update the status of any releases that are past their End Of Life date. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page.
- [x] Create a [new release](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases/new) in GitHub, with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, from the release branch created above as the target branch. Click on the "Choose a tag" dropdown and create a tag for the release with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. Ensure the release notes PR from above are merged. Add a link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Once you publish the release, confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Upgrade the [demo](https://demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org/) instance to the newly released version.
- [x] Use cht-conf to upload the configuration from the `cht-core/config/demo` folder to the `demo-cht.dev` server.
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*We're excited to announce the release of {{version}} of {{product}}*

See below for some highlights, read the [release notes]({{<paste-url>}}) for full details.

Following the CHT's support policy, versions {{versions}} are no longer supported. Projects running these versions should start planning to upgrade in the near future. For more details read the CHT [software support documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions).

## {{version}} Highlights

### [{{Highlight 1}}]({{<paste-url to section>}})

{{description of highlight section}}

### ### [{{Highlight 2}}]({{<paste-url to section>}})

{{description of highlight section}}

### [And more...]({{paste-url to section}})

We’ve also implemented loads of other improvements and fixed a heap of bugs.

```
- [x] Add one last update to the #development Slack channel and use the thread to lead an internal release retrospective covering what went well and areas to improve for next time.
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Add user-agent header to outgoing requests
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
A recent change in TextIt (or all RapidPro) blocks all requests that are lacking a `user-agent` header. We have recently added a `user-agent` header to outbound requests, and this needs to be applied to rapidpro requests as well. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add `user-agent` header to RapidPro requests. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Add user-agent to all outgoing requests, not just rapid-pro. 

**Additional context**
Reported on [the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/user-agent-header-in-rapidpro-integration-code/4928/11)

title: feat(#9936): add user-agent for all outgoing RapidPro requests
body:
This pull request introduces a new feature for automatically adding a `user-agent` header to HTTP requests in the `couch-request` library, while also removing redundant code from the `outbound` library. The changes include implementing a `getUserAgent` function, modifying request handling to include the `user-agent` header, and adding corresponding unit tests to ensure proper functionality.

fixes #9936 
### Changes to `couch-request` library:

* **Added `user-agent` header generation and inclusion**:
  - Introduced a `getUserAgent` function to dynamically create a `user-agent` string based on the CHT version, platform, and architecture. (`shared-libs/couch-request/src/couch-request.js`, [shared-libs/couch-request/src/couch-request.jsR29-R35](diffhunk://#diff-7c51430a26d41894740c0f40a3f2477eeea8b9d56e3adb60075f647cdecf9cb4R29-R35))
  - Updated the `setRequestOptions` function to include the `user-agent` header if it is not already set. (`shared-libs/couch-request/src/couch-request.js`, [shared-libs/couch-request/src/couch-request.jsL129-R150](diffhunk://#diff-7c51430a26d41894740c0f40a3f2477eeea8b9d56e3adb60075f647cdecf9cb4L129-R150))
  - Ensured `setRequestOptions` is awaited in the `request` function to handle the asynchronous `getUserAgent` call. (`shared-libs/couch-request/src/couch-request.js`, [shared-libs/couch-request/src/couch-request.jsL186-R200](diffhunk://#diff-7c51430a26d41894740c0f40a3f2477eeea8b9d56e3adb60075f647cdecf9cb4L186-R200))

* **Added unit tests**:
  - Mocked dependencies (`os` and `@medic/environment`) to simulate platform and version data. (`shared-libs/couch-request/test/couch-request.js`, [shared-libs/couch-request/test/couch-request.jsR36-R41](diffhunk://#diff-8406c6aa90be792d652a8e1a0df0824f3923709dba9ecdb690406cde25c2894bR36-R41))
  - Added tests to verify that the `user-agent` header is automatically added and does not override an existing `user-agent` header. (`shared-libs/couch-request/test/couch-request.js`, [shared-libs/couch-request/test/couch-request.jsR715-R738](diffhunk://#diff-8406c6aa90be792d652a8e1a0df0824f3923709dba9ecdb690406cde25c2894bR715-R738))

### Changes to `outbound` library:

* **Removed redundant `user-agent` code**:
  - Deleted the `getUserAgent` function and the associated `CHT_AGENT` constant, as this functionality is now centralized in the `couch-request` library. (`shared-libs/outbound/src/outbound.js`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4cd39b6dcdad1347e201fe0deaad5a6f78e739ce2c38078ffdf07a23d67bd49dL28) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4cd39b6dcdad1347e201fe0deaad5a6f78e739ce2c38078ffdf07a23d67bd49dL98-L103)
  - Removed the inclusion of the `user-agent` header in the `sendPayload` function, delegating this responsibility to the `couch-request` library. (`shared-libs/outbound/src/outbound.js`, [shared-libs/outbound/src/outbound.jsL186-L188](diffhunk://#diff-4cd39b6dcdad1347e201fe0deaad5a6f78e739ce2c38078ffdf07a23d67bd49dL186-L188)

title: fix(na): refactor copy static files to be futureproof
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

feat(#1234): add hat wobble
^--^(#^--^): ^------------^
|     |      |
|     |      + - > subject
|     |
|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: chore, feat, fix, perf.

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

<!-- DESCRIPTION -->

<!-- ISSUE NUMBER -->

This PR refactors the the [copy static file script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/build/copy-static-files.sh#L10) so that it is compatible with both GNU Coreutils and uutils coreutils implementations of the `cp` command.  Yes, here we are - believe it.  See [forum post](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/how-to-lint-on-the-command-line/4939/6) for more info.

the fix was to break out each recursive `cp` on to it's own line. 

If you have both versions of `cp` handy, you can prefer one vs the other by setting your `$PATH` correctly.  I had the uutils coreutils as default and the GNU one in `/usr/bin/cp`.  So I called this to make the GNU be called:

```
export PATH=/usr/bin/cp:$PATH
```


Then to test for regressions, call `./scripts/build/copy-static-files.sh`.  Success should show this when using GNU or uutils `cp`:

```
copy-static-files: copying
copy-static-files: done
```

Failure should show this only when using uutils `cp`:

```
copy-static-files: copying
cp: will not overwrite just-created 'api/build/static/admin/fonts' with 'webapp/src/fonts'
```

body:
feat(#9250): enhance Bikram Sambat date picker with advanced features # Description This PR enhances the Bikram Sambat date picker used in forms by integrating a more feature-complete component from the public repository [opensource-nepal/nepali-date-picker](https://github.com/opensource-nepal/nepali-date-picker). The existing picker was limited in functionality compared to the Gregorian version, affecting usability and consistency across date input fields. ### Improvements introduced: - Added a full calendar view with Month and Week display - Included "Jump to Today" functionality for quick access to the current date - Added a clear option to remove selected dates - Enabled navigation to next and previous months - Introduced year and date selection through dropdowns or navigation These changes aim to bring the Bikram Sambat date picker to parity with the Gregorian calendar experience, improving usability and user satisfaction, especially for users in regions where BS is the standard.

## 🎥 Implementation Demo Here's a quick demo of the enhanced **Bikram Sambat date picker** with improved UI and functionality across devices: - 🖥️ **Mobile View**: 👉 [Watch here](https://www.loom.com/share/f97e91faf86c4d4bb4a38ec84ad66e17?sid=fe920a0a-4dde-4019-8b37-b70c247bbb09) - 📱 **Desktop View**: 👉 [Watch here](https://www.loom.com/share/bc7f3f6a7fa445a3b0a76bf1b17262a3?sid=e4403244-e7c7-4b6a-9d50-0354d9720e9d) #9250 # Code review checklist - [x] UI/UX backwards compatible: Tested on both new and old designs (`can_view_old_navigation` enabled), including RTL language support. - [ ] Readable: Code is concise, uses descriptive names, and follows the [style guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/style-guide/). - [ ] Documented: Changes documented as needed on [cht-docs](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/). - [x] Tested: Includes appropriate unit or end-to-end tests. - [ ] Internationalised: All user-facing text is localizable. - [x] Backwards compatible: Works with existing configuration and data.       • String.prototype.match

      • String.prototype.replace
      • String.prototype.search
      • String.prototype.split

    • Iterator.prototype.drop

    • Iterator.prototype.find
    • Iterator.prototype.flatMap
    • Iterator.prototype.forEach
    • Iterator.prototype.map
    • Iterator.prototype.reduce
    • Iterator.prototype.some
    • Iterator.prototype.take

    • AsyncIterator.from

title: feat(#9838): refactor shared-libs/lineage to use cht-datasource for reading contacts
body:
# Description

This PR refactors the shared-libs/lineage library and its consuming code to use cht-datasource for reading contacts instead of directly using PouchDB. The changes maintain backward compatibility while centralizing contact read operations through cht-datasource.

## Details
- Updated shared-libs/lineage to use cht-datasource:
  - Added cht-datasource as a dependency
  - Modified the library to accept datasource as a parameter
  - Refactored key functions to use cht-datasource with fallbacks to the original implementation
  - Key functions updated: fetchLineageById, fetchDoc, fetchDocs, contactUuidByShortcode, fetchHydratedDocs

- Updated consuming code to use the refactored lineage library:
  - shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/index.js
  - api/src/controllers/hydration.js
  - api/src/controllers/contacts-by-phone.js
  - api/src/services/export/contact-mapper.js
  - api/src/services/export/report-mapper.js
  - api/src/services/export/message-mapper.js
  - api/src/manual-migrations/minify-contacts.js

# Issue

Closes #9838

- [x] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the [style guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/style-guide/), documented if necessary.
- [x] Tested: Unit tests pass, confirming that the refactored code maintains the same behavior
- [x] Backwards compatible: Works with existing data and includes fallback mechanisms to ensure robustness if cht-datasource operations fail

title: Convert couchdb and haproxy unit tests to javascript
body:
**Describe the issue**
Currently couchdb and haproxy tests use bash and bats. These are limiting because developers are not familiar with this testing framework and they require the supported software (bats) to be committed to the repository. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Convert all couchdb and haproxy tests to javascript. Since these tests are integration tests already - and require spinning up docker containers with the tested software, this is possible.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Leave it as it is.

title: Hide upgrade button in admin app for k8s deployments, while still allowing staging upgrades
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
For 1-click upgrades, instances hosted in k8s [use an additional service](https://github.com/medic/upgrade-service-kubernetes) to perform the deployment upgrade.

The service lacks a couple of critical functions: 
1. it does not do a fresh deployment by itself (requires a separate tool, like `helm` for example)
1. it does not allow new deployments - like adding new services that would need to run in their own containers
2. it does not sync versions between the new deployments and the original deployment tool (mentioned in 1)
3. itself does not have a clear upgrade path and there is no channel of communication where users can be informed that a new version of the tool has been released. 

We have two cases where this tool has failed: 
- when instances were redeployed using the original deployment tool after an upgrade was done and without updating the version in the values files. this caused the instance to downgrade to an older version - which is a potentially destructive event. 
- adding a [CouchDb Nouveau deployment](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9707#issuecomment-2870574703) that will be required for newer version of CHT-Core will require manual upgrades. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
No longer use the upgrade service for k8s deployments. 
Make changes to the admin app to call an API endpoint that will determine whether the instance is hosted in k8s, and if so, hide the "Upgrade" buttons, only showing the "Stage" buttons. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Somehow figure out which upgrades are safe to do and which are not, and inform users through the admin app about it. 
- change the principles of the upgrade service so that it can upgrade itself and add new deployments

title: feat(#9760): add support for authenticating users via OIDC
body:
# Description

Closes #9735

https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/pull/1875

This PR includes several interlocking changes all required for supporting SSO authentication via OIDC in the CHT.

1. Add api support for creating/updating users with `oidc_username` property.
    - `shared-libs/user-management` updated to support this property on requests made to the `/api/v?/users` endpoints. 
    - The property value is returned when retrieving users via the `/api/v?/users` endpoint.
    - When creating/updating a user, the `oidc_username` property cannot be combined with `password` or `token_login`.
        - Instead, when `oidc_username` is set, a random `password` value will be automatically generated for the user. 
    - The `oidc_username` value must be unique. There cannot be any existing users that already have the same value.
    - The server must be configured with `oidc_provider` in the app_settings.json when setting an `oidc_username` on a user.
1. Add support for creating/updating SSO users via the admin app UI
    - The create/update user modal in the admin app has been updated to include a new "SSO Email Address" text box.
    - The box is only displayed when `oidc_provider` is configured in the app_settings.json and the user does not have `token_login` enabled.
    - If a value is provided for "SSO Email Address", the user is not able to enter values for Token Login or the Password.
1. Add support for API endpoints to login as an OIDC user
    - `/medic/login/oidc/authorize` is used for starting the OIDC flow. Submit a GET request to this endpoint and a redirect url will be returned pointing to the OIDC provider with all the necessary query parameters.
    - `/medic/login/oidc` is used for finishing the OIDC flow and completing the login process. The OIDC provider will redirect the user back to this endpoint with all the necessary query parameters needed for finishing the OIDC flow.
        - Most importantly, the `authorization_code` query parameter should be provided (by the OIDC Provider) when calling this endpoint. The CHT api server will take this auth code and use it to make a back-channel connection to the OIDC Provider and get the user's id_token.
        - The id_token will include the user's `email` claim. The value for this `email` claim is then used to query for users with a matching `oidc_username`.
        - When one (and only one) user is found with a matching `oidc_username` value, the API server will generate a new Couch session cookie for that user (this mimics what happens during a normal logic process where the Couch `_session` endpoint is called with the user's credentials). 
        - The new Couch session cookie is provided on the response and from that point the user is validly logged in as a normal CHT user.
    - These endpoints can only be called when the server has been properly configured for SSO:
        - The `app_url` must be set in the app_settings.json
        - The `oidc_provider` object must be configured in the app_settings.json and include:
            - `discovery_url` - the URL of the OIDC provider's discovery endpoint
            - `client_id` - the unique identifier for the CHT server in the OIDC provider
        - The `client_secret` value for the CHT server from the OIDC provider must also be set in the CHT via the `/api/v1/credentials` endpoint.
1. Add support for showing a "Login with SSO" button on login page
    - When `oidc_provider` is configured in the app_settings.json, the normal CHT login page with be rendered with a "Login with SSO" button. 
    - Clicking this button will cause the user's browser to be automatically redirected to the OIDC Provider where they can authenticate before being automatically redirected back to the CHT app.
    - Selecting a locale on the login page will not affect the locale used in the app once the user has completed the OIDC login flow. Instead the locale used in the app will match the `locale` claim configured for the user in the OIDC provider (or will fall back to the default locale for the CHT instance).

title: Implement task sorting by priority
body:
#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Currently tasks are sorted only by due date, so users have to manually identify tasks that are most urgent. The update takes into account both a priority score and due date to prioritize tasks.

#### Describe the solution you'd like
Extend the sorting logic to sort tasks as follows:
1. Priority values are positive numbers
2. Higher priorities sort first
3. Equal priorities sort by due date
4. Invalid/missing values sort last while adhering to the above

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
1. Store an array of priorities per task for e.g. [not due, due, overdue], then let the WebApp pick the correct one. This turned out to be rigid and complex to maintain.
2. Sort entirely by due date and then priority. This does not fully capture the intended urgency based on individual conditions.
3. Sort overdue tasks by due date, and all other tasks by priority. This sounded great, but less consistent for borderline-due tasks.

title: feat(#9890): add mapping from OIDC to CHT user
body:
# Description

Closes #9890
Closes #9836
Closes #9938

Updates OIDC user configuration.  Instead of a boolean `oidc` field on the `_users` doc, there is now a string `oidc_username` field on the `_users` doc and a boolean `oidc_login` field on the `user-settings` doc.  This follows the pattern from token login where the auth-sensitive information is stored on the `_users` doc, while non-sensitive info is kept on the `user-settings` doc to allow the offline user UI logic to handle special cases for OIDC users.

Specifically, when a user had `oidc_login: true` in their user settings doc, they will not see the option in the app to update their password.

title: CHT running in Docker Helper doesn't upgrade CouchDB
body:
<!--
**Important**: This is a public repository. Anyone in the world can see what's posted here. If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the bug**
When you're running [CHT in Docker Helper](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/hosting/4.x/app-developer/#cht-docker-helper-for-4x) and you upgrade, CouchDB does not get upgraded.

**To Reproduce**
1. install a CHT 4.18 in [Docker Helper](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/hosting/4.x/app-developer/#cht-docker-helper-for-4x) 
2. log in as admin and upgrade to 4.19
3. note that CouchDB is on 4.18 and all other services are on 4.19


**Expected behavior**
CouchDB is upgraded to the 4.19 CouchDB image

**Logs**
Here's the list of services and image versions that `docker ps --format '{{.Names}} {{.Image}}'` shows:

```
nginx-1 public.ecr.aws/medic/cht-nginx:4.19.0
api-1 public.ecr.aws/medic/cht-api:4.19.0
sentinel-1 public.ecr.aws/medic/cht-sentinel:4.19.0
healthcheck-1 public.ecr.aws/medic/cht-haproxy-healthcheck:4.19.0
haproxy-1 public.ecr.aws/medic/cht-haproxy:4.19.0
couchdb-1 public.ecr.aws/medic/cht-couchdb:4.18.0
cht-upgrade-service-1 public.ecr.aws/s5s3h4s7/cht-upgrade-service:latest
```

**Environment**
- Instance: local dev
- Browser: NA
- Client platform: NA
- App: CHT in Docker Helper
- Version: 4.0.0 and up

**Additional context**
In testing, it's suspected that following production install steps avoids the issue.  This suggests possibly a folder hierarchy endemic to docker helper maybe?

title: feat(#5997): dynamic sorting of tasks by priority
Support opening contact edit form from task
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?** Enable editing a contact directly from a task. Currently, while the CHT allows creating a new contact based on type via a task, it does not support editing an existing contact directly through a task entry. This enhancement would build on existing functionality and streamline the "follow-up" process where one has to maintain patient information. **Describe the improvement you'd like** Setting an `action`'s `type` to "contact" and unpacking the entire contents of the linked contact into the `content` variable, facilitated by `modifyContent`, should allow for editing that contact directly. **Describe alternatives you've considered** Create an "intermediary" app form that gets opened by the task, passing in the relevant contact `_id`. This form contains a "button", essentially an anchor tag pointing to `contacts//edit`. Here's an example layout: | type | name | label | calculation | | -------------- | ------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ | | begin group | inputs | | | | begin group | contact | | | | hidden | _id | | | | hidden | name | | | | end group | contact | | | | end group | inputs | | | | calculate | _id | | ../inputs/contact/_id | | calculate | link | | concat(concat("#/contacts/", string(../_id)),"/edit") | The "redirect" `note`, placed below the `link` entry, displays as a button with the following HTML content: ``` Got to "${name}"
${link}
 ``` Problems with this approach: 1. It is unintuitive and difficult to train for CHWs. 2. It allows for unintended submission of intermediary forms, cluttering the reports view. 3. It loses the ability to use `modifyContent` with the intended `contact` form. **Additional context** https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/write-custom-transition-and-edit-contact-form-with-task/3334 https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/temporarily-increase-future-task-180-limit/4026

title: feat(#9957): dynamic sorting of tasks by priority and due date
body:
Closes https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9957

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
  Currently tasks are sorted only by due date. The update takes into account both a priority score and due date.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
  Implemented a refined sorting algorithm that (Sort by priority and then due date within the same priority):
  - Primarily sorts tasks by priority (higher numbers first)
  - For tasks with equal priority, sorts by due date (earlier dates first)
  - Handles invalid values consistently:
      - Tasks with invalid priorities move to end
      - Within same priority, invalid dates move to end
      - Maintains original order when both priority and date are invalid

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
****Alternative Solution 1****
Similar to the proposed solution, but with the priority property of a task not be a number, but an array, with one number representing the priority of the task when it is not due, one number for when it’s due and one number for when it’s overdue. Then web-app will just select the right number when sorting tasks, and not recompute priority based on due date.

****Alternative Solution 2****
Options for frontend sorting: 
- Sort by due date and then priority within the same due date.
- Sorting by Due date first for tasks above the due date, then by priority for tasks that are not due. 
- Sort by priority for tasks that are above due date, then by due date for tasks that are not due.

**Additional context**
- The solution maintains backwards compatibility with existing task structures
- Includes comprehensive test cases covering edge cases like:
  - Invalid date formats (null, false, undefined).
  - Invalid priority values (strings, negative numbers).
  - Duplicate priorities and dates.
  - Missing fields.

title: SSO flow does not support ports with CHT instances not on 443
body:
**Describe the issue**
When following the  [docs PR](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/pull/1875) to use CHT in Docker Helper to test with Keycloak, the port is lost for the redirect URI when the port is specified  (eg `https://192-168-68-26.local-ip.medicmobile.org:10448/`)

This applies currently to docker helper, but likely applies to any CHT instance not on port `443`

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Ensure there's no bugs in our implementation preventing the port from getting lost.  Note, it works when running the CHT in development mode (eg `http://localhost:5984`) just not on [docker helper](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/hosting/4.x/app-developer/#cht-docker-helper-for-4x)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
You can create a docker helper instance and the edit it's `.env` file to run on port `443` for HTTPS and then configure Keycloak and it works. 


----

**Note:** when we fix this, remove the text from [the Keycloak docs](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/pull/1875):

> Currently [there is an issue](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9981) that prevents the CHT docker helper from being on a random `104xx`  port.  Please edit the `cht_test.env` file and change the port to be: `NGINX_HTTPS_PORT=443` and restart your docker helper.

title: Investigate automatically triggering Couch compaction during upgrade staging
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
When staging a CHT upgrade, any new/updated views must be re-indexed. A by-product of the view indexing process is a significant amount of disk space. When Couch is busy trying to index views, it will not automatically run any compaction which is the process it uses to free up disk space from db index files that are no longer being used. (Possibly as you run out of disk space, Couch will make a desperate attempt to compact while it indexes??? 🤔)

When upgrading, you would _expect_ that the worst case scenario for disk usage is that the upgrade would require `<100%` additional disk space (in the worst case we would have to stage new versions of _all the Couch views_).  (This, of course, is assuming that no net-new large views are added during the upgrade.)  Unfortunately, this is not the case. Disk usage during upgrades has been measured as high as `<500%` during upgrades.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/968e8603-27fa-4fe9-9d26-4fc012f726f2)

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

My hypothesis is that much of this used disk space is just wasted space that could be freed up by triggering Couch compaction.  This would be a case of trading some CPU cycles for using less max disk space. Staging an upgrade would take more time (because of the CPU cycles being used for compaction instead of indexing).  We will need to measure the impacts when updating a production-level dataset, but it seems possible (likely?) that we can significantly reduce the max used disk space while only moderately lengthening the staging process.  

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

These issues are not exclusive, but https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/2849 also has likely impacts on how disk space is used during upgrades.

**Additional context**

More data:
- https://docs.google.com/document/d/1X0ztxCdmdGWo_-6PcHkwTTwvbgXQxR_h6W9JZGYEmWU/edit?tab=t.0
- https://docs.google.com/document/d/1TvnUyjDunhfxCw9b-djB6h8OBAVOY3PUWohsPhnFWl8/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.ct45ix9hvlwe

title: Require `app_url` to be set when enabling `token_login`
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**

Currently we [do not require](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/reference/app-settings/token_login/) the [`app_url` setting](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/reference/app-settings/#app_settingsjson) to be configured when enabling Token Login.  Instead, if the `app_url` is not set, we fall back to trying to get the URL off of the request sent to create/update the user.

This is annoying because it makes the code more messy and we have to pass in the appUrl value to the create/update user functions all the time regardless of if it is needed.  Additionally, the URL from the request could actually be invalid if the server is exposed on a non-standard port (e.g. not `443`). In that case the request will not have the port data and the token login links will not work unless the `app_url` value is configured.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We should just require the `app_url` to be configured when enabling `token_login`.  

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Honestly, we should just require `app_url` to be configured in general.  That would be the most future-proof solution here.

**Additional context**
The [create_user_for_contacts transition](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/reference/app-settings/transitions/#create_user_for_contacts) requires the `app_url` to be set in order to function.

title: chore: update GH action config to not require translations for publish
body:
# Description

When doing development that requires new translation strings we need to provide _values_ for the translation keys for each of the required languages or else the `translations` job will fail in CI.  However, early in the development process we may not know all the needed translation strings (or how they will eventually be used/displayed). Finalizing the UX often comes towards the end of development. That is the point where our [translation process](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/community/contributing/translations/#adding-new-keys) indicates we should reach out on the forum to ask for help translating the strings.  

I think it is useful to have the `translations` job continue to fail until values are actually provided for the required languages, but I would also like the CI run to still publish the Docker images for the branch even if `translations` fails. This will allow for easier manual testing (e.g. using the docker-helper to spin up instances from the branch images) without having to hack anything (like updating the workflow config or including placeholder translation values).

The CI is still in a "Failing" state when the `translations` job fails even if `publish` runs and passes successfully.  So, you still cannot merge a PR where the `translations` job fails.

<!-- COMPOSE URLS GO HERE - DO NOT CHANGE -->
