title: Investigate adding a relational database management system to cht core
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
CouchDB does not allow truly arbitrary queries, and for large datasets, Mango queries can be prohibitively slow.

To query CouchDB effectively, map-reduce views must be created, but these have several drawbacks:  
- They can compete with each other for resources, which can affect replication performance.  
- They use a significant amount of additional disk space, even when compacted and not reindexing.  
- They complicate upgrades because any changes require rebuilding indexes, which consumes large amounts of storage and can take a long time.

CouchDB’s schemaless nature also has limitations:  
- No enforced data consistency between related documents.  
- No explicit constraints (e.g., primary keys, foreign keys).

Separate projects are currently needed to overcome these limitations:  
- **cht-sync** or **couch2pg** for analytics and building dashboards.  
- **cht-interoperability** custom mediators for interoperability.

These require additional infrastructure and monitoring, and their data can easily become out of sync with the primary database in CouchDB:  
- For `cht-sync` and `couch2pg`, synchronization between CouchDB and PostgreSQL could be slow or stalled.  
- `cht-interoperability` relies on outbound push, which could be misconfigured, not running, or queued.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Allow `cht-core` to use a relational database management system (PostgreSQL) directly, without relying on a separate repository or external `couch2pg` process.

This would involve defining a relational schema for CHT data, similar to the one already in `cht-pipeline`.

Data inserted into CouchDB would be mapped to this relational schema and then inserted or updated in PostgreSQL. Possible approaches include:  
1. Move most of `cht-sync` into `cht-core`, with an integrated `couch2pg` process polling the changes feed, and use a built-in dbt process to map documents into tables.  
2. Use an integrated `couch2pg` process within `cht-core` to fetch data from CouchDB, but map documents to tables without dbt.  
3. Write directly to PostgreSQL whenever documents are written to CouchDB.

**Potential Use Cases**
- cht-sync:  
  - A separate database for dashboards and analytics would still be needed to avoid resource contention with the CHT.  
  - Building performant dashboards would be easier and more straightforward than querying schemaless JSON documents.  
  - Data freshness and accuracy would improve without relying on an external `couch2pg` process.

- Interoperability:  
  - A relational database is better suited for API development, which may require more flexible queries than map-reduce views can provide.  
  - `cht-interoperability` would no longer require outbound push, which is difficult to configure and architecturally awkward.

- Support & debugging:  
  - Developers could run arbitrary SQL queries for debugging, ad-hoc analytics, and exploration without creating temporary map-reduce views.

- **CHT Datasource**:  
  - Changing or developing new `cht-datasource` endpoints would be easier with more flexible query capabilities.

This list is not comprehensive; having a relational schema that is reliably up to date and queryable without defining map-reduce views could be useful in other contexts as well.

title: Investigate huge couchdb compaction metadata files
body:
**Describe the issue**
Couchdb compaction creates metadata and compaction files when running compaction for a shard.
These can many times larger than the size of the shard; largest observed was ~450GB for a shard of 12GB, 37x larger.
If compaction is run on many shards at the same time, and for more than one database, this can use terabytes and eventually use up all available storage space on the instance.

This causes couchdb to crash, and especially the compaction process is aborted.
These metadata and compaction files are then not automatically removed.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Couchdb should be able to run compaction withot using an unreasonable amount of storage space.
The extreme difference between the size of the metadata file and the shard file suggests that this is not normal, something in the compaction process is going wrong, and we need to investigate what exactly it is.

If this is "normal" and there is no way to prevent these extremely large files, the compaction process needs to be configured to avoid running compaction for all shards at once. There is a tradeoff there because if the shard is too fragmented, it makes compaction even larger and worse, so it's necessary to make sure compaction is able to keep up running fewer shards at a time.

But until proven otherwise, I would assume that this isn't normal and focus on what why exactly these metadata files are so large.

title: Support custom UI Extensions
body: **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** We recently encountered a syncing issue affecting CHWs for an extended period - over two months in some cases. Unfortunately, this was only discovered at a very late stage, which caused serious concern about potential data loss (e.g., cache clearing or stolen devices) and made resolving the issue a very high priority - right as other pressing work was underway. A tool to proactively indicate device connectivity or syncing issues would have reduced both downtime and overall impact. This feature would allow us to take a more proactive approach rather than just reacting after problems occur. **Describe the solution you'd like** It would be great if each implementation/flavour of CHT had the ability to configure or create pages specific to their context. For example, in our context, we require four screens: 1. **Connection/Sync Status** - Display CHWs’ device connection and syncing information so that we can identify issues such as syncing failures, device connectivity problems, or SIM/APN misconfigurations early. 2. **Integration Screen (iframe)** - Embed other apps we manage, so that CHAMP becomes a one-stop shop for all user needs without requiring navigation to a new browser tab. 3. **Landing Page** - A central hub for links to other pages, training materials, and additional resources. 4. Deduplicate Page - A space where, retroactively and on every sync, duplicates can be displayed for CHWs to address. The backend would flag items it cannot merge (that require human review), and once confirmed by a CHW as potential matches, OTLs would sign off and the data would be sent back for processing. These screens may not be relevant to every implementation, so the ability to add only the content you need, without affecting the wider community (until they require it), would be ideal. **Describe alternatives you've considered** Build each required screen directly into our fork of the app. **Additional context** Configurable pages were initially discussed with Nicole on the [UI Evolution](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/the-ui-evolution-of-the-cht/3515/10) forum thread. -------------------- Assets for Release Notes based of [_**draft**_ solution in PR](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/11050). As a draft this is subject to change https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44828b7b-526b-44f3-9a42-7c8e23f1a72d

title: Support Centralized SMS Gateway of Nepal run by Department of IT
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The Department of IT, Nepal has been running the centralized SMS gateway for a few years. Initially, it was focused on sending Bulk SMS, but now it can send A2P (Application to Person) SMS via API. Our goal is to enable CHT core to use this gateway for sending SMS messages in our Ministry of Health projects.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

We would like the CHT core to natively support the government-run SMS gateway of Nepal. By adding this support, our Ministry of Health projects can utilize the provided REST API to send SMS messages directly through this official gateway.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
1. RapidPro Messaging Gateway: We explored using RapidPro's External API, but encountered a limitation. The DoIT API does not support the international phone number format, which is a requirement for RapidPro.
2. RapidPro Webhook: Another option was to call the SMS API webhook via a RapidPro flow. However, this approach is inconvenient and introduces intermediate dependencies like CHT outbound and RapidPro flows, complicating the setup and maintenance.
3. CHT outbound: We could call the DoIT endpoint directly using CHT outbound, but it would not work for scheduled messages. Also, it would be difficult to handle multiple SMS per report (although DoIT API supports this).

**Additional context**
- DoIT Centralized SMS gateway: [Integration Guide](https://sms.doit.gov.np/developer-guide/#/)
- Limitations:
  - The SMS service is currently outgoing only (A2P: Application-to-Person). It does not support replies or incoming messages (SMS from a person).
  - It does not provide the status of sent messages via API; status checks are available through a web dashboard.
  - This service is restricted to government entities. They must sign an agreement with the Department of IT and potentially incur upfront and operational costs.

title: Sometimes running CHT via developer setup results in errors, 404 on /medic
body: **Describe the issue** @jkuester , @lorerod and @mrjones-plip all saw an issue that was hard to reproduce that when they ran the [developer setup](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/community/contributing/code/core/dev-environment/#the-happy-path-installation) that showed: * Errors in people tab: `Error fetching people` * Errors in Admin section on Users tab: `Error fetching users` * Console showed errors like `GET http://localhost:5988/medic 404 (Not Found) There was some thoughts that maybe downgrading from `master` to a branch like the Hosting TCO branch `9542_freetext_tco` might have caused, but this turns out to not be true. @jkuester tried: > Okay, well after a few hours of tinkering, I have been completely unable to repro these errors at all... :disappointed: Here is everything I tried: > > * Fresh install running couch from master (4.21.0-alpha) - works > * Downgrading Core to 4.20.x with Couch running 4.21.0-alpha works. > * Downgrading Couch to 4.20.0 works > * Upgrading Core back to master (with Couch on 4.20.0) works > * Running Couch 9542_freetext_tco with core master works > > All of this with Node v22.17.0. As well, here's some screenshots: **Describe the improvement you'd like** Figure out how to reproduce and solve the error **Describe alternatives you've considered** Really, it's filing this ticket and hope no-one every finds this again 🤞

title: Staging an upgrade with view changes on a large database causes couch http server to become unresponisve
body:
**Describe the bug**
When staging an upgrade, the CHT api server "pre-warms" any views that were changed by creating staged design documents, then sending a GET request to all the view endpoints for all views in all staged design documents.
When the database is large enough, indexing will take a long time and these requests will wait for 1000 seconds then time out.

An unknown process is causing this process to be run multiple times, which continuously sends more and more of these these view requests until they hit some limit.

The nginx and haproxy connection limits are quite high, so the limit they hit is the maximum number of acceptor processes in couchdb which by default is 2048.
When this limit is hit, new connections to couch's http process timeout, and couch appears to be unresponsive, although it is still running indexing normally in the background.

**To Reproduce**
1. Create an instance running 4.11.0
2. Using test-data-generator, upload at lest 10GB of data in data_record and contacts. At least 10GB is needed so that view indexing takes long enough for open requests to build up. 
3. Go to the upgrade page and click stage next to 4.21.0 to stage an upgrade.
4. Wait 10 minutes, or monitor current open connections at `/haproxy?stats`
5. When enough time has passed, or current open connections exceed 2048, go to any page and it will return 503 service unavailable.

**Expected behavior**
Pre-warming indexes by querying the view endpoints may not be necessary at all; creating the new staging ddocs will trigger indexing. 
If it is necessary, additional controls should be added so view indexing is run only once.

**Environment**
- Version: 4.11.0 upgrading to 4.21.0

**Additional context**
I'm not sure what exactly is triggering the multiple requests.
They are coming from https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/c06a703be4e26623e08f374b0e3cdf815c885ba0/api/src/services/setup/view-indexer.js#L62
The [v1 api upgrade controller](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/c06a703be4e26623e08f374b0e3cdf815c885ba0/api/src/controllers/upgrade.js#L11) could cause multiple requests, but the upgrade page actually polls the v2 version, which shouldn't.
[check-install](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/c06a703be4e26623e08f374b0e3cdf815c885ba0/api/src/services/setup/check-install.js#L99) also calls indexStagedViews, but it should run only once when the api starts.

It may be a moot point if the fix is to remove indexStagedViews entirely.

title: feat(#10224): Configurable Page Plugin POC
body:
Related issue: (#10224)[https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10224] # Table of Contents - [Introduction](#introduction) - [Config Run Down](#configuration-run-down) - [The Table Template](#the-table-template) - [The Iframe Template](#the-iframe-template) - [The Grid Template](#the-grid-template) - [The Dynamic Template](#the-dynamic-template) # Introduction: This solution is still in an early stage and the interface is also basic (for now). The aim of sharing it early is to get more eyes on the work and start a discussion about whether the approach makes sense and how it can be improved. The POC contains four template types to cover the needs we have at the moment. These are used here as examples to show what the plugin can do: - `table` - `iframe` - `grid` - `dynamic` # Configuration run down The configuration is defined in the `app_settings.json` file, under the `pages` block. Multiple pages can be specified, each with a unique identifier: ``` { ... "pages": { "my_page_1": { ... }, "my_page_2": { ... }, }, ... } ``` This identifier is used as a sub-path within the `custom` path in the app router and also serves as the translation key for the page title. Page can be set as either `primary` or `secondary`. Primary pages display in the main app bar while secondary pages appear in the hamburger menu: ``` { "pages": { "my_page_1": { "tab_type": "secondary", ... }, ... "grid": { "tab_type": "primary", ... }, } ... } ``` Page visibility can also be controlled per role using permissions: ``` { "pages": { "my_page_1": { "tab_type": "secondary", "permissions": [ "can_view_my_page_1" ], ... }, ... } ... "permissions": { ... "can_view_my_page_1": [ "national_admin" ], ... }, ... } ``` # The `table` template: This template is meant for data that can be displayed in a tabular form. A page header is included to provide context. It can be defined in two ways: - custom HTML content, which is rendered by the `DynamicTemplateRenderer` (see the Dynamic Template), or - a predefined header with a title (`

`) and an [expansion panel](https://material.angular.dev/components/expansion/overview) for the descriptive content. Controls, for now only a `reload` button, are also provided. The table takes up the rest of the available screen space. ## Table properties: | name | purpose | data type | | ------ | --------- | ----------- | | `page_header` | Defines the purpose of the page and provides context about the presented data | object | | `table_headers` | Defines columns, their order, and customization options | object (see below) | | `on_screen_load` | Code executed when the page loads. Supports async code and should return the object used to populate the table. Vars and context exposed to the function is limited (see function context section) | string | | `on_reload` | Code executed when the reload button is clicked. Receives the above load function in its context and should return the updated table data. | string | ## Predefined header properties: | name | purpose | data type | | ------ | --------- | ----- | | `title` | In-page content title | string | | `description_collapsed` | Description shown when the panel is collapsed | string | | `description_expanded` | Description shown when expanded. Can be plain text or HTML (rendered by `DynamicTemplateRenderer`) | string | | `expanded` | Default state of the panel | boolean | ## Column configuration options: |name|purpose|data type| |------|---------|----------| |`can_sort`| Enables sorting (`asc`, `desc`, or `none`) via the column header | boolean | |`display_value`| Column label shown to the user | string | |`pipe`| Applies predefined transformers (`date`, `decimal2`) | string | |`preprocess_hook`| Function to adjust cell values before display. Limited context is exposed to this function |string| ## Example implementation: A recent bout with syncing issues made it very clear that we needed some form of early detection system/dashboard for when app syncing starts misbehaving. Which could be due to a variety of reasons. For us this was a perfect storm of VPN related issues, very large syncing requests (possible due to attachments), and our nginx configuration being too [strict](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/gateway-timeouts-on-password-reset/4627/2?u=anro). | source | purpose | constraint | example result | |------------------------------------------|----------|------------|------------------| | `medic-logs` 's `connected-users` view | Lists active users with timestamps of their last server interaction. Helps identify connection issues and will be used to build up telemetry results per user | 2 months + 8 months offset to also capture "recently" inactive users | ``` {"id":"connected-user-temp", "key":1747059635000, "value":null } ``` | | [medic-users-meta](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/sync-issues-status-scrutiny/3359/3?u=anro) | Aggregated user docs used to calculate sync and connection results. Batched requests of 25 to handle volume | type: `telemetry`, `ms-since-last-replicated-date` entry exists, captured within the last 2 months, and the telemetry entry belongs to one of the entries in the `connected-users` list. Finally, only certain fields are queried as shown. | ``` { "metadata":{ "user":"medic", "year":2025, "month":6, "day":10, "aggregate_date":"2025-06-11T06:33:47.941Z" }, "dbInfo": { "doc_count": 129, "db_name": "medic" }, "metrics":{ "replication:medic:from:ms-since-last-replicated-date":{ "sum":3274331171, "min":1091443464, "max":1091443953, "count":3, "sumsqr":3573748205794198000 }, "replication:medic:to:ms-since-last-replicated-date": { "sum": 3274329903, "min": 1091442561, "max": 1091443818, "count": 3, "sumsqr": 3573745437894194700 } } } ``` | | [app metrics](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/reference/api/#get-apiv1express-metrics) (planned)| Will show request/response times and sizes | TBC | TBC | ### Metrics tracked | purpose | key | |---------|---------------| | When last the user made contact with the server. | `last_server_connection_date` | | What is the date when the user was able to sync `medic` records to the server | `latest_to_sync_date_ms`, `latest_from_sync_date_ms` | | What is the average amount of days between syncing to medic (adjusted for weekends), should help shed light on irregular syncing behaviour | `total_days_between_up_sync`, `total_days_between_down_sync` | | The gap in activity, is the user unable to log in and perform some action for extended periods | `total_inactive_days` | | Approximate doc count, could help shed some light on why syncing issues are occurring | `latest_approximate_device_doc_count` | Template exposed code context variables: | name | purpose | |-------|-----------| | `dbService` | The full CHT db service to perform various queries | | `moment` | The full [moment library](https://momentjs.com/) to perform date calculations | | `ctx` | At the moment, it refers to the `this` property | | `onScreenLoad` (only to the `on_reload` function) | To augment the page load function | Determining what to expose safely without foreclosing is a tricky endeavour, we would appreciate any guidance. ### Example code output: The metric keys mentioned above are used as the column names as well as the keys for the user specific entries when building up the results for the table. This is to determine which value belongs in which column. The example `on_screen_load/on_reload` output would be: ``` [ ... { "testing": { "last_server_connection_date": 1755169565027, "mostRecentTelemetry": 1754863198738, "latest_from_sync_date_ms": 1754863198738, "latest_to_sync_date_ms": 1754863198738, "latest_approximate_device_doc_count": 119, "total_days_between_down_sync": 51.00020707175926, "total_days_between_up_sync": 51.00020707175926, "total_inactive_days": 4, "entryCount": 4 }, "medic": { "last_server_connection_date": 1755502164104, "mostRecentTelemetry": 1754949582191, "latest_from_sync_date_ms": 1754949582191, "latest_to_sync_date_ms": 1754949582191, "latest_approximate_device_doc_count": 135, "total_days_between_down_sync": 62.26467842592592, "total_days_between_up_sync": 62.26467842592592, "total_inactive_days": 4, "entryCount": 4 }, "national_admin": { "last_server_connection_date": 1755513328477, "mostRecentTelemetry": 1755122398211, "latest_from_sync_date_ms": 1755122398211, "latest_to_sync_date_ms": 1755122398211, "latest_approximate_device_doc_count": 136, "total_days_between_down_sync": 0, "total_days_between_up_sync": 0, "total_inactive_days": 1, "entryCount": 1 } } ... ] ``` The results are in grouped in "buckets" per user. We also capture an additional property `entryCount` which is used to calculate the averages. If we look at the full example config below, we'll see this value is passed back into the `preprocess_hook`. ### Example config: ``` "pages": { ... "table": { "tab_type": "primary", "permissions": [ "can_view_table" ], "template": { "key": "table", "page_header": { "title": "Sync & Connectivity Dashboard", "description_collapsed": "Login data can be delayed by a few days", "description_expanded": "

NOTE: Replication tracking can be delayed by a few days due to how the telemetry records are created. Each time an action is performed on the client, a record will be created in the user's own meta db. The aggregate doc for the previous day is created when the first telemetry item is recorded each day. After which the singular telemetry docs will be removed from the user's specific db to reduce the amount of records required to sync. Sentinel wil then pick up these documents and copy them over to the communal meta database, this aggregation process occurs \"nightly\". Read more on the related CHT Forum Post

The goal is to reduce the need for users to manage multiple browser tabs on their devices. One intended use case is integration with a referral app (we have control over). A user could either navigate to the embedded app through a tab or menu option, or navigate directly to an existing referral entry through a configured contact link. Speaking under correction, because an app route pointing to the embedded site has been registered - we'll be able to append data to the URL when loading up the request. This is still being tested. title: unique() function fails for two subsequent requests
body: **Describe the bug** CHT offers validation [functions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/reference/app-settings/#rules) and we use unique() function to ensure that a pregnancy is not registered twice with same LMP date. This is ensured by the combinations of parameters passed to unique() method. In the above example, CHT ensures that a record with same patient_id, lmp_year, lmp_month, lmp_day combination is not already in the system. However, it has been seen on many instances that if user sends two messages at the same time (up to 20 seconds apart), the CHT fails to unique check and both records end up being written in the database without any error. **To Reproduce** 1. This can be probably reproduced in resource crunch instances with more data by sending/pretending SMS requests. The failure we've seen is on instances with 300K-400K records and running on EKS infrastructure. If you tune your instance to small resource constraint and have more data, then you can send two requests of the same type at once. If you are using docker helper or docker to run CHT instance, you can reduce the specs of docker spec by using following command. ```sh $ docker update --cpus=2 --memory=512m --memory-swap=1g container-name ``` 2. We've used unique check like this on LMP registration. But this can be anything. ```json { "property": "patient_id", "rule": "unique('patient_id','lmp_year','lmp_month','lmp_day')", "translation_key": "registration.lmp_date.duplicate_pregnancy" } ``` **Expected behavior** When unique() check is in place, you expect duplicate report to be marked as not unique. **Logs** The long time is taking between two calls: `calling transition.onMatch() for doc` and `finished transition registration`. View the log below, latest log first. **First Record** ``` 2025-08-17T04:31:54.831 DEBUG: finished transition registration doc 53bb6cd2-9492-4dd9-a9d9-8caa9a4d4d64 is changed seq null 2025-08-17T04:31:41.146 DEBUG: calling transition.onMatch for doc 53bb6cd2-9492-4dd9-a9d9-8caa9a4d4d64 and transition registration s ``` **Second Record (Duplicate of first)** ``` 2025-08-17T04:32:03.217 DEBUG: finished transition registration doc c661e5e3-ff76-44ef-9226-855111592395 is changed seq null 2025-08-17T04:31:46.850 DEBUG: calling transition.onMatch for doc c661e5e3-ff76-44ef-9226-855111592395 and transition registration seq null ``` As you can see, first record took 13s and second took 17s to complete these two action. I've already verified that CHT's validation checks happen right between these two calls. **Screenshots** As seen on the chart, the first record hit the CHT API at 04:31:41.146 and it starts parsing and running validation and completes them at 04:31:54.881. While this document was being processed, the second document also hits CHT API with exact same lmp date and patient id at 04:31:46.850 (~ after 5 seconds of the similar dup doc came, but before 8 seconds of completion of validating and writing that doc). The second document calls unique() and since the first document is not written to the database yet, it will return true and both record consider each other unique and CHT ends up writing both documents without any error. **Environment** - Instance: Gandaki Prod - Browser: Any - Client platform: Any - App: API - Version: 4.21.0 **Additional context** - [cht-gateway](https://github.com/medic/cht-gateway) is used to handle incoming sms from users and they are forwarded to CHT. - There's no issue in unique function if two requests are sent a minute or so apart.

title: Release 4.22.0
body:
# Planning - CHT Community 

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [x] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo.
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Checkout to a new `<issue>-update-version` branch (eg: `1234-update-version`) and set the version number in the `package.json` and `package-lock.json`. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`. Once the version is updated, submit a PR to `master` branch.
- [x] Ensure that issues associated with commits merged to `master` since the last release are closed and mapped to the milestone.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once the PR has been merged into `master`, and the `master` branch has the new version number, then the release process can start:

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development Slack channel using this template:
```
@channel I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by creating a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`) and then push the created tag.
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the team by writing a message in the #development Slack channel:
```
@channel, I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag. 
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make. 
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [ ] The beta tag will automatically trigger the scalability build. Once it passes, download the scalability results on S3 at medic-e2e/scalability/$TAG_NAME. If you do not have access to the scalability results ask someone in the #product-team who has access. Add the release `.json` file to `cht-core/tests/scalability/previous_results`. More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [x] Go to the [Issues tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues) and filter the issues with `is:issue label:"Affects: 4.x.x" ` , replace `4.x.x` with the previous version number. Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label.  
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labelled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [x] Collect known migration steps, descriptions, screenshots, videos, data, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. This information should already be on the issue, but if not, prompt the change author to provide it.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions) and update the EOL date of the previous release. Update the status of any releases that are past their End Of Life date. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page.
- [x] Create a [new release](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases/new) in GitHub, with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, from the release branch created above as the target branch. Click on the "Choose a tag" dropdown and create a tag for the release with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. Ensure the release notes PR from above are merged. Add a link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Once you publish the release, confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Upgrade the [demo](https://demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org/) instance to the newly released version.
- [x] Use cht-conf to upload the configuration from the `cht-core/config/demo` folder to the `demo-cht.dev` server.
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*We're excited to announce the release of {{version}} of {{product}}*

See below for some highlights, read the [release notes]({{<paste-url>}}) for full details.

Following the CHT's support policy, versions {{versions}} are no longer supported. Projects running these versions should start planning to upgrade in the near future. For more details read the CHT [software support documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions).

## {{version}} Highlights

### [{{Highlight 1}}]({{<paste-url to section>}})

{{description of highlight section}}

### ### [{{Highlight 2}}]({{<paste-url to section>}})

{{description of highlight section}}

### [And more...]({{paste-url to section}})

We’ve also implemented loads of other improvements and fixed a heap of bugs.

```
- [x] Go over the list of commits and individually notify contributing / interested community members about the release. 
- [x] Add one last update to the #development Slack channel and use the thread to lead an internal release retrospective covering what went well and areas to improve for next time.
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Replication for offline users can be blocked by indexing
body:
In the CHT, the documents that an offline user can replicate during sync are determined by CouchDB map-reduce views.  
These views define what documents offline users should have access to and index parent child relationships for contact documents, and a "replication key" for all documents.
For replication requests to succeed, these views must be up to date. If they are not, replication requests trigger indexing and **wait** until it finishes.

This creates a bottleneck where users cannot sync until indexing completes.  
- In moderate cases, sync time grows from seconds to minutes.
- In severe cases, sync can take hours and often times out.
- In many of these cases, the replication request itself could complete in seconds if it weren’t waiting for the indexer.

In addition to the performance issue itself, this bottleneck also makes performance harder to understand and analyze.  
Since replication requests block until indexing catches up, the throughput we need to optimize is not just the rate at which users sync. Instead it's the throughput of the background indexing process, which is harder to reason about because it depends on factors such as the number of shard, the number of CPUs, and the number of documents from other processes like sentinel or admin scripts.

(see [this forum post](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/investigate-adding-more-shards-as-a-potential-avenue-for-improved-performance) for more details)

---

## Expected Behavior

**High level:**
- Replication should never block for minutes or hours on indexing.
- Replication performance should degrade gracefully in resource constrained or high-traffic instances.
- Replication performance should not directly depend on documents inserted or updated by other processes.
- When deploying the CHT, it should not be necessary to tune shard counts, CPU allocation, or design documents until usage is very high.

**Low level:**
- Ideally, indexes required to determine which documents a user can access should be updated synchronously as new documents are inserted or updated.
  - This would allow us to optimize directly for the sync rate, rather than indirectly for indexing throughput.  
- However, CouchDB does not support this behavior with map-reduce views, so another option is to improve the indexing process as it currently is.

---

## Possible Solutions

1. **Keep replication dependent on background indexing processes but improve guarantees around freshness.**  
   Some possible examples:
   - Move replication views into their own design doc.
   - Rewrite replication views in Erlang to improve performance.
   - Limit resource contention from other processes.
   - Throttle new inserts/updates if views fall behind. 

2. **Change replication to update indexes synchronously on write.** 
   - Removes the possibility of waiting during replication.  
   - Would require significant changes, since CouchDB does not support this natively.  
   - Addresses the root problem directly.  

Related discussions and references:

- [Investigate adding more shards as a potential avenue for improved performance] (https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/investigate-adding-more-shards-as-a-potential-avenue-for-improved-performance/4831)
- Background on filtered replication and the custom CHT replication:  (https://gareth.nz/couchdb-filtered-replication.html)

title: Add AGENTS.md file
body:
**Describe the issue**
As AI tooling becomes more common, some "standards" are starting to coalesce. One is the use of an [AGENTS.md](https://agents.md/) file to give a quick project overview to coding agents.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We should add an `AGENTS.md` file to this repository (or perhaps multiple files, one at the root and one for each of the sub-projects... 🤔).  The exact _contents_ of the file seem to be mostly free-form markdown that describes the structure of the project, its development environment, and how to run the build/tests.

See [this example](https://github.com/jkuester/chtoolbox/blob/agents/AGENTS.md) of an `AGENTS.md` file I added to chtoolbox.  The contents of that file were mostly generated by [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai). So, if someone is looking for a place to start on this issue, just having OpenCode (or a similar tool) generate the file and then we can tweak it further from there.  

The most important thing is that whatever is in the file needs to be _correct_.  Also, at the very least, I think the file should include:

- Instructions on how to use the npm scripts to build the project and run tests 
    - Be specific on the unit vs e2e tests
- An overview of the project directory structure.
    - Where to put code vs tests, etc.
- Some context regarding code conventions

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

The main downside/risk I see with these `AGENTS.md` file is that they become stale and we forget to update them as the project changes. I think it is a bit early/unclear to see how useful or important these files will be, so it is hard to gauge impact.  Ultimately, I think we should not invest a huge amount of time here, but it seems work giving it a shot and we can quickly iterate based on results.

title: Increase nginx request limit beyond 32MB
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
As part of supporting large attachments for forms, we need nginx to allow requests that are over 32MB: 
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/nginx/nginx.conf#L15C5-L15C25

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We should keep the 32MB limit for json requests, but increase the limit for other mime types, especially media.

title: Improve replication performance by moving docs_by_replication_key to nouveau
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
Replication requires a call to a CouchDb view [`docs_by_replication_key`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/ddocs/medic-db/medic/views/docs_by_replication_key), often with a large payload of keys (depending on the number of contacts the user can see). These queries are the most costly part of replication, mainly because CouchDb is not very efficient in searching views by multiple keys. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Investigate whether moving this view to nouveau improves performance. 

**To Reproduce**
call the `api/v1/replication/get-ids` on `master` vs the feature branch using a large user and compare results. 

**Measurements**
Check the results from above. 
Also run the scalability suite against both branches and compare results. 
Check storage to make sure we don't regress - would be the case when the nouveau view is larger than the couchdb view. 
Check how long it takes to index 10.000 docs in the new view.

title: Investigate alternative ways to store and retrieve large media for forms (beyond PouchDB attachments)
body:
From research ticket [#10135](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10135), we concluded that devices with 1–1.5 GB RAM cannot reliably replicate or preview large media attachments stored as PouchDB attachments. Replication often stalls, crashes, or reports incomplete attachment storage.

Therefore, other approaches must be investigated, for example using the [the local file system api](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/capabilities/web-apis/file-system-access), or hybrid storage approaches, but not limited to that. 

The goal of this ticket is to explore alternatives that could enable CHT Core to reliably support large media attachments across device types.

title: fix(#9992): fix line wrapping in haproxy config
body:
The `base64` command by default inserts newlines every 76 characters for some strange historical reason.
This which breaks the HAProxy health config when the CouchDB username + password is too long. 

Adding the no-wrap flag prevents this and allows long credentials.

title: Remove permission can_view_old_navigation permission
body:
**Describe the issue**
We would like to remove the ability to use the old navigation and be forced to use the new navigation.  This effort is covered in #9665 , but looks to take a lot of work

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
While we still need to remove all the code per #9665 , we should just remove the `can_view_old_navigation` permission in [5.0](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/milestone/90). This will effectively force the change to happen sooner, but we can remove the code and tech debt at a later date in a 5.x and not have to wait until 6.0.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Do nothing and wait until 6.0 to do it all

title: fix(#8027): fix malformed partners doc
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

feat(#1234): add hat wobble
^--^(#^--^): ^------------^
|     |      |
|     |      + - > subject
|     |
|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: chore, feat, fix, perf.

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

<!-- DESCRIPTION -->

When a malformed partners document (content: `{}`) is uploaded via the cht tool, both the Admin app and Webapp
  throw fatal errors that completely block user functionality. The applications assumed the `resources` property
  existed when calling `Object.keys(res.resources)` and when setting partner properties, causing crashes that
  prevented users from accessing or fixing the malformed document.

  **Errors resolved:**
  - Admin app: `TypeError: Cannot set properties of undefined (setting 'partner-name')` when saving partners
  - Admin app: `TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object` when loading partners page
  - Webapp: `TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object` when accessing About page

  **Solution:**
  Added null checks and initialization of empty `resources` object when missing. This allows the UI to remain
  functional, enabling users to view and edit the partners list to correct malformed documents instead of
  experiencing fatal crashes.

  **Changes made:**
  - **Admin controller** (`images-partners.js`): Added null checks to initialize `resources` during document loading
   and attachment operations
  - **Admin service** (`resource-icons.js`): Added defensive null check in `getDocResources` method to return empty
  array
  - **Webapp service** (`resource-icons.service.ts`): Added defensive null check in `getDocResources` method to
  return empty array
  - **Tests**: Added comprehensive unit tests covering all malformed document scenarios, including new controller
  test file

<!-- ISSUE NUMBER -->

 Closes: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8027

title: Make downward sync time configurable
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Right now the downward sync time is pinned to 5 min and there's no way to change it.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We did an experiment to [build a branch](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10199/files)  that pinned this to 30 min instead of 5 min.  It would be great instead if this was an app settings change instead of needing a hard coded branch.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Do nothing and live with 5 min interval, continue to build one off branches as needed.

**Additional context**
It was theorized that eCHIS KE would see reduced server load if we made all clients sync at 30 min interval instead of 5. Given that eCHIS KE may (or may not!) want this in 5.0+, it seems logical to expose this as a configurable setting to admins.

title: Couchdb index views definition need to be updated to accomodate app hierarchy
body:
**Describe the bug**
CHT uses a lot of index views for it's various functionality, however the filtering for types is hardcoded in most of the views to what used to be traditional CHT hierarchy. Most of the CHT deployments no longer use the `district_hospital` -> `health_center` -> `clinic`, `person` after the introduction of [configurable hierarchy](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/reference/app-settings/hierarchy/) after CHT 3.7. However, underlying index views were not updated and since they are being queried in a lot of places, it might also have a lot of performance issue. 

**To Reproduce**
1. View all views in [ddocs](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/ddocs). For example, [contacts_by_type](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/contacts_by_type/map.js). They all use the traditional hierarchy and filter accordingly and sort accordingly. 

One of the impact of this is the places are not shown in correct order as expected on the instances where the hierarchy type is different. I haven't looked into too detail in other views and their usages, but this might have also caused performance issue in instances without the default hierarchy. 

**Expected behavior**
These views would be more useful and meaningful if indexes can use the app's actual hierarchy. Possibley reading from app_settings or somewhere else. 

**Environment**
- Instance: Any instances using custom hierarchy. For example: MoH Ke, MoH Nepal
- Browser: Any
- Client platform: Any
- App: webapp, admin, sentinel, api
- Version: 3.7+

core

    const bootstrap = () => bootstrapApplication(AppComponent, config);

<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

feat(#1234): add hat wobble
^--^(#^--^): ^------------^
|     |      |
|     |      + - > subject
|     |
|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: chore, feat, fix, perf.

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description
Change the graphql query from `getCommitsForRelease` function to get the list of co-authors by commit instead of just the actual author of the commit, and update the `formatCommits` function to support the list of authors. Part of this change was using a Set instead of an array because the Set is more efficient when we need to check for duplicates.

Closes #10023

title: Branch name escape logic broken for semver
body:
**Describe the issue**
We recently [updated our branch name escape logic](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/commit/61dc6b) to be compatible with Docker image tag syntax.  Unfortunately, we expanded the scope of the our naming schema to include `_`, which is valid for Docker image tags, but _is not valid semver_.  

I think we also use this value as "version" reported by the api server on development instances. Now we have [tests failing](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/runs/17690892325/job/50284597397?pr=10284) when the git branch name contains `_`.  

>   1) routing
>         unauthenticated routing
>           should display deploy-info to authenticated users:
>       AssertionError: "5.0.0-dependabot-npm_and_yarn-eslint-9.35.0.17690892325-1757733124020" is not valid semver: expected null to be truthy
>        at /home/runner/work/cht-core/cht-core/tests/integration/api/routing.spec.js:179:16
>        at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:105:5)

This is causing problems with the dependabot PRs because they often use branch names like: `dependabot/npm_and_yarn/eslint-9.35.0`.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

I think we simply need to make another update to our [branch escape function](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/61dc6b44f96bb0e90f28a51f3c7c817812429574/scripts/build/versions.js#L13) so the regex is `[^A-Za-z0-9.-]`.  This will cause all the `_` in the branch name to be replaced with `-`.  

To test the change:
- Checkout a branch with a name containing `_`.
- Update the [rounting.spec.js file](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/58a5e7d901c5946c4cdebd23611bf13db1c35b3f/tests/integration/api/routing.spec.js#L72) and set `describe.only` so only the tests in this file get executed.
- Try running the test test to make sure you can reproduce the failure: `npm run integration-all-local`.  
- Update the branch escape function as suggested above.
- Re-run the tests and confirm they all pass.

title: fix(APIs): CORS misconfiguration for credentials transfer
body:
### Summary
A server can send the `"Access-Control-Allow-Credentials"` CORS header to control when a browser may send user credentials in Cross-Origin HTTP requests. when the `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` header is `"true"`, the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header must have a value different from "*" in order to make browsers accept the header. Therefore, to allow multiple origins for Cross-Origin requests with credentials, the server must dynamically compute the value of the `"Access-Control-Allow-Origin"` header. Computing this header value from information in the request to the server can therefore potentially allow an attacker to control the origins that the browser sends credentials to.



### Description Of Changes
Fix this problem, we need to ensure that when `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` is set to `'true'`, we do not blindly echo any requested origin. This is best accomplished by introducing a whitelist of allowed origins and only setting `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` if the requested origin is strictly present in the whitelist. This matches the secure pattern described in the provided background. The fix should be applied inside the middleware added in lines 148–159 within `api/src/routing.js`. We should define a static array or object of allowed origins, check if the value in `req.headers.origin` matches one, and only then set `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. We must also ensure we never respond with `"null"` or `"*"`. We can keep the warning to further discourage unsafe usage.

To implement this, we need:
- An array or object (whitelist) of allowed origins.
- A sanitation/validation check in the middleware before setting the header.
- If the requested origin is not allowed, do not set `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` (or explicitly reject the request with a 403 error, though for compatibility we may prefer just skipping the header).

### References
[CORS, Access-Control-Allow-Origin](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Access-Control-Allow-Origin)
[CORS, Access-Control-Allow-Credentials](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Access-Control-Allow-Credentials)
[CORS Misconfigurations for Bitcoins and Bounties](http://blog.portswigger.net/2016/10/exploiting-cors-misconfigurations-for.html)
[CORS for developers, Advice for Resource Owners](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-cors-for-developers/#resources)

title: Requests will fail due to `fetch` implementation if headers are not sent within 5 minutes
body:
**Describe the bug**
We switched to `fetch` for all CHT internal or external requests: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/shared-libs/couch-request/src/couch-request.js#L209

However, `fetch` has an undocumented uneditable internal timeout of 5 minutes when waiting for headers. More details can be found [in this issue submitted against the node repo](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/46375). 

This means that any request we make, internally or externally, that does not receive headers within 5 minutes, will fail with this error: 

```
node:internal/deps/undici/undici:15445
      Error.captureStackTrace(err);
            ^

TypeError: fetch failed
    at node:internal/deps/undici/undici:15445:13
    at async /home/diana/.config/JetBrains/WebStorm2025.2/scratches/fetchtimeout.js:2:13 {
  [cause]: HeadersTimeoutError: Headers Timeout Error
      at FastTimer.onParserTimeout [as _onTimeout] (node:internal/deps/undici/undici:6821:32)
      at Timeout.onTick [as _onTimeout] (node:internal/deps/undici/undici:528:17)
      at listOnTimeout (node:internal/timers:608:17)
      at process.processTimers (node:internal/timers:543:7) {
    code: 'UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT'
  }
}
```

**Environment**
- App: api, sentinel
- Version: 4.17+

**Additional context**
I have accidentally run into this while I was running some performance tests, where I was requesting an endpoint that took more than 5 minutes to send headers. There have been no reports of this happening in production, but I am not expecting quick reports - due to how meticulous troubleshooting needs to be to reach this. 

As a workaround, I will investigate if: 
- PouchDb has the same issue
- if node-fetch library has the same issue

title: chore(#10294): correct branch escape logic for valid SemVer
body:
Closes #10294

### Description

The branch name escape logic was recently updated to be compatible with Docker image tags, which allows the `_` character. However, this output is also used as a SemVer pre-release version for development instances, and SemVer does not permit underscores.

This caused integration tests to fail with an `invalid semver` error on branches with names containing underscores, such as those automatically created by Dependabot (e.g., `dependabot/npm_and_yarn/...`).

### Implementation

This change updates the regular expression in the branch escape function to replace any character that is not a letter, number, dot, or hyphen with a hyphen (`-`).

Specifically, the regex was updated to `[^A-Za-z0-9.-]`, which now correctly converts underscores to hyphens, ensuring the generated version string is always SemVer compliant.

### Testing

I have successfully verified this fix locally by following these steps:
1.  Created a branch with an underscore in its name (`fix/semver_underscore_issue`) to reproduce the test failure.
2.  Applied the code change.
3.  Ran the full `npm run integration-all-local` test suite and confirmed that all tests passed, resolving the original assertion error.

title: More easily allow user-devices API  to be called
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Right now if you call the `/api/v2/export/user-devices` [API](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/reference/api/#get-apiv2exportuser-devices), it can take a very long time on very busy/very large instances.  If it takes more than 3600 seconds, it will timeout because of built in [maximums](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/b907fd210389e839b6c86acf6c1d92fda42a31c5/nginx/nginx.conf#L13). 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
An easy way to call the `user-devices`.  This could possibly be extending the time out for this one API path or improving the performance of the API to take <1hr or run in a batch mode and be notified when the process is done or other easy to use solution!

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
A work around was found to log into the VM where the CHT instance is running and make the call directly against the API container, bypassing `nginx`.  This looked something like:

1. ssh to production server
2. find IP of API instance `docker inspect  --format "{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}" $(docker ps -q --filter="name=api")`
3. call `tmux` 
4. using the IP from prior command and the production `medic` password, call the API via `curl` and save the output to a file: `curl -qs http://medic:<password>@172.18.0.5:5988/api/v2/export/user-devices > user-devices.json`
5.  disconnect from `tmux` with `ctrl + b` then `d` and disconnect from SSH
6. wait however many hours you need to 
7. ssh back into production server, connect to existing `tmux` with `tmux a`
8. if the process is still running, go to step 5
9. if the process is not running exit `tmux` and you're done 

**Additional context**
A national deployment had this happen on 5 instances and had to use the above work around. A large instance with per-existing heavy CPU use is currently taking over 3 hours to run.

title: Allow CHWs to filter Targets by Previous Month or Current Month
body: **What feature do you want to improve?** Since [4.10.0 release](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/releases/4_10_0/), supervisors can view the previous month's _Aggregate Targets_. It would be awesome if CHWs could also view `Last Month's` metrics in their Targets page (Analytics / Performance page). **Describe the improvement you'd like** Utilizing the same design and approach used to filter aggregate targets, the _chw-previous-performance-squad_ would like to implement a sidebar filter on the CHWs Analytics page to allow CHWs to view the `Previous Month` targets. - We will show and indicator (upto previous month) for the `All Time` targets when previous month is selected. **Describe alternatives you've considered** - CHWs task module can generate reports to view performance of previous months. However, this is not feasible because It is impossible for CHWs to review targets when they do not have tasks. - Add Indicators in the contact summary. However, this is not ideal because contact summaries already have a lot of details that generally focus on service delivery **Additional context** - The rationale for this suggested improvement is to support CHWs in seeing how their performance has changed from the previous month to the current month. - Additionally, being able to view previous month targets is important for CHWs who receive compensation for their previous months work. Here is a screenshot mock up of how the squad envisions implementing the feature.

title: Update custom reduce functions to use built-in reduce where possible
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
CouchDb custom reduce functions are notoriously slow. 
https://docs.couchdb.org/en/stable/maintenance/performance.html#built-in-reduce-functions
We have some reduce functions that can easily be updated to use the built-in ones. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
1. Replace reports_by_form reduce to _count https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/67bb273e2d20b775b27a6c0bdf20b169284aff1d/ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/reports_by_form/reduce.js#L4-L3

2. Investigate if we can replace `messages_by_contact_date` reduce function to be built-in
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/67bb273e2d20b775b27a6c0bdf20b169284aff1d/ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/messages_by_contact_date/reduce.js#L10-L9

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Leave them as they are. 

**Measurements**
Measure the time it takes to index 100.000 documents using the custom reduce vs the built-in reduce. Make sure the 100.000 documents would get indexed by the targeted view. 

**Additional context**
Thank you @1yuv for stumbling across this!

There is an old, orphaned page in app management that allows you to configure targets (`/admin/#/targets`). We should remove this page

We could maybe try to encourage two way sync of app settings server -> client and also server <- client

title: Identify and remove all unused couchdb views
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
We have some discussions ongoing on forum and community where CHT is not performing fast or is taking too much space. It appears that there are some views that were created in the past that are still on the codebase and that get created on all instances even though there's no specific use of those views. These viewes consume unnecessary disk space on the couchdb. 

For example, there's a view [data_records_by_anestor](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/ddocs/medic-db/medic-scripts/views/data_records_by_ancestor) which doesn't have any usage on CHT.  Some of the views on this` medic-scripts` folder may have been used somewhere outside of cht-core for some functionality of CHT. But view like `data_records_by_ancestor` doesn't appear to be used and if you look at the code, the file the code mentions it's being used no longer exists on repo.

If there are views that are not used and still being created, they consume unnecessary storage and CPU and RAM while running view warming process as well. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Identify all unused views and remove them safely. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Leave as is

**Measurements**
For a lumbini-ne a `medic` database with 5.3 GB data has 2.1GB views on `medic-scripts` folder only. 

**Environment**
- Instance: Any
- Client platform: Any
- App: Couchdb
- Version: All

title: Don't retry replication failures due to timeout
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
There are users on eCHIS Kenya with more than 200,000 documents. When these users attempt to initial replicate, a request is sent to `/api/v1/replication/get-ids` which times out after 1 hour (502 Gateway Timeout). The client automatically retries this request. The consequences of this can be even more severe for CHT because requests which are aborted by NGINX are not aborted by CouchDB.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Heavy requests failing due to timeout (502) should not be retried by the client. This leads to a single user interaction which generates continuous load on a CHT server for >3 hours. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->

**Additional context**
[Deciding to Retry](https://sre.google/sre-book/handling-overload/) from Google's SRE handbook. Our implementation leads to what they are calling a "combinatorial explosion".

title: Collect telemetry when user filters targets by previous month
body:
Currently in `webapp/src/ts/components/filters/analytics-filter/analytics-filter.component.ts` we log the telemetry with `this.telemetryService.record('sidebar_filter:analytics:target_aggregates:open');`.  This tells us when the filter has been _opened_ but does not indicate the user actually selected the Previous month.

We should probably collect another telemetry entry when the user actually filters by "Previous month".  Maybe something like: `sidebar_filter:analytics:previous_month`.

One interesting question is if we need to worry about distinguishing between filtering on the aggregate targets vs normal targets when it comes to collecting this telemetry data... 🤔 My initial thought here is that while the UI/features are similar, the motivations for the users to use the feature might be different enough that it would be valuable to have separate telemetry entries for each...  @Benmuiruri @paulpascal thoughts?

**Describe the bug**
This a scenario where a user's permissions are revoked, but those permissions are not reflected in the app.

title: Support API key authentication for accessing APIs
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, accessing CHT Core APIs requires username and password credentials. For integrations and automated systems, this can be cumbersome and less secure to manage compared to API keys. Also, if partners just want to allow access to certain api keys, they still need to provide user name and password, which grants access to other unwanted resources. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Enable API endpoint to be authenticated with authentication key and provide access to required endpoints from there. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Use as is which either restricts access to API, or exposes unnecessary security concerns for partners. 

**Additional context**
To implement #8340 on authenticated endpoint, it'd be better to have this feature added. Also, if any of the api endpoint requires authenticated access, they can use API endpoint.

title: Add support to cht-datasource for retrieving target intervals
Add support to cht-datasource for querying target intervals by contact ids
body:
NOTE: This issues depends on functionality being implemented in https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10343.

The existing [target aggregate](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/supervision/chw-aggregate-targets/) functionality needs to be able to load the target docs from the current reporting period for all "supervised" contacts.  

To support this functionality in cht-datasource (backed with a REST endpoint that _could_ be called by online users) we will need to change up the approach a bit.  Currently the target aggregates service [queries for the current target docs](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/bb9277a0fbe97285e84e67bf1fcfa6c43bd2749e/webapp/src/ts/services/target-aggregates.service.ts#L83) by just grabbing every `target` doc for a specific reporting period.  In the context of an offline user, this is basically what you want. You get the target docs for all the users that you have access to. For an online user, this would load the `target` docs for the reporting period _for all users_.  

When we implement this in cht-datasource we should modify the flow.  We take as a parameter the contact ids we want to load target docs for.  Then we make the same `all_docs` call to get all the target docs for the reporting period, but we set `include_docs: false` so only the ids are returned.  Then we filter the ids based on the ones that include one of the provided contact ids from the parameter.  Finally we use the remaining target ids to load the `target` docs directly by id and return them.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

I have considered a couple other approaches to querying the target docs, but IMHO these approaches are unnecessarily heavy/complex for the problem at hand:

- We could do separate `all_docs` calls for *each* of the `contact_id`s - this would not scale well when there are many child places, lots of round-trips to the DB (though they could be done in parallel).  
- We could add a view index for `target` docs to index the target docs by `reporting_period` and `owner`. This would let us directly query the target docs that we want, but it would be another view index to store (and one that is likely to not see heavy use).  Also this does not take any advantage of the structured `_id` values that target docs have.
- We could add a view index for `user-settings` docs (indexing by `contact_id`). This would mean we could directly query the `user-settings` and get direct access to data about the "supervised users". Then we can just select the `target` docs by _id since we have all the info we need. 
    - I like this because the view could be useful in other contexts besides just targets.  It still seems like unnecessary effort for the current needs (particularly since the webapp currently does not allow online users to load targets/aggregates) but we should keep this in mind for future optimizations.

## Details

### cht-datasource

- Update the `src/qualifier.ts` file to implement:

<details>
<summary>`src/qualifier.ts`</summary>

```ts
/**
 * A qualifier that identifies entities based their association with the identified contacts.
 */
export interface ContactUuidsQualifier {
  readonly contactUuids: [string, ...string[]]
}

export const byContactUuids = (contactUuids: [string, ...string[]]): ContactUuidsQualifier....
```

</details>

- Update the `src/target-interval.ts` file to implement:

<details>
<summary>`src/target-interval.ts`</summary>

```ts

  /**
   * Returns a function for retrieving a paged array of target intervals from the given data context.
   * @param context the current data context
   * @returns a function for retrieving a paged array of target intervals
   * @throws Error if a data context is not provided
   * @see {@link getAll} which provides the same data, but without having to manually account for paging
   */
  export const getPage = (context: DataContext): typeof curriedFn => {
    ...
    /**
     * Returns an array of target intervals for the provided page specifications.
     * @param qualifier the limiter defining which target intervals to return
     * @param cursor the token identifying which page to retrieve. A `null` value indicates the first page should be
     * returned. Subsequent pages can be retrieved by providing the cursor returned with the previous page.
     * @param limit the maximum number of identifiers to return. Default is 100.
     * @returns a page of target intervals for the provided specification
     * @throws InvalidArrgumentError if no qualifier is provided or if the qualifier is invalid
     * @throws InvalidArgumentError if the provided `limit` value is `<=0`
     * @throws InvalidArgumentError if the provided cursor is not a valid page token or `null`
     */
    const curriedFn = async (
      qualifier: ReportingPeriodQualifier & ContactUuidsQualifier,
      cursor: Nullable<string> = null,
      limit: number | `${number}` = DEFAULT_DOCS_PAGE_LIMIT
    ): Promise<Page<TargetInterval>> => {
      ...
    };
    return curriedFn;
  };

  /**
   * Returns a function for getting a generator that fetches target intervals from the given data context.
   * @param context the current data context
   * @returns a function for getting a generator that fetches target intervals
   * @throws Error if a data context is not provided
   */
  export const getAll = (context: DataContext): typeof curriedGen => {
    ...
    /**
     * Returns a generator for fetching all target intervals that match the given qualifier
     * @param qualifier the limiter defining which target intervals to return
     * @returns a generator for fetching all target intervals that match the given qualifier
     * @throws InvalidArgumentError if no qualifier is provided or if the qualifier is invalid
     */
    const curriedGen = (
      qualifier: ReportingPeriodQualifier & ContactUuidsQualifier,
    ): AsyncGenerator<TargetInterval, null> => {
      ...
    };
    return curriedGen;
  };
```

</details>

- Update the `src/local/target-interval.ts` to load the requested target doc to load the target docs.
  - I _think_ the local adapter implementation for `getPage` should be able to leverage the [`fetchAndFilter` function](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/f1bdfc07c0f4b1170e0d8be671cd27aa105baff4/shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/libs/doc.ts#L119) to load a page of  _ids_ for target docs.
    - The `getFunction` should call `allDocs` to load all the ids for the reporting period.
    - The `filterFunction` should filter the ids to only ones that contain one of the given contact UUIDs.
  - Once we get the target ids, we can take them and retrieve the actual target docs and return those as the `data` array for the page.
    - Use another call to `allDocs`, but this time with `include_docs: true` and the target doc ids set as the `keys` option.
- Update the `src/remote/target-interval.ts` to load the target docs by querying the (yet to be implemented) `/api/v1/target-interval` REST endpoint.
- Update the `src/index.ts`. In the `getDatasource` function, add new functions to the `targetInterval` property:

<details>
<summary>`getDatasource`</summary>

```ts
      targetInterval: {
...
        /**
         * Returns an array of target intervals for the provided page specifications.
         * @param reportingPeriod the reporting period for the target intervals
         * @param contactUuids the contact UUIDs for the target intervals
         * @param cursor the token identifying which page to retrieve. A `null` value indicates the first page should be
         * returned. Subsequent pages can be retrieved by providing the cursor returned with the previous page.
         * @param limit the maximum number of target intervals to return. Default is 100.
         * @returns a page of target intervals for the provided specifications
         * @throws InvalidArgumentError if no reporting period is provided
         * @throws InvalidArgumentError if no contact UUIDs are provided
         * @throws InvalidArgumentError if the provided cursor is not a valid page token or `null`
         * @throws InvalidArgumentError if the provided limit is `<= 0`
         * @see {@link getByReportingPeriodContactUuids} which provides the same data, but without having to manually 
         * account for paging
         */
        getPageByReportingPeriodContactUuids: (
          reportingPeriod: string, 
          contactUuids: [string, ...string[]],
          cursor: Nullable<string> = null,
          limit: number | `${number}` = DEFAULT_DOCS_PAGE_LIMIT
        ) => ...,

        /**
         * Returns a generator for fetching all target intervals in the reporting period for the given contact UUIDs.
         * @param reportingPeriod the reporting period for the target intervals
         * @param contactUuids the contact UUIDs for the target intervals
         * @returns a generator for fetching all target intervals with the given type
         * @throws InvalidArgumentError if no reporting period is provided
         * @throws InvalidArgumentError if no contact UUIDs are provided
         */
        getByReportingPeriodContactUuids: (reportingPeriod: string, contactUuids: [string, ...string[]]) => ...,
      }
```

</details>

### api

- Update the `src/controllers/target-interval.js` controller to have a `getAll` function. The controller should call your new cht-datasource function with data loaded from `req.query.reporting_period`, `req.query.contact_uuids`, `req.query.cursor`, and `req.query.limit`.  (See the `src/controllers/person.js` controller for example.)
- Update `src/routing.js` to route `/api/v1/target-interval` to your new controller function.

### Integration tests

- Add tests for the new `/api/v1/target-interval` endpoint functionality in `test/integration/api/controllers/target-interval.spec.js`
- Add tests for the new cht-datasource remote adapter functionality in `test/integration/shared-libs/controllers/target-interval.spec.js`
    - This should basically be a copy of your api endpoint tests but using the `getRemoteDataContext` and the cht-datasource interfaces instead of making direct REST calls.

title: Target aggregates not loading correctly for online users
body:
<!--
**Important**: This is a public repository. Anyone in the world can see what's posted here. If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the bug**
Target aggregates are available for both online and offline users. 
It seems that for online users, they do not work as expected. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Assign your online user to a place and grant them `can_aggregate_targets` permissions. 
2. Update your configuration and make at least one target be an aggregate. 
3. Create a child place under your user's facility and add a primary contact. Create a user associated with this primary contact. 
4. Login with this user visit the targets page. Sync. 
5. Load the target aggregates page with the online user and notice that no values come through. 

**Expected behavior**
The target document that the offline user has just created should appear in the aggregate calculation of the online user. 

Some curious behavior is happening as well. Checking browser logs, it seems that the page tries to load target aggregates from 3 months ago, finds none and then makes the same request to get the same contacts of a contact type multiple times. 

**Environment**
- Instance: local
- App: Webapp
- Version: master but suspecting older versions being affected

title: debug level messages printed on production instances
body:
**Describe the bug**
Per CHT [documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/hosting/cht/docker/logs/#setting-log-level), default log level is `info`, but we're seeing debug messages also printed on CHT API logs. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Go to your terminal and ensure you've access to the CHT production deployment. 
2. Run `kubectl -n instance_namespace logs cht-api-some-random-number | grep 'DEBUG`
3. You will see a lot of DEBUG entries. 

Alternatively, you can browse to observability if it's deployed, or medic's observability and search in the logs there. 

**Expected behavior**
Debug messages should not be logged if CHT's default log level is `info`. 

**Logs**
Below is the log from one of the Nepal's deployment.

title: API Error when upgrading 4.21.1 -> branch

title: fix(#10298): update device_by_user to use built-in reduce [DO NOT MERGE]
body:
<!--

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format

# Description

Updates `device_by_user` reduce function to be built-in `_last`. 

Performance results, querying database with 400.000 telemetry documents:

| branch | time | improvement | 
| --- | --- | ---- | 
| master | 1144s | |
| proposed | 33s | 34 times faster | 

Unfortunately, the new built-in reduce [`_last`](https://docs.couchdb.org/en/stable/ddocs/ddocs.html#last) was added in CouchDb 3.5, which means that upgrades from older versions of CHT, that use CouchDb 3.4 will fail. 

closes #10298
