title: add topics for Hacktober fest
body: We have decided to participate in [Hacktoberfest](https://hacktoberfest.com/participation/). To do so we need to add the `hacktoberfest` topic to the following repos: * [Core](https://github.com/medic/cht-core) * [Docs](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs) * [Conf](https://github.com/medic/cht-conf) * [Android](https://github.com/medic/cht-android) to do so, someone with GH admin perms needs to click the preferences cog and edit the description to include the new topic. It should show up here if have perms: then once in there, I guess add both `hacktoberfest` and `hacktoberfest-accepted`: Once the topic is added, I'll whip up a quick forum post and invite the community to join. As well, I'll respond to the [request we](https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/pull/755#issuecomment-3368014967) had to add the topic. Filing in CHT Core instead of Medic Infra repo for better community visibility \o/

title: fix(#10302): remove target page and related links
body: fix(#10302): remove orphaned Targets page from Admin app # Description This PR removes the deprecated **Targets** page in the Admin app (`/admin/#/targets`). The page allowed configuring targets from the Admin UI, but it was outdated and caused issues by overwriting the local app settings file on the server. These changes would then be overwritten again by CD runs or manual `cht-conf` updates, making the feature unreliable and a worst practice. ### Summary of changes - commented all templates, scripts, and controllers related to the Targets page - commented corresponding tests and references in routes or menus - Verified that the Admin app builds successfully and runs without errors - Confirmed that `/targets` is no longer accessible in the Admin UI ### Impact This cleanup eliminates outdated code, prevents accidental misuse of deprecated functionality, and reduces maintenance overhead. title: Switch to UUID v7 everywhere
body:
**Describe the issue**
UUID v7 is as random as UUID v4, but has an additional prefix nugget based on the unix timestamp. This enables uuids to be sortable based on the time when they were generated. I'm sure we will find some cool applications for this! 

CouchDb is already switching to using UUID v7 by default: https://github.com/apache/couchdb/pull/5699

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Switch to UUID v7 everywhere - including PouchDb (somehow?). V7 is already available in the latest version of the [`uuid` library](https://www.npmjs.com/package/uuid#uuidv7options-buffer-offset)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Keep using uuid v4

title: Duplicate contact detection does not always work as expected
body: **Describe the bug** CHT supports checking if other existing contacts are potential duplicates of the currently edited contact. This was added through https://github.com/medic/cht-core/commit/b965953914d786826ed6160812cc7797d67ae4a9 in 4.19 When the form fields are edited and the contact is no longer a duplicate, the duplicate contact alert should automatically disappear. However it does not. There is an e2e test checking for this interaction, but this test was always invalid due to an inconsistency of how forms were submitted. Once that inconsistency was fixed, the e2e test for duplicate contacts started legitimately failing: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/runs/18498841736/job/52711707609#step:18:2200 **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Create a new contact with name: "Mary", shortname "Jane", 32 years of age, and +40755232323 phone number. 2. Open a new create contact form under the same place as "Mary" and fill the form with same information: "Mary", "Jane", 32 (you can omit the phone number) 3. Notice that you get the duplicate contact alert: 4. Edit the name to be "Marylin" and hit submit and notice that you still see the same duplicate contact alert 5. Edit the short name to "Janey" and hit submit and notice that you still see the same duplicate contact alert **Expected behavior** According to this test: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/b965953914d786826ed6160812cc7797d67ae4a9/tests/e2e/default/contacts/duplicate-contacts.wdio-spec.js#L112 the alert should clear when the form data is changed and the contact is no longer a duplicate. I needed to change the age in order for the contact to be saved. **Video** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f55dade8-cbbf-455a-ba1f-37740a6456ec **Environment** - App: webapp - Version: 4.19+ **Additional context** Discovered after fixing e2e form submit function in https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10381

title: Selectively only index specific / necessary ddocs when upgrading to a new version
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The first step when upgrading to a new version is to download the new ddocs from the builds server and pre-index them. Right now, the algorithm pre-indexes _all_ ddocs from _all_ databases, to make sure that when the new version of API and Sentinel are up, all endpoints are ready to go and functionality can resume seamlessly. 

However, in some cases, indexing only _some_ ddocs might be a good idea because: 
- it would allow us to push changes to auxiliary ddocs that use new features from CouchDb: eg: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10298#issuecomment-3389050668
- for instances with large disk space usage, indexing only necessary ddocs would allow the upgrade without needing to provision a lot of extra disk space

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Some ddocs are required for API to start up, like `medic/_design/medic`, but others are not. We should identify which ddocs are not essential for API starting and create a new install option that will only index the essential ddocs. The full install option should still be available for instances that cannot accept any endoint downtime. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Somehow allow CHT admins to select which ddocs they want to index.

title: Using changes feed with _doc_ids filter causes performance issues.
body:
## Summary
When fetching documents from purging databases during replication and purging, the current implementation uses the `_changes` feed with a `_doc_ids` filter. This causes severe performance degradation when purging databases are large.

The purging databases [are queried](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/e9a0575e590dd54b559a3fc6210a8f1d92e30836/api/src/services/purged-docs.js#L62) [during replication](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/e9a0575e590dd54b559a3fc6210a8f1d92e30836/api/src/services/replication.js#L13), with all document ids that the user has access to.
And [during purging](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/e9a0575e590dd54b559a3fc6210a8f1d92e30836/sentinel/src/lib/purging.js#L123), with all ids matching a purging configuration.

In both cases, the intention is to get all documents from the purging database that match those ids from the medic database. 

### Current Implementation (changes feed)
The `_changes` endpoint with `_doc_ids` filter:
1. Gets every change in the purging database from sequence 0 to the latest change.
2. For each change, filters whether the change should be included in the result (whether its id is in the doc_ids filter list)
3. Performs a **linear search** using `lists:member/2` comparing each change against each doc id in the filter list

This has complexity: **O(n × m)** where n = number of changes, m = number of filter ids

### Real-World Impact
This behavior has been directly observed in a large production deployment.
For a typical sample user:
- They had access to 50,000 documents.
- There were 60,000,000 documents in a purging database.
- Each replication request for that user requires 3,000,000,000,000 comparisons

There is a purged docs cache so that not every replication request requires this, only when the cache cannot be used.
Purging tasks triggered by sentinel have the same pattern with batch_size * number of changes comparisons.

Affected production instances were monitoring using the erlang process list; it was observed that over half of all reductions (a measure of CPU usage) for sampled instances were spent only running those linear searches with `lists:member/2`. 
And up to 60 requests to the changes feed for purging documents were observed running concurrently.
This causes couch to not have enough CPU resources to serve other requests.

### Alternative Implementation (_all_docs)
Using `_all_docs` with `keys` parameter performs a btree lookup for each document id.

This has complexity: **O(m × log n)** where m = number of ids, n = database size

Even with tens of thousands of ids, this scales logarithmically with database size rather than linearly.

## Recommendation

Revert to using `_all_docs` with `keys` parameter for batch document retrieval from purging databases

body:
# Description

At some point the tests broke for the `demo` and `covid-19` configs.  I still think we should [remove the demo config completely](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/proposal-to-delete-demo-configuration-from-cht-core-and-use-default-config-on-demo-instance/4691) (since it is still just a duplicate of `default`), but as long as both of these configs are still in the cht-core repo we should keep the tests running (and run them in the CI).  

To fix the `demo` tests, I literally just copied the forms and test updates from the `default` config.

For the `covid-19` tests, the problem was that the new version of the test-harness/cht-form/enketo broke the workaround that used to work for these forms that depended on input from the Android app integration.  There is no official support in the test-harness for filling out data from the Android app integration, but you used to be able to use the harness to set values on form pages _even when the question was readonly_.  Now this is not possible in newer versions of the test-harness.  Instead, I updated the tests to inject the mock data from the Android integration as part of the `content` initially loaded into the form.  This is a bit more technical/verbose, but IMHO it is actually more "correct" when it comes to testing the form logic...

title: Store pre-purged doc counts per user
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Doc counts for users are a permanent factor for performance, both server-side and client-side. 
We store post-purging doc counts for when they replicate, but there is no visibility on the pre-purge doc counts, a number which impacts server performance. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
When storing user doc counts, also store pre-purging doc counts. 

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/src/services/replication.js#L19

title: Add information about slow aborted replication requests into /users-info responses
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
The `replication-count` log is updated with information each time a user successfully replicates, but not if users are unable to replicate.  Some heavy users never have a successful replication request because it takes a long time or requests timeout after 60 minutes at nginx. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
As an app developer, I am trying to monitor and discover heavy users and I rely on the `/api/v1/users-info` but there is no information for these very heavy users who can't complete replication. I'm hoping to capture something in that endpoint so we can monitor this - maybe even via watchdog one day.

Maybe on aborted request which take more than an hour, could get something like 

```
{
  "aborted": true,
  "processing_time": 60m
}
```

**Alternatives**
Log to the replication limit log how long it takes for every replication request to complete/close (success or failure).

**Additional context**
https://gitlab.echis.go.ke/echis-core/config-echis-2-0/-/issues/2904

title: Add granularity to users over replication limit monitoring
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Right now to find out if you have users over the 10k doc replication limit, you have two options:
* set up [Watchdog](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/hosting/monitoring/dashboards/#overview) and use the "User over replication limit" panel 
* Manually run an authenticated API call to the `/api/v1/users-doc-count` [API](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/reference/api/#get-apiv1users-doc-count) and process the JSON to try and find the user 

In fact, you'll likely have to do both: finding users over 10k docs in Watchdog just gives you a user count.  The API is where you'll find actual usernames.

This is tedious and hard to know when to take action (ie 8 users with 90k docs) and when to not worry (ie 200 users with 10,980 docs)

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
The  `/api/v1/users-doc-count` [API](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/reference/api/#get-apiv1users-doc-count) should be extended to report count of users in 10k groups in addition to the `count1` it gives now:

```json
  "replication_limit": {
    "count":  610
  },
```

To also include a breakdown of users by 10k groups.  This might like this:

```json
  "replication_limit": {
    "count":  9,
    "10k-count", 12
    "30k-count", 8
    "40k-count", 2
    "80k-count", 34
    "150k-count", 22
    "260k-count", 523
  },
```

Where each `*k-count` group denotes users who have that many 10s of thousands of docs.  For example, `"150k-count", 22` denotes that `22` users have between `150,000` and `159,000` docs 

Whether this exact JSON structure is used or another one doesn't matter.  The end goal should be that a CHT admins can easily know how much the different groups of users over 10k doc are affecting their system.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
A recent [forum post](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/cpu-impacts-of-users-with-10k-documents-how-to-fix-them/5413) covers how to do this today which presumably would be the best option.  Additionally, [alerts](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/hosting/monitoring/setup/#alerts) could be put in place on watchdog to proactively alert CHT admins of users over the 10k limit.

**Additional context**
A major national deployment has been chasing down performance issues which largely turned out to be caused by users over replication limits.  Having better systems to more quickly and more easily diagnose this situation would be helpful. 

Another issue was opened to consider [putting a hard limit](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10408) on the number of documents a user can sync.

A [second issue was filed](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10406) to try and track failed sync because of too high doc counts.

title: Put hard limit on number of documents offline users can synchronize
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Right now an offline user can be configured to synchronize an unlimited number of documents. While CHWs will [get a warning](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/releases/3_7_0/#warn-when-replicating-too-many-docs) about synchronizing >10k documents:
* they have little incentive to not continue.  How can they can control the number documents they sync? Should they not try and do their job?
* the cost on the server to synchronize high doc counts can be severely detrimental.  It [has been shown](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/cpu-impacts-of-users-with-10k-documents-how-to-fix-them/5413) that even a few users can negatively impact a server for thousands of other users.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We should add a feature put a hard limit on the number of documents a user can sync.  While Cinque is has just been merged, which should soften the negative impact on the server,  users with high doc counts are still unchecked with no upper bounds.

Admins are very aware of the consequences should be allowed to either raise the limit or turn it off.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Additional training could be done for end users around the meaning of the [warning](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/releases/3_7_0/#warn-when-replicating-too-many-docs).  Server admins could be more vigilant about monitoring and alerting on "[User over replication limit](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/hosting/monitoring/dashboards/#overview)".

**Additional context**
There's another issue to [improve monitoring of users above the 10k](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10407) limit.  Also, the aforementioned [forum post](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/cpu-impacts-of-users-with-10k-documents-how-to-fix-them/5413)  is a real world scenario where a national deployment was having challenges  keeping up with sync demands of users with 100ks of documents.

It may be that the CPU cost to calculate a full, raw document count (tasks, report, contacts etc) is too high and so we may choose to use a more cheap query of just number of contacts as a proxy for all documents.  Additional research could be done to quantify what this max number of contacts is to get numbers based on real world, production data.

A [second issue was filed](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10406) to try and track failed sync because of too high doc counts.

title: Centralized impact repository
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Often times potential new partners wonder: how effective is the CHT ?  Funders may wonder: what impact does the CHT have world wide:  Regional implementers may wonder: how effective could their future CHT deployment be?  Existing partners may ask: how can we easily share high level impact of our CHT deployment with our Ministry of Health?

Today these constituents are reliant on Medic [posting results](https://medic.org/q3-2024-impact-report/) of painstakingly gather metrics from CHT instances that either Medic hosts or through carefully negotiated memorandum of understanding (MOU) to share data.  The partner's side of the data often needs to be sanitized to remove personal health information and personally identifiable information through a process that may be bespoke for each partner.

An easy way for partners to share this data and for Medic to collect it would be a huge benefit to both parties.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
With the upcoming release of 5.0's [impact metrics API](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8340), there's been some discussion about having a Medic sponsored central server to collect anonymous impact metrics from the larger installed base of CHT Instances.  This would be a service that CHT administrators could easily configure to have the [well documented output](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/reference/api/#get-apiv1impact) of the impact API shared to a central service.  

Current suggestion is to make this an explicit opt in by 
very clearly prompting system administrators the first time [CHT Conf](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/community/contributing/code/cht-conf/) is run. They would be instructed their anonymous data impact is being shared to Medic and they can opt out at any time.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Existing process of MOUs could be persisted.  In theory, going forward, this would be simplified when partners upgrade to 5.0 as the impact API will be available to them to easily gather stats and share them or share a user that can remotely authenticate to gather the stats themselves.

**Additional context**
A great model for how this is done can be found in the [Anonymous Impact Tracker](https://www.openfn.org/impact) from [OpenFn](https://www.openfn.org/).  Some key benefits are:
* full transparency with what the data is and how it is used
* incentivizing the larger community to share their own data
* clear language that the data sharing is opt in with the ability to easily opt out a later date (note this is different than proposed above)

There's a whole slew of unanswered questions which will need to be resolved before we can implement this. Some, but for sure not all, are:
* while there was a [forum post](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/exposing-impact-metrics-from-the-api/5381) about the origin impact metric, the community needs to be brought into the loop for this feature as well. Presumably another forum post is best?
* How do we deal with spam?
* How do we deal with dozens of CHT Instances being spun up every day in CI that might auto send their "impact"?
* How do we deal with developer instances who might turn around and run [the TDG](https://github.com/medic/test-data-generator/) to smash 100k pregnancy reports into their instance which would then be shared up?
* As the metrics will be anonymous, do we need a way of associating the metrics to a CHT instance to know which global region it's in, for example?
* If the metrics are anonymous, how would this impact repository be able to generate this data point from the [most recent impact report](https://medic.org/q3-2024-impact-report/) "_Nepal, we added 800 new users and provided online refresher training to nearly 500 health workers across 21 municipalities, along with programmatic feedback and support_"
* Would the presence of a per CHT unique ID, which could sent with the impact metrics, be helpful for the above?  This would greatly ease in de-anonymizing the data though, is that an acceptable risk?
* Should the URL (or URLs) be configurable to where this data is sent so large national deployments could easily collect the data themselves?

title: Label performance data in /api/v1/express-metrics with user's role
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
The `/api/v1/express-metrics` endpoint exposing server performance information for all endpoints.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
The [prometheus-api-metrics](https://github.com/PayU/prometheus-api-metrics) library used by this endpoing includes the ability to add `labels` to each metric. This would let us segment performance data to provide higher levels of  transparency via watchdog.  

One question I am particularly interested in and which came up recently during eCHIS performance investigations is "when CHT replication is slow, which user roles are slowest"?

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->

**Additional context**
Since the  `/api/v1/express-metrics` is public and clear-text, labeling data with usernames is not OK. But exposing roles in clear-text seems fine. Welcome thoughts and debate. Or - what other labels would you want to segment by in watchdog?

title: Investigate and optimize CHT battery consumption
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. It is slow when I [...] -->
CHWs using CHT applications are experiencing significant battery drain on their devices. CHWs operate in low-resource and rural settings with limited power access, often requiring long travel times to reach charging infrastructure (grid or solar-based). High battery consumption directly impacts their ability to visit and provide care to their allocated households, reduces device lifespan, and negatively affects user experience.

Recently, @PhilipNgari engaged some CHWs in Kenya to understand how the eCHIS app ranks in power utilisation. This involved sharing [a 3rd party application](https://www.androidpolice.com/how-to-find-apps-draining-phone-battery/) and getting extracts from their phones, as shared in the [related forum post.
](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/optimizing-cht-apps-for-improved-battery-use-and-sustainability/5420)

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->
We need to 1) investigate and 2) optimize the CHT app's battery consumption.

The goal is to identify battery-intensive operations and implement optimizations that allow CHWs to work longer in the field without requiring frequent charging.

**Measurements**
<!-- Record at least one measurement that you think should be improved. Ex. 5 seconds, 200MB memory usage, etc -->
TODO

**Additional context**
<!-- Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here. -->

- Resource shared by @PhilipNgari about [Essential Strategies and Tools for Assessing Battery Performance in Your Android Application](https://moldstud.com/articles/p-essential-strategies-and-tools-for-assessing-battery-performance-in-your-android-application).
- Resource shared by @mrjones-plip 
> I think we could get some pretty great data by just adding a bit more info [about the battery level](https://developer.android.com/training/monitoring-device-state/battery-monitoring)  to the telemetry data [we're already collecting](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/guides/performance/telemetry/).
That same [developer.android.com](http://developer.android.com/) URL above also mentions detecting when the phone is charging and being more aggressive with battery intensive tasks
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7618

title: Send message state to clear if they are not good to mark for pending
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Many deployments in Nepal use SMS workflow and direct client messaging. Since CHT doesn't have a way to disable SMS recepient direction in case patient or someone in the hierarchy doesnt' have a phone, the message gets sent to the parent hierarchy, which is not the required behavior.

The workaround that deployments are using now is to [form an empty message](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/is-there-a-way-to-disable-sms-recipient-redirection/3921/2) if a phone number doesn't exist. The problem with this approach is, a lot of messages stay in scheduled state forever.
Recently, we had to [clear 62,000 scheduled messages ](https://github.com/medic/config-lumbini/issues/134#issuecomment-3474818745) from the past in one instance.

Leaving these messages in deployments forever like this prevents us from separating actual problem vs error driven logic.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
If a message can not be sent to pending state, it's good to send those message to clear state since we need to that periodically manually to clear the instance.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Leave as is and continue using the error centric design
- Allow a separate flag in CHT to not send message if the user doesn't have a phone

**Additional context**
[Private issue](https://github.com/medic/config-lumbini/issues/131)

title: Add telemetry for how many tasks the users see
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Workflows often get bloated or misconfigured. At this point, there is no way to know how many tasks are visible for a user at a given time except by analyzing data on the server, querying all user tasks, checking their statuses and filtering in the tasks that would be visible in a certain interval. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add a telemetry entry that will store how many tasks the user sees. This entry should be recorded each time tasks are recalculated. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None. 

**Additional context**
Came out of discussions during the task prioritization squad call.

title: Add indicator to targets page when previous month is selected
body:
As noted in the [design doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1zdJ1ySdSbriZODn7BDDAH9Hxg3qT0J9McGUIIrcafIU/edit?tab=t.ufay0fr37c8h#heading=h.s1wiyw3hzx4x) the target cards for the default config that display all-time metrics (and not ones scoped to a reporting period) have a subtitle of "All Time". This could be misleading when a user filters the targets to the previous month because the value show will actually be "up to the previous month".

The "All Time" targets are ones [configured](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/targets/targets-js/#targetsjs) with the date property as 'now' (or not set).  (So the value is calculated from all reports and not just those filtered for a specific reporting period (month).

Currently, the "All Time" subtitle is being populated [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/9337c841e9afd6c25652f534a6f0105f4675bd88/webapp/src/ts/modules/analytics/analytics-targets.component.html#L50), but this is just loading the configured `subtitle_translation_key` value from the target config.  So, with the default config, these target cards show "All Time" as the subtitle, but this translation is totally customizable and the subtitle could be set to anything.  

We need some kind of visual element (either on the page or in the card) that indicates to the user that the values shown are data up to the previous month.

title: fix(#10443): include default training forms in build script
body:
# Description

Closes #10443 

I considered a couple different options with regard to how to handle the necessary changes to the e2e tests (trying to avoid actually nerfing the default config during the test run). Most of the tests run with the admin user and so the Welcome Guide training form was going to pop up each time the user logged in.

1. One option was to just add extra code to the login function (probably the `cookieLogin` function in the login page util) to complete/cancel out of the training at the end of the login operation.  
    - This felt like the approach with the worst performance, though, since we would still be loading/unloading the training form in basically every test.
2. Another way was to write the training report for the admin user (so they would not be prompted to complete the training) [in the `setUserContactDoc` function](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/dd7eea3cb0d5bce98466d259f823cc9ea1013b94/tests/utils/index.js#L697) which gets run once at the beginning of all the tests to bootstrap the user's contact doc.
    - This would have the least impact (since we would only write the training doc once and then could add it to the list of PROTECTED_DOCS so it does not get removed). 
    - The downside of this is that you end up with an extra report permanently in the DB that you cannot easily get rid of. Also, that report affects the integration tests as well (even though it is not needed) since those tests run the same bootstrapping logic as the e2e tests.
3. The approach I ended up taking was to modify [the `setupUserDoc` function](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/dd7eea3cb0d5bce98466d259f823cc9ea1013b94/tests/utils/index.js#L128) so it writes the training doc for the default user along with the `user-settings` doc.
    - I am stretching the meaning of "user doc" in the function name to be "the docs needed for the user" instead of just "the user's `user-settings` doc". :grimacing: But, by doing both in the same function I can write both docs in one DB round-trip.
    - This function is only used by the `login`/`cookieLogin` functions in the login page util.
    - So, when executing a normal login for the default user, it will add the training report (if it does not already exist) before logging in.  This lets us avoid loading the training form upon login without an extra round-trip to the DB (and without leaking the training report into tests that are not using the default user (or are not logging into the webapp).
    - This approach feels most convenient/resilient since the tests can always delete the training report if they don't want to deal with it affecting the test run. Then it will automatically get added again the next time the login is called.

title: User telemetry DB reused when logging in as a different user
body:
**Describe the bug**

When switching to a different user (by logging out  and logging back in as a new user) it seems that the original user's Pouch telemetry DB (storing the user's un-aggregated telemetry data in the browser) gets re-used as the telemetry DB for the newly logged in user. 

I believe the blast radius of this issue is limited to just the telemetry for the current day. The next day after the new user logs in, a fresh telemetry DB should be created for the current user.

(Originally found via @benkags's tests added in https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10371.)

**To Reproduce**

1. On a fresh browser session (nothing cached) login as a user `user-a`
    - Use the browser console to confirm that a telemetry DB is created for `user-a`:
    - `await window.indexedDB.databases();`
    - You should see an entry like `_pouch_telemetry-2025-11-10-user-a` (but with the current date)
2. Log  out and then login again as a different `user-b`
    - Again use the browser console to check which DBs exist.
    - Note that new databases have been created for `user-b` _except_ that no `_pouch_telemetry-2025-11-10-user-b` exists.
    - Telemetry is still being recorded successfully, but it is being stored in `_pouch_telemetry-2025-11-10-user-a`

4. **Expected behavior**

I expected separate telemetry databases to be created for each user.

**Additional context**

When the Telemetry Service creates a fresh telemetry DB for the user for the day, the current username [is part of the DB name](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/602643f1e98b31f19da0bbf31e41d5e6d5d235d2/webapp/src/ts/services/telemetry.service.ts#L59).  However, when subsequent telemetry entries are written to the DB, the telemetry database to use is resolved only by [checking the prefix/format](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/602643f1e98b31f19da0bbf31e41d5e6d5d235d2/webapp/src/ts/services/telemetry.service.ts#L118) and [checking the date value](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/602643f1e98b31f19da0bbf31e41d5e6d5d235d2/webapp/src/ts/services/telemetry.service.ts#L215).  The telemetry service never actually checks the _username_ part of the telemetry DB name before using it....

I have not confirmed this yet, but I expect this has been a problem since at least `4.5.0` (when we refactored telemetry to use a DB per day).

title: fix(#10452): isolate telemetry DB per user to prevent cross-user data access
body:
# Overview
This fix addresses an issue where telemetry databases were not properly isolated per user. The changes ensure that each user can only access and operate on their own telemetry data by adding the current user's name as a suffix to the database name and filtering operations accordingly.

# Checklist
- [x] Code changes implemented to isolate telemetry DB per user
- [x] Database name generation updated to include user context
- [x] Aggregation logic modified to only process user-specific databases
- [x] Telemetry submission and retrieval restricted to current user's data

# Proof
The changes ensure that:
1. Each user gets their own telemetry database with name format including their username
2. Database operations like finding the current DB and aggregating historical data are filtered to only include databases belonging to the current user
3. This prevents cross-user data access and ensures data isolation

Closes #10452

title: fix(#10452): isolate telemetry DB per user and fix race condition
body:
# User telemetry DB reused when logging in as a different user

## Summary
This PR fixes two critical issues with the telemetry service:

1. Fixed telemetry DB isolation issue where databases were incorrectly shared between different users on the same day. The fix ensures that both date AND username are verified when selecting the appropriate telemetry database for a user.

2. Fixed a race condition in the submitIfNeeded method where the isAggregationRunning flag was improperly managed. The flag is now correctly set once before the DB processing loop and reset in a finally block to prevent race conditions.

## Changes Made
- Updated length check in getCurrentTelemetryDB and submitIfNeeded methods from >= 4 to >= 5 to properly handle DB name format
- Restructured submitIfNeeded method to properly manage isAggregationRunning flag with try/finally
- Added test case to verify that different users have separate telemetry databases on the same day

## Testing
- All existing tests pass
- New test added to prevent regression of the user isolation issue

## Verification
- Linting passes successfully
- Changes follow project conventions
- Race condition properly addressed

Closes #10452

It seems to me that this change doesn't fit any of the other categories defined in the [commit message format](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/community/contributing/code/workflow/#commit-message-format) documentation. It feels like "chore" is the closest category, but "chore" was defined as "Non-code" in that documentation. Please let me know if I should assign this change to a different category.

## Should this be broken into parts?

Would smaller commits with focused changes on each of the constant be preferred? For example, one PR for `'mm-online'`, another for `'service-worker-meta'`, and so on.

## `npm run build-dev` throws an error when the constants are used in `admin/src/js/services/session.js`

When I run `npm run build-dev` on this branch, I get an error with StringMap: `Error: StringMap expected string key`. I don't get this error on master.

This is also failing the compile step in github: 
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/runs/19305186560/job/55212091760?pr=10457

title: Configurable SMS Recipient Fallbacks & Disable "Sender" Default
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**

[SMS recipient resolution](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/reference/app-settings/#sms-recipient-resolution): Add alternate recipient(s) and way to disable the default behaviour of sending it back to the sender

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

I am requesting two specific enhancements to the recipient resolution logic:

- Priority/Fallback Lists: The ability to define a list of potential recipients. The system should attempt to resolve them in order and use the first valid phone number found.

- Disable Default Redirection: A configuration option to prevent the system from defaulting to the report sender (submitter) when no recipient is found.

CHT provides several ways to specify the [SMS recipient](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/reference/app-settings/#recipient-values-and-resolutions).

Example Use Case: I want to send a reminder related to a patient in a household.

I can either send it to:
- the patient using `patient.phone`
- or, to the household primary contact with `patient.parent.contact.phone`

I want this instead:

- If the patient has a phone number -> Send to `patient`.
- If patient has no number ->  Send to `patient.parent.contact` (Household Head).
- If neither has a number ->  Do not send the message. (Currently, CHT forces this message to the CHW/sender, which is confusing for them).

Proposed configuration syntax:
  Instead of a single string, allow an array for recipient:
```json
"recipient": [
  "patient.phone",
  "patient.parent.contact.phone"
],
"default_to_sender": false
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Form Calculation: Saving the phone number in the report during submission. Drawback: If the contact's phone number is updated later, the report data remains stale, and the SMS goes to the old number.

- Mustache Logic: I attempted to use {{#patient.phone}} blocks in the message template to suppress content if the number is missing. Drawback: This still triggers the message sending process, resulting in empty, failed messages cluttering the messages tab.

```
messages.registration.a.patient = {{#patient.phone}} Hi {{patient_name}}! You have been registered to our system with ID: ({{patient_id}}). {{/patient.phone}}{{^patient.phone}}{{/patient.phone}}
```

**Additional context**
Related CHT Forum discussion: [Is there a way to disable SMS recipient redirection?](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/is-there-a-way-to-disable-sms-recipient-redirection/3921)

title: Temporary downtime for replication and online search immediately after 5.0 upgrade
body:
<!--
**Important**: This is a public repository. Anyone in the world can see what's posted here. If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the expected behavior**

When upgrading from 4.x to 5.0, there is an initialization period during which CouchDB Nouveau builds new indexes. During this one-time index building process:

* Offline users will experience replication timeouts (1 hour) until indexing completes
* Online users will receive no results when performing freetext searches until indexing completes

**How to observe this**

1. Start with a 4.x instance containing a substantial amount of documents
2. Upgrade to 5.0.0
3. Immediately after upgrade, attempt to search as an online user or replicate as an offline user
4. Services will be temporarily unavailable while indexes build

**Expected timeline**

Once index building completes, replication and search will automatically resume normal operation:
* Small instances: Index building typically completes within an hour
* Large instances: Index building may take up to 24 hours

**Monitoring:** Navigate to `/_utils/#/activetasks` to track `search_indexer` tasks. When these tasks complete, all services are fully operational.

**Environment**
- Instance: NA
- Browser: NA
- Client platform: NA
- App: NA
- Version: 5.0.0 immediately after upgrading from 4.x 
 
**Additional context**
* This initialization period only occurs when upgrading from 4.x to 5.0
* Fresh 5.0 installations are not affected
* Subsequent upgrades from 5.0 to later versions are not affected
* Discovered [when testing 5.0 upgrade on production data set](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10420)

body:
Bumps [js-yaml](https://github.com/nodeca/js-yaml) to 4.1.1 and updates ancestor dependency [rewire](https://github.com/jhnns/rewire). These dependencies need to be updated together. Updates `js-yaml` from 3.14.1 to 4.1.1
Changelog

Sourced from js-yaml's changelog.

[4.1.1] - 2025-11-12

Security

  • Fix prototype pollution issue in yaml merge (<<) operator.

[4.1.0] - 2021-04-15

Added

  • Types are now exported as yaml.types.XXX.
  • Every type now has options property with original arguments kept as they were (see yaml.types.int.options as an example).

Changed

  • Schema.extend() now keeps old type order in case of conflicts (e.g. Schema.extend([ a, b, c ]).extend([ b, a, d ]) is now ordered as abcd instead of cbad).

[4.0.0] - 2021-01-03

Changed

  • Check migration guide to see details for all breaking changes.
  • Breaking: "unsafe" tags !!js/function, !!js/regexp, !!js/undefined are moved to js-yaml-js-types package.
  • Breaking: removed safe* functions. Use load, loadAll, dump instead which are all now safe by default.
  • yaml.DEFAULT_SAFE_SCHEMA and yaml.DEFAULT_FULL_SCHEMA are removed, use yaml.DEFAULT_SCHEMA instead.
  • yaml.Schema.create(schema, tags) is removed, use schema.extend(tags) instead.
  • !!binary now always mapped to Uint8Array on load.
  • Reduced nesting of /lib folder.
  • Parse numbers according to YAML 1.2 instead of YAML 1.1 (01234 is now decimal, 0o1234 is octal, 1:23 is parsed as string instead of base60).
  • dump() no longer quotes :, [, ], (, ) except when necessary, #470, #557.
  • Line and column in exceptions are now formatted as (X:Y) instead of at line X, column Y (also present in compact format), #332.
  • Code snippet created in exceptions now contains multiple lines with line numbers.
  • dump() now serializes undefined as null in collections and removes keys with undefined in mappings, #571.
  • dump() with skipInvalid=true now serializes invalid items in collections as null.
  • Custom tags starting with ! are now dumped as !tag instead of !<!tag>, #576.
  • Custom tags starting with tag:yaml.org,2002: are now shorthanded using !!, #258.

Added

  • Added .mjs (es modules) support.
  • Added quotingType and forceQuotes options for dumper to configure string literal style, #290, #529.
  • Added styles: { '!!null': 'empty' } option for dumper (serializes { foo: null } as "foo: "), #570.
  • Added replacer option (similar to option in JSON.stringify), #339.
  • Custom Tag can now handle all tags or multiple tags with the same prefix, #385.

Fixed

title: Remove medic-scripts from medic database post upgrade
body: **Describe the performance issue** As part of https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10322, we have removed the [medic-scripts]() ddoc from our build. However, this does not mean the removal of the ddoc from instances that upgrade from this version. Our installation script overwrites ddocs, but does not remove any - because we want to allow deployments to create their own ddocs that they maintain (and these ddocs exist). **Describe the improvement you'd like** Instead of entirely removing the ddoc, we should have just removed the views and left the ddoc in place. This would insure that the view space is cleared on upgrade. The removal of the ddoc itself can happen as part of a new major release. **Describe alternatives you've considered** None. **To Reproduce** Steps to record the performance metrics: 1. Install 4.21. 2. Upgrade to 5.0.0-beta.1 3. check fauxton for existent ddocs and notice that `medic-scripts` still exists. **Additional context** Noticed during test upgrade to 5.0.0.

title: Cannot upgrade to 5.x in AWS due to Persistent Volume settings
body:
<!--
**Important**: This is a public repository. Anyone in the world can see what's posted here. If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the bug**
During attempting the upgrade of the demo-cht instance to 5.x, the upgrade hit a roadblock caused by the helm chart configuration, where both CouchDb and Nouveau would need to attach the same Persistent Volume. 
In AWS EBS terms this is called MultiAttach, and most volume types cannot do this (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-volumes-multi.html#considerations)


**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Launch a 4.22 instance in AWS EC2 with a GP2 volume
2. Stage the 5.0.0 upgrade
3. Follow the upgrade steps here: https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/hosting/cht/migration/helm-charts-4x-to-5x-migration/
4. After a while, the instance will either crash or certain features that depend on Nouveau will not work (replication, online user search). 

**Expected behavior**
The upgrade should work. 

**Logs**
Checking pods, the 5.0.0 database containers fail to start, while the old couchdb container is still running (the old version of CouchDb): 
```
cht-api-69477c6f59                   1/1     Running             1 (3h16m ago)   3h22m
cht-couchdb-6ff5bbfc6d               1/1     Running             0               6h52m
cht-couchdb-858666b666               0/1     ContainerCreating   0               3h22m
cht-couchdb-nouveau-69f6d7bd9f       0/1     ContainerCreating   0               3h22m
cht-haproxy-78c94b569                1/1     Running             0               3h22m
cht-haproxy-healthcheck-54d548956c   1/1     Running             0               3h22m
cht-sentinel-f7bd94584               1/1     Running             0               3h22m
```

**Environment**
- Client platform: Kubernetes
- App: helm charts
- Version: 5.0.0

**Additional context**
We believe there are three options to fix this: 

A: The Sidecar Pattern 
Action: Move Nouveau to the same pod as CouchDb so they share storage
Why: Containers in the same Pod share storage and run on the same node automatically.

Option B: Separate Storage 
Action: Give nouveau its own, separate PVC.

Option C: Shared File System (Rare for databases) Use AWS EFS (ReadWriteMany) instead of EBS. 
Note: This is generally not recommended for database data files due to latency and IOPS limitations.

Discussing, we believe that option A is most suitable, because it doesn't require deployments to provision additional disk space for Nouveau, separate from CouchDb.

title: Release 5.0.1
body:
# Planning - CHT Community 

- [x] Create an GH Milestone for the release and add this issue to it.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.
- [x] Ensure that all issues are labelled correctly, particularly ensure that "Regressions" are labelled with "Affects: <version>" labels. The "Affects" label is used in a link in the Known Issues section of the release notes of that version so it has to match exactly. To make sure the label is correct go to the [release notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) and ensure the issue is listed.

# Development - Release Manager

When development is ready to begin one of the maintainers should be nominated as a Release Manager. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR to the release branch. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version patch`.
- [x] Ensure that issues from merged commits are closed and mapped to a milestone.
- [x] Write an update in the #stewardship-team Slack channel summarising development and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The Release Manager is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Manager

Once all issues have been merged into `master` then the release process can start:

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`).
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the community by creating a post titled `<major>.<minor>.<patch> Beta Releases` in the [development](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/development/7) category of the CHT forum using this [template](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/new-topic?title=%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.%3Cpatch%3E%20Beta%20Releases&body=Hi%20Everyone%0AI%E2%80%99ve%20just%20created%20the%20%60%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.%3Cpatch%3E-beta.1%60%20tag.%0APlease%20let%20me%20know%20if%20there%E2%80%99s%20any%20final%20update%20we%20need%20to%20make.%0AIf%20all%20is%20good%2C%20then%20in%2024h%2C%20I%20will%20start%20the%20release.%20Thanks%21&category=development).
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labelled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [x] Collect known migration steps, descriptions, screenshots, videos, data, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. This information should already be on the issue, but if not, prompt the change author to provide it.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Ensure that the release notes PR is merged before moving to next step.
- [x] Create a [new release](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases/new) in GitHub, with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, from the release branch created above as the target branch. Click on the "Choose a tag" dropdown and create a tag for the release with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. Add a link to the release notes page in the description of the release.
- [x] Once you publish the release, confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Upgrade the [demo](https://demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org/) instance to the newly released version.
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT Forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/), under the "Announcements - Releases" category using this [template](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/new-topic?title=Announcing%20the%20release%20of%20%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.%3Cpatch%3E%20of%20the%20CHT%20Core%20Framework&body=%2AAnnouncing%20the%20release%20of%20%7B%7Bversion%7D%7D%20of%20%7B%7Bproduct%7D%7D%2A%0AThis%20release%20fixes%20%7B%7Bnumber%20of%20bugs%7D%7D.%20Read%20the%20%5Brelease%20notes%5D%28%7B%7Burl%7D%7D%29%20for%20full%20details.&category=releases).
- [x] Go over the list of commits and individually notify contributing / interested community members about the release.
- [x] Go to the [Issues tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues) and filter the issues with `is:issue label:"Affects: 4.x.x" ` , replace `4.x.x` with the previous version number. Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label.
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: chore: bump node-forge from 1.3.1 to 1.3.2 in /webapp
body:
Bumps [node-forge](https://github.com/digitalbazaar/forge) from 1.3.1 to 1.3.2.
Changelog

Sourced from node-forge's changelog.

1.3.2 - 2025-11-25

Security

  • HIGH: ASN.1 Validator Desynchronization
    • An Interpretation Conflict (CWE-436) vulnerability in node-forge versions 1.3.1 and below enables remote, unauthenticated attackers to craft ASN.1 structures to desynchronize schema validations, yielding a semantic divergence that may bypass downstream cryptographic verifications and security decisions.
    • Reported by Hunter Wodzenski.
    • CVE ID: CVE-2025-12816
    • GHSA ID: GHSA-5gfm-wpxj-wjgq
  • HIGH: ASN.1 Unbounded Recursion
    • An Uncontrolled Recursion (CWE-674) vulnerability in node-forge versions 1.3.1 and below enables remote, unauthenticated attackers to craft deep ASN.1 structures that trigger unbounded recursive parsing. This leads to a Denial-of-Service (DoS) via stack exhaustion when parsing untrusted DER inputs.
    • Reported by Hunter Wodzenski.
    • CVE ID: CVE-2025-66031
    • GHSA ID: GHSA-554w-wpv2-vw27
  • MODERATE: ASN.1 OID Integer Truncation
    • An Integer Overflow (CWE-190) vulnerability in node-forge versions 1.3.1 and below enables remote, unauthenticated attackers to craft ASN.1 structures containing OIDs with oversized arcs. These arcs may be decoded as smaller, trusted OIDs due to 32-bit bitwise truncation, enabling the bypass of downstream OID-based security decisions.
    • Reported by Hunter Wodzenski.
    • CVE ID: CVE-2025-66030
    • GHSA ID: GHSA-65ch-62r8-g69g

Fixed

  • [asn1] Fix for vulnerability identified by CVE-2025-12816 PKCS#12 MAC verification bypass due to missing macData enforcement and improper asn1.validate routine.
  • [asn1] Add fromDer() max recursion depth check.
    • Add a asn1.maxDepth global configurable maximum depth of 256.
    • Add a asn1.fromDer() per-call maxDepth option.
    • NOTE: The default maximum is assumed to be higher than needed for valid data. If this assumption is false then this could be a breaking change. Please file an issue if there are use cases that need a higher maximum.
    • NOTE: The per-call maxDepth parameter has not been exposed up through all of the API stack due to the complexities involved. Please file an issue if there are use cases that require this instead of changing the default maximum.
  • [asn1] Improve OID handling.
    • Error on parsed OID values larger than 2**32 - 1.
    • Error on DER OID values larger than 2**53 - 1 .

title: Serialize lists of primitive values returned from External Apps as space-delimited strings
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The current [External Android App Launcher functionality](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/forms/app/#android-app-launcher) will serialize lists as JSON arrays when returning data back into the form model.  Then, the cht-core webapp code will [insert the data](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/544bd9a3f36da28cf68da1f2ab6271d6f626e330/webapp/src/js/enketo/widgets/android-app-launcher.js#L95) into repeats with the appropriate appearance.

This approach is really the only way to handle an array _of objects_ since you need the repeat with child fields to model the properties on each object.  However, it is a bit confusing when it comes to arrays of primitive values. In that case, there is no named property to put in the repeat to hold the array value.  This is why we end up having the `android-app-object-list` vs the  `android-app-value-list`...

Unfortunately, Enketo repeats are still pretty janky, particularly when you are using them in non-trivial ways.  In practice we have found lots of challenges supporting complex workflows involving things like nested repeats, repeats whose relevance changes, etc.  Anything we can do to avoid using repeats for complex operations in a form would be an improvement and I think we should be able to handle lists of _primitive values_ without needing a repeat or `android-app-value-list` appearance.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Enketo has great support for lists of primitive values (modeled as space-delimited strings).  These "node sets" can be produced by normal `select_multiple` questions where the value for the field is actually just a space-delimited string with all the selected values. So, [built-in functions](https://docs.getodk.org/form-operators-functions/#selected-at) like `selected-at` and `count-selected` can be used to parse any space-delimited string. 

When de-serializing a JSON array of primitive values  in the android-app-launcher widget, we could check if the associated form model field is a repeat with either the `android-app-object-list` or  `android-app-value-list`. If so, we keep the existing behavior (so the changes remain passive).  However, if the field is not a repeat, then we should de-serialize the JSON array as a space-delimited string stored directly in the named field.  Then all the down-stream form logic can process the value as a node set and operate accordingly.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Support for this functionality was originally added [in this cht-android branch](https://github.com/medic/cht-android/pull/398).  However, I think this would be a breaking change if we ship the changes there (since cht-android has a decide if it is going to return the field as a string or array without knowing if the field has the `android-app-value-list` appearance or not.  By making this change in cht-core, it should be passive for forms that are already using `android-app-value-list`, but will allow the new functionality for forms without that appearance.

**Additional context**

https://github.com/medic/cht-android/pull/398

See the forms here (https://github.com/medic/fake-health-pulse#using-fake-healthpulse-ai) for examples with and without repeats.

title: Support uploading attachments in `contact` forms
body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
`app` forms support uploading files when filling out the form (via the various supported ODK fields for attaching files/media/etc).  When the app form is completed, the files are included as attachments in the report doc.

Unfortunately, uploading attachments like this is not supported for contact forms. It seems that you can include the questions in your form, but the selected files are not actually stored as attachments to the contact doc when the form is submitted.  (They are just ignored.)  

## Describe the solution you'd like

We should support including any uploaded files as attachments to the contact document (as is done for app forms). 

### In Scope
* allowing uploads on contact forms
* uses existing files on the device
* allowing uploads when creating a contact
* allowing uploads when editing a contact 
* upload any file, pdf, image etc

### Out of Scope
* allowing uploads on sub-documents - eg the contact (sub-document) that can optionally get created when creating a household (primary document).  Work around is navigate directly to that contact after it's been created, an add the upload there if needed
* updating the the contact summary - no changes here. Upload thumbnails or file names or links will not be shown
* Allowing/prompting the user to take a photo instead of picking an existing file



## Additional context

[Forum thread](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/uploading-and-displaying-images-in-contact-forms/2024/8).

One additional feature we would likely need once this is implemented is some way to actually display images (and maybe other types of files 🤔) for a contact once they have been attached.  For reports, we have the [binary attachment tag](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/forms/app/#uploading-binary-attachments) that causes images to be rendered on the reports page.  Perhaps we could support a contact-summary [card or field](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/contact-summary/contact-summary-templated/#contact-summary) that would render an images....  This probably deserves its own issue if we want to pursue it, but it will depend on this one to just get the initial files attached to the contact doc.

title: feat(#10398): store pre-purged doc counts per user
body:
# Description
This PR addresses issue #10398 by adding visibility into "pre-purged" document counts in the replication limit log. Previously, only the post-purge count was stored, making it difficult to assess the performance impact of large user document sets before filtering.

## Changes
- Updated `replication.js` to pass `allowedIds.length` (pre-purge count) to the logging service.
- Updated `replication-limit-log.js` to:
    - Accept the new `prePurgeCount` argument.
    - Store it in the `medic-logs` document.
    - Treat significant changes in `prePurgeCount` (diff > 100) as a trigger to persist a new log entry.

[3.2.3]

Changed

  • Fix advisory GHSA-869p-cjfg-cm3x: createSign and createVerify now require that a non empty secret is provided (via opts.secret, opts.privateKey or opts.key) when using HMAC algorithms.
  • Upgrading JWA version to 1.4.2, adressing a compatibility issue for Node >= 25.

[3.0.0]

Changed

  • BREAKING: jwt.verify now requires an algorithm parameter, and jws.createVerify requires an algorithm option. The "alg" field signature headers is ignored. This mitigates a critical security flaw in the library which would allow an attacker to generate signatures with arbitrary contents that would be accepted by jwt.verify. See https://auth0.com/blog/2015/03/31/critical-vulnerabilities-in-json-web-token-libraries/ for details.

2.0.0 - 2015-01-30

Changed

  • BREAKING: Default payload encoding changed from binary to utf8. utf8 is a is a more sensible default than binary because many payloads, as far as I can tell, will contain user-facing strings that could be in any language. ([6b6de48])

  • Code reorganization, thanks [@​fearphage]! (7880050)

Added

  • Option in all relevant methods for encoding. For those few users that might be depending on a binary encoding of the messages, this is for them. ([6b6de48])

title: Figure out how to block adding extra view to bundled ddocs
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Adding views to bundled ddocs is potentially destructive, because adding or editing a view requires the reindexing of the **whole** ddoc, which will potentially cause some sort of downtime (depending on which ddoc, downtime can be total or partial - with only some services not working) and will require all the extra disk space that is required for the ddoc reindex. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Figure out a way to stop editing these ddocs. This way should still allow upgrades that would potentially add new views. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Limit to documentation. 

**Additional context**
In a large production instance, a new workflow required adding a new view. The managing team added the view to an existent ddoc, and the instance ran out of disk space while indexing.

title: Release 5.1.0
body:
# Planning - CHT Community 

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release and add this issue to it. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes for the CHT relate to updated software requirements (for example: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an API, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [x] Ensure that all issues are labelled correctly, particularly "UI/UX" and "Breaking change" labelled issues, if any. 
- [x] Ensure that "Regressions" are labelled with "Affects: <version>" labels. The "Affects" label is used in a link in the Known Issues section of the release notes of that version so it has to match exactly. To make sure the label is correct go to the [release notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) and ensure the issue is listed.
- [x] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond technical documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo.
- [x] Assign a maintainer as Release Manager for this release.

# Development - Release Manager

When development is ready to begin one of the maintainers should be nominated as a Release Manager. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Checkout to a new `<issue>-update-version` branch (eg: `1234-update-version`) and set the version number in the `package.json` and `package-lock.json`. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`. Once the version is updated, submit a PR to `master` branch.
- [x] Ensure that issues associated with commits merged to `master` since the last release are closed and mapped to the milestone.

# Releasing - Release Manager

Once the PR has been merged into `master`, and the `master` branch has the new version number, then the release process can start:

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Notify the community by creating a post titled `<major>.<minor>.<patch> Beta Releases` in the [development](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/development/7) category of the CHT forum using this [template](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/new-topic?title=%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.%3Cpatch%3E%20Beta%20Releases&body=I%27ve%20just%20created%20the%20%60%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.x%60%20release%20branch.%20Please%20be%20aware%20that%20any%20further%20changes%20intended%20for%20this%20release%20will%20have%20to%20be%20merged%20to%20%60master%60%20then%20backported.%20Thanks%21&category=development).
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by creating a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`) and then push the created tag.
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the community by adding a comment in the forum post created above using this template:
```
I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag. 
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make. 
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```

title: Remove dependency of on disk GH token for release notes
body:
**Describe the issue**
When you use the [release notes](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/scripts/release-notes) script, it requests you put a GitHub token on disk in a `token.json` file.  This is insecure as other [rogue apps](https://about.gitlab.com/blog/gitlab-discovers-widespread-npm-supply-chain-attack/) could harvest and exfiltrate this token. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Prompt the user for the token and only keep it in memory for the duration of the script's run time.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
* Keep it as is
* do a 1pass integration

title: chore(#10520): secure release notes script token, exclude dependabot commits
body:
<!--

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

This PR secures release notes script token, moves it to be run in CI and hide dependabot noise.  Specifically:
* defaults to CI running release notes script
* hard codes `cht-core` as repo and but still allows milestone to be passed in both in CI and locally
* allows easy development or re-run both via local execution 
*  securely using `gh`'s token when running locally
* refactoring of existing code per feedback
* wraps existing code in massive `main()` function so prompt for token comes first and actually waits instead of barreling ahead and having GH auth fail
* Adds URLs for commits as sometimes they have no issue, commit or PR number in them.
* Excludes dependabot commits from showing as errors/missing a milestone 

closes #10520 and #10613

## Testing

First delete `token.json` if you have one on disk.

### check local output 

See [release notes](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/10520-secure-release-notes-token/scripts/release-notes/README.md) to see sample screenshots and sample output.  Then test with different scenarios:

```
# should fail 'missing milestone'
GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) node index.js  

# should fail 'check commits'
GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) node index.js 5.1.0 

# should succeed and generate release-notes.md file
GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) node index.js  5.1.0  --skip-commit-validation
```


### check CI output

Call CI manually to run with different scenarios:

```
# should fail 'missing milestone'
gh workflow run release-notes.yml --ref 10520-secure-release-notes-token   

# should fail 'check commits'
gh workflow run release-notes.yml  -f milestone=5.1.0 --ref 10520-secure-release-notes-token   

# should succeed and generate artifact
gh workflow run release-notes.yml  -f milestone=5.1.0  -f skip_commit_checks='--skip-commit-validation' --ref 10520-secure-release-notes-token   
```

Make sure the artifact has the expected content.

### compare `master` vs `10520-secure-release-notes-token`

do the same tests above on `master` to ensure the markdown output is the same.  

**NB** - This branch skips all dependabot commits, so these will not be shown.  Note this when you're comparing outputs.

title: Replace magic strings with shared constants
body:
As part of the work in #9621, we created a new shared constants library (`@medic/constants`) to reduce the use of magic strings throughout the codebase. The initial work added `DOC_IDS.SERVICE_WORKER_META`, `DOC_TYPES.TRANSLATIONS`, `HTTP_HEADERS.REQUEST_ID`, `SENTINEL_METADATA.TRANSITIONS_SEQ`, `SENTINEL_METADATA.BACKGROUND_SEQ`, and `USER_ROLES.ONLINE`.

However, there are many more magic strings used throughout the codebase that should be converted to use shared constants. This parent issue tracks the work to add constants across multiple categories including document IDs, document types, and other common strings.

## Why this matters

Magic strings scattered throughout the codebase can lead to typos and make refactoring difficult. By centralizing these constants in a shared library, we:

- Reduce the risk of typos (if you misspell `DOC_IDS.SETTINGS`, you'll get a clear error)
- Make it easier to find all usages of a particular document ID
- Create a single source of truth for important values
- Make the code more maintainable and self-documenting

## Constants to add

Based on an analysis of the codebase, here are the most common magic strings that could be converted to constants:

### Document IDs (DOC_IDS)

- `settings`
- `resources`
- `privacy-policies`
- `branding`
- `partners`
- `target-aggregates`
- `migration-log`
- `extension-libs`
- `zscore-charts`

### Document Types (DOC_TYPES)

- `data_record`
- `person`
- `clinic`
- `contact`
- `district_hospital`
- `health_center`
- `task`
- `target`
- `user-settings`
- `form`
- `token_login`

### Other constant categories

Additional constants may be identified in other categories:

- **HTTP Headers** - Common header names
- **User Roles** - Role strings used throughout the application
- **Sentinel Metadata** - Local document IDs and sentinel-specific constants
- **Common Prefixes/Patterns** - Reusable string patterns like `org.couchdb.user:` or `messages-`

## Implementation approach

Each constant (or small group of related constants) should be added as a separate sub-issue to keep pull requests focused and easy to review.

### To succeed on this ticket, please:

1. Set up your [development environment](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/community/contributing/code/core/dev-environment/) and ensure it works by logging into your CHT instance.

2. Read the shared constants library file at `shared-libs/constants/src/index.js` to understand its structure. Notice how it exports several constant categories like `DOC_IDS`, `DOC_TYPES`, `HTTP_HEADERS`, etc.

3. Search for how existing constants are used throughout the codebase to understand the pattern:
   - For example, `DOC_IDS.SERVICE_WORKER_META` is used in files like `api/src/generate-service-worker.js`, `webapp/src/ts/services/db-sync.service.ts`, and `api/src/services/authorization.js`
   - Notice how the constant is imported from `@medic/constants` and used in place of the magic string

4. For the specific constant(s) you're working on:
   - Add the constant to `shared-libs/constants/src/index.js` in the appropriate category object (e.g., `DOC_IDS`, `DOC_TYPES`, etc.)
   - Follow the pattern of existing constants in that category
   - Search for all usages of the magic string throughout the codebase (use grep or your IDE's search)
   - Replace each occurrence with the new constant
   - Ensure imports from `@medic/constants` are added where needed

5. Build the project and run unit tests to ensure everything compiles and works correctly:

   ```bash
   npm ci
   npm run build-dev
   npm run unit
   ```

   Note: The constants library itself doesn't have unit tests, but running the full unit test suite should verify that your changes work correctly throughout the codebase.

6. If all tests pass, create a git commit with your changes following the [contribution guidelines](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/community/contributing/code/workflow/).

title: Support for persistent offline authentication for SSO/OIDC users (Offline-First SSO)
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
In ALMANACH clinical workflows, nurses/CHWs/Doctors operate in zero-connectivity zones for extended periods. Currently, if an SSO/OIDC session expires while offline, the CHT redirects to the Identity Provider (IdP) login page. Since there is no internet, the clinician is locked out of the app, preventing access to life-saving clinical algorithms and patient data.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- Enable Persistent Offline SSO so that users who have logged in online once can continue to access the app offline indefinitely (or for a long configurable period).
- Offline Token Persistence: Securely store OIDC refresh tokens/sessions locally.
- Parity: SSO users should have the same offline reliability as native CHT users.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Extending Session Cookies: Increasing web session TTLs is insecure, non-compliant with IT security policies

**Additional context**
This is critical for the ALMANACH project. In remote clinical settings, an SSO timeout is a "system failure" that blocks patient care.

title: feat(#10389): updates purging to store purges per contact
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

feat(#1234): add hat wobble
^--^(#^--^): ^------------^
|     |      |
|     |      + - > subject
|     |
|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: chore, feat, fix, perf.

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

Adds "purging-groups" which are structures built around the purge context: one contact and all reports and messages associated with it. 
When the user replicates and we need to get the full list of purged docs, instead of requesting docs individually, we request purge groups, which reduces the query key count to the number of contacts the user can see, instead of the complete list of docs. 
The documents that are not found within the groups are then requested individually, as before. 

Because we also have an API that returns whether a list of document ids are purged or not, the individual document purges will still be stored, and the groups are stored alongside. 

Performance gains for `api/v1/replication/get-ids` using generated data:
| Number of Docs | master (s) | proposed (s) | Difference (V2 - V1) | Change (%) |
|----------------|------------------------|------------------------|----------------------|------------|
| 5000           | 0.677                  | 0.587                  | -0.090 s             | -13.3%     |
| 10000          | 1.151                  | 0.802                  | -0.349 s             | -30.3%     |
| 15100          | 3.024                  | 3.259                  | +0.235 s             | +7.8%      |
| 28100          | 2.937                  | 2.077                  | -0.860 s             | -29.3%     |
| 42100          | 5.224                  | 4.144                  | -1.080 s             | -20.7%     |
| 97100          | 9.962                  | 6.401                  | -3.561 s             | -35.7%     |
| 374100         | 51.673                 | 21.450                 | -30.223 s            | -58.5%     |

The change targets users with *very large pre-purge doc counts* which are seeing a significant reduction in request time. 

Due to the addition of new data in the purge databases, there will be a size increase of these databases. The purge databases are generally not very large and do not have indexes, so this is a linear increase of about 40%. Our largest deployments (with 80 million docs) have purge databases that are 10 - 15GB - this would translate to an increase of ~5GB per purge database for this large deployment. 

closes #10389
