title: Investigate authorization for online users using postgres
body:
Currently, online users have access to all documents. It is a frequently requested feature that online users have authorization, so they only can only access documents that belong to them for some definition of "belong to them".

The current authorization for offline users is not suitable for online users for various reasons.

Using postgres instead of couchdb as a backend could make authorization possible or simpler by allowing queries to have additional conditions (or joins depending on the implementation) for authorization instead of relying on map reduce views.

It is not necessarily a requirement that authorization for online users is exactly the same as for offline users, but to start with it may be simpler to have mostly the same authorization; a user is attached to one or more `contacts` and has access to all documents where the `subject` (defined differently for each type of document) is a descendant of those contacts. 

Performance will be a key consideration; additional conditions for authorization need to not change the query plan to be much more expensive than the base query without authorization.

How to deal with the hierarchical authorization is another key consideration.
the current base models in cht-sync (as an example) store a single parent_id in contacts, which means that getting descendants of a contact is complicated; have to do multiple queries with increasing numbers of children, or recursive queries. 
Neither of which is a good option, so the alternative is to denormalize multiple layers of the hierarchy into each contact row. Then the problem becomes when a parent is changed ALL of its descendants have to be changed. This is already necessary in couchdb, so is likely to be the preferred option, as longer as it doesn't make the problem worse.

title: Define upgrade path from 5.x and 4.x releases to a postgres release
body:
When a postgres supporting release is released, existing 5.x and 4.x deployments will need a way to upgrade to it.

This is complicated because copying the entire database to postgres will take some time and features that were migrated to postgres should not be offline or very out of date while that is happening.

So the release must include a feature flags to allow api to use couchdb and unauthorized queries until postgres is up to date.
And a way to drop server side couchdb map reduce views after the postgres data is up to date, instead of as part of the release (without dropping them for offline clients)

title: Implement static analysis of github CI to check for security vulnerabilities
body:
**Describe the issue**
GitHub CI allows you to not pin versions, or to loosely pin them, which can lead to security situations that either you're shipping code with out knowing which version you're shipping, or you're shipping code which you can't easily audit for known security issues. There's other issues that can be audited as well with in many CI calls

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
By using an automated static analysis tool like `zizmor` ([see homepage on GH](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor)), we could do a one time on boarding of all CI systems (starting with CHT Core) and then with each release (with each quarter? month? week) update the CI to be secure according to our audit tool of choice.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Find another tool aside from `zizmor`.  Or maybe depend on [dependabot](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/keep-all-your-packages-up-to-date-with-dependabot/) - does that even look at CI?

  zizmor

title: Support "downtime upgrade" with minimal disk space requirements
body:
(Note that this issue is not focused on updates to cht-core to support upgrades in the long-term. Instead it is about exploring external options that can be operationalized by existing CHT instances to upgrade (without needing to take a new version first).)

**What feature do you want to improve?**

Currently when upgrading the CHT the new/updated ddocs are all staged simultaneously. (Re)-building the big ddocs takes an enormous amount of disk space, including both the space used by the staged indexes as well as the extra space used when building the view indexes.

If we allow for server downtime, we should be able to reduce the amount of disk space required when re-indexing.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

We should be able to execute an upgrade with the following process:

- Stop/remove all CHT containers
- Start Couch/Nouveau containers with the `target` image version
- Remove any ddocs that have been removed/updated from `current` to `target`.
- Call `_view_cleanup` and `_nouveau_cleanup` to remove index files from disk
- One-by-one add/warm each created/updated ddoc for `target`
- Finally end by starting all the rest of the CHT containers with the `target` image version.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

This cannot go in cht-core (at least that is not the target of this issue) because we want something that will be useful for existing CHT instances without them needing to upgrade to get access to the functionality. We also need something that can be used with both Docker Compose and k8s deployments. cht-conf actions seem like a good place to target.

Additionally, @mrjones-plip had the good idea that we could enhance the cht-upgrade-service (for Docker Compose deployments) to perhaps leverage the cht-conf functionality and do a down-time upgrade automatically (or maybe check a `settings` value and only do it when configured).

**Additional context**

Because of the functionality overlap with the existing `prestage` logic I have in chtoolbox, I have been initially piloting functionality in that repo.  We can either leverage chtoolbox directly for the upgrade, migrate the functionality to cht-conf, or just consume chtoolbox from cht-conf.

title: feat(#10509): support uploading attachments in contact forms
body:
# Description This PR adds attachment support to contact forms, enabling file uploads and binary field attachments similar to what already exists for report forms. ## What's Implemented Following discussion in #10509, the implementation was **simplified to match report form behavior**: all attachments attach to the main contact document only, regardless of form structure. ### Backend Changes 1. **File Widget Attachments**: Files uploaded through Enketo file widgets are extracted from `FileManager` and attached to the contact document 2. **Binary Field Attachments**: Base64-encoded binary fields (signatures, drawings) are extracted from XML and attached with XPath-based naming 3. **Attachment Naming**: Uses consistent patterns matching report forms: - File widgets: `user-file-{filename}` - Binary fields: `user-file/{form-id}/{xpath}` 4. **Edit Preservation**: Attachments automatically persist when editing contacts via `_defaults()` merge ### Implementation Details - **Location**: `ContactSaveService.prepareSubmittedDocsForSave()` (following [@jkuester's guidance](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10509#issuecomment-2542828754)) - **Code Added**: ~30 lines in `processAllAttachments()` method - **Services Reused**: `AttachmentService`, `FileManager`, `Xpath` utility - **Pattern**: Mirrors `EnketoService.xmlToDocs()` for report forms ## Test Coverage | Test Type | Count | Location | |-----------|-------|----------| | Unit Tests | 8 | `webapp/tests/karma/ts/services/contact-save.service.spec.ts` | | cht-form Integration | 2 | `tests/integration/cht-form/default/contact-with-attachments.wdio-spec.js` | | E2E Tests | 5 | `tests/e2e/default/contacts/contact-attachments.wdio-spec.js` | **Unit tests are intended to verify:** - File widget extraction and attachment to main document - Binary field extraction with XPath-based naming - Multiple attachments (mixed types) all attach to main document **E2E tests are intended to verify:** - Create contact with single image attachment - Create contact with multiple attachments (image + document) - Edit contact preserves existing attachments All added tests passing ✅ ## Manual Testing Performed - Created contacts with photo attachments via person-create form - Verified attachments saved to CouchDB with correct naming (`user-file-{filename}`) - Verified edit form displays existing attachment filename - Confirmed multiple contacts can have attachments independently
Details about manual testing ## Testing Photo Upload on Contact Create ## Step 1: Modified the Contact Form Please note that form modifications have not been committed. The file was modified locally. **File:** `config/default/forms/contact/person-create.xml` ### 1a. Added field to instance data (~line 922) ```xml ``` ### 1b. Added binding (~line 1062) ```xml
Screenshots ### Empty person create form with photo field ### Person create form with photo added ### Person edit form with photo shown
--- ## Not in Scope for V1 Per discussion in #10509, these are deferred: - ~~**UI Preview on Edit**: Attachments persist when editing, but users cannot see previews of existing attachments (can be added in V2)~~ preview on edit is included as per @dianabarsan's request in https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10570/#discussion_r2731500513 - **Multi-Document Routing**: Attachments in sibling/repeat sections all attach to main document (matches report behavior) - **Contact-Summary Integration**: Per issue description, this is out of scope ## AI Disclosure **AI Assistance**: This PR was developed using Claude Code. **How AI was used**: - Analysis of existing codebase patterns (EnketoService, AttachmentService) for consistency - Code generation for the `processAllAttachments()` method - Test writing following TDD methodology - Documentation and planning **Human oversight**: - I reviewed all generated code for correctness, security, and consistency with project patterns - I ran all tests manually to verify functionality - I made architecture decisions (V1 simplified approach based on reviewer feedback) - I iterated on implementation based on code review feedback - All commits include co-author attribution Closes #10509 # Code review checklist - [x] UI/UX backwards compatible: No UI changes in this PR. Existing contact forms continue to work unchanged. - [x] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the [style guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/style-guide/), documented if necessary. - [ ] Documented: Configuration and user documentation on [cht-docs](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/) - Form authors will need guidance on adding upload fields - [x] Tested: Unit tests, cht-form integration tests, and E2E tests all passing - [x] Internationalised: No user-facing text added - [x] Backwards compatible: Works with existing data and configuration. Existing contact forms without upload fields are unaffected. # License The software is provided under AGPL-3.0. Contributions to this project are accepted under the same license.

Bumps [tar](https://github.com/isaacs/node-tar) to 7.5.3 and updates ancestor dependency [@angular/cli](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli). These dependencies need to be updated together. Updates `tar` from 7.4.3 to 7.5.3
Changelog

Sourced from tar's changelog.

Changelog

7.5

  • Added zstd compression support.

7.4

  • Deprecate onentry in favor of onReadEntry for clarity.

7.3

  • Add onWriteEntry option

7.2

  • DRY the command definitions into a single makeCommand method, and update the type signatures to more appropriately infer the return type from the options and arguments provided.

7.1

  • Update minipass to v7.1.0
  • Update the type definitions of write() and end() methods on Unpack and Parser classes to be compatible with the NodeJS.WritableStream type in the latest versions of @types/node.

7.0

  • Drop support for node <18
  • Rewrite in TypeScript, provide ESM and CommonJS hybrid interface
  • Add tree-shake friendly exports, like import('tar/create') and import('tar/read-entry') to get individual functions or classes.
  • Add chmod option that defaults to false, and deprecate noChmod. That is, reverse the default option regarding explicitly setting file system modes to match tar entry settings.
  • Add processUmask option to avoid having to call process.umask() when chmod: true (or noChmod: false) is set.

6.2

  • Add support for brotli compression
  • Add maxDepth option to prevent extraction into excessively deep folders.

title: Implement task filtering
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. I'm always frustrated when [...] -->
When CHWs provide services in the community, they face challenges in navigating the CHT app. With numerous tasks listed, it often becomes difficult to scroll through and identify specific follow-up tasks for each use case.

To improve efficiency, [the community suggested](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/filter-option-for-task/4808) adding a filter option (similar to the reporting feature) that lets CHWs select a specific form/use case and view only the relevant tasks they need to complete.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->
Provide the ability to filter tasks by high priority and/or form/use case.

**Additional context**
<!-- Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here. -->
[Forum post](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/filter-option-for-task/4808)

# Description
This PR refactors the privacy policy handling logic across the admin, API, shared constants, and webapp modules.

### Key Changes:
* **Centralized Privacy Constants:** Moved hardcoded strings and policy identifiers into a shared constants module to ensure consistency across the stack.
* **API Endpoint Optimization:** Updated the API to handle policy retrieval more efficiently, reducing redundant database calls.

7.5

  • Added zstd compression support.
  • Consistent TOCTOU behavior in sync t.list
  • Only read from ustar block if not specified in Pax
  • Fix sync tar.list when file size reduces while reading
  • Sanitize absolute linkpaths properly

7.4

  • Deprecate onentry in favor of onReadEntry for clarity.

7.3

  • Add onWriteEntry option

7.2

  • DRY the command definitions into a single makeCommand method, and update the type signatures to more appropriately infer the return type from the options and arguments provided.

7.1

  • Update minipass to v7.1.0
  • Update the type definitions of write() and end() methods on Unpack and Parser classes to be compatible with the NodeJS.WritableStream type in the latest versions of @types/node.

7.0

  • Drop support for node <18
  • Rewrite in TypeScript, provide ESM and CommonJS hybrid interface
  • Add tree-shake friendly exports, like import('tar/create') and import('tar/read-entry') to get individual functions or classes.
  • Add chmod option that defaults to false, and deprecate noChmod. That is, reverse the default option regarding explicitly setting file system modes to match tar entry settings.

title: Update google-libphonenumber to support new Nepali number scheme (+977971xxxxxxx)
body: **Describe the bug** Ncell, a mobile network carrier in Nepal, has started issuing new mobile numbers beginning with `971` since Dec 2025 ([news article](https://kathmandupost.com/money/2025/12/09/ncell-starts-issuing-new-mobile-numbers-beginning-with-971)). These numbers are currently rejected by CHT. The validation fails because the current version of the `google-libphonenumber` library in `cht-core` does not include the definition for this new prefix. Current library version in cht-core: `3.2.42` (released `2025-06-06`). Latest version: [`3.2.44`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/google-libphonenumber/v/3.2.44) (released `2026-01-19`) **To Reproduce** 1. Attempt to submit a form with a phone number in the format +977971xxxxxxx. 2. Observe validation error stating the number is invalid. **Expected behavior** The valid phone number should be accepted. **Screenshots** **Environment** - Instance: any - Browser: any - Client platform: any - App: webapp - Version: all **Additional context** The format `+977971` was [added](https://github.com/google/libphonenumber/blame/870b9de45e41e958786573a59b7db0a326136e38/resources/metadata/977/ranges.csv#L18) to `google/libphonenumber` in version `9.0.10` on `2025-07-16`. The npm wrapper [`google-libphonenumber`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/google-libphonenumber) that we use [incorporated](https://github.com/ruimarinho/google-libphonenumber/commit/6c6e1a5323ca4318af6357d145479edc9a46db0b) this upstream change in version `3.2.43` (Released `2025-09-17`). Until we catch up with the library, we can use `"phone_validation": "partial"` in app-settings to check only the length of the phone number.

title: Add contributors to release note items
body:
**Describe the issue**
Right now we list every contributor at the bottom of the release notes in the "Contributors" section (eg [5.0.0](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/releases/5_0_0/#contributors)).  However, it's not clear who worked on which feature, bug fix etc.  

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
For each ticket in the release, we should add logic in the [release notes script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/scripts/release-notes) to add a link to the person's GH page.  This way, release note readers get a sense of breadth and depth of contributors. A good example of this can be seen on the WebdriverIO releases (eg [9.23.1](https://github.com/webdriverio/webdriverio/releases/tag/v9.23.1)).

Basically we'd take this:

> **Technical improvements**
> [#10420](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10420): Test Cinque & Nouveau on large production data set
> [#10023](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10023): Update release-notes script to include all commit co-authors in contributors list

And turn it into this:

> **Technical improvements**
> [#10420](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10420): Test Cinque & Nouveau on large production data set ([Elijah Karari](https://github.com/eljhkrr), [mrjones](https://github.com/mrjones-plip))
> [#10023](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10023): Update release-notes script to include all commit co-authors in contributors list ([Hsing Fu](https://github.com/HsingFuC))


**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I suspect just do nothing - maybe there's benefit for all contributors in the   "Contributors" section to all share equal attribution for the entire release 🤔

# Description

Title is deceptive as this PR does a few more things: 

### Upgrades wdio to latest
This is a minor release bump, but one dependent package `devtools` (used to communicate with the browser) was deprecated in wdio@9 and now it's being reused for something else (????). Dependabot keeps trying to upgrade this deprecated package to the new version and everything fails. 
The package has a replacement, called `lighthouse` which depends on a new protocol called BiDi - basically a web socket between the test runner and the browser where communication is bidirectional. it's super strong and can achieve waaaay more stuff than `devtools`, however it made a lot of our e2e tests unstable or fail, so when we upgraded to wdio@9, we chose to use the legacy protocol (devtools). 
This PR stabilizes all the tests so we can use BiDi and up to date packages. 

### Bumping minimum chrome version to 107. 
This was relatively straight forward, with some minor tweaks so that tests work both with `chromedriver` protocol and `BiDi`. 

### Some generic e2e test stabilizing. 🤞🏻 

### Changing retry protocol 

Instead of using mocha retry, which just retried one test, we now use wdio retry, which tries the whole spec. 

### Updates minimum chrome version in Webapp and in e2e tests

title: chore: bump webpack from 5.103.0 to 5.105.0
body:
Bumps [webpack](https://github.com/webpack/webpack) from 5.103.0 to 5.105.0.
Release notes

Sourced from webpack's releases.

v5.105.0

Minor Changes

  • Allow resolving worker module by export condition name when using new Worker() (by @​hai-x in #20353)

  • Detect conditional imports to avoid compile-time linking errors for non-existent exports. (by @​hai-x in #20320)

  • Added the tsconfig option for the resolver options (replacement for tsconfig-paths-webpack-plugin). Can be false (disabled), true (use the default tsconfig.json file to search for it), a string path to tsconfig.json, or an object with configFile and references options. (by @​alexander-akait in #20400)

  • Support import.defer() for context modules. (by @​ahabhgk in #20399)

  • Added support for array values ​​to the devtool option. (by @​hai-x in #20191)

  • Improve rendering node built-in modules for ECMA module output. (by @​hai-x in #20255)

  • Unknown import.meta properties are now determined at runtime instead of being statically analyzed at compile time. (by @​xiaoxiaojx in #20312)

Patch Changes

  • Fixed ESM default export handling for .mjs files in Module Federation (by @​y-okt in #20189)

  • Optimized import.meta.env handling in destructuring assignments by using cached stringified environment definitions. (by @​xiaoxiaojx in #20313)

  • Respect the stats.errorStack option in stats output. (by @​samarthsinh2660 in #20258)

  • Fixed a bug where declaring a module variable in module scope would conflict with the default moduleArgument. (by @​xiaoxiaojx in #20265)

  • Fix VirtualUrlPlugin to set resourceData.context for proper module resolution. Previously, when context was not set, it would fallback to the virtual scheme path (e.g., virtual:routes), which is not a valid filesystem path, causing subsequent resolve operations to fail. (by @​xiaoxiaojx in #20390)

  • Fixed Worker self-import handling to support various URL patterns (e.g., import.meta.url, new URL(import.meta.url), new URL(import.meta.url, import.meta.url), new URL("./index.js", import.meta.url)). Workers that resolve to the same module are now properly deduplicated, regardless of the URL syntax used. (by @​xiaoxiaojx in #20381)

  • Reuse the same async entrypoint for the same Worker URL within a module to avoid circular dependency warnings when multiple Workers reference the same resource. (by @​xiaoxiaojx in #20345)

  • Fixed a bug where a self-referencing dependency would have an unused export name when imported inside a web worker. (by @​samarthsinh2660 in #20251)

  • Fix missing export generation when concatenated modules in different chunks share the same runtime in module library bundles. (by @​hai-x in #20346)

  • Fixed import.meta.env.xxx behavior: when accessing a non-existent property, it now returns empty object instead of full object at runtime. (by @​xiaoxiaojx in #20289)

title: Freetext search causes excessive requests when getting a large number of results
body:
<!--
**Important**: This is a public repository. Anyone in the world can see what's posted here. If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the bug**
Simple freetext search seems to get all results for the search for every search "page" instead of getting one page at a time. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Have a large instance. your search term should yield more than 100 results.
2. Make a report freetext search - don't use other filters. 
3. It takes a long time to load the results. 
4. Scrolling to the next results page takes equal amount of time. 
5. Inspecting the console, you see many ajax requests to the server. 

**Expected behavior**
A single request should be made for one page of results. 

**Video**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63887612-724d-4fbe-a827-ee7202b39e87


**Environment**
- App: webapp
- Version: 5.0.0

title: fix(#10621): use default page size for freetext searching
body:
# Description

Updates the paged generator logic in cht-datasource (used in the freetext searching) to not hard-code the page limit to `100`. Instead it should use the _default_ page limit for the given paging function.  This means that when paging with a generator we should use the defaults from the [contants file](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/4d3c72f61a17d761f76bf6efbef3d13bf619f491/shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/libs/constants.ts).  (`100` per page _for docs_ and `10000` per page _for uuids_).  

Closes #10621

### AI Disclosure

title: feat(#10577): adds task filtering
body:
<!--

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

Adds following task filters:
1. Due date - radio with two options, that show either tasks that are overdue (or due today) or that are due in the future. 

2. Task type - checkboxes for every task type available in the task list

3. Area - identical to the reports area filter. will filter tasks based on the task owner lineage. 

Minor refactor to how we display (and filter) item lineage, changed from being filtered in _every_ component that will display items with lineage to using the store for user facilities and filtering lineage in the lineage pipe itself. 

### AI Disclosure
AI Assistance: This PR was developed using Claude Code.

#### How AI was used

- I instructed Claude to reuse the Reports filters component for tasks, including the types of filters and which fields should be used for filtering
- Instructed to write unit tests for the new and changed code
- Instructed to generate an e2e test code skeleton
- Added translations for all of the new translation keys
- Instructed and guided through doing a high level refactor of a repeated code pattern (of lineage filtering) 

Human oversight:

title: Release 5.0.2
body:
# Planning - CHT Community 

- [x] Create an GH Milestone for the release and add this issue to it.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.
- [x] Ensure that all issues are labelled correctly, particularly ensure that "Regressions" are labelled with "Affects: <version>" labels. The "Affects" label is used in a link in the Known Issues section of the release notes of that version so it has to match exactly. To make sure the label is correct go to the [release notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) and ensure the issue is listed.

# Development - Release Manager

When development is ready to begin one of the maintainers should be nominated as a Release Manager. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR to the release branch. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version patch`.
- [x] Ensure that issues from merged commits are closed and mapped to a milestone.
- [ ] Write an update in the #stewardship-team Slack channel summarising development and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The Release Manager is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Manager

Once all issues have been merged into `master` then the release process can start:

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`).
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the community by creating a post titled `<major>.<minor>.<patch> Beta Releases` in the [development](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/development/7) category of the CHT forum using this [template](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/new-topic?title=%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.%3Cpatch%3E%20Beta%20Releases&body=Hi%20Everyone%0AI%E2%80%99ve%20just%20created%20the%20%60%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.%3Cpatch%3E-beta.1%60%20tag.%0APlease%20let%20me%20know%20if%20there%E2%80%99s%20any%20final%20update%20we%20need%20to%20make.%0AIf%20all%20is%20good%2C%20then%20in%2024h%2C%20I%20will%20start%20the%20release.%20Thanks%21&category=development).
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labelled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [x] Collect known migration steps, descriptions, screenshots, videos, data, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. This information should already be on the issue, but if not, prompt the change author to provide it.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Ensure that the release notes PR is merged before moving to next step.
- [x] Create a [new release](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases/new) in GitHub, with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, from the release branch created above as the target branch. Click on the "Choose a tag" dropdown and create a tag for the release with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. Add a link to the release notes page in the description of the release.
- [x] Once you publish the release, confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Upgrade the [demo](https://demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org/) instance to the newly released version.
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT Forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/), under the "Announcements - Releases" category using this [template](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/new-topic?title=Announcing%20the%20release%20of%20%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.%3Cpatch%3E%20of%20the%20CHT%20Core%20Framework&body=%2AAnnouncing%20the%20release%20of%20%7B%7Bversion%7D%7D%20of%20%7B%7Bproduct%7D%7D%2A%0AThis%20release%20fixes%20%7B%7Bnumber%20of%20bugs%7D%7D.%20Read%20the%20%5Brelease%20notes%5D%28%7B%7Burl%7D%7D%29%20for%20full%20details.&category=releases).
- [x] Go over the list of commits and individually notify contributing / interested community members about the release.

title: Use db view/index pagination for freetext search
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
When doing a normal freetext search from either the People or Reports tab, we should only be hitting a single DB index/view.  I think this means we _should_ be able to "page" the query via the DB paging functionality and not have to pull back the entire results set before manually paging out the results we want.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

In `shared-libs/search`, we [are checking for the `ordered` property](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/d38cb4a56dd9110662186aec321cf78986c055fc/shared-libs/search/src/search.js#L104) to be present before using db pagination (even if there is only 1 request).  

The freetext requests do not set `ordered: true` (and never have).  This is despite the fact that the freetext views/indexes do have an ordering and so should be sorted in a predictable/useful way when they are returned.  I _think_ this means we should be able to update the freetext requests to set `ordered: true` so that when we are just doing a simple search with one of those requests, it does not have to pull back the whole results set.

**Measurements**
As was noted in the investigations around https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10621, we "page" the search results displayed in the app, only showing the user `25` results and then triggering another "search" for the next page when the user scrolls down.  This new search will again pull _all_ the search hits back before showing the user the next `25` results.  We should be able to just search for 25 results at a time instead of needing to manually page through all results for every page.

**Additional context**

It was almost 10 years ago when [Gareth added the `ordered` logic](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/commit/2d2c0bc04d12ef62ee348c78e57aa82a8ffb64df) and even then it was not applied to the freetext indexes.  Did he know something then, that we are missing now?  Or, have things change in the meantime such that db paging for these searches is now possible?    🤷 https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/2371

>  I think it can only be applied for the default views (`contacts_by_name` and `reports_by_date`) but they're used most often so would still be a big win.

title: Dependabot PRs fail compile test due to dependabot internals
body:
**Describe the issue**
Just the latest examples:
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10581
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10589
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10602
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10603

All fail in the same way: 
```
npm ci
npm error `npm ci` can only install packages when your package.json and package-lock.json or npm-shrinkwrap.json are in sync. Please update your lock file with `npm install` before continuing.
npm error
npm error Missing: chokidar@4.0.3 from lock file
npm error Missing: readdirp@4.1.2 from lock file
npm error Missing: chokidar@4.0.3 from lock file
npm error Missing: readdirp@4.1.2 from lock file
npm error Missing: chokidar@4.0.3 from lock file
npm error Missing: readdirp@4.1.2 from lock file
npm error Missing: chokidar@4.0.3 from lock file
npm error Missing: readdirp@4.1.2 from lock file
```

The issue is around dependabot _removing_ optional dependencies from package-lock.json https://github.com/dependabot/dependabot-core/issues/4795
It is not something that is being worked on. 
Example of how a person is fixing this in their fork: 
https://github.com/uuushiro/dependabot-core/commit/73844b783aa243efd0a7f29cc48fc0ab2abdd56c

This means that we are plagued with this forever. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

Suggestions by claude: 

 1. A CI check on Dependabot PRs that runs npm install --package-lock-only and verifies the lockfile is consistent (this would flag Dependabot's broken lockfiles before merge)
  2. A GitHub Action that auto-fixes Dependabot lockfiles by running npm install --package-lock-only and committing the result back to the PR branch
  3. An .npmrc with optional=false to tell npm to never install optional peer deps — making both npm and Dependabot agree on the same outcome

I think 3 is easiest. 1 doesn't really fix anything (still needs a human to fix the PRs). 2 is doable (claude made the action) but might be clunky?

title: Add `api` support for basic loading/serving UI Extensions
body:
- Add a new service: `src/services/ui-extension.js`  (follow patterns from [forms](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/e0c5407a90763ab5c3619cfb7b487d85f6bae75d/api/src/services/forms.js#L11-L10) and [extension-libs](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/e0c5407a90763ab5c3619cfb7b487d85f6bae75d/api/src/services/extension-libs.js) services.
    - Export `getScript` function that takes the UI Extension name as the parameter and returns the script attachment.
        -  Get the extension doc by id: `ui-extension:${name}`.
        - Return an object with the `data` value from `doc._attachments['extension.js']`.
    - Export `getAllProperties` function that reads all the ui-extensions and returns an array objects from the docs
        - We should remove the Couch specific fields (`_id`, `_rev`, etc) and then add an `id` field that is the doc `_id` without the `ui-extension:` prefix.
        - Be sure to use the `allDocs` Pouch function to load the ui-extension docs by an id range. 
- Add a new  controller: `src/controllers/ui-extension.js` (follow patterns from [extension-libs.js](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/e0c5407a90763ab5c3619cfb7b487d85f6bae75d/api/src/controllers/extension-libs.js))
    - Export a `list` function that just sends the results of service.getAllProperties as a json response.
    - Export a `get` function that calls service.getScript with the `req.params.name` parameter.
        - The returned script file should be buffered back on the response as `base64` and a Content-Type of `text/javascript`
- Update `src/routing.js` to route GET requests:
    - `/ui-extension` routes to controller.list
    - `/ui-extension/:id` routes to controller.get

Make sure to include unit tests for all the changes (except for `routing.js`).  Also, we will need to add a new integration test file to [tests/integration/api/controllers](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/e0c5407a90763ab5c3619cfb7b487d85f6bae75d/tests/integration/api/controllers).

title: Update `medic` db validation to support `ui-extension` doc type
body:
The [ddocs/medic-db/medic/validate_doc_update.js](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/2d44b01e239e4b4f8e5ec1bc04097bff49be2d95/ddocs/medic-db/medic/validate_doc_update.js#L10) logic will protect certain doc types so that only admin users can add/update them.

We should include the `ui-extension` doc type in this file (similar to how `form` type docs are also protected).  

I don't think there are any automated tests to add/update here, but we should manually test the validation.  Running `npm run build-dev` and then `npm run dev-api` should build the db config with the updated code and then deploy it to your local Couch instance.  Then you can test trying to write a doc with different users via curl:

```shell
curl -X POST http://medic:password@localhost:5984/medic -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"_id":    
  "ui-extension:hello-world", "type": "ui-extension"}' 
```

title: Optimize large map reduce views
body:
For large instances, map/reduce view indexes use up a significant amount of space, especially when rebuilding and uncompacted. Some of the largest views likely can be optimized.

Here are the sizes of the ten largest views from a representative (derived from production data) test instance. IN some instance different views will be larger or smaller because of the docs being indexed; if there are fewer tasks or reports, the views that index those types of documents will be smaller.
| ddoc | view | bytes | size |
|---|---|---|---|
| _design/medic | doc_summaries_by_id | 8925251727 | 8.31 GB | 
| _design/medic-client | docs_by_id_lineage | 6296722041 | 5.86 GB | 
| _design/medic-client | tasks_by_contact | 5964262455 | 5.55 GB | 
| _design/medic-client | doc_by_type | 3214188302 | 2.99 GB | 
| _design/medic-client | reports_by_place | 2960527616 | 2.76 GB | 
| _design/medic | tasks_in_terminal_state | 2091050375 | 1.95 GB | 
| _design/medic-client | visits_by_date | 2058151539 | 1.92 GB | 
| _design/medic | contacts_by_depth | 1748286714 | 1.63 GB | 
| _design/medic-client | reports_by_subject | 1695717337 | 1.58 GB |

title: Remove or optimize map reduce view doc_summaries_by_id
body:
The `doc_summaries_by_id` map reduce view is by far the largest view on the instances sampled.
This is because the values stored in the btree are relatively large (and it will index every report and every contact).

It is used only by online users and in admin; for offline users summaries are calculated on demand rather than being loaded from a view (see https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/4666).

Since there is already a precedent for calculating these summaries on demand I don't see any reason why they should still be stored in a map/reduce view.
Instead the duplicated summary functions can be moved into a single shared-lib where it can be shared between admin and webapp, and webapp doesn't distinguish between offline and online users; it just always get the summaries from the shared summary service.

## View: medic/doc_summaries_by_id

### Definition
- **Database:** medic (server-side only)
- **Map keys:** `doc._id`
- **Map values:** Summary object containing `_rev`, `from`, `phone`, `form`, `read`, `valid`, `verified`, `reported_date`, `contact`, `lineage`, `subject`, `case_id` (for reports) or `_rev`, `name`, `phone`, `type`, `contact_type`, `contact`, `lineage`, `date_of_death`, `muted` (for contacts)
- **Reduce:** None

### Usages
| # | File | Key/Options Used | Functional Purpose |
|---|------|------------------|--------------------|
| 1 | [`admin/src/js/services/message-queue.js:102`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/admin/src/js/services/message-queue.js#L102) | `{ keys: ids }` | Fetches contact summaries by IDs for the admin message queue to display recipient info. |
| 2 | [`admin/src/js/services/get-summaries.js:103`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/admin/src/js/services/get-summaries.js#L103) | `{ keys: ids }` | Fetches document summaries for admin data record display (remote/online mode). |
| 3 | [`webapp/src/ts/services/get-summaries.service.ts:111`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/services/get-summaries.service.ts#L111) | `{ keys: ids }` | Fetches document summaries for webapp data record display (online users only). |

**Note:** Both [`admin/src/js/services/get-summaries.js:59`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/admin/src/js/services/get-summaries.js#L59) and [`webapp/src/ts/services/get-summaries.service.ts:65`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/services/get-summaries.service.ts#L65) contain a **duplicated copy** of this view's map function logic as a client-side fallback for offline users (tagged with a warning comment referencing [medic/medic#4666](https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/4666)).

title: Optimize map reduce view doc_by_type
body:
The `doc_by_type` map reduce view is the third largest view on the instance sampled.
It emits an entry for every document in the database, but is used only for rare document types.

This can be change to not emit for the largest types, `task`, `data_record`, `contact`, and maybe `target` and `telemetry`.

It seems like an index for documents by their type might be useful in general or for some unknown reason in the future, but its not currently used that way and is very expensive to keep. 
If it's necessary in future to query for all `reports`, `tasks` or `contacts`,  the other views that index those types specifically can be used.

## View: medic-client/doc_by_type

### Definition
- **Database:** medic (synced to offline clients)
- **Map keys:** `[doc.type]`
- **Map values:** (none)
- **Reduce:** None

### Usages

title: Support configuring `max_age` parameter for OIDC login
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Originally discussed [on the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/oidc-sso-logout-on-shared-android-devices-idp-session-not-cleared/5513/2).  Currently the CHT [SSO functionality](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/hosting/sso/) supports basic OIDC authentication whereby the user actually authenticates via a 3rd-party auth provider. The OIDC flow results in the user's client being assigned a valid CouchDB session cookie (aka a valid CHT session cookie).  

When the user logs out of the app, the session cookie is cleared and they no longer have a valid CHT session.  _However_, depending details around the user's device and the 3rd-party auth provider, the user may still have an active session with the 3rd-party auth provider.  (E.g. in cht-android, we use an [Android Custom Tab](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/layout/webapps/overview-of-android-custom-tabs) to complete the OIDC auth flow which will have access to sessions on the user's default browser.)  This means that if the user again tries to login to the CHT via the SSO flow, they will be redirected to the 3rd-party auth provider. If they already have an active session there, the auth provider may just automatically redirect back to the CHT with the ID token for the user with the current session. This will cause the user to be logged back into the CHT with the same CHT user as before.

In many cases, this will be considered a feature (the CHT SSO functionality was designed/intended to work this way).  Take the case where a user is logged into their Google account on their phone and Google is configured as the 3rd-party auth provider for their CHT instance.  The first time this user opens their CHT app and selects the SSO Login, they can be automatically redirected to/from the Google auth page (without needed to re-authenticate) and the CHT will automatically log them in as the CHT user associated with that Google account.

_However_ (as described in the forum thread) this functionality is problematic in some cases (such as where a single device is shared by multiple users).  When trying to switch from one SSO user to another, the 3rd-party auth provider may not prompt for the second user to login and instead just return the id token for the first user (who's session with the auth provider is still valid).  The second user may not be prompted to login until the existing session with the auth provider is cleared.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We should support [passing the `max_age` parameter](https://auth0.com/docs/authenticate/login/max-age-reauthentication) when the CHT api server starts the OIDC login flow. Then we can validate the `auth_time` claim that is returned with the id token and ensure it is within the desired time window (e.g. `60s`).

From the [OIDC Spec](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html):

The `max_age` parameter is:

> OPTIONAL. Maximum Authentication Age. Specifies the allowable elapsed time in seconds since the last time the End-User was actively authenticated by the OP. If the elapsed time is greater than this value, the OP MUST attempt to actively re-authenticate the End-User. .... When max_age is used, the ID Token returned MUST include an auth_time Claim Value. Note that max_age=0 is equivalent to prompt=login.

The `auth_time` claim is:

> Time when the End-User authentication occurred. Its value is a JSON number representing the number of seconds from 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z as measured in UTC until the date/time. When a max_age request is made or when auth_time is requested as an Essential Claim, then this Claim is REQUIRED; otherwise, its inclusion is OPTIONAL.

When validating the id token:

> If the auth_time Claim was requested, either through a specific request for this Claim or by using the max_age parameter, the Client SHOULD check the auth_time Claim value and request re-authentication if it determines too much time has elapsed since the last End-User authentication. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Similar re-authentication functionality could be achived via the `prompt=login` parameter, but [the auth0 docs](https://auth0.com/docs/authenticate/login/max-age-reauthentication) note:

> The prompt=login mechanism can be subverted by simply stripping the parameter as it passes through the user agent (browser) and is only good for providing a UX hint to the provider (OP) in cases when the (RP) wants to display a link like:

**Additional context**

The changes to the CHT code _should_ be pretty simple.  I think we  could make the `max_age` parameter value configurable in the `oidc_provider` properties in the CHT instance settings doc. If a value is provided for that settings property, then our api code should provide it [when calling `client.buildAuthorizationUrl`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/2cbe9c10991de77e5ed7408432474800ea5185d4/api/src/services/sso-login.js#L97).  It looks like we can pass it directly when making the  `client.buildAuthorizationUrl` call like [in this example](https://github.com/panva/openid-client/discussions/828), or maybe we could just set the [default_max_age](https://github.com/panva/openid-client/blob/b77d87c1e2f5fef6fab501de615fb83a74a0251f/docs/interfaces/ClientMetadata.md#default_max_age) somehow?  

Then, when [calling `client.authorizationCodeGrant`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/2cbe9c10991de77e5ed7408432474800ea5185d4/api/src/services/sso-login.js#L119) we should pass the [`maxAge` property](https://github.com/panva/openid-client/blob/b77d87c1e2f5fef6fab501de615fb83a74a0251f/docs/interfaces/AuthorizationCodeGrantChecks.md#maxage) (maybe to 60 seconds) so that the `auth_time` claim is properly validated.

I think we can update our [SSO Login integration tests](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/58697bba201371326186e6d15ce39699688993f5/tests/integration/api/controllers/login.spec.js#L316) to include a test for this functionality.

title: Optimize indexes to reduce disk use (Hosting TCO)
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
While working on [Reduce disk space during upgrades](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10092) (TCO v2), some ideas were kicked around about how big current indexes are. Here's the top 3 from a production instance:

| view | size |
|---|---|
| doc_summaries_by_id  | 8.31 GB | 
| docs_by_id_lineage  | 5.86 GB | 
| tasks_by_contact  | 5.55 GB | 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Find a way to reduce the size of the data on disk within couch

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
There's some [brainstorms](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10092) in TCO v2 that might be viable, but they're mostly not being explored actively.

**Additional context**
Disk use continues to be a large concern for deployments that scale up (1k+ users) and that have multiple instances.

title: Support collecting targets/UHC for Bikram Sambat months
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Requested [on the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/cht-targets-feature-display-data-in-nepali-calendar-bikram-sambat/5515).  

Currently [CHT Targets](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/targets/) and UHC counts are collected and stored per user _per Gregorian calendar month_. It is possible to customize the _day of the month_ that target collection begins/ends by setting the [`uhc.visit_count.month_start_date` value](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/forms/configuring/uhc-mode/#settings) in the settings.  This allows for adjusting target collection to be based on the `nth` day of the month instead of the `1st`, but this value is bound to the day of the Gregorian calendar month.  

In regions that use the Bikram Sambat calendar, reporting cycles may be tied to BS months and not Gregorian months. In this case we would want the Target/UHC counts to reset at the beginning of the BS month (or in a fixed interval of days from the beginning of the BS month). 

**Describe the solution you'd like**

We should add configuration that would allow aligning the Target/UHC counts to reset at the beginning of the BS month instead of the Gregorian calendar month.  

@bhishankc a key question here that maybe you can help with is: `Is it possible for a BS month to ever start and end within the same Gregorian calendar month?`

If the answer is "no" (it is not possible), then I think the code changes necessary to support this feature should be localized to just the date logic we use for calculating when the intervals should start/stop. The updates may not be "simple", but they will be limited in scope.  

If the answer is "yes", then things get more spicy.  Currently target documents are stored for each user with an identifier that includes the `YYYY-MM` value for the Gregorian month. If two BS months can _start_ in the same Gregorian month, then we may have a collision for our target identifiers.  Any resolution here would seem to involve challenges with compatibility when enabling/disabling this configuration. (Maybe that is fine 🤷).

title: Add frontend performance benchmarking suite
body:
**Describe the issue**
We update dependencies, browers, and so on, but the actual impact on client-side performance is not easily calculated or tracked. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Add a performance benchmarking suite for client-side events. This should be an automated test, preferably run like all our other scalability suites, on an AWS machine, but for ease of development, we can keep this running in GH Actions machines. 

This test should output performance metrics for a variety of frontend events, like replication, first time opening contacts, and so on. I believe that we should gradually cover all performance tests we used to do manually on devices. <I will search for a reference to those docs and add it later>

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Keep guessing.

body:
Bumps [sass](https://github.com/sass/dart-sass) from 1.83.4 to 1.97.3.
Release notes

Sourced from sass's releases.

Dart Sass 1.97.3

To install Sass 1.97.3, download one of the packages below and add it to your PATH, or see the Sass website for full installation instructions.

Changes

  • Fix a bug where nesting an at-rule within multiple style rules in plain CSS could cause outer style rules to be omitted.

See the full changelog for changes in earlier releases.

Dart Sass 1.97.2

To install Sass 1.97.2, download one of the packages below and add it to your PATH, or see the Sass website for full installation instructions.

Changes

  • Additional fixes for implicit configuration when nested imports are involved.

See the full changelog for changes in earlier releases.

Dart Sass 1.97.1

To install Sass 1.97.1, download one of the packages below and add it to your PATH, or see the Sass website for full installation instructions.

Changes

  • Fix a bug with the new CSS-style if() syntax where values would be evaluated even if their conditions didn't match.

See the full changelog for changes in earlier releases.

Dart Sass 1.97.0

To install Sass 1.97.0, download one of the packages below and add it to your PATH, or see the Sass website for full installation instructions.

Changes

  • Add support for the display-p3-linear color space.

See the full changelog for changes in earlier releases.

Dart Sass 1.96.0

To install Sass 1.96.0, download one of the packages below and add it to your PATH, or see the Sass website for full installation instructions.

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from sass's changelog.

1.97.3

  • Fix a bug where nesting an at-rule within multiple style rules in plain CSS could cause outer style rules to be omitted.

1.97.2

  • Additional fixes for implicit configuration when nested imports are involved.

1.97.1

  • Fix a bug with the new CSS-style if() syntax where values would be evaluated even if their conditions didn't match.

1.97.0

  • Add support for the display-p3-linear color space.

1.96.0

  • Allow numbers with complex units (more than one numerator unit or more than zero denominator units) to be emitted to CSS. These are now emitted as calc() expressions, which now support complex units in plain CSS.

1.95.1

  • No user-visible changes.

1.95.0

  • Add support for the CSS-style if() function. In addition to supporting the plain CSS syntax, this also supports a sass() query that takes a Sass expression that evaluates to true or false at preprocessing time depending on whether the Sass value is truthy. If there are no plain-CSS queries, the function will return the first value whose query returns true during preprocessing. For example, if(sass(false): 1; sass(true): 2; else: 3) returns 2.

  • The old Sass if() syntax is now deprecated. Users are encouraged to migrate to the new CSS syntax. if($condition, $if-true, $if-false) can be changed to if(sass($condition): $if-true; else: $if-false).

    See the Sass website for details.

  • Plain-CSS if() functions are now considered "special numbers", meaning that they can be used in place of arguments to CSS color functions.

  • Plain-CSS if() functions and attr() functions are now considered "special

title: Add `api` support for `ui-extension` endpoints in service worker
body:
After we have added the `ui-extension` endpoints in https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10630, we also need to add support for generating the service worker file with the new endpoint data for offline users.

See the [pattern for extension-libs](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/14eeaea40d1c3035bea114f2d49bb739d32f54bf/api/src/generate-service-worker.js#L61) and add support to the `generate-service-worker.js` file for providing the UI Extension data via the service worker for offline users.  Load the data via the ui-extension service.

We only need to include extensions on the service worker if they are accessible to offline users. Check the `roles` property for the extension and only include the extension if there is no `roles` (the extension is accessible to all users) or at least one of the roles is `offline: true`.

Besides the unit tests, I think we also _might_ need to update the [service-worker e2e test](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/b9ddc064d82158b65cd801eb8488ccbab4838de0/tests/e2e/default/service-worker/service-worker.wdio-spec.js#L8) to account for these changes. Just want to assert that the `/ui-extension` url is present in the "initial list of cached resources"...

title: Investigate user doc_ids caching
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
Yesterday, during the porocut team call, @witash said that sync performance is the same whether there are changes or not. 

5 years ago, I put together a proposal to cache doc_ids in between sync calls, and use the interim changes feed additions to complete the list, if the difference in docs was sufficiently small (to not overload API): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Rg7KTmJnbMGnU0ZC4U54uySYVE9yCXzeP1QIrkMIL7I/edit?tab=t.0

A lot has changed in the replication endpoint since then, so the steps here might not be accurate, but the idea was: cache doc_ids, as changes come in, api should have a small buffer of "last" changes docs_by_replication_keys results (buffer size undecided, depends on memory footprint). if user connects again and less than X changes have been pushed since his last sync, complete his doc_ids with the new changes that were pushed instead of querying the view again. 

This idea was turned down at the time due to its increased complexity. 

However, since it has been voiced, I am bringing it back to life. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Investigate how we can cache user allowed doc_ids and use buffered changes feed to push new docs, instead of querying view every time. 

We would need to check a live deployment and check how many docs we expect to be pushed within the 5 minute interval between the user syncs. We would need to accommodate a buffer larger than this value. 
Also API is single threaded and we should avoid overloading it with CPU blocking tasks.

title: Add UI Extensions service to `webapp`
body:
Add a new `webapp/src/ts/services/ui-extensions.service.ts` file with the following:

```ts
interface UiExtensionProperties {
  readonly id: string,
  readonly type: string
  readonly roles?: string[]
  readonly icon?: string
  readonly title?: string
  readonly config?: Record<string, unknown>
}

interface UiExtension {
  readonly properties: UiExtensionProperties
  readonly Element: HtmlElement
}
```

## `class UiExtensionsService`

- Load available UI extension data from the `api/v1/ui-extension` endpoint
	- Can follow patterns from cht-datasource.service for loading the extension-libs.
	- Should also only keep extensions that do not have `roles` configured or ones where the user has at least one of the configured `roles`.
	   - Use the `SessionService.hasRole` method to check.
  - Can cache this property data since it will be accessed several times. 
- `getPropertiesByType(type: string): UiExtensionProperties[]` - return the properties for all  extensions with the given type
- `getProperties(id: string): UiExtensionProperties` - return the property data for the given type.
- `getExtension(id: string): UiExtension`
	- Follow the pattern [from the cht-datasource.service](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/dad316fa2875e356bc265e218869e70d131870fb/webapp/src/ts/services/cht-datasource.service.ts#L72) to load the UI extension code from the script file (via the  `/ui-extension/:id` endpoint).
		- Want to return the result of `module.exports` (which should contain the web component exported by the script) and the `element` property.

---

Add new unit test file:  `webapp/tests/karma/ts/services/ui-extensions.service.spec.ts`

title: Add UI Extensions Tab component to `webapp`
body:
Depends on https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10670

There are several interlocking pieces we need to add to render the UI Extensions in the webapp and handle routing to them:

## UI Extensions Tab Component

Add new files: `webapp/src/ts/modules/ui-extensions/ui-extensions-tab.component.ts/html`

The HTML file needs to have the same outer framework as the other "tab" pages.  See the [trainings.component.html](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/e33cd8738be9bbe1e3c34566fe07d7bf9fa9da6f/webapp/src/ts/modules/trainings/trainings.component.html) for example.  I think we need the `mm-tool-bar` at the top and then the `inner` and `inbox page` divs.  Then we need a custom wrapper div nested inside with the id: `ui-element-tab`.  Also , I think we can include similar `loader` logic to display a loading spinner while the extension code is being loaded.

For the `UiExtensionsTabComponent` class, we want to take the `ActivatedRoute` as a constructor parameter.  Then we can get the extension id via `route.snapshot.params['id']`.  With that id we can call the `UiExtensionsService.getExtension` method to get the actual web component code/properties.

The `UiExtensionsTabComponent` should have a property that references the wrapper div like:

```ts
@ViewChild('ui-element-tab') container!: ElementRef;`
```

From the `ngAfterViewInit()` method, Initialize the web component element with something like:

```ts
customElements.define(id, Element);
const element = document.createElement(id);
// TODO Set properties on element here before appending it.
this.container.nativeElement.appendChild(element);
```

We need to set the following properties:
- `cht` - the "CHT API" loaded from `CHTDatasourceService.get`. Contains versioned functions for interacting with the CHT data model (from cht-datasource) as well as utility functions for doing other things (extension-libs, translate, etc)
- `inputs` - wrapper object for all the _data_ inputs
    - `config` - the contents of the `config` property defined in the extension properties (useful if loading custom configuration)
    - `userContactSummary` - loaded from the `UserContactSummaryService`.

## UI Extensions Tab Route Guard Provider

Create a route guard in a new file: `webapp/src/ts/modules/ui-extensions/ui-extensions-route.guard.provider.ts` -  `UiExtensionsTabRouteGuardProvider implements CanActivate`.  See the [AppRouteGuardProvider](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/35662788c503441ef25ebe15ff99dbdd3bd2f104/webapp/src/ts/app-route.guard.provider.ts#L8) as an example.

When `canActivate` is called, call  `UiExtensionsService.getProperties` method with the `route.params['id]` value to get extension properties. Fail activation if the extension does not have a `type` of `app_main_tab` or `app_drawer_tab`.

## UI Extensions Routes

Create a new routes file: `webapp/src/ts/modules/ui-extensions/ui-extensions.routes.ts`. See the [training.routes.ts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/e33cd8738be9bbe1e3c34566fe07d7bf9fa9da6f/webapp/src/ts/modules/trainings/trainings.routes.ts#L8) as an example.

Export a parameterized route:

- `path` - `ui-extensions/:id`
- `component` - `UiExtensionsTabComponent`
- `canActivate` - `[UiExtensionsTabRouteGuardProvider]`

Update `webapp/src/ts/app-routing.module.ts` to include the new route.

---

Add new unit tests to the `webapp/tests/karma/ts/modules/ui-extensions` directory.

title: Add `webapp` support for showing `app_drawer_tab`  in the sidebar
body:
Update `webapp/src/ts/components/sidebar-menu/sidebar-menu.component.ts` to show entries for UI extensions with `app_drawer_tab` type.  Use the `UiExtensionsService.getPropertiesByType` method to load the relevant extensions and append the options to the end of the `moduleOptions` array.

- `routerLink` - `ui-extensions/${id}`,
- `translationKey` - `properties.title`,
- `resourceIcon` - `properties.icon`

The current implementation of the sidebar-menu component is a little weird about the separation of `moduleOptions` and `secondaryOptions`.  I think the evolution of the two arrays over the years has ended up on a place that does not make a lot of sense from a UX perspective. Currently the `moduleOptions` are displayed _above_ the storage status and sync status while the `secondaryOptions` are listed below.  

Part of the reason I think this was allowed to happen is that `moduleOptions` are basically never actually shown (and are a very legacy "feature" that was used at one time for some UI backwards compatibility).  To see any of the current `moduleOptions` (e.g. the "Messages" button), the user needs to have a permission like `can_view_messages,!can_view_messages_tab`, meaning the user should see messages, but not the messages _tab_ in the main bar.  

After some discussion in the squad meeting, the conclusion is to merge `moduleOptions` and `secondaryOptions` so that they both just show in the same list where `secondaryOptions` is currently rendered. We should add the UI Extensions entries to this same array.  The order should be:

- Current entries for `modulesOptions`
- UI Extensions
- Current entries for `secondaryOptions`


We also need to be sure that this functionality works for users with the `can_view_old_navigation` permission.

title: Store geolocation when submitting contact forms
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We store geolocation when submitting report forms, but not when submitting contact forms.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Store GPS coordinates when contact forms are submitted. 

Some considerations:

For reports, we store GPS coordinates every time the report is edited, so a report edited 3 times would have a GPS log with 3 entries. This might be ok for reports, because reports are not edited frequently and the GPS coordinates meaning is not connected to anything except the location of the submission. 

For contacts, the stored coordinates have meaning. Ideally they would be the approximate location of contact (their address). Contacts are expected to be edited frequently, and it's not necessary that the user be at the home of the contact in order to edit the contact. 
Maybe this bleeds a little more into _what we would use the coordinates for_, more than whether or not we should store additional entries on every edit. 

**Additional context**
This came up as part of the task prioritization squad and about ways to improve CHT UX experience.

title: Update CHT API service in `webapp` to include functions for getting translations and resources
body:
## Refactor `ResourceIconService`

We need to refactor the `webapp/src/ts/services/resource-icons.service.ts` to just be the more generic `CustomResourceService`. Then add a new method: `getResource(name: string): { content_type: string, data: string }`.  This function should just directly return the result of `getAttachment` for the `resources` doc.  

~~TODO Not sure if this method should return a Promise that waits on `this.initResources`.  (I think instead of that, if we run into a problem with the extension being loaded before the resources, we could expose the `this.initResources` so that the `UiExtensionsTabComponent` could await the loading of the resources before loading the extension.  This would allow the `getResource` function to remain sync and keep the extension code more simple.)~~

Edit: We should be safe with a _sync_ call here and can assume that the cache is already built.

## Extend CHT API returned from `CHTDatasourceService`

The CHT API returned from the `CHTDatasourceService.get` function will be injected into the extensions as the `cht` variable.  This api needs to include a few additional functions within the `v1` object:

- `translate(key: string, interpolateParams?:  Record<string, unknown>): string` - a wrapper around the `TranslateService.instant` method.
- `getResource(name: string): { content_type: string, data: string }` - a wrapper around the `CustomResourceService.getResource` method.

title: Geolocation acquisition timeout blocks submitting forms
body:
<!--
**Important**: This is a public repository. Anyone in the world can see what's posted here. If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the bug**
When we submit a form, the geolocation service tries to store GPS coordinates. The service tries to get GPS coordinates for 30 seconds before quitting: 

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/e21d8f8b0d1456ca5534ef19a944186b2e195a84/webapp/src/ts/services/geolocation.service.ts#L11

Ideally, the coordinates would be retrieved quickly and no wait would be required. 
However, when GPS signal is weak, coordinates acquisition can often exceed the 30 second timeout we have set. When this happens, and the user attempts to submit the form before the 30 second timeout expiry, they will see a spinner by the submit button for the remaining duration. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Make sure GPS permission is allowed
2. Go somewhere with weak GPS signal 
3. Try to submit a small form quickly
4. You wait for 30 seconds before submission actually happens

**Expected behavior**
This caused confusion in some deployments and this ended up having CHWs turn off their GPS entirely. Having to wait for 30 seconds is very frustrating. Such as in this video. 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f16c0be1-7ed3-4ba2-bbc3-2d6ac1fa60cd

**Environment**
- App: webapp
- Version: all

title: Investigate adding a built-in data backup solution
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We've had multiple production instances facing data loss due to disk failures, database corruption of unknown sources, where these instances either did not have backups set up or the backups were unusable. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'm proposing we investigate a built-in backup solution. 
This should not be considered a full backup solution, but rather an opt-out setup where critical data is saved in a secondary location. Think first-aid-kit vs hospital or fire extinguisher vs fire brigade. 

My initial thoughts would be to have a sidecar container that has access to two data volumes, one of them being the CouchDb data volume and the other being the secondary storage. Depending on the instance setup, this provides more or less safety. 
This container would save the CouchDb `medic data shards to the separate location. This will exclude indexes and secondary databases (however, we would maybe choose to include the _users database as well). Saving would happen daily (? or be configurable through an env parameter for example). 
The solution should also include scripts to restore data easily. 
The solution should be e2e tested in our CI suite. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
@jkuester suggested we somehow add the action to create the backups in cht-conf. 
@mrjones-plip suggested to display a nudge to backup in the Admin app. 
Other suggestions were to have an external service that does backup. 
Considerations: backups may need to be sent to different vm’s, disks, data centers.

Happy to hear thoughts!

title: UHC: Add place filtering based on collected data
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
With UHC enabled, the application displays the number of visits to a household in the LHS places list, and adds a new sorting based on visit count. But visits alone is proving to not be a sufficient indicator of offered health coverage. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Improve UHC by adding household filters based on collected data. 
One such example would be to display the number of pregnant women within the household. This filter would help identify households with high maternal-health needs. 

**Additional context**
[Forum thread](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/improving-the-community-coverage-strategy-based-on-collected-data/5521/5)

title: Implement free text search feature in tasks page
body: **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** In CHT 5.1.0, we added task filtering by due date, form and place. To further enhance user agency in filtering the task list, we can implement free text search similar to reports. **Describe the solution you'd like** Implement the search bar in the tasks page. At the least the search should be able to cover any contact name in the task lineage. The search would be done directly on the available task list, without accessing the database. This means that we need to implement search terms for tasks and a fuzzy matching for names. **Additional context** Part of smart task prioritization. -------------------- Assets for Release Notes based of [final solution in PR](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/11142): https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/88ce162d-cc67-43a7-b8f4-38281e8c1b8c

title: Implement telemetry to track task selection duration
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
The recent changes to the tasks page (filtering, sorting by priority, search) all have the potential to improve task list navigation for users. However we don't have a way to verify or quantify the improvement. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Implement a sort of task selection telemetry score, where we track how much time the user spends on the task list selecting which task to complete. 
A successful "score" would only be recorded when the user actually finds the task they wanted to complete and they complete it. Task completion time should not be part of the score, as that time depends on the task form. 
A failed "score" would be recorded when the user opens a task and closes it, because they have selected the incorrect one. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Add some sort of analytics, instead of telemetry, that would analyze user behavior. 

**Additional context**
Part of smart task prioritization squad.

title: Support Photo Capture for Sub-contacts Within Parent Registration Forms
body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

In community health contexts where CHWs register households with 10 or more members at once, the current workflow for capturing contact photos is highly inefficient and impractical.

Today, photo capture requires opening a `person-edit` form individually for each household member **after** the household registration is complete. For a household with 10 members, this means the CHW must:

1. Complete the household (`clinic-create`) registration form
2. Navigate back to each individual member's profile
3. Open the `person-edit` form for each person
4. Capture and submit the photo
5. Repeat steps 2–4 for every member

This results in the same action being performed 10+ times in a single household visit, creating a fragmented and repetitive workflow that is disconnected from the natural point of registration.

In practice, CHWs are likely to skip photo capture altogether due to the burden this imposes and directly undermining the purpose of the feature and reducing data quality at scale.

---

## Describe the solution you'd like

We would like support for **capturing photos (and other file attachments) for sub-contacts directly within a parent registration form**, such as `clinic-create`.

Specifically:

- Within the household registration form, as each household member is being registered, the CHW should be able to capture that member's photo inline as part of the same form flow
- The captured photo should be saved as an attachment on the respective person contact document upon form submission
- The photo should be **visible on the individual contact's profile page** in the CHT app once submitted,  just as it would be if captured via `person-edit`
- This should work **offline**, consistent with CHT's offline-first architecture

This would allow photo capture to happen at the natural point of registration, as part of a single uninterrupted workflow, significantly improving data completeness and CHW experience.
