title: Rate limiter can block requests with valid credentials that are unrelated to auth failures
body:
**Describe the bug**

The API rate limiter (`api/src/services/rate-limit.js`) tracks failed login attempts by multiple keys: client IP (`req.ip`), username, and password. It allows 10 failed attempts per 10-second window per key. When any key is exhausted, all requests matching that key are rejected with `429 Too Many Requests`.

Unrelated services with valid credentials (notably couch2pg) have been observed receiving `429 Too Many Requests` errors in a production deployment. 

This could happen when a reverse proxy forwards requests to the API without preserving the real client IP. When `req.ip` resolves to the proxy's internal IP for all requests, the IP-based rate limit key becomes shared across all users and services. Then failed login attempts from one client can trigger rate limiting for every client on the instance.

Also `429` responses also trigger `consume()`, so continued retries from any client continue the lockout.

**Impact**

If the proxy IP is shared across all requests, then 10 failed authentication attempts from any combination of users or services within a 10-second window will block every login request or request using basic authentication instance-wide.

Affected clients include:
- **couch2pg** and other automated scripts using basic auth for every request
- **Any user logging in** via the login page or API during the lockout window; although this hasn't been reported directly.
- **Other services** (e.g., interoperability tools, custom integrations) using basic auth

**To Reproduce**

The exact proxy configuration that triggers this behavior has not yet been confirmed. Using docker compose on an EC2 instance does **not** reproduce the issue, even though it does use nginx; the IPs that the api container gets in that case are the actual IPs, not proxy IPs. I still suspect this is happening on k3s deployments with an upstream nginx reverse proxy.

To confirm, we could check the API logs for the IP addresses associated with requests.

** Proposed fix **

It may be possible for the rate-limiter to use the X-Forwarded-For header instead of the proxy IP.

** Proposed workaround for couch2pg (no release required) **

couch2pg currently uses basic authentication on every request. It can be changed to use session-based authentication instead. Although couch2pg is supposed to be deprecated, this small change could bypass the issue for deployments that are unable or unwilling to upgrade to the version with a fix in cht-core.

title: [DMP 2026]: Add API endpoints for advanced contact management operations
body:
## Ticket Contents

Currently, the CHT (Community Health Toolkit) app allows users to perform basic contact management tasks such as creating an editing contacts. Users with the proper permissions can also delete contacts, but _only if there are no child contacts associated with the contact to delete._

More [advanced contact management](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/contact-management/moving-contacts/) current requires a system administrator to use the [`cht-conf` CLI tool](https://github.com/medic/cht-conf). `cht-conf` can perform operations like [moving](https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/blob/main/src/fn/move-contacts.js), [merging](https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/blob/main/src/fn/merge-contacts.js), and [deleting](https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/blob/main/src/fn/delete-contacts.js) contacts in the hierarchy (note that the `delete-contacts` action in cht-conf is _recursive_ so that it also deletes all the child contacts). Having this functionality in `cht-conf` creates friction for users who cannot perform these actions themselves through the webapp, especially when dealing with duplicate contacts or reorganizing health facility hierarchies.

It also forces services like [cht-user-management](https://github.com/medic/cht-user-management) to either re-implement these operations or else somehow leverage cht-conf under the hood to perform them.  

This project aims to add REST API endpoints in `cht-core` for these actions. The work can be done incrementally (one action at a time), giving it a limited initial scope with room to expand. The goal is simply to have api support for these operations. Updating the webapp to actually give the user access to these operations is _out of scope_. 

Edit: We decided to drop from `merge` from this project to better focus on polishing the bulk-operations API that was created to support delete/move. When adding support for `merge` in the future, we will be able to leverage this same bulk-operations API.  👍 

## Goals & Mid-Point Milestone

- [x] Understand the existing `cht-conf` move/merge/delete contact logic
- [x] Implement the delete-contacts API endpoint with support for recursive hierarchy deletion
- [x] Implement the move-contacts API endpoint for relocating contacts between parent hierarchies
- [ ] ~~Implement the merge-contacts API endpoint for combining duplicate contacts and reassigning all linked documents (reports, tasks) to the surviving contact~~
- [x] Write API documentation for all new endpoints in [cht-docs](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs)
- [x] **Goals achieved by mid-point milestone:** Delete-contacts and move-contacts API endpoints are functional with unit and integration tests

## Expected Outcome

New REST API endpoints available in `cht-core`:
- `DELETE /api/v1/contact/:uuid` (or `POST /api/v1/contact/:uuid/delete`) for recursively deleting a contact and its children in one step
- `POST /api/v1/contact/:uuid/move` for moving a contact (and its subtree) to a new parent
- ~~`POST /api/v1/contact/:uuid/merge` for merging two duplicate contacts, reassigning all linked documents to the surviving contact~~

These endpoints replace the need to use the `cht-conf` CLI for these operations, enabling them to be performed programmatically or through the webapp.

## Implementation Details

The existing `cht-conf` implementations serve as the reference for the core logic:
- [`cht-conf/src/fn/move-contacts.js`](https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/blob/main/src/fn/move-contacts.js)
- [`cht-conf/src/fn/merge-contacts.js`](https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/blob/main/src/fn/merge-contacts.js)
- [`cht-conf/src/fn/delete-contacts.js`](https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/blob/main/src/fn/delete-contacts.js)

New API controllers should be added in `api/src/controllers/` following the patterns established by the existing person, place, and report controllers.

Key technical considerations:
- TODO these actions may involve long-running processes.  We need to determine if we should block our REST response until the process actually completes (our typical approach for existing endpoints) or if we should implement some kind of "polling" pattern where we queue the operation and then immediately return a reference to it. Then the consumer can poll a `/api/v1/operation` endpoint to get the status (and know when it completes). 
- Permission model should follow the `hasAny` pattern (e.g. `can_delete_contacts` OR `can_edit`)
- Delete must handle recursive cleanup of child contacts and all associated documents
- Move must update parent lineage references across the entire subtree and linked documents
- Merge must handle conflict resolution and reassignment of all linked reports and tasks to the surviving contact

title: [DMP 2026]: Enhance Bikram Sambat support in CHT
body:
## Ticket Contents

The CHT has basic [Bikram Sambat (BS) calendar support](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/bikram-sambat/) used in [app forms](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/forms/app/#bikram-sambat-datepicker), but several quality-of-life issues make it incomplete for users in Nepal and other regions using this calendar system. The current date picker is minimal (no calendar view, no month navigation), the Reports tab filter still shows the Gregorian calendar even when the language is set to Nepali, there is a bug where dates convert incorrectly when no month is selected, and [targets/UHC counts](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/targets/) reset on Gregorian month boundaries instead of Bikram Sambat month boundaries.

This project is a collection of improvements to make Bikram Sambat a first-class calendar experience in the CHT. The work can be done incrementally (one issue at a time).

## Goals & Mid-Point Milestone

- [x] Understand the existing Bikram Sambat date picker implementation and the [`bikram-sambat`](https://github.com/nickshanks/bikram-sambat) library
- [x] Fix the bug where the date picker defaults to Baisakh (first month) when user hasn't selected a month, allowing incorrect date conversion
- [x] Upgrade the Bikram Sambat date picker with proper calendar view (month/weeks), month/year navigation, "today" button, and clear option
- [x] Integrate Bikram Sambat calendar into the Reports tab date filter (currently shows Gregorian even in Nepali mode)
- [x] Add configuration to align target/UHC count resets to Bikram Sambat month boundaries instead of Gregorian months
- [x] Write unit tests and e2e tests for all changes
- [x] **Goals achieved by mid-point milestone:** Date picker bug is fixed, date picker is fully upgraded, and Reports tab date filter uses BS calendar, with unit tests

## Expected Outcome

- A fully functional Bikram Sambat date picker with a proper calendar view, navigation controls, and parity with the Gregorian date picker UX
- The Reports tab date filter displays the Bikram Sambat calendar when the platform language is set to Nepali
- The date picker no longer silently defaults to Baisakh when no month is selected
- A new configuration option (e.g. in `app_settings`) that allows target/UHC counts to reset at the beginning of BS months instead of Gregorian months

## Implementation Details

The Bikram Sambat date picker widget lives in:
- `webapp/src/ts/` (Angular webapp components)

The [nepali-date-picker](https://github.com/opensource-nepal/nepali-date-picker) ([demo](https://leapfrogtechnology.github.io/nepali-date-picker/demo/)) can be used as reference for the improved date picker UI.

For the date picker bug: the widget currently converts the date even when the user hasn't selected a month, defaulting to Baisakh. The fix should either require month selection before conversion or handle the missing month gracefully.

For the Reports tab filter: the date filter component needs to detect when the platform language is Nepali and render the BS calendar instead of Gregorian. Date range conversions between BS and Gregorian will be needed for the underlying CouchDB queries.

For target/UHC alignment: currently targets are stored with an identifier that includes `YYYY-MM` for the Gregorian month. The [`uhc.visit_count.month_start_date`](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/forms/configuring/uhc-mode/#settings) setting controls the day targets reset. A new configuration would override this to use BS month boundaries instead.

Key technical consideration: an open design question exists around whether a BS month can ever start and end within the same Gregorian month, which could cause target document ID collisions.

title: ContactChangeFilterService.isRelevantChange uses ?? instead of ||, making isRelevantContact and isRelevantReport dead code
body:
## Description

`ContactChangeFilterService.isRelevantChange()` [uses](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/services/contact-change-filter.service.ts#L82-L86) the nullish coalescing operator (`??`) instead of logical OR (`||`):

```typescript
isRelevantChange(change, contact) {
  return this.matchContact(change, contact) ??
    this.isRelevantContact(change, contact) ??
    this.isRelevantReport(change, contact);
}
```

Since `matchContact()` always returns a boolean (`true` or `false`, never `null` or `undefined`), `false ?? expr` evaluates to `false` immediately — the `??` operator only falls through on `null`/`undefined`. This means `isRelevantContact()` and `isRelevantReport()` are never called.

## Impact
While testing the stock monitoring workflow we noticed a weird behavior, the summary being updated not frequently, and we were not able to know at that time, and it came out later when checking this `isRelevantChange` function:

The `user-contact-summary` cache is never invalidated when:
- A new report is submitted for a contact (e.g., stock monitoring reports)
- A child contact is added or modified

The cache only invalidates when the contact document itself changes (`matchContact` returns `true`).

This causes stale contact summaries in the UI until the contact doc is coincidentally modified or a full page reload occurs.

### Example: Stock monitoring

When a CHW submits a `patient_assessment_under_5` form, it creates an `sm_stock_report_chw` additional doc with `patient_id` = CHW's contact `_id`. The `isRelevantReport` method would correctly match this report via `registrationUtils.getSubjectIds`, but it is never called.

**Why it "sometimes works":** If sentinel processing or sync touches the CHW's person doc, the cache invalidates as a side effect. But reports alone never trigger invalidation.

## Fix

Replace `??` with `||`:

```typescript
isRelevantChange(change, contact) {
  return this.matchContact(change, contact) ||
    this.isRelevantContact(change, contact) ||
    this.isRelevantReport(change, contact);
}
```


cc: @dianabarsan or @jkuester , we would need your point of view on this.

title: Offline Re-authentication
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Users in areas with no internet connectivity are unable to log in to the CHT app even when app code and data are already cached on their device. When a session expires, health workers in hard-to-reach communities are fully locked out — despite the CHT being designed for offline-first day-to-day use.
Extending the session duration is not a viable workaround in our deployment. We have intentionally reduced sessions to 12 hours to strengthen account security, specifically because devices are shared among multiple users, there is a real risk of users not logging out after use, and the app captures strictly confidential patient data, including sensitive clinical health information.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Support offline re-authentication so that users who have previously authenticated online can re-authenticate on their device without an internet connection. The app should store a secure credential hash locally at the time of online login, and verify submitted credentials against that hash when the server is unreachable. This would allow uninterrupted access to cached data and workflows after a short session expires, without weakening server-side security controls.

The implementation should:
- Require at least one prior successful online login before offline re-authentication is possible
- Use a salted credential hash (not plaintext credentials) stored in secure local storage
- Not extend or modify the server-side session — offline login should be a client-side gate to locally cached data only
- Respect account disablement: if the account was disabled server-side, offline login should be invalidated upon next successful sync

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- **Extending session duration** - Not viable. We run 12-hour sessions intentionally due to shared devices and security policy.
- **SSO (OIDC)** - Currently requires a network round-trip to the identity provider, so it doesn't solve the offline case.

title: Multi-User Support on a Shared Device (Offline-Capable)
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
In shared-device deployments, multiple health workers use the same physical device. Currently, the CHT does not support caching credentials or data for more than one user on a device. When a new user logs in, the previous user's local session is lost, and each login requires an internet connection. This is a significant barrier in contexts where connectivity is intermittent and devices rotate between shift workers or community health teams.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Support multiple user accounts on a single device, each with its own offline-capable session. Specifically:

- Allow N user accounts to be registered on a device (ideally configurable by deployment administrators)
- Each account should maintain its own locally cached data and credential hash, isolated from other accounts
- Users should be able to switch between accounts from the login screen without requiring internet connectivity, provided they have previously logged in online at least once
- Account data isolation must be enforced: User A must not be able to access User B's cached records
- Deployments should be able to cap the number of cached accounts per device to manage storage

This directly addresses shared-device workflows common in community health settings, where a device may serve an entire team across shifts.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- **One device per user** — Not feasible in our deployment context due to cost and logistics.
- **Longer sessions** — Reduces security. Does not address the multi-user problem.
- **Token login** — Explicitly not supported for multi-user scenarios per CHT documentation.

**Additional context**
This feature has a dependency relationship with offline re-authentication (https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10719) Multi-user offline support is only meaningful if each user can also re-authenticate offline after a session expires. The two features complement each other and could be scoped as a cohesive "offline-first authentication" workstream.

title: fix: remove unnecessary backslash escapes in grep patterns
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format

# Description

## Fixes #9310

## Problem
When running 

scripts/docker-helper/cht-docker-compose.sh and initialising a new project, modern versions of grep emit warnings:

grep: warning: stray \ before :
grep: warning: stray \ before :


## Root Cause
Inside grep bracket expressions [...], most characters are already literal and do not need backslash escaping. The patterns on lines 59, 63 and 200 contained unnecessary backslashes (e.g. \., \_, \/, \- inside [...]), which newer grep versions correctly warn about.

## Fix
Line 59: Changed [A-Za-z0-9\.\\_\\/\\-]* → [A-Za-z0-9._/-]*
Line 63: Changed [0-9\\.]* → [0-9.]*
Line 200: Added -F (fixed-string) flag to avoid regex interpretation of service names
The patterns match exactly the same strings as before — no functional change.

## Testing
Ran ./cht-docker-compose.sh and initialized a new project. Confirmed no grep: warning messages appear in the output.

title: Fix bugs and typos in smsparser.js and related files
body:
## Bug 1 – String list parser always returns undefined
`for (const i of field.list)` + `field.list[i]` — `i` is an item not an index, always `undefined`.
All string list fields warn "Option not available" and never match.

**Fix:** Use `for (const item of field.list)` directly.

## Bug 2 – parseArray() crashes when def is null
`getParser(def, doc)` called before null-check on `def` → `parser` is `undefined`
→ `TypeError: parser is not a function`.

**Fix:** Move `if (!def || !def.fields) return []` to top of `parseArray()`.

## Typos
- `becuase` → `because` — `smsparser.js`, `infodoc.js`
- `succesfully` → `successfully` — `reminders.js`

## Files Affected
- `api/src/services/report/smsparser.js`
- `api/src/controllers/infodoc.js`
- `sentinel/src/schedule/reminders.js`

title: fix: correct typos and two bugs in smsparser.js
body:
PR: Close #10729 
## Changes

### Bug 1 – String field list parser
`for (const i of field.list)` yielded items not indices, making 
`field.list[i]` always undefined → string list fields never matched.
**Fix:** Iterate with `for (const item of field.list)`.

### Bug 2 – parseArray null crash  
`parser(def, doc)` was called before null-checking `def`, causing 
`TypeError` if def is null/undefined.  
**Fix:** Guard at the top before any parser calls.

### Typos
Fixed `becuase` → `because` (x2) and `succesfully` → `successfully` in comments/logs.

title: fix: add safety checks to prevent race condition in contact summary
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

feat(#1234): add hat wobble
^--^(#^--^): ^------------^
|     |      |
|     |      + - > subject
|     |
|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: build|feat|fix|perf|refactor|test|chore

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

In the default configuration, clicking a contact immediately after a page refresh could cause a crash (e.g., TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'type') in isReadyForNewPregnancy). This happens because the contact summary calculation is triggered before the contact data has fully loaded.

Fixes #10661

## Root Cause
Several functions in contact-summary-extras.js were directly accessing thisContact.type without first verifying if this contact was defined.

## Fix
Added null checks (!thisContact ||) to the following functions in the default configuration:
isActivePregnancy
isReadyForNewPregnancy
isReadyForDelivery

These functions now safely return false if the contact is missing, preventing the crash and stopping unnecessary "Feedback" error reports from being created.

## Testing
Manual: Verified in local CHT instance by refreshing the "People" tab and clicking a contact as fast as possible. No crash occurred.
Automated: Added a new unit test suite config/default/test/contact-summary-extras/race_condition.spec.js
 that confirms handled undefined inputs.

title: Remove docs_by_id_lineage map reduce view
body:
The `docs_by_id_lineage` map reduce view is one of the largest views on the instances sampled.
It emits for every ancestor of every document with a `contact` field; with _id as the value; which allows getting all ancestor documents in a single query with the `include_docs` parameter.

This could be replaced by two calls to `all_docs`; one to get the child document, which contains all the ancestors that would be emitted by the view, then a second call to `all_docs` with the ancestor `_ids` to get the actual documents. 

If this view was called with a lot of ids, it could be more efficient to make a single call to get all the documents with their ancestors instead of making two `all_docs` queries, with a large number of keys (the second query would have to have all the ancestor ids).

However, its not currently used that way; its always called with a single id, where it's not likely to be much more efficient than just making two `all_docs` calls.

Since it is very large, if its not too much worse to use all_docs, this view should be removed.

## View: medic-client/docs_by_id_lineage

### Definition
- **Database:** medic (synced to offline clients)
- **Map keys:** `[doc._id, depth]` (depth increments along parent chain)
- **Map values:** `{ _id: parent._id }` (for linked-document fetching with `include_docs`)
- **Reduce:** None

### Usages
| # | File | Key/Options Used | Functional Purpose |
|---|------|------------------|--------------------|
| 1 | shared-libs/lineage/src/hydration.js:231 | `{ startkey: [id], endkey: [id, {}], include_docs: true }` | Core lineage hydration: fetches a document and all its ancestors. Used by `fetchHydratedDoc` and `fetchLineageById` throughout the codebase. |
| 2 | shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/libs/lineage.ts:24 | `startkey: [id], endkey: [id, {}]` (via `queryDocsByRange`) | cht-datasource local data context lineage resolution. Used by `Person.v1.getWithLineage`, `Place.v1.getWithLineage`, `Contact.v1.getWithLineage`. |

title: Move tasks_by_contact to offline clients only
body:
The `tasks_by_contact` is one of the largest views one the instance sampled, which contains a large number of tasks. The map function is complicated, using prefixes for different cases and may emit multiple times per task document.

This view is only used by the rules engine in offline clients; it is never used by the server.
Similar to the freetext mapreduce views, it can be moved to a design document that is only for offline clients.

Ideally, it could be refactored to be more useful generally, but for a quick win, removing it from the server could have a large impact on index size.

## View: medic-client/tasks_by_contact

### Definition
- **Database:** medic (synced to offline clients)
- **Map keys:** Three emission patterns: (1) `'owner-' + owner` (non-terminal tasks), (2) `'requester-' + requester`, (3) `['owner', 'all', owner]` with value `{ state }`
- **Map values:** `{ state }` for the compound key pattern, none for string keys
- **Reduce:** None

### Usages
| # | File | Key/Options Used | Functional Purpose |
|---|------|------------------|--------------------|
| 1 | shared-libs/rules-engine/src/pouchdb-provider.js:42 | `{ startkey: 'requester-', endkey: 'requester-\ufff0', include_docs: true }` | Fetches all tasks by prefix (typically 'requester') for rules engine initialization. |
| 2 | shared-libs/rules-engine/src/pouchdb-provider.js:111 | `{ keys: ['requester-contactId', ...], include_docs: true }` | Fetches tasks for specific contacts by requester. |
| 3 | shared-libs/rules-engine/src/pouchdb-provider.js:116 | `{ keys: [['owner', 'all', contactId], ...] }` | Gets task row metadata by owner for specific contacts. Returns rows with `{ state }` values. |
| 4 | shared-libs/rules-engine/src/pouchdb-provider.js:119 | `{ startkey: ['owner', 'all'], endkey: ['owner', 'all', '\ufff0'] }` | Gets all task rows across all owners for rules engine enumeration. |

title: fix(#8816): support Couch admins pre-definied in `.ini` file
body:
<!--

|
+ -------------- > type: build|feat|fix|perf|refactor|test|chore

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

## Fixes: #8816 

## Root Cause: 
The CouchDB docker-entrypoint.sh script previously used a hardcoded grep search sequence (grep -Pzq "\[admins\]\n$COUCHDB_USER =") to verify if the server admin was already populated in cluster-credentials.ini. This approach is extremely fragile because it strictly requires the target user to appear on the exact line immediately following the [admins] header. If multiple admins exist, the check silently fails, causing the script to inadvertently append a duplicate [admins] block and corrupt the server configuration across container restarts.

## Solution: 
I replaced the fragile regex with a robust, POSIX-compliant awk INI parser exactly where the admin checks occur. This guarantees that the script targets exclusively within the active [admins] block and correctly parses the username key regardless of its position in the list or surrounding spaces. When the user is successfully identified, it cleanly skips the duplicate insertion and preserves the config integrity.

title: Cookies not being sent with `secure: true`
body:
**Describe the bug**
In our api code [for sending cookies to the user](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/589a9d49a6bc9f8a8af2dc38447b9265c736a5b1/api/src/services/cookie.js#L16) we have some logic for setting the [`secure` attribute](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Practical_implementation_guides/Cookies#secure).  (This attribute controls whether the cookie is only allowed to be sent via HTTPS and not just HTTP.) Unfortunately, this logic depends on the value of the `NODE_ENV` environment variable being set to `production`. Otherwise, we default to `secure: false`.  However, it seems that we are no longer setting the `NODE_ENV` value anywhere in our containers/config.  So, I do not think `secure` is ever getting set to `true` (even in production).  

(It is also worth noting that we need `secure: false` when running the server locally for cht-core development since that is via HTTP.)

**To Reproduce**
Deploy a CHT server production-style (e.g. via Docker Helper). 

Run this curl command with your instance info:

```shell
curl -v -k -X POST https://192-168-1-20.local-ip.medicmobile.org:37581 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"user":"medic","password":"password"}' 2>&1 | grep -i set-cookie
```

See that the result is:

```shell
< set-cookie: login=force; Path=/; SameSite=Lax
```

**Expected behavior**

The result of the curl command should include `Secure;`.  Like this:

```shell
< set-cookie: login=force; Path=/; Secure; SameSite=La
```

**Additional context**

This secure cookie logic based on `NODE_ENV` was added a long time ago: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/commit/ae75e27a13730287e033542129e4f6d616a02d5b.

I found this issue while reviewing [this PR](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10583) which is updating the logging to not be based on NODE_ENV.

--- 

I am not exactly sure what the best solution here is.  We need to be able to toggle the `secure` value on for production and off for development.  I wonder if maybe we just make `NODE_ENV=production` into our [api Dockerfile](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/Dockerfile) and call it good... 🤔   I suppose any time we are running in Docker, we are running with HTTPS, correct?

title: fix(#10754): set NODE_ENV to production in Docker images
body:
# Description:
This PR ensures that Secure; cookies are enabled by default in production while maintaining a functional, non-SSL development environment for integration and E2E testing.

Fixes #10754

# Problem
The logic in api/src/services/cookie.js relies on NODE_ENV=production to enable the Secure; flag. Since this variable was missing from the Docker images, cookies were being sent without the flag even in production environments.

**Changes:**
- Production Security: Added ENV NODE_ENV=production to both api/Dockerfile and sentinel/Dockerfile to ensure secure defaults for deployed containers.
- Test Compatibility: Introduced tests/cht-core-test.override.yml and updated tests/utils/index.js to force NODE_ENV=development during test execution. This allows the integration and E2E suites to run correctly in non-SSL environments (like local development or CI) without compromising production security.
- Architectural Alignment: Followed the environment configuration pattern currently being established in PR #10583.

# Description

### Fixes #10564

This PR stabilises the flaky training materials E2E test by resolving two timing-related race conditions:

**Hamburger Menu Click Failure:** Added a browser.pause(ELEMENT_DISPLAY_PAUSE) to openHamburgerMenu
 to ensure the CSS slide-in animation fully completes before Webdriver attempts to click any menu options. This prevents clicks from missing the animating element (which caused subsequent tests to fail on the /#/messages screen).
 
 
**Training Modal Timeout:** Adjusted the test's start_date generation to be exactly 1 minute in the past (Date.now() - 60000). This ensures the headless browser always evaluates the training as "active" immediately upon login, preventing the 15000ms timeout for #training-cards-form caused by minor clock skews between Node.js and the browser.


How should this be manually tested?
Because this is a flake fix, this should be validated by observing the E2E suites passing in CI environments without the intermittent timeouts and assertion errors seen in #10564.

title: Add task count labels to contacts list
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Sometimes users use the contacts tab, and the contacts list to navigate through their daily workflow. Currently contacts are sorted alphabetically and only the name is displayed. 
With UHC enabled, the number of household visits within the current month is also displayed. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Similar to UHC, where we add count of household visits to the contact RHS list, a similar feature where we display the number of tasks (or due tasks) has come up as being helpful. 
Like UHC, when this is enable, the user should be able to also sort the contacts based on the number of tasks. 

Mentioning that this should only be applied to households (leaf type places) where we already display a list of household tasks in the detail page. 

**Additional context**
Came up as a community suggestion through @JenniferMuli .

title: Provide per-form telemetry data (non-aggregated form fill start/end times)
body:
**Right now,** telemetry gives us aggregated data about how long forms take to fill out (like min, max, average, etc.). While this is useful we do lose visibility into individual form submissions.

**We’d like to store timestamps for each form directly in the data_record document:**

form_opened_at
form_submitted_at (already mostly covered by reported_date)

Having this per-submission timing would unlock a lot of practical insights:

Costing & budgeting – Understand how long each household visit actually takes
Travel estimation – Time gaps between submissions can approximate travel between households
Quality monitoring – Spot forms filled too quickly (possible data issues) or too slowly (training or complexity issues)
Workload analysis – Track CHN working hours, daily patterns, and field vs office time

Right now, we’re seeing many tasks not completed so these analysis would let us deep dive on the above metrics.

**Some alternatives** include
Using[ start and end ODK fields](https://docs.getodk.org/form-question-types/#hidden-questions) in each form , which are default ODK hidden fields that captures the timestamps.

title: feat(#10670): add ui-extensions service to webapp
body:
This PR introduces the `UiExtensionsService` to the webapp as part of the UI extensions feature.

The service is responsible for:
- Fetching UI extension properties from `/api/v1/ui-extension`
- Filtering extensions based on the current user's roles
- Lazy loading extension scripts from `/ui-extension/:id`
- Caching loaded extension scripts to avoid redundant network requests
- Exposing methods to retrieve extensions by type or ID

Unit tests are included covering:
- Initialization and single-load behaviour
- Role-based filtering logic
- Property lookup by type and ID
- Extension script loading, caching, and error handling

Closes #10670

title: Add purging summary to contacts
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Some deployments accumulate many reports per user over time, due to how their workflows are structured. To maintain acceptable client performance, the bulk of unimportant reports are purged, which deletes them permanently from the user's device. However there is no way maintain a summary of the patient history in a way. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Implement a call to a new configurable function, `purging-summary`. this function will receive context similar to the purging function and tasks and targets: a contact and all of the reports about this contact, but also which of these reports are purged. The function would return some json, which is computes a summary of relevant information about what is going to be purged. This json would be saved on the contact document as part of the purging action (skipping the update if the contents are not changed). 

So a contact would look like: 
```
{
  type: 'person',
  name: 'Jason',
  purging_summary: {
    past_assessments: 20,
    past_visits: 100,
    other_purged: 'historical_data'
  }
}
```

Some considerations: this would involve edits to contacts through purging, which would create more load on the server, and make purging take longer. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We thought about all sort of solutions, mostly revolving around somehow persisting the contact-summary - but that is a highly complex job.

title: Support collapsing contact-summary cards
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**

Contact-summary cards on the contact detail view are always fully expanded. In some cases (stock monitoring, immunizations, etc) the amount of details on the card means they take a lot of space on the screen.  To see content _below_ the card, users must do a lot of scrolling.  We want to allow users to collapse/expand cards by tapping the header.  Additionally, we can support a `collapsed` config property so cards can start collapsed.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

This is a _tentitive_ technical design.

Use a click handler on the existing header div and `*ngIf` to toggle field visibility. 

### 1 `webapp/src/ts/modules/contacts/contacts-content.component.html` (lines 46-67)

- Add `(click)="card.collapsed = !card.collapsed"`, `[attr.aria-expanded]="!card.collapsed"`, and `role="button"` to the `.action-header` div
- Add a chevron icon (`fa-chevron-right` when collapsed, `fa-chevron-down` when expanded) inside the header
- Wrap the `.row.flex.grid` div with `*ngIf="!card.collapsed"`

### 2. `webapp/src/css/inbox.less` (around the `.action-header` block at line 605)

Add styles scoped to `.compact-card .action-header` for collapsible behavior:
- `cursor: pointer` for interactive affordance
- Use flexbox (replacing float) to position h3 left and chevron right
- Subtle hover background color
- Chevron icon styling (size, color, margin)

Note: The existing `.action-header` uses `float: left` on h3 and `overflow: auto` for clearfix. The collapsible variant should use flexbox with `justify-content: space-between` instead, scoped only to `.compact-card` cards so other action-headers (tasks, reports, children) are unaffected.

### 3. `webapp/tests/karma/ts/modules/contacts/contacts-content.component.spec.ts`

Add unit tests tests for:
- Cards default to expanded when `collapsed` is undefined/false
- Cards with `collapsed: true` start with fields hidden
- Clicking header toggles field visibility
- `aria-expanded` reflects current state
- State resets when selected contact changes

### 4. `tests/e2e/default/contacts/contact-details.wdio-spec.js`

Update one of the contact summary card tests to validate current contact-summary cards are rendered "open" by default, but can be collapsed by tapping on the header.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

The current design I have provided here makes _all_ contact-summary cards "collapsible" (but only cards configured with `collapsed: true` are initially collapsed when the profile page loads).  Instead of allowing _any_ contact-summary card to be collapsed, we could make only certain cards collapsible (e.g. based on the card's config) while the other cards are not collapsible and just retain the default behavior.  From a code maintenance perspective, I think it is simpler to just make them all collapsible. So, as long as there is no concern about the UX, I would rather just keep it simple instead of needing logic to make some fixed and some collapsible....

Another thing we could also pursue in the future is making other sections on the contact profile page to also be collapsible.  If a user is on the profile page of a place and they want to see the "Reports", they first have to scroll past the contact-summary cards, People, and Tasks.  Each of these sections already has a header that theoretically could be updated to collapse the section just like we are doing for contact-summary cards....

**Additional context**

Originally discussed in a UI Extensions squad meeting.  @dianabarsan @binokaryg @eljhkrr feel free to add any additional details, corrections, or context.  👍

title: chore: bump node-forge from 1.3.1 to 1.4.0 in /webapp
body:
Bumps [node-forge](https://github.com/digitalbazaar/forge) from 1.3.1 to 1.4.0.
Changelog

Sourced from node-forge's changelog.

1.4.0 - 2026-03-24

Security

  • HIGH: Denial of Service in BigInteger.modInverse()
    • A Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability exists due to an infinite loop in the BigInteger.modInverse() function (inherited from the bundled jsbn library). When modInverse() is called with a zero value as input, the internal Extended Euclidean Algorithm enters an unreachable exit condition, causing the process to hang indefinitely and consume 100% CPU.
    • Reported by Kr0emer.
    • CVE ID: CVE-2026-33891
    • GHSA ID: GHSA-5gfm-wpxj-wjgq
  • HIGH: Signature forgery in RSA-PKCS due to ASN.1 extra field.
    • RSASSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepts forged signatures for low public exponent keys (e=3). Attackers can forge signatures by stuffing "garbage" bytes within the ASN.1 structure in order to construct a signature that passes verification, enabling Bleichenbacher style forgery. This issue is similar to CVE-2022-24771, but adds bytes in an addition field within the ASN.1 structure, rather than outside of it.
    • Additionally, forge does not validate that signatures include a minimum of 8 bytes of padding as defined by the specification, providing attackers additional space to construct Bleichenbacher forgeries.
    • Reported as part of a U.C. Berkeley security research project by:
      • Austin Chu, Sohee Kim, and Corban Villa.
    • CVE ID: CVE-2026-33894
    • GHSA ID: GHSA-ppp5-5v6c-4jwp
  • HIGH: Signature forgery in Ed25519 due to missing S < L check.
    • Ed25519 signature verification accepts forged non-canonical signatures where the scalar S is not reduced modulo the group order (S >= L). A valid signature and its S + L variant both verify in forge, while Node.js crypto.verify (OpenSSL-backed) rejects the S + L variant, as defined by the specification. This class of signature malleability has been exploited in practice to bypass authentication and authorization logic (see CVE-2026-25793, CVE-2022-35961). Applications relying on signature uniqueness (i.e., dedup by signature bytes, replay tracking, signed-object canonicalization checks) may be bypassed.
    • Reported as part of a U.C. Berkeley security research project by:
      • Austin Chu, Sohee Kim, and Corban Villa.
    • CVE ID: CVE-2026-33895
    • GHSA ID: GHSA-q67f-28xg-22rw
  • HIGH: basicConstraints bypass in certificate chain verification.
    • pki.verifyCertificateChain() does not enforce RFC 5280 basicConstraints requirements when an intermediate certificate lacks both the basicConstraints and keyUsage extensions. This allows any leaf certificate (without these extensions) to act as a CA and sign other certificates, which node-forge will accept as valid.
    • Reported by Doruk Tan Ozturk (@​peaktwilight) - doruk.ch
    • CVE ID: CVE-2026-33896
    • GHSA ID: GHSA-2328-f5f3-gj25

... (truncated)

title: feat(#10240): hide target counts past goal
body:
# Description ## Outdated goals **_This original approach has been superseded. See the Updated goals immediately below. For more context, please read the discussion._** 1. **Layout overlap**: When a count number is large, it overlapped with the "Goal X" label. Fixed by converting the `.count` block to a flex column layout so the goal label and count number stack vertically instead of colliding. 2. **Hide count past goal**: Adds a new permission `can_hide_target_count_past_goal`. When a user has this permission, the count number is hidden on any target where `pass >= goal`. The goal label remains visible. This behavior is off by default (empty roles array in the default config). ## Updated goals 1. Fix the layout overlap by centering the goal. 2. Add a field to the target object that allows people to specify that when the target is reached or exceeded, the UI is limited to showing the goal as the big number. For example if the target goal is 5000 and a user has reached a target count 10000, the UI for that target would show "Target 5000" in the small text at the top and "5000" in the larger text in the tile. 3. Any target data structure that does not have this field or does not have it set to true will default to the existing behavior -- the target count will be displayed even when it reaches or exceeds the goal. 4. No feature flag. Closes #10240 ## Companion PRs CHT-CONF: https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/pull/800 CHT-DOCS: https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/pull/2176 # Questions ## Layout overlap fix — approach feedback I fixed the overlap by replacing the absolute-positioned goal label with a stacked flex layout (`.count` becomes `display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center`, with the goal label above the count number, both centered). An alternative I considered was keeping the goal label in the top-right corner and adding right padding to `.number` when `.has-goal` is present (e.g., `.has-goal .count .number { padding-right: 80px; }`), which would be a smaller change but would offset the count number from true center. The padding approach would keep the count number visually off-center — it would be centered over the remaining space after reserving room for the goal label, not centered over the full card width. So on a wide card with a goal label, the big number would appear shifted left rather than truly centered. This approach is also fragile — it's a magic number that works for typical cases but can't guarantee no overlap for arbitrarily large numbers. Does the centered stacked layout work for you, or would you prefer the top-right approach?
Here is an example of the centering approach
Here is an example of the padding approach
## What to hide First off, if we center the goal, then do we need hiding? I've included it, but I want to raise the possibility that it might not be needed if we center the goal. I'm not sure what the use cases are, so I defer to you. In one of @dianabarsan's comments, she said we should be > adding a setting to not display the goal OR target count past the goal I chose to not display the target count because that was what I understood the suggestion to be. The example feature flag (`can_hide_target_count_past_goal`) mentioned in the issue points to that as the approach that was wanted, but it feels to me like having an empty target makes it look like the data is missing or the person has not met the goal. What is preferred? Hiding the target? Hiding the goal? Something else? Here are some screenshots with different options. I think Option 2 works best. I also wonder if maybe this isn't needed if we center both the goal and the target.
Option 1: Currently implemented -- hide only the target when goal is met or exceeded
Option 2: Hide only the goal when goal is met or exceeded
Option 3: Hide both the target and the goal when goal is met or exceeded
Option 4: Include a visual element showing the goal is met
# AI Disclosure I used Claude Code to help navigate the codebase, plan the approach, and write tests. I made all design decisions, reviewed all code, and verified the solution manually in the browser. I attributed Claude as a co-author on all commits that included the use of Claude Code. If you would like to see them, I can provide a copy of the directions I gave Claude Code when starting the planning. # Code review checklist - [x] UI/UX backwards compatible: Test it works for the new design (enabled by default). And test it works in the old design, enable `can_view_old_navigation` permission to see the old design. Test it has appropriate design for RTL languages. - [x] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the [style guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/style-guide/) - [x] Documented: Configuration and user documentation on [cht-docs](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/) - [x] Tested: Unit and/or e2e where appropriate - [x] Internationalised: All user facing text - [x] Backwards compatible: Works with existing data and configuration or includes a migration. Any breaking changes documented in the release notes. - [x] AI disclosure: Please disclose use of AI per [the guidelines](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/community/contributing/ai-guidelines/). ## Visual alignment fix for count widgets I adjusted the alignment of the target tiles to aligns the count number display across count widgets that have a goal and those that do not. Previously, the number position differed between the two variants, causing visual inconsistency when both types appeared on the same Targets tab. Fixed by adding a minimum height to the number container and using content justification to keep the number vertically centered regardless of whether a goal is present. ## Testing done ### Unit tests 14 unit tests cover the `AnalyticsTargetsComponent` in `webapp/tests/karma/ts/modules/analytics/analytics-targets.component.spec.ts`. The following cases are specifically tested for the `limit_count_to_goal` behavior: - `limit_count_to_goal: true`, `pass > goal` → displays `goal` as the count number - `limit_count_to_goal: true`, `pass === goal` (boundary case) → displays `goal` - `limit_count_to_goal: true`, `pass < goal` → displays actual `pass` value - `limit_count_to_goal` absent → displays actual `pass` value even when goal is exceeded - `limit_count_to_goal: true`, `goal: -1` (no goal) → displays actual `pass` value All 14 tests pass. ### Browser verification with dummy data A dummy target (`Earned Points`, `goal: 20000`) was temporarily added to the component to visually verify behavior in the browser under the following conditions: | Condition | `limit_count_to_goal` | `pass` | `goal` | Displayed | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Count exceeds goal, field set | `true` | 50,000 | 20,000 | 20,000 ✓ | | Count exceeds goal, field not set | absent | 50,000 | 20,000 | 50,000 ✓ | | Count below goal, field set | `true` | 19,999 | 20,000 | 19,999 ✓ | | Count equals goal (boundary), field set | `true` | 20,000 | 20,000 | 20,000 ✓ | #### Screenshots from testing
Screenshot: limit when target exceeds goal
Screenshot: no limit enforced when target exceeds goal
Screenshot: limit when target less than goal
Screenshot: limit when target equals goal
Screen recording: mobile-device-sized view https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/80d45dcc-d609-49e1-ac0b-53ad25e0aa37
### End-to-end verification with real config data The `active-pregnancies` target in `config/default/targets.js` was temporarily modified to `goal: 20, limit_count_to_goal: true` and uploaded to the running local instance using the local `cht-conf` build (which includes the companion schema and parse-targets changes). After logging in as a CHW user with 33 active pregnancies, the target card correctly displayed 20 (the goal) instead of 33 (the actual count), confirming the full data flow: `targets.js` → `cht-conf compile` → CouchDB → `rules-engine` → `target-state.js` → component → UI

title: perf(10749): move tasks_by_contact view to offline-only design document
body: # Description ### fixes: #10749 Every time the CouchDB server updated a document, it had to keep updating the tasks_by_contact index view on the server. Because tasks are high-volume (there are thousands of them), this indexing was slowing down the database server. I realised that the server doesn't need to index tasks by contact anymore because offline devices handle that on their local PouchDB databases instead. You moved the tasks_by_contact view configuration to the offline-only files so the server stops wasting resources indexing it. ### Problem: The tasks_by_contact view is a high-volume index that is only used by the rules engine on offline clients (mobile/web). When defined in the medic-client design document, the CouchDB server builds and stores this index, consuming significant disk space and processing power for zero benefit on the server. ### Solution: We moved the view definition into the client-side bootstrapper (webapp/src/js/bootstrapper/offline-ddocs). This ensures the view is only created on the client's PouchDB. ### Changes: Moved tasks_by_contact view from server ddocs to webapp/src/js/bootstrapper/offline-ddocs/medic-offline-tasks. Updated @medic/rules-engine to query the new _design/medic-offline-tasks location. Cleaned up the medic-client server-side design document by removing the redundant view. Updated @medic/memdown test harness to correctly load the new offline-only views for integration testing. ### Testing: **1. Rules Engine Integration Tests (220 Passing)** _______________ **2. Manual Bootstrapper Verification** # Code review checklist - [ ] UI/UX backwards compatible: Test it works for the new design (enabled by default). And test it works in the old design, enable `can_view_old_navigation` permission to see the old design. title: Forms display as narrow stripes after upgrade to 5.1 — duplicate nested col-sm-8 in right pane
body: **Description** After upgrading to CHT 5.1.0, forms (app forms and contact forms) render as narrow stripes occupying roughly 50% of the available width instead of filling the right pane. Inspecting the DOM reveals two nested `col-sm-8` Bootstrap grid column divs (see screenshot). This explains the issue, however I am not aware of a fix that we could do. It only occurs if CHT is displayed in tablet mode. If the screen is narrow enough, to qualify for the mobile experience, it works as expected. title: fix(#8974): correctly populate `end` field in forms
body:
# Description

The `end` meta field in CHT forms was always recording the same value as `start`, regardless of how long the user took to fill out the form.

Fixes #8974 

### Root Cause

In `prepareForSave`, CHT was firing: ```typescript $('form.or').trigger('beforesave'); ```

This had **two problems**:

**1. Wrong event name**
In enketo-core's `event.js`, the `BeforeSave` event is defined as:
```javascript
function BeforeSave() {
    return new CustomEvent('before-save', { bubbles: true });
}
```
CHT was firing `'beforesave'` — missing the hyphen, so the event 
name never matched.

**2. Wrong dispatch mechanism**
In enketo-core's `preload.js`, the `end` timestamp is updated inside
a native DOM listener:
```javascript
this.form.view.html.addEventListener(events.BeforeSave().type, () => {
    value = that.form.model.evaluate('now()', 'string');
    o.dataNode.setVal(value, 'datetime');
});
```
jQuery's `.trigger()` only fires jQuery-bound listeners and **never reaches native `addEventListener` listeners**. Since enketo-core 7.x (introduced in the Enketo Uplift in 4.0.0) dropped jQuery entirely, this callback was silently never executing — leaving `end` frozen at its preloaded value which matched `start`.

### Fix

Replaced the jQuery trigger with a native DOM dispatch on the correct
element in `enketo.service.ts`:
```typescript
// Before
$('form.or').trigger('beforesave');

// After
form.view.html.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('before-save', { bubbles: true }));
```

title: feat(#10695): adds interaction tracking service
body:
<!--

-->

# Description
 Closes #10695                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
  Adds an opt-in `InteractionTrackingService` that records user behavior on the tasks tab (list opens/scrolls/leaves, task opens/form submissions/completes/cancels, task-group navigation, task-filter usage) so analysts can study how CHWs work through their queues.                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
  **Service** (`webapp/src/ts/services/interaction-tracking.service.ts`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
  - Behind a new `can_track_task_interactions` permission; no-op for users without it.
  - Events are buffered in memory and persisted in batches to a per-day local PouchDB (`interaction-YYYY-M-D-{user}`). Buffer flushes on a 50-event threshold, on session end (navigating away from `/tasks`), and on the page-level `visibilitychange` listener wired in `app.component`.                                                                      
  - Per-day cap of 500 events; further events are dropped silently.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
  - On the next `init()` (typically next app load), any per-day DB that isn't "today" is aggregated into a single `type: 'interaction-log'` doc in the user's meta DB and the per-day DB is destroyed. The aggregate replicates to the server-side user-meta DB via the normal meta-DB sync.                                                                    
  - Aggregate `_id` is `interaction-{date}-{user}-{deviceId}`, so each (user, day, device) produces one doc — no day-spanning rows and no per-event rows in the meta store.                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
  **Tasks integration**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  - `tasks.component`, `tasks-content.component`, `tasks-group.component`, `tasks-sidebar-filter.component` all call into the service for their respective events.                                                                                                                                                                                              
  - `task_list:scroll` is throttled at 2 s.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
  **Tasks-group permission**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
  - Also adds `can_view_tasks_group` and gates the `/tasks/group` route on it. Bundled here because tracking the task-group flow only makes sense once that route is permission-controlled.                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
  **Tests**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  - New Karma unit spec for the service (~900 lines) covering init/permission/user-context handling, buffering thresholds, day rollover, the 500-event cap, aggregation of stale per-day DBs, ownership filtering across users, and error tolerance.                                                                                                            
  - New e2e spec (`tests/e2e/default/tasks/interaction-tracking.wdio-spec.js`) drives the full flow under a frozen "yesterday" clock so aggregation can be triggered within a single test. The clock is installed as a Date-only stub via `browser.addInitScript` (full fake-timers break zone.js scheduling); each test wipes server-side `task` docs and the  
  user's server meta DB before login so the rules engine regenerates tasks and `waitForAggregateDoc` doesn't pick up a prior run's aggregate.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  - Existing Karma specs for the tasks components updated to mock the new service.

I used Claude Code for developing and testing. I have made all design decisions and reviewed code for correctness, clarity and alignment with our standards.

# Description


### Fixes #10748


This PR removes the obsolete and resource-heavy docs_by_id_lineage map-reduce view from the medic-client design document and replaces the lineage-fetching logic with a more efficient two-step all_docs process.

The docs_by_id_lineage view was previously one of the largest views in the system, emitting every ancestor for every record. As identified in [Issue #10748](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10748), this can be replaced by direct document retrieval since the child document already contains the necessary ancestor chain.This PR removes the obsolete and resource-heavy docs_by_id_lineage map-reduce view from the medic-client design document and replaces the lineage-fetching logic with a more efficient two-step all_docs process.

The docs_by_id_lineage view was previously one of the largest views in the system, emitting every ancestor for every record. As identified in [Issue #10748](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10748), this can be replaced by direct document retrieval since the child document already contains the necessary ancestor chain.


### Changes


**Refactoring Fetch Logic**


shared-libs/lineage: Updated fetchLineageById in hydration.js to first fetch the child document via DB.get() and then retrieve all ancestors using their IDs in a single DB.allDocs() call.
shared-libs/cht-datasource: Updated getLineageDocsById in lineage.ts to implement the same two-step fetch strategy for local data contexts.
Ancestor Resolution: Maintained accurate lineage depth and order by ensuring that if an ancestor is missing, it is correctly represented as null in the resulting array.

**View Removal & Cleanup**
ddocs/medic-db: Deleted the docs_by_id_lineage view definition.
webapp/tests: Removed the now-obsolete docs_by_id_lineage.spec.js unit test.

### Test Updates


Updated mocks and unit tests in shared-libs/lineage, shared-libs/cht-datasource, admin, and webapp to match the new fetching pattern.
Updated API integration tests in server.spec.js to ensure the hydration endpoint remains fully functional without the view dependency.

title: Unable to hide individual fields inside a repeat from the report view
body: **Describe the bug** Unable to [hide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/translations/overview/#hiding-report-fields) individual form fields inside a [`repeat`](https://docs.getodk.org/form-logic/#repeating-questions) in the reports view. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Add a `repeat` to your app form 2. Add some fields (questions) inside the repeat 3. Add a column `instance::tag` and set it to `hidden` for some of the fields added in step 2 4. Convert and upload the app to CHT 5. Submit a report using that form 6. Check the report in the Reports tab 7. All fields inside `repeat` are visible **Expected behavior** The fields inside `repeat` which have been tagged as `hidden` should not be visible. **Screenshots** Here is a sample XLSForm repeat survey: repeat.properties.json: ```json { "title": [ { "locale": "en", "content": "Repeat" } ], "context": { "place": true, "person": true }, "icon": "icon-repeat", "hidden_fields": [ "hidden_props", "items.hidden_props" ] } ``` After I fill the form, I can still see the fields that should have been hidden: **Environment** - Instance: local - Browser: Chrome - Client platform: Windows - App: webapp - Version: tried on 5.x, but not specific to it **Additional context** CHT forum post: https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/how-do-i-hide-some-repeat-fields-on-a-report/5549

title: Replication get-ids can fail for extremely large users (over 150,000 documents)
body:
**Describe the bug**
If a user has more than 150,000 documents, `api/replication/get-ids` can fail with a 500 due to Array.push. 

Because 
```
[].push(...Array.from({ length: 130000 }).map(() => 2));
```

will throw 
```
Uncaught RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
```

Solution is never use spread push when dealing with large arrays. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Launch large CHT 5.x deployment
2. Create offline user at facility level with no replication depth
3. Try to sync
4. Sync errors after some time with a 500

**Expected behavior**
Maybe stopping a user with over 150,000 documents from replicating is good, but has to be intentional. 

**Logs**
```
2026-04-01T06:30:14.828 ERROR: Server error: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
    at getDocsByReplicationKeyNouveau (/service/api/src/services/authorization.js:640:10)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:105:5)
    at async Object.getContext (/service/api/src/services/replication.js:10:32)
    at async getDocIds (/service/api/src/controllers/replication.js:7:23) {
  [stack]: [Getter/Setter],
  [message]: 'Maximum call stack size exceeded'
} 
```

**Environment**
- App: api
- Version: 5.0.x, 5.1.x

**Additional context**

title: Implement failed user replication tracking
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Some time ago, in an effort to identify users with too many docs, we added the `replication-count` log (https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6251). However, this has a severe limitation where it requires the replication request to succeed in order to log anything. 
This means that the largest most broken users that can never log in are never captured, and these were the ones we were trying to detect and guard. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
This work should be expanded to also log _failed_ replications. We will not know the number of documents, but we might know _some_ data that can be useful for troubleshooting. 

**Additional context**
Seeing replication-count logs with 500.000 users, which means that at least one request succeeded.

title: fix(#10341): revoke permissions when user role is deleted from app_settings
body:
# Description

When a role is deleted via Admin > Roles & Permissions, it is removed from `app_settings.roles` but the references in `app_settings.permissions` remain. All three permission-checking codepaths only compared the user's assigned roles against the `permissions` object — they never verified whether those roles still existed in `app_settings.roles`. This meant users retained permissions from deleted roles indefinitely.

Fixes this by filtering a user's effective roles to only those still present in `app_settings.roles` before evaluating any permission. An empty or absent `roles` config falls back to no filtering (backwards compatible).

Three codepaths fixed:
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/auth.js` — used by the webapp frontend (contacts tab, sidebar, rules engine). Added `filterRolesByConfigured()` and an optional `chtRolesSettings` param to `hasPermissions()` and `hasAnyPermission()`.
- `shared-libs/user-management/src/roles.js` — used by user management logic (`can_skip_password_change`, `can_have_multiple_places`). `hasPermission()` now reads `config.get('roles')` and filters before checking `permissions`.
- `api/src/auth.js` — used by the API server (export, login, users controllers). 
Same filtering applied to the local `hasPermission()`.

`webapp/src/ts/services/cht-datasource.service.ts` updated to extract and forward `roles` from app settings alongside `permissions`.

Fixes #10341

title: Release 5.0.3
body:
# Planning - CHT Community 

- [x] Create an GH Milestone for the release and add this issue to it.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.
- [x] Ensure that all issues are labelled correctly, particularly ensure that "Regressions" are labelled with "Affects: <version>" labels. The "Affects" label is used in a link in the Known Issues section of the release notes of that version so it has to match exactly. To make sure the label is correct go to the [release notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) and ensure the issue is listed.

# Development - Release Manager

When development is ready to begin one of the maintainers should be nominated as a Release Manager. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR to the release branch. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version patch`.
- [x] Ensure that issues from merged commits are closed and mapped to a milestone.
- [x] Write an update in the #stewardship-team Slack channel summarising development and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The Release Manager is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Manager

Once all issues have been merged into `master` then the release process can start:

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by creating a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`) and then push it (e.g. `git push origin tag  <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`).
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully and images are built, notify the community by creating a post titled `<major>.<minor>.<patch> Beta Releases` in the [development](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/development/7) category of the CHT forum using this [template](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/new-topic?title=%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.%3Cpatch%3E%20Beta%20Releases&body=Hi%20Everyone%0AI%E2%80%99ve%20just%20created%20the%20%60%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.%3Cpatch%3E-beta.1%60%20tag.%0APlease%20let%20me%20know%20if%20there%E2%80%99s%20any%20final%20update%20we%20need%20to%20make.%0AIf%20all%20is%20good%2C%20then%20in%2024h%2C%20I%20will%20start%20the%20release.%20Thanks%21&category=development).
- [ ] Go to the [scalability action](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/workflows/scalability.yml) and on the top right, click into "Run workflow".  Under "Use workflow from" first choose "tags" then select the `<major>.<minor>.<minor>-beta.1` tag created above. Then "Run workflow". Once it passes, check for the scalability results [here](https://github.com/medic/scalability-results/tree/main/results). More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [ ] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [ ] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [ ] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labelled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
  - [ ] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [ ] Collect known migration steps, descriptions, screenshots, videos, data, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. This information should already be on the issue, but if not, prompt the change author to provide it.
  - [ ] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [ ] Ensure that the release notes PR is merged before moving to next step.
- [ ] Create a [new release](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases/new) in GitHub, with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, from the release branch created above as the target branch. Click on the "Choose a tag" dropdown and create a tag for the release with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. Add a link to the release notes page in the description of the release.
- [ ] Once you publish the release, confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [ ] Upgrade the [demo](https://demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org/) instance to the newly released version.
  - [ ] From the "App Management" admin console (`medic` user creds in 1Password), go to "Upgrades" and stage the upgrade for this version.
  - [ ] Clone `cht-core` repo and checkout the target tag (`git checkout <major>.<minor>.x` ) to ensure you have the proper version of the helm charts.
  - [ ] In your terminal, change to the `./cht-core/scripts/build/helm` directory.
  - [ ] Make sure you're using the dev EKS cluster: `kubectl config use-context arn:aws:eks:eu-west-2:720541322708:cluster/dev-cht-eks`
  - [ ] Ensure you have access to [EKS](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/hosting/medic/) and  to the [`demo-cht` namespace](https://github.com/medic/medic-infrastructure/issues/1344).) by calling this helm command. There should be no errors: `helm list -n demo-cht`
  - [ ] Download the current `values.yaml` data from the demo instance: `helm get values demo-cht --namespace demo-cht > values.yaml`
  - [ ] Edit the `values.yaml` file so `cht_image_tag` and `chtversion` properties have the new tag value `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`.
  - [ ] Use helm to upgrade the instance: `helm upgrade demo-cht . --namespace demo-cht -f values.yaml`
  - [ ] Refresh the "App Management" page and verify the instance upgraded. You may need to wait 5+ minutes until the upgrade succeeds.  Until then, you may see `50x` errors in the browser - be patient!
- [ ] Announce the release on the [CHT Forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/), under the "Announcements - Releases" category using this [template](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/new-topic?title=Announcing%20the%20release%20of%20%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.%3Cpatch%3E%20of%20the%20CHT%20Core%20Framework&body=%2AAnnouncing%20the%20release%20of%20%7B%7Bversion%7D%7D%20of%20%7B%7Bproduct%7D%7D%2A%0AThis%20release%20fixes%20%7B%7Bnumber%20of%20bugs%7D%7D.%20Read%20the%20%5Brelease%20notes%5D%28%7B%7Burl%7D%7D%29%20for%20full%20details.&category=releases).
- [ ] Go over the list of commits and individually notify contributing / interested community members about the release.
- [ ] Go to the [Issues tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues) and filter the issues with `is:issue label:"Affects: 4.x.x" ` , replace `4.x.x` with the previous version number. Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label.
- [ ] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.
