title: feat(#10650): support configuring max_age parameter for OIDC login
body:
<!--Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#10650 ): <subject>

Quick example:

feat(#1234): add hat wobble
^--^(#^--^): ^------------^
|     |      |
|     |      + - > subject
|     |
|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: build|feat|fix|perf|refactor|test|chore

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

This PR implements support for the OIDC `max_age` parameter to address issues with shared device scenarios where users may be automatically logged in as the previous user without being prompted for authentication.

## Changes Made

- Modified `api/src/services/sso-login.js`:
  - Updated `oidcServerSConfig()` to return both `idServerConfig` and `oidcProvider` settings
  - Added `max_age` parameter to authorization URL when configured in `oidc_provider` settings
  - Added `maxAge` validation to token verification to check the `auth_time` claim
  
- Added comprehensive test coverage in `api/tests/mocha/services/sso-login.spec.js`:
  - Test for `max_age` parameter in authorization URL (normal case)
  - Test for `max_age: 0` edge case in authorization URL
  - Test for `maxAge` validation in token verification (normal case)
  - Test for `maxAge: 0` edge case in token verification

## How It Works

When `max_age` is configured in the `oidc_provider` settings, the OIDC authorization flow will:
1. Include the `max_age` parameter in the authorization URL sent to the auth provider
2. The auth provider will check when the user last authenticated
3. If the time elapsed exceeds `max_age` seconds, the user will be prompted to re-authenticate
4. The returned ID token includes an `auth_time` claim which is validated against the configured `maxAge`

## Configuration

Add `max_age` (in seconds) to the `oidc_provider` configuration in the instance settings document:

```json
{
  "oidc_provider": {
    "discovery_url": "https://auth-provider.com/.well-known/openid-configuration",
    "client_id": "your-client-id",
    "max_age": 60
  }
}
```

Setting max_age: 0 is equivalent to prompt=login per the OIDC specification, forcing immediate re-authentication.

Fixes #10650

title: Message getting sent to pending state even after it is sent.
body:
A message is getting sent to pending state even after it is already sent to the same user. 

**Describe the bug**
Already sent messages are sent repeatedly (up to every 5 minutes, for up to 7 days) when a document has two scheduled_tasks with the same due date and one of them is stuck in scheduled state. This was seen in some of the instances randomly. Now, the issue has been occuring more frequently causing CHT to send up to 1900 SMS messages over period of 7 days. 

This means a single patient can receive the same SMS message up to ~2,016 times (7 days × 24 hours × 60 min / 5 min) in the worst case.

**Expected behavior**
Once the task is processed, it should no longer be sent to pending queue regardless of the state of other tasks. Process tasks in current window that are only in `scheduled` state. 

**Environment**
- Instance: All
- Browser: Any
- Client platform: Any
- App: webapp, sentinel
- Version: 4.22.0, 5.1.0, known to have existed on all 3.x versions as well

**Additional context*
I've posted detail on this in medic/config-lumbini/issues/221 (private repo).

title: chore: bump lodash from 4.17.23 to 4.18.1 in /admin
body:
Bumps [lodash](https://github.com/lodash/lodash) from 4.17.23 to 4.18.1.
Release notes

Sourced from lodash's releases.

4.18.1

Bugs

Fixes a ReferenceError issue in lodash lodash-es lodash-amd and lodash.template when using the template and fromPairs functions from the modular builds. See lodash/lodash#6167

These defects were related to how lodash distributions are built from the main branch using https://github.com/lodash-archive/lodash-cli. When internal dependencies change inside lodash functions, equivalent updates need to be made to a mapping in the lodash-cli. (hey, it was ahead of its time once upon a time!). We know this, but we missed it in the last release. It's the kind of thing that passes in CI, but fails bc the build is not the same thing you tested.

There is no diff on main for this, but you can see the diffs for each of the npm packages on their respective branches:

  • lodash: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm...4.18.1-npm
  • lodash-es: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-es...4.18.1-es
  • lodash-amd: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-amd...4.18.1-amd
  • lodash.templatehttps://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm-packages...4.18.1-npm-packages

4.18.0

v4.18.0

Full Changelog: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0

Security

_.unset / _.omit: Fixed prototype pollution via constructor/prototype path traversal (GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh, fe8d32e). Previously, array-wrapped path segments and primitive roots could bypass the existing guards, allowing deletion of properties from built-in prototypes. Now constructor and prototype are blocked unconditionally as non-terminal path keys, matching baseSet. Calls that previously returned true and deleted the property now return false and leave the target untouched.

_.template: Fixed code injection via imports keys (GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc, CVE-2026-4800, 879aaa9). Fixes an incomplete patch for CVE-2021-23337. The variable option was validated against reForbiddenIdentifierChars but importsKeys was left unguarded, allowing code injection via the same Function() constructor sink. imports keys containing forbidden identifier characters now throw "Invalid imports option passed into _.template".

Docs

  • Add security notice for _.template in threat model and API docs (#6099)
  • Document lower > upper behavior in _.random (#6115)
  • Fix quotes in _.compact jsdoc (#6090)

lodash.* modular packages

Diff

We have also regenerated and published a select number of the lodash.* modular packages.

These modular packages had fallen out of sync significantly from the minor/patch updates to lodash. Specifically, we have brought the following packages up to parity w/ the latest lodash release because they have had CVEs on them in the past:

  • lodash.orderby
  • lodash.tonumber
  • lodash.trim
  • lodash.trimend
  • lodash.sortedindexby
  • lodash.zipobjectdeep
  • lodash.unset
  • lodash.omit
  • lodash.template
Commits
  • cb0b9b9 release(patch): bump main to 4.18.1 (#6177)
  • 75535f5 chore: prune stale advisory refs (#6170)
  • 62e91bc docs: remove n_ Node.js < 6 REPL note from README (#6165)
  • 59be2de release(minor): bump to 4.18.0 (#6161)
  • af63457 fix: broken tests for _.template 879aaa9
  • 1073a76 fix: linting issues
  • 879aaa9 fix: validate imports keys in _.template
  • fe8d32e fix: block prototype pollution in baseUnset via constructor/prototype traversal
  • 18ba0a3 refactor(fromPairs): use baseAssignValue for consistent assignment (#6153)
  • b819080 ci: add dist sync validation workflow (#6137)
  • Additional commits viewable in compare view

title: Support calling extension-libs from form expressions
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
This comes out of a conversation with @ChinHairSaintClair at the UI Extensions squad meeting today!  The primary need is around having more complex logic in the [duplicate contact expressions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/forms/contact/#duplicate-check-expression).  The `duplicate_check.expression` property is just a JS expression that is evaluated to check if a contact is a duplicate. However, including complex logic in the expression gets challenging and difficult to maintain since it is just a single expression and does not really support being a proper function/script where you can declare variables, etc.  

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Thankfully, we already have a solution for creating arbitrary JS functions that can re-used across the app: [extension-libs](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/reference/extension-libs/)

I think we should add support for calling extension-libs from within the form expressions (so both `duplicate_check.expression` and `context.expression`.  This would allow for including more complex logic as a reusable function in an extension-lib, and then your form expression could simply call the function with the relevant parameters: `"expression": "extensionLib('dupcheck.js', existing, current)"`

**Additional context**
I think the implementation should be straight-forward.  We can add a new `extensionLib` method [to the XmlFormsContextUtilsService](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/b965953914d786826ed6160812cc7797d67ae4a9/webapp/src/ts/services/xml-forms-context-utils.service.ts).  That function can follow [similar logic](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/da5fe7f731303c6f69315b3992455125f539f91a/webapp/src/js/enketo/medic-xpath-extensions.js#L227) in our [extension-lib xPath feature](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/forms/app/#chtextension-lib) to get the extension-lib from the [CHTDatasourceService](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/622c625427f6b243fb20f8c95fc6442e2be591eb/webapp/src/ts/services/cht-datasource.service.ts) and then call the function with the provided parameters.  

@ChinHairSaintClair Please add any additional data/context! 🙏

title: feat(#10810): support calling extension-libs from form expressions
body:
# Description

Adds support for calling extension-libs from within form expressions (`duplicate_check.expression` and `context.expression`). This enables app developers to encapsulate complex logic (e.g. duplicate contact detection) in reusable extension-lib JS functions instead of maintaining it inline as a single expression string.

A new `extensionLib(libId, ...args)` method is added to `XmlFormsContextUtilsService`, following the same pattern used by the existing `cht:extension-lib` xPath function in `medic-xpath-extensions.js`. The method retrieves the extension-lib from `CHTDatasourceService` and invokes it with the provided arguments.

**Usage in duplicate check:**
```json
{
  "duplicate_check": {
    "expression": "extensionLib('dupcheck.js', existing, current)"
  }
}
```

title: fix: fail fast with helpful error when nginx container fails to start
body:
# Description

E2E setup runs `docker compose up -d` then polls `/api/info` via nginx on the host. If nginx cannot bind ports **80/443** (e.g. another service already listening), the nginx container may never run, but other services still start—so the old flow kept polling with **502** for a long time.

This change, after `docker compose up -d`, waits until the **nginx** container is **`running`**, or fails fast with a clear error if the container is missing, **exited**, or **dead**. Messages mention freeing **80/443** or setting **`NGINX_HTTP_PORT`** / **`NGINX_HTTPS_PORT`** (HTTPS tests already respect **`NGINX_HTTPS_PORT`** in `tests/constants.js`).

Closes #9491

title: test(#10492): stabilize flaky replace-user test by handling expected …
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

^--^(#^--^): ^------------^
|     |      |
|     |      + - > subject

|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: build|feat|fix|perf|refactor|test|chore

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

## Fixes #10492 

## Problem
The test creates new user for the first version of a contact to sync and conflicting replacements ignored was intermittently failing with done() called multiple times and a Document update conflict feedback document error.

This happened because when the original offline user syncs their version of the contact (with PENDING status), it creates a CouchDB conflict with the server's version (already updated to COMPLETE by otherUser). This conflict is intentional and expected — it's the core behavior this test verifies. However, the conflict caused the app to generate a feedback document with the message "Error selecting contact" / "Document update conflict", which made the test fail.

## Root Cause
The assertFeedbackDocs helper had two bugs:

"Document update conflict" and "Error selecting contact" were not in the ignore list, so they were treated as unexpected errors
Even when unexpected feedback docs were found, the function never threw an error — it silently passed, leaving stale feedback docs for subsequent test runs to detect

## Fix
Added "Document update conflict" and "Error selecting contact" to the feedbackDocsToIgnore list — these are expected side effects of the conflict scenario this test exercises
clearFeedbackDocs() is now always called (not just when there are no unknown messages) to prevent state leakage between tests
The function now correctly throws when truly unexpected feedback docs are found, making it an effective assertion rather than a silent no-op

title: fix(#10815): prevent helm crash on missing nested api/sentinel values
body:
# Description

This PR fixes a critical upgrade issue where older 5.1 `values.yaml` files lacking `sentinel:` or `api:` blocks cause a nil pointer crash during `helm upgrade`.

### Technical Implementation
* **Nil-Safe Access:** Replaced unsafe nested access patterns in the `sentinel` and `api` templates with the `(default (dict) .Values.block).key` pattern (matching existing conventions in `haproxy`). This safely falls back to default values without crashing if the parent block is missing.
* **Parity Fix:** Added the missing `| default "public.ecr.aws/medic"` fallback on the image line in `sentinel/deployment.yaml` to ensure parity with the API templates.
* **Regression Testing:** Added a `tests/backwards-compat.yaml` fixture mimicking a 5.1 values file and updated `validate-templates.sh` to reproduce the regression without `base.yaml`. All 13 tests now pass.

Fixes #10815

title: fix(#9834): make login page responsive to LTR <-> RTL switching

# Description

This PR introduces dynamic LTR <-> RTL layout switching to the login, password-reset, and token-login pages without requiring a page reload. 

**Implementation:**
* **Backend:** Updated `api/src/controllers/login.js` to extract the `rtl` flag directly from CouchDB translation documents and pass an encoded `rtlLocales` JSON array to the templates.
* **Frontend:** Added `getRtlLocales` and `setDirection` to `auth-utils.js`. The direction is now evaluated and injected into the `<html dir="...">` tag inside `baseTranslate` upon load and every locale switch.
* **Templates:** Added the `data-rtl-locales` attribute to `index.html`, `token-login.html`, and `password-reset.html`.
* **CSS:** Added `[dir="rtl"]` overrides in `style.css` to correctly flip the absolutely-positioned password visibility toggle icon.
* **Tests:** Added Mocha unit tests to verify the encoding behavior of `rtlLocales`.

body:
Bumps [hono](https://github.com/honojs/hono) from 4.12.9 to 4.12.12.
Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.12.12

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Middleware bypass via repeated slashes in serveStatic

Affects: Serve Static middleware. Fixes a path normalization inconsistency where repeated slashes (//) could bypass route-based middleware protections and allow access to protected static files. GHSA-wmmm-f939-6g9c

Path traversal in toSSG() allows writing files outside the output directory

Affects: toSSG() for Static Site Generation. Fixes a path traversal issue where crafted ssgParams values could write files outside the configured output directory. GHSA-xf4j-xp2r-rqqx

Incorrect IP matching in ipRestriction() for IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses

Affects: IP Restriction Middleware. Fixes improper handling of IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g. ::ffff:127.0.0.1) that could cause allow/deny rules to be bypassed. GHSA-xpcf-pg52-r92g

Missing validation of cookie name on write path in setCookie()

Affects: setCookie(), serialize(), and serializeSigned() from hono/cookie. Fixes missing validation of cookie names on the write path, preventing inconsistent handling between parsing and serialization. GHSA-26pp-8wgv-hjvm

Non-breaking space prefix bypass in cookie name handling in getCookie()

Affects: getCookie() from hono/cookie. Fixes a discrepancy in cookie name handling that could allow attacker-controlled cookies to override legitimate ones and bypass prefix protections. GHSA-r5rp-j6wh-rvv4

Users who use Serve Static, Static Site Generation, Cookie utilities, or IP restriction middleware are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.

# Description

### fixes: #10638 

This PR optimises the doc_by_type map-reduce view in the medic-client design document to reduce storage overhead and improve database performance.

**The Problem:** The doc_by_type view is currently one of the largest indexes in the database because it emits every single document. However, usage analysis shows that the application only uses this index for a few "metadata" types (form, translations, user-settings, etc.) and never for high-volume documents like Tasks or Reports.

**The Solution:** Updated the map function of the doc_by_type view to exclude the following heavy document types:

data_record (Reports)
task
contact
target
telemetry
The code was also refactored to use ES5-compatible syntax (var and indexOf) to ensure full compatibility with the CouchDB environment and to resolve IDE lint errors.

  • Deprecation: url.parse() usage has been replaced to address Node.js deprecation warnings. If you are on a recent version of Node.js, this resolves console warnings you may have been seeing. (#10625)

title: feat(#10559): add zizmor static analysis for GitHub Actions CI security
body:
# Description

Integrates [zizmor](https://docs.zizmor.sh/) — a GitHub Actions static analysis tool — into CHT Core CI, and remediates all findings it surfaces across our 9 existing workflows.

Closes #10559

### What zizmor found

Running `zizmor --offline .github/workflows/` against our repo surfaced:
- **45+ unpinned action references** (`@v4` tags instead of commit SHAs) — supply-chain risk if a third-party action's tag is silently moved to a malicious commit
- **7 of 9 workflows** with no explicit `permissions:` block, giving `GITHUB_TOKEN` broad write access by default
- **1 script injection vulnerability** in `release-notes.yml` — the free-text `workflow_dispatch` input `milestone` was interpolated directly in a `run:` shell command: `node index.js ${{ github.event.inputs.milestone }}`
- **1 over-privileged workflow** — `stale-prs.yml` had `actions: write` which is not needed for marking PRs stale
- **`@v6` typos** in `release-notes.yml` (v6 does not exist for `actions/checkout` or `actions/setup-node`)

### What this PR does

**New files:**
- `.github/workflows/zizmor.yml` — zizmor runs on every PR (offline to avoid rate limits), every push to `master`, and weekly on Sundays. Results upload to the GitHub Security tab as SARIF (Code Scanning).
- `.github/zizmor.yml` — suppression config. One finding is accepted rather than fixed(see suppression rationale below).

**Security fixes across all existing workflows:**
- `release-notes.yml` — fixed script injection: `milestone` input now goes through a quoted env var (`"$MILESTONE"`) instead of raw template interpolation in the shell command
- `stale-prs.yml` — removed `actions: write` (only `pull-requests: write` needed)
- All 9 workflows — added explicit `permissions:` blocks scoped to minimum required
- All 9 workflows — pinned every external action reference to a full 40-char commit SHA
  with the version tag preserved as a comment (e.g. `@abc123...  # v4`)

**Dependabot:**
- Added `github-actions` ecosystem to `dependabot.yml` — will open weekly PRs when
  pinned action versions are superseded, keeping SHAs current without manual effort

### Suppression rationale

`release-notes.yml` — `template-injection` on `skip_commit_checks` is suppressed in `.github/zizmor.yml` because:
- Input type is `choice`, constrained to `['', '--skip-commit-validation']` — no shell metacharacters possible in either value
- `workflow_dispatch` is only triggerable by org members with Actions write permission — not accessible to external actors
- The `milestone` input (free-text string) was **fixed**, not suppressed

# Code review checklist
- [ ] UI/UX backwards compatible — no UI changes
- [x] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the style guide
- [x] Documented: Configuration guidelines added to cht-docs (see parallel PR: medic/cht-docs#2185)
- [x] Tested: Validated locally (see test plan below)
- [ ] Internationalised — no user facing text
- [x] Backwards compatible: Existing workflows unchanged in behaviour; only permissions scoped and actions pinned
- [ ] AI disclosure: Please disclose use of AI per [the guidelines](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/community/contributing/ai-guidelines/).

# Test plan

### Verified locally (pre-merge)
- [x] Ran `zizmor --offline .github/workflows/` locally — all findings remediated or documented in `.github/zizmor.yml`
- [x] Validated YAML syntax for all 12 modified/new files — no parser errors
- [x] Confirmed all 19 unique action SHAs are exactly 40 hex characters — none truncated
- [x] Confirmed no unpinned external action references remain across any workflow file

title: chore(na): dependabot cooldown for main and adming apps
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

feat(#1234): add hat wobble
^--^(#^--^): ^------------^
|     |      |
|     |      + - > subject

|
+ -------------- > type: build|feat|fix|perf|refactor|test|chore

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

With recent supply chain attacks, [specifically on npm](https://socket.dev/blog/axios-npm-package-compromised),  we're trying to do a security in depth approach (see [pinning effort](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10837#issue-4241479122)).  Based off [my research](https://daniakash.com/posts/simplest-supply-chain-defense/), I think one defense is to add a [cooldown](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#cooldown-) to dependabot so that it doesn't suggest a PR to bump something released hours or even days ago that may have a vulnerability that hasn't been discovered yet.

This is obviously a balance as one of the other good defenses in depth is to always be up to date.  I think a 7 day cooldown period is a good trade off here.

Noteworthy is that this [doesn't prevent us](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#cooldown-) from getting security/CVE patches right away:

> The `cooldown` option is only available for version updates, not security updates.

title: fix(enketo): fix geopoint map rendering on first page of form
body:
# Description

When a geopoint widget with `appearance: maps` is on the first page of a form, it initializes while the loading spinner is displayed and the form is hidden. At that point `offsetWidth`/`offsetHeight` = 0, causing Leaflet to render the map greyed-out and off-center.

The existing `pageflip` handler only fixes the issue when navigating to subsequent pages. This fix adds a `ResizeObserver` to detect when the map container becomes visible and calls `invalidateSize()` once it has real dimensions. The observer disconnects immediately after to prevent memory leaks.

fixes #9268

# Code review checklist
- [x] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the style guide
- [x] Tested: Manual testing confirmed map renders correctly on page 1

title: Allow configuring phone number display format in outgoing SMS messages (strip country code)
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently, when SMS reminder messages (e.g., for ANC, Immunization, Nutrition) include a health facility's contact number, the number is displayed with the full international format including the country code prefix (e.g., +977XXXXXXXXXX). In Nepal, clients are accustomed to the standard 10-digit mobile number format and find the country code prefix confusing.

Example:
> "Dear [Client Name], your next ANC visit is due on [date]. Please visit [Health Facility]. For inquiries, contact +9779841XXXXXX."

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Provide a way to strip or format the default country code prefix from phone numbers when they are rendered in outgoing SMS message content. This could be a configurable function or template helper that removes the country code (as defined in app_settings) before inserting the phone number into the SMS body. For example, +9779841XXXXXX would be displayed as 9841XXXXXX in the SMS received by clients.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Storing facility contact number without the country code directly in the contact document at the time of the creation. However, this is not suitable for an ongoing project with a large number of contacts already added.

**Additional context**
We don't need to put the country code in the phone number field when creating a contact (using forms). It takes the default country code automatically.

Related:
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/3245

Thanks to @pawanshub for bringing this up to our attention.

title: Allow searching contacts by local phone number format without country code prefix
body: **What feature do you want to improve?** Currently, health workers cannot search for a client in the CHT app using the standard 10-digit mobile number (e.g., `9841XXXXXX`). They must include the `+977` country code prefix every time (e.g., `+9779841XXXXXX`), which is not how phone numbers are typically used or remembered locally. **Describe the improvement you'd like** Allow health workers to search for contacts using the local phone number format without the country code prefix. The search could automatically prepend the default country code defined in `app_settings`, or the matching logic could strip the country code from stored phone numbers before comparison. **Describe alternatives you've considered** A computed `unprefixed_phone` property could be stored on each contact document. However, for existing projects with a large number of contacts already registered, backfilling this property is not practical. **Additional context** We don't need to put the country code when entering a phone number in the forms. It takes the default country code automatically. Related: - #10846 Thanks to @pawanshub for bringing this up in our converstaion.

title: fix(#4692): use specific error codes instead of generic invalid_report

# Description

This PR replaces the generic `invalid_report` error code with more specific and meaningful error codes derived from the actual error.

Previously, all errors were assigned the same `invalid_report` code, making it difficult to analyze errors in analytics and debug issues.

title: Searching with Devanagari numerals no longer cross-matches Latin numeral contacts for online users (regression from 4.x)
body: **Describe the bug** In CHT 4.22.0, online users could search for contacts using either Latin numerals (e.g., `12345`) or Devanagari numerals (e.g., `१२३४५`) and both would return all matching contacts regardless of which numeral system was used in the contact name. For example, searching `12346` would return both "Person 12346" and "Person १२३४६". In CHT 5.1.1, this cross-matching no longer works for online users. Searching `12346` only returns "Person 12346", and searching `१२३४६` only returns "Person १२३४६". **To Reproduce** 1. Create two contacts: one named "Person 12346" (Latin numerals) and another named "Person १२३४६" (Devanagari numerals) 2. Log in as an online user 3. Go to the People tab 4. Search for `12346` 5. Observe that only "Person 12346" is returned 6. Search for 1१२३४६1 7. Observe that only "Person १२३४६" is returned **Expected behavior** Both searches should return both contacts, as was the behavior in 4.22.0 for online users. **Logs** **Screenshots** 4.22.0: --- 5.1.1: **Environment** - Instances: - Not working in [demo-cht](https://demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org/) (5.1.1) - Working in [gamma](https://gamma.dev.medicmobile.org/) (4.20.0) - Browser: Chrome - Client platform: - - App: webapp - Version: 5.x **Additional context** - This regression affects online users only. Offline users show the same behavior (no cross-matching) in both 4.22.0 and 5.1.1 but it would be great to support this for offline users as well. title: Allow custom headers in Sentinel outbound requests
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**  
We are running CHT Core 5.1.1 and integrating outbound data from Sentinel to a DHIS2 instance. The outbound requests are rejected because required HTTP headers are missing.  

Currently, Sentinel does not allow configuring custom HTTP headers. Only limited support for the `Authorization` header appears to exist, but other commonly required headers such as `x-api-key` or explicit `Content-Type` cannot be set.  

This makes it difficult or impossible to integrate with APIs like DHIS2 that require specific headers for authentication or request validation.

---

**Describe the solution you'd like**  
We would like Sentinel outbound requests to support configurable HTTP headers.  

This should allow defining:
- Custom headers (e.g. `x-api-key`)  
- Standard headers (e.g. `Content-Type: application/json`)  
- Flexible authentication mechanisms beyond the `Authorization` header  

Ideally, headers could be defined in the outbound configuration and applied to all outgoing requests.

---

**Describe alternatives you've considered**  
As a workaround, we considered introducing a reverse or forward proxy to intercept outbound requests and inject the required headers.  

However, this adds:
- Additional infrastructure complexity  
- Operational overhead  
- Extra points of failure  

A native solution within CHT Core would be preferable.

---

**Additional context**  
This limitation seems related to previous work on outbound headers (see https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9799), which introduced support for `Authorization` headers. However, full support for arbitrary/custom headers (e.g. `x-api-key`) is missing.  

Relevant source code:
- `shared-libs/outbound/src/outbound.js`  
- `shared-libs/couch-request/src/couch-request.js`  

Use case: Integration with DHIS2 requiring custom headers for authentication and request handling.

title: fix(#9993): resolve IDB race condition in telemetry service
body:
## Description

Fixes a race condition in the telemetry service that caused an `InvalidStateError: Failed to read the 'result' property from 'IDBRequest'`crash, which triggered unwanted feedback doc generation during e2e tests.

Fixes #9993

## Problem

When `submitIfNeeded()` called `db.destroy()` on old telemetry DBs, pending IDB requests were not fully settled before the current DB was opened. This caused an unhandled `InvalidStateError` promise rejection.

## Changes

- Added `await db.close()` before `await db.destroy()` in  `submitIfNeeded()` to flush all pending IDB requests first
- Fixed variable shadowing bug (`const db` → `let db`) so the catch block can correctly call `closeDataBase(db)` on failure
- Added 100ms delay after `submitIfNeeded()` before opening the current DB to let any lingering IDB transactions fully settle
- Added graceful `InvalidStateError` handling in `storeIt()` to prevent unhandled promise rejections from reaching the feedback doc system
- Updated unit tests to reflect new `close` + `destroy` ordering

title: feat(#6571): add security log scanner for credentials and errors in CI
body:
# Description

Adds a post-test credential scanner that runs automatically after every E2E and integration test job in CI, failing the build if credentials are detected in server logs.

Fixes #6571

## What was added

**`scripts/ci/.secretlintrc.json`** — Declarative config for [`secretlint`](https://github.com/secretlint/secretlint) that detects credential leaks in `*.log` files using two rule sets:

- `@secretlint/secretlint-rule-preset-recommend` — the standard secretlint preset
- `@secretlint/secretlint-rule-pattern` — custom patterns for CHT-specific cases:
  - `user:pass@host` URLs in any scheme, including `localhost` (the preset's basicauth rule requires a domain with a dot, so it would miss `localhost:5984`)
  - Credentials in URI query parameters (`?password=secret&token=abc&pass=abc`)
  - JSON key/value pairs (`"password":"..."`, `"pass":"..."`, `"token":"..."`, `"secret":"..."`)
  - `Authorization:` headers accidentally written to logs

Safe patterns (`Bearer ***`, `[REDACTED]`, `***`) are excluded via negative lookaheads in the config.

**`webapp/tests/mocha/unit/testingtests/secretlintrc.spec.js`** — 18 mocha/chai test cases that verify the secretlint config flags known-bad log lines and does not flag safe patterns.

**`.github/workflows/build.yml`** — One step added (`if: always()`) to both test jobs, positioned after the test run and before `Archive Results`:

- **Scan logs for credential leaks** — runs `secretlint` against `tests/logs/*.log`

## What was removed

- `scripts/ci/log-scanner.js` — replaced by secretlint
- `scripts/ci/log-scanner-allowlist.json` — patterns moved into the secretlint config

## Stress test results

| # | Scenario | Input | Expected | Result |
|---|----------|-------|----------|--------|
| 1 | Credential leak — URL | `https://admin:password123@localhost:5984` | exit 1, violation flagged | ✓ |
| 2 | Credential leak — JSON secret | `{"secret":"super-secret-token"}` | exit 1, violation flagged | ✓ |
| 3 | Credential leak — pass param | `GET /api?pass=hunter2` | exit 1, violation flagged | ✓ |
| 4 | Safe pattern — already redacted | `{"password":"[REDACTED]"}` | exit 0, no violation | ✓ |
| 5 | Safe pattern — Bearer masked | `Authorization: Bearer ***` | exit 0, no violation | ✓ |
| 6 | Safe pattern — URL without credentials | `GET http://localhost:5984/medic` | exit 0, no violation | ✓ |

title: feat(#10855): add custom outbound headers and proxy support
Don't run database compaction on every version upgrade
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currenlty, when users upgrade from one version to another, database compaction is run regardless of if there are any database changes or not or the fragementation value. For larger instances, this adds unnecessary load for the work that may not improve anything impactful.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Check if database comapction is required to run or not. Run it only when it is required. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Leave as it is. 

**Additional context**
Recently one large instance was upgraded to 5.1.0 and that ran index creation and database compactionf or few hours. After couple of weeks, we needed to apply 5.1.1 for quick fixes and since 5.1.1 does not have any index or view changes and this is running database compaction for 1 hour already. In scenarios like this where there is no database changes and database compaction is not necessary, we should not trigger database compaction.

title: fix(#10851): normalize Latin and Devanagari digits in Nouveau freetext queries
body:
# Description
This PR fixes a regression in online contact freetext search where equivalent Latin and Devanagari numerals no longer cross-matched.

In CHT 5.1.1, the Nouveau freetext query path searches only the exact numeral script entered by the user (for example, 12346 only matched Latin digits, and १२३४६ only matched Devanagari digits). This change restores cross-script matching by expanding freetext terms to both numeral systems at query generation time.

**Technical Implementation**
- Numeral Variant Expansion:  Updated Nouveau freetext query generation in `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/libs/nouveau.ts` to generate Latin and Devanagari numeral variants for each freetext input and combine them with OR.
- Keyed + Fuzzy Coverage:  Applied the same variant expansion for both keyed freetext queries (exact_match:"key:value") and fuzzy freetext queries (term*), preserving existing non-numeric behavior.
- Mixed Numeral Handling:  Variant generation supports mixed-script inputs (for example 1२3४) and deduplicates equivalent query variants before building the final query.

**Regression Testing**

Added unit test coverage in `shared-libs/cht-datasource/test/local/libs/nouveau.spec.ts` for:
- Cross-script matching:
  - Latin input (eg 12346) includes Devanagari variant
  - Devanagari input (eg १२३४६) includes Latin variant
- Edge numeric forms:
  - leading zeros (0123, ०१२३)
  - long numeric strings (9999999999)
  - mixed-script numerals (1२3४, १2३4, 12३४)
- Special characters with numerals
  - (123), 123-456, 123.456, +9876348

Fixes #10851

## Description

Adds a new `local_phone` Mustache template helper to `message-utils` that strips the country code prefix from phone numbers in outgoing SMS messages.

This allows SMS message authors to render phone numbers in local format without modifying stored contact data.

Closes #10846

### Usage example
Before: `+9779841234567`  
After:  `9841234567`

Template syntax:
Contact {{#local_phone}}{{facility_phone}}{{/local_phone}} for help.

The helper reads `default_country_code` from `app_settings`. If the phone number starts with `+{country_code}`, the prefix is stripped. Otherwise the number is returned unchanged. Existing templates without this helper are completely unaffected.

AI Disclosure: I used Claude to understand the codebase structure and explore possible approaches for implementing the Mustache helper. The final implementation, testing, and refinements were done by me, and I verified the behavior with SMS workflows to ensure correctness and backward compatibility.

title: fix(#10847): allow contact search by local phone number format
body:
## Description

Closes #10847

Currently, contacts can only be found by searching their full international phone number (e.g. `+9779841234567`). Users who type the local format (e.g. `9841234567`) get no results, even though the number refers to the same contact.

This PR fixes that by normalizing local phone number search terms into their international equivalent and generating an additional search request alongside the original. Both the local and normalized forms are searched, so contacts are found regardless of which format the user types.

### Changes
- `shared-libs/search/src/generate-search-requests.js` - when a search term looks like a phone number and does not start with `+`, normalizes it using `default_country_code` from `app_settings` and adds a second search request for the normalized form
- `shared-libs/search/test/generate-search-requests.js` -added 7 unit tests covering local format, international format, missing settings, invalid input, and type-filtered searches
- `webapp/src/ts/services/search.service.ts` - passes `settings` (including `default_country_code`) into the search filters so the search lib can use it

### Example
User searches: `9841234567`
Search now queries both: `9841234567` and `9779841234567`
Contact stored with `+9779841234567` is found 

Existing searches using `+9779841234567` are completely unaffected 

AI Disclosure: I used Claude to understand the codebase structure and explore possible approaches for implementing the local phone number normalization in search. The final implementation, testing, and refinements were done by me, and I verified the behavior with contact search workflows to ensure correctness and backward compatibility.

title: Migrate small Angular templates from structural directives to built-in control flow
body:
## Description Angular 17+ introduced [built-in control flow](https://angular.dev/guide/templates/control-flow) (`@if`, `@for`, `@switch`) as a replacement for the older structural directives (`*ngIf`, `*ngFor`, `*ngSwitch`). The new syntax is cleaner, doesn't require importing `NgIf`/`NgFor`/`NgSwitch` from `@angular/common`, and avoids the need for `` blocks for `else` cases. CHT-Core uses Angular 20 and currently has **61 template files** still using `*ngIf` and **30 files** still using `*ngFor`. Only one file (`about.component.html`) has been partially migrated so far. This issue covers migrating the **smallest and simplest** templates as a starting point. ## Scope Migrate the following small template files from structural directives to built-in control flow syntax: | File | Lines | Directives to migrate | |------|-------|-----------------------| | `webapp/src/ts/components/snackbar/snackbar.component.html` | 6 | 1 `*ngIf` | | `webapp/src/ts/components/panel-header/panel-header.component.html` | 6 | 1 `*ngIf` | | `webapp/src/ts/components/report-image/report-image.component.html` | 12 | 2 `*ngIf` | | `webapp/src/ts/modules/messages/messages-more-menu.component.html` | 12 | 1 `*ngIf` | | `webapp/src/ts/modals/feedback/feedback.component.html` | 17 | 1 `*ngIf` | | `webapp/src/ts/modals/check-date/check-date.component.html` | 19 | 1 `*ngIf` | ## Good first issue This is a great first issue because the changes are mechanical, well-scoped, and don't require domain knowledge of the CHT application. ### Steps 1. **Understand the transformation.** The basic pattern is: **Before** (`*ngIf`): ```html
Hello
Welcome
Please log in
 ``` **After** (`@if`): ```html @if (isVisible) {
Hello
} @if (isLoggedIn) {
Welcome
} @else {
Please log in
} ``` Similarly for `*ngFor` → `@for` (if encountered): ```html
  • {{item}}
    • @for (item of items; track item) {
  • {{item}}
    • } ``` 2. **See a real example.** Look at the changes in [PR #10880](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10880) which migrates `about.component.html` from `*ngIf`/`*ngSwitch` to `@if`/`@switch`. 3. **For each template file**, replace the structural directives with the new control flow syntax. 4. **Update the component's `imports` array.** After migration, if `NgIf`, `NgFor`, or `NgSwitch` are no longer used anywhere in the template, remove them from the component's `imports` array in the corresponding `.ts` file. For example, if `snackbar.component.html` no longer uses `*ngIf`, remove `NgIf` from the `imports` in `snackbar.component.ts`. 5. **Run the unit tests** to make sure nothing is broken: ```bash cd webapp && npx ng test -- --grep "SnackbarComponent\|PanelHeaderComponent\|ReportImageComponent\|MessagesMoreMenuComponent\|FeedbackComponent\|CheckDateComponent" ``` 6. **Run the app locally** and verify the affected components render correctly. Check both the happy path (element visible) and edge case (element hidden). ### Edge cases to watch for - If a `*ngIf` has an `else` clause (e.g., `*ngIf="condition; else elseBlock"`), make sure to convert the `` into an `@else` block and remove the now-unused ``. - If the directive uses `as` syntax (e.g., `*ngIf="obs$ | async as obs"`), convert to `@if (obs$ | async; as obs)`. - Some components may import `NgIf` but also use it in parts of the template you're not changing. Only remove the import if it's completely unused. ## References - [Angular Built-in Control Flow](https://angular.dev/guide/templates/control-flow) - [Angular Control Flow Migration Guide](https://angular.dev/reference/migrations/control-flow) - [First Time Contributors Guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/community/contributing/first-time-contributors/) - [Development Workflow](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/) - [Coding Style Guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/style-guide/) 💬 **Need Help?** Feel free to comment below with questions about setup, implementation, or anything else. We're happy to guide you through it!

title: Replace `any` types with proper interfaces in small service files
body:
## Description

Several small service files in the webapp use `any` where proper TypeScript types exist. Replacing these with correct types improves type safety and makes the code easier to follow.

## Scope

The following files need `any` replaced with proper types:

### 1. `webapp/src/ts/services/update-password.service.ts` (31 lines)

Line 23 declares `headers: any`. This can use `HttpHeaders` from `@angular/common/http` instead.

```ts
// Before
const headers: any = {
  "Content-Type": "application/json",
  Accept: "application/json",
  Authorization: "Basic " + window.btoa(username + ":" + currentPassword)
};

// After
const headers = new HttpHeaders({
  "Content-Type": "application/json",
  Accept: "application/json",
  Authorization: "Basic " + window.btoa(username + ":" + currentPassword)
});
```

### 2. `webapp/src/ts/services/user-login.service.ts` (41 lines)

Line 25 has the same `headers: any` pattern. Same fix as above.

### 3. `webapp/src/ts/services/cache.service.ts` (74 lines)

Lines 9-14 define the `caches` array with `any` in three places:

```ts
private caches: {
  docs: any;
  pending: boolean;
  invalidate: any;
  callbacks: any[];
}[] = [];
```

Also, `register(options)` on line 42 has an untyped parameter.

Create an interface for the cache entry and one for the options parameter. Look at how `register` is called across the codebase to determine what `docs`, `invalidate`, and `callbacks` should be typed as.

### 4. `webapp/src/ts/services/extract-lineage.service.ts` (44 lines)

Line 11 has an untyped `contact` parameter and line 16 uses `any` on the result object:

```ts
extract(contact) {
  const result: any = { _id: contact._id };
```

Define a minimal type for the contact parameter (needs `_id` and optional `parent`) and the return type.

## Existing pattern to follow

`webapp/src/ts/services/session.service.ts` already imports and uses `HttpHeaders`:

```ts
import { HttpClient, HttpHeaders } from "@angular/common/http";
// ...
httpOptions = { headers: new HttpHeaders({ Accept: "application/json" }) };
```

Follow this pattern for the header fixes.

## Steps

1. Pick one or more of the files listed above.
2. Replace `any` with the correct type. For headers, use `HttpHeaders`. For the others, define small interfaces in the same file or use existing types from the codebase.
3. Make sure the code still compiles:
   ```bash
   cd webapp && npx ng build
   ```
4. Run the relevant unit tests:
   ```bash
   cd webapp && npx ng test -- --grep "UpdatePasswordService\|UserLoginService\|CacheService\|ExtractLineageService"
   ```
5. Check that no existing functionality is broken.

title: refactor(#10883): replace any types in small service files
body:
## Summary

Per #10883, replace `any` types in four small webapp service files with proper TypeScript types. Follows the `HttpHeaders` pattern already used in `session.service.ts`.

## Changes

- **`update-password.service.ts`** and **`user-login.service.ts`**: swap the plain-object `headers: any` cast for `HttpHeaders` from `@angular/common/http`.
- **`cache.service.ts`**: model the cache entry and `register` options with explicit interfaces and generics:
  - `CacheRegisterOptions<T, C>` types `options.get` as `(done: CacheCallback<T>) => void` and `options.invalidate` as `(change: C) => boolean | undefined`.
  - `CacheEntry<T, C>` types `docs`, `pending`, `invalidate`, `callbacks`.
  - `CacheCallback<T>` types both subscriber callbacks and the `options.get` completion.
  - The `caches` field still holds the type-erased `CacheEntry` so `register` can be called with different `T` / `C` from multiple consumers without extra plumbing. Renamed the inner `callback` loop variable to `cb` so it doesn't shadow the outer closure's `callback` parameter.
- **`extract-lineage.service.ts`**: introduce a minimal `ContactLineage` interface (`_id?`, `parent?: ContactLineage`). The walk-up uses a local `next` binding so the chain keeps compiling under `strictNullChecks` (`minified.parent` is typed as `ContactLineage | undefined` otherwise).

## Test plan

- No behavior change; these services are still used exactly the same way from the call sites.
- Under `strictNullChecks` (on for the webapp), the updated files typecheck locally.

Fixes #10883

title: Automate helm deploy of Demo instance during release process
body:
**Describe the issue**
When releasing a new version of cht-core, there is [a series of manual steps](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/ca8e32d5dbd9a521ac382edce3de5abe668ea406/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/z_release_major.md?plain=1#L50) the release engineer must perform to upgrade the demo instance. Besides just being more manual effort, these steps also require that the engineer has a working local environment setup for running things like `kubectl` and `helm` (things not _normally_ required for CHT development).  Also, the engineer has to have the proper access level for the `demo-cht` namespace on EKS (something unlikely to be granted to non-Medic engineers).     

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Unless I am missing something, we _should_ be able to automate all of this via a new GitHub workflow that we can manually trigger against a specified tag.  (Another option would be to do it as a new job in the build workflow that is triggered _for  [when `upgrade` completes](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/0a62a6ad80177e0bd56b30f3ba1eb0594efc2d43/.github/workflows/build.yml#L435)`. The main challenge I see with that is we don't want to upgrade the demo instance _for all tags_, since that could cause downgrades when we publish new patches for older releases, etc.  We can always add more automation in the future, but for now it seems easiest to just make this a manual process (similar to the [release notes](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/workflows/release-notes.yml) and we can upgrade the demo instance on-demand.))

To be clear, I think the new GitHub workflow could do the following:

- Use the [`/api/v2/upgrade/stage` endpoint](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/reference/api/#/Upgrade/v2UpgradeStagePost) to stage the upgrade. We will need some kind of polling logic to wait for the staging to finish. Alternatively, we could use the [chtoolbox](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/reference/api/#/Upgrade/v2UpgradeStagePost) `upgrade --stage --follow` command which will call that endpoint and then wait for the upgrade to complete.
- With the tag version of cht-core checked out, go to the `./cht-core/scripts/build/helm` directory.
- Configure kubectl to use the `arn:aws:eks:eu-west-2:720541322708:cluster/dev-cht-eks` context.
- Download the current `values.yaml` data from the demo instance: `helm get values demo-cht --namespace demo-cht > values.yaml`
- Edit the `values.yaml` file so `cht_image_tag` and `chtversion` properties have the new tag value `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`.
- Use helm to upgrade the instance: `helm upgrade demo-cht . --namespace demo-cht -f values.yaml`
- Poll the [/api/v2/monitoring endpoint](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/reference/api/#/Monitoring/v2MonitoringGet) until `version.app` returns the expected value.
- Use cht-conf to upload the configuration from the `cht-core/config/demo` folder to the `demo-cht.dev` server.

As long as we have the proper GitHub secrets setup, I think all of these should be pretty simple to script.

title: fix: skip unnecessary database compaction on minor patch upgrades
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

feat(#1234): add hat wobble
^--^(#^--^): ^------------^

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

###  Description

### Fixes Issue #10862

Previously, deployment upgrades unconditionally triggered heavy database compactions (db.compact() and db.viewCleanup()). This caused unnecessary disk I/O load and delays, especially during minor patch updates. This PR optimises the process by skipping compaction unless design documents were altered or database fragmentation is critically high.


### Changes Made:
**api/src/services/setup/utils.js:** unstageStagedDdocs() now returns a list of modified databases. cleanup() uses this list to skip compaction on unchanged databases, triggering compaction only if db.info() yields a fragmentation ratio > 1.2.

**api/src/services/setup/upgrade-steps.js:** Restructured finalise () to pipeline the output string array from the unstageStagedDdocs utility natively into the cleanup() request parameter.

### Mocha Testing:
Updated upgrade-steps.spec.js and utils.spec.js to cover the new conditional compaction logic and ensure background errors are caught safely.
**Verification**
Ran completely green under all API setup integration layers, confirming the database.nouveauCleanup() continues completely uncontested, and unit limits reliably block heavy DB tasks when fragmentation is low.
Covered by 25+ successful tests inside the Mocha test suite.

title: Implement GHA concurrency
body:
**Describe the issue**
We (the org) has access to only a limited number of GitHub actions workers. With many changes getting pushed at the same time, frequently in quick succession over the same branch, new changes might be queued for a long time to have access to workers.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
GHA offers the option enabling maximum `concurrency`: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#concurrency

Config looks something like this: 
```
concurrency:

title: feat: p2p wifi hotspot sync - server apis and webapp integration
body:
# Summary

Adds P2P WiFi Hotspot sync capability to CHT, enabling CHWs in offline areas to push health data to a Supervisor's phone over a local WiFi connection. The Supervisor relays data to the msain server on next online sync.

This PR covers the server-side APIs and webapp integration. The related Android PR is at medic/cht-android#431.

## What's included

**Server API endpoints** (`api/src/p2p/`):
- `POST /api/v1/p2p/authorize` : Issues JWT token with ECDSA P-256 for offline device authentication
- `GET /api/v1/p2p/config/:facility_id` : Returns P2P configuration for a facility
- `GET /api/v1/p2p/revocation-list` : Returns revoked devices/users
- `POST /api/v1/p2p/telemetry` : Receives session telemetry (fire-and-forget)

**Webapp P2P module** (`webapp/src/ts/modules/p2p/`):
- Status page with host/peer controls, QR code display, sync progress
- History page showing past sync sessions
- Config service reads `p2p_sync` from app_settings
- Transit filter service hides relayed docs from UI (contacts, reports, search, tasks, targets)
- Transit purge service soft-deletes relayed docs after server delivery confirmed

**Key design decisions:**
- Roles are fully config-driven via `host_roles` and `peer_roles` in app_settings : no hardcoded role names
- Transit docs use soft-delete (`_deleted: true` + `purged: true`) with replication filter, not `db.remove()` which would create destructive tombstones
- Documents written with `new_edits: false` for automatic CouchDB deduplication
- Supports both new sidebar nav and old header nav
- 86 built-in translation keys

**Eg. of configuration:**
```json
{
  "p2p_sync": {
    "enabled": true,
    "host_roles": ["supervisor"],
    "peer_roles": ["chw"]
  }
}
```

## Files changed
- 6 new API endpoint files + routing
- 6 new Angular components/services
- 3 new P2P services (config, transit filter, transit purge)
- 86 translation keys
- Append-only modifications to: routing.js, sidebar-menu, header, contacts, reports, search, rules-engine, target-aggregates, db-sync, old-nav.less
- 5 test spec files

## Test plan
- [ ] P2P menu visible for users with configured host/peer roles
- [ ] P2P menu works in both old nav (dropdown) and new nav (sidebar)
- [ ] Authorize endpoint returns JWT for users with matching roles
- [ ] Config endpoint returns p2p_sync settings
- [ ] Transit docs filtered from contacts, reports, search, tasks, targets
- [ ] Purge triggers after successful server sync
- [ ] Unit tests pass: `npx mocha api/tests/p2p/**/*.spec.js`

# Description

### Fixes: #10872

This PR resolves the flakiness in the `auditing api db should only store 10 history entries` integration test. 

## Problem
The test was using a static 200ms delay (`utils.delayPromise(200)`) to wait for asynchronous audit records to be written to the database. In slow CI environments, 26 rapid document updates often took longer than 200ms to process, leading to intermittent `AssertionError: expected 5 to equal 7` failures.

## Solution
- **Enhanced Utilities**: Introduced a new polling helper `waitForAuditCount(docId, expectedCount)` in `tests/utils/index.js`. This utility sums the history length across all audit documents for a specific ID and retries until the expected count is reached (or timeout).
- **Update Test Logic**: Replaced the fragile `delayPromise` in `tests/integration/api/audit.spec.js` with the new polling logic. This ensures the test waits exactly as long as needed for the backend to finish processing.

-->

# Description

### Fixes #10878
This PR fixes a `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'doc')` in the Contacts Detail page that occurs when a user navigates between pages very quickly.

## Problem
The crash was caused by a race condition: when a user switches pages quickly, the Redux store clears the `selectedContact` (setting it to `null`). However, asynchronous callbacks or pending emissions from `XmlFormsService` and other background tasks were still executing and attempting to access properties like `.doc` on the now-null contact.

## Changes
- **Defensive Null Checks**: Added optional chaining (`?.`) throughout the `ContactsContentComponent` when accessing `selectedContact`.
- **Early Returns**: Implemented early returns at the beginning of `updateFastActions()` and within the subscription callbacks for `xmlFormsService`. If the component state has been cleared by navigation, these methods now exit gracefully instead of attempting to access null properties.

title: Add push failures counts to monitoring API
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Right now if a deployment has an integration with something like [RapidPro](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/messaging/gateways/rapidpro/), there might be push errors in the sentinel log.  However, there's no easy way to know how often or when these errors started without doing deep analysis in the logs.  For some deployments, like in Kubernetes, logs may be purged faster than they can be reviewed so the meta error analysis is impossible

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
[Like we have](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/hosting/monitoring/dashboards/#details) for outbound push or sentinel backlog, we should add an end point to `/api/v2/monitoring` that includes "push errors".  This should be exposed in such a way that they can be graphed over time to show an increase or decrease.  This might be "count of push errors in the past 5 min" or something.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
check the logs, ignore them and hope they fix themselves

**Additional context**
A large deployment had hundreds of thousands of errors in their sentinel logs.  This was so much that it **was causing a backlog in the sentinel queue** and it couldn't keep up to to process things like muting and other day to day sentinel tasks.  If there was an easy way to have a watchdog alert fire, that would have been very helpful.  See [internal Slack thread](https://medic.slack.com/archives/CHYAGKHN2/p1776090865934499?thread_ts=1775596121.899809&cid=CHYAGKHN2) as well as [this gist](https://gist.github.com/dianabarsan/09eb59224b9486f6c3819535fea6466e) with counts

from that gist here's some example errors in the sentinel log, which are endemic to the deployment, but give an idea of what we're looking for:

* 353,348 instances of  `Failed to push <UUID> to u5_assessment_caregiver: Credentials for 'rapidpro' have not been configure...`
* 100,381 instances of   `Failed to push <UUID> to caregiver_bounce_sms: Credentials for 'rapidpro' have not been configured. ...`
* 50,227 instances of   `Failed to push <UUID> to referrals: Error: 500 - "Request failed with status code 404"`

# Description
Adds a new `workflow_dispatch` workflow (`deploy-demo.yml`) that automates the manual demo instance upgrade during the release process. Instead of requiring a release engineer to have local `kubectl`/`helm` setup and EKS access, they can now just trigger this workflow from the Actions tab with a release tag.

title: Support order weight for header_tabs in webapp
body:
Blocked by https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10672 and https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10901

Currently the ordering of the header tabs ("Messages", "Reports", "People", etc) is fixed and non-configurable. For the new UI Extensions we are going to be adding more custom tabs.  Deployments want to be able to control the order that the tabs are displayed (which also should control which tab the user initially lands on).  This has been [repeatedly requested on the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/is-there-a-way-of-changing-the-order-of-the-tabs-of-cht/2093).  We should support the ability to configure a custom order "weight" that works both for default tabs and for `app_main_tab` UI Extensions.

Currently we have the [`header_tabs`](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/reference/app-settings/header_tabs/) config object that allows for setting custom icons for the header tabs. We should enhance the webapp to support reading a `weight` property from the `header_tabs` entries (and from the UI Extension properties being supported in https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10672).  Entries with a lower `weight` should be ordered first.  The default `weight` for the default header tabs should be:

- messages: `1`
- tasks: `2`
- reports: `3`
- contacts: `4`
- analytics: `5`

Any custom UI Extension entries should have a default weight of `6`.  Any entries with the same weight value should be ordered alphabetically.  

---

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10672 is updating `webapp/src/ts/services/header-tabs.service.ts` to return entries for the custom UI Extensions. This issue should order the returned array according to the `weight` property both from the `header_tabs` config as well as the UI Extension properties.  

We should also update the ordering of the sidebar tags in `webapp/src/ts/components/sidebar-menu/sidebar-menu.component.ts` based on this same `weight`.

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10901 is adding the UI Extensions to the legacy header menu.  We should update that functionality to also order the entries based on `weight`.

This PR adds support for dynamic navigation tabs in the CHT header using UI extensions of type app_main_tab. It also introduces a weight-based sorting system to allow developers to control the order of both system and custom tabs.

**HeaderTabsService:** Injected UiExtensionsService to fetch extensions of type app_main_tab. These are now merged with the standard system tabs (Messages, Tasks, Reports, etc.) in getAuthorizedTabs().

System tabs are assigned default weights (0, 10, 20, 30, 40).
UI extensions default to a weight of 0 but can be customised in the extension configuration.
The header now sorts all authorised tabs numerically by weight.

2. Bug Fixes & Refactoring
**State Mutation Fix:** Resolved a pre-existing bug in HeaderTabsService.get() where calling the method with settings would permanently modify the internal tabs array.
**Type Safety:** Updated UiExtensionProperties in UiExtensionsService to include the weight property and implemented explicit type casting for better TypeScript support.

3. Test Improvements
**HeaderTabsService Spec:** Added comprehensive test cases for dynamic merging and weight-based sorting.

title: feat(10908): add weight-based sorting for header tabs
body:
# Description

This PR implements a **configurable, weight-based ordering system** for header tabs, replacing the existing fixed ordering.

It allows deployments to control the order of tabs (and therefore the default landing tab) while ensuring consistent ordering across the **header**, **sidebar**, and **legacy navigation menu**.

---

### Key Changes
- Added support for an optional `weight` property in:
  - `header_tabs` configuration
  - UI Extension tab definitions
- Implemented centralized sorting logic in `HeaderTabsService`
- Updated components to consume the same sorted tab list:
  - Header (`header.component.ts/html`)
  - Sidebar (`sidebar-menu.component.ts`)
  - Legacy header dropdown menu
- Ensured backward compatibility when `weight` is not defined

---

### Sorting Logic

**Default weights:**
- messages → 1  
- tasks → 2  
- reports → 3  
- contacts → 4  
- analytics → 5  
- custom tabs → 6 (default)

**Ordering rules:**
1. Sort by `weight` (ascending)  
2. For equal weights, sort alphabetically by label  

---

### Result
- Enables flexible tab ordering for deployments  
- Provides consistent navigation across all UI areas  
- Supports extensibility for UI Extensions  

---

Closes #10908

title: Authorization context drops duplicate replication-key matches because `Set.add()` only adds one id
body:
<!--
**Important**: This is a public repository. Anyone in the world can see what's posted here. If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the bug**

While going through `api/src/services/authorization.js` I noticed when `findContactsByReplicationKeys()` resolves a replication key to multiple document IDs, only the first matching ID is added to `docIds`. The code uses `docIds.add(...keys)`, but Set.add() accepts a single argument, so additional IDs are ignored.

**To Reproduce**
<!--
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Go to '...'
2. Click on '....'
3. Scroll down to '....'
4. See error
-->
1. Stub `medic-client/contacts_by_reference` to return two or more rows for the same replication key.
2. Call `getScopedAuthorizationContext()` with a doc whose `docsByReplicationKey.key ` contains that replication key.
3. Inspect the `db.medic.allDocs()` call.
4. Observe that only the first matching document ID is included.

**Expected behavior**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen. -->
All matching document IDs for a replication key should be included in the set, so the authorization context reflects every match.

**Actual behaviour**

Only the first matching ID is kept, and the rest are dropped silently.

title: Add prefix when creating custom element name
body:
Currently when we [define a custom element](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/c8238ec5f1acb1ccad18fd966f2e7ffbaf7061c1/webapp/src/ts/modules/ui-extensions/ui-extensions-tab.component.ts#L42) in the page for a UI Extension, we are just using the UI Extension's `id` value as the name of the custom element. This has the unfortunate consequence of meaning that all the [requirements for a custom element name](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#valid-custom-element-name) are forced upon the UI Extension.  The `id` for the UI Extension is just the file name of the js/properties files in the `ui-extensions` config directory.  Since we use this `id` as the custom element name, it means that the file name for the UI Extension js/properties files must be a valid custom element name.

The biggest annoyances are the name must:

- Start with a lowercase ASCII letter (a-z)
- Contain at least one hyphen (-)

Instead of leaking this requirement from custom elements all the way down to the file names of the UI Extensions config, we should update [the webapp code](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/c8238ec5f1acb1ccad18fd966f2e7ffbaf7061c1/webapp/src/ts/modules/ui-extensions/ui-extensions-tab.component.ts#L42) so that we just prepend the `cht-` prefix to the UI Extension name when creating the custom element.

```ts
const extensionId = this.route.snapshot.params['id'];
const elementName = `cht-${extensionId}`;
```

---

The other half of this issue is that we should then relax the [validation logic in cht-conf](https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/blob/badcc659e2e33f9eab98dca664e4a9b4830299db/src/lib/upload-ui-extensions.js#L20) to not have specific requirements about the first character and to not require a hyphen.  

---

Both PRs should target the `10224-ui-extensions` in their respective repositories.

body:
## Description

Fixes #8226
Fixes https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/4543

When a `field-list` group has the `hidden` appearance (or all its contentsare hidden), Enketo still renders an empty page for that group. This isproblematic when using the `db-object-widget` to load contact data into a hidden top-level group.

title: feat(#10903): sub contact attachment routing
body:
# Description

 Every file uploaded in an Enketo form was attached to the **main** doc, regardless of which sub-document it was uploaded in. A photo added inside a CHW (sibling) section of a CHW Area creation form landed on the CHW Area doc; a file inside a `db-doc="true"` group or
  repeat landed on the report doc instead of the sub-report.

  This PR routes each upload and inline binary to the document that owns it, in **both** save pipelines:

  **Contact forms (#10903)**
  - Resolves the owner of each `[type=file]` / `[type=binary]` node by its form section: main section → primary doc, `<contact>`/`<parent>` section → the matching sibling doc, i-th `<repeat>` `<child>` → the i-th repeat doc. Unmatched uploads fall back to the main doc.
  - Filename sanitization and orphaned-attachment cleanup now run per-doc instead of main-doc-only.
  - Attachment size validation now runs on the contact save path (previously reports only).

  **Report forms (#10904)**
  - Routes uploads and inline binaries to their nearest `db-doc="true"` sub-document, falling back to the main report.
  - Writes each media field's value into `doc.fields` (repeat-index aware for the main doc), so the field value always resolves its attachment as `user-file-` + value.

  **Shared pipeline**
  Both services now delegate to a new `AttachmentRoutingService` (upload routing → inline-binary routing → per-doc finalize), parameterized by a small per-pipeline strategy (owner resolution, reference container, field path). Pure DOM primitives live in
  `attachment-routing.provider.ts`.

  ## Attachment naming & backwards compatibility

  - Inline-binary attachments on **newly saved** docs are named `user-file-<owner-relative-xpath>` (e.g. `user-file-photo`, `user-file-group/photo`, `user-file-my_repeat[2]/photo`) instead of the legacy `user-file/<form-id>/<xpath>`, and the field value now stores the bare
  reference. File-widget uploads keep the `user-file-<filename>` scheme.
  - **Existing docs are not migrated.** Legacy slash-named attachments are left intact on edit (covered by tests), and orphan cleanup only considers `user-file-`-prefixed names it can account for.
  - On edit, an untouched inline-binary field is preserved via a `data-attachment-ref` sidecar attribute stashed at load time; a fresh upload always wins over a stale sidecar. A dedicated spec pins the enketo-core merge behavior this relies on.
- Testing
  - Unit: routing primitives, shared pipeline, contact and report strategies, translation-service binary handling (sidecar stash/restore, no value bind-back).
  - E2E: sub-contact routing on create and edit, `db-doc` sub-report routing (including repeats and multiple sub-docs), untouched inline-binary preservation on report edit.
  - Closes #10903
  - Closes #10904
  - Closes #10791

title: draw.scss: Make drawing widget controls RTL-aware
body:
Description:
The Enketo drawing/signature/annotation widget in CHT uses hard-coded left positioning in draw.scss, which breaks layout in RTL languages (Arabic, Urdu, Hebrew).

Several instances (including file picker, file input, and hide-canvas button) are anchored using physical properties like left, causing controls to appear on the wrong side in RTL mode.

Fix:
Replaced physical positioning with CSS logical properties to support bidirectional layouts:

left: 0 → inset-inline-start: 0
left: 80px → inset-inline-start: 80px
left: 90px → inset-inline-start: 90px

Also updated one additional instance without an existing RTL TODO.

Impact:
Correct control alignment in RTL languages
No visual change in LTR
Scoped to webapp/src/css/enketo/draw.scss only

Why this version works better
Removes repetition (no need to list every code block)
Keeps problem → fix → impact structure
Signals low risk clearly (important for maintainers)
Keeps enough detail for reviewers to validate quickly

title: fix(#10913): limit freetext generator results to skip+limit to preven…
body:
Fixes #10913

When an online user searched contacts via select2, the freetext generator was calling `getUuidsByTypeFreetext` / `getUuidsByFreetext` which exhausted all matching results in 10,000-record batches before `getPageRows` sliced to the requested page size (e.g. 20). This caused repeated server requests and could crash the server with large datasets.

The fix makes `iterateGenerator` in `freetext-query.js` accept a `limit` parameter and break out of the generator loop early. `search.js` passes `options.skip + options.limit` as that limit, so only enough IDs to cover the current page are fetched.

title: Icon-only menu buttons have hardcoded English aria-label text
body:
**Describe the issue**

Some icon-only menu buttons in the webapp use hardcoded English `aria-label` values. Since these labels are primarily exposed to assistive technologies, screen reader users in translated deployments hear English labels even when the rest of the UI is localized.

**Affected files:**

- `webapp/src/ts/modules/reports/reports-more-menu.component.html` — `aria-label="Actions menu"`
- `webapp/src/ts/modules/messages/messages-more-menu.component.html` — `aria-label="Actions menu"`

- `webapp/src/ts/components/tool-bar/tool-bar.component.html` — `aria-label="Application menu"`

**Expected behavior**

Accessible labels should be translated using the existing translation pipeline so that screen reader users in non-English deployments hear localized labels.

**Actual behavior**

The labels are hardcoded in English.

**Suggested fix**

Add translation keys (`actions.menu`, `application.menu`) and bind them in the templates using `[attr.aria-label]="'key' | translate"`.

**Describe the bug**

The storage pressure progress bar has two problems:

1. The `aria-label` uses plain string syntax instead of Angular property binding, so screen readers read the literal expression text `'Used storage: ' + storageUsagePercentage.toFixed(2) + '%'` instead of the actual value.

title: fix(#10871): stabilize records.spec.js by skipping --tail=20 historical lines in waitForLogs
body:
# Description

Fixes the intermittent failure in `Import Records > JSON > parses and stores the passed JSON` (#10871).

**Root cause:** `waitForLogs` spawns `docker logs --tail=20 --timestamps` so the process starts outputting immediately (resolving the internal `ready` promise quickly). However, the same `data` handler that resolves `ready` also attempted regex matches against those 20 historical lines. If a previous settings change had logged `"Settings updated"` within the 50 ms `startTime` buffer, the watcher resolved `watcher.promise` immediately — before `updateCustomSettings` was even called. The `before()` hook returned with the `TEST` form not yet loaded into the API's in-memory config, causing the first test to fail with `Form not found: TEST`.

**Fix:** Skip regex matching entirely on the first data batch (which contains all the `--tail=20` historical lines). `startTime` is also moved into the first-batch handler so it is set after historical lines arrive, guaranteeing they all pre-date `startTime`. Subsequent batches contain only new log output and are matched normally.

Relates to: medic/cht-core#10871

title: feat(#9339): update phone widget to display formatted number in proxy input
body:
# Description

Closes #9339

Currently, when a user enters a phone number in the phone widget, the number gets normalized/formatted before being saved to the form's model (hidden input). However, the visible input field (proxy input) still shows the raw value the user originally typed. This can be confusing because what the user sees doesn't match what actually gets saved.

This change updates the `formatAndCopy` function to also set the proxy input's value to the formatted number after the change event fires. Now the user sees exactly what gets stored in the model.

**What changed:**
- In `formatAndCopy()`, after copying the formatted value to the hidden real input, we now also update the visible proxy input to display the same formatted value
- If the phone number is invalid (normalization returns `false`), the proxy input keeps the original value so the validation error still makes sense

**Example:**
- User types: `+1 (650) 222-3333`
- Before this change: proxy still shows `+1 (650) 222-3333`, model stores `+16502223333`
- After this change: proxy updates to `+16502223333`, model stores `+16502223333`

title: Fix RTL layout issues in Enketo drawing/signature widget
body:
####  Problem

The Enketo drawing/signature/annotation widget used hard-coded physical positioning (`left`) in `draw.scss`, which caused layout issues in RTL languages such as Arabic, Urdu, and Hebrew.

Several UI elements (file picker, file input, hide-canvas button) were incorrectly aligned because they relied on `left` instead of direction-aware properties.

#### Solution

Replaced physical CSS positioning with logical properties to ensure proper support for bidirectional layouts:

*  left: 0 → inset-inline-start: 0
*  left: 80px → inset-inline-start: 80px
*  left: 90px → inset-inline-start: 90px

Also updated an additional instance that did not previously include an RTL TODO.

#### Impact

* Fixes control alignment issues in RTL languages
* No visual changes in LTR layouts
* Change is scoped to `webapp/src/css/enketo/draw.scss` only
