# Description

### Fixes: #9860

This PR implements a server-check during the CHT API startup sequence to verify that the system is running against a compatible CHT-customized version of CouchDB.

## Problem:
Currently, the CHT API starts silently even when connected to a standard "vanilla" CouchDB image. Standard images lack specific CHT optimisations and configurations (such as session handling and cluster settings), which leads to:
- Users being randomly logged out due to incorrect session timeouts.
- Potential data corruption or loss in multi-node clusters.


## Changes:

**CouchDB Fingerprinting:** Added a custom [cht] configuration section to the official CHT CouchDB image (10-docker-default.ini).

**API Verification:** Added a new check (checkCouchDbFlavor) in the server-checks library. This check attempts to read the CHT fingerprint from CouchDB at startup.

**Fail-fast:** If the fingerprint is missing, the API will fail to start and provide a clear error message directing the user to the official hosting documentation.


 ## Testing:

Added unit tests in shared-libs/server-checks/test/checks.js to verify:
- Success: API starts correctly when fingerprint is present.
- Failure: API refuses to start when fingerprint is missing (e.g., standard CouchDB).

title: Admin Languages: Missing translations warning is shown incorrectly due to interpolated ng-show
body:
**Describe the bug**
In the Admin Languages screen, the warning banner for missing translations uses interpolated `ng-show` instead of a boolean AngularJS expression.

**Affected Files**
`admin/src/templates/display_languages.html:60`
Current pattern:
- `ng-show="{{localeModel.missing > 0}}"`

Because interpolation turns the expression result into the string `"true"` or `"false"`, AngularJS does not treat it as the intended boolean condition. This can cause the **"Missing translations"** warning to remain visible even when `localeModel.missing` is `0`.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Open **Admin > Languages**.
2. Load or create a language where `localeModel.missing` is `0`.
3. Expand that language panel.
4. Observe that the **Missing translations** warning may still be displayed.

**Expected behavior**
The warning should only be visible when a language actually has missing translations. 

**Actual behavior**
The warning can remain visible even when there are no missing translations.

**Additional context**
`ng-show` should receive an AngularJS expression directly, not an interpolated string.

title: updateMessageTaskStates crashes when allDocs returns rows without doc
body:
updateMessageTaskStates crashes when allDocs returns rows without doc

Describe the Bug

api/src/services/messaging.js assumes every row returned from db.medic.allDocs({ include_docs: true }) contains a doc. That assumption is not always true — CouchDB/PouchDB can omit doc for not_found, deleted, or race-condition rows.

When that happens, updateMessageTaskStates passes undefined entries into task lookup logic and throws a runtime exception:

TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'tasks')

Affected code:

  • api/src/services/messaging.js
    • updateMessageTaskStates (~line 281+)
    • getTaskForMessage (~line 29)
    • getTaskAndDocForMessage (~line 34)

Inside updateMessageTaskStates, rows are mapped without filtering missing docs:

const docs = results.rows.map(r => r.doc);
const stateChangesByDocId = applyTaskStateChangesToDocs(taskStateChanges, docs);

If any row has no doc, the call chain below crashes because doc is undefined:

applyTaskStateChangesToDocs(...)
  → getTaskAndDocForMessage(...)
    → getTaskForMessage(messageId, doc)
      → getTaskFromMessage(doc.tasks, uuid)  // ❌ crashes here

The function already handles partial failures for bulkDocs but does not defend against missing docs before task traversal.

To Reproduce

  1. Stub db.medic.query('medic-sms/messages_by_uuid', ...) to return rows with IDs.
  2. Stub db.medic.allDocs(...) to return one row with doc and one row without doc.
  3. Call updateMessageTaskStates(...).
  4. Observe crash before retry logic or graceful completion.

Expected Behavior

  • Rows missing doc should be silently skipped.
  • State changes referencing unknown/missing docs should be logged and dropped.
  • The function should still update all valid docs in the same batch and return a stable { saved: n } response.

Actual Behavior

A missing doc triggers an unhandled exception in task lookup, crashing the entire update operation.

Logs

TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'tasks')
    at getTaskFromMessage (api/src/services/messaging.js)
    at getTaskForMessage (api/src/services/messaging.js)
    at getTaskAndDocForMessage (api/src/services/messaging.js)
    at applyTaskStateChangesToDocs (api/src/services/messaging.js)
    at updateMessageTaskStates (api/src/services/messaging.js)

Screenshots

N/A

Environment

Field | Value -- | -- Instance | N/A (reproduced at unit test level) Browser | N/A Client platform | N/A App | api Version | N/A

Additional Context

allDocs with { keys, include_docs: true } does not guarantee a doc for every key — keys can be stale or deleted between queries. This is a known CouchDB/PouchDB behaviour, not an edge case.

Proposed Fix (~55–70 lines across service + tests)

  1. Sanitize rows before processing in updateMessageTaskStates:

    const docs = results.rows.map(r => r.doc).filter(Boolean);

  2. Add a defensive guard in getTaskAndDocForMessage to skip falsy docs early.

  3. Add logging for dropped state changes when no doc is available.

  4. Add unit tests in api/tests/mocha/services/messaging.spec.js:

    • Should skip missing docs without throwing.
    • Should still update valid docs in the same batch.
    • Should return the correct saved count.

Acceptance Criteria

  • [ ] No crash when allDocs includes rows without doc.
  • [ ] Existing successful update path is unchanged.
  • [ ] New tests pass and prove robustness for partial allDocs results.

title: fix(#10209): harden xsltproc against XML external entity attacks
body:
# Description

CHT api forwards admin-uploaded XForm XML to `xsltproc` via stdin to render the form HTML and the XForm model (`api/src/services/generate-xform.js`). `xsltproc` was invoked without any restrictions on external resource resolution, so an admin who could upload a form was able to embed an XXE payload that exfiltrated arbitrary files from the api container into the resulting form HTML. See [OWASP XXE](https://owasp.org/www-community/vulnerabilities/XML_External_Entity_(XXE)_Processing) / CWE-611.

The repository's own threat assessment in #10209 is that this is a defence-in-depth fix because the only attacker who reaches this code path is already an admin with the `medic` password and access to the (open-source) container contents. That said, removing the primitive entirely closes the door on chained attacks and any future code path that runs the same xsltproc invocation against less-privileged input.

## Approach

Two complementary defences in `api/src/services/generate-xform.js`:

1. **Reject XForms that declare a DOCTYPE or external entity.** CHT XForms have no legitimate reason to declare either construct, so a strict allowlist of safe input shapes is the cheapest and most reliable fix. The check strips XML comments first so that benign comments mentioning the literal text `<!DOCTYPE` / `<!ENTITY` are not flagged.

2. **Pass `--nonet` to xsltproc.** This causes libxml2 to refuse to resolve any external resource (DTDs, entities, stylesheets) over the network, providing defence in depth in case any future code path manages to slip a DTD past the input check.

The validation runs before `childProcess.spawn`, so tainted input never reaches xsltproc.

## Verification

`npm run unit-api` for the affected suite (`api/tests/mocha/services/generate-xform.spec.js`):

- Existing 46 tests still pass unchanged.
- 4 new tests cover the new behaviour:
  - `--nonet` is the first argument passed to every xsltproc spawn.
  - XForms with `<!DOCTYPE>` are rejected with a clear error message and `xsltproc` is never spawned.
  - XForms with `<!ENTITY>` are rejected with the same error.
  - XForms whose comments mention the literal text `<!DOCTYPE` / `<!ENTITY` are still accepted (no false positives on benign content).

`npm run lint` is clean for both modified files.

Fixes #10209

# Code review checklist
<!-- UI/UX, internationalisation are not affected by this server-side hardening. -->
- [x] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the [style guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/style-guide/)
- [x] Tested: New unit tests cover the rejection paths, the `--nonet` flag wiring, and the comment false-positive case
- [x] Backwards compatible: Real CHT XForms do not declare a DOCTYPE or external entities, so existing forms continue to render without change. New forms that legitimately need xsltproc keep working with `--nonet` in place.

title: fix(#10705): stop consuming rate limit on 429 responses
body:
# Description

The api rate-limit middleware tracks failed login attempts by client IP, basic-auth username, basic-auth password, and the body `user`/`password` fields, allowing 10 failures per key per 10 second window. Until now the finish handler also called `rateLimitService.consume` whenever a response went out with status code 429.

That double-counted the rate limiter's own response. When several clients share a single key (most importantly a single `req.ip`, because a reverse proxy is not forwarding the real client address), one badly behaved client can exhaust that shared key, after which every other caller gets 429 from the controller. Each of those 429 responses then re-consumed the victim's other keys (their valid username, their valid password), which could lock those credentials out instance-wide even though they had never sent a failing request. The reporter observed exactly this affecting `couch2pg` and other basic-auth integrations on production.

Limiting the finish handler to only authentication failures (401) keeps the protective behaviour against real brute-force attempts while letting unrelated callers recover as soon as the existing 10 second window elapses. The middleware still rejects requests upfront with 429 when the caller's keys are already over the limit; this PR only changes whether *that* rejection should re-punish the caller.

## Verification

`npm run unit-api` for the affected suite (`api/tests/mocha/middleware/rate-limiter.spec.js`):

- The pre-existing `consumes on 401` and `does nothing if not limited` cases still pass.
- The previous `consumes on 429` test, which asserted the buggy behaviour, has been replaced with `does not consume on 429 (#10705)` that asserts no consume call happens.
- New `does not consume on non-401 status codes` test guards the implicit contract that 200/4xx-other-than-401/5xx responses also do not trigger consumption.

`npm run lint` is clean for both modified files.

Fixes #10705

# Code review checklist
<!-- UI/UX, internationalisation, and documentation are not affected. -->
- [x] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the [style guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/style-guide/)
- [x] Tested: Unit tests cover the previous and new behaviour
- [x] Backwards compatible: The middleware still issues 429 for callers already over the limit and still consumes on real 401s; only the redundant double-consume on the rate limiter's own 429 has been removed.

title: Duplicate CLI command handling and lack of validation in build scripts
body:
### Description

The command dispatch logic in `scripts/build/cli.js` and `scripts/build/ddoc-compile.js` is duplicated and relies on direct access to `process.argv[2]` without proper validation.

This results in inconsistent and unclear behavior when invalid or missing commands are provided.

---

### Actual Behavior

* When no command is provided:

  * The script attempts to access `process.argv[2]` and may fail unpredictably depending on execution flow
  * No clear usage or guidance is shown

* When an unknown command is passed:

  ```bash
  node scripts/build/cli.js invalidCommand
  ```

  * The script throws an uncaught exception
  * Outputs a stack trace instead of a user-friendly message
  * Exit behavior is not explicitly controlled

* Similar command-handling logic is duplicated across:

  * `scripts/build/cli.js`
  * `scripts/build/ddoc-compile.js`

---

### Expected Behavior

* Commands should be validated before execution
* Missing or unknown commands should:

  * Display a clear, user-friendly error message
  * Optionally list available commands
  * Exit with a non-zero status code (e.g., `1`)
* Command parsing and validation logic should be centralized to avoid duplication

---

### Proposed Solution

* Extract command lookup and validation into a shared helper
* Update both CLI entrypoints to use this helper
* Add consistent error handling (try/catch + controlled exit)

---

### Impact

* Improves developer experience when using build scripts
* Prevents confusing stack traces for simple input errors
* Reduces duplication and improves maintainability

---

### Additional Context

I can work on a PR to centralize command validation and align error handling across these scripts, if this approach is acceptable.

fix(#10955): replace eval() with strict comparison for boolean CSV parsing
body:
## Description

Fixes #10955

Replaces the use of `eval()` in `assignCsvCellValue` with a direct strict comparison for converting `"TRUE"`/`"FALSE"` CSV strings to boolean values.

## Changes

**Before:**
```javascript
if (['TRUE', 'FALSE'].includes(data[attribute])) {
  // converts the "TRUE" or "FALSE" string to boolean
  data[attribute] = eval(data[attribute].toLowerCase());
}
```

**After:**
```javascript
if (['TRUE', 'FALSE'].includes(data[attribute])) {
  data[attribute] = data[attribute] === 'TRUE';
}
```

## Why

- `eval()` is flagged by ESLint's `no-eval` rule and security audit tools
- Using `eval()` for string-to-boolean conversion is unnecessary when a strict comparison works
- Reduces risk surface — even though the current guard limits input to "TRUE"/"FALSE", future code changes could weaken that guard
- No behavioral change — existing unit tests confirm `TRUE` → `true` and `FALSE` → `false`

## Test plan

- [x] Existing unit tests in `users.spec.js` cover this exact behavior (parseCsv tests verify TRUE→true, FALSE→false)
- [ ] Verify CSV bulk user upload still works correctly with boolean fields like `token_login`

- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.
- [x] Ensure that all issues are labelled correctly, particularly ensure that "Regressions" are labelled with "Affects: <version>" labels. The "Affects" label is used in a link in the Known Issues section of the release notes of that version so it has to match exactly. To make sure the label is correct go to the [release notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) and ensure the issue is listed.

# Development - Release Manager

When development is ready to begin one of the maintainers should be nominated as a Release Manager. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR to the release branch. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version patch`.
- [x] Ensure that issues from merged commits are closed and mapped to a milestone.
- [x] Write an update in the #stewardship-team Slack channel summarising development and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The Release Manager is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Manager

Once all issues have been merged into `master` then the release process can start:

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`).
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the community by creating a post titled `<major>.<minor>.<patch> Beta Releases` in the [development](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/development/7) category of the CHT forum using this [template](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/new-topic?title=%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.%3Cpatch%3E%20Beta%20Releases&body=Hi%20Everyone%0AI%E2%80%99ve%20just%20created%20the%20%60%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.%3Cpatch%3E-beta.1%60%20tag.%0APlease%20let%20me%20know%20if%20there%E2%80%99s%20any%20final%20update%20we%20need%20to%20make.%0AIf%20all%20is%20good%2C%20then%20in%2024h%2C%20I%20will%20start%20the%20release.%20Thanks%21&category=development).
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:

  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labelled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [x] Collect known migration steps, descriptions, screenshots, videos, data, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. This information should already be on the issue, but if not, prompt the change author to provide it.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Ensure that the release notes PR is merged before moving to next step.
- [x] Create a [new release](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases/new) in GitHub, with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, from the release branch created above as the target branch. Click on the "Choose a tag" dropdown and create a tag for the release with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. Add a link to the release notes page in the description of the release.
- [x] Once you publish the release, confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Upgrade the [demo](https://demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org/) instance to the newly released version.

  - [x] Clone cht-core and checkout the target tag to ensure you have the proper version of the helm charts.

# Description

### Fixes #9684

This PR implements a patch for enketo-core to resolve a persistent "no context element found" console error. The error occurs when adding or removing entries in a repeat group while another repeat group in the same form is empty and contains fields with relevant expressions.

### Solution
When a repeat group's instances change, Enketo triggers a global update that re-evaluates expressions for all fields. If a different repeat group is empty, Enketo's evaluate function fails to find a context node for its fields, resulting in a false-positive console error.

The patch modifies FormModel.prototype.evaluate to:

- Detect when a context node is missing but a selector path is provided.
- Return a type-appropriate default value (false for booleans, [] for node sets, NaN for numbers) instead of logging an error.
- Silence the console.error for these specific, expected cases.

### Patch Verification:
- Verified that the patch applies cleanly using patch-package.
- Verified that the logic correctly handles all XPath result types (boolean, string, number, node, nodes).

title: Invalid config parsing in authorization.js leads to silent failures and unclear logging
body:
**Describe the bug**
Configuration parsing in `authorization.js` does not properly validate values from `replication_depth`, which can lead to incorrect behavior or silent misconfiguration.

In particular:

* `Number.isNaN` checks may be applied to unparsed values
* Invalid `depth` or `report_depth` values are not consistently validated
* Missing or malformed configuration may not provide sufficient feedback

---

**To Reproduce**

1. Set an invalid value in configuration:

   ```json
   {
     "replication_depth": [
       { "role": "admin", "depth": "abc", "report_depth": "xyz" }
     ]
   }
   ```
2. Run the application
3. Observe behavior

---

**Expected behavior**

* Configuration values should be validated after parsing
* Invalid values should:

  * Log clear warnings with the actual invalid input
  * Fall back to default values safely
* No silent failures or misleading validation

---

**Logs**
Currently, invalid values may result in unclear or insufficient logging (e.g., logging parsed `NaN` instead of the original invalid input).

---

**Screenshots**
N/A

---

**Environment**

* Instance: N/A (local development)
* Browser: N/A
* Client platform: macOS / Linux
* App: API (`authorization.js`)
* Version: current main branch

---

**Additional context**
The issue stems from validating parsed values without preserving the original input, which reduces the usefulness of logs. Improving validation and logging would enhance reliability and debuggability without changing existing behavior.

title: fix(#7627): clean up canvas and animation on destroy
body:
# Description
When a form uses both the `countdown-widget` and the `geopicker` widget, the countdown widget was leaking memory. The `_init()` method appended a `<canvas>` element to the DOM and started an animation loop, but there was no `destroy()` method to clean either of them up when the form was submitted or cancelled.

This PR fixes the leak by implementing `destroy()` on the `Timerwidget` class to stop the animation loop and remove the canvas from the DOM. The `timer-animation` module already had a guard to stop animating when `canvas.isConnected` is false, which works alongside this fix.

Fixes #7627

title: fix(ci): stabilise shellcheck by using system binary and bypassing download
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

feat(#1234): add hat wobble

+ -------------- > type: build|feat|fix|perf|refactor|test|chore

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

### Fixes: #10113

This PR resolves the flaky ci-compile failures caused by GitHub rate limiting when downloading the shellcheck binary.

### **Problem:**
The shellcheck npm package attempts to download a precompiled binary from GitHub Releases on its first execution. In CI environments, multiple runners sharing the same IP addresses often trigger a 403 Forbidden | rate limit exceeded error, causing the build to fail intermittently during the lint-shell step.

### **Solution:**

**Environment Variable Override**: Introduced the SHELLCHECKJS_BIN environment variable in the global CI configuration. This tells the npm wrapper to use a specific local binary instead of attempting a download.

**System Installation**: Updated the build.yml workflow to explicitly install shellcheck via apt-get on the runner. This guarantees the tool is available offline and bypasses the unreliable network request.

### **Testing**
Verified locally that setting SHELLCHECKJS_BIN correctly overrides the npm package's default download logic and validates the path.
Confirmed that ubuntu-latest and ubuntu-22.04 runners support apt-get install shellcheck.

title: feat(#9875): support select_*_from_file external datasets in forms
body:
# **Description**

Adds support for `select_one_from_file` / `select_multiple_from_file` XLSForm question types in CHT forms.

When pyxform converts an XLSForm that uses e.g. `select_one_from_file items.xml`, it produces an XForm model with an external instance:
`<instance id="items" src="jr://file/items.xml"/>`

Enketo's constructor accepts an `options.external` array to inject these datasets. CHT already uses this mechanism for `contact-summary` and `user-contact-summary`, but no other external datasets were supported — so `select_*_from_file` forms rendered without choices.

This PR loads external datasets from CHT's **generic resources system** (`CustomResourceService`) and injects them alongside the contact summaries into `options.external` when initialising the Enketo form.

## **Supported URI scheme**

- `jr://file/items.xml` — the resource is XML and is parsed directly with `DOMParser`.

> Note: only XML external datasets are supported. Earlier iterations of this PR also handled CSV (`jr://file-csv/…`), but that was removed during review to keep the scope focused; if a referenced resource is missing (or is not XML), form loading fails fast with a clear error.

## **Data source**

Files are uploaded via `cht-conf`'s existing `upload-resources` action (list the file in `resources.json` and place it in the `resources/` directory) and stored as attachments on the shared `resources` CouchDB document — the same mechanism used for icons. This lets the same dataset be reused across multiple forms.

## **Implementation details**

- `ExternalInstance` interface extracted from the previously-private `ContactSummaryXml` and exported so `FormService` (and future callers) can type external instances.
- XML decoding/parsing lives in `CustomResourceService`: `getResource()` reads the attachment from its in-memory resource cache (no extra DB calls), and `getXml()` base64-decodes it, parses it to a `Document`, and caches the parsed result (keyed by filename) to avoid re-parsing across renders. The XML cache is cleared when the `resources` doc changes.
- `FormService.getExternalInstances()` traverses the form model for `instance[src][id]` nodes, resolving each via `getFilenameFromSrc` (URI-scheme detection) + `loadExternalInstance` (resource lookup + parse). The resulting instances are passed through the form context into Enketo's `options.external` alongside the contact summaries.

## Closes #9875

contact list endpoints.

Scope is the qualifier and the API surface only. The existing
`db.query('medic-client/contacts_by_phone', ...)` call sites are **not**
migrated by this ticket: review found that every one of them changes behaviour
when it moves onto the datasource — permissions, `isContact` filtering, or
input handling — and each change needs a decision of its own. That work is
#11442  No existing
read moves onto the new path here.

This is the **pilot ticket** for a series of view→qualifier migrations. The
other tickets in the series follow this recipe with the qualifier name and view
swapped. Subsequent tickets reference this one; review it carefully because
corrections here propagate to the rest.

The view (`ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/contacts_by_phone/map.js`):

```js
function(doc) {
  if (doc.phone) {
    var types = [ 'contact', 'district_hospital', 'health_center', 'clinic', 'person' ];
    if (types.indexOf(doc.type) !== -1) {
      emit(doc.phone);
    }
  }
}
```

Translates to: "all docs whose `phone` field is set and whose `type` is a
contact-shaped type, emit the phone as the key." Note the hard-coded type list
— it emits `type: contact` docs whose `contact_type` is not in settings, which
is why the datasource arms filter (see Requirements).

## Technical Context

**Components:**
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/qualifier.ts` — add `PhonesQualifier`,
  `byPhones`, `isPhonesQualifier`
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/contact.ts` — extend `getUuidsPage` /
  `getUuids` / `getPage` / `getAll` and the imperative `getDatasource()` surface
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/contact.ts` — dispatch arms
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/libs/doc.ts` — `queryDocsByKeys`
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/remote/contact.ts` — `phone` param
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/libs/parameter-validators.ts` — extend the
  shared assert helpers
- `api/src/controllers/contact.js` — `phone` query param on the two list
  endpoints

**Existing References:**
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/contact.ts` — the `getUuidsPage`
  dispatch arms (`isFreetextQualifier`, `isContactTypeQualifier`)
- PR [#10083](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10083) — create/update
  qualifiers + Local/Remote dispatch, the pattern this ticket follows
- PR [#11327](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/11327) — `byForm`, the
  plural-qualifier and `keys`-helper decisions reused here

## Requirements

### Qualifier

1. `PhonesQualifier` in `qualifier.ts`, plural and array-shaped:

   ```ts
   export type PhonesQualifier = Readonly<{ phones: [string, ...string[]] }>;
   ```

   `byPhones(phones)` dedupes with a `Set` in supplied-key order.
   `isPhonesQualifier` accepts only a non-empty array of non-blank strings.

2. Phone numbers are matched **verbatim** — leading `+`, country codes and
   internal formatting are passed through untouched, because the view does no
   normalisation and the qualifier must not either. Coercion is the caller's
   job; do not call `String(phone)` in the validator.

3. A blank or whitespace-padded entry is rejected rather than passed through: a
   padded number can only ever match nothing, so it is an argument error, not a
   silent empty page.

4. Expose `byPhones` through the existing `export * as Qualifier` re-export.

### Adapters

5. Local: dispatch arms in `getUuidsPage` and — via `getContactDocsPageFn` — in
   `getPage`. Both query the view with `keys` and filter rows through
   `isContact`, so the id path and the doc path return the same contacts.
   Without the filter the id path would hand back ids that
   `GET /api/v1/contact/{id}` then 404s, since `get` applies `isContact` too.
   Deduping in a stable order is what keeps the skip cursor meaningful between
   pages, since rows come back grouped in supplied-key order.

6. `queryDocsByKeys` in `local/libs/doc.ts` — the docs twin of the
   `queryDocIdsByKeys` helper #11327 added.

7. Remote: a `phone` param on both list endpoints.

8. Extend the shared assert helpers rather than duplicating them
   (`assertContactTypeFreetextPhonesQualifier`,
   `assertContactTypeIdsPhonesQualifier`), so no call site can still reach a
   two-qualifier assertion.

9. `getUuidsPageByPhones` / `getUuidsByPhones` / `getPageByPhones` /
   `getByPhones` on the imperative `getDatasource()` surface, next to
   `getPageByType`.

### API

10. A `phone` query param on `GET /api/v1/contact/uuid` and
    `GET /api/v1/contact`, accepting a comma-joined list. No new route and no
    `routing.js` change — paging, permissions and the OpenAPI shape stay on the
    established contract.

11. Precedence: on `/uuid`, `phone` over `type` and `freetext`; on `/contact`,
    `ids`, then `phone`, then `type`.

12. An object-shaped `phone` (`?phone[a]=b`, which `qs.parse` parses to an
    object) is rejected with a 400 rather than throwing.

13. The no-qualifier error message changes on both endpoints:
    `Either query param freetext or type is required` becomes
    `Either query param freetext, type or phone is required`. This is the only
    change visible to an existing API consumer.

### Tests

- Unit: the qualifier (valid and invalid input — empty array, non-string entry,
  blank, whitespace-padded), both local arms including the `isContact` filter
  on the id path, the remote adapter, the assert helpers, the controller.
- API integration: `?phone=`, comma-separated, repeated param, and the 400
  cases on both endpoints.
- Datasource integration: `getUuidsPage`, `getPage`, the generator,
  non-normalisation, a three-page cursor walk asserting exact ids and cursors,
  and a `type: contact` doc with an unconfigured `contact_type` that the view
  emits and neither phones path returns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `byPhones` lands in `qualifier.ts` and is reachable as `Qualifier.byPhones`,
  with valid and invalid input unit tests passing.
- Local and Remote adapters dispatch the qualifier on both the uuid path and
  the doc path, with adapter-level unit tests passing.
- `GET /api/v1/contact/uuid?phone=` and `GET /api/v1/contact?phone=` return
  `{ data, cursor }` matching the existing pagination contract.
- The uuid path and the doc path return the same set of contacts for the same
  numbers.
- `eslint .`, `npm run unit-api` and `npm run unit-shared-lib` pass.

## Constraints

- Backwards-compatible: existing `getUuidsPageByFreetext` / `getUuidsPageByType`
  calls continue to work unchanged. The no-qualifier error message is the one
  accepted change.
- No new top-level method on the `Contact.v1` namespace. The qualifier pattern
  is the explicit design constraint of this batch; the batch-shaped helpers go
  on the imperative `getDatasource()` surface instead.
- Do not relax `Input.v1.*Input._id?: never`. Client-supplied UUIDs go through
  the existing `idHint` curried-arg pattern in
  `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/libs/doc.ts`, not via qualifiers.
- Do not normalise phone numbers in the qualifier. The CouchDB view does not
  normalise; the qualifier must not either.
- Do not change the ddoc. Emitting the doc type as the view value would let the
  `isContact` filter run on `row.value` and save the uuid path an
  `include_docs`, but that is a ddoc change and a reindex — revisit if the
  phones uuid path ever gets a high-volume caller.
- Do not migrate any existing `contacts_by_phone` caller. That is a separate
  ticket, for the reasons in the Description.

## References

**Similar Implementations:**
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10083 — qualifier + Local/Remote dispatch pattern
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/11327 — plural qualifier, `keys` helper, query-param serialisation
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/9625 — the pagination-test discipline cited above

**Documentation:**
- `ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/contacts_by_phone/map.js`
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/README.md`

title: Fix dropdown closing on Android back button (remove jQuery, use ngx-bootstrap state)
body:
## Description
AndroidApiService handles the Android back button by closing UI elements like modals and dropdowns before navigating back.

Right now, dropdowns are being closed using jQuery by removing the .open class:

```
const $dropdown = $container.find('.filter.dropdown.open:visible');
if ($dropdown.length) {
  $dropdown.removeClass('open');
  return true;
}
```

But dropdowns have already been migrated to Angular (ngx-bootstrap), so this approach is outdated.

## Problem
This causes a mismatch between the UI and Angular state:

- The dropdown may disappear visually, but Angular still thinks it’s open
- Sometimes the dropdown isn’t detected at all
- This can break further interactions (clicks, toggles, etc.)

## Steps to Reproduce
- Open the app
- Open any dropdown (header/filter)
- Press the Android back button
- Notice inconsistent or broken behavior

## Proposed Fix
Instead of manipulating DOM with jQuery, we should use an Angular-based approach:

- Either track open dropdowns via a small service and call .hide() on them
- Or dispatch a global event that dropdown components listen to and close themselves
 
## Expected Result
- Dropdowns close cleanly on back press
- No state mismatch with Angular directives
- Removes reliance on jQuery for this logic

Please assign this issue to me. I am also open to suggestions.

title: Add `byShortcodes` and `byExternalRefs` qualifiers to `Contact.v1`
body:
---
title: Add `shortcodes` and `externalRefs` qualifiers to `Contact.v1` (over `medic-client/contacts_by_reference`)
type: improvement
priority: medium
domain: data-sync
labels:
  - cht-datasource
  - migration
---

## Description

Add `byShortcodes(shortcodes)` and `byExternalRefs(refs)` qualifiers to
`cht-datasource` so contacts can be looked up by shortcode (`patient_id` /
`place_id`) or by external reference (`rc_code`) through `Contact.v1`, and
expose both on the existing contact list endpoints.

Scope is the qualifiers and the API surface only. The existing
`db.query('medic-client/contacts_by_reference', ...)` call sites are **not**
migrated by this ticket: every one of them changes behaviour when it moves onto
the datasource — permissions, `isContact` filtering, the loss of the
key→id association the batch callers rely on, or input handling — and each
change needs a decision of its own. That work is #11443 . No
existing read moves onto the new path here.

The view (`ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/contacts_by_reference/map.js`):

```js
function(doc) {
  if (doc.type === 'contact' ||
      doc.type === 'clinic' ||
      doc.type === 'health_center' ||
      doc.type === 'district_hospital' ||
      doc.type === 'national_office' ||
      doc.type === 'person') {

    var emitReference = function(prefix, key) {
      emit([ prefix, String(key) ], doc.reported_date);
    };

    if (doc.place_id) {
      emitReference('shortcode', doc.place_id);
    }
    if (doc.patient_id) {
      emitReference('shortcode', doc.patient_id);
    }
    if (doc.rc_code) {
      emitReference('external', String(doc.rc_code).toUpperCase());
    }
  }
}
```

Translates to: "all docs whose `type` is a contact-shaped type; emit
`['shortcode', place_id]`, `['shortcode', patient_id]` and
`['external', RC_CODE]` for whichever fields are set." One view, two distinct
key spaces, so two qualifiers. Note the hard-coded type list — it emits
`national_office` docs and `type: contact` docs whose `contact_type` is not in
settings — which is why the datasource arms filter (see Requirements). Note
also the `.toUpperCase()` on `rc_code` only: `byExternalRefs` must upper-case
its input to preserve view parity, `byShortcodes` must not.

## Technical Context

**Components:**
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/qualifier.ts` — add `ShortcodesQualifier`,
  `byShortcodes`, `isShortcodesQualifier`, `ExternalRefsQualifier`,
  `byExternalRefs`, `isExternalRefsQualifier`
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/contact.ts` — extend `getUuidsPage` /
  `getUuids` / `getPage` / `getAll` and the imperative `getDatasource()` surface
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/contact.ts` — dispatch arms, reusing
  the `queryDocsByKeys` helper and `getContactDocsPageFn` from #11249
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/remote/contact.ts` — `shortcode` and
  `external_ref` params
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/libs/parameter-validators.ts` — extend the
  shared assert helpers
- `api/src/controllers/contact.js` — `shortcode` and `external_ref` query
  params on the two list endpoints

**Existing References:**
- #10973 / PR [#11249](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/11249) — the
  pilot. Branch from it (or rebase once it merges): the `PhonesQualifier`
  arms, `queryDocsByKeys` and the extended assert helpers are the pattern here.
- PR [#11327](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/11327) — `byForms`, the
  plural-qualifier and `keys`-helper decisions
- Branch `10976-by-shortcode-external-ref` (June) predates #11249's shape —
  singular + plural variants, a `POST /uuid` body, and callers migrated in the
  same commit. Do not revive it as-is.

## Requirements

### Qualifiers

1. Both plural and array-shaped, like `PhonesQualifier`:

   ```ts
   export type ShortcodesQualifier = Readonly<{ shortcodes: [string, ...string[]] }>;
   export type ExternalRefsQualifier = Readonly<{ externalRefs: [string, ...string[]] }>;
   ```

   `byShortcodes` / `byExternalRefs` dedupe with a `Set` in supplied-key order.
   The guards accept only a non-empty array of non-blank, non-padded strings.

2. `byShortcodes` matches **verbatim**. The view wraps the key in `String()`
   but does no trimming or case-folding, so the qualifier must not either.
   Coercion is the caller's job; do not call `String()` in the validator.

3. `byExternalRefs` upper-cases each entry in the builder, because the view
   emits `String(doc.rc_code).toUpperCase()`. `isExternalRefsQualifier`
   accepts only entries that are already upper-case
   (`ref === ref.toUpperCase()`), so a hand-built lower-case qualifier is
   rejected by the assert rather than silently matching nothing — the same
   reasoning as rejecting a padded value. Adapters trust the qualifier and
   build the `['external', ref]` key as-is.

4. A blank or whitespace-padded entry is rejected rather than passed through,
   for either qualifier: it can only ever match nothing, so it is an argument
   error, not a silent empty page.

5. Expose both through the existing `export * as Qualifier` re-export.

6. No union or mixed-prefix qualifier. A caller holding a mixed
   `[prefix, key][]` array splits it into a `byShortcodes` call and a
   `byExternalRefs` call; that is the migration ticket's concern.

### Adapters

7. Local: dispatch arms in `getUuidsPage` and — via `getContactDocsPageFn` —
   in `getPage`. Both build `['shortcode', s]` / `['external', r]` keys, query
   the view with `keys` through `queryDocsByKeys`, and filter rows through
   `isContact`, so the id path and the doc path return the same contacts and
   the id path never hands back an id that `GET /api/v1/contact/{id}` then
   404s. Deduping in a stable order keeps the skip cursor meaningful between
   pages, since rows come back grouped in supplied-key order.

8. A contact with both `patient_id` and `place_id` in the supplied list is
   emitted twice by the view. Each id appears at most once per page on both
   paths — apply the same id-set filter `fetchAndFilterIds` uses, since the doc
   path's `fetchAndFilter` does not dedupe on its own.

9. Remote: `shortcode` and `external_ref` params on both list endpoints,
   comma-joined like `phone`.

10. Extend the shared assert helpers from #11249
    (`assertContactTypeFreetextPhonesQualifier`,
    `assertContactTypeIdsPhonesQualifier`) to accept the two new shapes rather
    than adding new ones, so no call site can still reach a narrower assertion.

11. `getUuidsPageByShortcodes` / `getUuidsByShortcodes` / `getPageByShortcodes`
    / `getByShortcodes`, and the `ByExternalRefs` equivalents, on the
    imperative `getDatasource()` surface next to `getPageByPhones`.

### API

12. `shortcode` and `external_ref` query params on `GET /api/v1/contact/uuid`
    and `GET /api/v1/contact`, each accepting a comma-joined list or the
    parameter repeated. No new route and no `routing.js` change — paging,
    permissions and the OpenAPI shape stay on the established contract.

13. Precedence extends #11249's ordering: on `/uuid`, `phone`, then
    `shortcode`, then `external_ref`, then `type`/`freetext`; on `/contact`,
    `ids`, then `phone`, then `shortcode`, then `external_ref`, then `type`.
    Document it in the OpenAPI description of each param.

14. An object-shaped param (`?shortcode[a]=b`) is rejected with a 400 rather
    than throwing.

15. The no-qualifier error message on both endpoints lists the new params
    (`Either query param freetext, type, phone, shortcode or external_ref is
    required`; the `/contact` message starts with `ids`). This is the only
    change visible to an existing API consumer.

### Tests

- Unit: both qualifiers (valid and invalid input — empty array, non-string
  entry, blank, whitespace-padded; `byExternalRefs` upper-cases, and a
  hand-built lower-case `externalRefs` fails the guard), both local arms on
  both paths including the `isContact` filter, the remote adapter, the assert
  helpers, the controller.
- API integration: `?shortcode=` and `?external_ref=`, comma-separated,
  repeated param, mixed-case `external_ref`, and the 400 cases on both
  endpoints.
- Datasource integration: `getUuidsPage`, `getPage`, the generators, a
  three-page cursor walk asserting exact ids and cursors, a `national_office`
  doc and a `type: contact` doc with an unconfigured `contact_type` that the
  view emits and neither path returns, and a contact carrying both a
  `patient_id` and a `place_id` from the supplied list that appears once.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `byShortcodes` and `byExternalRefs` land in `qualifier.ts` and are reachable
  as `Qualifier.byShortcodes` / `Qualifier.byExternalRefs`, with valid and
  invalid input unit tests passing.
- Local and Remote adapters dispatch both qualifiers on the uuid path and the
  doc path, with adapter-level unit tests passing.
- `GET /api/v1/contact/uuid` and `GET /api/v1/contact` accept `shortcode` and
  `external_ref` and return `{ data, cursor }` matching the existing
  pagination contract.
- The uuid path and the doc path return the same set of contacts for the same
  keys.
- `eslint .`, `npm run unit-api` and `npm run unit-shared-lib` pass.

## Constraints

- Backwards-compatible: existing `getUuidsPageByFreetext` / `getUuidsPageByType`
  / `getUuidsPageByPhones` calls continue to work unchanged. The no-qualifier
  error message is the one accepted change.
- No new top-level method on the `Contact.v1` namespace. The batch-shaped
  helpers go on the imperative `getDatasource()` surface.
- Do not relax `Input.v1.*Input._id?: never`.
- Do not trim or case-fold in `byShortcodes`. Do not do anything but upper-case
  in `byExternalRefs`. The view is the parity contract.
- Do not introduce a union qualifier for mixed prefix arrays.
- Do not change the ddoc.
- Do not migrate any existing `contacts_by_reference` caller. That is
  #<migration-issue>, for the reasons in the Description.

## References

**Similar Implementations:**
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/11249 — the pilot: `byPhones`,
  `queryDocsByKeys`, `isContact` filtering on both paths, query-param
  precedence
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/11327 — plural qualifier, `keys`
  helper, query-param serialisation
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/9625 — the pagination-test discipline

**Documentation:**
- `ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/contacts_by_reference/map.js`
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/README.md`

title: Improve error handling to prevent silent failures across modules
body:

* Standardize error handling across modules
* Replace silent failures with explicit error messages or warnings
* Improve logging by adding contextual details such as module name, function, and input data
* Ensure critical failures are properly surfaced instead of being ignored

---

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

* Adding logs only in specific files instead of enforcing a consistent approach
* Continuing with the current setup and relying on manual debugging

title: fix(#8653): re-trigger db-object-widget when field becomes relevant
body:
# Description

When a `select-contact` field has its value pre-populated via a `calculation` and the field is initially non-relevant, the `db-object-widget` never loads the contact data. This happens because the `change` event that triggers `changeHandler()` is never fired when the field transitions from non-relevant to relevant it only fires when the user manually selects a contact.

This fix overrides the `enable()` method on the widget, which Enketo calls exactly when a field transitions from non-relevant to relevant. Inside `enable()`, if the hidden text input already has a pre-populated contact ID and the contact doc hasn't been loaded yet, we re-initialize Select2 with that value as `initialValue`. This triggers `getDoc()` → `setDoc()` → `change` event → `changeHandler()` → `updateFields()`, which correctly loads the contact data into the form.

<!-- ISSUE NUMBER -->
Fix #8653

title: fix(#10974): handle Android back button for dropdowns via Angular state
body:
This PR replaces the legacy jQuery-based dropdown closing logic in AndroidApiService with a modern Angular-native approach.

### Changes:
- Created `DropdownService` to track open `ngx-bootstrap` dropdowns.
- Created `DropdownTrackingDirective` (`mmDropdownTracking`) to automatically register/unregister dropdowns with the service.
- Refactored `AndroidApiService` to use `DropdownService.closeAll()` instead of jQuery DOM manipulation.
- Migrated `AnalyticsFilterComponent` to use `ngx-bootstrap` dropdowns.
- Applied the tracking directive to dropdowns in Header, Analytics, Date, and Sort filters.
- Updated `AndroidApiService` unit tests.

This ensures that dropdown state remains synchronized with Angular when closed via the hardware back button, resolving inconsistencies and potential UI breakage.

title: Nouveau query escaping misses documented special characters
body:
## Description

The `escapeKeys` function in `shared-libs/nouveau/src/index.js` does not escape all characters listed in its own documentation comment.

The comment on line 1-3 references the [CouchDB Nouveau query syntax](https://docs.couchdb.org/en/stable/ddocs/nouveau.html#query-syntax) and lists these characters as requiring escaping:

```
+ - && || ! ( ) { } [ ] ^ " ~ * ? : \ /
```

The current implementation escapes: `+ - & | ! ^ " ~ * ? : [ ]`

**Missing:** `(`, `)`, `{`, `}`, `\`, `/`

## Impact

The `escapeKeys` function is used to build `key:(...)` Nouveau queries in:
- `api/src/services/authorization.js:631` — replication key collection
- `sentinel/src/lib/purging.js:274` — purging record lookup

If a replication key or subject ID ever contains any of the unescaped characters (particularly `)` which would break out of the `key:(...)` grouping), the Nouveau query would be malformed. In practice, subject IDs are UUIDs and CouchDB usernames which don't contain these characters, so this is a latent correctness bug rather than an active breakage.

## Steps to reproduce

```js
const { escapeKeys } = require('@medic/nouveau');
console.log(escapeKeys('key)value'));  // outputs: key)value  (should be: key\)value)
console.log(escapeKeys('key/value'));  // outputs: key/value  (should be: key\/value)
```

title: Login password visibility icon does not update after toggling
body:
## Description

Clicking the password visibility (eye) icon on the login page toggles the input type between `password` and `text`, but the icon itself does not update to reflect the current state.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f677ff4-c5d8-44e9-a658-54a00db70d0c

## Root cause

`api/src/public/login/script.js:264` calls `togglePassword` with only one argument:

```js
togglePassword(PASSWORD_INPUT_ID)
```

But `api/src/public/login/auth-utils.js:113` expects two arguments:

```js
const togglePassword = (passwordInputId, passwordContainerId) => {
    ...
    document.getElementById(passwordContainerId)?.classList.toggle('hidden-password');
};
```

Since `passwordContainerId` is `undefined`, the `hidden-password` CSS class on `#password-container` is never toggled, so the icon stays in its initial state.

The password reset page does this correctly (`password-reset.js:138`):
```js
togglePassword('password', 'password-container');
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Navigate to the login page
2. Enter any text in the password field
3. Click the eye icon to show the password
4. Observe: the password text is revealed, but the icon still shows the "show password" state instead of switching to "hide password"

## Expected behavior

The icon should toggle between show/hide states when clicked, matching the password reset page behavior.

title: Generated web manifest is invalid when branding title contains JSON-special characters
body:
## Description

The generated `manifest.json` becomes invalid JSON when the branding title contains double quotes, backslashes, or other JSON-special characters.

## Root cause

`api/src/templates/manifest.json:3` interpolates the branding name as raw text:

```json
"name": "{{ branding.name }}"
```

`api/src/services/manifest.js:14-17` renders this via Lodash `_.template` with the raw `interpolate` setting, so no escaping is applied. A branding name like `CHT "Community"` produces:

```json
"name": "CHT "Community""
```

which is invalid JSON. The same issue applies to `branding.icon` on line 9:

```json
"src": "/img/{{ branding.icon }}"
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Set branding title to a string containing a double quote (e.g. `CHT "Community"`)
2. Restart the API server (or trigger manifest regeneration)
3. Fetch `/manifest.json`
4. Observe: the response is malformed JSON

## Impact

Broken `manifest.json` prevents PWA installability and may cause browser warnings. While branding names with quotes are uncommon, backslashes in icon filenames are more plausible.

## Suggested fix

JSON-escape the interpolated values before inserting them into the template, or build the manifest as a JavaScript object and use `JSON.stringify` to generate the output.

title: Login redirect drops query parameters after successful authentication
body:
## Description

When a user is redirected to the login page from a URL containing query parameters, the query parameters are lost after successful authentication. The user is redirected back to the correct path but without the original query string.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Attempt to access a URL with query parameters while unauthenticated, e.g. `/reports?search=malaria&sort=date#selected`
2. Get redirected to the login page
3. Log in successfully
4. Observe the redirect URL

## Expected Behavior

User is redirected to `/reports?search=malaria&sort=date#selected` (full original URL preserved).

## Actual Behavior

User is redirected to `/reports#selected` — query parameters are stripped.

## Root Cause

In `api/src/controllers/login.js`, the `resolveUrl()` helper correctly preserves query parameters:

```js
const { pathname, search, hash } = resolvedUrl;
return pathname + search + hash;
```

However, `sanitizeRequestedRedirect()` re-parses the resolved URL and drops `parsed.search`:

```js
const parsed = new URL(resolved, 'resolve://');
const path = parsed.pathname + (parsed.hash || '');
```

## Suggested Fix

Include `parsed.search` in the path construction:

```js
const path = parsed.pathname + (parsed.search || '') + (parsed.hash || '');
```

And add test coverage in `api/tests/mocha/controllers/login.spec.js`.

## Impact

Any workflow that relies on deep links with query parameters loses context after login — filtered report views, shared links, bookmarked pages with state, etc.

title: fix: global URL slash normalization corrupts query parameter values
body:
## Description

The global middleware in `api/src/routing.js` normalizes double slashes in request URLs:

```js
req.url = req.url.replace(/\/+/g, '/');
```

This operates on the entire `req.url` string, which includes the query string. Any query parameter containing a URL or double slash gets corrupted.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Send a request with a URL-like value in a query parameter:
   ```
   GET /some/path?redirect=https://example.com/a//b
   ```
2. Observe the middleware rewrites it to:
   ```
   GET /some/path?redirect=https:/example.com/a/b
   ```

## Expected Behavior

Only the pathname portion should be normalized. Query parameters should be preserved as-is:
```
/some/path?redirect=https://example.com/a//b
```

## Actual Behavior

The entire URL string including query params is modified:
```
/some/path?redirect=https:/example.com/a/b
```

## Root Cause

`req.url` contains both the pathname and query string (e.g. `/path?key=value`). The regex `\/+/g` matches all consecutive slashes, including those inside query parameter values.

## Suggested Fix

Split the URL at the query boundary and only normalize the pathname:

```js
app.use((req, res, next) => {
  const [pathname, ...rest] = req.url.split('?');
  req.url = pathname.replace(/\/+/g, '/') + (rest.length ? '?' + rest.join('?') : '');
  next();
});
```

## Impact

Any route that receives URL-like values in query parameters (redirects, callback URLs, external references) will have those values silently corrupted before reaching the handler.

title: fix(#10999): only normalize slashes in URL pathname, not query params
body:
## Description

Fixes #10999

The global middleware in `api/src/routing.js` normalizes double slashes by replacing all consecutive slashes in `req.url`:

```js

```

Since `req.url` includes the query string, this corrupts any query parameter containing URL-like values or double slashes.

**Example:**
- Input: `/some/path?redirect=https://example.com/a//b`
- Before fix: `/some/path?redirect=https:/example.com/a/b`
- After fix: `/some/path?redirect=https://example.com/a//b`

## Code Change

```js

// After
const [pathname, ...rest] = req.url.split('?');
req.url = pathname.replace(/\/+/g, '/') + (rest.length ? '?' + rest.join('?') : '');
```

The fix splits the URL at the query boundary, normalizes only the pathname, and preserves the query string as-is. It also handles edge cases like multiple `?` characters in the URL.

title: Deceased contact deletion navigates using matrix params instead of route params
body:
## Description

After a deceased contact is deleted, the app navigates to the parent contact using Angular matrix parameters instead of route parameters, resulting in an incorrect URL.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a contact marked as deceased
2. Delete the contact
3. Observe the URL after deletion

## Expected Behavior

Navigation should go to:
```
/contacts/<parent-id>
```

## Actual Behavior

Navigation goes to:
```
/contacts;id=<parent-id>
```

This happens because `contacts-deceased.component.ts` line 72 uses:
```ts
this.router.navigate(['/contacts', { id: parentId || null }]);
```

In Angular, passing an object as a route segment creates matrix parameters (`/contacts;id=value`), not a path segment. The contacts route definition expects a path parameter:
```ts
{ path: ':id', ... }
```

## Suggested Fix

```ts
this.router.navigate(parentId ? ['/contacts', parentId] : ['/contacts']);
```

This navigates to `/contacts/<parent-id>` when a parent exists, or `/contacts` if there is no parent.

## Impact

After deleting a deceased contact, users may land on the wrong contacts view instead of seeing the parent contact. This affects the contact management workflow.

title: fix(#11001): use route params instead of matrix params for deceased contact navigation
body:
## Description

Fixes #11001

After a deceased contact is deleted, `contacts-deceased.component.ts` navigates using Angular matrix parameters instead of route parameters:

```ts
// Before — creates /contacts;id=parent-id (matrix params)
this.router.navigate(['/contacts', { id: parentId || null }]);

// After — creates /contacts/parent-id (route params)
this.router.navigate(parentId ? ['/contacts', parentId] : ['/contacts']);
```

The contacts route expects a path parameter (`:id`), not matrix params. This mismatch causes the user to land on the wrong view after deletion instead of seeing the parent contact.

## How to reproduce

1. Navigate to a contact that has a deceased child contact
2. Open the deceased child contact
3. Delete the contact
4. Observe the URL — it shows `/contacts;id=<parent-id>` instead of `/contacts/<parent-id>`

title: fix: exact 1-year and 1-month ages display as lower units due to off-by-one comparison
body:
## Description

`getDateDiff()` in `webapp/src/ts/services/format-date.service.ts` uses a strict greater-than comparison against `ageBreak.min`:

```ts
if (Math.abs(diff) > ageBreak.min) {
```

Since both the years and months age breaks have `min: 1`, exact boundary values (exactly 1 year, exactly 1 month) fail the check and fall through to the next smaller unit.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a patient born exactly 1 year ago (e.g. today is 2026-05-05, DOB is 2025-05-05)
2. View the patient's age on their contact page

## Expected Behavior

Age displays as **1 year**.

## Actual Behavior

Age displays as **12 months** because `Math.abs(-1) > 1` is `false`, so the years break is skipped and months is used instead.

Same issue for exactly 1 month — displays as ~30 days.

## Root Cause

The ageBreaks config:
```ts
ageBreaks: [
  { unit: 'years', key: { singular: 'y', plural: 'yy' }, min: 1 },
  { unit: 'months', key: { singular: 'M', plural: 'MM' }, min: 1 },
  { unit: 'days', key: { singular: 'd', plural: 'dd' }, min: 0 },
]
```

With `min: 1` and `>` (strict), a diff of exactly 1 does not match. It needs `>=` to include the boundary.

## Suggested Fix

Change the comparison to include the boundary:

```ts
if (Math.abs(diff) >= ageBreak.min) {
```

The days break (`min: 0`) is unaffected since `>= 0` still matches all non-negative values.

## Impact

Patient ages and date differences are core clinical information displayed throughout the app. A 1-year-old showing as "12 months" is confusing for health workers.

title: fix(#11003): include boundary values in age break comparison
body:
## Description

Fixes #11003

`getDateDiff()` in `format-date.service.ts` uses strict greater-than (`>`) when comparing the date difference against `ageBreak.min`. Since both years and months age breaks have `min: 1`, exact boundary values (exactly 1 year, exactly 1 month) fail the check and fall through to the next smaller unit.

**Example:** A patient born exactly 1 year ago displays as "12 months" instead of "1 year".

## Code Change

```ts
// Before
if (Math.abs(diff) > ageBreak.min) {

// After
if (Math.abs(diff) >= ageBreak.min) {
```

The days break (`min: 0`) is unaffected since `>= 0` matches the same values as `> 0` for this context (the fallback at line 110 already handles the 0-day case).

## Test plan

- [x] Added test: exactly 1 year old displays with singular year key (`y`)
- [x] Added test: exactly 1 month old displays with singular month key (`M`)
- [x] Existing tests for 5 years, 16 months, 50 days, 1 day, 0 days, and age-at-death all continue to pass
- [x] ESLint passes

title: Release notes script crashes when commit author has null GitHub user
body:
## Description

The release notes generation script in `scripts/release-notes/index.js` assumes every commit author returned by the GitHub GraphQL API has a non-null `author.user` object. GitHub returns `user: null` for commits made with unlinked email addresses or by deleted GitHub accounts.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a commit in the release range where the commit author's email is not linked to a GitHub account
2. Run the release notes script
3. Script crashes with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'login')`

## Root Cause

Two locations access `author.user` without null checks:

**Line 168** — `commitMadeByDependabot()`:
```js
commit.authors.nodes.forEach((author) => {
  if (BOTS.includes(author.user.login)) {  // crashes if user is null
```

**Line 324** — `formatCommits()`:
```js
authors.forEach((author) => {
  const { login, name, url } = author.user;  // crashes if user is null
```

Also **line 179** — `getCommitAuthorString()`:
```js
authors.forEach((author) => {
  authConcat += ` (${author.user.login})`;  // crashes if user is null
```

## Expected Behavior

The script should skip commits with null GitHub users or fall back to the commit author name/email from the Git metadata.

## Actual Behavior

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'login')
```

## Suggested Fix

Guard against null `author.user` in all three locations:

```js
// commitMadeByDependabot
if (author.user && BOTS.includes(author.user.login)) {

// getCommitAuthorString
if (author.user) {
  authConcat += ` (${author.user.login})`;
}

// formatCommits
const user = author.user;
if (user && user.login && !ignoreLogins.has(user.login)) {
```

## Impact

A single commit with an unlinked author can block release note generation during release preparation.

title: fix(#11005): guard null GitHub user in release notes script
body:
## Description

Fixes #11005

The release notes generation script crashes with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'login')` when a commit in the release range was authored by someone whose email is not linked to a GitHub account or whose account has been deleted. The GitHub GraphQL API returns `user: null` in these cases.

## Code Changes

Added null guards in three locations in `scripts/release-notes/index.js`:

1. **`commitMadeByDependabot()`** (line 168) — check `author.user` before accessing `.login`
2. **`getCommitAuthorString()`** (line 179) — skip authors with no GitHub user
3. **`formatCommits()`** (line 324) — skip authors with no GitHub user

All three follow the same pattern: if `author.user` is null, skip that author instead of crashing.

## Test plan

- [x] Authors with valid GitHub users are unaffected
- [x] Authors with null users are silently skipped
- [x] ESLint passes
