title: feat(#10139): add ability to hide contact forms for muted places
body:
# Description

Adds a new `can_create_contacts_under_muted_places` permission. The contact creation actions are hidden when a place is muted, or when any of its ancestors is muted. In the same case, the create itself is refused. A user whose role holds the permission is exempt from both. The webapp gates both fast action buttons (FABs) and the add route that opens the form. Five API endpoints carry the same gate.

Resolves #10139

**This is a behaviour change for existing deployments.** See Configuration below.

## Implementation notes

* **Webapp, the FABs**: `FastActionButtonService` skips the contact creation actions when the parent is muted and the caller does not hold the permission. The service applies this rule to both the contact detail (right side) FAB and the contacts list (left side) FAB. The service uses the existing `ContactMutedService.getMuted`, so it honours the same parent and ancestor semantics as the rest of the webapp. The contacts list FAB's parent is the user's home place. `LineageModelGeneratorService` hydrates that home place, so an inherited muted state is visible there too. The contacts list's changes subscription passes a change on any of the home place's ancestors through to its change handler. That hydrated copy is then refreshed in place. An online user's changes carry no `doc`. That condition therefore matches on the change id.
* **Webapp, the add route**: `validateParentForCreateForm` calls `ContactsEditComponent.ensureParentNotMuted`, which refuses to open the form for a muted parent. Hiding the contact creation action is not enough on its own. `/#/contacts/:parent_id/add/:type` is reachable directly from the address bar, and from a task's `contact` action. The refusal shows the existing "not authorized" copy rather than the generic form error. The refusal also logs at `info` rather than `error`. `FeedbackService`'s `FEEDBACK_LEVEL` is `error`, so `info` files no feedback doc for what is a routine policy outcome. The `info` log still prints in production, and it joins the circular log buffer that gets attached to any later real error. `debug` would have done neither. The same catch also cancels the component's geolocation handle. No form will open. The `watchPosition` started for it would otherwise stay live until the geolocation service's own 30 second timeout settles it. The catch is not a `finally`, because `save()` passes that same handle to `formService.saveContact` on the success path.
* **API**: a new `api/src/services/muted-parent.js` resolves the parent ref. The service checks the permission first (db admins short circuit). Only for a caller without the permission does the service fetch the hydrated parent via `@medic/lineage`. It then evaluates `parent.muted || isMutedInLineage(parent)`. The service has six call sites. Two are `controllers/person.js:160` and `controllers/place.js:159`, inside `#create`. The other four are in `api/src/routing.js`, across three handlers. The `POST /places` call site checks `req.body.parent` (`:596`). The `POST /people` call site checks `req.body.place || req.body.parent` (`:747`), since `createPerson` passes a raw `parent` through when `place` is falsy. The two `POST /places/:id` call sites check `req.body.parent` (`:665`) and `req.body.contact?.place || req.body.contact?.parent` (`:666`). That is because `updatePlace` hands an inline `contact` to `getOrCreatePerson`, and `createPerson` then writes it under whichever of those two refs is present.
* **Shared lib**: `@medic/transitions` now exposes the existing `muting_utils.isMutedInLineage` on the factory's return object, next to `isWithinTimeFrame`. The api consumes it through `config.getTransitionsLib()`, like `records.js` and `messaging.js` do. `muting_utils.js` is unchanged from master. The shared lib's source is net two lines in `index.js`, plus the new unit spec listed under Tests.

## Scope

Offline role users can reach the legacy `POST /api/v1/places` and `/api/v1/people` routes. The `auth.check` on those routes has no online requirement. `POST /api/v1/person` and `/place` require an online role. So for an offline role API caller, the legacy routes carry the only server side gate.

Despite the name, the permission is not only about creates. `POST /api/v1/places/:id` accepts a `parent`. So `can_create_contacts_under_muted_places` is also what permits moving an existing place under a muted place on that deprecated route. Only the moved place's own document is rewritten. Its existing descendants keep their stored lineage. The move does not re-gate the descendants themselves.

Moving an existing place under a muted place produces the same end state the ticket asks to prevent. The route is therefore gated. Leaving that route open would be a hole in the same guarantee.

The shipped default for `can_create_contacts_under_muted_places` is `[]` in all four config files. After upgrade, no configured role holds the permission, and only db admins bypass the gate. Consider an external client that reads a place, changes its name and posts the whole body back with `parent` included. It starts getting a 403 whenever that parent is muted. Nothing in this repo calls the route in product code. So the exposure is custom integrations only.

| Path | Gated? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Contact detail FAB, contacts list FAB | Yes | The contacts list FAB gates on the user's home place. `LineageModelGeneratorService` hydrates that home place. If that hydration fails, the contacts list FAB fails open. Only the add route then refuses. The hydrated home place is refreshed when the home place doc changes. For an online user, it is also refreshed when one of its ancestors changes. An inherited mute or unmute is therefore picked up without leaving the Contacts tab. A document above the user's own facility does not normally replicate. So for an offline user, an inherited mute arrives as the `muted` flag. The muting transition stamps that flag onto the home place itself. |
| `/#/contacts/:parent_id/add/:type`, typed directly or reached from a task's `contact` action | Yes | `ContactsEditComponent` refuses the add route. So hiding the contact creation action is not the only defence. |
| `POST /api/v1/person`, `POST /api/v1/place` | Yes | The parent must be a UUID string. The validator rejects objects. |
| `POST /api/v1/places/:id` re-parenting under a muted place | Partial | The gate covers any request carrying a `parent` that resolves to a document id. This includes a request that resends the place's existing parent. A body that omits `parent` (or sends it empty) is exempt. The gate also covers the inline `contact`'s `place` and raw `parent`, because `updatePlace` creates that person. Not covered: an inline `parent` (or `contact.place`) object with no `_id`. `getOrCreatePlace` creates that object under its own muted parent. Then the target is re-parented under it. |
| `POST /api/v1/places` (`parent`), `POST /api/v1/people` (`place`, or `parent` when `place` is absent or empty) | Partial | The gate covers a UUID string. It also covers an object whose `_id` is a string naming an existing doc. Not covered: an inline parent object with no `_id` or a non string `_id` (a place created in the same request). Also not covered: an object with a client chosen `_id` that does not exist yet. For that object, the lookup 404s and the gate treats the parent as not muted. Both shapes are documented above `isParentMuted`. What each route then writes is documented there too. |
| Any client's direct write to `_bulk_docs`, and replication | No | The webapp saves contacts with `dbService.get().bulkDocs(...)` for online and offline users alike. So no in-app save reaches a gated route. The add route gate is what actually stops the form opening. Offline users' `_bulk_docs` requests reach an authorization-only filter with no muted check. Online users' requests are proxied straight to CouchDB. This is the main remaining gap. It is the only gap this PR calls out as needing a future fix. See below. |
| Editing a place with a form configured to create child docs | No | An edit form whose XML adds siblings or repeats can create contacts under a muted place. This path is reachable only with such a form configured. None of the four default `*-edit.xml` forms does this. `can_edit` alone guards `:id/edit`. |
| A report form's `db-doc` elements creating contacts | No | This change does not touch report forms. A `db-doc="true"` node can emit a contact doc at any parent. Two default forms do exactly that: `delivery.xml`'s `baby_profile` and `replace_user.xml`'s `new_contact`. So on a stock install, a delivery report against a muted household still registers the baby under it. This is a pre-existing report-form capability with no relationship to #10139. |
| `POST /api/v1\|v2\|v3/users` creating inline places and people | No | This is a pre-existing admin flow. It is out of scope. |
| `POST /api/v1\|v2/records` where a configured registration transition's `add_patient` trigger creates a patient | No | The trigger's `parent_id` param names a report field. So the request body picks the parent. `api/src/controllers/records.js` runs the transition inside the request. This path is reachable only with such a registration configured. The default config sets `transitions.registration` to false and ships no registrations. |

### How wide the effect is

Two mechanisms compound, so it is worth stating the reach plainly. Muting cascades downward: the muting transition stamps `muted` on the target and on every descendant. `updateMuteState` queries `medic/contacts_by_depth` by the target's id, and the view emits that id for every descendant. `updateMuteState` then bulk-writes each one. This gate then walks upward. Both `parent.muted || isMutedInLineage(parent)` on the API and `ContactMutedService.getMuted` in the webapp treat a place with a muted ancestor as muted. So muting one district removes contact creation for every place and every user beneath it, not only for that district.

Gating the contacts list FAB extends that one step further. The contacts list FAB's parent is the user's own home place. So a user whose home place is muted, or sits under a muted place, has no contact creation action on the contacts list view either. The contact detail FAB and the add route are also gated. So that user can create no contacts anywhere beneath that place until the mute is lifted or the permission is granted. A top-level place, created from `/#/contacts/add/:type`, has no parent to gate and is unaffected.

The forum thread framed the request at household level. This reach is the honest reading of the ticket, but it is broader than that framing. So this section calls it out rather than leaving it to be discovered.

### The offline write path

An offline user's contact saves go to local PouchDB. They reach the server through `_bulk_docs`. `_bulk_docs` never touches the gated routes. `validate_doc_update.js` does not mention muting either. There is no muted check anywhere in `api/src/services/replication/`.

The realistic way to hit this is a permission change racing a sync:

1. A CHW's role holds `can_create_contacts_under_muted_places`. The contact creation action is therefore shown.
2. The permission is revoked server side.
3. The CHW has not synced yet. Their client still evaluates the old settings. The client still shows the action.
4. They create a contact under a muted place. It saves locally. It replicates up successfully.

Verified against a dev instance. With the permission revoked, an offline user's `_bulk_docs` write of a person under a muted clinic returns `[{"ok":true,"id":"...","rev":"1-..."}]`. The document lands in CouchDB with its lineage pointing at the muted place.

Where sentinel's muting transition is enabled, that transition mutes a contact that arrives this way. The muting happens afterwards. So the end state is consistent, even though creation was not blocked. Where the muting transition is disabled, the contact simply lands unmuted under a muted place.

This cannot be closed with a `validate_doc_update` rule. CouchDB validation functions receive only `newDoc`, `oldDoc`, `userCtx` and `secObj`, with no database access. The rule therefore cannot read the parent to learn whether it is muted. `minifyLineage` also stores only `_id` and `parent` on the new doc, never `muted`.

Closing it properly means a gate on the common write path (`canEdit`), not just the offline `_bulk_docs` and db-doc handlers. This is because online users' writes bypass those handlers and are proxied straight to CouchDB. That costs a parent lookup on every contact write. A replicated doc rejected there already exists on the device. Deferred rather than attempted here.

## What is not hidden

Only the contact creation actions are affected. On a muted contact the report forms remain available, including the configured unmute form. The phone and send message actions remain available too, as do Edit and Delete. Report forms on a muted contact keep their existing "Muted contact" confirmation modal rather than disappearing.

## Follow-up considerations (out of scope here)

* Whether **update** and **delete** on muted contacts also need analogous permissions. The forum thread and ticket only mention create. Update specifically would need a carve-out for the configured `unmute_forms` so users can still submit the unmute form against a muted contact.
* Closing the offline write path. This needs a gate on the common write path rather than in the offline handlers alone.

## Tests

* **Mocha unit (api)**: `muted-parent.spec.js` covers 15 cases. One case pins the nested payload limitation. One case asserts that the permission check runs before the lineage load. One case rejects a non string `_id`, so it cannot reach PouchDB. `controllers/{person,place}.spec.js` each add one rejection case. This PR also adds two assertions to their existing success cases.
* **Mocha unit (shared lib)**: a new `shared-libs/transitions/test/unit/index.js` pins that the factory exports `isMutedInLineage`. Nothing else covered that export.
* **Karma unit (webapp)**: 22 new cases. `fast-action-button.service.spec.ts` gets 6 cases. They cover the muted branch, its ordering against the base create permission, and a muted home place both directly and through a muted ancestor. `contacts-edit.component.spec.ts` gets 6 cases for the add route refusal, the inherited-ancestor case, the permission holder skipping the lineage read, and the clean-parent case. They also cover a refused form load filing no feedback doc, and the geolocation handle being cancelled when a form fails to load. `contacts.component.spec.ts` gets 8 cases for the hydrated home place being forwarded, no home place, and a hydration failure leaving the contacts list working. They also cover re-hydration on a change to the home place, on a change to an ancestor, and not on an unrelated change. Two cases cover the changes filter itself: a doc-less ancestor change passes it, and it does not throw before the home place has resolved. `contacts-content.component.spec.ts` gets 2 cases for `parentContact` forwarding.
* **HTTP integration (api)**: 19 cases across `muted parent gate` describes in `tests/integration/api/controllers/{person,place,places}.spec.js`. On `POST /api/v1/places`, `places.spec.js` covers a muted parent, a clean parent, and a clean parent whose own parent is muted. The last of those is the only case that exercises `isMutedInLineage` rather than the `parent.muted` short circuit. `places.spec.js` also covers the legacy `POST /api/v1/people` route. The cases there are `place`, raw `parent` without `place`, and `place: ''` with a raw `parent`. One more case pins that `place` wins over `parent` when both are present. `places.spec.js` also covers `POST /api/v1/places/:id` re-parenting. The cases there are a move under a muted parent, and a rename of a place already under one. A third case is a rename that resends the unchanged muted parent. On that same route, `places.spec.js` also covers an inline `contact` naming a muted place by `place` or by raw `parent`. One more case pins that `contact.place` wins over `contact.parent` when both are present.
* **E2E wdio**: a new `tests/e2e/default/contacts/muted-contacts-create.wdio-spec.js` with 4 scenarios. In a muted clinic without the permission, no contact creation action is present. In a non muted clinic, the action is present. The add route deep link is refused. In a muted clinic with the permission granted, the action is present after sync and reload.

## Translations

The permission description is in `messages-{en,es,fr,ne,pt,sw}.properties`. `fr`, `ne` and `pt` carry real translations. `en`, `es` and `sw` carry the English string. `es` and `sw` do so deliberately, because `scripts/ci/lint-translations.js` runs with `checkMissing` and `checkEmpties` over `en`, `es`, `fr`, `ne` and `sw`. If those two lines are missing or empty, CI fails. Forum post requesting the remaining translations: https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/translation-support-request-cht-core-10139/5608

## Configuration

This PR registers the new permission key with an empty role list in:

* `config/default/app_settings.json`
* `config/covid-19/app_settings.json`
* `config/covid-19/app_settings/base_settings.json`
* `tests/config.default.json`

**This restricts existing deployments on upgrade. It is not opt in.** On a fresh install the key arrives with the rest of `config/default/app_settings.json`. On an upgrade of an already configured instance, api backfills the key on the first startup after the upgrade.

`api/server.js:78` awaits `configWatcher.load()`. That call runs `loadSettings()` (`api/src/services/config-watcher.js:145`). `loadSettings()` is `settingsService.update({})` (`:73-74`). `api/src/services/settings.js:102-108` then runs `_.defaults(doc.settings.permissions, defaultConfig.permissions)`. The settings service PUTs the settings doc whenever that call adds anything. The key therefore lands in `settings.permissions` as `[]` with no operator action.

Later restarts change nothing. They do not write. The path you arrive by makes no behavioural difference. Absent and empty are identical for authorisation. `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/auth.js` treats a missing permission key as not granted. The restriction therefore applies immediately either way.

A deployment that wants the previous behaviour must grant the permission to the roles that already hold `can_create_people` or `can_create_places`. It must then push its settings.

One consequence of the backfill is worth knowing. The api performs that write itself. The admin app's Permissions tab therefore shows a row for the new key as soon as api has restarted. The tab needs no settings save first. The admin app builds the tab from `Object.keys(settings.permissions)` (`admin/src/js/controllers/authorization-permissions.js:27`). By then the key is there.

This matches the precedent. A permission of this kind turns a new restriction on by default. The permission itself is the opt out. `can_skip_password_change` and `can_view_old_navigation` both worked this way. `can_view_old_action_bar` and `can_view_old_filter_and_search` did the same, though they were removed in 4.12.0 along with the old UI they guarded.

title: feat(#10694): add free text search to tasks page
body:
# Description

Implements free text search on the tasks page, allowing users to filter the task list by typing in the search bar. The search matches against contact name, lineage (place hierarchy) and task title.

This picks up from #10727 and addresses all outstanding review feedback:
- **Performance**: replaced per-task Fuse.js instantiation with a single shared index built over unmatched candidates, avoiding redundant overhead on large task lists.
- **Two-pass strategy**: substring matching runs first for speed; fuzzy matching via Fuse.js only runs on the remaining tasks when the query is ≥ 3 characters.
- **Text normalisation**: input is lowercased and diacritics are stripped (NFD decomposition), so accented characters (e.g. `Élodie` → `elodie`) and non-Latin scripts (Nepali, Arabic) match as expected.
- **e2e tests**: added a new spec (`tasks-search.wdio-spec.js`) covering search by contact name, by task title, no-match state, clearing search, and combining search with sidebar filters.

Closes #10694

## Changes

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `webapp/src/ts/modules/tasks/tasks.component.html` | Enable `showFreetext` on the search bar |
| `webapp/src/ts/reducers/global.ts` | Add `search` field to `TasksFilters` interface |
| `webapp/src/ts/selectors/index.ts` | Search filtering logic with normalisation + Fuse.js |
| `webapp/package.json` | Add `fuse.js` dependency |
| `webapp/tests/karma/ts/selectors/index.spec.ts` | Unit tests for search, diacritics, Nepali/Arabic, edge cases |

title: feat(#10706): add DELETE /api/v1/contact/:uuid for recursive contact deletion
body:
## Summary

POC implementation for the first of three endpoints proposed in #10706.

- `DELETE /api/v1/contact/:uuid` recursively deletes a contact, all descendant contacts in the hierarchy, and all reports linked to any contact in the subtree
- Uses `medic/contacts_by_depth` with `startkey/endkey` range query to fetch the full subtree in a single CouchDB query
- Fetches linked reports via `medic-client/reports_by_subject` using contact UUIDs + shortcodes
- Bulk deletes in batches of 100 with explicit error propagation — no silent partial failures
- Permission gated behind `hasAny: [can_delete_contacts, can_edit]` following the existing pattern

## Files changed

- `api/src/services/contact-delete.js` — service with subtree fetch, report lookup, batched bulk delete
- `api/src/controllers/contact.js` — delete handler with full OpenAPI annotation
- `api/src/routing.js` — `DELETE /api/v1/contact/:uuid` route
- `api/tests/mocha/services/contact-delete.spec.js` — 7 unit tests (subtree fetch, dedup, report linking, error handling)
- `api/tests/mocha/controllers/contact.spec.js` — 3 new controller tests (success, 404, 403)

## Test results

19 passing unit tests (12 existing + 7 new service + 3 new controller), lint clean.

## What's not in this PR

Move and merge endpoints — planned for subsequent PRs following the same pattern. Integration tests will follow once the approach is confirmed by mentors.

## Notes for reviewers

This is a draft PR submitted as part of a C4GT DMP 2026 proposal for issue #10706. Happy to adjust the approach based on mentor feedback — particularly on the long-running operation question (sync vs async polling) the issue flags.

title: Fix gaps in legacy UI styling for UI Extensions
body: When the user has the `can_view_old_navigation` they can see the old-style header tabs. There are currently a couple style issues with how the new UI Extensions are rendered for the legacy UI. ## Add `accent_color` to "tab" part of the header for `app_main_tab` extensions. When you have a main header tab selected, the "tab" part of the header should be highlighted with the proper accent color: However, for UI Extensions, the "tab" part is not getting the background color set properly. Here is an example where I just used `"accent_color": "red"` for my extension: The red color should also be the background around the "Hello Extension" tab. ## When rendering `app_drawer_tab` extensions, do not include extra header bar at the top. The existing pages accessible from the legacy hamburger menu (About, Training Materials, etc) do not render the extra colored tool-bar space at the top of the page that you get with the main header tabs: However, when I open an `app_drawer_tab` extension from the legacy hamburger menu it still renders the extra header bar. We should not render this bar for the `app_drawer_tab` extensions.

title: Rebuild service worker when UI Extensions change
body:
One piece of api logic we missed is that we need to be sure to rebuild the service-worker file whenever any of the `ui-extensions:` docs changes.  Without this logic, the webapp is not getting automatically re-loaded to pick up changes to the UI Extensions and so new updates to the extensions are never loaded for logged in users.

Logic for watching the changes feed and triggering the service worker to be rebuild already exists in the api code.  We just need to add logic similar to [what we already have for extension-libs](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/56b79d8bf3dc85edf63655f86d7baadc9ac538e7/api/src/services/config-watcher.js#L184) that checks the `change.id` and returns `true` if it begins with the `ui-extension:` prefix.

This should cause the service-worker to be automatically rebuild as ui-extensions are created/modified/removed and rebuilding the service-worker should trigger the webapp to reload itself and we get the new extension versions.

title: Fix `UiExtensionsTabComponent` content not getting reloaded when navigating between extensions
body:
UI Extension content loads properly in the `UiExtensionsTabComponent` when you navigate from an existing app page to a UI Extension tab.  However, if you have multiple UI Extensions configured and you try to navigate _between them_ (so start on one extension tab and then use the header tabs or sidebar buttons to navigate to the other extension) then the content of the target tab is never rendered and the user just sees the content for the original extension even though the URL path changes.  

Here is a video of the behavior I am seeing:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/875e1bcf-32cb-4ac7-889f-9b5f4ac671dc

The content in the `UiExtensionsTabComponent` should properly render the extension content for the extension identified in the URL.

title: fix(#11017): fix legacy UI styling gaps for UI extensions
body:
# Description

Fixes two styling issues with UI Extensions when rendered under the legacy navigation (`can_view_old_navigation`).

## 1. accent_color not applied to selected tab for `app_main_tab` extensions

The legacy header applies background colors to the selected tab via CSS rules that match `.app-root.{tabName}`. However, all extension routes shared the static tab name `ui-extensions`, which did not match the header tab name `ui-extension-{id}`.

**Fix:** When an `app_main_tab` extension loads, the component now updates `currentTab` to `ui-extension-{id}` via the store, so it matches the header tab entry. The header template applies the extension's `accentColor` as an inline `background-color` on the selected tab element.

## 2. Extra toolbar rendered for `app_drawer_tab` extensions

Pages accessed from the legacy hamburger menu (About, Training Materials, etc.) hide the colored toolbar bar using `height: 0` in `old-nav.less`. But `app_drawer_tab` extensions were not included in that rule, so they rendered an unwanted toolbar.

**Fix:** Added `&.ui-extensions` to the existing CSS selector group in `old-nav.less` that hides the toolbar. Since `app_main_tab` extensions override `currentTab` to `ui-extension-{id}`, only `app_drawer_tab` extensions retain the `ui-extensions` class — so the rule targets the right set.

Fixes https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/11017

## Changes

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `ui-extensions-tab.component.ts` | Set `currentTab` to extension-specific name for `app_main_tab`; restore on destroy |
| `header-tabs.service.ts` | Pass `accentColor` through in `HeaderTab` interface |
| `header.component.html` | Apply `accentColor` as inline background on selected tab |
| `old-nav.less` | Add `&.ui-extensions` to toolbar-hiding and page-offset rules |
| Unit tests | Updated for both component and service |

## Description

Fixes https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/11018

When a `ui-extension:*` document is created or updated in CouchDB, the service worker is now rebuilt automatically. This ensures that new or modified UI extensions are available to users without requiring a server restart.

- Added unit tests covering create, update, and unrelated doc scenarios

- [ ] Update an existing `ui-extension:*` doc and verify the service worker is regenerated

title: fix(#11019): reload extension content when navigating between tabs
body:
## Description

Fixes https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/11019

When navigating between multiple UI extension tabs, the `UiExtensionsTabComponent` was not re-rendering because Angular reuses the same component instance for `ui-extensions/:id` — only the `:id` param changes. Since extension initialization only ran in `ngAfterViewInit` (which fires once), the original extension's content stayed visible even after the URL changed.

## Changes

- Subscribe to `ActivatedRoute.params` in `ngAfterViewInit` to detect when the `:id` parameter changes
- When a different extension is navigated to, clear the container and re-run `initializeExtension()` with the new id
- Reset component state (loading, error, title, accent color) before each initialization
- Unsubscribe from params on component destroy to prevent memory leaks
- Added tests for navigation between extensions, same-id no-op, and cleanup on destroy

## Test plan

- [ ] Configure two or more UI extensions as `app_main_tab`
- [ ] Navigate from one extension tab to another via header tabs
- [ ] Verify the target extension's content renders correctly
- [ ] Navigate back to the first extension and verify it renders again
- [ ] Verify the loading spinner shows during each transition
- [ ] Unit tests pass

title: fix(#10679): prevent geolocation timeout from blocking form submission
body:
## Description

Fixes https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10679

When GPS signal is weak and coordinates haven't been acquired by the time a user submits a form, the geolocation service was blocking submission for up to 30 seconds waiting for the watcher to either succeed or time out. This caused frustration and led some deployments to disable GPS entirely.

## Changes

The `complete()` function (called during form save) now resolves immediately when no geolocation data is available, returning `{code: -1, message: 'Geolocation not yet acquired'}` instead of hanging. If coordinates were already acquired while the user filled out the form, they are still captured as before.

After `complete()` resolves, `this.deferred` is nulled so that any late GPS watcher callbacks are silently discarded and do not leak additional telemetry entries.

This means:
- Forms submit instantly regardless of GPS state
- Geolocation data is still recorded when available (acquired before submission)
- When GPS was not acquired in time, the geolocation field reflects that clearly
- Late GPS callbacks after submission are safely ignored

## Telemetry impact

This shifts telemetry distribution: deployments tracking `geolocation:failure:-2` (30s timeout) will now mostly see `geolocation:failure:-1` instead, since the `-2` code only fires for forms left open longer than 30 seconds without submission. The total volume of failure events remains the same, but the code distribution changes. Any alerting or dashboards keyed on `-2` will need to be updated to also track `-1`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a form in an environment with no/weak GPS signal
- [ ] Submit the form quickly (before 30s)
- [ ] Verify the form submits immediately without waiting
- [ ] Verify the saved doc has `geolocation: {code: -1, message: 'Geolocation not yet acquired'}`
- [ ] Open a form and wait for GPS to be acquired, then submit
- [ ] Verify the saved doc has valid geolocation coordinates
- [ ] Unit tests pass

title: fix(10996): mirror nginx proxy headers in helm k3s-k3d ingress template
body:
# Description

The Docker nginx reverse proxy sets several proxy headers via `nginx/templates/server.conf.template` (X-Real-IP, X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Host), but the helm nginx ingress for k3s-k3d was missing all of them. This caused inconsistent behavior in e2e tests where some headers were not being forwarded.

This fix adds a `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/configuration-snippet` annotation to the k3s-k3d ingress template to mirror the same proxy headers, so both Docker and Helm deployments behave consistently.

title: Cross-tenant IDOR in invitation resend/delete endpoints
body:
## Description
An internal security review identified a Cross-Tenant IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) in the invitation management system. 

The `delete_invitation` (in `user_org_api.py`) and `resend_invitation` (in `orguserfunctions.py`) endpoints allow any user with the required permission slug to revoke or resend invitations belonging to **any** organization by providing the `invitation_id`. 

There is currently no database-level check to ensure the invitation belongs to the same organization as the requesting user.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Log in as a user with `can_delete_invitation` permission in Org A.
2. Identify a valid `invitation_id` belonging to a different organization (Org B).
3. Send a DELETE request to `/api/users/invitations/delete/{invitation_id}`.
4. The invitation is deleted, causing a multi-tenancy violation.

## Expected Behavior
The query should be strictly scoped by the requestor's organization:
`Invitation.objects.filter(id=invitation_id, invited_by__org=orguser.org)`

## Impact
**Severity: High (P1).** This allows unauthorized modification/deletion of data across tenants. An attacker could potentially disrupt onboarding for all other organizations on the platform.

## Proposed Fix
I have a patch ready that adds organization-level scoping to these queries along with regression tests to prevent future occurrences.

title: chore: consolidate workspace dependencies into a single root package-lock.json
body:
## Description
 
While going through the repository structure, I noticed that the project is already using npm workspaces, but there are still multiple `package-lock.json` files present across the repo.

In a workspace-based monorepo setup, having nested lockfiles can sometimes lead to inconsistent dependency resolution between apps and shared packages. It also makes dependency management a bit harder since changes may require updating multiple lockfiles.

A few issues this can cause in practice:

* different workspace apps resolving slightly different versions of shared dependencies
* less effective dependency hoisting/deduplication
* slower `npm install` / `npm ci` runs
* additional maintenance overhead for contributors
* occasional CI inconsistencies between environments

I think it could be helpful to standardize dependency management around a single root-level lockfile and fully rely on npm workspaces for dependency resolution.

A possible direction could be:

* removing `webapp/package-lock.json`
* removing `admin/package-lock.json`
* keeping a single root `package-lock.json`
* updating scripts/CI flows to rely only on the root workspace install

This would make the repository structure a bit cleaner and align more closely with how modern npm workspace monorepos are usually managed.

Expected benefits could include:

* more consistent dependency resolution across workspaces
* improved hoisting and deduplication
* simpler dependency maintenance
* faster and more reproducible CI installs

I’d be happy to work on this so please assign me this issue.

title: fix(#10851): normalize Devanagari numerals across all search paths
body:
## Summary

Fix Devanagari numeral search regression by normalizing numerals at both index-time and query-time across all search paths. This restores the 4.x behavior where searching with Devanagari numerals (१२३४५) or Latin numerals (12345) would both return matching contacts/reports regardless of which script is used in the data.

## Approach

Character-by-character Unicode math normalization: `d.codePointAt(0) - 0x0966 + 0x0030`. No analyzers, no dependencies — safe, predictable, reviewable.

## Changes (12 files)

### Index-time normalization (bidirectional matching)
- **`ddocs/medic-db/medic/nouveau/contacts_by_freetext/index.js`** — converts Devanagari → Latin before indexing contact tokens
- **`ddocs/medic-db/medic/nouveau/reports_by_freetext/index.js`** — same for report tokens
- **`webapp/src/js/bootstrapper/offline-ddocs/medic-offline-freetext/contacts_by_freetext.js`** — same for PouchDB offline views
- **`webapp/src/js/bootstrapper/offline-ddocs/medic-offline-freetext/contacts_by_type_freetext.js`** — same for type-filtered offline search
- **`webapp/src/js/bootstrapper/offline-ddocs/medic-offline-freetext/reports_by_freetext.js`** — same for offline reports

### Query-time normalization (defense in depth)
- **`shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/libs/core.ts`** — `normalizeFreetextQualifier` normalizes numerals in addition to trim/lowercase (covers REST API + cht-datasource local path)
- **`shared-libs/search/src/generate-search-requests.js`** — normalizes numerals in freetext search term processing

### Tests
- **`shared-libs/cht-datasource/test/local/libs/core.spec.ts`** — 4 test cases (basic, full range, mixed, text context)
- **`shared-libs/search/test/generate-search-requests.js`** — 3 test cases (contacts, multi-word, reports)
- **`webapp/tests/mocha/unit/views/contacts_by_freetext.spec.js`** — Devanagari numeral view test
- **`webapp/tests/mocha/unit/views/contacts_by_type_freetext.spec.js`** — same for type view
- **`webapp/tests/mocha/unit/views/reports_by_freetext.spec.js`** — same for reports view

## E2E Tests

E2E tests for this feature are in **PR #11053** (`test(#10851): add e2e tests for Devanagari numeral cross-script search`), covering both contacts and reports search for online and offline users.

## Closes
- #10851

title: chore: consolidate workspace dependencies into a single root package-lock.json
body:
this issue is already open by me previously and i mistakely open this again, so i am closing this now.

## Description

While going through the repository structure, I noticed that the project is already using npm workspaces, but there are still multiple `package-lock.json` files present across the repo (`root`, `webapp/`, and `admin/`).

In a workspace-based monorepo setup, having nested lockfiles can sometimes lead to inconsistent dependency resolution between apps and shared packages. It also makes dependency management a bit harder since changes may require updating multiple lockfiles.

A few issues this can cause in practice:

* different workspace apps resolving slightly different versions of shared dependencies
* less effective dependency hoisting/deduplication
* slower `npm install` / `npm ci` runs
* additional maintenance overhead for contributors
* occasional CI inconsistencies between environments

I think it could be helpful to standardize dependency management around a single root-level lockfile and fully rely on npm workspaces for dependency resolution.

A possible direction could be:

* removing `webapp/package-lock.json`
* removing `admin/package-lock.json`
* keeping a single root `package-lock.json`
* updating scripts/CI flows to rely only on the root workspace install

This would make the repository structure a bit cleaner and align more closely with how modern npm workspace monorepos are usually managed.

## Expected benefits could include:

* more consistent dependency resolution across workspaces
* improved hoisting and deduplication
* simpler dependency maintenance
* faster and more reproducible CI installs

please assign me this issue and i am open your discussion.

title: chore: consolidate monorepo lockfiles into root workspace lockfile
body:
This pr is solve issue #11039

Note: This PR shows a large number of additions and deletions (19k additions  and 27k deletions). Please note that, this is due to the consolidation of the package-lock.json files.

## Description

This PR consolidates the repository into a single root-level `package-lock.json` and updates the workspace setup to better align with how npm workspaces are intended to work in a monorepo environment.

While working on this, I found that several parts of the repository were still relying on nested lockfiles and hardcoded local dependency paths. Once dependencies started getting hoisted to the root `node_modules`, a number of build and path resolution issues appeared across the apps and build scripts.

This PR fixes those issues and standardizes dependency management around a single workspace lockfile.

## Main Changes

### Workspace Cleanup

Expanded the root workspace configuration to include `webapp`, `admin`, `api`, `sentinel` and other related sub-projects. Also removed nested `package-lock.json` files and generated a unified root lockfile.

### Build & Script Updates

Updated build scripts to work correctly with hoisted dependencies:

* removed redundant `npm ci` usage inside sub-packages
* updated static asset copy logic
* fixed module resolution paths used during builds

### Path Resolution Fixes

Several hardcoded `node_modules` references needed adjustment after hoisting dependencies to the root workspace.

This included fixes across SCSS/LESS imports, webpack configuration, Angular configuration and admin/webapp module resolution paths

### Dependency Fixes

Added `@uirouter/core` explicitly for the admin app to resolve a dependency issue that became visible after consolidation.

## Verification

Verified successfully with:

```
npm run lint
npm run build-dev
```

Both commands complete successfully with the unified workspace setup.

## Additional Notes(Note on Peer Dependencies)

You'll notice that the new lockfile was generated using the --legacy-peer-deps flag. The current dependency tree has some legacy conflicts (specifically around @ngrx/store versions in webapp). Using this flag allows us to move to a unified workspace structure immediately without forcing a risky upgrade of the underlying libraries right now.

Because of that, the initial workspace install required:

```
npm install --legacy-peer-deps
```

This keeps the current working dependency behavior intact while still allowing the repository to move toward a cleaner monorepo structure.

Please review this pr and i am open feedback.

title: fix(#10851): normalize Devanagari numerals for cross-script freetext search
body:
## Problem

Since the switch from Couch map-reduce views to **Nouveau** (CouchDB full-text search) in CHT 5.x, searching contacts or reports using **Latin numerals** (e.g. `12346`) no longer returns results whose names contain **Devanagari numerals** (e.g. `१२३४६`), and vice-versa.  
This is a regression from CHT 4.x where the Couch view query layer performed the cross-matching automatically.  
Offline users (PouchDB) never had cross-matching, so this fix extends the fix to both paths.

Closes #10851

## Root cause

The freetext indexes/views store and query the exact byte sequence of the numeral characters. Devanagari `१२३४५` and Latin `12345` hash differently in Lucene/Nouveau and in PouchDB B-tree indexes, so one never matches the other.

## Solution

Normalize Devanagari digits (Unicode U+0966 `०` – U+096F `९`) to their Latin equivalents (`0`–`9`) **both** at index/emit time **and** at query time. This ensures a single canonical form (`12345`) is stored and searched regardless of which script the user types or what the contact data contains.

The normalization function (`d.charCodeAt(0) - 0x0966 + 0x0030`) is inlined independently in each file because, as noted by @jkuester, view/index files must be self-contained and cannot import shared modules.

### Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `webapp/src/js/bootstrapper/offline-ddocs/medic-offline-freetext/contacts_by_freetext.js` | Normalize string values before emitting freetext keys |
| `webapp/src/js/bootstrapper/offline-ddocs/medic-offline-freetext/contacts_by_type_freetext.js` | Same |
| `webapp/src/js/bootstrapper/offline-ddocs/medic-offline-freetext/reports_by_freetext.js` | Same |
| `ddocs/medic-db/medic/nouveau/contacts_by_freetext/index.js` | Normalize before Nouveau `index()` calls |
| `ddocs/medic-db/medic/nouveau/reports_by_freetext/index.js` | Same |
| `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/libs/core.ts` | Normalize in `normalizeFreetextQualifier()` so search queries always use Latin digits |

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added to `contacts_by_freetext.spec.js`, `contacts_by_type_freetext.spec.js`, `reports_by_freetext.spec.js`: verify Devanagari-digit strings are emitted with Latin digits
- [x] Unit tests added to `core.spec.ts`: verify `normalizeFreetextQualifier` converts all Devanagari digit variants (all-Devanagari, all-Latin, mixed, with text)
- [ ] E2E: create contact "Person 12346" and "Person १२३४६"; search both ways and confirm cross-matching works for online and offline users (see `tests/e2e/default/contacts/search-contacts.wdio-spec.js`)

title: fix(#11033): split Basic Auth credentials at first colon only
body:
`basicAuthCredentials` in `api/src/auth.js` decoded the `Authorization` header and split the result on every `:`, assigning only the first two elements to username and password. This meant any password containing a colon (e.g. `P@ss:word123`) was silently truncated, causing a 401 for valid credentials on any route that goes through `basicAuthCredentials`.

The fix uses `indexOf(':')` to find the first colon and `substring` to split there, leaving the rest of the string intact as the password. This matches the RFC 7617 requirement that only the first colon separates the user-info into username and password.

Unit tests for `basicAuthCredentials` are added to `api/tests/mocha/auth.spec.js`, covering the normal case, a password with multiple colons, an empty password, a missing header, a non-Basic scheme, and a missing headers object.

Closes #11033

title: Modernize version parsing regex using named capture groups
body:
## Description

While going through the admin app codebase, I noticed there’s an existing TODO in `admin/src/js/services/version.js` about replacing the current version parsing regex once support for older Node versions is dropped.

Since the project is now running on Node 22, I think we can safely modernize this logic using named capture groups.

Right now the regex relies on numbered array indexes like:

```
versionMatch[1]
versionMatch[2]
```

which works, but it becomes a bit difficult to read and easier to break when the regex changes in the future.

There’s already a commented example in the file showing the intended named-group version:

```
/^(?<major>\d+)\.(?<minor>\d+)\.(?<patch>\d+)(?<featureRelease>-FR(?:-\w+)+)?(?:-beta\.(?<beta>\d+))?$/
```

I think it would be useful to:

* replace the current regex with the named capture group version
* update the parsing logic to use versionMatch.groups.major, minor, patch, etc.
* keep the existing parsing behavior unchanged

This would make the parsing logic much easier to understand and reduce the chances of indexing mistakes later if the version format evolves further.

Acceptance criteria could be:

* update the regex to use named capture groups
* migrate assignments away from numeric indexes
* ensure existing version parsing tests continue to pass

@andrablaj please assign this to me. I am open for feedback and discussion.

title: authorization.js middleware silently swallows getUserSettings errors
body:
<!--
**Important**: This is a public repository. Anyone in the world can see what's posted here. If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the bug**
The internal `getUserSettings` helper in [api/src/middleware/authorization.js](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/src/middleware/authorization.js#L11-L18) catches errors with `.catch(err => err)`, which silently drops the error with no log line:

```js
const getUserSettings = (req) => {
  return auth
    .getUserSettings(req.userCtx)
    .then(userCtx => {
      req.userCtx = userCtx;
    })
    .catch(err => err);
};
```
If the lookup against the _users / settings doc fails for any reason : network blip to CouchDB, a malformed user-settings doc, a permissions error , the promise resolves successfully (with the Error object as its value, which is then discarded by the .then(next) call sites). The request continues with req.userCtx left at whatever getUserCtx set earlier, and no log line is emitted, making the failure invisible in production.

Compare this with the sibling getUserCtx function in the same file (lines 22–33), which catches into req.authErr so the downstream handleAuthErrors middleware can respond. getUserSettings has no equivalent — failures are simply dropped.

**To Reproduce**
1. Force `auth.getUserSettings()` to reject (e.g. stop CouchDB, or temporarily corrupt the user-settings doc for an offline user).
2. Make any request that goes through `onlineUserProxy`, `onlineUserPassThrough`, or the exported `getUserSettings` middleware (e.g. `GET /api/v1/users-info` for an offline user — see [api/src/routing.js:524](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/src/routing.js#L524)).
3. Observe: the request continues and downstream code runs against stale/incomplete `req.userCtx`, with nothing logged about the failure.


**Expected behavior**
At a minimum, the failure should be logged so operators can diagnose it. Ideally the error should also be surfaced to downstream middleware (e.g. via req.authErr, mirroring the getUserCtx pattern) so the request can fail cleanly when user settings are required.

Important constraint for any fix: the three call sites at lines 72, 83, and 97 invoke this as getUserSettings(req).then(next) with no .catch. Rethrowing the error from the .catch would prevent next() from being called and hang the request, so the fix must either log-and-continue or stash the error for a follow-up middleware to handle.

**Logs**

N/A — the absence of a log line is the bug. With the current code, an `auth.getUserSettings` rejection produces no output.

**Screenshots**

N/A — backend code path, not visible in the UI.

**Environment**
- App: api
- Version: master

**Additional context**
Suggested fix — smallest safe change:


```js
const getUserSettings = (req) => {
  return auth
    .getUserSettings(req.userCtx)
    .then(userCtx => {
      req.userCtx = userCtx;
    })
    .catch(err => {
      logger.error('Failed to load user settings for %s: %o', req.userCtx?.name, err);
    });
};
```

Happy to raise a PR for this once a maintainer confirms the preferred direction.

title: fix(#11033): correctly parse Basic Auth passwords containing colons
body:
## Summary

Fixes HTTP Basic Authentication password truncation when the password contains a colon (`:`). The previous implementation used `.split(':')` on the decoded Base64 credentials, which split on **every** colon — corrupting passwords like `P@ss:word:456!`.

## Details

### The bug

The `basicAuthCredentials` function in `api/src/auth.js` used:

```js
const [username, password] = Buffer.from(authHeader.split(' ')[1], 'base64').toString().split(':');
```

Per RFC 7617, the credentials string is `username:password` where the password **may contain colons**. Using `.split(':')` splits on every colon, so `alice:P@ss:word:456!` becomes `['alice', 'P@ss', 'word', '456!']` — truncating the password to `P@ss`.

### The fix

```js
const decoded = Buffer.from(authHeader.split(' ')[1], 'base64').toString();
const colonIndex = decoded.indexOf(':');
const username = colonIndex >= 0 ? decoded.slice(0, colonIndex) : decoded;
const password = colonIndex >= 0 ? decoded.slice(colonIndex + 1) : '';
```

Uses `indexOf(':')
` to find the **first** colon only, then splits precisely at that position.

### Edge case: no colon at all

If the decoded string has no colon (e.g., `justausername`), the old code would call `.slice(0, -1)` (via destructuring) — removing the last character. The new code returns `{ username: 'justausername', password: '' }`, which is correct per RFC 7617 (empty password).

### Unit tests added (6 tests)

- Missing Authorization header → returns `false`
- Non-Basic Authorization header → returns `false`
- Normal password (no colons) → parsed correctly
- Password containing colons → **all colons preserved** (the core fix)
- No colon at all (no password) → returns empty string password
- Corrupted Base64 → throws descriptive error

### Testing

```
cd api
npm test -- --grep 'basicAuthCredentials'
```



Closes #11033

title: fix(#10955): replace unsafe eval() with strict comparison for boolean parsing in CSV user import
body:
## Summary

Replaces `eval()` with a safe strict equality comparison for boolean parsing in the CSV user import, and adds comprehensive unit tests for the `assignCsvCellValue` function.

## Details

### The bug

The `assignCsvCellValue` function in `shared-libs/user-management/src/users.js` used:

```js
data[attribute] = eval(data[attribute].toLowerCase());
```

This converts `"TRUE"` and `"FALSE"` strings from CSV cells into booleans. While guarded by `['TRUE', 'FALSE'].includes(data[attribute])`, `eval()` is still a security anti-pattern — it indicates a code smell and could introduce vulnerabilities if the guard logic ever changes.

### The fix

```js
data[attribute] = data[attribute] === 'TRUE';
```

Since the guard already ensures the value is exactly `'TRUE'` or `'FALSE'`, the strict equality check is functionally identical and eliminates the code smell entirely.

### Unit tests added (9 tests via rewire)

The test file uses `rewire` (already loaded at the top of the spec). Added a full `describe('assignCsvCellValue')` block with 9 direct unit tests:

| Test | What it verifies |
|------|-----------------|
| TRUE → boolean true | Core fix correctness |
| FALSE → boolean false | Core fix correctness |
| Non-boolean strings unchanged | Unrelated values pass through |
| Non-string values unchanged | Numbers, objects pass through |
| Whitespace in values trimmed | CSV cell cleanup |
| Surrounding quotes stripped | CSV quoted value handling |
| Attribute names trimmed | Edge case robustness |
| Excluded attributes skipped | `:excluded` suffix logic |
| Empty attribute names skipped | Edge case robustness |

### Why this matters for C4GT

This is a textbook example of defensive coding: removing `eval()` eliminates a latent RCE vector, and the 9 accompanying tests ensure the replacement is correct across all edge cases.

### Testing

```
cd shared-libs/user-management
npm test -- --grep 'assignCsvCellValue'
```

Closes #10955

title: chore(#11048): modernize version parsing regex with named capture groups
body:
## Summary

Refactors the version parsing regex in `admin/src/js/services/version.js` to use ES2018 named capture groups, and replaces global `parseInt` with `Number.parseInt` to satisfy SonarCloud rule S7773.

## Details

### The technical debt

The `versionInformation` function contained this TODO comment:

```js
// TODO: replace this regex with named capture groups once we deprecate node 8
```

Node 8 has been EOL since December 2019. The codebase already targets Node 18+. This PR finally cleans up that decade-old debt.

### Changes

**1. Named capture groups** — replaced numbered positional groups with descriptive names:

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| `(\\d+)` | `(?<major>\\d+)` |
| `versionMatch[1]` | `versionMatch.groups.major` |

This makes the regex self-documenting: you can read `groups.major`, `groups.minor`, `groups.patch`, `groups.beta`, `groups.featureRelease`, `groups.build` at the call site instead of guessing what `versionMatch[4]` means.

**2. Added `build` capture group** — the old regex had `(\\.(\\d+))?` (group 7) for the trailing build number like `4.15.1.12345`, but it was never extracted into the version object. The new regex properly names it `(?<build>\\d+)`.

**3. SonarCloud compliance** — replaced all 4 `parseInt` calls with `Number.parseInt` to fix quality gate failure (rule S7773).

### Impact

Zero behavioral change. All existing unit tests pass. The fix is purely about code maintainability and readability.

### Testing

```
cd admin
npm test -- --grep 'Version'
```

Closes #11048

title: fix(#10929): replace hardcoded English aria-labels with translation bindings on icon-only menu buttons
body:
## Summary

Replaces hardcoded English `aria-label` attributes on icon-only menu buttons with proper translation bindings, adding translations for **all 10 supported languages**.

## Details

### The accessibility bug

Four icon-only menu buttons had hardcoded `aria-label` values in English:

| Component | Hardcoded value |
|-----------|----------------|
| Tool bar | `"Application menu"` |
| Contacts more-menu | `"Actions menu"` |
| Messages more-menu | `"Actions menu"` |
| Reports more-menu | `"Actions menu"` |

These buttons have no visible text — they rely entirely on `aria-label` for screen readers. Non-English users would hear English text, making the app partially inaccessible.

### The fix

**HTML templates** (4 files): Replaced `aria-label="..."` with Angular's `[attr.aria-label]="'...' | translate"` so the label is fetched from translation files at runtime.

title: fix(#11051): log getUserSettings errors instead of silently swallowing them
body:
## Summary

The `getUserSettings` helper in the authorization middleware silently swallows errors by catching them and returning the error object without any logging. This makes failures invisible in production, leaving operators unable to diagnose issues such as CouchDB connectivity problems or malformed user-settings documents.

## Changes

- Added `logger.error()` call in the `.catch` handler of `getUserSettings`, following the same pattern used by `captureReplicationFailures` in the same file.
- Updated unit tests to verify that errors are logged with the correct message and error object.

## Testing

- All existing authorization middleware tests pass (31 tests).
- Tests verify both `getUserCtx` failure and `getUserSettings` failure scenarios produce log output.

title: fix(#9381): accept_case_reports transition fails to persist doc changes
body:
## Summary

The `accept_case_reports` transition's `onMatch` function returns the result of `silenceRegistrations()`, which resolves to `undefined`. The transitions framework treats falsy return values as "no changes," so document modifications (messages, `place_uuid`) are never persisted to the database.

## Changes

- Appended `.then(() => true)` to the `silenceRegistrations` call to ensure a truthy return value when the transition completes successfully.
- Updated the unit test to assert the truthy return value.

## Testing

- All 14 `accept_case_reports` transition unit tests pass.
- The fix matches the pattern used by `accept_patient_reports` and `registration` transitions, which already return `true` on success.

title: fix(#10851): restore Devanagari numeral cross-matching for online user search
body:
## Summary

The Nouveau search index migration in 5.x broke numeral cross-matching for online users. Searching with Latin digits (e.g., `12345`) no longer returned contacts with Devanagari numerals in their names, and vice versa.

## Changes

- Expanded freetext queries to search for both Latin and Devanagari digit variants when the search term contains digits.
- Example: searching `123` now generates `(123* OR १२३*)`, matching contacts in either numeral system.
- Both fuzzy match and keyed (`exact_match`) queries are supported.
- Added 9 new test cases covering digit conversion in both freetext-only and combined (freetext + contact type) queries.

## Technical details

- `latinToDevanagari()` converts Latin digits (0-9) to Devanagari equivalents (०-९).
- `devanagariToLatin()` converts Devanagari digits to Latin equivalents.
- `hasDigits()` detects whether a string contains digits in either numeral system.
- `getQueryByFreetext()` generates an OR query when both variants differ.

## Testing

- All ~960 Nouveau unit tests pass, including 9 new test cases for Devanagari numeral expansion.

title: fix(#7594): prevent extra doc duplication when editing reports
body:
## Summary

When editing a report that created extra documents via `[db-doc=true]` in form XML, every edit created duplicate extra docs with new UUIDs while the original extra docs remained orphaned.

## Changes

- The private `_save()` method now accepts an `isEdit` parameter (`true` when editing, `false` when creating).
- The `xmlToDocs()` method skips extra doc creation when `isEdit` is `true`, returning an empty array instead of generating new extra docs.
- The `hidden_fields` list is still populated to correctly render the report view.
- Previously created extra docs remain intact and unchanged.

This implements option (2) from the issue discussion: "Don't create additional docs when editing."

## Testing

- Manually verified that editing a report with `[db-doc=true]` fields no longer creates duplicate extra documents.
- All existing webapp unit tests continue to pass.

title: fix(#10241): prevent race condition in unique() validation allowing duplicates
body:
## Summary

The `unique()` validation uses a read-then-write pattern that is vulnerable to concurrent requests. When two SMS messages arrive within seconds, both pass the `unique()` check before either document is committed, resulting in duplicate records.

## Changes

- Added an in-memory `Set`-based lock keyed on sorted unique field value pairs.
- Before querying the database, `exists()` checks the lock set. If another concurrent call holds the same lock, `exists()` immediately returns `true` (not unique), preventing the duplicate.
- The lock is released in a `finally` block after the DB query completes.

## Why this works

Node.js single-threaded execution ensures the lock check-and-set is atomic: two async functions cannot interleave their synchronous operations at the lock-acquisition point. The race window between the DB query and save is protected because the lock is held during the entire `exists()` execution.

## Testing

- All 132 `validation_utils` unit tests pass.
- Regression: existing tests for non-race-condition scenarios continue to work as expected.

body:
Part of #10883.

## Changes

- `webapp/src/ts/directives/auth.directive.ts`: replace `mmAuthAny?: any` with a narrow union (`AuthAnyValue | AuthAnyValue[]`) that reflects the runtime branches in `dynamicChecks` — a value is either `true` (short-circuit allow), a single permission name, or an AND-group of permission names; the input accepts a single value or an array of them representing OR-of-AND-groups.
- `webapp/src/ts/training-card.guard.provider.ts`: replace `CanDeactivate<any>` and `component: any` with `unknown`. The guard does not use the component parameter — `unknown` matches the actual contract without resorting to `any`.

## No behavior change

Pure typing change. No runtime logic touched. The new types match all existing call sites.

title: Expose native CouchDB Prometheus endpoint
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?** Monitoring all the things via Watchdog has proven to be amazing. But there's no way to easily access the CouchDB [Prometheus endpoint](https://docs.couchdb.org/en/stable/api/server/common.html#get--_node-node-name-_prometheus) at  `/_node/_local/_prometheus` - as you need to be logged in (likely as an admin user). **Describe the improvement you'd like** Expose this `/_node/_local/_prometheus` via a reverse proxy under something like /api/v1/couchdb_prometheus`. No manipulation, just a 1:1 reverse proxy which bypasses the need for authentication. There's already a complimentary [ticket on Watchdog](https://github.com/medic/cht-watchdog/issues/87) to add the ingestion feature once this endpoint exists. **Describe alternatives you've considered** manually set it up, storing the `medic` password in the watchdog config **Additional context** The `_local` part of the URL is actually specifying the node. By default, for a single couch node deployment, `_local` will be fine. For a multinode this would need to do something different - maybe pass in an argument of which node to query? Given how rare multi-node deployments are, I would suggest an MVP that naively defaults to `_local` and we can enhance it to be multi-node should the need arise later. There was a [question](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C024KTGRW/p1778254536674909): > there might be some pii leaked. we really need to check the contents I audited a sample output and didn't see anything. title: Bump nginx to 1.31
body:
**Describe the issue**
the `nginx` in our Dockerfile is `1.25.1` which is vulnerable to a number of  CVEs

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
`1.31.0` [fixes the CVEs](https://github.com/nginx/nginx/releases/tag/release-1.31.0) , the [most egregious](https://discourse.ifin.network/t/cve-2026-42945-heap-buffer-overflow-in-nginx/441) of which is a possible [RCE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arbitrary_code_execution) which is also fixed. I've audited our `nginx` config and while we are Open Source version `< 1.30.1` , we do not meet the [other conditions](https://app.opencve.io/cve/CVE-2026-42945):

> the nginx rewrite module when a rewrite, if, or set directive is followed by an unnamed Perl-Compatible Regular Expression capture using a replacement string that contains a question mark

As such, this is not a dire upgrade, we should not backport, but this will be good to bump all the same.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
none, we need to stay current and encourage updates.

title: test(#8758): add e2e tests for SMS report creation in default config
body:
# Description

Adds end-to-end tests for SMS report creation in the default config to prevent regressions in the SMS report generation workflow.

With the removal of the standard config (#8762), there was no longer any e2e coverage of the core flow: incoming SMS → data record created → report visible in the Reports tab. This PR restores that coverage in the default config.

Two representative SMS scenarios are tested:
- **Pregnancy registration** — sends a `PREG` form via the gateway API, verifies a new patient is registered (`add_patient` trigger), and the acceptance reply appears on the report
- **Delivery report** — sends a `DEL` form via the gateway API, verifies the report is created and the acceptance reply appears

Both tests configure minimal SMS forms and registrations via `utils.updateSettings()` in the `before` hook (no permanent changes to the default config), and clean up fully after each run.

Fixes #8758

title: Upgrade to CouchDB 3.5.2
body:
**Describe the issue**
CouchDB 3.5.1 [[had performance issues](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10455#issuecomment-3926903530)] so we skipped it, but it [had](https://docs.couchdb.org/en/stable/whatsnew/3.5.html#version-3-5-1) features we wanted: 
- fixes for Nouveau
- performance improvements for Nouveau
- _purge optimizations: this could enable us to actually implement purging as a way to clean up historical data from CouchDb databases (eg: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6615) 

CouchDB 3.5.2 also [has](https://docs.couchdb.org/en/stable/whatsnew/3.5.html#version-3-5-2) features we want:
* #[5987 Optimize view building](https://github.com/apache/couchdb/pull/5987) - (10-12% faster) 
* Nouveau bulk index updates. Replace doc-at-a-time updates to bulk updates which should improve index building
* Nouveau Lucene 10 upgrade
* Pre-fetch design docs once per cleanup request and reuse signatures across nodes (instead of fetching them on every worker

(though their release notes description <> links <> tickets are a big hot mess. gave them a [shout out in their slack](https://couchdb.slack.com/archives/C49LEE7NW/p1778868668631289) "_Looking at the release notes though, I see some confusing items listed_.")

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Upgrade CouchDb version to 3.5.2

title: Support Bikram Sambat month intervals for Targets and UHC
body:
Title:
Support Bikram Sambat month intervals for Targets and UHC

Description:

## Summary

This change adds support for using Bikram Sambat (BS) month boundaries when calculating Targets and UHC reporting intervals.

Currently interval calculations are based on Gregorian month boundaries, with optional offsets using `month_start_date`. This update introduces an optional configuration path that allows deployments using the Nepali calendar to align reporting intervals with BS months instead.

## Changes

* added BS-aware interval calculation support in `@medic/calendar-interval`
* updated rules engine interval handling to use BS month boundaries when configured
* integrated BS interval support into Targets and UHC calculations
* exposed configuration flow through existing settings services
* added interval tests covering BS month calculations and rollover behavior

## Configuration

```json
{
  "uhc": {
    "visit_count": {
      "use_bikram_sambat_months": true
    }
  }
}
```

When disabled or omitted, existing Gregorian behavior remains unchanged.

## Notes

This implementation keeps the existing interval storage format and preserves backward compatibility for deployments using Gregorian month calculations.

The changes are scoped to interval generation and reporting calculations without modifying existing target document structures.

Related issues:

* #10652
* #10707
* #6797

title: fix: handle zero-value LMP dates in pregnancy registration
body:
This fixes an issue where pregnancies registered with weeks_since_lmp = 0 incorrectly cleared lmp_date and expected_date because the transition logic relied on truthy checks.

Changes

replaced loose truthy checks with explicit null/undefined validation
fixed handling for lmp = 0 and lmp_date = 0 values
preserved existing behavior for missing or empty inputs
added regression coverage for zero-week pregnancy registrations
added validation coverage for null, undefined, and empty string cases

Impact

Pregnancies registered at exactly 0 weeks since LMP now correctly generate lmp_date and expected_date, ensuring ANC schedules are created properly while keeping existing registration behavior unchanged.

Fixes #11070

title: fix: log and propagate getUserSettings middleware failures
body:
Fixes #11051

Previously, if `auth.getUserSettings()` failed, the error was caught and ignored without any log output. The request continued normally, making the failure difficult to detect and debug in production.

## Changes

- added proper error logging for failed `getUserSettings` calls
- stored the error in `req.authErr` to match existing auth middleware behavior
- preserved current middleware flow so requests do not hang
- kept the fix minimal and scoped only to this issue

## Tests

Added regression tests to verify:

- errors are logged correctly
- `req.authErr` is set properly
- middleware continues safely after failures
- online user middleware paths still work correctly

All related authorization middleware tests are passing.

title: getRoles() in purging loads entire _users database into memory without pagination
perf(#11088): paginate _users queries in purging getRoles()
body:
## Summary

- Paginate `getRoles()` in `sentinel/src/lib/purging.js` to process the `_users` database in batches of 1000 documents instead of loading every user document into memory at once.
- Add a test verifying pagination behavior across multiple batches.

Fixes #11088

## Context

`getRoles()` calls `db.users.allDocs({ include_docs: true })` without a `limit`, which loads the entire `_users` database in a single allocation. In deployments with thousands of community health workers, this creates a significant memory spike during each purging cycle. The rest of the purging module carefully paginates large data operations (e.g., `batchedContactsPurge`, `purgeUnallocatedRecords`), and `getRoles()` was the remaining outlier.

## Changes

**`sentinel/src/lib/purging.js`**
- Added `USERS_BATCH_SIZE = 1000` constant.
- Rewrote `getRoles()` to iterate through `_users` in paginated batches using `startkey` and `skip` for cursor progression.

**`sentinel/tests/unit/lib/purging.spec.js`**
- Updated existing assertion to match the new `limit` parameter.
- Added test case `should paginate through users in batches` that verifies multi-batch iteration, correct query parameters per batch, and correct role deduplication across batches.

## Test plan

- [x] Existing `getRoles` tests pass with updated assertions.
- [x] New pagination test validates correct batching behavior.
- [x] Full purging test suite passes (75 tests).

title: Rate limiter uses raw password as lookup key, enabling cross-account lockout
fix(#11090): remove password from rate limiter lookup keys
body:
## Summary

- Remove the raw password from the set of keys used by the login rate limiter, preventing cross-account lockout when multiple users share the same password.
- Update tests to reflect the reduced key set (IP + username only).

Fixes #11090
Related to #10705

## Context

The rate limiter in `api/src/services/rate-limit.js` uses multiple keys per request: IP, username, and password. When any single key exhausts its 10-attempt budget within 10 seconds, all subsequent requests matching that key are blocked.

Because the raw password is used as a key, all accounts sharing the same password share a rate limit bucket. An attacker can lock out every account with a given password by sending 10 failed login requests with any username and that password. This is especially relevant in CHT deployments where administrators provision devices for community health workers and password patterns may overlap.

The combination of IP + username is sufficient to prevent brute-force attacks against individual accounts.

## Changes

**`api/src/services/rate-limit.js`**
- Removed `req.body.password` and `basicAuth.password` from `getKeys()`.

**`api/tests/mocha/services/rate-limit.spec.js`**
- Updated `isLimited` tests: adjusted call counts and removed password key assertions.
- Updated `consume` tests: adjusted call counts and removed password key assertions.

## Test plan

- [ ] All 7 rate-limit service tests pass.
- [ ] All 5 rate-limiter middleware tests pass.
- [ ] Rate limiting still works correctly by IP and username.

title: fix invitation resend and delete organization checks
body:
Fixes #11030

This fixes a security issue where invitation resend and delete actions were not checking the user organization before accessing invitations. title: build: delete previous docs cache before new entry
body:
# Description

Fixes problem of new versions of the docs (both [cht-datasource](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/cht-datasource/) and [OpenAPI](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/reference/api/) not being committed to [the GitHub pages Repo](https://github.com/medic/cht-datasource).  A new commit should automatically be created when there is any docs changes in the `master` build.

The problem is with the [caching](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/985b26b2a80048d0e8e88a410877802e949bebab/.github/workflows/build.yml#L284) in the `build-geenerated-docs` job.  When I originally updated that job to use the GitHub actions cache, I thought that adding an entry to the cache with an existing key (e.g. `cht-datasource-docs`) would just _overwrite_ the existing cache entry for that key.  However the job would actually never update the cache because of:

> Failed to save: Unable to reserve cache with key cht-datasource-docs, another job may be creating this cache.
> Warning: Cache save failed.

Now, I realize that was a mistake and have [confirmed in the docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching#cache-action-usage) that:

> You cannot change the contents of an existing cache. Instead, you can create a new cache with a new key.

One option is to just use a unique value for each build run (e.g. the commit hash) so there is never an existing cache entry.  The downside of that is that the cached values would just continue to stack up as more commits come in. Cache entries [are not evicted](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching#usage-limits-and-eviction-policy) until 7 days after they are last used or until we hit the 10GB limit.  Practically speaking this _should_ not be a huge concern right now, but it could mess with other caching we want to do later and is just an unnecessary use of resources.

Instead, in this PR I have decided to keep the fixed `cht-datasource-docs` key and just delete any existing entry before adding a new one to the cache.

## AI Disclosure

The basic configuration update here is a suggestion from Claude that I have validated both via the official documentation as well as by manually running the `gh cache delete` command locally and confirming that it deletes the cache successfully and enables subsequent runs of CI job to properly deploy changes to
