title: fix(#11070): setExpectedBirthDate drops expected_date when weeks_since_lmp is 0
body:
## Summary

The `setExpectedBirthDate` function in `registration.js` uses truthy checks (`if (lmpDate)` and `if (lmp)`) to determine whether an LMP date or weeks-since-LMP value was provided. Because JavaScript treats `0` as falsy, a valid `weeks_since_lmp` value of `0` silently causes both `expected_date` and `lmp_date` to be set to `null`.

This is a clinically significant bug: mothers registered at exactly 0 weeks since LMP (just conceived) miss their entire ANC follow-up schedule because no `expected_date` is calculated.

## Root Cause

```javascript
const lmp = getWeeksSinceLMP(doc);
if (lmp) {                          // ← 0 is falsy, this branch is skipped
  start = moment(doc.reported_date).startOf('day');
  start.subtract(lmp, 'weeks');
}

if (!start) {                       // ← start is still undefined
  doc.lmp_date = null;              // ← dates incorrectly nullified
  doc.expected_date = null;
  return;
}
```

## Changes

**Source** (`shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/registration.js`):
- Changed `if (lmpDate)` → `if (lmpDate !== undefined)` (defense in depth for both code paths)
- Changed `if (lmp)` → `if (lmp !== undefined)`
- The `!start` guard is preserved — when neither an LMP date nor weeks_since_lmp is provided, dates are still correctly set to null

**Tests** (`shared-libs/transitions/test/unit/pregnancy_registration.js`):
- Updated `'setExpectedBirthDate sets lmp_date and expected_date to null when lmp 0'` → now asserts correct dates when `weeks_since_lmp = 0`
- Updated `'zero lmp value only registers patient'` to verify both `lmp_date` and `expected_date` are correctly populated

## Testing

```
cd shared-libs/transitions
UNIT_TEST_ENV=1 npx mocha ./test/unit/pregnancy_registration.js
# 26 passing ✓
```

title: Contacts list does not apply fallback sorting when contacts_default_sort is unset
body:
## Describe the bug

When `contacts_default_sort` is not configured, the contacts list does not consistently apply a fallback/default sorting behavior.

The contacts component currently depends on the configured value from `getContactsDefaultSort(settings)`, but when the setting is unset or missing, the list can fall back inconsistently instead of explicitly defaulting to the standard contacts ordering behavior.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Remove or unset `contacts_default_sort` from settings
2. Open the contacts list
3. Observe the contacts ordering behavior

## Expected behavior

The contacts list should apply a stable default sorting behavior even when `contacts_default_sort` is not configured.

## Proposed solution

Apply an explicit fallback/default sort value when `contacts_default_sort` is undefined so the contacts list behavior remains consistent.

title: feat(#9261): add --project-name and --cht-version flags to cht-docker-compose.sh
body:
# Description

Closes #9261.

The `cht-docker-compose.sh` script previously relied entirely on interactive prompts (`read -rp`, `select` menus), making it impossible to use in CI/CD pipelines or scripted workflows. This was the root cause of the `stdin.write('y\n')` workaround in [medic/cht-conf#620](https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/pull/620), which is fragile and breaks any time a prompt is added or removed.

This PR adds two optional flags to the script:

| Flag | Short | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `--project-name NAME` | `-n` | Create or start a named project without interactive prompts |
| `--cht-version VERSION` | `-V` | Specify the CHT version to use (defaults to latest) |

**New non-interactive usage:**
```bash
# Create a new project using the latest CHT version
./cht-docker-compose.sh --project-name myproject

# Create a new project with a specific CHT version
./cht-docker-compose.sh --project-name myproject --cht-version 4.10.0

# Start an existing project by name (skips creation if .env already exists)
./cht-docker-compose.sh --project-name myproject
```

**All 4 existing usage patterns are fully preserved (no breaking changes):**
```bash
./cht-docker-compose.sh                         # interactive (unchanged)
./cht-docker-compose.sh ENV-FILE.env            # start by file (unchanged)
./cht-docker-compose.sh ENV-FILE.env stop       # stop (unchanged)
./cht-docker-compose.sh ENV-FILE.env destroy    # destroy (unchanged)
```

**Implementation details:**
- Argument parsing replaced with a standard `while`/`shift` flag loop; flags must precede any positional `.env` argument (conventional Unix behaviour)
- Project name is sanitized (lowercased, non-alphanumeric chars replaced with `_`) matching the existing interactive behaviour
- If `--project-name` is given and the `.env` already exists, the script skips creation and starts the existing project using its existing `.env`, compose files, and data in `$HOME/.medic/cht-docker/`
- `--help` / `-h` moved into the flag loop and updated to document the new flags
- Unknown flags produce an error message and exit 1

# Code review checklist

- [x] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the [style guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/style-guide/)
- [ ] Documented: Configuration and user documentation on [cht-docs](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/)~~
- [x] Tested: Mocha unit tests added (`scripts/docker-helper/tests/cht-docker-compose.spec.js`); `npm run unit-docker-helper` runs 11 tests covering all new flags and backwards-compatible paths; `npm run lint` passes clean
- [ ] Internationalised~~
- [x] Backwards compatible: All 4 existing positional usage patterns preserved unchanged; existing `.env` files, compose files, and project data directories are read without modification

title: feat(#10973): adding byPhone qualifier
body:
closes #10973 

This PR adds `byPhone` and `byPhones` qualifiers to datasource, and migrates all the callers of `contacts_by_phone` to use datasource.

The migrated callers are listed in the #10973 
- `shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/`: `update_sent_by.js`, `registration.js`, `self_report.js`, `update_clinics.js`
- `shared-libs/validation/src/validation_utils.js`
- `admin/src/js/services/message-queue.js`
- `webapp/src/js/enketo/widgets/phone-widget.js`, `webapp/src/ts/services/integration-api.service.ts`

The diff is a little large, but most of the changed lines are tests.

Some notes:
This is the first qualifier that cannot be combined with other qualifiers.
`contact_type` and `freetext`, the existing qualifiers for contacts, COULD be combined because of the `contacts_by_type_freetext` view.
Phone cannot, and the other qualifiers that we will add will also need similar rules.
So, added some validation around that; one thing to note is that invalid combinations of qualifiers will return 400.
In the target controller, `byContactId` and `byContactIds` also cannot be combined, and it silently picks `byContactId`; so this is not totally consistent, but I think that's a bit different because its the singular/plural version of essentially the same qualifier instead of a totally different parameter.

This qualifier also needs to support multiple (and many) parameters, to have the same behavior as querying the couch view with `keys` instead of a single `key`.

There are multiple ways to do that, this branch adds a second related plural qualifier, `byPhones`, following the precedent of `byContactId`/`byContactIds`, and exposes a second `POST` endpoint where the parameters are sent as a JSON body. This differs from `byContactIds`, where multiple parameters are sent as a comma joined GET parameter; the reason is that for bulk phone lookups, there could be a large number of parameters, where its awkward to send as a comma joined GET parameter. 

It's not consistent with `byContactIds`, so an open question is should that be changed also, or should `byPhones` be implemented differently?
Another options would be to keep the request body but still use GET.

Another thing to note is the `collectUuidsByPhone(s)` helper, which was to get around some oddness in the enketo phone-widget; it can't use `await for` so it needs this helper to convert it to a promise.

There were some somewhat unrelated changes to tests to keep them concise as we add more qualifiers; tests for `byPhone`/`byPhones` are parametrized, which sacrifices some readability for conciseness (otherwise have to duplicate entire tests), and added a helper in `shared-libs/cht-datasource/test/local/contact.spec.ts`: `queryBackends`. title: feat(#10675): add e2e tests for UI Extensions
body:
# Description

Closes https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10675

The main goal of this PR was to add e2e tests.  I ended up needing to fix a few more bugs along the way:

- The app was not properly refreshing for online users when a UI Extension's `.js` file was modified:
    - I updated the changes feed watcher in `app.component.ts` to include UI Extension files (since these are not included in the service worker).
- Changes to online-only extension properties were not being reflected in the app for Online users (even after reloading the app):
    - I updated the `generate-service-worker.js` code in api to include the properties for _all_ extensions (even the online-only ones) in the hash value for the service worker. I think since the `/ui-extensions` endpoint was registered with the service worker glob, the browser was automatically caching the first response from that endpoint even for online users and was not busting the cache on changes to online-only extensions because the service-worker hash was never changing.
- Loading resources in an extension (via the new `getResource` function) was failing for online users when refreshing the page because the extension loaded before the resource cache was warm.
    - I exposed an `init` method on the CustomResourceService so the CHTDatasourceService can wait for the cache to be warm.
- Errors thrown from within the custom web component were not being captured in a feedback doc.
    - I updated the `ui-extensions-tab.component.ts` to listen for these errors and set them in the `console.error` when they come.

## AI disclosure

I worked a lot with Claude on this, going back and forth on the different issues, etc. I have carefully pulled apart all of the code and confirmed it works as expected and does exactly what we want. Everything that is left here has either been heavily modified or reviewed by me.

title: chore(#10224): include docs for Datasource in site
body:
# Description

This is a bit of prep work ahead of #10224 being resolved.  When UI Extensions are released, that will be the official first time these cht-datasource APIs are actually available/useful for external configuration code (since the custom UI Extensions have access to the APIs and can leverage the `async` functionality!  Access to these APIs is provided by injecting the result of [getDatasource](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/cht-datasource/functions/getDatasource.html) into the extensions at `this.cht`.  

However, as you can see by looking at the docs in the link, we do not actually have very clean documentation for the _imperative_ cht-datasource APIs.  The [function-level TS doc](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/ae8f2824e4a06757ceb66defbf01c8abdac8dc61/shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/index.ts#L66) is not even pulled through into the docs site. :disappointed:   This is because we have not really defined the returned "Datasource" as a formal type/interface (but it is just a return type).

The main goal of this PR is to add proper documentation for a `Datasource` interface that gets included in the docs site. This involved several changes:

- I exported a top-level `Datasource` interface to hold the documentation. The `getDatasource` function returns this type.
- For better maintainability, I broke out all the sub-concept levels (person/place/etc) into their own `Datasource` interfaces along with their own internal `getDatasource` functions and moved the code into the related files.  Everything still rolls back up through the top-level `Datasource`, but this is way more maintainable and scalable. 
- Instead of using the README as the ["root" documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/cht-datasource/index.html) for the TSDoc site, I have used the `@packageDocumentation` annotation in the `index.ts` file to make that file's docs the entry-point for the cht-datasource docs site.  
  - This becomes the "public" front for these APIs (with an emphasis on pointing to the `Datasource` interface, which is what most folks care about).
  - The README focus is now on "internal" documentation regarding cht-datasource details that are really only relevant for cht-core developers.
- I made a few minor tweaks to the existing cht-datasource TSDocs to eliminate the existing warnings when generating the docs site (mostly exporting missing base types).
  - I had to make a small change to the `generate-openapi.js` script because the new `Datasource` interface is, of course, not referenced in any of our OpenAPI docs (as expected). The unreferenced schema was causing the OpenAPI json generation to fail.

## AI Disclosure

Claude was super useful for producing/implementing the `Datasource` interfaces. However, if you look at my first commit, you can see that it has all these changes but leaves the unit tests totally untouched (and they still pass). This gave me high confidence that migration was properly executed.

Beyond that, pretty much all of the other minor docs changes, etc are my own doing.

title: Bump nginx to 1.31.1
body:
**Describe the issue**
the `nginx` in our Dockerfile is `1.31.1` which is vulnerable to a  recent  CVE

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
`1.31.1` [fixes the CVE ngx_http_rewrite_module vulnerability CVE-2026-9256](https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000161377)  which is a possible [RCE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arbitrary_code_execution) which is also fixed. Like last [time](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/11075), I've audited our `nginx` config and while we are Open Source version `< 1.31.0` which is vulnerable, we do not meet the requirements:

> a rewrite directive uses a regex pattern with distinct, overlapping Perl-Compatible Regular Expression (PCRE) captures (for example, ^/((.*))$) and a replacement string that references multiple such captures (for example, $1$2) in a redirect or arguments context

Like list time,  this is not a dire upgrade, we should not backport, but this will be good to bump all the same.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
none, we need to stay current and encourage updates.

title: fix(#7594): edit reports without duplicating their extra docs
body:
# Description

Editing a report created with `db-doc="true"` extra-document sections used to duplicate every extra doc on each save. This PR fixes the duplication and adds a policy that lets form authors choose how extra docs behave on edit.
-  Each  `db-doc` child's id is now written into a direct `<_id>` node inside its section, so it serialises into `doc.fields` and recovered on edit.
- **`db-doc-edit` attribute.** New attribute `link | readonly ` lets the form author declare intent, with a safe type-based default: non-contacts default to `link` (the report owns the data), contacts to `readonly` (they have their own editor). Authored via an `instance::db-doc-edit` XLSForm column — no cht-conf change needed.
- Only the fields the parent user changed *this* edit  are overlaid onto the CouchDB document - independent edits and transition-added fields are preserved.

Fixes #7594

- [x] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the [style guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/style-guide/)

- [x] Backwards compatible: Existing reports without a stored `<_id>` still work — their **first** edit duplicates once (no id to recover yet), then stabilises on subsequent edits. No migration. `recreate` reproduces the pre-fix behaviour exactly for forms that want it.

title: build: redact CouchDB sequence strings from logs to prevent secretlint f…
body:
<!--

+ -------------- > type: build|feat|fix|perf|refactor|test|chore

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description
### Fixes: #11117 

We run CouchDB in CI with `debug` mode. This outputs highly detailed logs containing cluster update sequences (`update_seq`). These sequences are long, high-entropy tokens (e.g., `1-g1AAAABXeJz...`) that mimic secret keys and are flagged as false positives (such as Vercel App Refresh Tokens) by the `@secretlint/secretlint-rule-preset-recommend` rules. 

The existing `grep -Ev` drop filter in `scan-logs.sh` does not catch these sequence strings when they are returned in standard REST API JSON responses or within multi-line exception blocks.

This PR introduces an explicit redaction filter for CouchDB sequence strings to resolve these scanner false positives.

## Changes
1. **Log Redaction Filter**: Added a `sed` command in `scripts/ci/scan-logs.sh` to pre-process the logs before they reach `secretlint`. The filter replaces CouchDB update sequence patterns (`seq [0-9]+-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`) with `seq [REDACTED]`.
2. **Unit Testing**: Added a unit test suite in `webapp/tests/mocha/unit/testingtests/secretlintrc.spec.js` to verify that sequence strings are matched and redacted correctly, and that the redacted lines pass security scanning.
3. **Format Compliance**: Handled stylistic line length limits (`@stylistic/max-len`) in the unit test file by splitting long test inputs into concatenated strings.

title: chore: bump axios and appium
body:
Bumps [axios](https://github.com/axios/axios) and [appium](https://github.com/appium/appium/tree/HEAD/packages/appium). These dependencies needed to be updated together. Updates `axios` from 1.13.3 to 1.16.0
Release notes

Sourced from axios's releases.

v1.16.0 — May 2, 2026

This release adds support for the QUERY HTTP method and a new ECONNREFUSED error constant, lands a substantial wave of HTTP, fetch, and XHR adapter bug fixes around redirects, aborts, headers, and timeouts, and welcomes 23 new contributors.

⚠️ Notable Changes

A handful of fixes in this release are either security-adjacent or change observable behaviour. Please review before upgrading:

  • Fetch adapter now enforces maxBodyLength and maxContentLength. These limits were silently ignored on the fetch adapter prior to 1.16.0 — anyone relying on them as a safety net (DoS protection, accidental large uploads) had no protection. (#10795)
  • Proxy requests now preserve user-supplied Host headers. Previously, the proxy path could overwrite a custom Host. Virtual-host-style routing through a proxy will now behave correctly. (#10822)
  • Basic auth credentials embedded in URLs are now URL-decoded. If you have percent-encoded credentials in a URL (e.g. https://user:p%40ss@host), the decoded value is what now goes on the wire. (#10825)
  • parseProtocol now strictly requires a colon in the protocol separator. Strings that loosely parsed as protocols before may no longer match. (#10729)
  • Deprecated unescape() replaced with modern UTF-8 encoding. Non-ASCII URL handling is now spec-correct; consumers depending on legacy unescape() quirks may see different output bytes. (#7378)
  • transformRequest input typing change was reverted. The typing change introduced in #10745 was reverted in #10810 after follow-up review — net behavior is unchanged from 1.15.2. (#10745, #10810)

🚀 New Features

  • QUERY HTTP Method: Added support for the QUERY HTTP method across adapters and type definitions. (#10802)
  • ECONNREFUSED Error Constant: Exposed ECONNREFUSED as a constant on AxiosError so callers can match connection-refused failures without comparing string literals (closes #6485). (#10680)
  • Encode Helper Export: Exported the internal encode helper from buildURL so userland param serializers can reuse the same encoding logic that axios uses internally. (#6897)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • HTTP Adapter — Redirects & Headers: Cleared stale headers when a redirect targets a no-proxy host, fixed the redirect listener chain so listeners no longer stack across hops, restored the missing requestDetails argument on beforeRedirect, preserved user-supplied Host headers when forwarding through a proxy, and properly URL-decoded basic auth credentials. (#10794, #10800, #6241, #10822, #10825)
  • HTTP Adapter — Streams & Timeouts: Preserved the partial response object on AxiosError when a stream is aborted after headers arrive, honoured the timeout option during the connect phase when redirects are disabled, and resolved an unsettled-promise hang when an aborted request was combined with compression and maxRedirects: 0. (#10708, #10819, #7149)
  • Fetch Adapter: Enforced maxBodyLength / maxContentLength in the fetch adapter, set the User-Agent header to match the HTTP adapter, preserved the original abort reason instead of replacing it with a generic error, and deferred global access so importing the module no longer throws a TypeError in restricted environments. (#10795, #10772, #10806, #7260)
  • XHR Adapter: Unsubscribed the cancelToken and AbortSignal listeners on the error, timeout, and abort code paths to prevent leaked subscriptions. (#10787)
  • Error Handling: Attached the parsed response to AxiosError when JSON.parse fails inside dispatchRequest, prevented settle from emitting undefined error codes, and tightened the parseProtocol regex to require a colon in the protocol separator. (#10724, #7276, #10729)
  • Types & Exports: Aligned the CommonJS CancelToken typings with the ESM build, fixed a compiler error caused by RawAxiosHeaders, and re-exported create from the package index. (#7414, #6389, #6460)
  • UTF-8 Encoding: Replaced the deprecated unescape() call with a modern UTF-8 encoding implementation. (#7378)
  • Misc Cleanup: Resolved a batch of small inconsistencies and gadget-level issues across the codebase. (#10833)

🔧 Maintenance & Chores

  • Refactor — ES6 Modernisation: Modernised the utils module and XHR adapter to use ES6 features, and tidied the multipart boundary error message. (#10588, #7419)
  • Tests: Hardened the HTTP test server lifecycle to fix flaky FormData EPIPE failures, fixed Win32 platform support for the pipe tests, and corrected an incorrect test assumption. (#10820, #10791, #10796)
  • Docs: Documented paramsSerializer.encode for strict RFC 3986 query encoding, updated the parseReviver TypeScript definitions and configuration docs for ES2023, added timeout guidance to the README's first async example, and expanded notes around the recent type changes. (#10821, #10782, #10759, #10804)
  • Reverted: Reverted the transformRequest input typing change from #10745 after follow-up review. (#10745, #10810)
  • Dependencies: Bumped actions/setup-node, the github-actions group, and postcss (in /docs) to their latest versions. (#10785, #10813, #10814)
  • Release: Updated changelog and packages, and prepared the 1.16.0 release. (#10790, #10834)

🌟 New Contributors

We are thrilled to welcome our new contributors. Thank you for helping improve axios:

  • @​singhankit001 (#10588)
  • @​cuiweixie (#7419)
  • @​iruizsalinas (#10787)
  • @​MarcosNocetti (#10680)
  • @​deepview-autofix (#10729)

  • Basic auth credentials embedded in URLs are now URL-decoded. If you have percent-encoded credentials in a URL (e.g. https://user:p%40ss@host), the decoded value is what now goes on the wire. (#10825)
  • parseProtocol now strictly requires a colon in the protocol separator. Strings that loosely parsed as protocols before may no longer match. (#10729)
  • Deprecated unescape() replaced with modern UTF-8 encoding. Non-ASCII URL handling is now spec-correct; consumers depending on legacy unescape() quirks may see different output bytes. (#7378)
  • transformRequest input typing change was reverted. The typing change introduced in #10745 was reverted in #10810 after follow-up review — net behavior is unchanged from 1.15.2. (#10745, #10810)

🚀 New Features

  • QUERY HTTP Method: Added support for the QUERY HTTP method across adapters and type definitions. (#10802)
  • ECONNREFUSED Error Constant: Exposed ECONNREFUSED as a constant on AxiosError so callers can match connection-refused failures without comparing string literals (closes #6485). (#10680)
  • Encode Helper Export: Exported the internal encode helper from buildURL so userland param serializers can reuse the same encoding logic that axios uses internally. (#6897)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • HTTP Adapter — Redirects & Headers: Cleared stale headers when a redirect targets a no-proxy host, fixed the redirect listener chain so listeners no longer stack across hops, restored the missing requestDetails argument on beforeRedirect, preserved user-supplied Host headers when forwarding through a proxy, and properly URL-decoded basic auth credentials. (#10794, #10800, #6241, #10822, #10825)
  • HTTP Adapter — Streams & Timeouts: Preserved the partial response object on AxiosError when a stream is aborted after headers arrive, honoured the timeout option during the connect phase when redirects are disabled, and resolved an unsettled-promise hang when an aborted request was combined with compression and maxRedirects: 0. (#10708, #10819, #7149)
  • Fetch Adapter: Enforced maxBodyLength / maxContentLength in the fetch adapter, set the User-Agent header to match the HTTP adapter, preserved the original abort reason instead of replacing it with a generic error, and deferred global access so importing the module no longer throws a TypeError in restricted environments. (#10795, #10772, #10806, #7260)
  • XHR Adapter: Unsubscribed the cancelToken and AbortSignal listeners on the error, timeout, and abort code paths to prevent leaked subscriptions. (#10787)
  • Error Handling: Attached the parsed response to AxiosError when JSON.parse fails inside dispatchRequest, prevented settle from emitting undefined error codes, and tightened the parseProtocol regex to require a colon in the protocol separator. (#10724, #7276, #10729)
  • Types & Exports: Aligned the CommonJS CancelToken typings with the ESM build, fixed a compiler error caused by RawAxiosHeaders, and re-exported create from the package index. (#7414, #6389, #6460)
  • UTF-8 Encoding: Replaced the deprecated unescape() call with a modern UTF-8 encoding implementation. (#7378)
  • Misc Cleanup: Resolved a batch of small inconsistencies and gadget-level issues across the codebase. (#10833)

🔧 Maintenance & Chores

  • Refactor — ES6 Modernisation: Modernised the utils module and XHR adapter to use ES6 features, and tidied the multipart boundary error message. (#10588, #7419)
  • Tests: Hardened the HTTP test server lifecycle to fix flaky FormData EPIPE failures, fixed Win32 platform support for the pipe tests, and corrected an incorrect test assumption. (#10820, #10791, #10796)
  • Docs: Documented paramsSerializer.encode for strict RFC 3986 query encoding, updated the parseReviver TypeScript definitions and configuration docs for ES2023, added timeout guidance to the README's first async example, and expanded notes around the recent type changes. (#10821, #10782, #10759, #10804)

title: Distribute nouveau across all couch nodes in multi-node deployments
body:
In CHT deployments with a multi-node CouchDB cluster, Nouveau runs as a sidecar on **only the first CouchDB node** (`couchdb-1`), and the single `nouveau` Service routes **all** Nouveau traffic to that one node. Search indexing and query load is therefore concentrated on `couchdb-1` instead of being distributed across the cluster.

This is ok for freetext search, which is not important for scaling, but Nouveau is also on the **sync / replication path** 
(`api/src/services/replication/authorization.js`), so a single Nouveau instance becomes a scaling bottleneck failure for sync in deployments that run multi-node CouchDB.

**Current behaviour**

Two pieces of the Helm chart only allow a single `nouveau` container:

1. **`scripts/build/helm/templates/couchdb/deployment.yaml`**  in the  clustered branch the `cht-couchdb-nouveau` sidecar is created only if  `{{- if eq $nodeNumber 1 }}`

2. **`scripts/build/helm/templates/nouveau/service.yaml`** — a single `nouveau` service whose selector is `cht.service: couchdb-1` in clustered mode, so even   if other nodes had a sidecar, traffic would still only reach node 1.

The more difficult blocker is the hard-coded `nouveau` URL baked into the `couchdb` image:

```ini
# couchdb/10-docker-default.ini
[nouveau]
enable = true
url = http://nouveau:5987
```

Because `10-docker-default.ini` is shipped inside the `cht-couchdb` image, every couchdb node points at the single `nouveau` service name, and there is no way currently to point at a separate `nouveau` instance in the same pod.

**Desired behaviour**

- A `cht-couchdb-nouveau` sidecar on **every** couchdb pod
- Each couchdb pod configured with a url pointing to the same nouveau sidecar

**Approaches considered**

| Approach | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| Mount per-node ConfigMap with `[nouveau] url` under `/opt/couchdb/etc/default.d` | most helmish but breaks `entrypoint.sh` |
| initContainer writes `local.d/20-nouveau-url.ini` into the writable PVC |  Worked in testing but a very messy workaround | 
| Make image's `10-docker-default.ini` URL env-driven; chart sets per-node | Not tested yet, would be preferred if possible |

**References**

- Sidecar split: `fix(#10481): set nouveau as a sidecar container (#10482)`
- Hard-coded URL: `couchdb/10-docker-default.ini:48`
- Sidecar gate: `scripts/build/helm/templates/couchdb/deployment.yaml` (`if eq $nodeNumber 1`)
- Service selector: `scripts/build/helm/templates/nouveau/service.yaml` (`cht.service: couchdb-1`)

title: Support for finding users by their oidc_username via /api/v#/users
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The Kenyan CHP Registry acts as an OIDC Provider for the eCHIS Kenya CHT app.
CHA users of the registry have a corresponding user account in eCHIS with matching `oidc_username`. 
The CHA is assigned to N-CHUs (N-facility_ids) in both the registry and eCHIS.
When a CHU is reassigned in the registry, an integration makes it so the CHU is also reassigned in CHT.
One step in the integration is that it needs to find and update users based on their oidc_username.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'm looking for an API endpoint which lets my find or update the user based on their `oidc_username`. /api/vX/users?oidc_username=cha@registry.com

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I'm encoding the oidc_username and manually setting the user's `username` based on it (eg. `cha@registry.com` yields `registry_user_cha_at_registry_dot_com`) and looking up the user by the encoding

**Additional context**
<!-- Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here. -->

title: fix(#10875): sentinel wait for transitions infodoc to be valid
body:
Another attempt to resolve the api/sentinel race.
Add invalid_rev to infodocs for synchronous transitions to mark that transitions are in progress, and the infodoc is not yet valid for that revision.
after transitions are run and the document is saved, the infodoc is saved again, with transitions and with invalid_rev removed.

A previous version also added a valid_rev with explicitly the revision that the infodoc is valid for, but removed it since it's never used; the abscence of an invalid_rev implies that the infodoc is valid for the current revision.
If saving the medic doc fails, it clears invalid_rev from the infodoc to allow retry.

There is no cleanup for other stale infodocs where invalid_rev is never cleared, but this can only happen if there's an error other than 409 saving the infodoc the second time, or if its interrupted between saving the medic doc and the infodoc.

To actually fix the race, if sentinel finds an infodoc with invalid_rev set (doesn't actually use the rev, just the presence of the flag), it waits 100ms and then tries again until the infodoc had invalid_rev removed, for a maximum of 5 times. after 5 retries, it logs an error and continues to the next change without running transitions.

`invalid_rev` is only set by `processDocs` (synchronous changes from api), and only `processChanges` (from sentinel) will wait for it. It also applies only to transitions. This is to avoid adding extra db chatter where it isn't really needed.

A previous commit also add invalid_rev and waiting to `processChanges`, but removed because it does not actually fix anything; sentinel does not support concurrency, and there isn't currently a case where api should wait for sentinel to finish.

Closes #10875

title: feat(#10676): store geolocation when submitting contact forms
body:
# Description

Adds a GPS capture widget for household contact forms.

## Create flow

GPS acquisition starts automatically when the form renders (progress bar with a 30s
timeout).

- **Success** — a home/other context question appears; picking either sets the field to
  `captured` and records the context
- **Failure** (weak signal, timeout, unavailable) — Retry button, plus a "Save without
  location" checkbox the CHW must check to proceed
- **Permission denied** — same checkbox, with a permission-specific message; if the CHW
  grants permission mid-form, the widget recovers into the normal create flow

## Edit flow

When the contact being edited already has a valid `geolocation`, the widget shows a
"Location already saved" badge and a 4-option radio group instead:

1. **Keep**
2. **Change location** (home)
3. **Not at household** (other)
4. **Remove**

GPS starts silently in the background; the two capture options are disabled until it resolves successfully, and are re-disabled (with a revert to Keep if one was selected) on any failure. A CHW is never able to select "capture new" without a live location behind it. Editing a contact with no existing location falls back to the create flow.

## Data written to the contact doc

```json
{
  "geolocation": { "latitude": 1.23, "longitude": 4.56, "accuracy": 10, ... },
  "geolocation_log": [
    { "timestamp": 1234567890000, "recording": { ... }, "is_home": true }
  ]
}
```

`geolocation` is set from a successful *home* capture, cleared on Remove, and left as the
contact's original value for Keep, "not at household" captures, and failed captures.
`geolocation_log` is append-only and carries an `is_home` flag per entry. Report forms are
untouched by this PR. The widget is contact-form only, and the report save path was kept
on its pre-#10676 shape.

## Architecture

Widget logic lives in `household-geolocation-widget.js`, kept UI-only. All doc-mutation
logic was pulled into a new `ContactGeolocationService`, called from `FormService.saveContact()`
via a single `applyGeolocation()` method that unconditionally sets `doc.geolocation` for
each of the widget's four terminal states (kept / skipped / captured-home / captured-other),
regardless of what the submitted form's own fields produced. The contact's pre-edit
`geolocation`/`geolocation_log` are captured once, client-side, at render time (via `dataset`
attributes on the capture input — the same mechanism the widget already used for context) so
save time needs no DB read to restore them.

## AI Disclosure

Claude Code was used extensively throughout this PR: implementing the widget and the
`ContactGeolocationService`, writing unit/integration/e2e tests, running refactors,
and drafting responses to review feedback. I directed
the architecture and design decisions, reviewed and tested every change before committing, and
made the call on tradeoffs. This description was also drafted by Claude Code and edited by me.

Resolves #10676

title: fix(#9491): fail fast with helpful error when nginx container fails to start
body:
# Description

Fixes #9491. This continues the work by @SnehaChaursia in #10816, which became inactive. See that PR for the original description and the full change.

This revision only adds the fixes for the review feedback left on #10816:

- **Detect the port conflict case via `State.Error`** (the issue #9491 scenario). The original check looked only at `Status`, which never catches this case: a failed port bind leaves the container in `created` (not `exited`/`dead`), so the old code burned all 30 retries before a generic timeout fired. Inspecting the full `State` and checking `State.Error` fails fast with the real reason.
- Surface the underlying `docker inspect` error when the container is missing, and include `ExitCode` in failure messages.
- De-duplicate the repeated port hint into a single constant.

title: feat(#6615): adds archiving
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

^--^(#^--^): ^------------^
|     |      |
|     |      + - > subject
|     |
|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: build|feat|fix|perf|refactor|test|chore

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

 # Add document archiving (cold storage)

  Adds an end-to-end archiving pipeline that moves documents out of the `medic` db
  into a new `medic-archive` db, leaving no trace in the changes feed.
  
  Closes #6615

  ## How it works

  - **`POST /api/v1/archive`** (db admins only) accepts a `text/csv` body of doc ids —
    one per line, streamed, capped at 32MB. Ids are split into archive job docs of at
    most 100,000 ids each (stored in `medic-sentinel` with the id list as an attachment),
    so a mid-payload failure leaves already-created jobs queued and retrying is safe.
  - **Sentinel** processes the job queue on a configurable schedule (new `archive`
    settings key: `text_expression`/`cron` plus an optional `duration` bound; unbounded
    when omitted). For each batch it:
    1. copies archivable docs (contacts, reports, tasks, targets) with attachments to
       `medic-archive` (`new_edits: false`),
    2. records an `archived: true` audit entry per doc (`@medic/audit.recordArchiving`),
    3. purges the docs and their sentinel info docs — every leaf revision, including
       conflicts — so archived docs vanish from the changes feed.
    Jobs are resumable via a cursor, record their errors, and are quarantined after 20
    failed attempts instead of blocking the queue. Critical view indexes are re-warmed
    every 10 batches so archiving doesn't outpace the indexers.
  - **Replication** treats archived docs as deletions, so already-synced clients drop
    them on their next sync.

  ## Also in this PR

  - New `@medic/archiving-utils` shared lib (job attachment encode/decode).
  - `MAX_REQUEST_SIZE` and the `archive:` id prefix centralized in `@medic/constants`.
  - Duration parsing centralized in sentinel's `lib/scheduling.js`; reminders now use it.

  ## Testing

  - Unit, integration (api + sentinel schedules), and e2e coverage included.
  - Manually verified on a local instance with 1,000,000 docs: queue drained in ~28
    minutes with zero job errors; verified 0 archived ids remain in the changes feed,
    all info docs purged, and audit entries present for every archived id.

## AI disclosure

Heavily used Claude, especially for testing, verifications, and late-development checks and refactors.

v4.12.22

What's Changed

  • chore: update vitest to v4 and cleanups by @​BlankParticle in honojs/hono#4952
  • fix(mime): specify charset parameter per MIME type instead of mechanical detection by @​renatograsso10 in honojs/hono#4912
  • fix(compress): respect Accept-Encoding when encoding option is set by @​LeSingh1 in honojs/hono#4951
  • fix(deno): echo negotiated WebSocket subprotocol in upgrade response by @​ATOM00blue in honojs/hono#4955
  • feat: add msgpack as a compressible content type by @​na-trium-144 in honojs/hono#4957

New Contributors

  • @​renatograsso10 made their first contribution in honojs/hono#4912
  • @​LeSingh1 made their first contribution in honojs/hono#4951
  • @​ATOM00blue made their first contribution in honojs/hono#4955
  • @​na-trium-144 made their first contribution in honojs/hono#4957

Full Changelog: https://github.com/honojs/hono/compare/v4.12.21...v4.12.22

v4.12.21

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

app.mount() strips mount prefix using undecoded path, causing incorrect routing for percent-encoded paths

Affects: app.mount(). Fixes prefix stripping using the raw URL pathname instead of the decoded path, where percent-encoded characters in the mount prefix or path could cause the prefix to be removed at the wrong position, resulting in the sub-application receiving an incorrect path. GHSA-2gcr-mfcq-wcc3

IP Restriction bypasses static deny rules for non-canonical IPv6

Affects: hono/ip-restriction. Fixes IP address comparison using string equality, where non-canonical IPv6 representations of a denied address — such as compressed forms or hex-notation IPv4-mapped addresses — could bypass static deny rules. GHSA-xrhx-7g5j-rcj5

Cookie helper does not sanitize sameSite and priority, allowing Set-Cookie injection

Affects: hono/cookie. Fixes missing validation of sameSite and priority options against injection characters (;, \r, \n), where user-controlled input passed to either option could inject additional attributes into the Set-Cookie response header. GHSA-3hrh-pfw6-9m5x

JWT middleware accepts any Authorization scheme, not only Bearer

Affects: hono/jwt, hono/jwk. Fixes missing scheme validation in the Authorization header, where any two-part header value was accepted regardless of the scheme name, allowing non-Bearer schemes to pass JWT authentication. GHSA-f577-qrjj-4474

Users who use app.mount(), hono/ip-restriction, hono/cookie, or hono/jwt/hono/jwk are encouraged to upgrade to this version.

body:
Bumps [select2](https://github.com/select2/select2) from 4.0.13 to 4.1.0.
Release notes

Sourced from select2's releases.

Select2 4.1.0

Breaking changes

  • The minimum jQuery version supported is the latest version in the 1.x, 2.x, 3.x, and 4.x series (#5525, #5955)
  • Removed support for legacy Internet Explorer (versions older than IE 11) (#5834)
  • Removed modules deprecated in 4.0.0 (#5815)
    • Removed legacy support for <input /> tags
    • Removed legacy support for initSelection
    • Removed legacy support for query
    • Removed old select2/compat/matcher module
  • Removed undocumented CSS-related options (#5815)
    • Removed dropdownCss option
    • Removed adaptDropdownCss option
    • Removed containerCss option
    • Removed adaptContainerCss option
  • The containerCssClass option has been renamed to selectionCssClass (#5815, #5847)
  • Significant changes to the HTML/CSS for the selection area impacting custom themes (#5842)
  • New CSS classes for the dropdown results to better target highlighted / selected results (#5841)
  • The search box in the selection area for multiple selects has been changed from an <input /> to a <textarea> to support pasting multiple lines (#5806)
  • Change tab key to select the currently highlighted option instead of just closing (#5759)
  • Tags will be highlighted first in the results even if other options have been selected (#5812)

New features / improvements

  • dropdownCssClass and selectionCssClass are now available in all builds of Select2 (#5815)
  • Calls to get the currently selected options are now considerably faster on large datasets (#5775)
  • Selected results in the dropdown should now be properly announced to screen readers (#5841)
  • Significant improvements were made to make the selection area accessible (#5824, #5842, #5916, #5942, #5973)
  • Allow pasting multiple lines into the search field for tokenization (#5806)
  • Add support for jQuery 4.0.0 (#6332)
  • Add originalEvent to close trigger arguments (#6079)

Bug fixes

  • Resize the selection search on close to properly display the placeholder (#5766)
  • Change internal data ID generation to be more unique and prevent conflicts with numeric IDs (#5840)
  • Internet Explorer 11 no longer steals focus of search box while tagging (#5842)

title: feat(#10761): add task count labels and sorting to contacts list
body:
## Description

Adds task count labels to the contacts list for leaf-type places (households), 
similar to how UHC visit counts are displayed. Also enables sorting contacts 
by task count.

### Changes
- `search.service.ts`: Added `getTaskCounts()` method that queries 
  `contacts_by_parent` and `tasks_by_contact` CouchDB views to compute 
  per-household task counts. Wired into `_search()` in parallel with 
  visit date enrichment.
- `contacts.component.ts`: Added `canViewTaskCount()` (gated on 
  `can_view_tasks` permission), `taskCountExtras` flag, 
  `setTaskCountDetails()` (gated on `count_tasks` contact type flag), 
  and `isSortedByTaskCount()`.
- `contacts.component.html`: Added task count badge next to visit count badge.
- `reducers/contacts.ts`: Added `sortByTaskCount` branch to `orderBy()` 
  (descending, alphabetical tiebreak).
- `sort-filter.component.*`: Added `taskCountExtras` input and 
  "By number of tasks" sort option.
- `search-bar.component.*`: Passes `taskCountExtras` through to sort filter.
- `messages-en.properties`: Added `contacts.results.sort.task.count` key.
- `config/default/app_settings.json`: Added `count_tasks: true` to clinic 
  contact type as reference configuration.

### How to enable
1. Set `"count_tasks": true` on the desired leaf-place contact type in 
   app settings.
2. Grant `can_view_tasks` permission to the user role.

Closes #10761

body:

To determine which users fail to replicate, a user needs to cross-check user replication count docs with failure logs and check for the timestamp overlap.

title: Add `byDateRange` qualifier to `Report.v1` (replaces `medic-client/reports_by_date`)
body:
---
title: Add `byDateRange` qualifier to `Report.v1` (replaces `medic-client/reports_by_date`)
type: improvement
priority: medium
domain: data-sync
labels:
  - cht-datasource
  - migration
---

## Description

Replace `db.query('medic-client/reports_by_date', ...)` call sites in cht-core with a typed `byDateRange({from, to, descending?})` qualifier on `Report.v1.getUuidsPage`.

The view implementation:

```javascript
function(doc) {
  if (doc.type === 'data_record' && doc.form) {
    emit([doc.reported_date], doc.reported_date);
  }
}
```

Today's caller in `shared-libs/transitions/src/lib/utils.js:106` uses this view with `start_key`/`end_key` to fetch reports inside a window, sometimes with `descending: true`.

Part of the cht-datasource view→qualifier migration series; pattern established in #10973.

## Technical Context

**Components:**
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/qualifier.ts` — add `DateRangeQualifier`
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/report.ts` — extend `getUuidsPage`'s declarative API
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/report.ts` — add dispatch arm
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/remote/report.ts` — add dispatch arm
- `api/src/controllers/report.js` — new route `GET /api/v1/report/by-date-range?from=&to=&descending=&cursor=&limit=`
- `api/src/routing.js` — wire the route

**Existing References:**
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/report.ts` — pattern for the `getUuidsPage` dispatch arms (already has `isFreetextQualifier` arm)
- PR [#10083](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10083) — added the create/update qualifiers + Local/Remote dispatch. Same pattern as this ticket.

## Requirements

### Adapter Additions

1. **DateRangeQualifier type:**

```typescript
export type DateRangeQualifier = Readonly<{
  from: number;          // epoch ms (inclusive)
  to: number;            // epoch ms (inclusive)
  descending?: boolean;  // default false
}>;
export const byDateRange = (range: { from: number | string; to: number | string; descending?: boolean }): DateRangeQualifier => {
  const fromTs = toEpochMs(range.from);
  const toTs   = toEpochMs(range.to);
  if (Number.isNaN(fromTs) || Number.isNaN(toTs)) {
    throw new InvalidArgumentError(`Invalid date range [${JSON.stringify(range)}].`);
  }
  if (fromTs > toTs) {
    throw new InvalidArgumentError(`from > to in date range [${JSON.stringify(range)}].`);
  }
  return { from: fromTs, to: toTs, descending: !!range.descending };
};
export const isDateRangeQualifier = (q: unknown): q is DateRangeQualifier =>
  isRecord(q) && hasField(q, { name: 'from', type: 'number' }) && hasField(q, { name: 'to', type: 'number' });
```

`toEpochMs` accepts the same formats as `Input.v1.ReportInput.reported_date` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ`, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, or epoch ms), per PR #10083.

2. Extend `Report.v1.getUuidsPage` JSDoc for new qualifier shape.

3. Add dispatch arm to `local/report.ts`:
   - When `isDateRangeQualifier(qualifier)`, query `medic-client/reports_by_date` with `{ start_key: [from], end_key: [to], descending }`
   - When `descending`, swap start/end keys (PouchDB requires `start_key > end_key` when descending)

4. Add dispatch arm to `remote/report.ts` calling the new endpoint.

5. Add API endpoint and wire it.

6. Expose `byDateRange` from cht-datasource's `index.ts` under `Qualifier`.

### Caller Sweeps

| File:line | Today | Replacement |
|---|---|---|
| `shared-libs/transitions/src/lib/utils.js:106` | `db.medic.query('medic-client/reports_by_date', options)` | `Report.v1.getUuidsPage(byDateRange({from, to, descending}), null, limit)` then `Report.v1.get` for hydration |

Re-grep before merging: `grep -rnE "query\(['\"]medic-client/reports_by_date['\"]" webapp/src admin/src shared-libs` to confirm only the listed caller exists.

### Tests

- Unit: `test/qualifier.spec.ts` — `byDateRange` valid/invalid inputs; reject `from > to`; accept string + epoch-ms forms
- Unit: `test/local/report.spec.ts` — both `descending: false` and `descending: true` paths
- Unit: `test/remote/report.spec.ts` — endpoint called with correct query string
- Caller-side: existing transitions tests stay green; add a sinon-spy test asserting expected `Report.v1.*` invocation
- Pagination: walk two cursor pages with `limit: 5` for both directions; cover the edge case `from === to`

## Acceptance Criteria

- `byDateRange` qualifier in `qualifier.ts` with unit tests passing
- Local and Remote adapters dispatch new qualifier with unit tests passing
- `GET /api/v1/report/by-date-range` endpoint returns `{ data, cursor }`
- The transitions caller swapped; `grep` returns zero matches
- `npm run unit-shared-lib` and `npm run unit-api` pass

## Constraints

- Backwards-compatible: existing calls continue unchanged
- No new top-level `Report.v1` method
- Do not relax `Input.v1.*Input._id?: never`
- Sort tie-break is `_id ASC` regardless of `descending` to prevent pagination duplicates when many reports share a `reported_date`. The CouchDB view does not specify tie-break behaviour, so this stricter rule is acceptable.
- Cursor encoding for `descending: true` must encode the direction so the next page continues correctly. Encode as `${reportedDate}|${id}|${direction}` or use opaque base64; document the choice in JSDoc.

## References

- PR #10083 — date format flexibility (string + epoch ms)
- PR #9625 — freetext search pagination discipline
- Pilot: #10973

title: Add `byVerification` qualifier to `Report.v1` (replaces `medic-client/reports_by_verification`)
type: improvement
priority: medium
domain: data-sync
labels:
  - cht-datasource

## Description

Replace `db.query('medic-client/reports_by_verification', ...)` call sites in cht-core with a typed `byVerification(value: boolean | null)` qualifier on `Report.v1.getUuidsPage`. The verification field is tri-valued (`true` = verified, `false` = refuted, `null` = unverified). The qualifier accepts an explicit `null` to ask for unverified reports.

Read `ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/reports_by_verification/map.js` on branch HEAD to confirm the emit-key shape used for each tri-state value.

Part of the cht-datasource view→qualifier migration series; pattern established in #10973.

## Technical Context

**Components:**
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/qualifier.ts` — add `VerificationQualifier`
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/report.ts` — extend `getUuidsPage`'s declarative API
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/report.ts` — add dispatch arm
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/remote/report.ts` — add dispatch arm
- `api/src/controllers/report.js` — new route(s) for tri-state lookup
- `api/src/routing.js` — wire the route(s)

**Existing References:**
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/report.ts` — pattern for the `getUuidsPage` dispatch arms (already has `isFreetextQualifier` arm)
- PR [#10083](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10083) — added the create/update qualifiers + Local/Remote dispatch. Same pattern as this ticket.

## Requirements

### Adapter Additions

1. **VerificationQualifier type:**

```typescript
export type VerificationQualifier = Readonly<{ verification: boolean | null }>;
export const byVerification = (verification: boolean | null): VerificationQualifier => {
  if (typeof verification !== 'boolean' && verification !== null) {
    throw new InvalidArgumentError(`Invalid verification value [${JSON.stringify(verification)}].`);
  }
  return { verification };
};
export const isVerificationQualifier = (q: unknown): q is VerificationQualifier =>
  isRecord(q) &&
  ((typeof (q as { verification?: unknown }).verification === 'boolean') ||
   (q as { verification?: unknown }).verification === null);
```

`undefined` must throw — caller has to be explicit.

2. Extend `Report.v1.getUuidsPage` JSDoc for tri-state qualifier shape.

3. Add dispatch arm to `local/report.ts`:
   - When `isVerificationQualifier(qualifier)`, query `medic-client/reports_by_verification` with appropriate key shape per the view contract (key shape derived from map function — confirm before drafting)

4. Add dispatch arm to `remote/report.ts`. Decide on route shape: either `GET /api/v1/report/by-verification?value=true|false|null` (string-encoded `null` documented), or split into `GET /by-verification/:value` + `GET /by-verification/unverified`. Pick one and document in the controller's JSDoc.

5. Add API endpoint(s) and wire them.

6. Expose `byVerification` from cht-datasource's `index.ts` under `Qualifier`.

### Caller Sweeps

Enumerate via `grep -rnE "query\(['\"]medic-client/reports_by_verification['\"]" webapp/src admin/src shared-libs` before drafting. Replace each with `Report.v1.getUuidsPage(byVerification(value), null, limit)`.

### Tests

- Unit: `test/local/report.spec.ts` — all three values dispatch to the correct view key
- Unit: `test/remote/report.spec.ts` — all three values produce the correct endpoint call
- Caller-side: each modified caller keeps existing tests green
- Pagination: walk two cursor pages with `limit: 5` for at least one value

## Acceptance Criteria

- `byVerification` qualifier in `qualifier.ts` with unit tests covering all three valid values plus invalid inputs
- Local and Remote adapters dispatch new qualifier with unit tests passing
- API endpoint(s) return `{ data, cursor }` for all three values
- All callers swapped; `grep` returns zero matches
- `npm run unit-shared-lib` and `npm run unit-api` pass

## Constraints

- Backwards-compatible: existing calls continue unchanged
- No new top-level `Report.v1` method
- Do not relax `Input.v1.*Input._id?: never`
- Strict boolean-or-null: do not coerce `'true'` strings or `'null'` strings in the qualifier validator
- Document the chosen Remote-adapter URL shape (single endpoint vs. split) in the controller JSDoc so callers know how to encode the `null` case

- PR #9625 — pagination discipline
