title: Add `bySubjects` qualifier to `Report.v1`
body:
---
title: Add a `subjects` qualifier to `Report.v1` (over `medic-client/reports_by_subject`)
type: improvement
priority: medium
domain: data-sync
labels:
  - cht-datasource
  - migration
---

## Description

Add a `bySubjects(subjects)` qualifier to `cht-datasource` so reports can be
looked up by the subject they are about — a shortcode (`patient_id` /
`place_id` / `case_id`) or a UUID (`patient_uuid` / `place_uuid`) — through
`Report.v1.getUuidsPage` / `getUuids` and `Report.v1.getPage` / `getAll`, and
expose it on both existing report endpoints: `?subject=` on
`GET /api/v1/report/uuid` beside `freetext` / `form`, and on
`GET /api/v1/report` beside `ids`.

Scope is the qualifier and the API surface only. The existing
`db.query('medic-client/reports_by_subject', ...)` call sites are **not**
migrated by this ticket: most of them read the matched key off each row,
which no qualifier-based read returns, and each needs a decision of its own.
That work is #11444. No existing read moves onto the new path here.

This ticket follows the recipe established by the pilot, #10973 (PR #11249):
the qualifier is accepted by both the uuid path and the doc path, as
`byPhones` is on `Contact.v1.getUuidsPage` and `Contact.v1.getPage`, and each
endpoint gains a query param rather than a route. `Report.v1.getPage` /
`getAll` widen from `IdsQualifier` to accept it. #11151 (PR #11327, `byForms`)
put its qualifier on the uuid path only; bringing `byForms` onto the doc path
is a follow-up, not this ticket.

A qualifier that works on one path but not the other is a trap a caller only
finds by hitting a 400, and a caller that needs report bodies should not have
to page ids and then re-fetch them by id. That is the reason for the doc path.

The view (`ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/reports_by_subject/map.js`):

```js
function(doc) {
  if (doc.type === 'data_record' && doc.form) {
    var emitField = function(obj, field) {
      if (obj[field]) {
        emit(String(obj[field]), doc.reported_date);
      }
    };

    emitField(doc, 'patient_id');
    emitField(doc, 'place_id');
    emitField(doc, 'case_id');

    if (doc.fields) {
      emitField(doc.fields, 'patient_id');
      emitField(doc.fields, 'place_id');
      emitField(doc.fields, 'case_id');
      emitField(doc.fields, 'patient_uuid');
      emitField(doc.fields, 'place_uuid');
    }
  }
}
```

Translates to: "every report, emitted once per subject-identifying field it
sets, keyed by that field's value as a string." Up to eight rows per report,
and the key is the bare value — a shortcode and a UUID share one key space,
so one qualifier covers both. Because a report is emitted once per field, one
report can match several of the supplied subjects; that is why both adapter
arms dedupe (see Requirements).

## Technical Context

**Components:**
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/qualifier.ts` — add `SubjectsQualifier`,
  `bySubjects`, `isSubjectsQualifier`
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/report.ts` — extend `getUuidsPage` /
  `getUuids` and `getPage` / `getAll`, and the imperative `getDatasource()`
  surface
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/libs/doc.ts` — `queryDocsByKeys` (the
  same helper #11249 adds; whichever lands second reuses it) and a doc-side
  counterpart to `fetchAndFilterIds` that dedupes by `_id`
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/report.ts` — a uuid arm reusing
  `queryDocIdsByKeys` from #11327, and a doc arm on `queryDocsByKeys`
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/remote/report.ts` — `subject` param on both
  routes
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/libs/parameter-validators.ts` — extend
  `assertFreetextOrFormsQualifier`; add an ids-or-subjects assert for the doc
  path
- `api/src/controllers/report.js` — `subject` query param on
  `GET /api/v1/report/uuid` and `GET /api/v1/report`

**Existing References:**
- #10973 / PR [#11249](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/11249) — the
  pilot: the qualifier shape and validation rules, a qualifier on both the
  uuid and doc paths, `queryDocsByKeys`, and the object-shaped-param guard.
- PR [#11327](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/11327) — `byForms` on the
  uuid path: the `queryDocIdsByKeys` helper, the comma-joined param, the
  freetext-first precedence, and the assert-helper extension.

## Requirements

### Qualifier

1. `SubjectsQualifier` in `qualifier.ts`, plural and array-shaped:

   ```ts
   export type SubjectsQualifier = Readonly<{ subjects: [string, ...string[]] }>;
   ```

   `bySubjects(subjects)` dedupes with a `Set` in supplied-key order.
   `isSubjectsQualifier` accepts only a non-empty array of non-blank,
   non-padded strings.

2. Subjects are matched **verbatim**. The view wraps the value in `String()`
   but does no trimming or case-folding, so the qualifier must not either.
   Coercion is the caller's job; do not call `String()` in the validator.

3. A blank or whitespace-padded entry is rejected rather than passed through:
   it can only ever match nothing, so it is an argument error, not a silent
   empty page. An empty array is rejected for the same reason (unlike
   `IdsQualifier`).

4. Shortcodes and UUIDs can be mixed in one call. The qualifier does not know
   or care which kind each entry is; the view does not either.

5. Expose `bySubjects` through the existing `export * as Qualifier` re-export.

6. The `bySubjects` JSDoc says that results are grouped in the order of the
   given subjects, and that paging requires passing them in the same order
   with each cursor. The cursor is a row skip over rows grouped by key, so a
   caller that reorders the subjects between pages gets duplicates and misses
   reports.

### Adapters

7. Local, uuid arm: a dispatch arm in `getUuidsPage`, next to the forms arm.
   The view emits the bare value as the key, so the deduped subjects are the
   `keys` as given — no wrapping, unlike `reports_by_form`'s `[form]`. Query
   through `queryDocIdsByKeys` and `fetchAndFilterIds`, which collapses the
   repeats from a report matching more than one supplied subject so each id
   appears at most once per page. Deduping the keys in a stable order keeps
   the skip cursor meaningful between pages.

8. Local, doc arm: a dispatch arm in `getPage`, next to the ids arm, over the
   same deduped keys through `queryDocsByKeys`. With `include_docs` a report
   matching several of the requested subjects comes back once per match, each
   row carrying the whole doc, so the arm dedupes by `_id` on top of the
   report-type filter, giving each report at most once per page. The uuid and
   doc arms derive their keys from one place so they page the same rows. Ids
   are matched first, so a qualifier satisfying both shapes behaves as before.

9. Deduplication is per page, not across the generator: `getUuids` and
   `getAll` can yield the same report twice if its rows fall on different
   pages. Document that on `getUuids`, `getAll` and the imperative helpers; do
   not try to fix it here.

10. Remote: a `subject` param on the uuid endpoint, comma-joined like `form`,
    and on the doc endpoint, comma-joined like `ids`. Freetext, then form, are
    matched first on the uuid endpoint and ids first on the doc endpoint, so
    existing callers are unchanged.

11. Extend `assertFreetextOrFormsQualifier` to accept the new shape (rename
    accordingly). `getPage` / `getAll` assert an ids-or-subjects qualifier,
    added beside `assertIdsQualifier`, which other callers keep. In both, a
    subject-shaped invalid input gets an `Invalid subjects` message;
    everything else keeps the original error verbatim (`Invalid freetext` /
    `Invalid identifiers`), as #11327 did for forms.

12. `getUuidsPageBySubjects` / `getUuidsBySubjects` next to
    `getUuidsPageByForms`, and `getPageBySubjects` / `getBySubjects` next to
    `getPageByIds`, on the imperative `getDatasource()` surface.

### API

13. A `subject` query param on `GET /api/v1/report/uuid` and on
    `GET /api/v1/report`, accepting a comma-joined list or the parameter
    repeated. No new route and no `routing.js` change. `ids` on
    `GET /api/v1/report` becomes optional.

14. Precedence on `GET /api/v1/report/uuid`: `freetext`, then `form`, then
    `subject`. No qualifier at all keeps throwing the freetext error the
    endpoint has always thrown. Precedence on `GET /api/v1/report`: `ids`,
    then `subject`. With neither, the 400 message changes from
    `Query param ids is required` to
    `Either query param ids or subject is required`; this is the one visible
    change to an existing request and goes in the PR description. Both
    documented in the OpenAPI descriptions.

15. An object-shaped `subject` (`?subject[a]=b`) is rejected with a 400 rather
    than throwing, on both endpoints.

16. The OpenAPI descriptions of both endpoints state that each identifier (or
    report) appears at most once on a page and why.

17. The new `subject` params carry `x-since: 5.4.0`. 5.3.x is cut.

### Tests

- Unit: the qualifier (valid and invalid input — empty array, non-string
  entry, blank, whitespace-padded; mixed shortcodes and UUIDs; dedupe order),
  the local uuid arm including the per-page dedupe, the local doc arm
  including the per-page dedupe with full docs and the cursor landing past
  the rows read rather than the docs kept, the remote adapter on both routes,
  both assert helpers, and the controller for both routes including
  precedence and the 400 cases (empty list, padded, object-shaped).
- API integration, both endpoints: `?subject=`, comma-separated, repeated
  param, mixed shortcode and UUID returned once, `ids` precedence on
  `/report`, the 400 cases (empty, padded, object-shaped, invalid cursor),
  and a three-page cursor walk asserting exact ids and cursors.
- Datasource integration: `getUuidsPage` / `getUuids` and `getPage` /
  `getAll` with `bySubjects`: the page, the generator, non-normalisation, a
  report that sets both `patient_id` and `fields.patient_uuid` queried by
  both values and returned once, and a three-page cursor walk asserting exact
  ids and cursors.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `bySubjects` lands in `qualifier.ts` and is reachable as
  `Qualifier.bySubjects`, with valid and invalid input unit tests passing.
- Local and Remote adapters dispatch the qualifier on both the uuid path and
  the doc path, with adapter-level unit tests passing.
- `GET /api/v1/report/uuid?subject=` returns `{ data, cursor }` matching the
  existing pagination contract, with each id at most once per page.
- `GET /api/v1/report?subject=` returns `{ data, cursor }` of report docs
  matching the existing pagination contract, with each report at most once
  per page.
- `eslint .`, `npm run unit-api` and `npm run unit-shared-lib` pass.

## Constraints

- Backwards-compatible: existing `getUuidsPageByFreetext` /
  `getUuidsPageByForms` / `getPageByIds` calls and `?freetext=` / `?form=` /
  `?ids=` requests continue to work unchanged, including their error
  messages, with the single exception in requirement 14.
- No new top-level method on the `Report.v1` namespace. The qualifier goes on
  the existing `getPage` / `getAll` rather than a new function.
- Do not relax `Input.v1.*Input._id?: never`.
- Do not normalise subjects in the qualifier. The view does not; the
  qualifier must not either.
- Do not chunk the keys inside the adapter. The CouchDB view takes the whole
  `keys` array; a SQLite-backed adapter that needs a parameter limit chunks
  on its own side.
- Do not change the ddoc.
- Do not migrate any existing `reports_by_subject` caller. That is #11444,
  for the reasons in the Description.

## References

**Similar Implementations:**
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/11249 — the pilot: qualifier shape
  and validation rules, both paths, the same helpers
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/11327 — `byForms`: the same uuid
  function, the same endpoint
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/9625 — the pagination-test discipline

**Documentation:**
- `ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/reports_by_subject/map.js`
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/README.md`

title: Add `byForm` qualifier to `Report.v1` (replaces `medic-client/reports_by_form` page query)
body:
---
title: Add `byForm` qualifier to `Report.v1` (replaces `medic-client/reports_by_form` page query)
type: improvement
priority: medium
domain: data-sync
labels:
  - cht-datasource
  - migration
---

## Description

Replace `db.query('medic-client/reports_by_form', ...)` page-query call sites in cht-core with a typed `byForm(formCode)` qualifier on `Report.v1.getUuidsPage`.

Scope is the page query only. Some callers also use this view with `group: true` for counts, or `key: [form], limit: 1` for sampling — those aggregate variants are out of scope and require a different shaped operation (e.g. `Report.v1.countByForm`). They stay on `db.query` until a separate ticket addresses the aggregate API surface.

Part of the cht-datasource view→qualifier migration series; pattern established in #10973.

## Technical Context

**Components:**
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/qualifier.ts` — add `FormQualifier`
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/report.ts` — extend `getUuidsPage`'s declarative API
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/report.ts` — add dispatch arm
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/remote/report.ts` — add dispatch arm
- `api/src/controllers/report.js` — new route `GET /api/v1/report/by-form/:formCode`
- `api/src/routing.js` — wire the route

**Existing References:**
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/report.ts` — pattern for the `getUuidsPage` dispatch arms (already has `isFreetextQualifier` arm)
- PR [#10083](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10083) — added the create/update qualifiers + Local/Remote dispatch. Same pattern as this ticket.

## Requirements

### Adapter Additions

1. **FormQualifier type:**

```typescript
export type FormQualifier = Readonly<{ form: string }>;
export const byForm = (form: string): FormQualifier => {
  if (!isString(form) || form.length === 0) {
    throw new InvalidArgumentError(`Invalid form [${JSON.stringify(form)}].`);
  }
  return { form };
};
export const isFormQualifier = (q: unknown): q is FormQualifier =>
  isRecord(q) && hasField(q, { name: 'form', type: 'string' });
```

The form code is the doc's `form` field (e.g. `pregnancy`, `anc_followup`). Do not normalise.

2. Extend `Report.v1.getUuidsPage` JSDoc for new qualifier shape.

3. Add dispatch arm to `local/report.ts`:
   - When `isFormQualifier(qualifier)`, query `medic-client/reports_by_form` with `key: [qualifier.form]`

4. Add dispatch arm to `remote/report.ts` calling the new endpoint.

5. Add API endpoint and wire it.

6. Expose `byForm` from cht-datasource's `index.ts` under `Qualifier`.

### Caller Sweeps

Audit `grep -rnE "query\(['\"]medic-client/reports_by_form['\"]" webapp/src admin/src shared-libs` before drafting. **Out-of-scope callers** — those passing `group: true` or `reduce: true` or using single-result sampling — stay on `db.query` and are preserved with a comment referencing the follow-up aggregate-API ticket. Only the page-query callers swap to `byForm`.

### Tests

- Unit: `test/qualifier.spec.ts` — `byForm` accepts non-empty strings; rejects empty + non-string
- Unit: `test/local/report.spec.ts` — dispatch arm hits the right view + key
- Unit: `test/remote/report.spec.ts` — endpoint called with correct path
- Caller-side: each modified caller keeps existing tests green
- Pagination: walk two cursor pages with `limit: 5`
- Aggregate-preservation: confirm aggregate callers (if any) are NOT touched by this ticket — `grep -rnE "query\(['\"]medic-client/reports_by_form['\"][^)]*reduce" webapp/src admin/src shared-libs` should return the same matches before and after

## Acceptance Criteria

- `byForm` qualifier in `qualifier.ts` with unit tests passing
- Local and Remote adapters dispatch new qualifier with unit tests passing
- `GET /api/v1/report/by-form/:formCode` endpoint returns `{ data, cursor }`
- Page-query callers swapped; aggregate-query callers explicitly preserved with a comment
- `npm run unit-shared-lib` and `npm run unit-api` pass

## Constraints

- Backwards-compatible: existing calls continue unchanged
- No new top-level `Report.v1` method
- Do not relax `Input.v1.*Input._id?: never`
- Do not normalise the form code
- Aggregate variants (`group: true`, `reduce: true`, `limit: 1` sample) are out of scope. The qualifier-extension pattern doesn't fit count/sample operations — those need narrower operations like `Report.v1.countByForm`. File a follow-up ticket for the aggregate API surface; do not fold it into this ticket.

## References

- PR #10083 — qualifier + dispatch pattern
- PR #9625 — pagination discipline
- Pilot: #10973

title: Add `byPlaces` qualifier to `Report.v1` (replaces `medic-client/reports_by_place`)
body:
---
title: Add `byPlaces` qualifier to `Report.v1` (replaces `medic-client/reports_by_place`)
type: improvement
priority: medium
domain: data-sync
labels:
  - cht-datasource
  - migration
---

## Description

Replace `db.query('medic-client/reports_by_place', ...)` call sites in cht-core with a typed `byPlaces([uuid, ...])` qualifier on `Report.v1.getUuidsPage`. The qualifier means "give me reports whose place hierarchy includes any of these place UUIDs."

The view emits one row per ancestor place in the report contact's parent chain — a hierarchy-walking emit. Read `ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/reports_by_place/map.js` on branch HEAD for the authoritative shape.

Caller-side, the qualifier is flat: caller passes a list of place UUIDs and gets matching reports. Hierarchy walking happens at emit time inside the Local adapter and is invisible to the caller.

Part of the cht-datasource view→qualifier migration series; pattern established in #10973.

## Technical Context

**Components:**
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/qualifier.ts` — add `PlacesQualifier`
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/report.ts` — extend `getUuidsPage`'s declarative API
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/report.ts` — add dispatch arm
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/remote/report.ts` — add dispatch arm
- `api/src/controllers/report.js` — new route `POST /api/v1/report/by-places` (POST because of array body; GET with comma-separated also acceptable, document the choice)
- `api/src/routing.js` — wire the route

**Existing References:**
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/report.ts` — pattern for the `getUuidsPage` dispatch arms (already has `isFreetextQualifier` arm)
- PR [#10083](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10083) — added the create/update qualifiers + Local/Remote dispatch. Same pattern as this ticket.

## Requirements

### Adapter Additions

1. **PlacesQualifier type:**

```typescript
export type PlacesQualifier = Readonly<{ places: ReadonlyArray<string> }>;
export const byPlaces = (places: string[]): PlacesQualifier => {
  if (!Array.isArray(places) || places.length === 0) {
    throw new InvalidArgumentError(`Invalid places [${JSON.stringify(places)}].`);
  }
  for (const p of places) {
    if (!isString(p) || p.length === 0) {
      throw new InvalidArgumentError(`Invalid place UUID in array [${JSON.stringify(p)}].`);
    }
  }
  return { places: Object.freeze([...places]) };
};
export const isPlacesQualifier = (q: unknown): q is PlacesQualifier =>
  isRecord(q) && Array.isArray((q as { places?: unknown }).places);
```

2. Extend `Report.v1.getUuidsPage` JSDoc for new qualifier shape.

3. Add dispatch arm to `local/report.ts`:
   - When `isPlacesQualifier(qualifier)`, query `medic-client/reports_by_place` with `keys: qualifier.places`
   - Result `_id` set MUST be deduplicated (a report may match multiple ancestor places); document in JSDoc

4. Add dispatch arm to `remote/report.ts` calling the new endpoint.

5. Add API endpoint and wire it. Document the URL shape choice in the controller's JSDoc.

6. Expose `byPlaces` from cht-datasource's `index.ts` under `Qualifier`.

### Caller Sweeps

Audit `grep -rnE "query\(['\"]medic-client/reports_by_place['\"]" webapp/src admin/src shared-libs` before drafting. Replace each with `Report.v1.getUuidsPage(byPlaces([...]), null, limit)`.

### Tests

- Unit: `test/qualifier.spec.ts` — `byPlaces` rejects empty array, non-string elements; accepts valid arrays; verify result is frozen
- Unit: `test/local/report.spec.ts` — dispatch arm hits the right view; result `_id` set is deduplicated
- Unit: `test/remote/report.spec.ts` — endpoint called with correct body/query
- Caller-side: each modified caller keeps existing tests green
- Pagination: walk two cursor pages with `limit: 5`
- Hierarchy depth: include a fixture where a report's contact is at depth N inside one of the queried places — confirm it appears in the result set

## Acceptance Criteria

- `byPlaces` qualifier in `qualifier.ts` with unit tests passing
- Local and Remote adapters dispatch new qualifier with unit tests passing
- API endpoint returns `{ data, cursor }`
- All callers swapped; `grep` returns zero matches
- Result `_id` set is deduplicated
- `npm run unit-shared-lib` and `npm run unit-api` pass

## Constraints

- Backwards-compatible: existing calls continue unchanged
- No new top-level `Report.v1` method
- Do not relax `Input.v1.*Input._id?: never`
- Result `_id` set MUST be deduplicated. The CouchDB view emits multiple rows per report (one per ancestor place); `Page<string>.data` must contain each `_id` at most once.

## References

- PR #10083 — qualifier + dispatch pattern
- PR #9625 — pagination discipline
- Pilot: #10973

title: Nouveau requests timeout after 30 seconds
body:
<!--
**Important**: This is a public repository. Anyone in the world can see what's posted here. If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the bug**
CouchDb version 3.5.0 connects to Nouveau using `ibrowse` library. 
https://github.com/apache/couchdb/blame/020a52c765105cfdb36c084b41fae060d3554030/src/nouveau/src/nouveau_api.erl#L323

Ibrowse default timeout is 30s: https://github.com/cmullaparthi/ibrowse/blob/master/src/ibrowse.erl#L335
https://github.com/cmullaparthi/ibrowse/blob/master/src/ibrowse.erl#L618

If the timeout is exceeded, CouchDb just logs a `notice` and fails the request with:
```
{ error: 'unknown_error', reason: 'req_timedout' }
```
CouchDb Logs show: 
```
[notice] 2026-06-08T00:00:30.990758Z couchdb@127.0.0.1 <0.140288108.5> 2eaa86ef85 haproxy.<server>:5984 10.42.1.56 medic POST /medic/_design/medic/_nouveau/docs_by_replication_key 500 ok 30009
```

To Reproduce (not verified yet).
1. Launch CHT in a very small server or reduce the CPU through compose capabilities.  
2. Make a relatively large Nouveau Query. 
4. See error

**Expected behavior**
Requests should not timeout. 

**Workaround**
This means that the only way to fix this is to make smaller requests.

**Environment**
- Instance: production
- App: Nouveau
- Version: 5.0.0+

**Additional context**
I found this when checking purging status on a 5.0.1 instance. Purging had been failing consistently with the same error.

title: Bump bikram-sambat to 1.8.1
body:
There was an issue in bikram-sambat library which generates wrong Bikram sambat date for certain dates as reported in medic/bikram-sambat#31

Without this, currently CHT gives wrong expected date of delivery in Bikram sambat to end users and this impacts all Nepal instances plus any instances using bikram-sambat calendar.

title: Use latest bikram-sambat release (1.8.1)
body: **Describe the bug** We use [bikram-sambat](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bikram-sambat) and [bikram-sambat-bootstrap](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bikram-sambat-bootstrap) packages to convert dates between Gregorian and Bikram Sambat. Recently, a new version of `bikram-sambat` has been released that fixes some incorrect days in the current year (2083 BS): - https://github.com/medic/bikram-sambat/pull/32 We need to use it so that CHT users do not get the wrong dates in the date calculations (such as EDD) and also in the UI. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Go to https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/bikram-sambat/ 2. Input the date: - Day: 1 - Month: 7 (कार्तिक) - Year: 2083 3. Output date in Gregorian is: `2026-10-17` **Expected behavior** The date should be `2026-10-18`. Sources: - https://nepalipatro.com.np/en/calendar/bs/2083-07-01 - https://english.hamropatro.com/date/2083-7-1 **Logs** N/A **Screenshots** **Environment** - Instance: Any - Browser: Any - Client platform: Any - App: webapp - Version: all **Additional context** Since the current year is affected, we need to correct it soon. Similar to: - https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9842

title: Allow single,  summarizing  notification
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
We shipped [Android notifications](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9255) in [5.1](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/releases/5_1_0/#android-notifications). This fires an alert per task.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Instead of firing one alert per task, offer the ability to fire just one summarizing the notifications.  Something like "You have 30 vaccinations due today"

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Deal with existing limit of only showing ~8 alerts in the pull down menu, with the rest queued up behind those.

**Additional context**
 In Nepal, they're looking at using the feature, but want a way to handle many dozens of notifications (eg 30 vaccination tasks due today). This would compliment the [alert by type ticket](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/11160) nicely

title: Allow alerts by task type
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
We shipped [Android notifications](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9255) in [5.1](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/releases/5_1_0/#android-notifications). This fires an alert per task, no matter what the task type.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Instead of firing one alert per task no matter the type, offer the ability to fire alerts for only certain task types

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Dealing with a single stream of notifications, regardless of type 

**Additional context**
In Nepal, they're looking at using the feature, but want a way to handle many dozens of notifications (eg 30 vaccination tasks due today), and being able to limit which ones alert would be helpful.  This would compliment the [alert summary ticket](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/11159) nicely.

title: Enable deep link from alerts to tasks by type
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
We shipped [Android notifications](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9255) in [5.1](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/releases/5_1_0/#android-notifications). When a user clicks the pull down menu for the alert, they're taken to list of all tasks.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
5.1 also delivered the feature of [task filters](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/releases/5_1_0/#task-filtering-gui). It would be really helpful if when you clicked an alert, you went to the list of tasks filtered by the type of task you clicked.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Deal with the big list of all tasks

**Additional context**
In Nepal, they're looking at using the feature, but want a way to handle many dozens of notifications (eg 30 vaccination tasks due today), and being able go to a specific type of tasks would be helpful. This would compliment the [alert summary](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/11159) and [alert by type](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/11160) tickets nicely.

title: feat(#10626): add recursive contact hierarchy delete service
body:
## Summary

First slice of the delete endpoint for #10706 (sub-issue #10626). Adds the core service that recursively deletes a contact, all of its descendant contacts, and all reports for which any of those contacts is the subject.

Faithful port of `cht-conf`'s `delete-hierarchy.js`, adapted to write directly to CouchDB instead of staging documents to disk:

- Subtree fetched via `medic/contacts_by_depth` (`{ key: [id] }`, tombstone-filtered), matching cht-conf's `getContactWithDescendants`.
- Subject reports fetched via `medic-client/reports_by_subject`, keyed by each contact's uuid and shortcode (the view indexes both).
- Documents marked `_deleted` and written via `bulkDocs` in batches of 100; per-document errors are surfaced in the result rather than swallowed.
- Pre-flight size guard: hierarchies larger than 5,000 contacts are rejected with a clear message, to avoid silently exceeding the HTTP gateway timeout on very large subtrees. The service is kept separate from any transport concern so an async/queued path can be layered on later without changing this logic.

No new CouchDB views.

## Scope

Service layer and unit tests only. Wiring (controller, route, OpenAPI) and integration tests follow in separate PRs. Two deliberate enhancements over the cht-conf reference (clearing a deleted primary contact's parent reference, and removing reports authored by deleted contacts) are also split into their own PRs so each can be reviewed independently.

## Files

- `api/src/services/contact-hierarchy.js`
- `api/tests/mocha/services/contact-hierarchy.spec.js` (8 unit tests)

title: Inject user data into UI Extension
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
The UI Extensions Tab component [currently injects](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/0c3087069d45dad4322a7a5f6c80e5d5bf4ddc97/webapp/src/ts/modules/ui-extensions/ui-extensions-tab.component.ts#L106) several `inputs` properties when bootstrapping a new UI Extension (including the `userContactSummary`). However, it would be useful + convenient to include a `user` property that contains the current user's `user-settings` doc (just like the [`inputs/user` data](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/forms/configuring/form-inputs/#user-data) provided for forms.  

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

Inject the `user-settings` doc as `input.user`.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Require that any data about the current user be loaded from the cookie or the user's contact-summary.  It is not very convenient, for example, when you just want to get the current username....

**Additional context**

This was scoped out of the original UI Extension work, but has [again come up](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10224#issuecomment-4678911383) as development begins on actual extensions.

title: fix(#8011): prevent BS date conversion when month is not selected
body:
# Description

The Bikram Sambat date picker widget converted dates even when the user hadn't selected a month. Since the month field is `type="hidden"` and only receives a value when the user clicks the dropdown, typing into the day or year fields triggered `bikram_sambat_bs.initListeners()` conversion with an empty month - which defaulted to Baisakh (month 1), silently saving an incorrect date.

This PR adds a guard that checks all three fields (day, month, year) are filled before allowing conversion to proceed. If any field is missing, the Gregorian output is cleared.

Fixes #8011

title: feat(#10626): clear deleted contact's parent reference on delete
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #11163 (the core delete service). This handles one extra case: when the contact being deleted is the primary contact of a place that isn't itself being deleted, clear that place's `contact` field so it doesn't end up pointing at a deleted doc.

It uses `updateParentContacts` from `@medic/bulk-docs-utils` (set up the same way as in `api/src/services/replication/bulk-docs.js`), and skips any parent that's also in the delete set so nothing gets written twice.

This sits on top of #11163, so the diff here currently includes that commit too. The new work is just the second commit.

One thing worth flagging: cht-conf's `delete-hierarchy.js` doesn't clear parent references, so this goes a little beyond the reference behaviour. I added it so a place isn't left pointing at a contact that no longer exists, but happy to drop it if you'd rather stay closer to cht-conf.

title: chore: bump esbuild and tsx
body:
Bumps [esbuild](https://github.com/evanw/esbuild) and [tsx](https://github.com/privatenumber/tsx). These dependencies needed to be updated together. Updates `esbuild` from 0.25.3 to 0.28.1
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.1

  • Disallow \ in local development server HTTP requests (GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)

    This release fixes a security issue where HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server could traverse outside of the serve directory on Windows using a \ backslash character. It happened due to the use of Go's path.Clean() function, which only handles Unix-style / characters. HTTP requests with paths containing \ are no longer allowed.

    Thanks to @​dellalibera for reporting this issue.

  • Add integrity checks to the Deno API (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr)

    The previous release of esbuild added integrity checks to esbuild's npm install script. This release also adds integrity checks to esbuild's Deno install script. Now esbuild's Deno API will also fail with an error if the downloaded esbuild binary contains something other than the expected content.

    Note that esbuild's Deno API installs from registry.npmjs.org by default, but allows the NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY environment variable to override this with a custom package registry. This change means that the esbuild executable served by NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY must now match the expected content.

    Thanks to @​sondt99 for reporting this issue.

  • Avoid inlining using and await using declarations (#4482)

    Previously esbuild's minifier sometimes incorrectly inlined using and await using declarations into subsequent uses of that declaration, which then fails to dispose of the resource correctly. This bug happened because inlining was done for let and const declarations by avoiding doing it for var declarations, which no longer worked when more declaration types were added. Here's an example:

    // Original code
{
  using x = new Resource()
  x.activate()
}

    // Old output (with --minify)
    
new Resource().activate();
    

    // New output (with --minify)
    
{using e=new Resource;e.activate()}

  • Fix module evaluation when an error is thrown (#4461, #4467)

    If an error is thrown during module evaluation, esbuild previously didn't preserve the state of the module for subsequent module references. This was observable if import() or require() is used to import a module multiple times. The thrown error is supposed to be thrown by every call to import() or require(), not just the first. With this release, esbuild will now throw the same error every time you call import() or require() on a module that throws during its evaluation.

  • Fix some edge cases around the new operator (#4477)

    Previously esbuild incorrectly printed certain edge cases involving complex expressions inside the target of a new expression (specifically an optional chain and/or a tagged template literal). The generated code for the new target was not correctly wrapped with parentheses, and either contained a syntax error or had different semantics. These edge cases have been fixed so that they now correctly wrap the new target in parentheses. Here is an example of some affected code:

    // Original code
new (foo()`bar`)()
new (foo()?.bar)()

    // Old output
    
new foo()bar();
    
new (foo())?.bar();

Changelog: 2025

This changelog documents all esbuild versions published in the year 2025 (versions 0.25.0 through 0.27.2).

    Previously the specification for package.json disallowed import path specifiers starting with #/, but this restriction has recently been relaxed and support for it is being added across the JavaScript ecosystem. One use case is using it for a wildcard pattern such as mapping #/* to ./src/* (previously you had to use another character such as #_* instead, which was more confusing). There is some more context in nodejs/node#49182.

title: feat(#10626): add DELETE /api/v1/contact/:uuid endpoint
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #11163 and #11167. This adds the HTTP layer for the delete service: `DELETE /api/v1/contact/:uuid`.

By default, deleting a contact that still has children is rejected with a 400, so a single call can't wipe out a whole branch of the hierarchy by accident. Pass `?recursive=true` to delete the contact along with its descendants and the reports they're the subject of. An unknown id returns 404. The endpoint is online-only and gated on `can_delete_contacts` or `can_edit`.

The `recursive` option on the service lives in this PR rather than #11163, since it only matters once there's a transport in front of it deciding whether a recursive delete is allowed.

This sits on top of #11163 and #11167.

## Changes

- `api/src/controllers/contact.js` (delete handler + OpenAPI annotation)
- `api/src/routing.js` (route registration)
- `api/src/services/contact-hierarchy.js` (recursive option)

title: Add document-returning `getPage` / `getAll` to `Contact.v1` and `Report.v1`
body:
## Description

`Contact.v1` and `Report.v1` currently expose only **ID-returning** paginated queries
(`getUuidsPage` / `getUuids`) plus **single-document** lookups (`get` / `getWithLineage`). There is
no qualifier-driven method that returns a *page of documents*. The only document-returning paginated
methods in cht-datasource live on the typed nouns `Person.v1` / `Place.v1` (`getPage` / `getAll`),
and those accept `byContactType` **only**.

This is a blocker for the view→qualifier migration series. Any existing `db.query(view, { include_docs:
true })` call that returns **many** documents keyed by something other than contact-type
(e.g. contacts by phone/freetext, reports by freetext) has no one-shot datasource equivalent today —
it would have to migrate to `getUuids(qualifier)` followed by a per-ID `get`, i.e. an **N+1**. That is
not acceptable for bulk call sites.

This ticket adds document-returning `getPage` / `getAll` to `Contact.v1` and `Report.v1`, accepting
the **same qualifier union** as their existing `getUuidsPage`, so a bulk `include_docs` view call
migrates to a single paginated call. It is a **prerequisite** for the doc-returning view migrations;
it does not itself sweep any callers.

**Components:**
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/contact.ts` — add `getPage` (paginated) + `getAll` (generator),
  accepting `ContactGetUuidsQualifier`, returning `Page<v1.Contact>` / `AsyncGenerator<v1.Contact>`
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/report.ts` — same, accepting the report freetext qualifier,
  returning `Page<v1.Report>`
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/contact.ts` — `getPage` dispatch reusing the views already
  used by `getUuidsPage`, doc-returning
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/report.ts` — `getPage` dispatch
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/libs/doc.ts` — add `queryDocsByKeys` (doc-returning sibling
  of the existing `queryDocIdsByKeys`)
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/remote/contact.ts` / `remote/report.ts` — `getPage` calling the new
  endpoints
- `api/src/controllers/contact.js` / `report.js` — new doc-page handlers, reusing the existing
  declarative qualifier table
- `api/src/routing.js` — wire `GET /api/v1/contact` and `GET /api/v1/report`

**Existing References:**
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/person.ts:78,113` — `getPage` / `getAll` pattern to mirror
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/person.ts:90` — local `getPage`: a single `include_docs`
  view query (`queryDocsByKey`) + `fetchAndFilter`. No N+1.
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/libs/doc.ts:82` (`queryDocsByKey`), `:23` (`getDocsByIds`,
  bulk `allDocs`), `:135` (`queryDocIdsByKeys` — the ID sibling of the helper to add), `:152`
  (`fetchAndFilter`)
- `api/src/routing.js:660,735` — `GET /api/v1/place` / `GET /api/v1/person` → `getAll` doc-page
  endpoints (the precedent; bare `/api/v1/contact` and `/api/v1/report` GET are currently unused)
- PR for #10973 — added `queryDocIdsByKeys` and the declarative qualifier table in
  `api/src/controllers/contact.js`

## Requirements

### Datasource additions

1. **`Contact.v1.getPage` / `getAll`** mirroring `Person.v1` (`contact.ts`), but typed to the contact
   qualifier union and the `v1.Contact` (person-or-place) return shape:

```typescript
export const getPage = (context: DataContext): typeof curriedFn => {
  assertDataContext(context);
  const fn = adapt(context, Local.Contact.v1.getPage, Remote.Contact.v1.getPage);

  const curriedFn = async (
    qualifier: ContactGetUuidsQualifier,
    cursor: Nullable<string> = null,
    limit: number | `${number}` = DEFAULT_DOCS_PAGE_LIMIT
  ): Promise<Page<v1.Contact>> => {
    assertCursor(cursor);
    assertLimit(limit);
    assertContactGetUuidsQualifier(qualifier);
    return fn(qualifier, cursor, Number(limit));
  };
  return curriedFn;
};
// getAll wraps getPage via getPagedGenerator, exactly like person.ts:113
```

2. **`Report.v1.getPage` / `getAll`** — same shape, report freetext qualifier, `Page<v1.Report>`.

3. **`queryDocsByKeys`** in `local/libs/doc.ts` — doc-returning sibling of `queryDocIdsByKeys`:

```typescript
export const queryDocsByKeys = (
  db: PouchDB.Database<Doc>,
  view: string
) => async (
  keys: unknown[],
  limit: number,
  skip: number
): Promise<Nullable<Doc>[]> => queryDocs(db, view, { include_docs: true, reduce: false, keys, limit, skip });
```

4. **Local dispatch** (`local/contact.ts`), reusing the same views as `getUuidsPage`:
   - `isContactTypeQualifier` / `isPhoneQualifier` → `queryDocsByKey` + `fetchAndFilter(isContact)`
     — single query.
   - `isPhonesQualifier` → `queryDocsByKeys` + `fetchAndFilter(isContact)` — single query.
   - freetext → nouveau/offline returns **IDs** (no doc shortcut), so hydrate the page's IDs with the
     existing `getDocsByIds` (one batched `allDocs`). Bounded to one extra batched call per page —
     **not** N+1 — and the nouveau cursor passes through unchanged.

5. **Remote dispatch** (`remote/contact.ts` / `remote/report.ts`) — `getPage` calling the new
   doc-page endpoints with the same query-param serialization used by the ID-page (incl. the
   comma-joined `phones`).

6. **API endpoints** — `GET /api/v1/contact` and `GET /api/v1/report` returning `{ data, cursor }`
   pages of documents. The contact handler reuses the existing declarative qualifier table so
   validation / mutual-exclusion stays single-sourced. Wire in `routing.js`.

7. Expose convenience methods on the `Contact.v1` / `Report.v1` `Datasource` interfaces
   (e.g. `getPageByType` / `getByType`, `getPageByFreetext` / `getByFreetext`, `getPageByPhone`, …)
   following the existing naming.

### Tests

- Unit: `test/local/contact.spec.ts` / `test/local/report.spec.ts` — each `getPage` dispatch arm hits
  the right view with `include_docs: true` and the right key(s); freetext arm hydrates via
  `getDocsByIds`.
- Unit: `test/remote/contact.spec.ts` / `test/remote/report.spec.ts` — endpoints called with correct
  path/params.
- Unit: `test/contact.spec.ts` / `test/report.spec.ts` — `getPage` asserts cursor/limit, `getAll`
  drains pages.
- Controller: `api/tests/mocha/controllers/{contact,report}.spec.js` — doc-page handler builds the
  qualifier from the table and returns the page.
- Integration: `tests/integration/api/controllers/{contact,report}.spec.js` — walk two cursor pages
  with `limit: 5` for a type and a freetext query.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `Contact.v1.getPage` / `getAll` and `Report.v1.getPage` / `getAll` accept the same qualifiers as
  their `getUuidsPage` and return documents, with unit tests passing.
- Local adapters resolve each page in a single view query (type/phone) or one query + one batched
  `allDocs` hydrate (freetext) — **no per-document fetch**.
- `GET /api/v1/contact` and `GET /api/v1/report` return `{ data, cursor }` pages of documents.
- `npm run unit-shared-lib` and `npm run unit-api` pass.

## Constraints

- Backwards-compatible: `getUuidsPage` / `getUuids` / `get` / `getWithLineage` unchanged.
- No `include_docs` flag on the ID-page — doc-page is a separate method/endpoint, matching the
  existing ID-vs-doc split.
- No N+1: type/phone arms are a single `include_docs` query; the freetext arm is one query + one
  batched `getDocsByIds`.
- Reuse the declarative qualifier table in the contact controller; do not duplicate
  mutual-exclusion rules.
- Pagination/cursor semantics identical to `getUuidsPage` (skip-based for views, opaque nouveau
  cursor for freetext).

## References

- `Person.v1.getPage` / `Place.v1.getPage` — pattern + local single-query implementation
- #10973 — `byPhone`/`byPhones` qualifiers, `queryDocIdsByKeys`, declarative controller table
- #10976 — `byShortcode`/`byExternalRef` (a downstream consumer if any of its callers need docs)

body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #11163, #11167 and #11172. This adds the integration tests for the delete work: end-to-end coverage of `DELETE /api/v1/contact/:uuid` against a real API and CouchDB.

The spec seeds a small hierarchy (district > health center > clinics, each with people and a report) and checks the cases the unit tests can't reach end-to-end: a recursive delete removes the contact, its descendants and their reports while leaving ancestors untouched; a leaf delete clears the surviving parent's primary-contact reference; a non-recursive delete of a contact that still has descendants is rejected with 400; an unknown id returns 404; a user without `can_delete_contacts` gets 403; and an offline user gets 403 because the endpoint is online-only.

This sits on top of #11163, #11167 and #11172, so the diff here currently includes those commits too. The new work is just the integration spec.

title: Offline sync over degraded connectivity: WAL-based alternative to CouchDB replication
body:
Hi,

I've been building ZamSync, a Rust sync engine for clinic networks in low-connectivity environments (2G, satellite, power outages mid-transfer). I think the CHT sync layer is the closest public analog to what it addresses, so worth raising here.

CouchDB replication is designed for well-connected environments. When a TCP connection drops mid-sync, it restarts from the last checkpoint, which is expensive on 23 kbps links. ZamSync uses an append-only WAL with Hybrid Logical Clocks and Version Vectors: each node tracks exactly which events every peer has seen and sends only the delta on reconnect. No duplicates, no full restarts, crash-safe (WAL survives power cuts).

Static binary, under 10 MB RAM on a Raspberry Pi 3, no runtime dependencies.

Concrete question: when CHT field devices reconnect after hours or days of disconnection, does CouchDB replication handle the sync cleanly in practice, or do you see timeout and corruption issues that require manual intervention? I'm curious what the actual failure modes look like at scale.

GitHub: https://github.com/Etoile-Bleu/ZamSync
Deep dive: https://dev.to/etoile_bleu/-i-built-a-sync-engine-for-clinics-that-run-on-2g-and-lose-power-mid-transfer-here-is-why-and-18od

body:

# Description

In our release notes script we expect the commit objects with users to look like this:

```json
[
  {
    "user": {
      "login": "mrjones-plip",
      "name": "mrjones",
      "url": "https://github.com/mrjones-plip"
    }
  }
]
```

but some times it has a null entry like this:

```json
[
  {
    "user": null
  },
  {
    "user": {
      "login": "OriginalGary",
      "name": "Original Gary",
      "url": "https://github.com/OriginalGary"
    }
  }
]
```

The fix is to then be more defensive and check the variable is set before referencing it. 

See CI that [successfully ran](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/runs/27656592229) against this branch.

## Summary

First bit of the move work, the next operation in #10706 after delete. This one's just groundwork, no endpoint yet. It ports the lineage helpers from cht-conf that the move (and later merge) service will need, so it's only plain functions with tests for now.

These don't exist server-side, so I put them in a new `api/src/services/hierarchy/` folder:

title: Release 5.2.0
body:
# Planning - CHT Community 

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release and add this issue to it. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes for the CHT relate to updated software requirements (for example: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an API, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [x] Ensure that all issues are labelled correctly, particularly "UI/UX" and "Breaking change" labelled issues, if any. 
- [x] Ensure that "Regressions" are labelled with "Affects: <version>" labels. The "Affects" label is used in a link in the Known Issues section of the release notes of that version so it has to match exactly. To make sure the label is correct go to the [release notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) and ensure the issue is listed.
- [x] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond technical documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo.
- [x] Assign a maintainer as Release Manager for this release.

# Development - Release Manager

When development is ready to begin one of the maintainers should be nominated as a Release Manager. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Checkout to a new `<issue>-update-version` branch (eg: `1234-update-version`) and set the version number in the `package.json` and `package-lock.json`. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`. Once the version is updated, submit a PR to `master` branch.
- [x] Ensure that issues associated with commits merged to `master` since the last release are closed and mapped to the milestone.

# Releasing - Release Manager

Once the PR has been merged into `master`, and the `master` branch has the new version number, then the release process can start:

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Notify the community by creating a post titled `<major>.<minor>.<patch> Beta Releases` in the [development](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/development/7) category of the CHT forum using this [template](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/new-topic?title=%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.%3Cpatch%3E%20Beta%20Releases&body=I%27ve%20just%20created%20the%20%60%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.x%60%20release%20branch.%20Please%20be%20aware%20that%20any%20further%20changes%20intended%20for%20this%20release%20will%20have%20to%20be%20merged%20to%20%60master%60%20then%20backported.%20Thanks%21&category=development).
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by creating a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`) and then push it (e.g. `git push origin tag  <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`).
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully and images are built, notify the community by adding a comment in the forum post created above using this template:
```
I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag. 
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make. 
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [x] Go to the [scalability action](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/workflows/scalability.yml) and on the top right, click into "Run workflow".  Under "Use workflow from" first choose "tags" then select the `<major>.<minor>.<minor>-beta.1` tag created above. Then "Run workflow". Once it passes, check for the scalability results [here](https://github.com/medic/scalability-results/tree/main/results). More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [x] Go to the [Issues tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues) and filter the issues with `is:issue label:"Affects: 5.x.x" ` , replace `5.x.x` with the previous version number. Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 5.x.x` label.  
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labelled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [x] Collect known migration steps, descriptions, screenshots, videos, data, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. This information should already be on the issue, but if not, prompt the change author to provide it.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions) and update the EOL date of the previous release. Update the status of any releases that are past their End Of Life date. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page.
  - [x] Ensure that the release notes PR is merged before moving to next step.
- [x] Create a [new release](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases/new) in GitHub, with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, from the release branch created above as the target branch. Click on the "Choose a tag" dropdown and create a tag for the release with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. Add a link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Once you publish the release, confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Upgrade the [demo](https://demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org/) instance to the newly released version.
  - [x] From the "App Management" admin console (`medic` user creds in 1Password), go to "Upgrades" and stage the upgrade for this version.
  - [x] Clone `cht-core` repo and checkout the target tag (`git checkout <major>.<minor>.x` ) to ensure you have the proper version of the helm charts.
  - [x] In your terminal, change to the `./cht-core/scripts/build/helm` directory.
  - [x] Make sure you're using the dev EKS cluster: `kubectl config use-context arn:aws:eks:eu-west-2:720541322708:cluster/dev-cht-eks`
  - [x] Ensure you have access to [EKS](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/hosting/medic/) and  to the [`demo-cht` namespace](https://github.com/medic/medic-infrastructure/issues/1344).) by calling this helm command. There should be no errors: `helm list -n demo-cht`
  - [x] Download the current `values.yaml` data from the demo instance: `helm get values demo-cht --namespace demo-cht > values.yaml`
  - [x] Edit the `values.yaml` file so `cht_image_tag` and `chtversion` properties have the new tag value `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`.
  - [x] Use helm to upgrade the instance: `helm upgrade demo-cht . --namespace demo-cht -f values.yaml`
  - [x] Refresh the "App Management" page and verify the instance upgraded. You may need to wait 5+ minutes until the upgrade succeeds.  Until then, you may see `50x` errors in the browser - be patient!

title: Support extension-libs in translations and outgoing messages
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Whenever we need a new way to transform text in translations or outgoing messages, we have to add a new helper to cht-core itself.

The set of [helpers available](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/20098db389458e36fc1cd38e448288505378ae11/shared-libs/message-utils/src/index.js#L338-L360) for message rendering is fixed and built into core (date, datetime, local_phone, bikram_sambat_date), so every new need means a code change and a new release. That doesn't scale and prevents projects from customizing their own message content.

This is especially limiting for outgoing messages/SMS, where the translated string is only run through Mustache plus those fixed built-in helpers.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
It would be great if projects could define their own custom helpers using [extension-libs](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/reference/extension-libs/) (or something similar) and use them in translations and outgoing messages. It will then work consistently whether the message is produced in the app (webapp) or on the server (outgoing SMS).

Usage examples:
- Devanagari numerals in an outgoing SMS, e.g. `{{#to_devanagari}}{{patient_id}}{{/to_devanagari}}`
- Age in a death notification, calculated from the contact profile's `date of birth`, e.g. `{{contact.name}} has reported death of {{#age}}{{patient.date_of_birth}}{{/age}} years old {{patient_name}} ({{patient_id}})`

This would let configurers add new message logic without needing a cht-core change every time.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Continue adding a new built-in helper to cht-core for each new need (the current approach, requires a core change and release every time).
- Pre-compute derived values upstream in forms and pass them into the message. It works for some cases, but doesn't work for SMS forms.

**Additional context**
Raised in #3245; related to #10846. Per discussion with @jkuester, supporting this on the server side should be technically possible but would need some careful design (e.g. how server-side code loads and refreshes extension-libs), and we'd want to avoid duplicating logic between the server and the webapp.

Note that translations already support variable substitution in some surfaces  e.g. contact-summary fields (`translate: true` + `context`). That covers substituting values you've already computed, but not running transformations on them, and it isn't available on the outgoing-message path. This request is about that transformation/custom-logic piece.

title: Improve flaky test resolution process
body:
**Describe the issue**
Currently the flaky test resolution process constitutes of: 
1. test fails 
2. human observes test fails
3. human roughly verifies if this is an isolated flake, caused by work in progress or frequent flake
4. human opens ticket on GH to fix test
.....
12. human fixes test

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
I want to introduce some automation in the first part of the process by (ideally): 

1. test fails on `master`
2. have a GHA that runs a script that checks if the test failed before
3. GHA opens a ticket (if it doesn't exist yet) to fix the test with details about the failed test and previous failures list. 
4. if ticket already exists, GHA adds a comment with the details about the most recent failures.

title: API fails to initialize after Node 22.23 release
body:
<!--
**Important**: This is a public repository. Anyone in the world can see what's posted here. If you are posting screenshots or log files, please **carefully examine them for** the presence of any kind of **protected health information** (PHI). Images or logs containing PHI _must_ be posted in fully-redacted form, with no visible PHI.
-->

**Describe the bug**
Node 22.23 was released yesterday. https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v22.23.0

It contains a security fix that introduces a known bug into native fetch. 

> Node's CVE-2026-48931 fix ("http: fix response queue poisoning in http.Agent", commit 0a22d40180, shipped in 24.17.0 and 22.23.0) changed post-response socket teardown, so the data listener is still attached when close fires → the heuristic misfires and emits a false ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE.

**To Reproduce**
All CI tests have been failing since the release yesterday. 

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/runs/27778033111/job/82198573574
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/runs/27771546973/job/82203001705

**Expected behavior**
API should start. 

**Logs**
```
2026-06-18T18:39:13.740 INFO: Checks passed successfully 
2026-06-18T18:39:13.774 INFO: Extracting initial documents… 
2026-06-18T18:39:13.813 INFO: Extracting initial documents completed successfully 
2026-06-18T18:39:13.813 INFO: Merging translations… 
2026-06-18T18:39:13.892 INFO: Translations merged successfully 
2026-06-18T18:39:13.892 INFO: Loading translations… 
2026-06-18T18:39:14.434 INFO: Translations loaded successfully 
2026-06-18T18:39:14.444 INFO: Running installation checks… 
2026-06-18T18:39:14.446 INFO: API listening on port 5988 
2026-06-18T18:39:14.452 ERROR: Fatal error initialising API 
2026-06-18T18:39:14.453 ERROR: FetchError: Invalid response body while trying to fetch http://haproxy:5984/medic-test/_all_docs?include_docs=true&startkey=%22_design%2F%22&endkey=%22_design%2F%EF%BF%B0%22: Premature close
    at PassThrough.<anonymous> (/service/api/node_modules/node-fetch/lib/index.js:217:52)
    at PassThrough.emit (node:events:519:28)
    at emitErrorNT (node:internal/streams/destroy:170:8)
    at emitErrorCloseNT (node:internal/streams/destroy:129:3)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:89:21) {
  message: 'Invalid response body while trying to fetch http://haproxy:5984/medic-test/_all_docs?include_docs=true&startkey=%22_design%2F%22&endkey=%22_design%2F%EF%BF%B0%22: Premature close',
  type: 'system',
  errno: 'ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE',
  code: 'ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE',
  [stack]: [Getter/Setter],
  name: 'FetchError'
} 
```

**Environment**
- Instance: dev
- App: api
- Version: `master`

I am suspecting this is coming through the `node:22-alpine` image that we base API and Sentinel off of. So no released version is affected.

Release notes

v4.12.26

What's Changed

  • fix(lambda-edge): satisfy Deno lib types for Content-Length body encoding by @​yusukebe in honojs/hono#5013
  • ci: publish to npm from CI with OIDC trusted publishing by @​yusukebe in honojs/hono#5028

Full Changelog: https://github.com/honojs/hono/compare/v4.12.25...v4.12.26

v4.12.25

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

CORS Middleware reflects any Origin with credentials when origin defaults to the wildcard

Affects: hono/cors. Fixes the wildcard origin reflecting the request Origin and sending Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true when credentials: true is set without an explicit origin, where any site a logged-in user visited could make credentialed cross-origin requests and read responses from cookie-authenticated endpoints. GHSA-88fw-hqm2-52qc

Body Limit Middleware can be bypassed on AWS Lambda by understating Content-Length

Affects: hono/body-limit on AWS Lambda (hono/aws-lambda, hono/lambda-edge). Fixes the request being built with the client-declared Content-Length while the body is delivered fully buffered, where a client could declare a small Content-Length with a much larger body and slip past the configured size limit. GHSA-rv63-4mwf-qqc2

Path traversal in serve-static on Windows via encoded backslash (%5C)

Affects: serveStatic on Windows (Node, Bun, Deno adapters). Fixes the path guard allowing a lone backslash, where an encoded backslash (%5C) decoded to \ was treated as a separator by the Windows path resolver, letting a single URL segment escape into a middleware-guarded subtree. GHSA-wwfh-h76j-fc44

AWS Lambda adapter merges multiple Set-Cookie headers into one value, dropping cookies on ALB single-header and Lattice

Affects: hono/aws-lambda. Fixes multiple Set-Cookie response headers being joined into one comma-separated value for ALB single-header responses and VPC Lattice v2, where the value could not be split back into individual cookies and clients silently dropped or misparsed them. GHSA-j6c9-x7qj-28xf

Lambda@Edge adapter keeps only the last value of a repeated request header, dropping the rest

Affects: hono/lambda-edge. Fixes repeated request headers being written with overwrite instead of append, where only the last value of a header such as X-Forwarded-For reached the application and the remaining values were silently dropped. GHSA-wgpf-jwqj-8h8p

body:
**Describe the issue**
The cht-conf integration tests run cht-conf commands against the project's `config/defualt` folder. These commands sometimes end up updating those files. These updates should not be committed, as they are most of the time not a result of the ongoing work on the branch. 

The committer has the chore of excluding and rolling back those files every time they run local integration tests. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Run integration tests against a copy of `config/default`.

title: feat(#11146): adds replication-health/failures endpoint
body:
<!--

|     |      + - > subject

|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: build|feat|fix|perf|refactor|test|chore

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

 Adds an admin-only API endpoint to identify users who are failing to replicate, to help operators troubleshoot replication issues (e.g. tracking down heavy-doc users degrading server performance).
Adds missing integration tests for limit log endpoint. 

  Closes #11146.


  ### New endpoint

  `GET /api/v1/replication-health/failed` (DB admins only) — returns users that appear unable to replicate within a recent window.

  Query parameters:
  - `days` (default `30`) — staleness window; a user is considered only if they have **not** successfully replicated within this many days.
  - `min_failures` (default `1`) — minimum replication failures **within the window** for a user to be listed.

  A user is listed when both hold:
  1. they logged at least `min_failures` replication failures inside the window, and
  2. they have not successfully replicated within the window — either their replication-count log is older than the cutoff, or they have no replication-count log at all (never successfully replicated).

  Each entry returns `user`, `last_replication_date` (null if never replicated), `failures_in_window` (what `min_failures` is applied to), and `failures_since_last_replication` (context; null if never replicated).


  ### Supporting changes

**`users-doc-count` limit log now always updates.** Previously the replication-count log was only rewritten when doc counts/dates drifted past a threshold; it now rewrites on every successful replication so its `date` reliably reflects the last successful replication, which the new endpoint depends on.

## AI disclosure

Code developed with the help of Claude.

Recently I added some debug logging to show which messages were failing the assertions, to assess whether the failures were valid or not. Turn out they were. 

This is a document that has _two_ messages that have been sent, even though it should have only one:

title: feat(#11174): add getpage and getall endpoints
body:
closes #11174 

Implements getPage/getAll for Contact.v1 and Report.v1

A few notes:

This PR does not attempt to do any refactoring to remove duplication, which makes the diff larger but otherwise too many unrelated changes are added in one branch. I think later we can go back and do some refactoring in a separate PR.
This replaces https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/11175 which did attempt some refactoring at the same time, but will be harder to review, even though its fewer LoC.

Qualifiers differ a little bit from the ticket description.
I did not add freetext qualifiers to these, but instead added `IdsQualifier` to both, and `ContactTypeQualifer` to contacts.
More qualifiers will be added later as needed.
I used `IdsQualifier` instead of `UuidsQualifier`, which is inconsistent with what is already there, but the preference is to call identifiers `ids` instead of `uuids`.

title: Remove redundant map reduce view registered_patients
body:
The `registered_patients` map reduce view is redundant. It is almost an exact copy of `reports_by_subject` — both index `data_record` reports by their subject's patient/place shortcode.

Maintaining a second, near-identical index over every report is wasteful. The view can be removed and its consumers repointed at `reports_by_subject`.

`reports_by_subject` is a strict superset of `registered_patients`: it emits the same `patient_id`/`place_id` keys (plus `case_id`, `patient_uuid`, and `place_uuid`) for the same `data_record` reports. Every consumer of `registered_patients` already post-filters the returned docs through `registrationUtils.isValidRegistration`, which discards error docs, non-registrations, and unconfigured forms — so the extra docs surfaced by `reports_by_subject` are trimmed back to exactly what `registered_patients` would have returned.

Two differences need to be handled when switching:
- **Key coercion:** `registered_patients` emits `String(id)` keys; `reports_by_subject` emits the raw value. To preserve matching for any numeric `patient_id`/`place_id`, `reports_by_subject` should coerce its emitted keys with `String()`.
- **Duplicate emits:** `reports_by_subject` emits a key from both the top-level property and `doc.fields`, so a single report can be returned more than once per key. Consumers must de-duplicate the returned docs by `_id` (`getReportsBySubject` in transitions already does this).

## View: medic-client/registered_patients

### Definition
- **Database:** medic-client (synced to offline clients)
- **Map keys:** `String(doc.patient_id)`, `String(doc.place_id)` (falling back to `doc.fields.patient_id` / `doc.fields.place_id`)
- **Map values:** (none)
- **Reduce:** None

### Usages
| # | File | Key/Options Used | Functional Purpose |
|---|------|------------------|--------------------|
| 1 | [`shared-libs/transitions/src/lib/utils.js:165`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/shared-libs/transitions/src/lib/utils.js#L165) | `{ key/keys, include_docs: true }` | `getRegistrations` — fetches registration reports for one or more shortcodes, then filters to valid registrations. |
| 2 | [`api/src/services/export/message-mapper.js:122`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/src/services/export/message-mapper.js#L122) | `{ keys: patientIds, include_docs: true }` | Hydrates scheduled-task messages with their patient registrations for the messages export. |
| 3 | [`admin/src/js/services/message-queue.js:135`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/admin/src/js/services/message-queue.js#L135) | `{ keys: shortcodes, include_docs: true }` | Loads patient/place registrations for the admin message-queue view. |
| 4 | [`webapp/src/ts/services/format-data-record.service.ts:41`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/services/format-data-record.service.ts#L41) | `{ key: shortcode, include_docs: true }` | Loads registrations for a report's patient/place when formatting scheduled-task messages for display. |

Note: removing the view (and the `String()` change to `reports_by_subject`) triggers a one-time view reindex on upgrade.

body:
Bumps [@ngx-translate/core](https://github.com/ngx-translate/core) from 16.0.4 to 18.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from @​ngx-translate/core's releases.

v18.0.0

@ngx-translate/core@18.0.0 and @ngx-translate/http-loader@18.0.0 are now stable on npm (latest).

v18 is the major API-cleanup release: standalone providers everywhere, signal-based internals, the default → fallback rename finalized, and the deprecated surface removed. It also resolves three long-standing semantic gotchas and baselines the workspace on Angular 22 / TypeScript 6.0.

Highlights

  • Standalone-first setup. TranslateModule is gone — use provideTranslateService() / provideChildTranslateService() (works in standalone and NgModule apps).
  • New *translateBlock="let t" structural directive for cleaner template translations.
  • New isLoading: Signal<boolean> — true while any use() load is in flight; read it for language-switching spinners.
  • Isolated subtrees are now truly isolated — own events, lookups, and language state.
  • Angular 18–22 supported (16 and 17 dropped); built and tested against Angular 18/19/20/21/22.

Breaking changes — required edits

TranslateModule removed. Replace TranslateModule.forRoot({...}) / forChild({...}) with provideTranslateService({...}) / provideChildTranslateService({...}). The pipe, directive, and service are standalone.

Deprecated default* symbols removed — rename:

Removed Replacement
defaultLang fallbackLang
setDefaultLang() setFallbackLang()
getDefaultLang() getFallbackLang()
onDefaultLangChange onFallbackLangChange
DefaultLangChangeEvent FallbackLangChangeEvent
langs getLangs()
setValue() (util) insertValue()

Also removed: useDefaultLang and defaultLanguage config fields (along with TranslateModule).

Deprecated (still works, warns once): using element text content as a key (<span translate>Hello</span>). Use [translate]="'KEY'", the translate pipe, or *translateBlock. It will be removed next major.

Potentially breaking — low impact (behavior changes)

  • A failed use() no longer mutates state. On loader failure, currentLang() / lastUseLanguage stay at the prior value instead of switching to the failed language. Use isLoading() or the returned Observable's error channel to drive switching UI.
  • Isolated subtrees no longer see ancestor translationChange$ events, nor borrow keys from outer scopes. Isolation now means own events + own lookups + own language state. If you wanted shared translations with subtree-scoped state, use provideChildTranslateService({ extend: true }).
  • instant() "unloaded language" warning is deduplicated per isolated subtree (was once per service instance).
  • ITranslateService gains isLoading: Signal<boolean>. If you mock it via implements/extends ITranslateService, add isLoading = signal(false).asReadonly(). See the "Mocking TranslateService" recipe in the README.
  • Loader errors are now logged instead of silently swallowed.

Migration

Full step-by-step guide: https://ngx-translate.org → Getting Started → Migration Guide.

title: feat(#10706): add bulk operation document model
body:
# Description

First piece of the bulk operation framework from the #10706 design: the shared document model that delete, move and merge all build on.

Adds the `@medic/bulk-operations` shared library with:
- the action types (`archive`, `set-contact`, `delete-user`), statuses, and document id prefixes
- `buildBulkOperation(actionOperations, date)`, which builds the log document (`medic-logs`, read by the polling endpoint) and one action document per action type (`medic-sentinel`, processed by Sentinel in batches), cross-linked both ways
- the per-item params stored in a base64 json `operations` attachment, so advancing an action's cursor later does not rewrite the whole list

No dependency on the archiving work, so it can land on its own. The queue helper that writes these docs and the `GET /api/v1/bulk-operations/{id}` polling endpoint follow next.

title: feat(#10706): add bulk operation status endpoint
body:
# Description

Adds `GET /api/v1/bulk-operations/{id}` so a caller can poll the progress of a bulk operation (delete, move or merge) by its id. It returns the operation's log document from the `medic-logs` database, with the per-action status and the count of changes so far.

The service only resolves ids that carry the `bulk-operation:` prefix, so the endpoint can't be used to read the other log documents that share `medic-logs`. Online users only; a missing or non bulk-operation id returns 404. Documented with an OpenAPI annotation.

Builds on #11222 (the `@medic/bulk-operations` doc model). Until that one merges into the feature branch, the diff here also includes the doc model; it'll narrow to just the endpoint once #11222 lands.

title: Don't allow PRs to be merged that will be flagged in release notes script.
body:
**Describe the issue**
In [slack](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C03H77DKY0M/p1772155075106489) (private link) a question was asked:

> Hey all! I wonder if folks have thoughts on what PRs get added to a milestone/release?
>
> I wanted A) get consensus and B) have explicit rules about which to include vs exclude so it's fast and easy for release engineers.

The issue is that release engineers go to run the [automatic release note generation script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/scripts/release-notes), but it always finds either PRs without issues that don't have a type, or an issue that doesn't have a type, or [some other error](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/scripts/release-notes#sample-error-output). Some [work was done](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10613) to support ignoring Dependabot commits, but this is still arduous for release engineers and ends up being subjective as to what to include. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Block PRs from being merged that will cause the release note script to fail.  While changes may be made to the issue/PR after it has been merged, this should go a long way to smoothing things over.  [From Slack](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C03H77DKY0M/p1782195582923519?thread_ts=1772155075.106489&cid=C03H77DKY0M):

> Where I do fully agree with you is the merge-time discipline — requiring the right labels/milestone before a PR can be merged

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Manually resolve the conflicts the release notes script finds.

title: Add CI to unassign issues with no open PR and no activity for 4 weeks
body:
**Describe the issue**
We have many issues that are assigned, but have not been active for a long time and have no open PRs.  This makes it confusing to maintainers and new contributors alike.  

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Add CI to un-assign issues with no open PR and no activity for 4 weeks. After 3 (2?!) weeks CI can add a comment that in 1 week the issue will be unassigned.

If an issue is commented on, then the 4 week timer gets reset.  If a PR is opened, the check will fail and no timer will be set.

This compliments automated stale PR handling we [deployed](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10086) in Jun 2025

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Manually un-assign as @andrablaj  so often does 😅
