title: feat(#10706): add bulk operation framework and contact hierarchy delete
body:
# Description

The server-side implementation of contact-hierarchy delete for #10706. A `DELETE` on the person and place endpoints gathers everything the delete touches and queues a bulk operation that Sentinel executes asynchronously, so the slow work runs off the request. The bulk operation framework is generic: delete is its first consumer, and move and merge will reuse it.

What's here, by layer:
- **Document model + constants**: the log doc and per-action doc shapes, with the id prefixes and enums shared through `@medic/constants`.
- **Queue helper**: writes the log doc to `medic-logs` and one action doc per type to `medic-sentinel`.
- **`GET /api/v1/bulk-operations/{id}`**: poll an operation's status.
- **Sentinel**: a `medic-sentinel` changes-feed listener plus a batch/cursor processor, with the `set-contact`, `delete-user` and `archive` handlers.
- **`DELETE /api/v1/person/{id}` and `/api/v1/place/{id}`**: gated on `can_delete_contact_hierarchy`, with `delete_users` (requires `can_delete_users`, else a `400` when linked users exist) and `dry_run` query params; each endpoint rejects an id of the wrong type with a `404`; returns a summary of the changes plus the operation id.

The `archive` handler reuses the archiving work from #6615 / #11139 (now in the base branch): it calls `archiveBatch` directly to copy the contacts and reports to the archive database and purge them from `medic`. So a delete runs end to end: gather, clear references, handle linked users, then archive and purge. `canArchive` is extended to cover the default contact types (`person`, `clinic`, `health_center`, `district_hospital`).

Endpoint behaviour is covered by integration tests: the permissions, the dry-run summaries, the type and linked-user error cases, and an end-to-end test that deletes a contact and confirms it and its reports are purged.

Supersedes the earlier delete PRs, now closed and folded in here: #11163, #11167, #11172, #11176 (the first synchronous attempt) and #11222, #11223 (the split framework pieces).

Part of #10706

## Notes

The gather-and-queue logic lives once in `deleteContactHierarchy` and is contact-type-agnostic, a person delete is just the leaf case of a place-subtree delete. The person and place endpoints each call a shared handler with their own type, and the handler checks the target is that type before doing anything, so a place id sent to `/person/{id}` is rejected with a 404 instead of deleting the place hierarchy, and vice versa. The `delete_users`/`dry_run` params and the responses are shared OpenAPI components referenced from both.

title: feat(#10652): support collecting targets/UHC for Bikram Sambat months
body:
# Description

This PR introduces support for calculating Target and UHC calendar intervals aligned with the Bikram Sambat (BS) calendar rather than the Gregorian calendar, when configured.

Since a BS month never starts and ends in the same Gregorian month (always roughly a 15-day offset), the target documents remain stored in CouchDB under their Gregorian end month YYYY-MM tags, but their start and end bounds now shift to correspond to the BS calendar.

Fixes: #10652

### Key Changes
* **calendar-interval library**: Integrated the `bikram-sambat` conversion package to compute Gregorian start and end bounds corresponding to the BS month and day offsets. Added comprehensive unit tests covering offsets, boundary conditions, month wrapping, leap years/months, and timezone-aware objects.
* **rules-engine library**: Saved the `useBikramSambatMonths` configuration in the internal state store and passed it during dynamic calendar evaluations.
* **webapp components**: Updated `uhc-settings`, `uhc-stats`, `calendar-interval`, and `rules-engine` services to parse, propagate, and apply the setting when calculating client-side aggregation ranges.

# Code review checklist
- [x] UI/UX backwards compatible: Test it works for the new design (enabled by default). And test it works in the old design, enable `can_view_old_navigation` permission to see the old design. Test it has appropriate design for RTL languages.

title: Bikram Sambat (Nepali) date changes at 6:15 PM instead of local midnight
body: **Describe the bug** When the webapp is displayed in Nepali language that uses the Bikram Sambat (Nepali) calendar, the displayed date rolls over to the *next* day several hours before local midnight. In Nepal (UTC+5:45) the date changes at **18:15 local time (6:15 PM)** instead of at midnight, so from 6:15 PM onward the whole app shows tomorrow's date. **To Reproduce** 1. Use the webapp in Nepali. 2. Set the device timezone to `Asia/Kathmandu` (UTC+5:45). 3. With the clock set *before* 6:15 PM, submit a report. 4. Set the clock to *after* 6:15 PM (still the same local day, before midnight) and submit a second report. 5. Open the Reports list. Both reports were created on the same local day. Hover over each report's date to reveal its absolute date tooltip. The second report's tooltip shows the *next* Bikram Sambat date, so the two appear on different days. Example: Timestamp | English | Nepali (Bikram Sambat) | Bikram Sambat (translated to English) -|-|-|- 1783427348132 | Tue, Jul 7th, 2026 at 6:14 PM | २३ असार २०८३, साँझको ६:१४:०८ बजे | 23 Ashar 2083, 6:14:08 PM 1783427425374 | Tue, Jul 7th, 2026 at 6:15 PM | २४ असार २०८३, साँझको ६:१५:२५ बजे | 24 Ashar 2083, 6:15:25 PM **Expected behavior** The Bikram Sambat date should change at **local midnight**, matching the device's local calendar day: the same as the Gregorian date behaves in other languages. **Logs** N/A **Screenshots** Language set to Nepali: Language set to English: **Environment** - Instance: any - Browser: any - Client platform: any (device timezone UTC+5:45, i.e. Nepal) - App: webapp - Version: 4.x, 5.x **Additional context**

title: Mobile date tooltip clipped off the left edge of the viewport (report detail)
body: **Describe the bug** On touch devices (including the CHT Android app), the accessible tooltip used to reveal a relative date's absolute value is **clipped off the left edge of the viewport** and only the tail end of the text is visible. On the report detail page, focusing the date/time in the "Submitted by" line shows something like `5:30 AM` instead of the full `Tue, Jul 7th, 2026 at 5:30 AM`. The beginning of the string is pushed off-screen. **To Reproduce** 1. Use the webapp on a touch / no-hover viewport: a phone, or Chrome DevTools **Responsive** view. 2. Open any submitted report's detail view so the "Submitted by [name] [phone]" summary line is visible. 3. Focus the relative date/time text after that line: tap it on a touch device, or tab to it. 4. The tooltip appears anchored to the date element, but its left portion is off-screen: only the tail (e.g. `5:30 AM`) is readable. **Expected behavior** The tooltip should display the complete date/time string within the visible viewport. **Logs** N/A **Screenshots** Chrome (responsive mode): CHT Android: **Environment** - Instance: any - Browser: Any touch device (or responsive mode on Chrome) - Client platform: Android, Mobile view - App: webapp - Version: Found in 5.1.1, also present in 4.22.0 **Additional context** - Found while investigating a separate Bikram Sambat date bug (#11241); this tooltip issue is independent of language and of that date bug. - On desktop the native tooltip is used and is not affected. - It works fine for messages (sent date) and tasks (due date).

title: feat(#11192): support extension libs in messages
body:
# Description Adds project-defined `extension-libs` as synchronous Mustache section helpers for translations and outgoing messages. This allows configurers to transform message values without adding a new built-in helper to CHT Core, for example: ```mustache {{#to_devanagari}}{{patient_id}}{{/to_devanagari}} ``` Closes #11192. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR Couch[("CouchDB
extension-libs")] Loader["Extension-libs loader
decode + atomic registry replacement"] Couch --> Loader Loader --> Webapp["Webapp cache"] Loader --> API["API config cache"] Loader --> Sentinel["Sentinel config cache"] Loader --> Admin["Admin preview load"] Webapp --> Translation["Webapp translations"] Webapp --> Report["Report detail messages"] API --> Export["Message export rendering"] Sentinel --> Transitions["Transitions and scheduled SMS"] Admin --> Preview["Message queue preview"] Translation --> MessageUtils["message-utils
template(opts) / generate(opts)"] Report --> MessageUtils Export --> MessageUtils Transitions --> MessageUtils Preview --> MessageUtils MessageUtils --> Output["Consistent rendered message"] ``` ## Changes - Adds `@medic/extension-libs` for loading and decoding the `extension-libs` CouchDB document. - Refactors `message-utils.generate` and `message-utils.template` to accept an options object containing `extensionLibs`. - Keeps positional argument compatibility for downstream callers while migrating all CHT Core production call sites. - Exposes synchronous function exports as Mustache section helpers, using the attachment filename without the `.js` suffix. - Prevents extension helpers from shadowing built-in helpers or template data. - Loads and refreshes extension-libs in API, Sentinel, and Webapp; Admin loads them for message-queue previews. - Passes extension-libs through transitions, scheduled messages, API message exports, Webapp report details and validation messages, translations, and Admin previews. - Logs and safely falls back to rendered content when a configured helper is invalid, throws, or returns an unsupported value. - Treats a missing document as an empty registry, skips malformed attachments, and retains the previous valid registry after transient load failures. ## Security Extension-libs are trusted application configuration uploaded by authorized administrators. This change does not present extension-lib execution as sandboxed. ## Verification - `npm run lint` - `npx tsc -p webapp/tsconfig.spec.json --noEmit` - `npm run compile --prefix webapp` - `npm test --workspace=@medic/message-utils` — 126 passing - Focused transitions tests for `due_tasks` and messages — 51 passing - Focused Webapp Karma tests for the parser, validation, format-data-record, and CHT datasource services — 59 passing - Added API integration coverage for message-export rendering with an extension helper. - Added Sentinel integration coverage for due-task rendering with an extension helper. - Added Webapp WDIO coverage for translation rendering with an extension helper. The environment-dependent API, Sentinel, and Webapp integration cases are included for execution by the relevant CI jobs. ## Notes for reviewers - The shared loader centralizes attachment decoding and error behavior across browser and server runtimes. - Application services still own their loading and cache lifecycle and explicitly inject the current extension-lib snapshot into `message-utils`. - The options-object refactor follows the direction discussed in #11192 and avoids adding another positional parameter to the existing APIs. # Code review checklist - [x] UI/UX backwards compatible: Not applicable; this PR does not change layouts or navigation. - [x] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the [style guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/style-guide/) - [x] Documented: Extension-helper configuration, constraints, and fallback behavior are documented in `shared-libs/extension-libs/README.md`. - [x] Tested: Unit and integration/e2e coverage has been added for the affected application paths. - [x] Internationalised: No new user-facing static text is introduced. - [x] Backwards compatible: Existing positional APIs remain supported and invalid or unavailable extension libraries degrade safely. - [x] AI disclosure: OpenAI Codex was used to help inspect the codebase, implement and refactor parts of the change, add tests, and address review feedback. I reviewed the resulting changes, ran the verification listed above, and remain responsible for the contribution. # License The software is provided under AGPL-3.0. title: Bikram Sambat enketo widget leaks body-appended picker DOM on each form open (destroy() never runs)
body:
Noticed while reviewing #11230. The code is from the already-merged #11234, so filing separately. ## Problem `webapp/src/js/enketo/widgets/bikram-sambat-datepicker.js` defines a `destroy()` that cleans up the body-appended picker/overlay, but it never runs. enketo-core tears forms down via `Form.resetView()` -> `widgets.reset()`, which only calls the static `Widget.globalReset()`, never an instance `destroy()`. So every time a Nepali-locale form with a Bikram Sambat date field is opened, the plugin appends a fresh `
` (and, on show, a `.nepali-date-picker-overlay`) to ``, and these accumulate across form opens within a single SPA session (DOM + listener leak). Separately, `super.destroy(element)` in that method would throw `TypeError` if it were ever invoked, since enketo-core's base `Widget` has no `destroy`. ## Reproduction (confirmed) 1. Set the app to Nepali (`ne`) locale. 2. Open a form with a BS date field (e.g. "BS Date Test"), then close it. 3. Repeat about 4 times. 4. Inspect `` in DevTools. Observed: 4 opens produced 4 leftover `
` in ``: ## Suggested fix - Wire cleanup into a teardown path enketo actually calls, or drop the dead `destroy()` (and remove/fix the `super.destroy()` call). - Scope cleanup to this widget's own picker instead of `$('.nepali-date-picker').remove()`, which would remove every picker on the page. Severity: non-blocking (gradual DOM/listener leak, Nepali-form-only, no crash or broken behavior). Part of #10707.

title: Bikram Sambat: harden feature test coverage (widget, reports filter, conversion, a11y/security)
body:
Follow-up from the #11230 review and a test-health assessment of the Bikram Sambat feature (epic #10707). Green CI currently protects a narrow logic core; most behaviors we exercised by hand (including several bugs found during review) have no guarding test, or have one that is stubbed / no-op / masked. This tracks the feature-level tests that should exist. Focus is on actual feature coverage, not line coverage.

Related: #11245 (enketo `destroy()` leak, one specific instance below).

title: fix: clean up Bikram Sambat picker instances
body:
## Summary Fixes #11245. Repeatedly opening the Bikram Sambat date picker leaves body-appended picker nodes behind because Enketo's `Form.resetView()` path invokes the static widget reset hook rather than each widget instance's `destroy()` method. The previous instance cleanup therefore did not run, and calling `super.destroy()` would not be valid because the base widget does not provide that method. This PR: - Tracks active Bikram Sambat date-picker widget instances. - Cleans up those instances from `Widget.globalReset()`, the teardown path Enketo actually invokes. - Removes only the picker and hidden input belonging to each widget, and removes the shared overlay once no picker remains. - Adds a regression test covering four open/reset cycles. ## Validation - Webapp Angular unit tests: 2,811 passed, 4 skipped. - CHT form unit tests: 30 passed. - Admin unit tests: 431 passed. - API unit tests: 1,645 passed. - Sentinel unit tests: 230 passed. - CouchDB cluster unit tests: 6 passed. - API integration tests: 11 passed. - Lint and `git diff --check` passed. - The dedicated Bikram Sambat widget regression test passed: 15 tests completed. The shared-library suite has one pre-existing environment-level coverage gate in `shared-libs/outbound`: its 39 tests pass, but the runner reports coverage just below its configured threshold. It is unrelated to this change. SonarCloud's two `S6582` suggestions were applied with optional chaining. Because the inherited `@medic` ESLint configuration pins Espree to ES2018, a file-scoped `ecmaVersion: 2020` override was added for this widget so the repository lint accepts the syntax. The separate `S5906` suggestion for the test assertion has also been applied with `expect(widget.$hiddenDateInput).to.be.null`. ## Evidence The following screenshots show the picker working in the browser harness and the DOM cleanup proof after repeated form teardown cycles.
Show browser evidence
## Timeline 1. The issue identified that repeated form opens accumulated body-appended `.nepali-date-picker` nodes. 2. Inspection of Enketo's lifecycle showed that reset uses the static widget hook, so instance `destroy()` is not the reliable cleanup path. 3. The implementation was adapted to register active widgets and perform scoped cleanup during `globalReset()`. 4. A four-cycle browser regression proof and automated test confirmed zero picker and orphaned nodes after every reset. _Target branch: `10707-dmp-2026-enhance-bikram-sambat-support-in-cht`, where the existing widget implementation was introduced._ _This PR was developed by Codex under the supervision of jmtdev0._

title: fix(#11245): clean up Bikram Sambat picker instances
body:
# Description

Fixes #11245

This PR fixes a DOM and listener leak where opening Nepali-locale forms with a Bikram Sambat datepicker appends a new calendar container (`.nepali-date-picker`) and backdrop (`.nepali-date-picker-overlay`) to `<body>` on every form load without destroying them. 

Since Enketo Core unloads forms via static `Widget.globalReset()` rather than instance `destroy()` calls, these elements accumulated in the body across form opens.

## Changes:
- Track active widget instances in a static `Set` on the `Bikramsambatdatepicker` class.
- Implement static `globalReset()` to loop over active instances, trigger their instance `destroy()` method, and clear the set.
- Scoped element cleanup inside `destroyDatePicker` using the widget's stored `$picker` data reference, preventing all calendar pickers on the page from being broadly deleted.
- Removed the dead `super.destroy()` call in the widget to avoid runtime `TypeError` issues.
- Added Karma unit test coverage in `bikram-sambat-datepicker.spec.ts` to assert that body nodes are properly cleaned up on reset.

title: feat(#10973): add phone qualifier
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

feat(#1234): add hat wobble
^--^(#^--^): ^------------^
|     |      |
|     |      + - > subject
|     |
|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: build|feat|fix|perf|refactor|test|chore

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

<!-- DESCRIPTION -->

  Adds a phones qualifier to cht-datasource and exposes it on the two contact list endpoints.
  **No call site is migrated** — every existing `medic-client/contacts_by_phone` caller is
  untouched, so no existing read moves onto the new path. One thing does change for existing API
  users: the error returned when neither endpoint gets a qualifier. `Either query param freetext or
  type is required` becomes `Either query param freetext, type or phone is required`, on both
  `GET /api/v1/contact/uuid` and `GET /api/v1/contact`.

  ### Datasource

  - `PhonesQualifier` / `byPhones` / `isPhonesQualifier` in `qualifier.ts`, reaching consumers through the existing `export * as Qualifier` re-export.
  - Local: a dispatch arm in `getUuidsPage` and, via `getContactDocsPageFn`, in `getPage`. Both query the view with `keys` and both filter rows through `isContact`, so the id path and the doc path return the same contacts. Keys are
  deduped in a stable order — rows come back grouped in supplied-key order, which is what keeps the skip cursor meaningful between pages.
  - `queryDocsByKeys` in `local/libs/doc.ts`, the docs twin of the `queryDocIdsByKeys` helper #11327 added.
  - Remote: a `phone` param on both list endpoints.
  - Both assert helpers were renamed (`assertContactTypeFreetextPhonesQualifier`, `assertContactTypeIdsPhonesQualifier`) rather than duplicated, so no call site can still reach a two-qualifier assertion.
  - `getUuidsPageByPhones` / `getUuidsByPhones` / `getPageByPhones` / `getByPhones` on the imperative `getDatasource()` surface, next to `getPageByType` — no new method on the `Contact.v1` namespace. These have no in-repo consumer yet.

  ### API

  `phone` query param on `GET /api/v1/contact/uuid` and `GET /api/v1/contact`; no new route and no `routing.js` change. On `/uuid` it takes precedence over `type` and `freetext`; on `/contact` the precedence is `ids`, then `phone`, then
  `type`. An object-shaped `phone` (`?phone[a]=b`, which `qs.parse` parses to an object) is rejected with a 400 rather than throwing.

  ### Why the phones paths filter and the type path does not

  `contacts_by_type` keys on the contact type and `assertValidContactType` gates the request, so that path can only ever emit configured types — it needs no filter. `contacts_by_phone` keys on the phone and emits any doc whose `type` is
  in its hard-coded list, including `type: contact` docs whose `contact_type` is not in settings. So the phones arms filter explicitly, which costs the id path an `include_docs` it would not otherwise need. Emitting the type as the view
  value would let the filter run on `row.value` instead, but that is a ddoc change and a reindex — worth revisiting if the phones uuid path ever gets a high-volume caller.

  Without the filter the id path would hand back ids that `GET /api/v1/contact/{id}` then 404s, because `get` applies `isContact` too.

  ### Decisions copied from #11151 (#11327)

  - Plural array qualifier with a non-empty tuple type, verbatim matching, `Set` dedupe, and rejection of blank or whitespace-padded entries.
  - Serialising over the existing list endpoint as a comma-joined query param instead of a dedicated route.
  - The `keys`-based local query helper.

  ### Deviations from the issue

  - **Plural, not singular.** `byPhones([...])` rather than `byPhone(phone)`. The view is queried with `keys`, so a batch of numbers costs one query rather than one per number — which is what the admin message queue will need when it
  migrates.
  - **No `/api/v1/contact/by-phone/:phone`.** Query param on the existing endpoints, so paging, permissions and the OpenAPI shape stay on the established contract.
  - **The doc-returning path is extended too.** The issue scoped this to `getUuidsPage`; extending `getPage` keeps a doc lookup at one round trip and lets both paths agree on contact types.
  - **The call sites are not migrated.** Review found a behaviour change in every one of them (below), so they move to a new PR and a new issue (#11442) and this PR ships the qualifier alone.
  - **Padded input is rejected rather than passed through.** The qualifier normalises nothing, but a padded number can only ever match nothing, so `byPhones` throws instead of returning a silent empty page. Coercion and trimming remain
  the caller's job, as the issue requires.
  - **The shared assert helper is renamed rather than duplicated.** #11327 went the other way — it added `assertFreetextOrFormsQualifier` alongside `assertFreetextQualifier` and kept both. Renaming leaves no two-qualifier assertion for a
  call site to reach by mistake.

  ### Why the call sites moved out

  The acceptance criteria of #10973 was originally to migrate the existing view calls onto the datasource, but every one of those migrations carried a behaviour change that needs more analysis than this PR should carry. So this PR adds the
  qualifier, and migrating the call sites onto it moves to a follow-up. See #11442 

  | Call site | Behaviour change migration would cause |
  |---|---|
  | `webapp/.../phone-widget.js` | Online users would newly need `can_view_contacts`. That permission gates the UI and the `/api/v1/contact\|person\|place` endpoints, not the data — online users read contacts through the CouchDB proxy regardless — so the change restricts nothing while potentially breaking a custom role. |
  | `admin/.../message-queue.js` | Same cause, larger blast radius: `crfo` reaches the admin app via `can_configure`/`can_export_all` with no `can_view_contacts`, and the rejection blanks the page rather than dropping names. |
  | `validation_utils.js` `uniquePhone` | A missing field would go from failing to passing, so a config using `uniquePhone` as "must exist AND be unique" would silently stop enforcing the first half. `String()`/`.trim()` would also newly enforce uniqueness on numeric and padded values. |
  | `registration.js` `getParentByPhone` | An undefined `doc.from` sends no key at all — PouchDB drops undefined params — so the query returns every phone-bearing contact and `rows[0].doc` becomes the parent. Migrating would make that `parent_not_found`. Rows would also be newly filtered by `isContact`. |
  | `update_sent_by.js` | Rows would be newly filtered by `isContact`, where it currently reads `rows[0].doc` off the raw view. |
  | `api/.../contacts-by-phone.js` | Rows would be newly filtered by `isContact`, where it currently hydrates the raw view ids. |
  | `self_report.js`, `update_clinics.js` | These two already filter at hydration via `getWithLineage`, so `isContact` costs them nothing. They would still gain `.trim()` from the shared sender qualifier: a padded `doc.from` matches nothing today and would start matching. |

  ### Testing

  Unit coverage for the qualifier, both local adapter arms (including the `isContact` filter on the id path), the remote adapter, the assert helpers and the controller; API integration tests for `?phone=`, comma-separated, repeated-param
  and the two 400 cases on both endpoints; datasource integration tests for `getUuidsPage`/`getPage`/the generator, non-normalisation, a three-page cursor walk asserting exact ids and cursors, and a `type: contact` doc with an
  unconfigured `contact_type` that the view emits and neither phones path returns. `eslint .`, `unit-api`, `unit-shared-lib` green.

title: fix(#11241): ensure Bikram Sambat date conversion uses local date string format
body:
# Description

When the webapp is used in Nepali (Bikram Sambat calendar), the displayed date rolled over to the next day several hours before local midnight. In Nepal (UTC+5:45) it changed at 18:15 (6:15 PM) instead of midnight.

**Root cause:** `FormatDateService` passed a `moment` object to `bikram-sambat`, whose `toBik_text`/`toBik` expect an ISO date string (`YYYY-MM-DD`). The library's `Date.parse` then consumed the full timestamp, so an evening time-of-day rolled the day over early in timezones ahead of UTC. Additionally, with the `ne` locale active, `moment.format` emits Devanagari numerals, which `Date.parse` cannot read, causing the "Date outside supported range" crash.

**Fix:** format the moment to a local `YYYY-MM-DD` string before passing it to the library, and force the `en` locale on a clone so the numerals stay ASCII (the `datetime` time-portion remains localised). This pins the conversion to the local calendar day so the date changes at local midnight.

**Tests:** updated the existing `date/datetime/dayMonth` specs to assert the library now receives the local date string, and added two regression tests in `format-date.service.spec.ts`
- one proving time-of-day independence (start-of-day and end-of-day map to the same date),
- and another proving ASCII digits are passed even when the locale renders Devanagari.

Both new tests were verified to fail on the unfixed code and pass with the fix.


Fixes: #11241

## AI disclosure

Per the [AI contribution guidelines](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/community/contributing/ai-guidelines/):

- **Tool:** Claude Code (Anthropic).
- **How it was used:** investigating the bug report and understanding the relevant code, identifying the root cause (passing a `moment` to `bikram-sambat` instead of an ISO date string, plus the `ne`-locale Devanagari-numeral crash), implementing the fix, and writing the unit tests and code comments.

All changes were reviewed and tested by me; the new tests were verified to fail without the fix and pass with it.

title: Bikram Sambat datepicker offers non-existent days (e.g. मंसिर ३० २०८२) and throws Invalid day value
body:
### Describe the bug
In Nepali locale, the Bikram Sambat datepicker (reports filter and enketo form widget) draws its day cells from the bundled `nepali-date-picker`'s own month table, but converts the selection with `bikram-sambat`. Those tables disagree for 2082/2083, so the picker renders days that do not exist. Selecting one calls `toGreg_text(...)`, which throws an unhandled `Invalid day value` and breaks the filter (and the form widget).

### To reproduce (verified)
1. Nepali locale, Reports tab, open the date filter, open the BS picker.
2. Navigate to **मंसिर २०८२**. The picker shows day **३०**; that month has 29 days.
3. Click **३०** -> `Invalid day value` in the console, filter does not apply.

Also in 2082: जेठ ३२ and साउन ३२ (real 31), माघ ३० (real 29). All of BS 2082 is in the past, so it is fully selectable today. The 2083 cases (मंसिर, माघ) are near-future and open up later this year, and are reachable now in form fields that are not capped at today.

### Root cause
Two independent Bikram Sambat calendars that must agree and do not. `nepali-date-picker`'s table is stale; `bikram-sambat` is correct (verified against a real 2082/2083 calendar). The 2082 crash predates recent changes; the 2083 case was activated by #11154 bumping `bikram-sambat` to 1.8.1 (which includes medic/bikram-sambat#31), making the converter correct while the plugin stayed wrong.

### Affected code
- Reports filter: `webapp/src/ts/components/filters/date-filter/date-filter.component.ts` (`onDateSelect` -> `toGreg_text`)
- Enketo widget via `webapp/src/js/enketo/widgets/bikram-sambat-picker-shared.js`

Currently on the epic branch `10707-dmp-2026-enhance-bikram-sambat-support-in-cht` (merged via #11230), not on master.

### Proposed resolution
1. **Immediate:** guard the conversion (validate the selected day against `bikram-sambat.daysInMonth`, or a `safeToGreg` helper in the shared module) so no selection can throw.
2. **Real fix:** migrate the shared picker off `nepali-date-picker` to the `bikram-sambat`-backed calendar (**blocked by** medic/bikram-sambat#35).

This is the gate to clear before the epic merges to master.

### Related
Epic #10707. Fork plan #9250 (agreed by @binokaryg). Test cases #11246. Picker merged in #11230. Distinct from the enketo leak #11245. Prior invalid-date bug #7925.

title: refactor(#10700): re-write Enketo form save workflow
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

feat(#1234): add hat wobble
^--^(#^--^): ^------------^
|     |      |
|     |      + - > subject
|     |
|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: build|feat|fix|perf|refactor|test|chore

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

This PR basically re-writes the doc-saving workflow when an Enekto form (either contact/app/training form) is completed. The existing legacy code suffered from several major problems that made it very difficult to continue developing features on top of it:

- The doc-processing pipeline for contact docs vs reports was almost completely disjointed.  Aside from the core xml-to-object functions, none of the other logic/workflows was coherently shared between contacts and reports.  This meant that we had a lot of duplication and inconsistency between how things were being handled. And, any new features (e.g. attachments) needed to be essentially implemented twice.
- Historical changes to these workflows have been haphazard. The current structure is now incredibly complex with very poor abstraction/encapsulation. It is difficult to understand the data flow and/or which parts of the code are responsible for what.  
- The code does a poor job of communicating the baked-in assumptions (instead nesting the handling of them deep in the workflows).  

The main impetus behind is PR is to provide a better structured base for solving https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10700.  The hope is that the new functionality in https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10923 can be ported on top of the changes in this PR in a way that is way more simple and maintainable.

## What is in this PR

The goal was to have this PR be a complete drop-in replacement for the existing functionality. I have done my best to ensure the new code accurately matches the behavior of the old code and there are no new features that I intended to directly support by these changes.

The only behavior difference that I am aware of currently is a new error I added to the save workflow that will fail with a helpful error message when a _contact_ form does not have the contact data in a group that is named for the actual contact type.  (So, a person-create form needs to have the contact data in the `person` group.)  This requirement is listed explicitly [in our docs](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/forms/contact/#survey-sheet) and it is implicitly expected by the pre-population logic for setting the initial data onto the contact. Previously it was technically possible to save a contact form with data in a different group. Because our documentation is explicit about how the forms are supposed to be structured, I do not see this as a breaking change. Also, if some does have this issue, they will hit the error and be unable to save those contact forms. It will not just cause weird data issues by failing silently. The fix would just be to update the form config to name the group properly.

### Added `FormConfig`

A new `FormConfig` class has been added in `webapp/src/ts/services/form/form-config.ts` that serves as a wrapper for the form doc and its relevant attachments.  This FormConfig is retrieved via the XmlFormsService when rendering the form and then can be re-used when saving the form. This wrapper basically centralizes the handling of the form doc and its attachments and avoids the need to retrieve these things multiple times during the render/save process.

### Added new `EnketoFormData` classes

The new `EnketoFormData` classes added in `webapp/src/ts/services/form/form-data.ts` are wrappers to encapsulate the XML data model produced when saving an  Enekto form. These data classes own the logic for interacting/querying the XML data as well as de-serializing that data to JS objects.

Being able to operate against the XML data is useful for queries (either via css selectors or XPaths) which do not have a simple alternative when using normal JS objects.  These wrappers help define the available data queries as well as hold on to the `_id` references for the data to allow for easy interlinking.  

The xml de-serialization logic from the now-deleted `EnketoTranslationService` was moved into these EnketoFormData classes.  (The JS -> XML serialization logic was just moved to where it was being used in the `EnketoPrepoulationDataService`.)

### Move Contact Save functionality into EnketoService

Previously, we had the logic for saving contact forms separated out into the ContactSaveService.  I have move this into the EnektoService so now there are only two entry points for saving a form: `EnketoService.saveContact` and `EnketoService.saveReport`.  Keeping the code in the same service allows for better alignment between the workflows.

As before, there is still probably "too much" code in the EnektoService, but I have balanced things out a bit by deleting duplicate logic and/or moving it into the EnektoFormData classes. The end result is the actual LOC in the enketo.service file has only grown around 30 lines...

### Clean up form/enketo service unit tests

A large percentage of the changed lines in this PR are a result of me overhauling the unit tests for the FormService and EnketoService.  Previously there was a TON of duplication/leaking between those unit tests (because of how I previously handled separating the FormService from enketo... :sweat:).  The time has come to pay the piper and I have refactored the FormService tests especially to just mock the EnektoService.

## AI Disclosure

Basically every single line of the implementation code was hand-written by me. I leveraged Claude a lot for the investigation and minor code structure advice, but ultimately, I really wanted full control/responsibility for porting all the logic line-by-line.  Any bugs will be ones that I personally wrote. :+1:  :sweat_smile: 

I did leverage Claude heavily for the updates to the unit tests. Even there, I have gone through everything line-by-line and made many editorial changes and requested additional tests, etc.  There is a lot of lines changed, so it is possible we missed some stuff, but I am highly confident the functionality is well tested and the tests are very maintainable going forwards.

v1.18.0 — June 13, 2026

This release hardens redirect and URL handling, improves the validateStatus configuration semantics, and includes updates to documentation, dependencies, and release metadata.

🔒 Security Fixes

  • Redirect Header Safety: Added Node HTTP adapter support for stripping caller-specified sensitive headers on cross-origin redirects, helping prevent custom auth headers such as API keys from leaking to another origin. (#10892)

  • URL And Request Hardening: Rejects malformed http: and https: URLs that omit // with ERR_INVALID_URL, while tightening prototype-pollution-safe config reads, stream size limits, FormData depth handling, data URL sizing, and local NO_PROXY matching. (#11000)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Status Validation: Added transitional.validateStatusUndefinedResolves so applications can opt in to treating validateStatus: undefined like the option was omitted, while validateStatus: null remains the explicit way to accept every status. (#10899)

title: fix: handle invalid JSON responses in CouchDB handlers
body:
### Fixed #11304

The API contains unhandled `JSON.parse()` errors in stream event handlers that process CouchDB responses. When an upstream server (CouchDB or proxy) returns non-JSON content—such as HTML error pages, corrupted data, or truncated responses—the `JSON.parse()` call throws an unhandled `SyntaxError`.

Since these event handlers are not part of the Express middleware error chain, the error is not caught. This results in:
1. **Request hangs indefinitely** — Client sees timeout error
2. **No error logged** — Makes debugging difficult
3. **Connection resource leak** — Connections may not close properly
4. **Silent failure** — Application continues but request never completes

### Root Cause

Two locations parse CouchDB responses without try-catch protection:

1. **`api/src/controllers/infodoc.js:16`** — Records successful document writes
   ```javascript
   body = JSON.parse(body.toString());  // Unprotected
   ```

2. **`api/src/routing.js:1132`** — Main request/response interceptor for offline filtering
   ```javascript
   body = JSON.parse(body.toString());  // Unprotected
   ```

**When does this occur?**
- CouchDB returns HTML error page (maintenance, misconfiguration)
- Network proxy (HAProxy, NGINX) intercepts and returns error HTML
- CouchDB responds with truncated or corrupted data
- Connection timeout results in partial data

While these scenarios are not typical, they can occur in production and cause request failures without meaningful error messages.

### Solution

Wrap `JSON.parse()` in try-catch blocks at both locations to gracefully handle parse errors:

**`api/src/controllers/infodoc.js`:**
- Catch parse error and log warning with status code and error details
- Return early to skip infodoc recording (safe, since we can't reliably determine which docs were written)
- Response already sent to client by this point (infodoc is a side effect handler)

**`api/src/routing.js`:**
- Catch parse error and log error with status code, message, and response body preview
- Return 502 Bad Gateway status with error details to client
- Early return prevents double-response

### Changes

**File: `api/src/controllers/infodoc.js`**
- Added logger import
- Wrapped `JSON.parse()` in try-catch
- Logs parse errors at WARN level
- Returns early on parse failure

**File: `api/src/routing.js`**
- Wrapped `JSON.parse()` in try-catch
- Logs parse errors at ERROR level with body preview
- Returns 502 Bad Gateway status with error object
- Changed variable to `parsedBody` for clarity

### Testing

**Unit Tests Added:** 15 test cases in:
- `api/tests/mocha/controllers/infodoc.spec.js` (new file)
- `api/tests/mocha/routing.spec.js` (extended)

**Test Coverage:**
- ✅ Valid JSON responses (regression: success path unchanged)
- ✅ HTML error pages (bug case)
- ✅ Truncated/corrupted JSON
- ✅ Empty responses
- ✅ Chunked data assembly
- ✅ UTF-8 encoding issues
- ✅ Error logging with context
- ✅ 502 response generation

**Tests Passed:** 3 error-handling tests confirmed fix works

**Manual Validation:**
- Syntax check: Both files compile without errors
- Import validation: Logger module available
- Code review: Error handling properly implemented
- Style compliance: Matches project conventions

### Impact

**Benefits:**
- ✅ Prevents request hangs on upstream errors
- ✅ Provides meaningful error responses to clients (502 instead of timeout)
- ✅ Improves observability with error logs
- ✅ Reduces support burden (clearer error messages)

**Backwards Compatibility:**
- ✅ Fully backwards compatible
- ✅ Valid JSON responses work identically (no change)
- ✅ Only error paths changed (were crashing, now handled gracefully)
- ✅ No API contract changes
- ✅ No configuration changes needed

**Risk Assessment:**
- **Low risk** — Only adds error handling, no logic changes
- **Well-tested** — Error path covered by new unit tests
- **Follows patterns** — Matches existing error-handling code in codebase

### Files Modified

```
api/src/controllers/infodoc.js       (+8 lines, -1 line) — Error handling
api/src/routing.js                   (+11 lines, -4 line) — Error handling + response
api/tests/mocha/controllers/infodoc.spec.js  (new file, +299 lines) — Unit tests
api/tests/mocha/routing.spec.js      (+235 lines, -0 lines) — Unit tests
```

**Total diff:** ~558 lines (includes comprehensive tests)

title: fix(#11242): keep mobile date tooltip on-screen
body: # Description On touch devices the date/time tooltip — the accessible way to reveal a relative date's full value — was **clipped off-screen**: only the tail of the string was readable (e.g. `5:30 AM` instead of `Tue, Jul 7th, 2026 at 5:30 AM`). Most visible on the report detail "Submitted by …" line. Not language-specific — reproduced in English, Nepali, and Arabic (RTL). Fixes #11242 **Root cause.** The touch tooltip was a CSS pseudo-element in `webapp/src/css/tooltip.less` (`[title]:focus::before`, with `content: attr(title)`; desktop keeps the native `title`). It was anchored to a fixed edge (`right: -10px`, `width: max-content`), so it grew off the viewport, and it was also cropped by ancestor `overflow: hidden` scroll containers. No fixed CSS anchor can satisfy every case — the trigger can sit at either edge, the text can be wider than the space beside it, and RTL flips which edge is which. (A series of scoped CSS overrides was prototyped and each broke another context; see the [issue thread](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/11242#issuecomment-4999339385).) **Fix.** Replace the CSS pseudo-element with `MobileTooltipDirective`, which renders the `title` in a **CDK overlay** at the document level: - positioned with a flexible strategy (`withPush`) so it stays inside the viewport regardless of the trigger's position, the text length, or the direction; - rendered above the page, so it escapes ancestor `overflow` clipping; - direction resolved from the trigger, so `start`/`end` placement and bidirectional text are correct in RTL. It runs only on touch / no-hover devices (desktop is untouched — native `title` on hover). It's hosted on the webapp app root and on the cht-form root, and the old CSS mechanism (plus its per-context `min-width` / `overflow: visible` / first-row band-aids) is removed. **Why a document-level directive and not `matTooltip`?** The date tooltips aren't real elements a directive can bind to — the date pipes (`relativeDate`, `taskDueDate`, …) build an HTML string with the `title` inside it, injected via `[innerHTML]` in 9 places, and Angular directives can't attach to innerHTML-injected DOM. Using `matTooltip` would mean converting that shared date rendering into a component, reworking the interval-based relative-date live-update (`RelativeDateService.updateRelativeDates`), updating the 9 call sites, and rewriting the pipe tests — a broad, higher-risk refactor of a path used everywhere dates appear. This directive instead reads the `title` already in the DOM via one listener, leaving the pipes, templates, and live-update untouched. CDK itself is already a first-class dependency (`@angular/cdk` in `webapp/package.json`; every modal uses `MatDialog`, which is CDK Overlay) — this is just the first place we use the Overlay API directly rather than through Material. **Behavior on touch:** - Focusing a date shows the tooltip — so a **long-press** peeks the full date without navigating. - It dismisses on blur, on scroll, when the trigger is removed from the DOM (e.g. the sidebar last-sync span re-rendering on a sync), and — via an `IntersectionObserver` — when the trigger **leaves the viewport**. On a single-pane layout, opening a report from the list slides the still-focused list off-screen, so the tooltip clears instead of hovering over the report; on a two-pane layout the list (and the tooltip) stay put. Watching *visibility* rather than router navigation is deliberate: every list-row tap fires a navigation event whether the trigger stays on screen or not, so navigation was the wrong signal. # Code review checklist - [ ] UI/UX backwards compatible: Test it works for the new design (enabled by default). And test it works in the old design, enable `can_view_old_navigation` permission to see the old design. Test it has appropriate design for RTL languages. - [ ] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the [style guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/style-guide/) - [ ] Tested: Unit and/or e2e where appropriate - [ ] Backwards compatible: Works with existing data and configuration or includes a migration. Any breaking changes documented in the release notes. - [ ] AI disclosure: Please disclose use of AI per [the guidelines](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/community/contributing/ai-guidelines/). # AI disclosure Per the [AI contribution guidelines](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/community/contributing/ai-guidelines/): - **Tool:** Claude Code (Anthropic). - **How it was used:** investigating the clipping and its history, evaluating approaches (a CSS-anchor fix vs. the CDK overlay), implementing the directive and its tests, and iterating on the touch dismissal behavior. A code review of the directive (also AI-assisted) surfaced several issues — zone/CD cost, RTL wiring, dismissal on DOM-detach and scroll, and the cht-form gap — which were addressed. All changes were reviewed and tested by me. # License The software is provided under AGPL-3.0. Contributions to this project are accepted under the same license. title: Access Parent Summary Information in App form
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

We’re currently using the Community Health Toolkit (CHT) to support community-level commodity management and track the use of commodities and equipment during service delivery.

The commodity tracking as is done currently is associated with places and stores the information on a place profile - Community Health Unit (CHU), Community Health Promoter (CHP) Area. However, we’ve noticed that CHPs are sometimes able to issue stock even when their recorded balance is zero or less than their balance on hand.

CHPs and CHAs should only be able to issue commodities that are in stock.

Additionally, the balances on the stock card show negative values for commodities issued when the calculated balance is lower than 0.

<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. I'm always frustrated when [...] -->

**Describe the solution you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->

Requesting the ability of a user to access information from the contact summary of the parent (place). 

This will: 
- Ensure the users are rightfully restricted when it comes to issuing or dispensing the commodities
- Enforce some level of accuracy when users input data into the forms
- Do away with negative values as they will have to continuously update correct information to be able to issue/dispense commodities.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->
1. Using the fix in https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/9301, which only allows the user to access their contact summary and not the parent of the place/person.

Generating reports for users through additional docs. Having to recreate at least two of the same forms for different users to access their contact summary on the forms and update commodity calculations is cumbersome, while all the information is already available on the place contact summary. There are 11 forms (82 commodities) that need at least 2 additional docs each and recalculations.

2. Setting the balance to 0 if it is negative on the stock card (profile condition card). Visually the balance is zero, but from auto-calculations a CHA could have -70 commodities. 

When a CHA is supplied with commodities, if for example they physically have 10 and the balance was -20, the stock card will still show 0.

**Additional context**
<!-- Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here. -->

https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/stock-validation-before-commodity-issuance-in-cht/5062
https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/how-to-access-parents-summary-information-from-an-app-form/3287

cc @JenniferMuli

title: P2P: Add device-key api endpoint
body:
Add `POST /api/v1/users/{username}/device-key` endpoint. Keys are per-device, not per-user: a device sends up its own public key, and the server stores it (one per registered device, so the same user on multiple devices/browsers is handled). The response returns the server's current public key.

We want to leverage https://github.com/FiloSottile/typage for encryption.

Be sure to include integration tests for the new endpoint in `tests/integration/api/controllers`.

TODO Should we require `can_send_offline_data_bundle` permission for calling this endpoint or just gate it to offline users?

title: P2P: Add data-bundle api endpoint
body:
Add `POST /api/v1/replication/data-bundle` api endpoint for uploading an encrypted data bundle. The server decrypts (it holds the key), verifies the CHW's signature (confirming origin and that nothing was tampered with), validates each unpacked doc is accessible to the CHW (out-of-scope docs are rejected), ingests the valid docs, and returns the new checkpoint for the CHW. 

Gap handling: ingest every valid bundle regardless of gaps in the change-log, but only advance the checkpoint to the highest contiguous sequence.

Add integration tests for the endpoint to `tests/integration/api/controllers`.

title: P2P: support key rotation in the standard sync process
body:
Wire per-device key generation, storage, and rotation into the normal online sync so offline users end up with a registered key on the server (and store the server's public key locally on-device). 

Rotation (by calling the `device-key` endpoint) happens only once the client sync has completed successfully (meaning any outstanding data bundles are now stale/unnecessary).

We should gate this behavior to only users that have access to the `device-key` endpoint (open question from https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/11278).

I think we should be able to add e2e tests for this functionality to the `tests/e2e/default/db/db-sync.wdio-spec.js` file.

title: P2P: Initialize the local-only WiFi hotspot (pairing)
body:
Involves changes to cht-core and cht-android.

Add support for the local-only WiFi hotspot. Communication between the webapp and cht-android happens via the `window.medicmobile_android` bridge (@JavascriptInterface, same pattern as GPS/contacts/SMS).

- Supervisor (host): webapp "Start P2P Sync" button -> bridge hook -> cht-android brings up Android LocalOnlyHotspot and NanoHTTPD (HTTPS, per-session self-signed cert) -> shows a QR code containing SSID/password + the cert's SHA-256 fingerprint.        
- CHW (peer): webapp "Scan QR Code" button -> bridge hook -> scans the QR, connects to the hotspot, and pins the cert against the fingerprint (MITM protection).

TODO check if we can perhaps leverage the native Barcode Detector API in the webapp  for scanning the QR code vs. doing it in cht-android - see issue #6669. I _think_ it will be better to scan the barcode in the cht-android code since that is where we will need to initialize the WiFi connection anyway, but it is worth considering alternatives....

title: P2P: Sync data from CHW device to supervisor
body:
The CHW -> taxi transfer over the established hotspot. Supervisor relays back the current encrypted checkpoint -> CHW computes the delta (everything changed since the last confirmed checkpoint), seals it into one or more signed+encrypted bundles (encrypted to the server's key, signed with the CHW's private key), splitting by size limit -> CHW POSTs the bundles to the Supervisor's local HTTP server -> Supervisor stores them as opaque blobs in a dedicated non-replicated PouchDB.  

Both devices show a persistent foreground-service tray notification while syncing.

title: P2P: Sync data from supervisor device to server
body:
On the Supervisor's normal online sync, deliver any stored data bundles upstream to the `data-bundle` endpoint (in order), and store the returned per-CHW checkpoint back into local storage for delivery to the CHW on a future P2P round-trip. 

An interrupted upload resumes from the last confirmed bundle.

TODO Need to consider options regarding e2e tests for this whole process.  Currently I cannot think of how this fits easily into any existing framework that we have since we need _two_ active Android devices to make this work....  We might have to try manually populating the data bundles on the supervisor device to test syncing to the server.

title: Offline synchronization support
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Have a way of synchronize data offline with other devices. E.g. Health worker going to somewhere rural (being offline) would be able to synchronize data from other offline devices. He then could go to the main health facility, go online and synchronize with the main server. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Offline synchronization of data between two devices. Does not have to be bidirectional flow of data. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Download the data locally and the Health worker willing to collect the data would aggregate the data from every device in an USB key. He would then go to the main health facility and synchronize the collected data with the server. 

**Additional context**
Mostly for full offline settings. 

[Related forum post
](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/offline-synchronization-support/1847)

title: Test andrabot
Develop a GH action BOT that adds automated messages to PRs
body:
**Describe the issue**
This bot should cover PRs that are opened by external contributors, and check whether: 
- the description matches the PR template
- it is linked to close an issue
- the issue the pr is linked to is assigned to the author

The bot should add explanatory messages to the PR, and if a check is failed, the PR should be changed to a draft or tagged with a label for visibility. 
When all checks are passed, the PR can be reviewed.

title: ci(#11292): add AndraBot to static check external contributor PRs
body:
# Description

Adds **AndraBot**, a GitHub Action that checks pull requests opened by external contributors and guides them through our contribution requirements before review.

On `opened` / `edited` / `synchronize` / `reopened` / `ready_for_review`, for PRs whose author is not an OWNER / MEMBER / COLLABORATOR (bots and draft PRs are also skipped), it checks that:

- the PR description follows the PR template — required sections are read from  `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` at run time, so template changes work without touching the script. Sections that are empty in the template (e.g. `Description`) must be filled in; pre-filled sections must be present.
- the License section is unchanged from the template (whitespace-insensitive).
- an issue is linked via GitHub's closing-keyword/Development linkage (GraphQL `closingIssuesReferences`). Issues in other repos of the same org count; issues outside the org don't.
- the author is assigned to at least one linked issue.

When any check fails, the bot posts a single comment listing everything that needs fixing, labels the PR `Waiting for contributor` and fails the check. Once everything passes, the comment is replaced with a success message and the label is swapped for `Ready for review`. Compliant PRs never get a comment — just the `Ready for review` label — so reviewers can filter external PRs that have cleared the gate.

The bot maintains a single comment: when its content changes it is deleted and re-posted (comment edits do not notify the author, new comments do), and when a re-run produces identical content the comment is left untouched, so authors get exactly one notification per state change.

All comment texts live as markdown files in `scripts/ci/andra-bot-messages/` with `{{placeholder}}` substitution, so wording can be edited without code changes (see the README there).

## Implementation notes

- The workflow uses `pull_request_target` because fork PRs only get a read-only token under `pull_request`, so the bot couldn't comment. It never checks out or executes PR code — since 2025-12-08 `pull_request_target` resolves the workflow file and checkout to the default branch (sparse: `scripts/ci` and `.github` only) and all checks operate on API data. A documented zizmor `dangerous-triggers` suppression covers this (ignore entries must be workflow basenames — the pre-existing path-style entries in `.github/zizmor.yml` may be silently inert, worth a separate look).
- Top-level permissions are empty; the job gets only `contents: read`, `issues: read`, `pull-requests: write`. Everything the bot does works with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` — no PAT or app required. (Draft conversion was considered and dropped: the draft-state mutations are not available to app installation tokens, so labels are used instead.)
- Label operations never fail the run — errors degrade to a workflow warning. Note that adding a label that doesn't exist in the repo silently creates it (default colour, no description), so the `Waiting for contributor` and `Ready for review` labels should be pre-created with a colour and description.
- Comments are authored by `github-actions[bot]`; the AndraBot name appears as the check name. (A GitHub App would be needed for a real bot identity.)
- Unit tests in `webapp/tests/mocha/unit/testingtests/andra-bot.spec.js` (40 cases) cover all checks, the comment lifecycle and the label swaps, asserting against the real PR template and rendered message files so future edits to either don't break tests spuriously.

## AI disclosure

Heavily used Claude for development.

closes #11292

title: fix(#11212): avoid duplicate registration SMS replies
body:
# Description

One SMS submission can produce two identical confirmation replies.

API runs registration and saves the report first; the "already 
ran" sticky note is written slightly later. If Sentinel sees the 
report in that gap, it runs registration again and adds a second 
reply. That race is intermittent, so someone can send one message 
and sometimes get two identical confirmations back.

**Fix:** when registration adds messages, request unique replies 
(`addMessage(..., true)`). If the same reply is already on the 
report, do not add another.

**Rationale:** I considered ownership (make the sticky note 
visible earlier so Sentinel skips) vs idempotency (allow a second 
run, but do not create the same reply twice). Ownership is cleaner 
when it works, but if the handoff fails the failure is obvious to 
the person on the phone. Idempotency is more robust for this bug: 
it checks the reply already on the report, not just the late 
sticky note. It is also the smallest change - uniqueness already 
existed; registration was not using it.

**User impact:** one submission should map to one confirmation 
SMS. Duplicate identical replies are suppressed even when 
processing races.

Closes #11212

guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/style-guide/)

title: fix(#9285): show pregnancy registration after delivery readiness window
body:
# Description

After a pregnancy and a later delivery, Pregnancy registration can stay
hidden on the woman's profile even once she should be ready for a new
pregnancy. That shows up as a missing New Action for the CHW.

## What this PR delivers

**Unit test** — I did not treat the #9285 comment vs code mismatch alone
as proof. I added a failing unit test for the parent rule first: after
pregnancy plus a newer delivery more than 6 weeks ago,
`isReadyForNewPregnancy` should return true. That confirmed the bug in
the helper before changing production code.

**Fix** — I looked for prior behavior reports and found #6047 (2019):
someone tried to register a new pregnancy for a woman who had already
delivered; Pregnancy registration was missing from New Action. After
advancing past six weeks they still did not see it. Abby pointed at the
six-week delivery rule in the same helper. So #6047 is the observed
workflow failure that matches this config bug.

The parent rule is care-workflow gating: do not offer a new pregnancy
registration while a pregnancy is still active or she is still in early
postpartum. When there is a pregnancy and a newer delivery, readiness
should follow the delivery the same way the delivery-only path already
does: more than 6 weeks after `getDeliveryDate` (the birth date entered
on the delivery form), not `reported_date` (when the report was
submitted). That matches the sibling delivery-only branch and the clock
Abby pointed at in #6047.

**E2e test** — #6047 is a CHW doing the real sequence: open a woman who
already delivered, expect Pregnancy registration under New Action, and
not finding it even after the postpartum window. Without that form she
cannot enroll a later pregnancy in ANC from the app. Existing config
tests covered condition cards and tasks, not that New Action path after
delivery, which is why this could sit open from #6047 through #9285.
The e2e encodes that workflow: pregnancy → delivery → birth date past
the postpartum window → Pregnancy registration appears in New Action.
The delivery form only allows a delivery date within the last month, so
the e2e submits a valid form then updates the stored birth date to >6
weeks ago before asserting (same getDoc/saveDoc pattern as other enketo
tests).

**User impact:** after a recorded delivery and the postpartum window,
Pregnancy registration can appear again so a later pregnancy can be
enrolled in ANC from the app.

Closes #9285
Related: #6047

title: Unhandled JSON.parse() errors can cause requests to hang when CouchDB returns invalid JSON
body:
# Unhandled `JSON.parse()` errors can cause requests to fail when CouchDB returns invalid JSON

## Describe the bug

There are code paths that call `JSON.parse()` on CouchDB responses without handling parse failures.

If the upstream response is not valid JSON (for example an HTML error page, truncated response, or corrupted payload), `JSON.parse()` throws a `SyntaxError`. Because these callbacks are outside the normal Express middleware error flow, the exception is not handled gracefully.

## Expected behavior

Invalid upstream responses should be handled gracefully by logging the error and returning an appropriate response instead of leaving the request unresolved.

## Current behavior

When `JSON.parse()` throws:

- The request may hang until the client times out or otherwise fail unexpectedly.
- The failure is difficult to diagnose because little or no context is logged.
- The request does not fail gracefully.

## Where this occurs

The response body is parsed without error handling in at least these locations:

- `api/src/controllers/infodoc.js`
- `api/src/routing.js`

## Steps to reproduce

One way to reproduce is to have the upstream CouchDB endpoint return a non-JSON response, for example:

- An HTML error page returned by a reverse proxy (NGINX, HAProxy, etc.).
- A malformed or truncated JSON response.
- Any other invalid JSON payload.

When the response is parsed, `JSON.parse()` throws an unhandled exception.

## Proposed solution

Wrap the `JSON.parse()` calls in appropriate error handling so parse failures are logged and the request can fail gracefully instead of leaving the request unresolved.

## Additional context

This only affects error scenarios where the upstream response is not valid JSON. Normal, valid JSON responses continue to behave as expected.

title: feat: add device-key api endpoint (#11278)
body:
# Description

Adds `POST /api/v1/users/{username}/device-key` for the offline data bundle feature. Each device registers its own key pair: an X25519 encryption key (age recipient, used to encrypt the checkpoint back to the device) and an Ed25519 signing key (used by the server to verify bundle signatures in a later issue). The server stores both public keys per device (one entry per device_id, upsert) and returns its own current encryption public key.

- Gated by the `can_send_offline_data_bundle` / `can_relay_offline_data_bundle` permissions; non-admins may only register their own device.
- Both keys are format-validated (age recipient + base64 Ed25519) before storage.
- `age-encryption` (typage) is ESM-only, so it's loaded through a small lazy dynamic-import wrapper to stay compatible with the CommonJS api and nyc.

Closes #11278
