title: Add basic CI support for AI PR review
body:
## Describe the issue

LLM-supported coding has increased the velocity with which code can be written. However, those code changes must still be reviewed in a PR by a human before being accepted.  Properly reviewing a pull request is a non-trivial task and a large percentage of maintainers' time is spent on this.  The PR review is one of the primary bottlenecks in the CHT development process. Currently, many pull requests are sitting open, just waiting on reviews.

### Long-term Goal - ship better code faster

My overall goal around LLM-supported PR reviews is to _reduce the amount of time_ it takes for a human reviewer to effectively review a PR.  The primary way I want to do this is by ensuring the code changes in the PR are high-quality before a human reviewer ever looks at it. This is the same kind of value we get already from static analysis (SONAR/esLint/etc).  Code changes that are clean and bug-free at the start of the code review just take less time to review since the human reviewer does not have to engage in a feedback loop with the author to get the code cleaned up.

Beyond just a "smarter SA tool" for reviewing code correctness, LLMs also have the potential to be able to provide useful insights about things like: 
 
- Does the PR actually solve the issue?
- Does the PR do what it claims in the description?
- Did anything significant change in the PR that was not documented in the description?
- Should it be broken up into multiple smaller PRs?
- Is there a better way to solve the issue than the one chosen by the PR?

The LLM's answers to these questions should not be considered authoritative (or even correct), but they could be useful considerations for the author/reviewer. (Less about shipping faster, and more about shipping better...)

### Risks

#### Cost

Tokens are not free and a useful review will use a lot of tokens (though, my goal is to carefully design the review approach to make the most efficient cost-effective use of tokens).  We do have some pro-bono tokens currently that can be used particularly as we evaluate this functionality. One thing it will be important to measure is how many tokens it takes to review a PR of a particular size.  Going forwards we can use the learnings here to do a more informed cost-benefit analysis.

Especially for our initial "soft-launch" in this issue (and perhaps going forwards too, depending on how our policies/budget evolve) the AI review will only be _manually triggered_ by maintainers.  It will not automatically run on all PRs. 

#### Noise

In my initial testing, I have found that AI can provide very helpful review feedback.  However, going forwards we may find this does not hold true for many PRs.  Or, more likely, we identify some feedback that is more useful than others.  We should be able to tune the noise from the AI review, directing it to review certain things and not others, etc.  

Also, since the reviews will be manually triggered, any noise will be "self-service" 😅 and only heard when a maintainer wants to.  

#### Automation bias

One final risk I want to highlight here is the opposite of noise.  It is possible the review feedback will be so high quality that it gives the human reviewers a false sense of complacency when it comes to reviewing the code (assuming if there were problems in the PR, the AI would have caught it).  

Going forwards we need to be cognizant of this and as maintainers we will need to intentionally resist this tendency.  At the same time, I think that eventually we could able to build organizational confidence in some aspects of the AI reviewing such that it allows human reviewers to ignore some parts of the diff and focus their efforts on the more important aspects.  

For example, we _could_ decide that our automated combination of linting/test-execution/code-coverage/ai-review was sufficient to make a manual review of the unit tests in the PR unnecessary.  If we decide on that policy (as a team) then there would be no expectation for a reviewer to go line-by-line through unit tests on each PR.  (This is purely hypothetical for now, though, and the current expectation is still that all unit test changes are reviewed.)

## Describe the improvement you'd like

My plan for this issue is to add an new CI workflow that can only be triggered when a maintainer leaves a comment on a PR (e.g. starting with something like `/review`).  This workflow will launch two jobs:

- One job will use [alibaba/open-code-review](https://github.com/alibaba/open-code-review) to do a line-by-line review of the _code correctness_ (are there any logic bugs in the code? etc).  
  - OCR supports granular tuning of rules/files.
  - The output from OCR comes in the form of a PR review, complete with inline comments/suggestions on the relevant lines of code. 
- The other job will spin up a Claude Code instance to perform a more holistic (and open-ended) evaluation of the PR as a whole (backed by the context from the PR description and linked issues and maybe eventually the relevant plan/spec file). This is the piece that will answer many of the questions listed above like "Does the PR actually solve the issue?"
  - Currently, I am planning to implement this as a new skill in [medic/cht-ai-tools](https://github.com/medic/cht-ai-tools) (which would allow for re-use across repos and even for running locally).  

## Describe alternatives you've considered

### Code review as a service

CodeRabbit, GitHub Copilot, Quodo, etc.  More automated and less "roll your own", but also less flexible and portable.  I don't really like the idea of being vendor-locked.  At this time, one of the main reasons not to go this way is that it means we cannot use our free Anthropic credits....

Anthropic/Claude do offer a beta [code review service](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review).  Customization options and tuning are limited and it is billed separately from our API credits.... 😓 

My favorite option I found here was SonarCloud's [gitar](https://www.sonarsource.com/products/gitar/) (which does offer a free tier for open source repos).  We are getting good use out of Sonar's static analysis, so there is a natural fit. And Sonar is not one of those flash-in-the-pan VC-backed AI startups, so it seems like the service might actually still exist 3mo from now... 😅 

### Other open source options

#### pr-agent

[the-pr-agent/pr-agent](https://github.com/the-pr-agent/pr-agent) is one of the most popular projects in this space and I spent a lot of time evaluating it.  It supports the same two phase approach I am proposing where it does line-by-line code correctness checking as well as an overall evaluation of the PR holistically against the linked issues.  Ultimately I decided to not go with this library for a couple reasons:

- The overall health of the OCR project seems better
  - OCR has good momentum, lots of contributors, and some organizational backing that does not seem focused on pivoting the project in a commercial/proprietary direction (even if the org is Alibaba... 😬) 
  - pr-agent, on the other hand has a lot of marketshare from their first-mover status, but Quodo clearly dumped the project into the open source and has moved on with their commercial offering instead.  There is community support, but it is unclear how focused/dedicated it will be in the long-term.
- Supporting the more holistic side of the PR review is a big plus for pr-agent, but this probably needs to be the most subjective/custom part of the review. So, we get the most value from rolling-our-own here and there would be the most risk from the pr-agent side that its reviews would not be as useful/targeted as we needed.  
- Lastly, there is no way of getting around the fact that the pr-agent code/documentation is extremely _sloppy_.  The whole project feels a bit half-baked, like humans were not very involved in most of it... 🤦 

#### Claude Code plugins

There are a few official Anthropic "skills" for Claude: [pr-review-toolkit](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/main/plugins%2Fpr-review-toolkit), [code-review](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/main/plugins%2Fcode-review).  Neither of these seemed to really fulfill what we wanted to achieve. From a token efficiency perspective, I think it is best to keep the agent work very focused. It seems like these skills would probably not be sufficient for efficient and consistent reviews of large PRs...

#### Honorable Mention

[miracodeai/mira](https://github.com/miracodeai/mira) is a newer entry in the open source AI code review space.  Its pursuing a larger feature set than OCR, but does not have the same momentum.  I think it is worth keeping an eye on, though, because they could end up with something very compelling.

title: Capture video-playback telemetry for `media::video` form elements
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

We have incorporated  videos inside CHT forms to help CHWs explain concepts to clients during home visits and currently a set of short child-development clips inside the `infant_child` visit form (e.g. *Play 6–12 months*, *Talk 24–36 months*), embedded via `media::video::en/sw`.

We want to expand that library. Before we invest in creating more videos, we need to know whether the ones already deployed are actually being used. Right now we have no way to tell:

- Are CHWs tapping play on the videos at all?
- Which videos get played most / least often?
- Do CHWs play them all the way through, or stop halfway?
- Does play frequency vary by CHW, by facility, by client's age group?

Without answers, the program team is deciding "add more child-development videos" or "add malaria-prevention videos" or "add nutrition videos" blind. If CHWs are skipping the current videos entirely, the fix is behaviour change (training, form re-ordering, etc) rather than more content. If certain videos get watched and others don't, we need to understand why before duplicating patterns.

We looked at the existing telemetry captured in `medic-user-*-meta` and there's nothing media-related. CHT's telemetry today covers app performance (form load times, page render duration, sync duration, storage) but not media element interactions. We also checked whether the standard `<video>` element inside a form emits anything to telemetry but  we didn't fund any. 

The closest indirect signals we could use (time-on-form-page from telemetry; a required post-video question in the form itself) all rely on CHW self-report or proxies too weak to make content decisions on.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Extend CHT's telemetry to capture per-video interaction events when a `media::video` element renders inside a form, ideally including:

- **Play events** — video was tapped to play (with the video file name / form / question name)
- **Completion events** — video ran to `ended` (natural completion, not user-scrubbed)
- **Duration watched** — total seconds actually played, so partial views are visible (played 30% vs 90%)
- **Replay count** — how many times a CHW replayed within one form session

These would follow the existing telemetry doc pattern (per-user-per-month `telemetry-YYYY-MM-<user>-<device>`) so the aggregation and monitoring pipeline stays the same. Analytics teams could then answer "of the N `infant_child` visits this month, X played `play_6_12.mp4`, of which Y watched to completion, and average watch duration was Z seconds".

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- **A required post-video question in the form** ("What was the main message of the video?"). Zero engineering, works today, but it's CHW self-report — a CHW can fill in a plausible answer without showing the video, and we get no timing/completion detail.
- **Interpreting `page-render-time` telemetry** on the video's containing page. Long dwell doesn't necessarily mean "watched the video" — the CHW might be counselling the client verbally, or have left the tablet open. Too noisy for content-decision quality.


**Additional context**

For scale: the JnA app has around a thousand CHWs conducting daily home visits with a stable set of videos in-form. If we can validate video engagement before expanding the library, we can channel content-creation effort into the videos that actually reach caregivers. If we can't, we're guessing.

title: Switch bulk-delete to "soft-delete" instead of archive
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
The bulk-delete framework added to the feature branch in https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/11236 as based on the archiving functionality (being added in github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/11139).  However, after [significant discussion](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/how-should-we-handle-deleted-contacts-reports-in-cht-sync/5691) we have determined that archiving is not the best way to handle these deletes because the archived data is not removed from down-stream data stores (e.g. cht-sync > Postgres).  

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Instead of leveraging the archiving framework, we should update the Sentinal `batch-operations/archive.js` to just be `batch-operations/delete.js` and implement soft-delete's directly in that file (the logic should roughly parallel what we are already doing for archive).

- Add a new `medic-delete` database
- When the delete operation is executed:
  - Retrieve all the docs to be deleted: `await db.medic.allDocs({ attachments: true, keys: ids, include_docs: true, conflicts: true });`
  - Set `deleted_date` property.
  - Save them to the `medic-delete` database.
  - Purge the related info docs from the `medic-sentinel` database.
  - Delete the docs in the `medic` db (save them with only the `_deleted: true` property and nothing else).

title: Delete the demo config
body:
**Describe the issue**
In the CHT Core repo we [have 3 configs](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/config): Demo and Default and COVID-19.  The default config is what ships with every CHT deployment by default.  The Demo config is what runs on `demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org`.  However, the Demo config does not get updated like the default config does.  The default config is an integral part of CHT Core's CI, so is always up to date.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Like we did with [the standard config](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8757) some years ago, we should delete the demo config.  This will mean less tech debt and more focus on improving just one config instead of multiple.  

There's efforts to improve the demo config (add [landing page](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/11260) and add [ICCM](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/11259)), but these can just be done on the default config.  It'll be a big win for default config to [not have](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/11260) "No message selected" by default when you first log in. 



There will be some blockers and related cleanup in docs and other repos likely to achieve this - I'll look to link those issues! For example, the demo instance  `demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org` will need to be converted to use the default config instead of demo config.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Do nothing and keep maintaining both the demo and default configs.

title: feat(#11349): soft delete instead of archiving for bulk delete
body:
# Description

Closes #11349

Bulk delete has been copying docs to the archive database and purging them from `medic`. A purge leaves no trace in the changes feed, so downstream stores such as cht-sync never learn the doc is gone, which is what the [forum discussion](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/how-should-we-handle-deleted-contacts-reports-in-cht-sync/5691) settled. Docs are now copied to a new `medic-delete` database and deleted in `medic`, so the tombstone still reaches offline devices and everything downstream of them.

**How it works.** The sentinel `bulk-operations/archive.js` handler becomes `delete.js` and does the work directly rather than going through the archiving job framework. Per batch it reads the docs with their attachments, writes a copy carrying `deleted_date` to `medic-delete`, then deletes the docs in `medic`. A doc that is already deleted or purged is skipped, since there is nothing left to do for it. The copy is written before the delete, so a crash in between leaves a doc that is copied and still live, which re-running corrects; the other order could lose it. The copy keeps the original revision (`new_edits: false`), so a re-run is a no-op rather than a conflict.

**Two details beyond a straight port of the archive steps:**

- Every live leaf revision is deleted, not only the winner. Deleting just the winner would promote a conflict and the doc would come back. That is what `conflicts: true` on the read is for.
- `_conflicts` is a query time field rather than part of the document, so it is dropped from the stored copy.

**The action is renamed** from `archive` to `delete`, which also renames the key it contributes to the summary the endpoint returns, so `summary: { archive: { contacts, reports } }` is now `summary: { delete: { contacts, reports } }`.

**Replication needs no change.** `getDocIdsToDelete` already reports any doc whose `_all_docs` row is flagged deleted, so the tombstone is enough on its own and there is nothing to look up in `medic-delete`. The archive database check stays where it is, for the standalone archiving feature.

**Infodocs are left to `background-cleanup`**, which already marks the infodoc `_deleted` for every deleted doc it sees on the changes feed, so the handler does not touch them.

**`medic-delete` uses the default database security**, the same as `medic-archive`, and Sentinel creates it on its first write.

**Not in this PR.** The locking mechanism discussed on the issue is still open, pending the question about the fifth conflict check.

**Testing.** 12 unit tests for the handler, covering the copy-then-delete ordering, conflicting leaves, already deleted or purged docs, individually rejected writes, and each failure path. `unit-sentinel` 318 passing, above its coverage threshold. The delete integration tests assert the copy lands in `medic-delete` and that `medic` returns `reason: "deleted"` rather than `"missing"`, which is the behaviour the whole change is about.

title: Allow special large 4.21 deployments to archive data without reindexing mapreduce views
body:
Upgrading from 4.x to 5.x normally requires rebuilding all indexes in both the `medic` and `medic-client` ddocs.

Because rebuilding indexes take up so much extra space, this blocks large instance that are unable or unwilling to provision 5x space from upgrading.

[Archiving](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/11139) is expected to be released in 5.3, and is expected to significantly reduce the amount of disk space used by indexes.
If it was possible to archive **before** reindexing, it could unblock those large deployment from upgrading.

The majority of the view changes between 4.22 and 5.3.0 are removing views; especially freetext views and some map reduce views.
So the code mostly does not depend on changes to the views, and can still work if the views were still there.
The exception is [this change](https://github.com/medic/sht-core/pull/10325) to impact metrics, which may be less important than allowing the upgrade and can be temporarily disabled.

So, upgrading to a feature release which includes all the code from 5.3.0, but does not make any changes to the views since 4.22, would allow deployments to upgrade to a version with archiving without reindexing (except for nouveau). Then archive data to reduce the size of the indexes, and upgrade to 5.3.0 to actually remove the freetext views, when the reindexing would be much smaller.

title: feat(#11356): revert removing views
body:

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

Ships all of the 5.3 code with the `medic` and `medic-client` view definitions pinned to 4.22, so a 4.22 deployment can upgrade without rebuilding any mapreduce index. Large instances can then archive to shrink the dataset, and take the real index rebuild on the 5.3.0 upgrade afterwards, when it is far cheaper.

Most of the removed views are dead code on master — their consumers moved to nouveau or to the client-only `medic-offline-*` ddocs — so restoring them costs nothing but disk. Two exceptions needed code changes.

## Changes

**`medic-client` — restored to the 4.22 definitions (23 views)**
- Restored `contacts_by_freetext`, `contacts_by_type_freetext`, `reports_by_freetext`, `tasks_by_contact`, `total_clinics_by_facility`, `docs_by_id_lineage`, `registered_patients`
- Reverted the `doc_by_type` and `reports_by_subject` map functions
- Dropped the `_count` reduces on `contacts_by_type` and `reports_by_form`, restoring the old `reports_by_form/reduce.js`

**`medic` — restored to the 4.22 definitions (10 views)**
- Restored `docs_by_replication_key` and `doc_summaries_by_id`, the two largest indexes and the only files by which `medic` differed from 4.22

Neither is read by any code path: both consumers now use the nouveau `docs_by_replication_key` index. `medic-scripts` is left emptied as on master — that is a pure removal, so there is nothing to rebuild and the old index files are reclaimed at `_view_cleanup`.

**Code changes forced by the ddoc revert**
- `GET /api/v1/impact` returns `501`. The endpoint counts via the `_count` reduces added in #8340, which this PR removes. `api/src/services/impact.js` is left in place unused so 5.3.0 can restore the endpoint by reverting the controller alone. Its OpenAPI annotation is removed rather than given a fake success response, since Spectral requires every documented operation to declare a 2xx/3xx.
- Reverted #11215, so registration lookups use `registered_patients` again instead of `reports_by_subject`.

The six `reduce: false` call sites added by #8340 are left alone — they were defensive against the reduce that PR introduced, and are harmless no-ops without it.

title: Flaky api integration test: db-doc handler restricts offline users PUT
body:
**Describe the issue**

`tests/integration/api/controllers/db-doc.spec.js`, "db-doc handler > restricts offline users > PUT",
fails intermittently across unrelated branches:

```
  1) db-doc handler
       restricts offline users
         PUT:

      AssertionError: expected '3-' to equal '2-'
      + expected - actual

      -3-
      +2-

      at tests/integration/api/controllers/db-doc.spec.js:1682
```

Example run: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/runs/32158623452/job/95786035402 (branch
`11151-report-by-form-qualifier`).

The test saves four contacts, PUTs six updates as an offline user, waits for Sentinel, then asserts
the exact `_rev` prefix of each doc's infodoc:

```js
chai.expect(a1._rev.substring(0, 2)).to.equal('3-');
chai.expect(a2._rev.substring(0, 2)).to.equal('2-');
chai.expect(d1._rev.substring(0, 2)).to.equal('2-');   // :1682
...
```

Those numbers are only stable if API and Sentinel always write the infodoc in the same order, and
nothing guarantees that.

**What is racing**

For a newly created document, two independent processes write its infodoc.

API records the write from the proxy response handler in `api/src/controllers/infodoc.js:15`:

```js
proxyRes.on('end', () => {
  ...
  infodoc.recordDocumentWrite(body.id);            // :20
  ...
  infodoc.recordDocumentWrites(successfulWrites);  // :54
});
```

Nothing awaits this. It is dispatched *after* CouchDB has committed the document, and the HTTP
response returns to the client independently of whether it has finished.

Sentinel picks the same write up off the continuous changes feed. `processChange`
(`shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/index.js:91`) calls `infodoc.get(change)` at `:71`, which
goes to `resolveInfoDocs(changes, writeDirtyInfoDocs = true)` and creates the infodoc if it is
missing (`shared-libs/infodoc/src/infodoc.js:59-66`). It then writes again via `saveTransitions`.

Whoever gets there first creates it, which changes how many revisions the infodoc ends up with:

| order | writes | final infodoc rev |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API first | API creates (`1-`) → Sentinel `saveTransitions` (`2-`) | `2-` |
| Sentinel first | Sentinel creates (`1-`) → Sentinel `saveTransitions` (`2-`) → API `recordDocumentWrites` (`3-`) | `3-` |

`sentinelUtils.waitForSentinel` only waits on Sentinel, so the test can read the infodoc at either
count. Which one wins depends on how quickly API's unawaited write completes versus how quickly
Sentinel's transitions queue reaches the change — in practice, on whether Sentinel happens to be
idle. That is why it fails on branches that have nothing to do with infodocs.

Container logs from the run above show the inversion for `d_put_1`, the first of the four setup docs
and the only one Sentinel reached before API's write (`172.18.0.5` = sentinel, `172.18.0.7` = api):

```
15.740  sentinel  transitions: queue drained
15.783  sentinel  change event on doc d_put_1
15.879  api       recordDocumentWrites() timestamp
15.896  sentinel  nothing changed skipping saveDoc for doc d_put_1
15.942  sentinel  PUT /medic-test-sentinel/d_put_1-info 201
16.093  api       POST /medic-test-sentinel/_bulk_docs 201     <- third write
16.184  sentinel  a_put_1 processed   (after 16.093, API won)
16.302  sentinel  a_put_2 processed   (after 16.093, API won)
16.456  sentinel  d_put_2 processed   (after 16.093, API won)
```

Sentinel had just drained its queue, so it took the first change immediately and finished it in
~160ms — faster than API's unawaited round trip. The other three arrived after API's write and
asserted correctly, which is why the failure is a single off-by-one assertion rather than four.

**To reproduce**

Delay API's write so Sentinel always wins:

```js
// api/src/controllers/infodoc.js
setTimeout(() => infodoc.recordDocumentWrites(successfulWrites), 500);
```

```sh
npm run integration-all-local                        # builds images, runs the whole suite
npm run ci-integration-all -- \
  --spec tests/integration/api/controllers/db-doc.spec.js   # narrow, against a running stack
```

The `d1`/`a2`/`d2`/`n1` assertions then fail with `'3-'` on every run.

**Production consequence**

When sentinel creates the infodoc it does so from a change whose doc was fetched from CouchDB, so
`change.doc._rev` is always set:

```js
const infoDoc = blankInfoDoc(change.id, !change.doc._rev && Date.now());  // infodoc.js:59
```

`initial_replication_date` is therefore written as the string `'unknown'`, and
`recordDocumentWrite[s]` (`infodoc.js:178`, `:200`) only ever assigns `latest_replication_date`, so
it is never repaired. `change.info` is that same infodoc, so the muting transition runs in the same
pass with `'unknown'`:

```js
mutingUtils.isMutedInLineage(doc, new Date(infoDoc.initial_replication_date).getTime())  // muting.js:53
```

`new Date('unknown').getTime()` is `NaN`, and in `isMutedInLineage`
(`shared-libs/transitions/src/lib/muting_utils.js:285`) `new Date(parent.muted).getTime() <= NaN` is
always false, so a new contact created under a muted parent is not muted. More likely on a lightly
loaded server, for the same reason the test fails. That one CI run wrote 184 infodoc revisions
carrying `"initial_replication_date":"unknown"`.

**Related**

- #10875 - earlier flaky integration tests on API/Sentinel timing.
- #10748 - makes race conditions more likely by speeding up the time between sentinel and api
- #11326 / PR #11341 - removes `modifyInfoDoc`'s create-on-404 fallback. Adjacent, but a different
  creation site; it does not change the ordering described here.

This major release:

  • Converts the codebase to TypeScript
  • Updates the packaging for better ESM/CJS compatibility and modernizes the build output
  • Requires that action.type must be a string
  • Continues to mark createStore as deprecated

This release has breaking changes.

This release is part of a wave of major versions of all the Redux packages: Redux Toolkit 2.0, Redux core 5.0, React-Redux 9.0, Reselect 5.0, and Redux Thunk 3.0.

For full details on all of the breaking changes and other significant changes to all of those packages, see the "Migrating to RTK 2.0 and Redux 5.0" migration guide in the Redux docs.

title: feat(#8248): display UHC visit stats in the contact hierarchy view
body: # Description ## Problem UHC mode only surfaces "days since last visit" and "number of visits" in the contacts LHS list, which shows the level immediately below the user's facility. With hierarchies that have one or more levels *between* the CHW area and the household (e.g. `District → Supervisor Area → CHW Area → Village → Household`), CHWs see villages in the list instead of households, so UHC information is never visible and cannot be used to prioritise visits, even though the same information already appears for households in People search results. ## Solution Show the same UHC visit information (last-visited date, overdue styling, visit count vs. goal badge) on the children lists of the contact detail page, for every child whose contact type is configured with `count_visits: true`. This makes UHC mode usable at any hierarchy depth: opening a village/FCHV area shows each household's visit status directly. | Before | After | |:-:|:-:| | | | closes #8248 ## How it works - A new batched `UHCStatsService.getVisitStats` resolves visit stats for a whole children list at once, using the existing `contacts_by_last_visited` and `visits_by_date` views. It runs one keyed query for the last-visited dates of the displayed contacts, then per-contact visit queries (the same shape `getHomeVisitStats` has always used) only for contacts visited within the current UHC interval, batched to bound concurrency. The same path serves online and offline users: measured on a 10k-contact/20k-report device db, the keyed query takes ~6ms for a 50-child list vs ~300ms for the whole view (see benchmark in the issue), so stats are simply re-queried on refresh with no cache to keep current. - The badge formatting (last visited, overdue, visit count vs. goal) was extracted from `ContactsComponent` into a shared `UHCVisitDisplayService`, so the LHS list and the children lists render identically. The same service exposes `getChildrenVisitStats`, the children-list orchestration used by the contacts effects. - The children render immediately; visit stats load in the background and are merged into the rows by contact id when ready. - When a visit report about a displayed child syncs in, only the stats refresh (debounced), instead of reloading the whole profile. ## Testing - New/updated unit tests: `uhc-stats.service.spec.ts` (batched keyed stats, interval prefilter, bounded concurrency, aggregated per-contact failure handling, permission caching/retry), `uhc-visit-display.service.spec.ts` (badge formatting and children-list stats), `contacts.effects.spec.ts` (background stats load, debounced refresh, selection-change races), `contacts-content.component.spec.ts` (change filtering, stats-only refresh routing), `reducers/contacts.spec.ts` (merge by id), `contact-change-filter.service.spec.ts` (`isVisitReport`). - Manually validated on a `District → CHN Area → FCHV Area → Household` hierarchy with an offline user: badges match the LHS list and search results for the same households; title: Refactor reports-by-contact indexing to be done in `docs_by_replication_key`
body:
**Describe the issue**
The `reports_by_freetext` index contains [sketchy mapping for the `contact`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/776c51e580b1eab47999c51c27358ea76c0b8c1f/ddocs/medic-db/medic/nouveau/reports_by_freetext/index.js#L55) of the report that is [used by cht-conf](https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/blob/aec94134b1ff4e4bbdd5540501ad52aabf1bd66c/src/lib/api.js#L272) to find reports that were written by a given contact (important during the move-contacts action).

This mapping is super out of place because it really has nothing to do with "freetext" searching and, as far as I can tell, there is no real benefit to keeping this here in this index.  

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Instead, I would like to update the `docs_by_replication_key` index to properly handle the get-reports-by-contact functionality.  It is already [storing the "submitter" value](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/180c29ecf597407216bb1a292c6cfab1e2e780f1/ddocs/medic-db/medic/nouveau/docs_by_replication_key/index.js#L77) in the index.  We just need to update the index to actually [index the field](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/180c29ecf597407216bb1a292c6cfab1e2e780f1/ddocs/medic-db/medic/nouveau/docs_by_replication_key/index.js#L17).  

We can also update the offline `reports_by_freetext` view to [also not emit the contact value for the report](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/776c51e580b1eab47999c51c27358ea76c0b8c1f/webapp/src/js/bootstrapper/offline-ddocs/medic-offline-freetext/reports_by_freetext.js#L52).  This was only included here for feature parity with the server-side index.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

We could leave things how they are, but it is just confusing tech debt to have things this way.  Another issue with the current approach is that there is no good way right now to get the report+submitter id pairs with one query (without pulling back the whole docs).  The `reports_by_freetext` index does not store the submitter value and the `docs_by_replication_key` does not index the submitter value.  So, currently you have to query both to get the whole picture.

We could also just create a new index (none of the other existing indexes really seem to come even close to covering it).  However, this really seems relevant to `docs_by_replication_key` since most of the reason to care about getting reports-by-contact is because those are some of the reports accessible to replicate for the user.

title: Contacts list shows raw translation key `contact.last.visit.unknown` for never-visited contacts in UHC mode
body: **Describe the bug** With [UHC mode configured](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/building/forms/configuring/uhc-mode/#configuration), contacts that have never been visited show the raw translation key `contact.last.visit.unknown` as their row summary in the contacts list, instead of the translated "Last visit unknown" text. The code requests the key `contact.last.visit.unknown` (line 308), which does not exist in any translation file. Both naming variants already sit a few lines apart in the code: the other branch of the same method uses the correctly-named sibling `contact.last.visited.date` (line 315): https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/2ea5b4e759e391a8ee29803a1030aeb7ec521c7f/webapp/src/ts/modules/contacts/contacts.component.ts#L305-L318 The correct key, `contact.last.visited.unknown` ("Last visit unknown"), exists and is translated in all 10 languages shipped with cht-core: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/2ea5b4e759e391a8ee29803a1030aeb7ec521c7f/api/resources/translations/messages-en.properties#L462 **To Reproduce** 1. Configure UHC mode: `uhc.visit_count` in app settings, grant `can_view_last_visited_date` to an offline role, set `count_visits: true` on the household contact type. 2. Log in as an offline user with that role. 3. Go to the People tab, and sort by or view the list showing households. 4. A household with no visit reports shows `contact.last.visit.unknown` as its summary line. **Expected behavior** The row summary shows the translated `contact.last.visited.unknown` text ("Last visit unknown"). **Logs** **Screenshots** **Environment** - App: webapp - Version: 4.7.0 and later **Additional context** - This is a regression introduced in `4.7.0`: the cognitive-complexity refactor for #8803 (#8887, f21520d7) accidentally renamed the key while moving the code (`contact.last.visited.unknown` → `contact.last.visit.unknown`). - Deployments may have worked around this by defining a custom translation for `contact.last.visit.unknown`. After the fix such deployments will get the `contact.last.visited.unknown` text instead — stock, or their own custom translation of that key if they had one from before 4.7 — worth a line in the release notes. - The alternative — renaming the key in the translation files to match the code — was considered, but fixing the code seems preferable: `contact.last.visited.unknown` is the long-standing key name that deployment configs may target, it keeps the pair consistent with the sibling key `contact.last.visited.date` used within the same method. - Found while working on #8248, where the same display logic is reused for the contact detail page's children lists. Fixing it separately so it can be backported independently of that feature. - AI disclosure: the regression was identified, reproduced, and this report drafted with assistance from Claude Code, human-reviewed and verified. Per [the guidelines](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/community/contributing/ai-guidelines/).

title: fix(#10706): update delete bulk operation summary to match move
body:
# Description

Delete and Move share one OpenAPI summary schema, but they do not return the same shape.

Delete returns:

- `archive: { contacts, reports }`
- `set-contact: number`
- `delete-user: number`

Move returns:

- `set-parent: number`
- `set-contact: { reports, places }`

So `set-parent` is undocumented, and `set-contact` is declared as an integer while Move returns an object under that key. A generated client cannot parse that field without already knowing which endpoint produced it.

The shared `BulkOperationQueued` and `BulkOperationDryRun` responses are what forced one summary schema to cover both operations. This splits them into `DeleteContactSummary` and `MoveContactSummary`, each with its own queued and dry-run response, and points all four endpoints at the right one.

There is no runtime change. Both services already returned these shapes; only the description was wrong.

## Why this is safe to change now

These endpoints have not reached `master`, so the spec has never been published with them and no generated client depends on the old description. After the feature branch merges this becomes a published-contract change instead.

## Verification

- `node scripts/build/generate-openapi.js` succeeds and the spec lints
- All four endpoints reference the correct response component
- `BulkOperationSummary` is no longer present
- ESLint passes on the three changed files
- The generated `openapi.json` is not committed

## Interaction with #11355

This overlaps with #11355 only in the delete summary block, where that PR renames the runtime action from `archive` to `delete`. If this merges first, #11355 should keep `MoveContactSummary` and the endpoint-specific responses and change `DeleteContactSummary.archive` to `DeleteContactSummary.delete`.

Closes #10706

title: Add automatic archiving of outdated task documents
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
With the addition of [archiving](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/commit/fd7ab0310c3b00e070b408f01bd077d64614851e) on demand, there is a pathway to automatically archive documents that are out of active use (with certainty). 

Examples of such documents are, for example, tasks in terminal state older than 6 months, which are [already automatically purged](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/sentinel/src/lib/purging.js#L516). 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Remove the automatic taks purging, and enable automatic task archiving. 

**Additional context**
Some things need to be considered here: 
- for automatic purging, all that the users need to do is setup purging, and this is handled automatically
- archiving is turned on by default, and works on demand based on a user provided list of docs
- once this feature is enabled, there will be significant "catching up" when archiving runs, especially on instances that have lots of historical data. Likely slightly higher than the impact of purging the same tasks (because more writes are involved).

title: fix(#11370): find authored reports by submitter, not freetext contact
body:
# Description

Move stopped finding the reports its contacts authored after the feature branch was synced with master. Four integration tests catch it, all the same way:

```
set-contact: { places: 1, reports: 0 }   actual
set-contact: { places: 1, reports: 1 }   expected
```

The cause is #11371. It removed the `contact:<id>` emission from `reports_by_freetext`, on the grounds that a contact mapping had nothing to do with freetext search, and made `submitter` searchable on `docs_by_replication_key` instead. Move queries exactly that removed emission with `exact_match:"contact:<lowercased id>"`. #11371 landed on master on 26 August and move (#11311) merged into the feature branch on 26 August, so the two crossed and neither side saw the other. cht-conf's equivalent consumer was already migrated in medic/cht-conf#838.

Worth being explicit about the failure mode: nothing errors. A move silently skips every report its contacts authored and leaves them caching a lineage that no longer holds.

## The fix, which is also a simplification

Finding those reports previously took two index reads: a freetext query for the report ids, then an `_id` query on `docs_by_replication_key` to read the author out of stored fields, because `submitter` was stored but not searchable. Now that it is searchable, one query by `submitter` returns both the report and the author its guard has to check, so `getReportIdsByCreator` and `getReportAuthorIds` collapse into a single `getReportAuthorPairs`.

Two details the single query changes:

- Ids are matched **verbatim** rather than lowercased, because this index uses the keyword analyser. That is what the #11370 test for `submitter` does.
- Because chunked queries can each return the same report, hits are de-duplicated as they arrive rather than relying on a `Set` of ids built by a first pass.

## Blast radius

Move was the only cht-core consumer of the removed emission. The other `reports_by_freetext` references (`shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/report.ts`, `local/libs/nouveau.ts`, `api/src/services/monitoring.js`) are genuine freetext search and unaffected.

## Verification

- 25 unit tests passing in `api/tests/mocha/services/move-contact.spec.js`, rewritten for the single-query design
- `unit-api` 1729 passing, coverage above every threshold
- ESLint clean

The four integration tests that currently fail on #11275 are the regression test for this; they should pass with this change.

## Why this matters now

#11275 cannot go to master while move is broken on the feature branch.

Closes #10706

title: perf(#11376): auto archive tasks
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

feat(#1234): add hat wobble
^--^(#^--^): ^------------^
|     |      |
|     |      + - > subject
|     |
|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: build|feat|fix|perf|refactor|test|chore

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description
 Sentinel archives expired tasks and targets automatically, and stops purging them.

Once the job queue is drained, `fetchNextJob` builds one **automatic** job instead of returning nothing:

  - **tasks** — terminal tasks whose `emission.endDate` is older than 60 days, read from `medic/tasks_in_terminal_state`. 
  - **targets** — targets whose reporting interval tag is more than 6 months old

  Both go into a **single job** of at most `AUTO_ARCHIVE_JOB_SIZE` (50k) ids: tasks first, and targets are only read when the tasks don't fill it. The job is flagged `automatic: true`, so it is distinguishable in the job logs.

  **One automatic job per run.** This keeps manually queued jobs ahead of automatic ones. Jobs created during a run are told apart by their missing `_rev`, since `persistJob` doesn't write it back.

  **The expiration boundaries move to `archiving.js`.** `TASK_EXPIRATION_PERIOD` (60 days) and `TARGET_EXPIRATION_PERIOD` (6 months) are the same values purging used.

  **Breaking change**: tasks and targets are no longer purged

  `purgeTasks` and `purgeTargets` are removed from `purging.js`

closes #11376

title: feat(#11279): add data-bundle api endpoint
body:
Closes #11279

# Description

Adds `POST /api/v1/replication/data-bundle` for the offline data bundle feature. A relaying device (the taxi) uploads one or more encrypted bundles from an offline peer. Per bundle the server verifies the peer's signature, decrypts with the peer's per-device server key, validates each doc as the peer through the existing offline write-authz, ingests it, and returns a sealed checkpoint.

- Ingest uses `new_edits:false` so original revisions are preserved and a doc arriving via both P2P and direct sync dedups instead of conflicting.
- Gap handling: every valid bundle is ingested; the per-device checkpoint only advances to the highest contiguous sequence.
- The returned checkpoint is signed with the server's per-device key and encrypted to the device, so the taxi relays it blindly and the peer can trust it (an unsigned checkpoint could be forged, causing the peer to skip unsent data).

Bundle and token formats are documented in the service (canonicalisation, envelope, and sealed-checkpoint contracts) for the CHW client work in #11282 / #11283.

Builds on #11305 (device keys), which is now merged into `11284-offline-sync`, so this diff contains only the data-bundle changes.

title: Stale PRs are not automatically closed
body:
**Describe the issue**
The `Stale PRs` GH action should automatically close PRs that are marked as stale 10 days after after, however that is not happening, as can be seen in this PR https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10856 that has been stale from Jun 1st. 

Checking the GH action run logs, it seems that this PR, along with others were skipped because they were processed in a previous run. 

Apparently the action uses a cache to store previous runs, and because our repo cache settings are so persistent, the action read a 3 month old cache entry. 

After manually deleting the cache, I ran the action again, and this time the actual issue was illustrated: there is a limit of 30 operations per run: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/runs/33453666020/job/99721634481 and running the operations the 2nd time will read a persisted state from cache. 

It seems that the 3 month old cache entry failed to be cleared somehow, and it permanently cached that some PRs were already processed, preventing further checks. 
Apparently, the `actions: write` permission is required to _update_ the caches: https://github.com/actions/stale/issues/1159

Increasing the number of operations and adding the `actions: write` permission is likely to fix this.

title: feat(#11280): register device keys after a successful sync
body:
Closes #11280

# Description

Wires per-device offline data bundle keys into the normal sync. A user holding `can_send_offline_data_bundle` generates an ECDSA P-256 keypair with Web Crypto, registers the public half with `POST /api/v1/users/{username}/devices/{device_id}/keys`, and keeps the private half in IndexedDB as a non-extractable `CryptoKey`, with the server's encryption public key in the same record. The private key can sign and cannot be read back, by us or by anything with a dev console.

Registration runs once the startup session check resolves, and again after any fully successful sync, so a device does not depend on sync timing for its first key. `device_id` reuses the existing telemetry device id rather than introducing a second device identity.

**Not Ed25519**: Web Crypto only offers it from Chrome 137 and the webapp still supports far older, so the api verifies P-256 too.

Signing out drops the local key, so signing back in registers a fresh one. A password change (or deleting the user) drops every device key server side, and only the device that typed the new password knows it happened, so without this the others would come back believing their key was still good and be refused every time they sent anything.

The envelope now carries `payload_header_sha256`, and api checks it against the age header off the front of the stream before writing any doc. Without it the signature says who sent a bundle but not what is in it, so anyone able to read the server's public key off a device could pair their own ciphertext with a captured envelope. Hashing the header rather than the body is what keeps the check affordable, and it binds the body because the file key is wrapped inside that header to the server's key.

Also declares `can_send_offline_data_bundle` and `can_relay_offline_data_bundle` in the default app settings, with empty role lists (opt-in). Without this the permission the endpoints already enforce cannot be granted.

- [x] Backwards compatible: No behaviour change for users without the permission

title: feat: enhanced geo for contacts and tasks
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

feat(#1234): add hat wobble
^--^(#^--^): ^------------^
|     |      |
|     |      + - > subject
|     |
|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: build|feat|fix|perf|refactor|test|chore

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

<!-- DESCRIPTION -->

 Adds maps to contact profiles and the Tasks tab, rendered from OpenStreetMap vector tiles using Leaflet and usable offline.

  **Contact profile map** — a new `map` contact-summary filter. `MapPipe` validates the geolocation and the new `mm-map` component renders it. Templates branch on `field.filter === 'map'`. Adds the `geolocation` card to the default config.

  **Tasks map page** — new `/tasks/map` route with a toolbar button. Markers come from the filtered task list, so sidebar filters and search apply to the map too. A task's location is resolved from the task subject's own `geolocation`, falling back to its parent household; this reuses the lineage `tasks.component.ts` already fetches, so there are **no additional DB reads**. Markers are badged with patient name and task type, overdue tasks are coloured differently, and clicking one opens the task. The device position is drawn with its accuracy circle and each marker's distance appears in its label. The map opens centred on the user's facility.

  **Vector tiles instead of raster** — tiles come from `vector.openstreetmap.org` (Shortbread schema, z0–14) and are drawn on canvas by `protomaps-leaflet`, which overzooms z14 data for closer views. No WebGL requirement. The basemap style is hand-written (`map-style.ts`): water, land classes, buildings, four road tiers, rail, boundaries, and place/water/street labels — deliberately muted so markers stay dominant. Raster tiles are still used by the enketo geopicker and are untouched.

  **Offline** — a workbox `runtimeCaching` route caches tile responses (`CacheFirst`, 30-day expiry, entry cap, `purgeOnQuotaError` so tiles are evicted before replicated data). `MapTilesPrefetchService` then downloads the z14 tiles covering 5 km around the user's facility, at most once a day after a fully successful sync, skipping already-cached tiles and aborting cleanly if the connection drops. Exposed via `CHTCore.MapTiles` for inspection.

  **CSP fix (worth a look on its own)** — precached documents are replayed by the service worker together with their stored response headers, and the precache revision hashed only page content. A CSP-only change therefore produced an identical revision and **never reached existing clients** until `index.html` happened to change. The directives are now extracted into `api/src/csp.js`, shared by `routing.js` and the service-worker generator, and mixed into the precache revisions of the navigable documents so a policy change forces a refetch. This is a pre-existing bug, not one introduced here.

  Also fixes a few map-specific issues found while testing: Leaflet computing its layout before the container is laid out (ResizeObserver), mobile panes created off-screen at the correct size (one-shot deferred `invalidateSize`), and the mobile back button stranding the URL on `/tasks/map` (which then made the toolbar button a no-op) because `NavigationService.goBack()` only handles routes with an `:id`.

  Unit tests cover the pipe, the map component (markers, badges, user location, fixed centre, resize/teardown), the tasks map page, the prefetch service, and the updated service-worker config.

#11400

title: chore: bump sanitize-html from 2.17.5 to 2.17.7
body:
Bumps [sanitize-html](https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/tree/HEAD/packages/sanitize-html) from 2.17.5 to 2.17.7.
Changelog

Sourced from sanitize-html's changelog.

2.17.7 (2026-08-13)

Security

  • Fixed an XSS / URL scheme policy bypass affecting configurations that allow the SVG animation elements (animate, animateColor, animateMotion, animateTransform or set) together with attributeName and one of the animation value attributes. The default configuration was not affected, as these elements are not in the default allowedTags. apostrophecms was not affected. Thanks to koyokr for responsibly disclosing the vulnerability (GHSA-g8qq-57p8-ggw5).

2.17.6 (2026-07-10)

Fixes

  • Allow transformTags to emit text when textFilter is set, even if the tag is initially empty. This is consistent with the documentation. Thanks to spokodev for the fix.

Security

  • Fixed an XSS/allowlist bypass in which the contents of a raw-text element (textarea or xmp) nested inside an svg or math root were re-emitted without HTML-escaping. sanitize-html treated that content as inert raw text because htmlparser2 10.x classified raw-text elements by tag name and ignored the namespace, but a real HTML5 parser treats textarea/xmp as ordinary foreign elements inside SVG/MathML and re-parses their contents as live markup. As a result, markup and event-handler attributes that the allowlist never permitted (for example <svg><textarea><img src=x onerror=alert(1)>) could survive sanitization and execute in the browser. This is now fixed on two fronts: htmlparser2 was upgraded to 12.x, which is namespace-aware and parses textarea/xmp inside SVG/MathML as ordinary elements, so their non-allowlisted children (such as the injected img) are dropped by the allowlist instead of being preserved as raw text; and any raw-text content sanitize-html still emits for these tags (at HTML integration points such as foreignObject/mtext, or outside foreign content) is always HTML-escaped. The default configuration is not affected; the precondition is an allowedTags that includes svg or math together with textarea or xmp. Thanks to khoadb175 for responsibly disclosing the vulnerability.
  • Fixed a mutation-XSS / allowedTags bypass affecting configurations that allow the textarea or xmp raw-text tags. htmlparser2 10.x did not recognize an end tag with a trailing solidus (e.g. </textarea/>) as closing the element, so it kept the following markup as raw text, but a spec-compliant browser treats </textarea/> as a valid close and parses that markup as a live element. Because raw-text content was re-emitted without escaping, a payload such as <textarea></textarea/><img src=x onerror=...> could smuggle non-allowlisted, executable markup through the sanitizer. The default configuration was not affected. This is now defended at two layers: htmlparser2 was upgraded to 12.x, whose tokenizer closes these end tags correctly, and the raw text sanitize-html emits for these tags is always escaped so no < can reopen a tag when the output is re-parsed (textarea, an RCDATA element whose entities htmlparser2 decodes, is escaped like normal text, while xmp, a raw-text element, has only its angle brackets escaped to avoid double-encoding already-encoded entities). Because htmlparser2 is ESM-only from version 11 onward, sanitize-html now requires Node.js >=22.12.0 (the first 22.x release in which require() of an ES module is available unflagged). Thanks to bibu123456 for reporting the vulnerability and Kayiz-PT for coordinating the disclosure (GHSA-jxwj-j7wr-gfrw).

title: Add offline map support to the CHT
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
CHWs and supervisors capture household geolocations (#10676), but the app never shows them on a map. There is no way to:
  - see *where* a household is when viewing its contact profile — coordinates are stored and can be viewed in plain text only (or require some smart rendering / UI extensions for any kind of non-text rendering). 
  - plan a day of work from the tasks list: tasks show *who* and *when*, but not *where*
  - use any of this in the field, where connectivity is intermittent or absent — any map feature must keep working offline.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
*Contact profile map*
  - A new `map` contact-summary filter: a card field with `filter: 'map'` and a `contact.geolocation` value renders an interactive map centered on the household, with a marker. Invalid/missing coordinates render nothing.

*Tasks map page*
  - A new view under the Tasks tab showing one marker per task in the (filtered) task list.
  - A task's location is resolved from the task subject's `geolocation`, falling back to the subject's parent (a person's household). Overdue tasks get a distinct marker color.
  - Each marker shows a permanently visible distance badge (`315 m`, `4.1 km`) measured from the device's current position. Additionally the markers can show different data, that is TBD at this point.  Location failures (denied/unavailable/timeout) silently omit distances.
  - Tapping a marker opens the task.

## Solving displaying maps offline is the real core issue to be resolved here. 

  *Offline options*
  - Map tiles are OSMF vector tiles (Shortbread schema, `vector.openstreetmap.org`, zooms 0–14 with client-side overzoom), rendered on canvas via `protomaps-leaflet` 
  - The service worker runtime-caches tile responses. Any map viewed online keeps working offline; vector tiles make an area's tile set small enough (~120 tiles / a few MB for a 20 km square) that future area prefetch is feasible.

*Offline area coverage around the facility*
  - View-driven caching isn't enough — a map never opened online is blank in the field. The app should prefetch all tiles within a radius of the user's facility while online refreshing when the facility or radius changes.
  - The radius should be a deployment setting, defaulting to ~10 km. One production instance measured users' monthly movement at only ~5 km (a single project, but it suggests the default is on the low side; tile counts scale with radius²). Thank you @PrjShrestha for these real world numbers!! 
  
**Describe alternatives you've considered**

  - *OSM iframe embed*: simplest, but needs `frame-src` opened in the CSP, isn't styleable, can't work offline.
  - *Raster tiles* (Leaflet + `tile.openstreetmap.org`): fine online, but covering a 10 km radius offline is ~6,000 tiles / ~90 MB per user and breaches the OSM tile policy's bulk-download limits.
  - *MapLibre GL + ready-made Shortbread style*: full OSM cartography for free, but ~250 KB gzipped, needs WebGL (risky on low-end Androids), workers (`worker-src blob:`), and self-hosted glyphs/sprites. The fallback if the hand-written canvas style proves too limited.
  - *Tiles in PouchDB / per-facility extracts via replication*: reinvents tile caching with more moving parts.


 **Additional context**

  - Depends on stored contact geolocation (#10676).
  - CSP: `connect-src` gains `vector.openstreetmap.org`; no `frame-src` changes.
  - The tile URL should eventually be configurable so large deployments can point at a self-hosted Shortbread tile source; the OSMF service is community infrastructure.
  - Out of scope here, natural follow-up: explicit "download map for my area" prefetch (e.g. 1 km around the user's facility) with progress UI and a storage cap.

title: Create AI skill to help debug users who cannot login (specifically targeting users with too many docs)
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
"User X cannot log in" is one of the most common support escalations for CHT deployments, and it's deceptively hard to triage: upon logging in, users often see endless loading screens with no other symptoms. This is sometimes due to one-off server-side issues (with containers that are crashed, overloaded instances or downtime), but can persist for some users. The most likely cause for persistence is that the user has very many documents assigned to them. 
Even with the latest improvements in performance, a user with 1 million documents is likely to experience this (we have seen users with a million documents actually succeeding getting the list of document ids from the server, the first step in replication). 

Diagnosing that case requires knowledge that spans login, authorization, `replication_depth`, `needs_signoff`, purge rules, and version-specific endpoints. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**

An AI skill (per the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format — plain markdown + files, portable to any LLM/agent harness) that walks any CHT deployer through diagnosing why a user cannot log in, grounded in cht-core's actual code paths (exact endpoints, error strings, thresholds, log signatures).

 Key design points of the prototype:

- **Two execution modes, chosen by the user up front**: *autonomous* (the agent runs read-only diagnostics itself, credentials via session env vars) and *guided* (the agent emits copy-paste curl commands, the human runs them and pastes output back — works with any LLM, no tool access, and the agent never sees the instance URL or credentials).
- **Structured triage tree** covering: credentials/401s, rate-limiting (10 failures/10s, keyed on IP + username + password string), SSO/OIDC and token-login failures, `_users` vs `medic` user-doc inconsistencies, forced password change, missing `facility_id`, and — as the deepest branch — replication volume.
- **Too-many-docs deep-dive**: uses the same pathways replication uses (`/api/v1/users-info`, `medic/contacts_by_depth` per-depth histograms, `docs_by_replication_key` — Nouveau on ≥5.0.0, map view on 4.x) to attribute volume (contacts vs reports vs tasks, which branch of the hierarchy, which role's `replication_depth`) and produce a ranked remediation menu (purge rules, `replication_depth`, `needs_signoff` review, hierarchy changes, online role). Explicitly rules out "raise the limit" (hardcoded at 10,000).
- **Diagnose + recommend only** — the skill never modifies the instance.
- Version-aware: knows which endpoints exist since when (e.g. `replication-failure-logs` / `replication-health` since 5.2) and degrades gracefully on older instances.


**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Documentation-only: a troubleshooting guide on docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org
- Relying on the hosted CHT Docs / Code Context MCP servers alone
- A dedicated CLI tool: higher build/maintenance cost, and doesn't help users of chat-only AI tools; the guided mode covers that audience with zero tooling.

**Additional context**
A working prototype [exists](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/compare/debug-with-claude) (SKILL.md + triage-tree / too-many-docs / curl-cookbook references) and has been through several live test iterations. Open questions to resolve in this issue:

- Where should it live? (cht-core `.claude/skills/`, a dedicated repo, or alongside docs?)
- Testing protocol before recommending it to partners (guided-mode UX has needed several iterations: response latency, selection prompts vs free text, output filtering with `jq`).
- Whether to publish the MCP server as an installable package vs keeping it bundled.

title: chore: bump @xmldom/xmldom
body:
Bumps and [@xmldom/xmldom](https://github.com/xmldom/xmldom). These dependencies needed to be updated together. Updates `@xmldom/xmldom` from 0.9.10 to 0.9.12
Release notes

Sourced from @​xmldom/xmldom's releases.

0.9.12

Commits

Fixed

  • Security: parsing a deeply or repeatedly namespaced document no longer consumes quadratic memory; the in-scope namespace map is inherited through the prototype chain instead of being copied for every prefix-declaring element (O(N) instead of O(N²)), preventing a denial-of-service reachable from DOMParser.parseFromString with default options. Serialized output is byte-identical. GHSA-965w-775f-mr7g
  • Security: attribute de-duplication during parsing is now O(M) instead of O(M²); the NamedNodeMap parse-time dedup path uses a null-prototype membership index, so a well-formed document with a hostile number of duplicate attributes can no longer wedge the parse. Attribute order and duplicate resolution (last value wins, first position kept) are byte-identical, preserving the XML no-duplicate-attributes well-formedness constraint. GHSA-8344-3jmq-59r6
  • Security: HTML raw-text parsing no longer amplifies output on a missing or case-mismatched closing tag; the closing tag is matched case-insensitively per the WHATWG HTML RAWTEXT end-tag rule and a missing closing tag is handled explicitly, preventing a denial-of-service. Output for well-formed input is unchanged. GHSA-6mj3-qw4j-hgrw
  • Security: malformed-input recovery is now linear instead of quadratic — the malformed tag-name scan terminates at an embedded <, and Node.prototype.normalize() merges adjacent text nodes in O(K) instead of O(K²) (also reachable programmatically), per normalize() in the WHATWG DOM spec. DOM output is unchanged; only the reported error text differs. GHSA-93r5-fhx6-vmg9

title: chore: bump fast-uri from 3.1.5 to 3.1.7 in /webapp
body:
Bumps [fast-uri](https://github.com/fastify/fast-uri) from 3.1.5 to 3.1.7.
Release notes

Sourced from fast-uri's releases.

v3.1.7

⚠️ Security Warning

This is a security release that fixes the following high-severity security advisories:

  • GHSA-qw65-cvwx-89v3 — authority injection via an unvalidated port in serialize()
  • GHSA-58mr-gqgx-xq4g — host confusion via unbalanced or misplaced IP-literal brackets

Users of the v3.x release line should upgrade to v3.1.7.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/fastify/fast-uri/compare/v3.1.6...v3.1.7

v3.1.6

⚠️ Security Warning

This release addresses the following high-severity security advisories:

  • GHSA-5jgf-p345-68v8 — host confusion via skipped IDN canonicalization on scheme-relative references
  • GHSA-fph4-wmhf-6fwf — server-side request forgery via repeated hostname percent-decoding
  • GHSA-f65p-4m7j-42xc — server-side request forgery via malformed IPv6 normalization
  • GHSA-jqff-g426-hqxp — host confusion via percent-encoded scheme normalization

Users of the v3.x release line should upgrade to v3.1.6.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/fastify/fast-uri/compare/v3.1.5...v3.1.6

Commits
  • 412e40a Bumped v3.1.7
  • 9f4c943 fix: backport port and IP-literal validation to v3.x (#216)

body:

paths have moved: the releases folder is now `content/en/releases` rather
than `content/en/core/releases`, and the separate feature release page has
been folded into the main releases page (so the link needs the
`#feature-releases` anchor). This updates the links in
`z_release_patch.md`, `z_release_major.md` and `z_release_feature.md`.

While in there I also corrected the beta tag in the scalability step: it
read `<minor>-beta.1` but the tag built two lines above it is

Closes #11409.

#11409 is the dead-links half of #11361, split out so it can be fixed on
its own. The step-ordering review that #11361 also asks for is not
covered here - that needs someone who runs the release process - so

title: Dead links and a wrong beta tag name in the release issue templates
body:
**Describe the bug**

Three of the links in the release issue templates under
`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` no longer resolve, and one step names the wrong
tag. This is the "links that don't resolve" half of #11361, split out so
it can be fixed on its own.

`z_release_patch.md`, `z_release_major.md`, `z_release_feature.md`:

- The releases folder link points at
  `cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases`; the folder is now
  `content/en/releases`.
- `z_release_feature.md` links to a separate feature-release docs page
  that has been folded into the main releases page, so the link needs the
  `#feature-releases` anchor on that page instead.

`z_release_patch.md`, `z_release_major.md`:

- The scalability step tells the release manager to select the
  `<minor>-beta.1` tag, but the tag built two steps above it is
  `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`, i.e. `<patch>-beta.1`.

**To Reproduce**

1. Open a release issue from any of the three templates.
2. Follow the "Create a new document for the release in the releases
   folder" link - GitHub shows a 404.

**Expected behavior**

Every link in the release templates resolves, and the scalability step
names the tag that was actually created.

**Additional context**

The step-ordering review that #11361 also asks for is not covered here -
that needs someone who runs the release process. PR to follow for the
links and the tag name.

title: 5.3: `use_bikram_sambat_months` + Nepali language breaks form loading, contact creation and UI extensions
body: **Describe the bug** When `uhc.visit_count.use_bikram_sambat_months` is `true` and the user's language is Nepali, most of the webapp fails with `Error: Date outside supported range: २०२६-०९-१६ AD`. Root cause: `moment`'s built-in `ne` locale has a `postformat` hook that rewrites ASCII digits to Devanagari, and CHT sets that locale globally in [`language.service.ts:71`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/34500dbad0c3bebe2716a6b6c624da023f2d8689/webapp/src/ts/services/language.service.ts#L71). Two places in `rules-engine.service.ts` then format a date and pass the resulting **string** to `bikram-sambat`'s `toBik()` without forcing English. Note that in both, the Gregorian branch immediately below does call `.locale('en')` — only the Bikram Sambat branch missed it: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/34500dbad0c3bebe2716a6b6c624da023f2d8689/webapp/src/ts/services/rules-engine.service.ts#L604-L610 https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/34500dbad0c3bebe2716a6b6c624da023f2d8689/webapp/src/ts/services/rules-engine.service.ts#L623-L629 Under `ne` this yields `२०२६-०९-१६`. `toBik()` calls `Date.parse()` on it, gets `NaN`, so its `while (days > 0)` loop never runs and it falls through to the throw at `bikram-sambat/src/index.js:48`. **To Reproduce** 1. On a 5.3.0 instance, set `uhc.visit_count.use_bikram_sambat_months` to `true` (with `month_start_date: 1`). 2. Log in as an offline user whose contact is a person. 3. Switch the language to Nepali (नेपाली). 4. Open the `+` menu on Reports, or open a contact, or open a form from a task. 5. The list is empty / the page fails, and a feedback doc is recorded with the error above. **Expected behavior** Bikram Sambat reporting months work in Nepali. This feature is only useful to Nepali-language users, and Nepali is the only language in which it fails. **Logs** ``` Error: Date outside supported range: २०२६-०९-१६ AD at M (main.js:1:3434486) at n.getTargetIntervalTag (main.js:1:2661080) at Generator.next () at n.fetchTargetDocs (main.js:1:2664295) ``` **Screenshots** _Screenshots are from a dev instance; all names and phone numbers shown are anonymised test data._ **Environment** - Instance: test instance, also replicated locally - App: webapp - Version: 5.3.0 (build `5.3.0.33417070350`) - Language: `ne` (does not reproduce in `en`) **Additional context** Impact: everything below funnels into `_getTargetDocs` (`target-aggregates.service.ts:308`), which has no `try/catch`. Ranked by frequency in the captured console logs: | Console error | Source | Impact | | --- | --- | --- | | `Error fetching form definitions` | `app.component.ts:564`, `reports.component.ts:220` | App-wide; report form list / `+` menu empty on every route | | `Training Cards :: Error fetching forms.` | `training-cards.service.ts:176` | Training cards never appear | | `Error fetching allowed contact forms` | `contacts.component.ts:526`, `contacts-content.component.ts:366` | Cannot create contacts | | `Error initializing UI extension` | `ui-extensions-tab.component.ts` | Extension page shows "Error fetching ui-extension" wrapping a targets stack trace | | `Error selecting contact` | `contacts.effects.ts:190` | Contact detail page fails to load | | `Error fetching relevant forms` | `contacts-content.component.ts:402` | No form actions on a contact | | `Error loading form.` | `reports-add.component.ts:254`, `tasks-content.component.ts:304` | Forms will not open from a task or a new report | Not affected: current-month targets (uses `calendarIntervalService` directly), previous-month targets and `getReportingMonth` (both guarded, degrade silently to empty), the analytics aggregates page (throws but the component renders an error state), and all non-Nepali users. Proposed fix: force the English locale before formatting: ```js const bsEnd = toBik(moment(currentInterval.end).locale('en').format('YYYY-MM-DD')); ``` Four sites share the unlocalised pattern. The first two are what crash today; the other two are latent, and worse when they do fire, because neither surfaces an error — they silently produce Gregorian values instead: 1. [`rules-engine.service.ts:604`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/34500dbad0c3bebe2716a6b6c624da023f2d8689/webapp/src/ts/services/rules-engine.service.ts#L604) — `getTargetIntervalTag`, CURRENT period. **Crashing today.** 2. [`rules-engine.service.ts:623`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/34500dbad0c3bebe2716a6b6c624da023f2d8689/webapp/src/ts/services/rules-engine.service.ts#L623) — same method, PREVIOUS period. **Crashing today.** 3. [`shared-libs/calendar-interval/src/index.js:63`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/34500dbad0c3bebe2716a6b6c624da023f2d8689/shared-libs/calendar-interval/src/index.js#L63) — silently returns Gregorian reporting periods instead of Bikram Sambat ones. See the first comment. 4. [`shared-libs/rules-engine/src/provider-wireup.js:290,294,299`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/34500dbad0c3bebe2716a6b6c624da023f2d8689/shared-libs/rules-engine/src/provider-wireup.js#L285-L301) — `getTargetDocTag`, all three of its `.format()` calls. It *writes* the target doc tag that sites 1 and 2 read, so a divergence means reads and writes silently disagree. Only `:294` reaches `toBik` and can throw; `:290` (the `use_bikram_sambat_months: false` branch) and `:299` (the `catch` fallback) never throw at all — they would just write a Devanagari tag that no reader can match. `:290` is the branch the workaround below switches onto. Note for site 3: `referenceDate` there is caller-supplied and `.locale()` mutates in place, so it needs `referenceDate.clone().locale('en')`. Sites 1, 2 and 4 construct a fresh `moment` and can call `.locale('en')` directly. Already fixed elsewhere: [`format-date.service.ts:74`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/34500dbad0c3bebe2716a6b6c624da023f2d8689/webapp/src/ts/services/format-date.service.ts#L74) carries exactly this fix, with a comment referencing #11241 — same bug class, established fix pattern. `api/src/services/export/dhis.js:85` has the same shape but is safe: only the webapp and admin ever call `moment.locale()`, never API or sentinel. > **AI Disclosure:** Investigated and drafted with Claude Code (Opus 5). It traced the call path through the 5.3.0 source, reproduced the `moment`/`bikram-sambat` interaction locally, and queried the instance's feedback and target documents for the evidence cited here and in the first comment. I have reviewed the findings and the proposed fix.

title: fix(#11413): handle Nepali locale when calculating BS dates
body:
# Description

Fixes #11413.

When Moment's Nepali locale is active, its `postformat` hook converts formatted digits to Devanagari. The resulting date strings were passed to `bikram-sambat`, causing target interval lookups to throw or causing target document tags to diverge.

This change forces English formatting at the boundaries where Gregorian dates are serialized for Bikram Sambat conversion and target tags. The calendar interval path uses a cloned moment so caller and global locale state remain unchanged.

Regression coverage includes webapp current and previous interval tags, shared calendar interval calculation, target document tags with BS enabled, Gregorian mode, and the Gregorian fallback after conversion failure.

## Validation

- `shared-libs/calendar-interval`: 38 passing
- `shared-libs/rules-engine`: 224 passing
- Targeted webapp Karma: 59 tests completed; the local runner only reported Windows `EPERM` errors while writing generated coverage artifacts
