title: Flaky e2e test: ongoing-replication.wdio-spec.js
body:
**Describe the issue**
 `tests/e2e/default/db/ongoing-replication.wdio-spec.js` fails in the `ci-webdriver-default-data` job and does not recover after 3 retries. The failing tests vary between attempts, but `should download settings updates` failed in all 4 attempts.

Failing run: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/runs/33872718726/job/101027453190 (PR #11379, branch `11376-auto-archive-tasks`, commit 74cb5b91a)

The same spec failed the same way on `master` on 2026-08-24: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/runs/32771323761/job/97577328763 (`should download settings updates` + `should handle deletes` x3). 

 ## Results per attempt

  | Test | Attempt 1 | Attempt 2 | Attempt 3 | Attempt 4 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | should download new documents | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
  | should handle updates to existing documents | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
  | should download new forms and update forms | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
  | should download new languages and language updates | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
  | should download settings updates | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
  | should handle deletes | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |
  | should handle conflicts | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

  ## Errors

- `should download settings updates` (all attempts):
```
  AssertionError: expected undefined to equal true   // attempt 1
  AssertionError: expected null to equal true        // attempts 2-4
      at Context.<anonymous> (tests/e2e/default/db/ongoing-replication.wdio-spec.js:163:39)
```
preceded by: 
```
  Error: element ("mm-modal-layout") still not displayed after 10000ms
      at async closeReloadModal (tests/page-objects/default/common/common.wdio.page.js:419:7)
  Reload modal has not showed up
```

- `should handle updates to existing documents` (attempts 1, 2):
```
  AssertionError: expected false to equal true
      at Context.<anonymous> (tests/e2e/default/db/ongoing-replication.wdio-spec.js:112:66)
```
- `should handle deletes` (attempt 3):
```
  Error: Timeout of 240000ms exceeded. The execution in the test "ongoing replication should handle deletes" took too long.
```

- `should download new languages and language updates` (attempt 4): repeated
```
Error: waitUntil condition timed out after 10000ms
      at async syncAndWaitForSuccess (tests/page-objects/default/common/common.wdio.page.js:448:7)
```
  ending in `Error: Failed to sync after 10 retries`.


Job artifact (API, sentinel, haproxy and browser console logs): https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/runs/33872718726/artifacts/9938099160
  
  - In every `should download settings updates` failure, the API log shows the `PUT /api/v1/settings?replace=1` followed by `Detected settings change - reloading`, and ~2s later the client's `GET /api/v1/replication/get-ids` is logged with no status (`- - - ms`), i.e. the connection was closed before the response finished:
    12:52:22.298 RES: ... PUT /api/v1/settings?replace=1 HTTP/1.1 200 31 84.828 ms
    12:52:22.303 INFO: Detected settings change - reloading
    12:52:24.609 RES: ... GET /api/v1/replication/get-ids HTTP/1.1 - - - ms
    12:52:25.597 REQ: ... GET /medic-test/?end=should_download_settings_updates
  Same pattern at 12:54:12.053 and 12:56:01.280 for the retries. The test asserts on the local settings doc ~3s after the PUT, so it looks like the sync is being treated as finished (or the page reloaded) while the medic replication that would download the settings doc was aborted.
  - No 5xx responses in haproxy/API logs and no API/sentinel errors in the failure window.

title: chore: bump svgo from 4.0.2 to 4.1.0
body:
Bumps [svgo](https://github.com/svg/svgo) from 4.0.2 to 4.1.0.
Release notes

Sourced from svgo's releases.

v4.1.0

This minor release upgrades the SAX parser and introduces stricter XML validation. It also includes important security hardening for removeScripts, dependency updates, and improvements to the test and regression infrastructure.

Support SVGO

If SVGO is valuable to you or your organization, please consider supporting the project on OpenCollective. Your sponsorship helps fund ongoing maintenance and security work.

Stricter XML validation

SVGO now uses sax 1.6.1, upgraded from 1.5.0 (#2257).

The new parser version validates numeric character references against the ranges permitted by XML. Invalid references are now rejected in both text and attributes, including:

  • disallowed control characters such as &[#1](https://github.com/svg/svgo/issues/1);, , and ;
  • UTF-16 surrogate code points such as �;
  • invalid XML code points such as .

Valid boundary values—including U+0020, U+D7FF, U+E000, U+FFFD, and characters through U+10FFFF—remain supported.

Parser failures are consistently exposed as SvgoParserError errors with an Invalid character entity reason.

This is an intentional behavior change: malformed SVGs that were previously accepted may now produce a parser error, while valid XML documents are unaffected.

Security

The removeScripts plugin has been hardened against several script-execution bypasses:

  • Filters executable data: URLs containing HTML, XHTML, or SVG documents while preserving inert data such as PNG images, and filters legacy vbscript: URLs (#2263).
  • Sanitizes content inside SVG <foreignObject> elements by removing HTML event-handler attributes, srcdoc, and executable URLs from action, data, formaction, href, and src, while preserving non-executable HTML and visual content (#2264).
  • Recognizes namespace-prefixed SVG <a> elements and removes ASCII tabs and newlines before checking URL schemes, preventing values such as java&[#9](https://github.com/svg/svgo/issues/9);script: from bypassing detection while preserving elements in unrelated custom namespaces (#2268).

These changes address:

  • GHSA-4vpr-x523-8j87
  • GHSA-w27v-7q3p-w38r

Dependencies

  • Upgraded css-select to v6 and css-what to v7, and updated SVGO's custom selector adapter for css-select v6 (#2244).

Project maintenance

@​TrySound is back as an active SVGO maintainer.

Many thanks to @​KTibow, @​SethFalco, and @​XhmikosR for maintaining and improving SVGO over the past several years.

title: chore: bump hono from 4.13.1 to 4.13.7 in /webapp
body:
Bumps [hono](https://github.com/honojs/hono) from 4.13.1 to 4.13.7.
Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.13.7

Security fixes

This release includes a fix for the following security issue:

hono/jsx renders plain strings unescaped in boundary components, leading to XSS

Affects: Suspense, ErrorBoundary, and Context.Provider in hono/jsx, and renderToString() / renderToReadableStream() in hono/jsx/dom/server. Fixes missing HTML escaping for a plain string placed directly as a child or fallback of these components, or as the root value of the server rendering functions, so untrusted strings could be emitted as markup. GHSA-hxh3-vqpv-xpqv

Users who render untrusted strings inside Suspense, ErrorBoundary, or Context.Provider, or pass them directly to hono/jsx/dom/server, are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.

v4.13.6

What's Changed

  • fix(client): keep a param value of "index" in $url() and $path() in honojs/hono#5297
  • fix(client): normalize root WebSocket URLs in honojs/hono#5291
  • fix(types): allow symbol keys in Context get and set fallbacks in honojs/hono#5300
  • chore: bump editorconfig-checker in honojs/hono#5336
  • refactor(on-handler): use forEach for consistent handler iteration in honojs/hono#5326

Full Changelog: https://github.com/honojs/hono/compare/v4.13.5...v4.13.6

v4.13.5

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Query parser reads parameters after the URL fragment, causing cache-key and proxy interpretation differentials

Affects: Cache Middleware and applications behind a proxy, WAF, or logging layer that inspects query strings. Fixes query parsing that did not stop at the URL fragment, so a ? after a # was treated as the start of a query string and the application could read parameters that the other component never saw. GHSA-crvj-82cr-hjcx

Incomplete fix for CVE-2026-39408: toSSG() still writes files outside the output directory

Affects: toSSG() for Static Site Generation. Fixes a path normalization gap where consecutive parent-directory segments in ssgParams values were not fully collapsed, bypassing the containment check added in 4.12.12. GHSA-gqvv-2mrq-wpjv

Unbounded dot-notation nesting in parseBody() can cause memory exhaustion

Affects: parseBody() when dot-notation parsing is enabled. Fixes unbounded expansion of dot-separated field names, where a small request body could allocate a disproportionately large object graph and concurrent requests could exhaust the heap. GHSA-g6gw-c38x-mqfc

Users who use Cache Middleware, deploy behind a proxy or WAF that inspects query strings, use Static Site Generation, or use parseBody({ dot: true }) are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.

title: Contact page "1 week" / "2 weeks" task filter shows every task when the language is Nepali
body: **Describe the bug** On a contact's page, the Tasks card has "1 week", "2 weeks" and "View all" filters. With the app language set to Nepali, the 1-week and 2-week filters show every task, including tasks due weeks or months away. Cause: `filterTasks` builds the cutoff with `moment().add(weeks, 'weeks').format('YYYY-MM-DD')`. Under the Nepali locale, moment renders the digits in Devanagari, so the cutoff becomes something like `२०२६-०९-१६`. Task due dates are written by the rules engine as ASCII `YYYY-MM-DD` strings. Every ASCII digit sorts before every Devanagari digit, so `task.dueDate <= taskEndDate` is true for any pair of dates and the filter lets everything through. https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/372677567640d1d3e77e6e46f168fe69a8a9e218/webapp/src/ts/modules/contacts/contacts-content.component.ts#L348-L354 **To Reproduce** 1. Log in as an offline user who has a contact with a task due more than 7 days from today (9 days in the screenshots). 2. With the language set to English, open the contact. Under "1 week" the task is hidden and "No tasks in the next week." is shown; under "2 weeks" it appears. 3. Switch the language to Nepali (नेपाली) and open the same contact. 4. Under "1 हप्ता" the same task is listed. To see the due date on the task row as in the screenshots ("9 days left" / "९ दिन बाँकी"), set `task_day_limit` in app settings to at least the number of days until the task is due. The default is 4, so with default settings the row appears without a counter. The bug does not depend on this setting. **Expected behavior** The filter applies the same window in every language. A task due in 9 days is hidden under "1 week" and shown under "2 weeks", in Nepali as in English. **Logs** None. Nothing throws, so no console error and no feedback doc is written. **Screenshots** Week |English (correct)|Nepali (incorrect)| |:-:|:-:|:-:| 1|| 2|| **Environment** - Instance: local dev instance - Browser: Chrome - App: webapp - Version: 5.3.0 (present since 3.8.0) - Language: `ne`. Does not reproduce in `en`. **Additional context** Present since 3.8.0: #6041 changed this filter from a moment comparison to a string comparison, and the same commit moved the rules engine into `shared-libs`, where it formats due dates with a separate copy of moment that never has its locale set. Same root cause as #10525, #11241 and #11413: a date is formatted for machine use while the global moment locale is Nepali. Like #10525, this fails silently and shows wrong data rather than an error. The fix is the same one-liner used there: ```js const taskEndDate = weeks ? moment().add(weeks, 'weeks').locale('en').format('YYYY-MM-DD') : null; ``` **AI Disclosure:** Investigated and drafted with Claude Code (Fable 5.1); reproduced manually by me.

title: Use one helper for locale-independent date strings instead of per-site .locale('en') guards
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**

Three bugs so far have the same cause: a date is formatted with `moment(...).format('YYYY-MM-DD')`, the active Nepali locale rewrites the digits into Nepali numerals (Devanagari script: `2026-09-16` becomes `२०२६-०९-१६`), and the string is then fed to something that expects ASCII digits (`bikram-sambat`, a string comparison, a document id).

- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/10525
  - Aggregate targets showed 0 in Nepali. Fixed in #10423.
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/11413
  - Bikram Sambat months crashed form loading, contact pages and UI extensions in Nepali. Fix in #11414 (not merged yet), one `.locale('en')` at each of four sites.
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/11422
  - Contact page task filter shows every task in Nepali. Open.

The `.locale('en')` guard itself comes from the fix for a timezone bug, which had to start formatting dates as strings and added the guard so the new string could not pick up Nepali digits:

- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/11241

Three more sites make the same mistake, plus one related inconsistency the same helper would remove. None of the three is reachable today, for reasons that are accidental rather than designed, and each future caller has to rediscover the rule. It would be better to have one helper that produces the ASCII date string, so the next site is correct without anyone remembering it.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

Add one shared helper, for example in `@medic/calendar-interval` (already a dependency of both the rules engine and the webapp), along the lines of:

- `toLocalIsoDate(momentOrTimestamp)` returning `YYYY-MM-DD` in ASCII regardless of the global locale, and
- `getIntervalTag(interval, useBikramSambatMonths)` returning the `YYYY-MM` target-doc tag, used by both the code that writes target docs and the code that reads them.

Passing a `Date` to `bikram-sambat` instead of a string is not an alternative: `toBik()` is `Date.parse()` underneath, and #11241 showed that a full timestamp rolls the day in timezones ahead of UTC. The helper has to format the local calendar date.

Then move these call sites onto it:

1. Task state dates in the rules engine. `dueDate`, `startDate`, `endDate` and `timestampAsDate` are formatted with `YYYY-MM-DD`, saved into task docs and compared as plain strings. Not reachable today because code under `shared-libs/` is bundled with the root copy of moment, and only the webapp copy ever has its locale set. If the two copies are ever merged (a dependency bump could do it), the shared-lib fixes in #11414 become what keeps reporting periods and target tags on the Bikram Sambat calendar, and these lines become a real bug: every ASCII digit sorts below every Nepali digit, so mixed-locale comparisons go one way regardless of the dates.

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/372677567640d1d3e77e6e46f168fe69a8a9e218/shared-libs/rules-engine/src/task-states.js#L72-L74

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/372677567640d1d3e77e6e46f168fe69a8a9e218/shared-libs/rules-engine/src/task-states.js#L114

2. DHIS export. Another copy of the target-tag builder, outside the scope of #11414. Safe because nothing in API sets a locale, but it must produce exactly the same tag as `provider-wireup.getTargetDocTag` or the export reads zero target docs.

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/372677567640d1d3e77e6e46f168fe69a8a9e218/api/src/services/export/dhis.js#L82-L92

3. `bikram_sambat_date` in message-utils, raised in the review of #11414. It builds the `YYYY-MM-DD` string through `formatDate`, which uses the global locale unless one is passed. Not changed in #11414. Passing `'en'` closes it on its own; either way the string should come from the helper so the guard lives in one place. MoH Nepal SMS templates use `{{#bikram_sambat_date}}`.

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/372677567640d1d3e77e6e46f168fe69a8a9e218/shared-libs/message-utils/src/index.js#L327-L342

4. No fallback on the reading side. `getTargetIntervalTag` in the webapp has no `try/catch` around `toBik`, while `getTargetDocTag` (writer) and `calendar-interval.getInterval` both fall back to Gregorian. Only reachable for dates after 2034-04-13, where the library's data ends (BS 2090), but the writer and the reader behave differently when the conversion fails. A shared `getIntervalTag` means the two cannot behave differently.

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/5f6d5fb03aeb227b3c350442e64ca3e3c184616e/webapp/src/ts/services/rules-engine.service.ts#L604-L606

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/5f6d5fb03aeb227b3c350442e64ca3e3c184616e/shared-libs/rules-engine/src/provider-wireup.js#L285-L301

The sites that already carry a `.locale('en')` guard should move onto the helper as well, so there is one implementation of the rule instead of eleven copies: the four sites patched in #11414 (`calendar-interval`, `provider-wireup.getTargetDocTag`, and both branches of `getTargetIntervalTag`), `format-date.service.ts` from #11241, and the two in `date-filter.component.ts`.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Keep adding `.locale('en')` per site, as the fixes for #10525, #11241, #11413 and #11422 do. Works, but each new bug is only found in production by Nepali users, and with #11414 there are eleven such guards in five files.
- Stop setting the global moment locale in `language.service.ts` and pass the language explicitly to the display code (`FormatDateService`, the date filter, `message-utils.formatDate`, which already accepts a locale). This removes the whole class at once, but touches every display site and would need checking against the Enketo date widgets, so it is a larger change than a helper.

**Additional context**

- The contact page task filter has the same cause and is live for Nepali users today; it is reported separately as #11422 with its own one-line fix.
- The existing regression test for the pattern is in `format-date.service.spec.ts` (#11241): it defines a throwaway locale whose `postformat` hook emits Nepali digits. The helper's tests can reuse that.

**AI Disclosure:** Drafted with Claude Code (Fable 5.1), which located the remaining call sites and confirmed the bundling behaviour from the built `main.js`. I have reviewed the findings.

title: Release 5.3.1
body:
# Planning - CHT Community 

- [x] Create an GH Milestone for the release and add this issue to it.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.
- [x] Ensure that all issues are labeled correctly, particularly ensure that "Regressions" are labeled with "Affects: <version>" labels. The "Affects" label is used in a link in the Known Issues section of the release notes of that version so it has to match exactly. To make sure the label is correct go to the [release notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/releases/#release-notes) and ensure the issue is listed.
- [x] Assign a maintainer as Release Manager for this release.

# Development - Release Manager

When development is ready to begin one of the maintainers should be nominated as a Release Manager. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Ensure all tickets in the Milestone are closed and merged to `master`.
- [x] Check out the target release branch `<major>.<minor>.x`. For example if you're patching `5.2.0`, you would check out `5.2.x` branch.
- [x] Cherry-pick all commits from `master` into the target release branch that fix the issues in this patch release.
- [x]  Run `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major>.<minor>.<patch>` which sets version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json`. Commit these changes before the next step.
- [x] Run the [helm chart build script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/build/helm/package-chart.sh) (eg `./package-chart.sh 5.3.0`). This creates a tarball and updates `index.yaml` for the helm chart. Commit these changes as we'll need to cherry-pick it later to `master`.

# Releasing - Release Manager

Once all issues have been merged into `master` then the release process can start:

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by creating a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`) and then push it (e.g. `git push origin tag  <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`).
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully and images are built, notify the community by creating a post titled `<major>.<minor>.<patch> Beta Releases` in the [development](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/development/7) category of the CHT forum using this [template](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/new-topic?title=%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.%3Cpatch%3E%20Beta%20Releases&body=Hi%20Everyone%0AI%E2%80%99ve%20just%20created%20the%20%60%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.%3Cpatch%3E-beta.1%60%20tag.%0APlease%20let%20me%20know%20if%20there%E2%80%99s%20any%20final%20update%20we%20need%20to%20make.%0AIf%20all%20is%20good%2C%20then%20in%2024h%2C%20I%20will%20start%20the%20release.%20Thanks%21&category=development).
- [x] Go to the [scalability action](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/workflows/scalability.yml) and on the top right, click into "Run workflow".  Under "Use workflow from" first choose "tags" then select the `<major>.<minor>.<minor>-beta.1` tag created above. Then "Run workflow". Once it passes, check for the scalability results  ["results" directory](https://github.com/medic/scalability-results/tree/main/results). More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/tests/scalability#readme).
- [x] Go to the [Issues tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues) and filter the issues with `is:issue label:"Affects: 5.x.x" ` , replace `5.x.x` with the previous version number. Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 5.x.x` label.
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/releases/) page:
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labeled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
  - [x] Go to the [Release notes generator](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/workflows/release-notes.yml) and Follow [the docs](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/scripts/release-notes) for how to create the release notes, being for check for, and fix, errors.  When there are no errors, download the artifact that the release notes.
  - [x] Move the document you just downloaded into the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/releases), naming it `<major>_<minor>_<patch>.md` (eg `5_3_0.md`)
  - [x] Collect known migration steps, descriptions, screenshots, videos, data, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. This information should already be on the issue, but if not, prompt the change author to provide it.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Edit the main release notes `_index.md` [page](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/blob/main/content/en/releases/_index.md) to add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions) and update the EOL date of the previous release. Update the status of any releases that are past their End Of Life date. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page, being sure to include the date of the release.
  - [x] Ensure that the release notes PR is merged before moving to next step.
- [x] To ensure helm charts are published, open a PR against `master` to cherry-pick the helm chart commit from the target release branch. Make sure this PR is merged before proceeding. 
- [x] Create a [new release](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases/new) in GitHub, with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, from the release branch created above as the target branch. Click on the "Choose a tag" dropdown and create a tag for the release with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. Add a link to the release notes page in the description of the release.
- [x] Once you publish the release, confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the `staging.dev.medicmobile.org` by running this `curl` call. Ensure you see the correct `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`:
   ```
   curl -s https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases | jq '[.rows[] | select(.key[0]=="release")] | max_by(.value.time)'
   ```
- [x] Upgrade the [demo](https://demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org/) instance to the newly released version.
  - [x] From the "App Management" admin console (`medic` user creds in 1Password), go to "Upgrades" and stage the upgrade for this version.
  - [x] Clone `cht-core` repo and checkout the target tag (`git checkout <major>.<minor>.x` ) to ensure you have the proper version of the helm charts.
  - [x] In your terminal, change to the `./cht-core/scripts/build/helm` directory.
  - [x] Make sure you're using the dev EKS cluster: `kubectl config use-context arn:aws:eks:eu-west-2:720541322708:cluster/dev-cht-eks`
  - [x] Ensure you have access to [EKS](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/hosting/medic/) and  to the [`demo-cht` namespace](https://github.com/medic/medic-infrastructure/issues/1344).) by calling this helm command. There should be no errors: `helm list -n demo-cht`
  - [x] Download the current `values.yaml` data from the demo instance: `helm get values demo-cht --namespace demo-cht > values.yaml`
  - [x] Edit the `values.yaml` file so `cht_image_tag` and `chtversion` properties have the new tag value `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`.
  - [x] Use helm to upgrade the instance: `helm upgrade demo-cht . --namespace demo-cht -f values.yaml`
  - [x] Refresh the "App Management" page and verify the instance upgraded. You may need to wait 5+ minutes until the upgrade succeeds.  Until then, you may see `50x` errors in the browser - be patient!
- [x] Announce the release on the Forum under the "Announcements - Releases" category by using this [template](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/new-topic?title=Announcing%20the%20release%20of%20%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.%3Cpatch%3E%20of%20the%20CHT%20Core%20Framework&body=%2AAnnouncing%20the%20release%20of%20%7B%7Bversion%7D%7D%20of%20%7B%7Bproduct%7D%7D%2A%0AThis%20release%20fixes%20%7B%7Bnumber%20of%20bugs%7D%7D.%20Read%20the%20%5Brelease%20notes%5D%28%7B%7Burl%7D%7D%29%20for%20full%20details.&category=releases).
- [x] Go over the list of commits and individually notify contributing / interested community members about the release.
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: chore(#11346): add optional AI review CI workflow
body:
# Description

Closes https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/11346 

Adds a new GitHub actions workflow that can be optionally triggered on a PR by maintainers by setting an `ai-review` label on the PR.  The workflow runs two distinct AI reviews of the code changes in the PR:

- `code-review` - This job uses https://github.com/alibaba/open-code-review to do a line-by-line review of the code in the PR looking for code-level bugs, errors, etc.
- `completeness-review` - This job uses the `cht-pr-review` skill from https://github.com/medic/cht-ai-tools to validate the contents of the PR against the requirements documented in the PR description and in any linked issue(s).

OCR will leave in-line comments for any of its finding and the completeness-review report will be documented in a top-level comment on the PR.

## Telemetry

OpenTelemetry metrics are collected from both jobs and are sent to Langfuse for aggregation.  In addition, the execution output data for both jobs is attached to the CI run as artifacts and can be downloaded for further analysis (useful for debugging, etc). 

## opencodereview rules

Most of the value in the open-code-review system is in the ability to easily extend the review functionality with custom rules that can be tuned for the specific repo.  I have added an initial set of rules here. The goal is not so much to be comprehensive, but to just give us a baseline to start from.  We will want to continue tuning these as we get more data about reviews in cht-core.

## AI Disclosure

Claude was used heavily when researching/designing/authoring this.  I have carefully reviewed all the changes and have done extensive testing with an almost identical setup over in https://github.com/jkuester/chtoolbox.  

# Code review checklist
- [X] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the [style guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/style-guide/)
- [X] AI disclosure: Please disclose use of AI per [the guidelines](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/community/contributing/ai-guidelines/).



# Compose URLs
If Build CI hasn't passed, these may 404:

* [Core](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/medic:medic:11346-add-ai-review/docker-compose/cht-core.yml)
* [CouchDB Single](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/medic:medic:11346-add-ai-review/docker-compose/cht-couchdb.yml)
* [CouchDB Cluster](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/medic:medic:11346-add-ai-review/docker-compose/cht-couchdb-clustered.yml)

title: Plan bulk operations at execution time
Retry Bulk Operation Actions on Transient Failures
body:
## Goals

- A handler or plan failure that might succeed on a second try (CouchDB unavailable, a network blip, a write conflict with a concurrent edit) is retried instead of being recorded as permanent, and keeps being retried until it works.
- The cool-down ramps: the first retry is immediate, then one minute, two, and so on up to five minutes, then every five minutes indefinitely.
- Every handler becomes idempotent, so re-running a batch converges instead of reporting spurious guard failures.

## Handler contract

Today a handler returns the operations that failed and any thrown error fails the whole batch. The contract becomes:

- **Return** the operations that failed *permanently*: missing doc, guard mismatch, a row error other than `conflict`,  an operation with no id. These are recorded in `failed_operations` and never retried.
- **Throw** for anything that stopped the batch being processed as a whole: a rejected read or write, or rows that came back `conflict`. The batch is re-run on the next attempt with the cursor unmoved. Consider using a new named `RetryableError` so we can distinguish between expected retryable errors and unexpected errors (that should just fail the action.).

| Handler | Already applied looks like | Treat as |
|---|---|---|
| `set-parent` | `doc.parent` deep-equals `op.parent` | success, skip the write |
| `set-contact` | `doc.contact` deep-equals `op.contact` (both absent counts) | success, skip the write |
| `delete` | no row doc in `medic` | success (already the case) |
| `delete-user` | `deleteUser` rejects with a 404 | success |

## Handler errors that we can retry

- Any error coming back from a PouchDB call with a status of `408`, `409`, or `5xx` - issue with Couch, not with the operation. Need to retry until Couch improves.
- Any `bulkDocs` entry that comes back with `error: 'conflict'` - simultaneous edit.  Try again with the updated `_rev`.

# Description

Fixes a crash when selecting a contact if the reports array contains undefined entries.

title: Record why an outgoing SMS failed, so recoverable failures can be retried (Nepal DoIT gateway)
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
The Nepal DoIT SMS outgoing service, [`api/src/services/nepal-doit-sms.js`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/2b9065540a96ad7205a56913b7285123d6ee6ade/api/src/services/nepal-doit-sms.js), added in #10225 / #10230.

When a send fails, the service records a fixed reason phrase derived from the HTTP status rather than the error the gateway actually returned, so every `422` is recorded identically on the message doc. It also treats every `422` as final, although the gateway uses that one status both for account-level conditions that clear on their own and for recipients that can never be delivered to.

It would be better to record what the gateway reported and use it to decide whether a failure is worth retrying, so that a recoverable condition resolves itself once it clears instead of requiring manual recovery.


**Describe the improvement you'd like**
1. Carry the gateway's actual error into `details` instead of a constant — for example `{ code: 422, reason: 'UnprocessableContent', error: <body.errors> }`. The object form is already supported downstream (docs exist carrying `{"reason": "generic; errorCode=0"}`). Bound the stored length and leave message content out.
2. Use that reason to classify `422` rather than treating it as one thing.
3. Consider surfacing an account-level failure more prominently than a log line, since that class of error stops every outgoing message on an instance at once rather than affecting one recipient.
4. Include the message id in the [error log line](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/2b9065540a96ad7205a56913b7285123d6ee6ade/api/src/services/nepal-doit-sms.js#L118), so an entry can be tied back to a message.

The three cases item 2 needs to separate:

| Situation | Appropriate handling |
| --- | --- |
| Account-level condition, e.g. no balance remaining | retryable — the message should send once the condition clears |
| Gateway rejects a specific recipient number | terminal |
| Recipient never resolved — `to` holds a literal template string such as `patient.phone` rather than a number | terminal, and must never be retried |

The ordering matters: **capturing the reason is a prerequisite for the retry change**, not merely a diagnostic nicety. The third case returns the same `422` as the first and can never succeed, so retrying `422` without knowing the reason would loop on those messages indefinitely.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- *Make all `422`s retryable without recording the reason.* The smallest change, but unsafe — it would retry messages whose recipient never resolves, forever.

- *Rely on the API logs for the reason.* This is effectively today's position. The reason exists only in the pod log, subject to whatever log retention the deployment has, whereas the message doc persists indefinitely. Diagnosing a `failed` message after log retention has elapsed is not possible at all.

- *Leave recovery operational — reset messages to `pending` by script when someone notices.* Workable but manual, and the script has no reliable way to select the right messages, since the docs record no usable reason and the three cases above are indistinguishable.

- *Ask the gateway to resend.* Not available — the DoIT aggregator does not retry failed messages automatically and offers no resend from its dashboard, unlike CHT gateway.


**Additional context**
`STATUS_MAP` holds `detail` as a constant per HTTP status, which is why a `422` always records `UnprocessableContent`. It is also where `500` carries a `retry` flag and `422` does not:

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/2b9065540a96ad7205a56913b7285123d6ee6ade/api/src/services/nepal-doit-sms.js#L7-L15

`generateStateChange` copies that constant straight into `details`, and that is all that reaches the message doc:

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/2b9065540a96ad7205a56913b7285123d6ee6ade/api/src/services/nepal-doit-sms.js#L53-L66

The gateway's own error text is already in scope at the point of failure — `err.message` carries both the status and the body, for example `422 - {"errors":"Balance not enough"}` — and is logged, then dropped two lines later:

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/2b9065540a96ad7205a56913b7285123d6ee6ade/api/src/services/nepal-doit-sms.js#L116-L123

There is also a related asymmetry worth settling in the same change. If the gateway signals the same condition as HTTP `200` with an unrecognised `status` field instead of as a `422`, `validateSuccessResponse` returns `false`, `sendMessage` returns `undefined`, and the message is retried indefinitely — the opposite of the `422` path:

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/2b9065540a96ad7205a56913b7285123d6ee6ade/api/src/services/nepal-doit-sms.js#L68-L83

So the same real-world situation is handled as terminal or as endlessly retryable depending only on how the gateway chooses to signal it.

title: fix(#11422): use ASCII digits for task filter cutoff regardless of locale
body:
# Description

`ContactsContentComponent.filterTasks` compares `task.dueDate` (always an ASCII `YYYY-MM-DD` string) against `moment().add(weeks, 'weeks').format('YYYY-MM-DD')`. `format()` renders the digits in the active moment locale, so with Nepali (`ne`) the cutoff comes out in Devanagari (e.g. `२०२६-०९-१७`). Every ASCII date string compares as less than that, `task.dueDate <= taskEndDate` is always true, and the "1 week" / "2 weeks" filter shows every task.

The fix formats the cutoff with the `en` locale so the comparison is always ASCII vs ASCII, the same approach taken in #11414 for the rules engine.

Added two unit tests for `filterTasks`: one for the normal window behaviour, and a regression test that switches the moment locale to `ne`. Without the fix the regression test fails with `expected [ 'task-3-days', 'task-9-days', 'task-30-days' ] to deeply equal [ 'task-3-days' ]`; with the fix the spec file passes (34/34).

Closes #11422

title: Migrate the `medic-client/contacts_by_phone` call sites onto the `phones` qualifier
body:
---
title: Migrate the `medic-client/contacts_by_phone` call sites onto the `phones` qualifier
type: improvement
priority: medium
domain: data-sync
labels:
  - cht-datasource
  - migration
---

## Description

Split out of #10973, which is scoped to adding the qualifier itself.

PR #11249 added `byPhones` to `cht-datasource` and exposed it on both contact
list endpoints, but migrated **no** call site. Review found that every one of
the eight existing `medic-client/contacts_by_phone` readers changes behaviour
when it moves onto the datasource, and each of those changes needs a decision
that the qualifier PR should not be making on its own.

This ticket is that work. It is not a mechanical sweep: the three causes below
affect different callers differently, and two of them are visible to
configurations in the field.

**The three behaviour changes**

1. **Permissions.** The datasource's remote context reads through
   `/api/v1/contact`, which is gated by `can_view_contacts`. The CouchDB proxy
   the callers use today is not. Any online caller that migrates newly requires
   that permission.
2. **`isContact` filtering.** `contacts_by_phone` emits any doc whose `type` is
   in its hard-coded list, including `type: contact` docs whose `contact_type`
   is not in settings. Both datasource phones paths filter rows through
   `isContact`, so a migrated caller stops seeing those docs.
3. **Input handling.** `byPhones` rejects blank and whitespace-padded numbers
   rather than passing them through to a query that can only ever match
   nothing. Callers that today hand the view a padded, numeric, or `undefined`
   value get a thrown error or a different result instead of a silent empty
   page.

## Technical Context

**Components:**
- `webapp/src/js/enketo/widgets/phone-widget.js` — `getContactIdsForPhone`
- `admin/src/js/services/message-queue.js` — `getRecipients`
- `shared-libs/validation/src/validation_utils.js` — `uniquePhone`
- `shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/registration.js` — `getParentByPhone`
- `shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/update_sent_by.js`
- `shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/self_report.js`
- `shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/update_clinics.js`
- `api/src/controllers/contacts-by-phone.js`

**Existing References:**
- PR [#11249](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/11249) — added the
  qualifier and the API surface this ticket consumes; its description carries
  the per-call-site analysis summarised below.
- #10973 — the qualifier ticket this one is split out of.
- #11328 — the equivalent follow-up split out of #11151, for the
  `reports_by_form` callers the qualifier pattern did not fit.

**What already exists to migrate onto:**
- `Qualifier.byPhones([...])`, `Contact.v1.getUuidsPage` / `getUuids` /
  `getPage` / `getAll`
- the imperative surface: `getUuidsPageByPhones`, `getUuidsByPhones`,
  `getPageByPhones`, `getByPhones` on `getDatasource(ctx).v1.contact`
- `GET /api/v1/contact/uuid?phone=` and `GET /api/v1/contact?phone=`, both
  accepting a comma-joined list

None of these have an in-repo consumer yet. This ticket gives them one.

## Requirements

### Call sites

| Call site | Today | What migration changes | Decision needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `webapp/src/js/enketo/widgets/phone-widget.js:20` | `{ key: phoneNumber }`, ids only | Online users would newly need `can_view_contacts`. The permission gates the UI and the `/api/v1/contact\|person\|place` endpoints, not the data — online users read contacts through the CouchDB proxy regardless — so the change restricts nothing real while potentially breaking a custom role. | Accept the new permission requirement, or keep this caller on `db.query`. |
| `admin/src/js/services/message-queue.js:99` | `{ keys: phoneNumbers }`, batch, ids only | Same cause, larger blast radius: `crfo` reaches the admin app via `can_configure`/`can_export_all` with no `can_view_contacts`, and the rejection blanks the page rather than degrading to messages without recipient names. | Same decision, plus whether a failed lookup should degrade rather than reject. |
| `shared-libs/validation/src/validation_utils.js:146` (`uniquePhone`) | `{ key: value }`, `!rows.length` | A missing field goes from failing to passing, so a config using `uniquePhone` as "must exist AND be unique" silently stops enforcing the first half. `String()`/`.trim()` at the boundary would also newly enforce uniqueness on numeric and padded values. | Whether `uniquePhone` on a missing field passes or fails; whether to coerce/trim before calling. Needs a release note either way. |
| `shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/registration.js:419` (`getParentByPhone`) | `{ key: options.doc.from, include_docs: true }`, takes `rows[0].doc` | An undefined `doc.from` sends no key at all — PouchDB drops undefined params — so the query returns *every* phone-bearing contact and `rows[0].doc` becomes the parent. Migrating makes that `parent_not_found`. Rows are also newly `isContact`-filtered. | Confirm `parent_not_found` is the wanted outcome for a missing sender (it almost certainly is) and release-note it. |
| `shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/update_sent_by.js:28` | `{ key: doc.from, include_docs: true }`, reads `rows[0].doc` off the raw view | Rows newly `isContact`-filtered. | Confirm dropping unconfigured `type: contact` docs is correct here. |
| `api/src/controllers/contacts-by-phone.js:115` | `{ key: normalizedPhone }` then `lineage.fetchHydratedDocs` | Rows newly `isContact`-filtered, where it currently hydrates the raw view ids. Note it normalises the phone *before* querying, so it is the one caller already doing the trimming `byPhones` demands. | Confirm the filter; decide whether to keep `fetchHydratedDocs` (lineage) or move to `getPage`, which does not hydrate lineage. |
| `shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/self_report.js:32` | `{ key: String(doc.from) }` | Already filters at hydration via `getWithLineage`, so `isContact` costs it nothing. Would gain `.trim()`: a padded `doc.from` matches nothing today and would start matching — or throw, if trimming is left to the qualifier. | Lowest risk of the eight. Migrate, and pick where the trim happens. |
| `shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/update_clinics.js:64` | `query(..., params)` | Same as `self_report.js`. | Same. |

Migrate every site whose decision comes out in favour. Any site deliberately
left on `db.query` keeps a comment pointing at whatever ticket covers it, as
#11151 did for its aggregate callers.

### Tests

- Each migrated caller keeps its existing suite green. The suites that assert
  `db.medic.query` arguments — `shared-libs/transitions/test/unit/transitions/registration.js`,
  `self_report.js`, `shared-libs/transitions/test/integration/transitions.js` —
  assert the datasource call instead. Do not keep both.
- Cover each behaviour change that is *accepted* with a test that pins the new
  behaviour: missing sender → `parent_not_found`; unconfigured `type: contact`
  doc → not returned; missing field → whatever `uniquePhone` is decided to do.
- For `message-queue.js`, cover the batch path: one datasource call for N
  numbers, recipients still matched to the right messages.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every migrated call site reads through `cht-datasource`; any site left behind
  carries a comment saying why and which ticket covers it.
- `grep -rnE "query\(['\"]medic-client/contacts_by_phone['\"]" webapp/src admin/src api/src shared-libs/transitions/src shared-libs/validation/src`
  returns only the deliberately-skipped sites. The view name legitimately
  survives in `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/contact.ts` and its tests.
- `npm run unit-shared-lib`, `npm run unit-api`, `npm run unit-admin` and
  `npm run unit-webapp` pass.
- Every accepted behaviour change is in the release notes.

## Constraints

- `admin/src/js` is bundled through ng-annotate's 2015 acorn and cannot use
  `async`/`await`. `message-queue.js` stays promise-chained.
- Do not make `byPhones` normalise. Coercion and trimming are the caller's job;
  that is the parity constraint inherited from #10973 and it does not change
  here.
- Do not change `ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/contacts_by_phone/map.js`.
  Emitting the doc type as the view value would let the `isContact` filter run
  on `row.value` and save the uuid path an `include_docs` — worth its own
  ticket if the admin message queue migrates and the extra read shows up, but
  it is a ddoc change and a reindex, so it is out of scope here.
- Keep the permission question a deliberate decision, not a side effect. If a
  caller migrates and starts requiring `can_view_contacts`, that goes in the
  release notes.

## References

**Similar Implementations:**
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/11249 — the qualifier this ticket consumes
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/11327 — `byForm`, whose out-of-scope
  callers were split into #11328 the same way

**Documentation:**
- `ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/contacts_by_phone/map.js`
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/README.md`

title: Migrate the `medic-client/contacts_by_reference` call sites onto the `shortcodes` and `externalRefs` qualifiers
body:
**Title:** Migrate the `medic-client/contacts_by_reference` call sites onto the `shortcodes` and `externalRefs` qualifiers

---
title: Migrate the `medic-client/contacts_by_reference` call sites onto the `shortcodes` and `externalRefs` qualifiers
type: improvement
priority: medium
domain: data-sync
labels:
  - cht-datasource
  - migration
---

## Description

Split out of #10976, which is scoped to adding the qualifiers themselves.

#10976 adds `byShortcodes` and `byExternalRefs` to `cht-datasource` and
exposes them on both contact list endpoints, but migrates **no** call site.
Every one of the nine existing `medic-client/contacts_by_reference` readers
changes behaviour when it moves onto the datasource, and each of those changes
needs a decision that the qualifier PR should not be making on its own.

This ticket is that work. It is not a mechanical sweep: the four causes below
affect different callers differently, one of them is a correctness risk for
shortcode generation, and two are visible to configurations in the field.

**The four behaviour changes**

1. **Permissions.** The datasource's remote context reads through
   `/api/v1/contact`, which is gated by `can_view_contacts`. The CouchDB proxy
   the callers use today is not. Any online caller that migrates newly
   requires that permission. The webapp picks the remote context for
   online-only users (`cht-datasource.service.ts`) and the admin app always
   uses it.
2. **`isContact` filtering.** `contacts_by_reference` emits any doc whose
   `type` is in its hard-coded list, including `national_office` and
   `type: contact` docs whose `contact_type` is not in settings. Both
   datasource paths filter rows through `isContact`, so a migrated caller
   stops seeing those docs. For most callers that is a harmless narrowing.
   For `isIdUnique` it is the opposite: a shortcode held by a filtered doc
   looks free, so the id generator can hand it out twice.
3. **Loss of the key→id association.** Six of the nine callers send a batch
   of keys and read `row.key[1]` off the result to work out *which* key each
   contact matched. The datasource returns a page of ids or docs with no key
   attached. A migrated batch caller either re-derives the match from the
   returned doc (`patient_id` / `place_id` / `rc_code`), which means using the
   doc path and paying `include_docs`, or issues one call per key.
4. **Input handling.** `byShortcodes` and `byExternalRefs` reject blank,
   padded and non-string entries rather than passing them through to a query
   that can only ever match nothing. Callers that today hand the view a
   numeric shortcode or an `undefined` reference get a thrown error where they
   used to get a silent empty result — or, if they add `String()` at the
   boundary, start matching numeric references that never matched before.

Two callers also have no datasource context to migrate onto (see below).

## Technical Context

**Components:**
- `webapp/src/ts/services/get-subject-summaries.service.ts` — `processReferences`
- `admin/src/js/services/get-subject-summaries.js` — `processReferences`
- `admin/src/js/services/message-queue.js` — `getSubjectsAndRegistrations`
- `shared-libs/lineage/src/hydration.js` — `contactUuidByShortcode`
- `shared-libs/transitions/src/lib/utils.js` — `getContact` (behind
  `getContactUuid` / `getContact`)
- `shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/utils.js` — `isIdUnique`
- `shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/update_clinics.js` — `getContactByRefid`
- `shared-libs/rules-engine/src/pouchdb-provider.js` — `contactsBySubjectId`
- `api/src/services/replication/authorization.js` — `findContactsByReplicationKeys`

**Existing References:**
- #10976 — the qualifier ticket this one is split out of.
- #11442 — the equivalent follow-up split out of #10973, for the
  `contacts_by_phone` callers. Same causes 1, 2 and 4; this ticket adds 3.
- #10019 / PR [#10026](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/10026) — an
  earlier, closed attempt to move `shared-libs/lineage` onto the datasource.

**What will exist to migrate onto (from #10976):**
- `Qualifier.byShortcodes([...])`, `Qualifier.byExternalRefs([...])`,
  `Contact.v1.getUuidsPage` / `getUuids` / `getPage` / `getAll`
- the imperative surface: `getUuidsPageByShortcodes`, `getPageByShortcodes`,
  `getByShortcodes` and the `ByExternalRefs` equivalents on
  `getDatasource(ctx).v1.contact`
- `GET /api/v1/contact/uuid` and `GET /api/v1/contact` with `?shortcode=` and
  `?external_ref=`, both accepting a comma-joined list

**Where a data context already exists:** `api/src/services/data-context.js`,
`shared-libs/transitions/src/data-context.js`,
`admin/src/js/services/data-context.js`, the webapp's
`CHTDatasourceService`. `shared-libs/lineage` and `shared-libs/rules-engine`
have none: lineage is built from `(Promise, DB)` and the rules engine's
provider from a PouchDB instance.

## Requirements

### Call sites

| Call site | Today | What migration changes | Decision needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `webapp/src/ts/services/get-subject-summaries.service.ts:118` | `{ keys: [['shortcode', ref], ...] }`, ids only; `findSubjectId` matches `row.key[1] === id.toString()` | Cause 3: needs the doc path to map each summary's reference back to a contact, so the ids-only query becomes `include_docs`. Cause 1 for online users. Cause 4: a numeric reference is sent raw today and never matches the view's `String()` key; coercing at the boundary makes it start matching. | Doc path or per-reference calls. Accept the new permission for online users. Whether numeric references should resolve (they arguably always should have). |
| `admin/src/js/services/get-subject-summaries.js:110` | Same as the webapp copy | Same, and the admin app is always online so cause 1 always applies. `admin/src/js` cannot use `async`/`await`. | Same. |
| `admin/src/js/services/message-queue.js:135` | `{ keys: referenceKeys }`, ids only; `findIdByKey` on `row.key[1]` | Cause 3 and cause 1. Sits in the same `$q.all` as the `reports_by_subject` query that #<11150-migration-issue> migrates; a role reaching the message queue without `can_view_contacts` gets a rejected page rather than one without patient/place names. | Doc path or per-key calls. Same permission decision as #11442's `getRecipients` in the same file; make it once. Sequence with the `reports_by_subject` migration of this function. |
| `shared-libs/lineage/src/hydration.js:248` (`contactUuidByShortcode`) | `{ keys }`, ids only; `row.key[1]` to build a shortcode→uuid `Map`, falling back to the shortcode itself | No data context: the lib is constructed with `(Promise, DB)` by api, sentinel, transitions and admin. Migrating means adding a context to the factory signature at every construction site, which is the #10019 problem. Cause 3 as well. | Whether to give lineage a data context here or leave this caller on `db.query` with a comment pointing at a lineage-specific ticket. Recommend the latter. |
| `shared-libs/transitions/src/lib/utils.js:120` (`getContact`) | `{ key: ['shortcode', id], include_docs }`, warns on `rows.length > 1`, returns `rows[0].doc` or `.id` | Rows newly `isContact`-filtered (cause 2). Keeping the "more than one contact" warning needs `limit: 2` rather than `1`. Cause 4: `shortCodeId` is guarded for falsiness but not type; a numeric value throws instead of matching nothing. | Confirm the filter. Keep the warning or drop it. Coerce or guard at the boundary. |
| `shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/utils.js:62` (`isIdUnique`) | `{ key: ['shortcode', id] }`, `!rows.length` | **Cause 2 is a correctness risk here.** The id generator uses this to avoid re-issuing a shortcode. A shortcode held by a `national_office` doc or an unconfigured `type: contact` doc is in the view but filtered by the datasource, so it reports as unique and gets assigned again. | Either leave this caller on `db.query` with a comment, or accept the risk explicitly with a release note. Recommend leaving it. |
| `shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/update_clinics.js:26` (`getContactByRefid`) | `{ key: ['external', doc.refid], include_docs, limit: 1 }`, then `contactTypesUtils.getContactType` | Already discards non-contacts, so cause 2 costs nothing. `refid` is upper-cased on save (#5373), so the builder's upper-casing is a no-op. Cause 4: an undefined `refid` is sent as `['external', null]` today and matches nothing; `byExternalRefs([undefined])` throws, so guard before calling. Already has `dataContext` in scope. | Lowest risk of the nine. Migrate; add the guard. |
| `shared-libs/rules-engine/src/pouchdb-provider.js:57` (`contactsBySubjectId`) | `{ keys, include_docs }`; returns matched doc ids plus the subject ids that matched nothing, using `row.key[1]` to tell them apart | No data context: the provider takes a PouchDB instance. Cause 3: which subject ids missed has to be re-derived from the returned docs' `patient_id` / `place_id`. Offline hot path; the provider already chunks `keys` at `MAX_QUERY_KEYS`. | Whether to inject a data context into the provider (the webapp's `rules-engine.service.ts` would supply it) or leave this caller with a comment. Depends on the same decision for the `reports_by_subject` calls in this file (#<11150-migration-issue>). |
| `api/src/services/replication/authorization.js:456` (`findContactsByReplicationKeys`) | `{ keys }`, `row.key[1]` to map each replication key to doc ids, falling back to the key as a doc id, then `allDocs` | **Security-sensitive.** Cause 2: a subject that is a filtered doc drops out of the replication-key resolution, and its shortcode falls through to `allDocs` as a doc id and misses, so the reports about it can leave the user's replication scope. Cause 3 as well. Has `dataContext` available. | Confirm with whoever owns replication that narrowing to configured contacts is acceptable here, or leave on `db.query`. Do not migrate this one on the strength of the sweep alone. |

Migrate every site whose decision comes out in favour. Any site deliberately
left on `db.query` keeps a comment pointing at whatever ticket covers it, as
#11151 did for its aggregate callers.

### Tests

- Each migrated caller keeps its existing suite green. The suites that assert
  `db.medic.query` arguments — `shared-libs/transitions/test/unit/utils.js`,
  `shared-libs/transitions/test/unit/patient_registration.js`,
  `admin/tests/unit/services/message-queue.spec.js`,
  `webapp/tests/karma/ts/services/get-subject-summaries.service.spec.ts`,
  `api/tests/mocha/services/replication/authorization.spec.js` — assert the
  datasource call instead. Do not keep both.
- Cover each behaviour change that is *accepted* with a test that pins the new
  behaviour: unconfigured `type: contact` doc → not returned; numeric
  reference → whatever is decided; undefined `refid` → no lookup.
- For every batch caller that moves to the doc path, cover the association:
  N keys in, each summary/message/subject matched to the right contact, and a
  key that matches nothing handled the way it is today.
- Integration: `tests/integration/sentinel/transitions/registration.spec.js`
  and `tests/integration/transitions/sentinel-api-transitions.spec.js` stay
  green without modification.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every migrated call site reads through `cht-datasource`; any site left
  behind carries a comment saying why and which ticket covers it.
- `grep -rnE "query\(['\"]medic-client/contacts_by_reference['\"]" webapp/src admin/src api/src shared-libs/*/src`
  returns only the deliberately-skipped sites. The view name legitimately
  survives in `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/contact.ts` and its tests.
- `npm run unit-shared-lib`, `npm run unit-api`, `npm run unit-admin` and
  `npm run unit-webapp` pass.
- Every accepted behaviour change is in the release notes.

## Constraints

- `admin/src/js` is bundled through ng-annotate's 2015 acorn and cannot use
  `async`/`await`. Both admin callers stay promise-chained.
- Do not make `byShortcodes` coerce or trim. Coercion is the caller's job;
  that is the parity constraint inherited from #10976.
- Do not change `ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/contacts_by_reference/map.js`.
  Emitting the doc type as the view value would let `isContact` run on
  `row.value` and save the uuid path an `include_docs`, and emitting the
  matched field would restore the key association without docs — both are
  ddoc changes and a reindex, so out of scope here.
- Do not give `shared-libs/lineage` or `shared-libs/rules-engine` a data
  context as a side effect of this sweep. If either is decided on, it is its
  own change with its own ticket.
- Keep the permission question a deliberate decision, not a side effect. If a
  caller migrates and starts requiring `can_view_contacts`, that goes in the
  release notes.

## References

**Similar Implementations:**
- #11442 — the `contacts_by_phone` caller migration, same shape of ticket
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/11327 — `byForms`, whose out-of-scope
  callers were split into #11328 the same way

**Documentation:**
- `ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/contacts_by_reference/map.js`
- `shared-libs/cht-datasource/README.md`

title: Migrate the `medic-client/reports_by_subject` call sites onto the `subjects` qualifier
body:
---
title: Migrate the `medic-client/reports_by_subject` call sites onto the `subjects` qualifier
type: improvement
priority: medium
domain: data-sync
labels:
  - cht-datasource
  - migration
---

## Description

Split out of #11150, which is scoped to adding the qualifier itself.

#11150 adds `bySubjects` to `cht-datasource` and exposes it on
`GET /api/v1/report/uuid`, but migrates **no** call site. The original ticket
listed one caller; there are seven readers of
`medic-client/reports_by_subject`, and every one of them changes behaviour
when it moves onto the datasource. Each of those changes needs a decision
that the qualifier PR should not be making on its own.

This ticket is that work. It is not a mechanical sweep, and two of the seven
are not qualifier-shaped queries at all.

**The four behaviour changes**

1. **Ids, not docs.** Every caller queries with `include_docs: true` and works
   on the docs — usually to run `registrationUtils.isValidRegistration` over
   them. `bySubjects` is on the uuid path only, because `Report.v1.getPage`
   takes an `IdsQualifier` and nothing else. A migrated caller does
   `getUuids(bySubjects(...))` then `getAll(byIds(...))`: two round trips
   where there was one, on paths that run per document per transition in
   sentinel and per task-refresh in the rules engine.
2. **Loss of the key→doc association.** Three callers send a batch of subjects
   and read `row.key` off each row to work out which subject a report is
   about. The datasource returns ids with no key attached. A migrated caller
   re-derives the match from the doc's own subject fields
   (`registration-utils` already has `getSubjectIds` / `getSubjectId`), or
   issues one call per subject.
3. **Deduplication moves.** The view emits a report once per subject field,
   so every caller currently `uniqBy(_id)`s the rows. The datasource dedupes
   within a page but not across the generator, so a caller that drops its own
   dedupe on the strength of the adapter's can start seeing a report twice
   when its rows straddle a page.
4. **Permissions and input handling.** The remote context reads through
   `/api/v1/report/uuid`, gated by `can_view_reports`; the CouchDB proxy is
   not. And `bySubjects` rejects an empty array, a padded value or a
   non-string where the view today returns an empty result, so a caller that
   builds `keys` from optional fields needs a guard.

Two callers also have no datasource context to migrate onto (see below).

## Technical Context

**Components:**
- `webapp/src/ts/services/format-data-record.service.ts` — `getRegistrations`
- `admin/src/js/services/message-queue.js` — `getSubjectsAndRegistrations`
- `api/src/services/export/message-mapper.js` — `hydrate`
- `shared-libs/transitions/src/lib/utils.js` — `getReportsBySubject`, behind
  `getRegistrations`; consumed by `registration.js`, `due_tasks.js`,
  `muting_utils.js`, `accept_case_reports.js`, `accept_patient_reports.js`
- `shared-libs/rules-engine/src/pouchdb-provider.js` — `taskDataFor` and
  `allTaskData`
- `shared-libs/search/src/generate-search-requests.js` — `subjectRequest`

**Existing References:**
- #11150 — the qualifier ticket this one is split out of.
- #11442 — the equivalent follow-up split out of #10973, for the
  `contacts_by_phone` callers.
- #11328 — the aggregate follow-up split out of #11151, the precedent for
  leaving a non-qualifier-shaped caller behind with a comment.

**What will exist to migrate onto (from #11150):**
- `Qualifier.bySubjects([...])`, `Report.v1.getUuidsPage` / `getUuids`
- the imperative surface: `getUuidsPageBySubjects`, `getUuidsBySubjects` on
  `getDatasource(ctx).v1.report`
- `GET /api/v1/report/uuid?subject=`, accepting a comma-joined list

**Where a data context already exists:** `api/src/services/data-context.js`,
`shared-libs/transitions/src/data-context.js`,
`admin/src/js/services/data-context.js`, the webapp's
`CHTDatasourceService`. `shared-libs/rules-engine` has none: its provider is
built from a PouchDB instance.

## Requirements

### Call sites

| Call site | Today | What migration changes | Decision needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `webapp/src/ts/services/format-data-record.service.ts:41` (`getRegistrations`) | `{ key: shortcode, include_docs }`, `uniqBy(_id)` | Cause 1: two round trips on an offline PouchDB. Cause 4 for online users. Guarded for falsiness only, so a numeric shortcode throws where it matched nothing before. | Accept the second round trip. Coerce or guard at the boundary. |
| `admin/src/js/services/message-queue.js:136` | `{ keys: shortcodes, include_docs }`; `findRegistrations` matches `row.key === message.context[field]` | Causes 1, 2 and 4. Sits in the same `$q.all` as the `contacts_by_reference` query that #<10976-migration-issue> migrates; the admin app always uses the remote context, and `admin/src/js` cannot use `async`/`await`. | Re-derive per-message registrations from the doc's subject fields. Same permission decision as #11442's `getRecipients` in the same file. Sequence with the `contacts_by_reference` migration of this function. |
| `api/src/services/export/message-mapper.js:125` (`hydrate`) | `{ keys: patientIds, include_docs }`, valid-registration filter, `getRecordRegistrations` matches `row.key === record.patient.patient_id` | Causes 1 and 2. Runs once per export batch, so the extra round trip is cheap. Has `dataContext` available. | Re-derive the per-record match from the doc. Migrate. |
| `shared-libs/transitions/src/lib/utils.js:176` (`getReportsBySubject`) | `{ key \| keys, include_docs }`, `uniqBy(_id)`, optional `isValidRegistration` filter; returns `[]` when neither `id` nor `ids` is given | Cause 1 on the hottest path of the seven: called from four transitions, `muting_utils` and the scheduler, several times per incoming report. Cause 3: keep the caller's dedupe. Cause 4: `ids: []` reaches the view today and returns `[]`; `bySubjects([])` throws, so the early return has to cover it. | Accept the second round trip for sentinel, or measure first. Keep `uniqBy`. Extend the guard. |
| `shared-libs/rules-engine/src/pouchdb-provider.js:142` (`taskDataFor`) | `{ keys, include_docs }` through `dbQuery`, which chunks at `MAX_QUERY_KEYS`; post-filters by `getSubjectId(report) ∈ subjectIds` | No data context: the provider takes a PouchDB instance. Cause 1 on the offline task-refresh path. The existing chunking would move to the caller's side of the qualifier, or be dropped if the adapter is measured not to need it. | Whether to inject a data context into the provider (the webapp's `rules-engine.service.ts` would supply it) or leave this caller with a comment. Depends on the same decision for `contactsBySubjectId` in this file (#<10976-migration-issue>). |
| `shared-libs/rules-engine/src/pouchdb-provider.js:49` (`allTaskData`) | `{ include_docs }`, no key — every report that has any subject | Not a qualifier query; it is a full-view scan used to seed the rules engine. Nothing in `Report.v1` expresses "all reports with a subject". | Leave on `db.query` with a comment. Out of scope for the qualifier pattern. |
| `shared-libs/search/src/generate-search-requests.js:153` (`subjectRequest`) | Builds a `{ view, params: { keys } }` request descriptor for the search lib's view-intersection engine | Not a caller of the view; the search lib composes and intersects several view requests and this is one of them. Migrating it means migrating the search lib, which #11151 did not do for `reports_by_form` either. | Leave as-is, as #11327 left `reports_by_form` in the same file. |

Migrate every site whose decision comes out in favour. Any site deliberately
left on `db.query` keeps a comment pointing at whatever ticket covers it, as
#11151 did for its aggregate callers.

### Tests

- Each migrated caller keeps its existing suite green. The suites that assert
  `db.medic.query` / `DB().query` arguments —
  `shared-libs/transitions/test/unit/lib/utils.js`,
  `shared-libs/transitions/test/unit/utils.js`,
  `admin/tests/unit/services/message-queue.spec.js`,
  `api/tests/mocha/services/export/message-mapper.spec.js`,
  `webapp/tests/karma/ts/services/format-data-record.service.spec.ts` —
  assert the datasource calls instead. Do not keep both.
- Cover each behaviour change that is *accepted* with a test that pins the new
  behaviour: `ids: []` → `[]` without a datasource call; a report matching two
  supplied subjects → returned once; numeric shortcode → whatever is decided.
- For every batch caller, cover the association: N subjects in, each
  message/record matched to the right registrations, and a subject with no
  registrations handled the way it is today.
- `shared-libs/rules-engine/test/integration.spec.js` and
  `shared-libs/transitions/test/integration/transitions.js` stay green
  without modification.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every migrated call site reads through `cht-datasource`; any site left
  behind carries a comment saying why and which ticket covers it.
- `grep -rnE "reports_by_subject" webapp/src admin/src api/src shared-libs/*/src`
  returns only the deliberately-skipped sites. The view name legitimately
  survives in `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/report.ts` and its tests.
- `npm run unit-shared-lib`, `npm run unit-api`, `npm run unit-admin` and
  `npm run unit-webapp` pass.
- Every accepted behaviour change is in the release notes.

## Constraints

- `admin/src/js` is bundled through ng-annotate's 2015 acorn and cannot use
  `async`/`await`. `message-queue.js` stays promise-chained.
- Do not add a doc-returning `bySubjects` path to `Report.v1.getPage` to make
  the migration cheaper. If the second round trip proves too expensive for
  sentinel or the rules engine, that is a design change for its own ticket,
  not a side effect of this one.
- Do not make `bySubjects` coerce or trim. Coercion is the caller's job; that
  is the parity constraint inherited from #11150.
- Do not change `ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/reports_by_subject/map.js`.
- Do not give `shared-libs/rules-engine` a data context as a side effect of
  this sweep. If it is decided on, it is its own change with its own ticket.
- Keep the permission question a deliberate decision, not a side effect. If a
  caller migrates and starts requiring `can_view_reports`, that goes in the
  release notes.

## References

**Similar Implementations:**
- #11442 — the `contacts_by_phone` caller migration, same shape of ticket
- #11328 — the aggregate `reports_by_form` follow-up, the precedent for
  leaving non-qualifier callers behind

**Documentation:**
- `ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/reports_by_subject/map.js`

title: feat(#11150): add by subjects qualifier
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

feat(#1234): add hat wobble
^--^(#^--^): ^------------^
|     |      |
|     |      + - > subject
|     |
|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: build|feat|fix|perf|refactor|test|chore

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

<!-- DESCRIPTION -->

Adds a subjects qualifier to cht-datasource. It finds reports by the subject they are about, identified by either a shortcode (`patient_id`, `place_id`, `case_id`) or a UUID (`patient_uuid`, `place_uuid`). The qualifier is also exposed on both report list endpoints. **No call site is migrated.** Every existing `medic-client/reports_by_subject` caller is untouched; that work is #11444.

Two things change for existing API users:

- On `GET /api/v1/report`, `ids` is now optional. With neither `ids` nor `subject`, the error changes from `Query param ids is required` to `Either query param ids or subject is required`.
- On `GET /api/v1/report/uuid`, an object-shaped `form` (`?form[a]=b`, which `qs.parse` parses to an object) is now a 400 instead of a 500. It goes through the same list parser as `subject`.

### Datasource

- `SubjectsQualifier` / `bySubjects` / `isSubjectsQualifier` in `qualifier.ts`, reaching consumers through the existing `export * as Qualifier` re-export. The qualifier has the same shape and validation rules as `byPhones` and `byForms`: a non-empty tuple, verbatim matching, `Set` dedupe in the order given, and rejection of blank or whitespace-padded entries. Shortcodes and UUIDs can be mixed, because the view puts both in one key space.
- Local, uuid path: a dispatch arm in `getUuidsPage` beside the forms arm, using `queryDocIdsByKeys` and `fetchAndFilterIds`. The view emits the bare value as the key, so the deduped subjects are the `keys` as given, with no `[form]`-style wrapping.
- Local, doc path: a dispatch arm in `getPage` beside the ids arm, using `queryDocsByKeys` (from #11249) and a new `fetchAndFilterUniqueDocs` in `local/libs/doc.ts`. With `include_docs`, a report matching several requested subjects comes back once per match, each copy with the full doc. The helper drops repeats by `_id` on top of the report-type filter. Both arms build their keys the same way, so they page over the same rows.
- Remote: a comma-joined `subject` param on both routes.
- `assertFreetextOrFormsQualifier` is renamed to `assertFreetextFormsOrSubjectsQualifier`, and `assertIdsOrSubjectsQualifier` is added beside `assertIdsQualifier`, which its other callers keep. Subject-shaped invalid input gets an `Invalid subjects` message; everything else keeps its existing error.
- `getUuidsPageBySubjects` / `getUuidsBySubjects` / `getPageBySubjects` / `getBySubjects` on the imperative `getDatasource()` surface. There is no new method on the `Report.v1` namespace: `getPage` / `getAll` now accept `IdsQualifier | SubjectsQualifier`.

### API

A `subject` query param on `GET /api/v1/report/uuid` and `GET /api/v1/report`. It accepts a comma-joined list or the parameter repeated. There is no new route and no `routing.js` change.

- Precedence on `/uuid`: `freetext`, then `form`, then `subject`. With none of them given, the endpoint still returns the freetext error it returns today.
- Precedence on `/report`: `ids`, then `subject`.
- An object-shaped `subject` is rejected with a 400 on both endpoints.

### Duplicates

`reports_by_subject` emits a report once for every subject field it sets. That happens even for a single subject: a report with both `patient_id` and `fields.patient_id` set to `X` is emitted twice under `X`. So one report can produce several rows.

- **Within a page**, each report appears at most once. The paged methods and both endpoints guarantee this.
- **Across pages**, the cursor is a row skip and can't carry the ids already returned, so a report can reappear on a later page. The OpenAPI descriptions and JSDoc say so.
- **The generators** (`getUuids` / `getAll` and the imperative `get*BySubjects` / `getByIds` / `getUuidsByForms`) track the ids they have yielded and yield each report at most once. The cost is one id string per distinct report for the life of the generator. This applies to every qualifier rather than only subjects, which avoids a special case.

### Deviations from the issue

- **The generators dedupe across pages.** The issue (requirement 9) said to document the cross-page duplicates and leave them. But when a caller passes both a contact's UUID and its shortcode, as `getSubjectIds` does, cross-page duplicates are the normal case, not an edge case. Deduping in the generator is a `Set` and a few lines.
- **Integration tests are split by concern rather than duplicated.** The cht-datasource integration tests go through the remote adapter to the same endpoints, so they cover the data behaviour: shortcode, UUID, a report matched by both returned once, an empty page, a three-page cursor walk with exact ids and cursors, and the generators. The API integration tests cover only query-string handling: comma list, repeated param, `ids` precedence, and the empty-list 400. The padded, object-shaped and invalid-cursor 400s are covered by the controller and qualifier unit tests instead.
- **No non-normalisation tests.** Tests asserting that an unchanged value is passed through unchanged were left out.

### Testing

Unit tests cover:
- the qualifier
- both local adapter arms, including per-page dedupe and, for `fetchAndFilterUniqueDocs`, the cursor landing past the rows read rather than the docs kept
- the remote adapter on both routes
- both assert helpers
- generator dedupe
- the controller on both routes, including precedence and the 400 cases

**Describe the issue**
`Form service > save > attachGeoToReport > appends to an existing geolocation_log rather than replacing it` fails intermittently by one millisecond:

```
AssertionError: expected [ ..., { timestamp: 1789986113548, recording: { latitude: 9, longitude: 9 } } ]
