title: feat(#11433): plan bulk operations at execution time
body:
# Description

Closes #11433

A bulk operation is now planned when Sentinel runs it, not when the API receives it. The API validates the request, records the intent as a single log document, and returns an id. Sentinel plans the operation when it reaches it, so every plan sees the result of every operation before it, and a plan can never be stale by the time it is applied.

**The API, synchronously.** Parse the request, assert permissions, fetch the target through the type-specific `get` so a place id sent to the person endpoint is still a `404`. Then advisory validation through the shared library, which is still a `400`. A dry run returns `200 { summary }` without writing anything. Otherwise a single log doc is written to `medic-logs` and the response is `202 { id }`. The API no longer writes action docs.

**Sentinel, asynchronously.** The changes feed on `medic-logs` is only a wake-up signal. Each pass asks the database what to do next, in a fixed order of preference: the oldest action doc, then the oldest `running` log (which means every action has run, so the operation is finished), then the oldest `queued` log (which means plan it). Action docs are written before the log says `running`, so an interrupted plan is always "queued with action docs" and can be told apart from a finished operation, which is "running with none".

**The shared library.** `shared-libs/bulk-operations` holds the query and planning logic in one place. Each planner exposes `validate(params)` and `plan(params)`, so Sentinel can dispatch on the operation type without knowing anything about deletes or moves. The API uses it for advisory validation and dry runs, Sentinel for the authoritative plan. `lineage-constraints` moved here too and now throws a `ValidationError`, which the API maps to a `400` and Sentinel records on the log.

**What replaces what.** The `async.queue`, `enqueue`, `inProgress` set and `loadInitialQueue` are gone: startup and normal running are the same loop, and the scheduler never holds more than one item so there is nothing to deduplicate. `runOperations` and `saveProgress` survive unchanged. The old `processAction` no longer writes a per-action status or decides operation-level completion, and its log write throws instead of being swallowed.

**API surface changes.**

- The `202` body is now `{ id }`; `BulkOperationQueued` loses `summary`.
- The dry-run body is unchanged, and is documented as a point-in-time estimate that is recomputed when the operation runs.
- The poll endpoint gains `type`, `params`, `status` and `error`, and the per-action entries lose `status`. Callers should treat the operation as finished when its `status` is `completed` or `failed`, rather than inspecting every action.

**Two judgement calls worth a look in review:**

- A missing move destination is still a `404`, not a `400`. The planner would report it as a validation failure, but the existing behaviour and its test expect a `404`, so the handler still resolves the destination itself.
- The issue specifies `queue(type, params, requester)` but does not name a field for it on the log doc. It is recorded as `requested_by`, following `bulk_uploaded_by` on the bulk upload log, which is the only comparable field and lives in the same database. Happy to rename.

**Testing.** A new `shared-libs/bulk-operations` suite covers both planners and the lineage constraints (45 tests). The Sentinel suite covers the scheduler: each `pullNext` rule, the write order at plan time, a plan that fails validation, and an action doc that could not be written. The API service tests now cover the handlers, with the planning itself tested in the library. `unit-api` 1704 passing, `unit-sentinel` 328 passing, `shared-libs/bulk-operations` 45 passing, all above their coverage thresholds.

The integration tests were updated for the new model. The helper that waits for an operation now waits on the operation's status rather than on its actions, which are absent until it has been planned. Two tests replace the one that depended on the API writing action docs: one asserts that only the log is written while Sentinel is down and that the operation completes once it starts, and one queues a move, removes the destination before Sentinel plans it, and asserts the operation fails with the reason on the log.

title: fetchAndFilter drops a document from a paged result
body:
**Describe the bug**

`fetchAndFilter` in `shared-libs/cht-datasource/src/local/libs/doc.ts` fills a page by fetching more rows when the filter rejects some. It then sets the next cursor with `currentSkip + currentLimit - overFetchCount`.

That subtraction counts documents, but `skip` counts rows. When a rejected row sits after the first surplus accepted row, the cursor lands too far to the right, and every accepted document in the gap is lost. Those documents were fetched and passed the filter. `.slice(0, limit)` discarded them, and the cursor never goes back for them.

The `noMoreResults` check at line 184 also runs before the full page check at line 188, so a surplus on the last fetch is discarded and the caller gets `cursor: null`.

Nothing logs and nothing throws. The page comes back full and the cursor chain looks healthy, so a caller cannot detect the loss.

The paths that reach this are the ones whose filter can reject a row: `Contact.v1.getPage` and `Report.v1.getPage` with an ids qualifier, where an id is missing or points at another type; the phones qualifier on `Contact.v1.getPage` and `Contact.v1.getUuidsPage`, where the phone view emits a document that is not a configured contact type; and offline freetext search for contacts and reports. The contact type, `byForms`, person, place and target paths do not reach it, because their view keys on the property the filter tests, so nothing is rejected.

There is a second, smaller problem in the same file. `fetchAndFilterIds` builds its dedup `Set` inside one page request, so a document can come back on two pages. Only the offline freetext views emit a document more than once, and their one consumer, `getIntersection` in `shared-libs/search/src/search.js`, already removes duplicates. A cross page guarantee needs the cursor to carry state, which is a larger change, so this ticket does not ask for it. The rule worth recording is that a caller must dedupe when the view can emit a document more than once.

**To Reproduce**

Store five documents that are not contacts, then three that are. Read them back by id with a page size of 2.

```
curl -s -u medic:password -X POST http://localhost:5984/medic/_bulk_docs \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"docs":[
    {"_id":"ff-bad-1","type":"data_record","form":"X","reported_date":1700000000000},
    {"_id":"ff-bad-2","type":"data_record","form":"X","reported_date":1700000000000},
    {"_id":"ff-bad-3","type":"data_record","form":"X","reported_date":1700000000000},
    {"_id":"ff-bad-4","type":"data_record","form":"X","reported_date":1700000000000},
    {"_id":"ff-bad-5","type":"data_record","form":"X","reported_date":1700000000000},
    {"_id":"ff-good-1","type":"person","name":"FF Good 1","reported_date":1700000000000},
    {"_id":"ff-good-2","type":"person","name":"FF Good 2","reported_date":1700000000000},
    {"_id":"ff-good-3","type":"person","name":"FF Good 3","reported_date":1700000000000}]}'

curl -s -u medic:password "http://localhost:5988/api/v1/contact?ids=ff-bad-1,ff-bad-2,ff-bad-3,ff-bad-4,ff-bad-5,ff-good-1,ff-good-2,ff-good-3&limit=2"
```

At a page size of 2 the answer is `["ff-good-1","ff-good-2"]` with `cursor: null`. At a page size of 3 it is all three. `ff-good-3` is a contact in the requested list, and at a page size of 2 it never arrives, while the null cursor reports the list as complete.

**Expected behavior**

The page holds `limit` documents. The cursor points at the first row the page did not use. `cursor: null` means the result set is complete.

**Environment**

- App: `cht-datasource`, reached through api and webapp
- Version: 4.18.0 and later. The function is unchanged since 4.12.0, but no caller could reject a row before 4.18.0. The released 5.3.0 and 5.3.1 both carry it.

One suggestion for whoever picks this up. Stopping the scan when the page is full, counting the rows consumed, and taking the cursor from that count fixes it. A sweep of every accept and reject pattern up to length 10, at page sizes 1 to 5, gives 1007 wrong results now and none with that change, at the cost of about 9% more requests. Every existing test that asserts an exact cursor value keeps its value, including `test/local/libs/doc.spec.ts:608`, the one unit test with a real rejection. The regression test belongs in the `describe('fetchAndFilter')` block of `shared-libs/cht-datasource/test/local/libs/doc.spec.ts`, and the smallest fixture is six rows at a page size of 2, where rows 1, 2 and 6 fail the filter.

title: feat(#11281): add an offline sync pairing screen
body:
# Description

Closes #11281 (webapp half). The android half is medic/cht-android#443.

Adds an `offline-sync` page where one device hosts a session and another joins it by scanning a QR code. The page talks to cht-android only through `OfflineSyncService`, over the `medicmobile_android` bridge.

The entry shows in both navigations (header and sidebar) when the user holds the permission for that side AND the device can do it:
- host: `can_relay_offline_data_bundle` and `offline_sync_host_available()`
- join: `can_send_offline_data_bundle` and `offline_sync_join_available()`, never for an online-only user, since the server refuses their bundles

On the web, the menu entry now shows to offline users who hold either offline sync permission, and the page tells them it needs the Android app, so the feature can be found on the instance. Online-only users, admins included, don't see it on the web.

Hosting needs Android 8 and joining works on everything we support, so the webapp asks the app instead of guessing from a version. An app older than this webapp has the bridge but not these methods, so it counts as no bridge: the entry stays hidden and the page says "Mobile app required" instead of throwing.

Android answers through three `AndroidApi.v1` callbacks: `resolveOfflineSyncHostingResult`, `resolveOfflineSyncPairing` and `offlineSyncPermissionsResolved`. What it sends is always a code, so all the wording lives in the translation files, en es fr ne sw. The Nepali and Swahili strings could use a native speaker's eye.

The two permissions are documented in medic/cht-docs#2267 (draft until release).

title: Use consistant formatting in XLSXForms
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**

All our forms in cht-core (particularly the `default` ones) are old and getting rough-around-the-edges.  Particularly their formatting and look/feel has drifted over the years so they are not super consistent or cohesive. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We can leverage the `form format` command in https://github.com/jkuester/chtoolbox to give the forms a consistent look/feel.  This will also give them conditional formatting rules to keep the formatting correct as the content of the forms change in the future.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

https://github.com/Sjlver/yxf is another option for auto-formatting XLSXforms. However, it does not work dynamically and its formatting style does not seem well optimized for large forms with lots of group nesting.

title: Syncing issues with rebuilt Nouveau index after archiving
body:
**Describe the bug**

Replication errors have been observed on one production instance when a Nouveau index was dropped and rebuilt after documents had been purged from the CouchDB using the new [archiving endpoint](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/technical-overview/data/performance/archiving/).  

Extensive investigation has identified several CouchDB issues that are involved:

- https://github.com/apache/couchdb/issues/6118
- https://github.com/apache/couchdb/issues/6132

We are working with the Couch team to fix/validate these issues and plan to include the patched version of Couch in an upcoming CHT release.   

The core problem, as it is experienced in the CHT, is that re-building a Nouveau index (such as the one used for driving the user replication logic) from scratch (e.g. updating the design doc or dropping/re-adding the design doc) when documents have been purged from the Couch database (e.g. with the `/archive` endpoint) simply fails. The Nouveau service hits an error. Without that index, the server is unable to calculate which docs belong to which user and so users are not able to sync.      

**Expected behavior**
It should work with no errors. 

**Environment**
- Version: `5.3.0`

**Additional context**
@eljhkrr @witash Please supply any additional corrections or details!  🙏

title: test(#6495): make sentinel schedule tests timezone independent
body:
# Description `npm run unit-sentinel` failed when the machine's timezone isn't a whole number of hours from UTC (e.g. `Asia/Kolkata` +5:30, `Asia/Kathmandu` +5:45, `Australia/Adelaide`), and also in a few zones with odd historical offsets (`Africa/Monrovia`, `Pacific/Kiritimati` in 1970) or large positive offsets (`Pacific/Auckland`). The production code is fine. Sentinel runs `later` in local time (`later.date.localTime()` in `lib/scheduling.js`) and uses local `startOf('hour')` / local dates, but the tests hard-coded UTC-aligned expected values. The "calculation issue" suspected in 2020 came from pinning only moment's timezone (via moment-timezone) while `later` kept using the device timezone. This PR changes tests only: - `reminders.spec.js`: `getSchedule` and `matchReminder` tests use fixed **local** wall-clock times (June 2021) instead of UTC literals / ticks from the 1970 epoch. - `outbound.spec.js`: the "due cron" test sets the clock to 03:05 local time and sets `later`'s local-time mode explicitly for the test (restored afterwards), instead of inheriting it from whichever spec loaded first. - `archiving.spec.js`: the auto-archive clock is set to local noon so the server's local date is 27 Aug in every zone. **Testing** - Full `npm run unit-sentinel` (including coverage thresholds) passes in 11 timezones: UTC, Europe/Rome, Asia/Kolkata, Asia/Kathmandu, Australia/Adelaide, America/St_Johns, Pacific/Kiritimati, Pacific/Pago_Pago, Canada/Pacific, Africa/Monrovia, Pacific/Auckland. Before this change, 7 of them failed. - To check the tests still catch real regressions, I broke the code under test on purpose and confirmed the edited tests fail: reminder window start (`startOf('day')`, dropping the one-day lookback), `later` in UTC instead of local time (this one wasn't detectable before), outbound cron never due, archiving expiry 60 → 59 days. - `npm run lint` passes; full unit suite passes. Possible follow-ups (not in this PR, happy to open issues if useful): - A sentinel TZ-matrix script like webapp's `unit:mocha:tz`, so this can't regress. - `outbound.spec.js` fails 3 tests when run on its own, even in UTC (it relies on the transitions lib being initialised by specs that load earlier). **Test output** (`npm run unit-sentinel`)
Before: master's tests with TZ=Asia/Kolkata (5 failing) ``` 277 passing (10s) 5 failing 1) outbound schedule execute should only process queued tasks with due "cron" or non-existent "cron" field: AssertionError: expected 1 to equal 2 + expected - actual -1 +2 2) reminders getSchedule should return date from next schedule for cron: AssertionError: expected '2021-06-17T11:30:00.000Z' to equal '2021-06-17T11:00:00.000Z' + expected - actual -2021-06-17T11:30:00.000Z +2021-06-17T11:00:00.000Z 3) reminders matchReminder should return false if no schedule: AssertionError: expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal [ Array(1) ] + expected - actual [ { "descending": true - "endkey": "reminderlog:formA:-1800000" + "endkey": "reminderlog:formA:0" "limit": 1 "startkey": "reminderlog:formA:86400000" } ] 4) reminders matchReminder should query allDocs with correct keys: AssertionError: expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal [ Array(1) ] + expected - actual [ { "descending": true - "endkey": "reminderlog:formB:-1800000" + "endkey": "reminderlog:formB:0" "limit": 1 "startkey": "reminderlog:formB:86400000" } ] 5) reminders matchReminder should return correct prev schedule when no results: AssertionError: expected [ 1, 1970-01-02T00:00:00.000Z, …(1) ] to deeply equal [ 1, 1970-01-02T00:00:00.000Z, …(1) ] + expected - actual [ 1 [Date: 1970-01-02T00:00:00.000Z] - [Date: 1969-12-31T23:30:00.000Z] + [Date: 1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z] ] ```
After: this branch with TZ=Asia/Kolkata (282 passing) ``` 282 passing (11s) ```
After: this branch in 11 timezones (all passing) ``` UTC 282 passing (10s) Europe/Rome 282 passing (9s) Asia/Kolkata 282 passing (9s) Asia/Kathmandu 282 passing (9s) Australia/Adelaide 282 passing (11s) America/St_Johns 282 passing (11s) Pacific/Kiritimati 282 passing (11s) Pacific/Pago_Pago 282 passing (11s) Canada/Pacific 282 passing (11s) Africa/Monrovia 282 passing (11s) Pacific/Auckland 282 passing (11s) ```

body:
Bumps [undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici) to 7.30.0 and updates ancestor dependency . These dependencies need to be updated together. Updates `undici` from 7.29.0 to 7.30.0
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v7.30.0

What's Changed

  • [Backport v7.x] fix: selectively re-enable SIMD for ppc64 by @​github-actions[bot] in nodejs/undici#5794
  • Backport upgrade diagnostics lifecycle fixes to v7.x by @​BridgeAR in nodejs/undici#5783
  • [Backport v7.x] fix: honor backpressure in decompression interceptor by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5837
  • fix: close rejected HTTP/2 WebSocket streams on v7.x by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5876
  • test(fetch): make pull-dont-push exceed any socket buffer by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5889

Full Changelog: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/compare/v7.29.1...v7.30.0

v7.29.1

⚠️ Security fixes

High severity

  • GHSA-w293-vg96-wgc3: BalancedPool could drop function-valued connection options while cloning its configuration, including custom TLS certificate validation callbacks. Undici now preserves connect and legacy tls options when creating upstreams. Fixed by f690157d.
  • GHSA-rfgv-xxqx-mfg5: a WebSocket server could select a subprotocol when none was requested, causing an uncaught TypeError that could terminate the process. Undici now rejects the handshake with protocol error 1002. Fixed by 6615e017.

Medium severity

  • GHSA-3wwx-pv8p-q78v: a malformed permessage-deflate payload exceeding the configured decompression limit could emit an unhandled zlib error and terminate the process. Undici now destroys the inflater after reaching the limit. Fixed by 63cf698b.
  • GHSA-rx4f-c7p8-82vq: an unclean WebSocketStream close could create an unobserved rejected promise when its writable stream was locked, potentially terminating the process. Undici now propagates the failure through the retained writable stream controller. Fixed by 1858656e.
  • GHSA-2jfj-6hjv-fm6j: shared caches could store and replay responses containing Set-Cookie, disclosing one user's cookies to another caller. Undici now excludes these responses from shared caches, including existing entries and revalidation paths. Fixed by b6c5a002.
  • GHSA-3xpg-4rpp-hhhm: the decompression interceptor did not bound decoded output, allowing compressed responses to consume excessive memory. Undici now limits every decompression stage to 64 MiB by default and supports a configurable maxSize. Fixed by 2c7d7e12.
  • GHSA-pmjh-fq2x-6v4x: a terminal retry failure after response headers were exposed could orphan the original response body, causing consumers to hang indefinitely. Undici now propagates the terminal error to the exposed body. Fixed by 3c672659.

Low severity

  • GHSA-8436-99hf-9mmv: cache interceptors could store and replay responses to unsafe HTTP methods such as POST or DELETE. Undici now restricts cache reads and writes to safe methods while preserving invalidation by successful unsafe requests. Fixed by b61d9432.
  • GHSA-2gqq-gqf2-x968: the dump interceptor could treat an oversized chunked response as successfully truncated when no Content-Length was present. Undici now enforces maxSize against received bytes and aborts oversized responses. Fixed by 21693f40.
  • GHSA-r53p-7pc4-xj5r: the retry interceptor could concatenate a resumed response with inconsistent framing into downstream output, enabling response splitting or corruption. Undici now validates Content-Range against the original response framing before resuming. Fixed by cd8af90b.

What's Changed

  • [v7.x] drop: remove Node.js 26 from shared-builtin CI build by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5592
  • fix(h2): honour headersTimeout by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5604
  • fix(h2): keep the connection ref'd while requests are outstanding by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5605
  • ci: increase Windows workflow timeout on v7.x by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5621
  • fix(h2): retire the request that completed, not the head of the queue by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5618
  • fix(h2): settle a request whose stream is cancelled by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5607
  • perf: reduce EventSourceStream parser allocations (#5032) by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5646

title: fix(#7048): export each message once in the messages export
body:
# Description The messages export (Admin → Import & export data → Messages) wrote the same message several times. I reproduced it on current `master` with a local CHT: I sent 3 messages from the webapp (one to a single contact, one to two recipients) with no SMS gateway, and the downloaded CSV had **10 rows instead of 3**. So it also affects messages with several recipients, not only `pending` ones. **Cause:** the export reads doc ids from the `medic/messages_by_state` view, which emits one row per message plus an extra `pending-or-forwarded` row for pending/forwarded messages. `message-mapper.getDocIds` returned one id per row, and the export then wrote *all* of a doc's messages for every copy of the id. A doc with N messages came out about N² times, plus extra copies while pending. The repeats are usually in different batches, because the view is sorted by state and due date. **Fix** (the view is unchanged: `messaging.js` and sentinel's `due_tasks` also use it): - `message-mapper.js` flags that its ids can repeat (`hasDuplicateDocIds`). - `export-data.js`: for such exports, the reader remembers which docs it has already written and skips repeats, within a batch and across batches. When a whole batch is repeats, it fetches the next batch instead of ending the export. - `controllers/export-data.js`: when the HTTP response closes, the export stream is destroyed, so a cancelled download stops querying CouchDB. Without this, a download cancelled during a long run of repeat-only batches (e.g. the `pending-or-forwarded` block) kept querying until that run ended. Only the messages export de-duplicates. The close handler applies to all CSV exports, but only changes anything when a download is closed before it finishes. **Testing** - New unit tests, each failing before the change: - `exports each message once when the view lists its doc once per message`: view-shaped rows, paged 2 at a time. Before: 10 message ids for 3 messages. - `fetches and writes a doc once when it repeats within and across batches` - `keeps reading after a batch made only of already exported docs` - `stops querying when the export is destroyed during a run of already exported docs`. Before: 997 queries after destroy. - `stops the export when the response closes` (controller). Before: the stream was not destroyed. - `npm run lint` and the full unit suite pass. - Manual, on a local CHT (API from this branch vs `master`, same database): - messages: 10 → **3** rows (same unique rows); - reports, contacts and feedback CSVs byte-for-byte identical to `master`; - with 3,000 docs of each type, all exports are complete. Cancelling a download partway stops the export (no further CouchDB requests) with no errors in the API log. **Downloaded CSVs** from my manual test on a local CHT: I sent one message to one contact and one message to two recipients from the webapp (no SMS gateway, so they stay `pending`), then used Admin → Import & export data → Messages → Download. Same database, exported once with `master` and once with this branch.

title: feat(#9536): add a read only fhir facade
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

feat(#1234): add hat wobble
^--^(#^--^): ^------------^
|     |      |
|     |      + - > subject
|     |
|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: build|feat|fix|perf|refactor|test|chore

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

<!-- DESCRIPTION -->

Serve CHT documents as FHIR R4 resources at /api/v1/fhir, driven entirely by app_settings.fhir: Patient (person contacts), Encounter (reports) and the Observations an Encounter projects from its form fields.

- shared-libs/cht-fhir: a pure mapping library. Config and a CHT document in, a FHIR resource or a query plan out. A closed, hard-coded element catalog for the three resource types, scoped config validation, and query planning over cht-datasource only.
- api: read and search endpoints, plus the generated conformance resources (metadata, StructureDefinition, ValueSet, ConceptMap, CodeSystem) and $catalog/$diagnostics for operators.
- shared-libs/cht-fhir/README.md is the configuration reference; fhir-mapping.json is a worked example.


Some notes:

The most substantial piec of this PR is the configuration and mapping.
It deliberately does not use FML, the existing outbound push mapping, or any other mapping library to do the mapping. This is to keep things simple and target specifically to CHT->FHIR mapping; FML adds a lot of complexity, as does any other mapping library, and outbound push style mapping is too generic.

But that does mean a new configuration format; it's described in README.md so I won't repeat it here, buts it's important to design and review carefully since when (actually if) this is ever used it will be difficult to change later.

There is also a lot of mapping logic hardcoded in `mapper.ts`. This is deliberate; a lot of mapping tasks are going to be common to all cht deployments, so it can use what it knows about the CHT data structure and FHIR resources to do some mapping automatically that would otherwise be boilerplate, or need to be supported by a broader config.

In the first version, only certain resources are supported, and these are hardcoded in `catalog.ts`. Future version may also allow this to be configurable, but for the first version it simplifies things a lot to just have the supported resources hard coded.

The other parts should be straightforward; there's a new controller for api that does some fhir boilerplate and a little query planner to translate fhir requests to datasource requests. It uses datasource only, never direct couch queries, so it can't currently use some of the views that would be helpful, like `reports_by_subject` or `contacts_by_reference`.  There already PRs to add those to datasource so it won't be too hard to update the facade once they are available.

All this code is generated by claude code, but with careful line by line review.

I tried to keep it minimal, but it ends up being ~5000 lines, with 2000 lines of functional code and the rest tests, comments, and other things. It can't be too much smaller than that and still be complete; one thing that could still be removed is the conformance resources but strict conformance is a goal of this project, and its only a few hundred more lines, so I decided to leave it in.

<!-- ISSUE NUMBER -->

closes #9536

- [ ] UI/UX backwards compatible: Test it works for the new design (enabled by default). And test it works in the old design, enable `can_view_old_navigation` permission to see the old design. Test it has appropriate design for RTL languages.

# Description

<!-- DESCRIPTION -->

Adds `byShortcodes` and `byExternalRefs` qualifiers to cht-datasource over `medic-client/contacts_by_reference`, and exposes them as `shortcode` / `external_ref` params on `GET /api/v1/contact/uuid` and `GET /api/v1/contact`. Follows the `byPhones` pattern from #11249. No existing `contacts_by_reference` caller is migrated (that's #11443).

- `byShortcodes` matches verbatim. `byExternalRefs` upper-cases its input to match the view's `rc_code.toUpperCase()`. A hand-built lower-case qualifier fails the guard.
- Local: phones, shortcodes and external refs share one keyed-view helper. Both the uuid and doc paths filter through `isContact` (the view emits `national_office` and unconfigured `type: contact` docs). Both paths also return each contact at most once per page, since a contact with both `patient_id` and `place_id` in the supplied list is emitted twice.
- The existing assert helpers are extended to accept the new shapes rather than duplicated. They keep their `...Phones...` names.
- Precedence on `/uuid` is `phone`, then `shortcode`, then `external_ref`, then `type`/`freetext`. On `/contact`, `ids` comes before all of them.
- The only change visible to existing API users is the no-qualifier 400 message, which now lists the new params.

title: chore(#11465): fix `ai-review` workflow
body:
# Description

Closes #11465
 
Both of the review jobs were failing for different reasons. I have tested this exact configuration on [forked PR](https://github.com/jkuester/chtoolbox/pull/385) in chtoolbox and confirmed it works.

## `code-review` failure

The OCR run was failing on all PRs. This was caused by OCR breaking its own action by trying to auto-update right as the action spins up... :facepalm:   Fixed by setting the envar to prevent the auto-update.

## `completeness-review` failure

The Claude run was failing on PRs from forks because we are checking out the PR head on a `pull_request_target` run without setting the [necessary `allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/securely-using-pull_request_target).

Basically we have to have that permission to be able to run on PRs from forks. This is okay and part of the risk we are mitigating by only allowing the workflow to be manually triggered by maintainers (instead of running it automatically).  Nothing in the workflow executes code from the fork.

I have done some further hardening in the job by limiting read access to only the working directory and by adding a tool use hook that hard blocks all bash/monitor executions except for what is needed by  the skill.  

## AI Disclose

This is all Claude's fault.

v1.20.0 — August 19, 2026

This release hardens runtime option handling, adds RFC 9110 status-code aliases, fixes Node.js and XHR reliability issues, and refreshes project tooling and documentation.

⚠️ Breaking Changes & Deprecations

  • HTTP Status Naming: Added ContentTooLarge (413) and UnprocessableContent (422), while retaining PayloadTooLarge and UnprocessableEntity as backward-compatible deprecated aliases. (#11082)

🔒 Security Fixes

  • Runtime Option Handling: Hardened behavioral configuration reads against shared and foreign prototype pollution and normalized unsafe interceptor replacement objects. This also clarifies Fetch redirect and custom implementation behavior, HTTP/2 DNS and proxy handling, CIDR-based NO_PROXY matching, and malformed data URI rejection; see the PR for documented compatibility effects. (#11141)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Interceptor Lifecycle: Prevented unbounded handler-array growth by trimming trailing ejected interceptors without changing iteration semantics, and kept interceptor operations safe when the public handlers field is nullish. (#11087, #11118)
  • Request Error Preservation: Prevented custom Error.prepareStackTrace implementations that return non-string values from replacing the original request failure with an unrelated TypeError. (#11109)
  • XHR Reliability: Navigation-canceled requests now reject with ECONNABORTED instead of resolving with status 0, while successful downloads flush their final progress callback during the live loadend dispatch. (#11094, #11121)
  • Node.js Socket Memory: Removed request-context retention from per-socket error listeners, preventing completed response data from being pinned for the lifetime of pooled keep-alive sockets. (#11091)
  • Core Methods and HTTP Errors: Prevented structural method-header buckets from leaking into outgoing headers, standardized invalid DNS lookup and httpVersion failures as AxiosError.ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE, and corrected the timeoutErrorMessage merge strategy. (#11096)

v1.19.0 — July 22, 2026

This release raises the form-data security floor, adds configuration and type-system capabilities, and fixes NO_PROXY matching, interceptor errors, progress reporting, and serialization edge cases.

🚀 New Features

  • Configuration Extensibility: Preserved own-enumerable symbol-keyed fields through mergeConfig and added a generic params type across public TypeScript declarations, responses, errors, adapters, and serializers. (#11043, #11081)
  • Header Parameter Parsing: Added the opt-in AxiosHeaders.parseParameters() parser for quote-aware, RFC-style HTTP parameter parsing while preserving legacy parsing behavior. (#11051)
  • HTTP Status Codes: Added the missing Cloudflare 520 WebServerReturnsAnUnknownError status and matching ESM/CJS declarations. (#11067)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Form Data Conversion: Limited formDataToJSON path splitting to dot and bracket notation, preserving literal punctuation in keys, and removed browser-facing Buffer.from usage from toFormData to avoid unnecessary polyfills. (#11006, #11018)

  • Proxy Bypass: Canonicalized IPv4 shorthand, octal, and hexadecimal forms during NO_PROXY matching and honored * entries within comma- or space-separated bypass lists. (#11029, #11053)

  • Cancellation: Propagated already-aborted input signals immediately when composing abort signals. (#11035)

  • Header Handling: Preserved empty first values for duplicate singleton headers and made AxiosHeaders#getSetCookie() consistently return arrays for present values. (#11036, #11037)

  • URL Handling: Included normalized, safely redacted offending URLs in malformed-protocol errors and removed repeated trailing slashes when combining base URLs. (#11008, #11038)

  • Progress Events: Clamped malformed negative progress values to zero and ensured final Node.js download progress events are delivered before streamed responses close. (#11039, #11040)

  • Error and JSON Serialization: Serialized Set values as arrays in JSON-compatible snapshots and synthesized useful AxiosError messages from otherwise-empty AggregateError instances. (#11044, #11059)

  • Content-Length Enforcement: Corrected base64 data: URL size estimation so maxContentLength is enforced consistently by the HTTP and Fetch adapters. (#11061)

  • Synchronous Interceptors: Prevented requests from being dispatched after synchronous request interceptors fail unless their paired rejection handler resolves successfully. (#11071)

title: feat(#11434): retry bulk operation actions on transient failures
body:
# Description

Closes #11434

A failure that might work on a second try no longer fails the operation. The batch is left where it was and presented again once its cool-down has passed: immediately the first time, then a minute at a time up to five, and every five minutes after that, for as long as the failure lasts.

**What counts as worth retrying.** A new `RetryableError`, plus a helper that classifies a PouchDB failure by status (`408`, `409` and any `5xx`) and one that spots a `conflict` row. Everything else is unexpected and still fails the action, so a genuine bug does not turn into an infinite retry.

**The handler contract.** Handlers still return the operations that failed *permanently*: a missing doc, a guard mismatch, a row error other than `conflict`, an operation with no id. They now **throw** for anything that stopped the batch running as a whole, which leaves the cursor where it was so the batch that failed is the batch that runs next.

**Every handler is idempotent**, which matters more than it looks: without this, a re-run reads the doc it already updated, sees the guard no longer matches, and reports a spurious permanent failure.

| Handler | Already applied looks like | Treated as |
|---|---|---|
| `set-parent` | `doc.parent` deep-equals `op.parent` | success, write skipped |
| `set-contact` | `doc.contact` deep-equals `op.contact`, with both absent counting as equal | success, write skipped |
| `delete` | no row doc in `medic` | success (already the case) |
| `delete-user` | `deleteUser` rejects with a 404 | success |

**The scheduler** records the failure on the doc as `error_count` and `next_attempt_date`, and leaves work alone until it is due. Since an outstanding action always wins over planning, nothing else is planned while one is cooling down. `error_count` is what the archiving jobs already call the same thing.

A plan that fails for a repeatable reason gets the same treatment, which is only possible because #11433 moved planning into Sentinel.

**Two bugs found along the way, both in code this PR builds on:**

- `saveProgress` did `get`, mutate, `put`, return the doc. `put` does not update `_rev` on the doc it was given, so the caller was left holding a revision one behind and the action was deleted with it. That conflicted, and `deleteDocsFrom` never checked the rows, so it passed silently: the action survived, the next pass picked it up, rewrote the same entry on the log and deleted it on the second attempt. Every action that processed a batch paid for that. It now carries over the revision its own write reported, and a delete that did not happen raises.
- The tests stubbed `put` as resolving `undefined`, where CouchDB returns `{ ok, id, rev }`. That is part of why the above was invisible. The stub is realistic now and the assertion checks the new revision is the one used.

**Testing.** The Sentinel suite covers the backoff ramp, a handler asking to retry (cursor unmoved, nothing recorded, action left in place), the failure count lengthening the cool-down, a plan kept queued, an unexpected failure still failing the action, work skipped while it cools down, and a finished operation left alone when the view has not caught up. `unit-sentinel` 361 passing, `unit-api` 1706 passing, `shared-libs/bulk-operations` 50 passing, all above their coverage thresholds.

There is also an integration test for the cool-down, since none of the above proves it against a real CouchDB: an action part way through a retry is left untouched while it waits, and then runs on the wake-up Sentinel scheduled for itself.

title: chore(#9820): upgrade to latest @medic/eslint-config
body:
# Description

Closes #9820 

Main goal here (and source of many of the line changes) was bumping to the latest `@medic/eslint-config` (along with newer versions of various other eslint deps).

Also uplifting some other dependencies:

- Patch and minor bumps across the board.
- A set of major bumps that needed little or no code change.

The main thing driving a lot of the major version bumps was a choice to move forwards with consuming "ESM-only" versions of the dependencies.  In general, our CommonJS module setup can work with ESM dependencies _as long as those deps do not use top-level `await`s._ Those are technically valid for ESM, but will break `require`s from CJS. IMHO we don't have any better options here than to consume the newer versions ands rely on our automated tests to catch any module-loading issues. An ESM re-write is not a super high priority right now (though the power of Ai makes it tempting... :thinking:).  I would rather carefully use newer versions here vs just getting stuck further and further behind on all of these... 

## Lint config and autofixes (`@medic/eslint-config` 1.2, ESLint plugin majors)
- `eslint.config.js`: removed the local `@stylistic/*` rules that duplicated rules now provided by `@medic/eslint-config`. Only the deliberate overrides remain, e.g. `indent` with `SwitchCase: 1`.
- Mechanical lint autofixes across `config/default/`, tests and a few webapp/shared-lib files: brace style, dot notation instead of `obj['prop']`, consistent returns, spacing. `config/default/app_settings.json` was rebuilt from the updated config sources.
- `eslint-plugin-jsdoc`:
  - disabled `jsdoc/require-throws-type`, because TypeDoc drops `{Type}` annotations on `@throws`
  - switched `@typeParam` to `@template` in `cht-datasource/src/libs/core.ts`
- `config/default/*-extras.js`: `isNaN` changed to `Number.isNaN` to fix Sonar findings.

## Test tooling (chai 5, chai-as-promised 8, chai-exclude 3, sinon-chai 4, sinon 22, mocha 12, nyc 18, rewire 9)
- The chai plugins are now ESM packages loaded with `require()`, so imports were changed to `require('…').default`. This touches the mocha and wdio configs and the shared-lib test setup files.
- I have removed a number of local `use` calls for plugins that are already being used in shared config (and so do not need the call in the test file).  These lines would have to have been updated anyway with the ESM changes.
- admin: chai 5 no longer ships the browser `chai.js` file that admin's karma tests load. admin now has its own `chai@^4` devDependency, and karma loads it from `admin/node_modules`.
- `cht-datasource`: added explicit `types` lists to `tsconfig.json`/`tsconfig.build.json`, and removed casts in tests that are no longer needed

## AI Disclosure

Did a lot of the changes here using Claude through [paseo.sh](https://paseo.sh/). I have carefully reviewed/confirmed all changes.

## Major dependency version bumps

| Package | Before → After | Type | What made it a major |

title: feat(#10280): make the replication interval configurable
body:
# Description

The webapp syncs offline users with the server every 5 minutes, and this is hard-coded. This PR adds a global app setting, `replication_interval_minutes`, so a deployment can sync less often to reduce server load.

**How it works**
- **Not set** (or `null`): 5 minutes, so nothing changes for existing projects.
- **A number from 5 to 60** (fractions are fine, e.g. `7.5`): the periodic sync runs at that interval. The maximum is 60 because timers can pause while a device sleeps, so much longer intervals may not fire in practice.
- **Anything else** (`1`, `4.99`, `61`, `"30"`, `"abc"`…): 5 minutes, plus one console warning naming the setting and the value.
- The metadata database syncs every 30 minutes or at the configured interval, whichever is longer.
- The setting is read once, when `DBSyncService` is created. A changed value is used after the device has downloaded the new settings and the app has been reloaded (the usual "Update available" prompt).
- Startup sync, **Sync now**, and uploads after local changes work as before.

**Changes after review** (thanks @jkuester)
- Minimum is now the 5-minute default.
- The interval is loaded once and cached in a readonly property, instead of on every sync. Because reading the settings is asynchronous, it is a cached promise that both timers wait for.
- Removed the `typeof` check.
- The metadata interval is `Math.max(30 min, interval)`.
- Maximum lowered to 60 minutes, and no fallback around the settings read.
- Docs: medic/cht-docs#2268, plus a follow-up for the 60-minute maximum.

**Testing**
- New unit tests in `db-sync.service.spec.ts` (fake timers): the 5 and 60 limits, fractions, invalid values, overlapping first syncs, going online before the setting has loaded, metadata timing, and online-only users. All 76 tests in the file pass, and so do `npm run lint` and `npm run unit-webapp`.
- Manual test on a local CHT built from this branch, with an offline `chw` user in Chrome. For each value I changed the setting on the server, synced, and reloaded from the "Update available" prompt. I recorded the sync timers the app created and timed the 5- and 10-minute ones in real time:

| `replication_interval_minutes` | Sync every | Metadata every | Console warning |
|---|---|---|---|
| not set | 5 min (downloads at 0.2, 5.2, 10.2 min) | 30 min | no |
| `5` | 5 min | 30 min | no |
| `7.5` | 7.5 min | 30 min | no |
| `10` | 10 min (downloads at 11.5, 21.5 min) | 30 min | no |
| `60` | 60 min | 60 min | no |
| `1`, `4.99`, `61`, `"abc"`, `"30"` | 5 min | 30 min | yes |
| removed again | 5 min | 30 min | no |

Before the reload the app kept the old value, as expected.

Closes #10280

# Code review checklist

title: Release 5.3.2
body:
# Planning - CHT Community 

- [x] Create an GH Milestone for the release and add this issue to it.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.
- [x] Ensure that all issues are labeled correctly, particularly ensure that "Regressions" are labeled with "Affects: <version>" labels. The "Affects" label is used in a link in the Known Issues section of the release notes of that version so it has to match exactly. To make sure the label is correct go to the [release notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/releases/#release-notes) and ensure the issue is listed.
- [x] Assign a maintainer as Release Manager for this release.

# Development - Release Manager

When development is ready to begin one of the maintainers should be nominated as a Release Manager. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Ensure all tickets in the Milestone are closed and merged to `master`.
- [x] Check out the target release branch `<major>.<minor>.x`. For example if you're patching `5.2.0`, you would check out `5.2.x` branch.
- [x] Cherry-pick all commits from `master` into the target release branch that fix the issues in this patch release. Create a PR into the release branch for these cherry-picks.
- [x]  Run `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major>.<minor>.<patch>` which sets version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json`. Commit these changes before the next step.
- [x] Run the [helm chart build script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/build/helm/package-chart.sh) (eg `./package-chart.sh 5.3.0`). This creates a tarball and updates `index.yaml` for the helm chart. Commit these changes, then cherry-pick that commit onto a branch off `master` and open a PR for it. This PR must be merged before publishing the release on GitHub in the Releasing section below.

# Releasing - Release Manager

Once all issues have been merged into `master` then the release process can start:

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by creating a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`) and then push it (e.g. `git push origin tag  <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`).
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully and images are built, notify the community by creating a post titled `<major>.<minor>.<patch> Beta Releases` in the [development](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/development/7) category of the CHT forum using this [template](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/new-topic?title=%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.%3Cpatch%3E%20Beta%20Releases&body=Hi%20Everyone%0AI%E2%80%99ve%20just%20created%20the%20%60%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.%3Cpatch%3E-beta.1%60%20tag.%0APlease%20let%20me%20know%20if%20there%E2%80%99s%20any%20final%20update%20we%20need%20to%20make.%0AIf%20all%20is%20good%2C%20then%20in%2024h%2C%20I%20will%20start%20the%20release.%20Thanks%21&category=development).
- [x] Go to the [scalability action](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/workflows/scalability.yml) and on the top right, click into "Run workflow".  Under "Use workflow from" first choose "tags" then select the `<major>.<minor>.<minor>-beta.1` tag created above. Then "Run workflow". Once it passes, check for the scalability results  ["results" directory](https://github.com/medic/scalability-results/tree/main/results). More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/tests/scalability#readme).
- [x] Go to the [Issues tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues) and filter the issues with `is:issue label:"Affects: 5.x.x" ` , replace `5.x.x` with the previous version number. Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 5.x.x` label.
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/releases/) page:
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, they have human readable descriptions, and that they're correctly labeled. In particular: they have one "Type" label, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate.
  - [x] Go to the [Release notes generator](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/workflows/release-notes.yml) and Follow [the docs](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/scripts/release-notes) for how to create the release notes, being for check for, and fix, errors.  When there are no errors, download the artifact that the release notes.
  - [x] Move the document you just downloaded into the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/releases), naming it `<major>_<minor>_<patch>.md` (eg `5_3_0.md`)
  - [x] Collect known migration steps, descriptions, screenshots, videos, data, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. This information should already be on the issue, but if not, prompt the change author to provide it.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Edit the main release notes `_index.md` [page](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/blob/main/content/en/releases/_index.md) to add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page, being sure to include the date of the release. Update the status of any releases that are past their End Of Life date.
  - [x] Ensure that the release notes PR is merged before moving to next step.
- [x] To ensure helm charts are published, make sure the helm chart PR you opened in the Development section is merged before proceeding.
- [x] Create a [new release](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases/new) in GitHub, with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, from the release branch created above as the target branch. Click on the "Choose a tag" dropdown and create a tag for the release with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. Add a link to the release notes page in the description of the release.
- [x] Once you publish the release, confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the `staging.dev.medicmobile.org` by running this `curl` call. Ensure you see the correct `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`:
   ```
   curl -s https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/_design/builds/_view/releases | jq '[.rows[] | select(.key[0]=="release")] | max_by(.value.time)'
   ```
- [x] A [Push Helm Charts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/workflows/release-helm-charts.yml) run will be triggered when the release build completes. Confirm the run completes successfully and the new release is listed on `docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/cht-core/index.yaml`.
- [x] Upgrade the [demo](https://demo-cht.dev.medicmobile.org/) instance to the newly released version.
  - [x] From the "App Management" admin console (`medic` user creds in 1Password), go to "Upgrades" and stage the upgrade for this version.
  - [x] Clone `cht-core` repo and checkout the target tag (`git checkout <major>.<minor>.x` ) to ensure you have the proper version of the helm charts.
  - [x] In your terminal, change to the `./cht-core/scripts/build/helm` directory.
  - [x] Make sure you're using the dev EKS cluster: `kubectl config use-context arn:aws:eks:eu-west-2:720541322708:cluster/dev-cht-eks`
  - [x] Ensure you have access to [EKS](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/hosting/medic/) and  to the [`demo-cht` namespace](https://github.com/medic/medic-infrastructure/issues/1344).) by calling this helm command. There should be no errors: `helm list -n demo-cht`
  - [x] Download the current `values.yaml` data from the demo instance: `helm get values demo-cht --namespace demo-cht > values.yaml`
  - [x] Edit the `values.yaml` file so `cht_image_tag` and `chtversion` properties have the new tag value `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`.
  - [x] Use helm to upgrade the instance: `helm upgrade demo-cht . --namespace demo-cht -f values.yaml`
  - [x] Refresh the "App Management" page and verify the instance upgraded. You may need to wait 5+ minutes until the upgrade succeeds.  Until then, you may see `50x` errors in the browser - be patient!
- [x] Announce the release on the Forum under the "Announcements - Releases" category by using this [template](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/new-topic?title=Announcing%20the%20release%20of%20%3Cmajor%3E.%3Cminor%3E.%3Cpatch%3E%20of%20the%20CHT%20Core%20Framework&body=%2AAnnouncing%20the%20release%20of%20%7B%7Bversion%7D%7D%20of%20%7B%7Bproduct%7D%7D%2A%0AThis%20release%20fixes%20%7B%7Bnumber%20of%20bugs%7D%7D.%20Read%20the%20%5Brelease%20notes%5D%28%7B%7Burl%7D%7D%29%20for%20full%20details.&category=releases).
- [x] Go over the list of commits and individually notify contributing / interested community members about the release.
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Fix typos in comments, test descriptions and log messages
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Spelling in code comments, test descriptions and a few log/error messages. There are about 48 typos across 38 files: for example "Failured to upload initial config document" and "server responsed with" in log messages, "No templateUrl speficied." in the admin modal service, and many in test names.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Fix the unambiguous misspellings. This changes no behavior, translations or data. Where a log message's wording is asserted in a test (the `outbound` "responded" message), the test expectation is updated to match.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Leaving them as they are. One typo is deliberately excluded: "case-insenstive" sits in a comment inside the `contacts_by_reference` CouchDB view, and editing it would change the design doc and force a view reindex on upgrade.

**Additional context**
A PR will follow. It was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code), which will be disclosed in the PR per the AI guidelines.

title: chore(#11477): fix typos in comments, test descriptions and log messages
body:
# Description

This PR fixes 48 misspellings across 38 files. It changes spelling only, no behavior.
- **Comments and JSDoc** in `api/`, `shared-libs/`, `webapp/src/ts/` and `admin/src/`, e.g. overriden, delimted, keybaord, formated, and "contant type" → "contact type".
- **Log and error message text:**
  - "Failured to upload initial config document" → "Failed to upload…" (`api/src/upload-default-docs.js`)
  - "server responsed with" → "server responded with" (`shared-libs/outbound`). The three test expectations that assert this message are updated to match.
  - "No templateUrl/controller speficied." → "specified." (`admin/src/js/services/modal.js`). No test asserts these strings.
- **Test names, comments and assertion messages** (e.g. exlamation, unknwon, langauge, equivilent, recipent). None of these are test input data.
- **Docs and config comments:** two READMEs and a Helm values comment.

**Deliberately not changed**
- "case-insenstive" in a comment inside `ddocs/medic-db/medic-client/views/contacts_by_reference/map.js`. Editing a CouchDB view changes the design doc and would trigger a view reindex on upgrade.
- Identifiers and data: `contianer` (a shell variable in `cht-docker-compose.sh`) and `non.exisiting.key` (message-key test data).
- Non-English strings, likely-vendored `openrosa2html5form.xsl`, minified libs, and domain terms (ANC, checkin).
- `messages-en.properties`: no real typos were found, so no translation keys or values change.

Closes #11477

# Code review checklist
- [x] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the [style guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/style-guide/)
- [ ] Tested: Not run locally (node_modules isn't installed on the machine that prepared this). `node --check` passes on all 31 changed `.js` files, the 7 `.ts` edits are inside comments or string literals, and the changed YAML parses. CI will run lint and unit tests.
- [x] AI disclosure: Prepared with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5). It ran a `codespell` sweep, checked each candidate in context, and made the edits. A human contributor is accountable for the PR, which stays a draft until they have reviewed it.

title: Server-side purging requests 200k hits per shard from `docs_by_replication_key`, exhausting Nouveau heap
body:
**Describe the bug**

Sentinel's contact purge (`getRecordsForContactsBatch` in `sentinel/src/lib/purging.js`) queries the `docs_by_replication_key` Nouveau index with `limit: nouveau.RESULTS_LIMIT` (200,000):

```js
const opts = {
  q: `key:(${subjectIds.map(nouveau.escapeKeys).join(' OR ')}) AND type:data_record`,
  limit: nouveau.RESULTS_LIMIT,   // 200 * 1000
};
```

CouchDB passes `limit` unchanged to every shard, so on a `q=12` database one purge query can make Nouveau build and serialize up to 12 × 200,000 hits at once. CouchDB then holds the merged result. On a production instance this used ~1.4 GB of serialized JSON in a single query and caused `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space` in the Nouveau server. The purge run then failed.

This is the same oversized query behind #11153. There, purging failed consistently with `req_timedout` because CouchDB's Nouveau client gave up after 30s. The conclusion in that issue was that "the only way to fix this is to make smaller requests", but it was closed by #11162, which upgraded to CouchDB 3.5.2 and set `[nouveau] request_timeout` to 1h (`couchdb/10-docker-default.ini`, 5.2.0+). The query itself was not changed. Each shard search now runs to completion (~200s per shard in the logs below, which would have timed out before), so the failure has moved from a timeout to a Nouveau OOM. With a 1h timeout, an oversized query can also hold Nouveau heap and threads for minutes rather than 30s.

The large limit doesn't help the purge either:

- `getRecordsForContacts` stops collecting at `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` (20,000), and anything over that throws `MAX_BATCH_SIZE_REACHED`. A 200k page can therefore be up to 10× bigger than the most the caller will accept, before the per-shard multiplier.
- On `MAX_BATCH_SIZE_REACHED` the contact batch size is halved (1000 → 500 → … → 1), and each step sends another query of the same shape. Discovering that a batch is "too big" can cost several oversized queries in a row.
- Hits that matched through the `needs_signoff` lineage keys are fetched and then thrown away in JS (`isRelevantRecordEmission`). For contacts high in the hierarchy, those discarded hits can be most of the result.

**Secondary impact: Nouveau index left unusable until restart**

The OOM also hit a concurrent index `/update` on one shard. Lucene closed that shard's `IndexWriter` but its write lock stayed held inside the JVM. Every later request for that shard index failed until the Nouveau process was restarted:

```
INFO  IndexManager: removing closed index couchdb@127.0.0.1/shards/bffffffd-d5555551/medic.<ts>/<sig>
INFO  IndexManager: opening couchdb@127.0.0.1/shards/bffffffd-d5555551/medic.<ts>/<sig>
ERROR LoggingExceptionMapper: Error handling a request: ...
! org.apache.lucene.store.LockObtainFailedException: Lock held by this virtual machine: /data/nouveau/.../index/10/write.lock
```

Every query on `docs_by_replication_key` then fails, because all shards must respond. That includes replication authorization in API (`getDocsByReplicationKeyNouveau`). The lock leak is a CouchDB/Nouveau robustness issue and should be reported upstream separately. The trigger, though, is the oversized query from purging.

**To Reproduce**

1. Have a `medic` database with `q > 1` and a hierarchy where a batch of ≤1000 contacts matches well over 20k `data_record` emissions in `docs_by_replication_key` (e.g. many `needs_signoff` reports under high-level places).
2. Configure a purge function and schedule.
3. Let sentinel purging run.
4. Watch Nouveau: each shard's `POST /index/.../search` returns a response of hundreds of thousands of hits (~117 MB each in our case), and heap usage spikes.

Reproduced locally at a smaller scale with generated data:

- `cht-couchdb:5.3.0` + `cht-couchdb-nouveau:5.3.0`, `medic` created with `q=12`, the real `docs_by_replication_key` index.
- Hierarchy: 1 district_hospital → 10 health_centers → 100 clinics → 1 CHW + 50 patients each (5,211 contacts).
- 150,000 `data_record`s submitted by the clinic CHWs about their patients, 60% with `fields.needs_signoff`.
- A script that copies the query logic of `getRecordsForContacts` / `getRecordsForContactsBatch` (same `q`, `limit`, `BATCH_LIMIT`, `isRelevantRecordEmission` filter, `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` halving), with contacts in `contacts_by_type` order.

Results:

1. **`limit` is applied per shard.** `{"q":"type:data_record","limit":5000}` made every one of the 12 shards return exactly 5,000 hits (~2.97 MB each, 35.7 MB total) for a 5,000-hit answer.
2. **Hit size matches production.** Purge-shaped queries got ~4.5 MB per shard for ~7.9k hits, ≈580 B/hit (production: 117 MB / 200k ≈ 585 B/hit).
3. **Most of what is fetched is not used.** The first contacts batch (clinics, district, health centers, then persons) matches every `needs_signoff` report through the lineage keys:
   ```
   batch=1000: query → 94,728 hits (24.7 MB); query → 11,850 hits
     kept=23,670 → MAX_BATCH_SIZE_REACHED, halving to 500
   batch=500:  query → 93,468 hits (24.4 MB), kept=8,670
   TOTAL: 3 queries, 200,046 hits fetched, 52 MB, for 8,670 usable rows
   ```
4. **OOM.** With the Nouveau heap scaled down to match the smaller dataset (`-Xmx128m`), the first purge query fails the same way as in production:
   ```
   ERROR ... LoggingExceptionMapper: Error handling a request: ab579984db3fc355
   ! java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
   "POST /index/.../shards/d5555552-eaaaaaa6/.../search HTTP/2.0" 500 110 ...
   ```
   Sentinel gets `500 internal_server_error`. An unrelated 1-hit query on the same index at the same moment failed with `rexi_EXIT {invalid_json}` (it recovered within seconds).
5. **Smaller pages avoid the OOM.** With the same 128 MB heap and a 2,000-hit page, there was no OOM and the results were identical. It took 101 round trips, though, because nothing stops paging early and the discarded lineage hits are still fetched (see fixes 2 and 3).

The `LockObtainFailedException` lock leak did not reproduce in 3 rounds of OOMs with index updates running at the same time. Nouveau recovered on its own each time.

**Expected behavior**

Purge queries should fetch pages small enough that Nouveau and CouchDB memory stays bounded and independent of shard count. They also shouldn't ask for more hits than the caller can use.

title: Uplift WebdriverIO (`@wdio/*`) beyond 9.31.2
body:
**Describe the issue**

While uplifting dependencies (#11474), from 9.31.2 to 9.32.0, the e2e suites started failing, mainly in the "More Options Menu" specs.

Claude suspects the cause is [webdriverio#15615](https://github.com/webdriverio/webdriverio/pull/15615) (9.32.0). On BiDi sessions (the wdio 9 default for Chrome), `aria/...` selectors are now resolved with the browser's accessibility-name locator (`browsingContext.locateNodes`) instead of the previous XPath heuristic. The same `aria/` selector can now match a different element than before.  The behavior here seems inconsistent at best. I was able to get CI to pass eventually on `9.32.0`, but even then it has to retry a number of tests several times before they would pass (and the run too +2x longer than normal).  

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

Claude's suggested next steps are:

- [ ] Remove the exact `9.31.2` pins on `@wdio/*` in `package.json` (back to `^`)
- [ ] Re-run the e2e suites (core, mobile, lowLevel, upgrade, visual, cht-form) on the latest wdio.
- [ ] Audit `aria/` selectors (~44 uses under `tests/`) for code that depends on *which* element is matched, especially:
  - chained `parentElement()` / sibling navigation from an `aria/` match
  - attribute checks (`aria-disabled`, classes) on the matched element or its ancestors
  - `aria/` selectors whose label matches several elements (the new locator may pick a different one)
- [ ] Prefer explicit lookups (e.g. `ancestor-or-self::*[...]` XPath, or ids/data attributes) over relative DOM navigation
- [ ] Remove any dependabot ignore added for `@wdio/*`.
- [ ] Consider bundling the wdio 10 upgrade (needs Node ≥ 22.19 and Appium 3 for `appium-uiautomator2-driver` 8).

title: feat(#11438): record DoIT gateway failure reasons and retry balance errors
body: # Description **Problem.** The Nepal DoIT SMS service (`api/src/services/nepal-doit-sms.js`) stored a fixed label per HTTP status, so every `422` was recorded as `UnprocessableContent` and treated as final. A `Balance not enough` outage therefore failed messages permanently, and nothing on the doc said why. Two more cases were wrong: a `200` with `status: 1` and a non-empty `invalid_number` was marked `sent`, and a `200` JSON reply with an unrecognised `status` was retried forever (and enough of those block the 25-message queue). **What changed** (one file; the HTTP request itself is unchanged). The rules follow @binokaryg's answers on the issue (a month of production logs + live API probes): | Gateway outcome | Result | Stored `state_details` | |---|---|---| | `422` with a string `errors` matching `/balance/i` | retried: no change, logged with the message id | none (no doc write per retry) | | any other `422` (incl. `errors.mobile` validation, i.e. unresolved recipients) | `failed` | `{ code: 422, reason: 'UnprocessableContent', error }` | | `401` (rotated/expired key: account-level, like balance) | retried: no change, logged with the message id | none | | `500`, `504`, other HTTP errors, network/JSON-parse errors | retried (as before) | none | | `200`, `status: 1` (or `'1'`), empty or missing `invalid_number` | `sent` (a warning is logged when it's missing or not an array) | `'Processed'` (as before) | | `200`, `status: 1` (or `'1'`), non-empty `invalid_number` | `failed` | `{ code: 200, reason: 'InvalidNumber', error: '["98…"]' }` | | `200`, a JSON object with any other `status` (unknown or missing) | `failed` | `{ code: 200, reason: 'InvalidResponse', error: }` | | `200`, a body that is not a JSON object (HTML page, empty or text body) | retried: no change, logged at error with the message id and a body excerpt | none | `error` is the gateway's own `errors`/`message` text (or a body excerpt), cut to 255 UTF-16 units and made well-formed with `toWellFormed()` (Node ≥ 22.15 per `engines`). A split surrogate pair would make CouchDB reject the whole batch write (`invalid UTF-8 JSON`), losing every state change in it and resending those messages each minute; we reproduced that and guard it with tests. Error log lines now include the message id; account-level retries (balance, `401`) are logged once, at `warn`, instead of an error line plus a warning. **Choices worth flagging** - Success needs `status` exactly `1` or `'1'` (master matched both; `true` or `' 1 '` are not accepted). Per @binokaryg's follow-up, a missing or non-array `invalid_number` still counts as success (with a warning), so a gateway format change can't fail every message; only a non-empty array fails. `401` is now retried (with a warning) instead of failed. - A `200` whose body is not a JSON object (a proxy, maintenance or nginx page; couch-request returns those as text) is not a gateway verdict, so it is retried like the `504` page, as @binokaryg asked in review. - An empty or malformed `application/json` body still throws inside couch-request before we see it, so it stays on the retry path, like network errors. - The `Invalid number.` test data comes from the DoIT guide; per the maintainer it never occurs in production. The production-backed cases are `errors.mobile` and the `invalid_number` response. - Not in this PR (agreed on the issue): a cap on how old a retried message may be, and surfacing account-level failures in monitoring (`messaging.outgoing.gateway`) / `GET /api/balance`. Messages already `failed` by the old code are not retried automatically. **How it was tested** - Unit: `api/tests/mocha/services/nepal-doit-sms.spec.js` (43 tests), e.g. `retries a 422 balance error instead of failing the message`, `matches any balance error case-insensitively`, `fails a number the gateway lists as invalid, logging the message id` (the maintainer's live response), `fails any other status in a successful response, without mapping it to an HTTP status`, `keeps recorded response bodies bounded and well-formed`, `stores a well-formed error when the cut splits a character, whatever the error source`, `still retries a 504 gateway page`. On master's service 36 of them fail; each new rule was also checked against deliberately broken variants. `npm run lint` and all unit suites (webapp, admin, shared-libs, api, sentinel, couchdb) pass. - End-to-end on a local CHT (CouchDB + this API) against a fake DoIT gateway returning real DoIT-style bodies, 19 scenarios, master vs this branch, over an outage and a top-up. Before: the rejected number is `sent`, balance messages stay `failed` after the top-up, unknown/empty `200`s are retried forever. After: balance messages are `sent` after the top-up, everything terminal is attempted once, a successful sibling is sent exactly once, no CouchDB errors. - From the app UI: messages to a contact with a working number are `sent` exactly once (happy path); a message sent to a contact whose number the (fake) gateway rejects with the maintainer's `invalid_number` response ends up `failed` (`InvalidNumber`) in the conversation view; on master it shows `sent`. - Admin app, Outgoing messages → Due, before / after: before after admin queue 18 sms user message failed Note: the screenshots predate the last two commits; since then a `401` and a non-JSON `200` page are retried (the message stays pending) instead of failed. Closes #11438 # Code review checklist - [x] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the [style guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/style-guide/) - [x] Tested: Unit and/or e2e where appropriate - [x] Backwards compatible: Works with existing data and configuration or includes a migration. Any breaking changes documented in the release notes. - [x] AI disclosure: Please disclose use of AI per [the guidelines](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/community/contributing/ai-guidelines/). title: fix(#11490): nouveau results limit
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

feat(#1234): add hat wobble
^--^(#^--^): ^------------^
|     |      |
|     |      + - > subject
|     |
|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: build|feat|fix|perf|refactor|test|chore

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

<!-- DESCRIPTION -->

## Reduce nouveau result limit from 200K to 20K
## Allow authorization nouveau query to page through results if more than the limit

Authorization currently would silently drop results if `docs_by_replication_key` returned more than `RESULTS_LIMIT` results.
This wasn't any issue because with a limit of 200K, authorization would fail for any users with more documents than that anyway.
With a smaller limit, its more likely that it will actually be reached by normal users, so its necessary to allow authorization to page through multiple pages of results. A 20K limit means only larger users will need multiple pages, but some larger users will likely surpass that limit. 

## Change purging's nouveau query to not include `needs_signoff` results.

This change is related because this is likely what allowed > 200K results to be returned from nouveau.
In `docs_by_replication_key`, a `needs_signoff` report adds every contact in its submitter's lineage to key, besides its subject. Purging queried by key, so each batch also pulled in every `needs_signoff` report below those contacts. `isRelevantRecordEmission` then explicitly removed all of those reports from the results. For high-level places this could be most of the result. It also tripped `MAX_BATCH_SIZE_REACHED` on hits that would be discarded anyway, which caused needless batch halving.

The double negatives can be confusing, but we can be very sure that this doesn't change the results: the index function always puts the subject into `key`, and adds lineage ids only when it also stores `needs_signoff`. The old filter dropped a hit only when it was `needs_signoff` and its subject wasn't in the queried ids. Those are exactly the hits that matched only through lineage.

Changing the query to query by `subject` directly instead of `key` means that only reports with a matching subject are returned, and higher level contacts are not more expensive than leaf contacts.

## Out of scope

Two things are not addressed in this PR to keep it minimal and hopefully allow it to be released quickly.
datasource does not use results limit, so it is still possible to trigger out of memory errors in nouveau by requesting a huge limit. This can be addressed in a different PR.
The purging algorithm keeps its current behavior when more than the maximum number of results are returned, which is to throw away the already loaded results, reduce the batch size by half, and try again. This could use a refactor, also in a different branch to keep this PR small.

title: fix(#11449): preserve filtered page rows

# Description

Fixes filtered pagination so its cursor advances by the source rows actually consumed to fill a page, rather than by the number of accepted documents. This prevents accepted contact/report records in an over-fetch surplus from being skipped on the next page.
